_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-05-as-built-baseline · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-05T18:55:16Z

Establish the fork's measured starting point: the adopted workspace, untouched, builds and passes its `blitz-tests`
integration suite on THIS host, with each step's wall-clock and the host facts that make the run reproducible on
record. It is the first rung of the version's infrastructure-first order (intent.md §Principles), and every later
chunk's gates read against it — "Fork CI reached" compares its CI leg with this local reading.

The chunk writes no product code (scope §Boundaries). Two things are ASSERTED green — the workspace build and the
blitz-tests suite (with its one font-skip site proved not to skip) — and four wider gates are RECORDED, never counted
green: `cargo test --workspace` (CI's test leg), `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`
and rustdoc `-D warnings` — leaned on the operator's word at P4 ("Record them", the overseer: "the baseline states
where every done-gate stands before any code moves"). The build figure is from-empty: `cargo clean` runs first (P4
fork, operator's word "cargo clean first").

Per arch §Stack and Technologies + §Established Decisions [Dependency pinning] [Build profiles], test-plan §2 §5 §9,
security-plan §Dependency Security, design-system §Typography, obs-plan §2 §5 §8, a11y-plan §1 §3.

1. **Host facts, re-measured at implement time** — run the probes research used (research.md §Host facts measured):
   `uname -srm`, `/etc/os-release` NAME/BUILD_ID, `nproc`, `free -g`, `rustc -V`, `cargo -V`, `rustup show
   active-toolchain`, `pacman -Q fontconfig openssl pkgconf python`, `fc-match sans-serif|serif|monospace`, and
   whether `PAINT_TREE_BENCH_HTML` / `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` / `RUSTFLAGS` are set (set/unset only — never a value dump).
   A fact that moved since P3 is recorded as measured now, with the P3 reading beside it.
2. **Clean** — `cargo clean` at the project root, so the first gate run's `build` entry is a from-empty compile.

3. **Cold gate run** — fire the `## Test Commands` block (/implement P2's firing form). This is the COLD reading:
   take each entry's seconds and outcome word from the gate trail. Entry `test -s …/evidence/baseline.md …` (the
   evidence probe) is RED on this first run by construction — the record does not exist yet; it is not a defect.

4. **Write the record** — create `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-05-as-built-baseline/evidence/baseline.md` (Write tool)
   with exactly these six `##` sections, in order:
   - `## Host` — step 1's facts; toolchain read against MSRV `1.91.0` / edition 2024 and the flake's unused `1.90.0` pin;
     the Arch stand-ins for CI's `libfontconfig1-dev` + build-time python3; the fonts fontconfig resolves.
   - `## Commands` — every gate `run` verbatim, the profile (dev — no `--release`, no `production`/`p2`), the feature
     basis (workspace defaults; blitz-tests forces blitz-dom `accessibility`/`floats`/`system-fonts`; no
     `--no-default-features`; `log-times`/`log-frame-times`/`log-phase-times` off), and that CI's `opt-level = 2 → 0`
     rewrite was NOT applied because it touches only `[profile.p2]` (Cargo.toml:210 — research §Patterns detected).
   - `## Wall-clock` — per entry: cold seconds (step 3, after `cargo clean`), warm seconds (step 5); the basis of each
     stated in one line.
   - `## Tests` — blitz-tests tallies from the log's `test result:` lines (passed · failed · ignored, summed over the
     61 result lines — 59 files + lib unittests + doc-tests; P5 baseline: 255 · 0 · 3), the ignored set named (`paint_tree_bench`, 3 `#[ignore]` — research's grep), `incremental_oracle`'s
     own result, and the font-skip reading (the `--nocapture` entry's output lacks `skipping: no usable font`).
   - `## A11y-bearing files` — pass/fail per file: `accessibility_hidden`, `accessibility_roles`,
     `focusability_updates`, `interaction_state_teardown`, `harness_smoke`, `scrollbars`, `scrollbar_drag`.
   - `## Wider gates` — each recorded entry's outcome as its own summary (exit, the tool's last summary line, counts of
     warnings/errors where it prints them); a red one names its owner-to-be for the wrap (see Implementation notes).
   Summaries and exit statuses only: no raw log is copied into the tree (obs-plan §8), no env dump (security-plan
   §Secret Management).

5. **Warm gate run** — fire the block again. Every asserted entry must be green, the evidence probe included; append
   the warm seconds to `## Wall-clock`.
- `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-05-as-built-baseline/evidence/baseline.md` — the baseline record (six sections, step 4)
- none

No boot-path and no live leg in this chunk: it touches no source, so there is no `smoke` entry and no harness verb
(`scripts/agent-run.*` is owned by "Stand test contract"). The four wider gates are report-only (`expect = []`,
outcome `recorded` — never counted green): their reading is the baseline's content, not its acceptance. No entry
reads CI, so no `operator` entry exists and the tree guard below reads the worktree base-less. The record
`evidence/baseline.md` has no producing entry by construction: /implement step 4 authors it from the gate trail
(it is a document, not a runtime artifact a command emits); the evidence probe and the credential probe verify it.

  the chunk's edits is the same tree. Classify it first: host-local (a missing system package, a font) → fix on the

     Record which ones in `evidence/instrument-red.md`.

7. **ci.yml** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`).
   - Add a workflow-level `permissions: contents: read`. Every job only checks out, restores or saves caches and
     uploads artifacts, and none of those needs a `GITHUB_TOKEN` scope beyond `contents: read`.
   - SHA-pin every `uses:` with the tag kept as a trailing comment. Re-resolve each SHA at implement time
     (research.md lists the 2026-10-05 readings). Each `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` step pinned by SHA gets an explicit
     `toolchain:` input (`stable`, or `1.91` for MSRV), because the `@stable` branch name no longer selects it.
   - `test-features-default`'s rust-cache step gets a `shared-key` (e.g. `workspace-test`), and its save rule is
     unchanged.
   - New job `audit` ("Dependency audit"): `needs` the four fast jobs. Steps: checkout, rust-toolchain stable,
     `taiki-e/install-action` (SHA-pinned) with `tool: cargo-deny@0.20.2`, then `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh
     audit`, then the failure-log upload. No cache step.
   - New job `a11y` ("Accessibility (a11y) tests"): `needs` the four fast jobs. Steps: checkout, rust-toolchain
     stable, rust-cache with the same `shared-key` and `save-if: false`, `libfontconfig1-dev`, `bash
     .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh a11y`, failure-log upload.
   - New job `coverage` ("Coverage report"): `needs` the four fast jobs. Steps: checkout, rust-toolchain stable with
     `components: llvm-tools-preview`, `taiki-e/install-action` with `tool: cargo-llvm-cov@0.9.1`,
     `libfontconfig1-dev`, `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh coverage`, an upload named `coverage-report` of
     `target/coverage/` (`retention-days: 7`, on success), and the failure-log upload. No cache step.
   - The upstream-only workflows are not edited (§Constraints).

8. **Host prerequisite for the coverage leg.** Run `rustup component add llvm-tools-preview` on the dev host
   (absent there, research.md §Measurements). This is an operator-visible host change, recorded in
   `evidence/host.md`.

9. **Run the gates** (§Test Commands) and write `evidence/` readings. These are: the instrument red→green
   (step 6), the audit firing set (step 5), the Cargo.lock delta, the coverage summary's TOTAL line, and the
   a11y counts.
- `deny.toml` — cargo-deny graph (targets, all features) and the per-ID advisory ignores with reasons
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — workflow `permissions`, SHA pins with `toolchain` inputs, `shared-key` on the test cache, jobs `audit` / `a11y` / `coverage`
- `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh` — `doc` workspace-wide `--no-deps`; new arms `audit` / `a11y` / `coverage`
- `.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py` — new invariants (pins, permissions, legs, doc form, a11y name, coverage artifact); pin-tolerant cache matcher
- `Cargo.lock` — rustls 0.23.43 → 0.23.45
- `apps/browser/Cargo.toml` — `doc = false` on the `blitz` bin
- `packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs` — 3 doc-link fixes
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs` — 2 doc-link fixes
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/replaced.rs` — bare URL to an autolink
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/traversal.rs` — 2 redundant link targets
- `examples/transparent/src/main.rs` — 1 doc-link fix

Host gates come first (entries 1-14), then the operator pass (entries 15-18). There is no boot path and no `live`
leg: the chunk changes CI legs, a lockfile entry, doc text and one manifest key, so there is no smoke and no
self-verify (no UI surface). This sentence is the record of that absence. The local pre-push gate is `bash
.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast`, and it rides inside the push entry, so the operator pass re-runs it before every
push and fix push. The CI reads need the operator's commit and push first, because /implement never commits, so the
hygiene entry, the push and the CI reads are `operator` entries. They use
`/home/turbolet/.claude/skills/andromeda-tools/scripts` as `{tools_dir}`, substituted literally. `--wait 3000`
covers the pipeline this chunk produces. Its Cargo.lock change re-keys every rust cache once (arch §Occupied
Resources → CI infrastructure), and the uncached coverage leg runs cold. Phase Setup 5a read the last warm run at
431 s, and the first cold build-branch run was 1255 s. Entry 18 records the per-job timings. If the coverage job
lengthens the pipeline wall-clock, that is RECORDED, not gated: it is the overseer's ask at the P4 fork, and the
shared-cache-key lever is for a later chunk. The instrument this chunk extends runs red before green at

body:
- (CARRY / arch) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` runs `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked` under
  `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings"` and exits 0 with no `output filename collision` line. The 9 errors in blitz-dom,
  blitz-vibey-script and transparent are gone, and ci.yml's docs job runs that same leg (per architecture
  §Stack and Technologies → Code quality; §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD).

- (tests) The rustdoc fixes change no behaviour: `cargo test --workspace --locked` sums to `407 0 3` (passed ·
  failed · ignored), the test-plan §9 Local baseline (per test-plan §9 Local baseline).

- (security) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh audit` (cargo-deny advisories over `deny.toml`) exits 0 at the
  chunk's tree. Every ignore is per-ID with a written reason (no blanket allow), and RUSTSEC-2026-0285 is out of
  Cargo.lock (rustls 0.23.45) (per security-plan §Bootstrap phases `dep-audit-tooling-install`,
  `dep-security-ci-gate`; §Dependency Security).

- (security) Every `uses:` in ci.yml is pinned to a 40-hex commit SHA, and ci.yml declares a workflow-level
  `permissions: contents: read` with no job-level grant. `test_ci_workflows.py` asserts both (per security-plan
  §Dependency Security → Pinning; §Authentication & Authorization).

- (a11y) ci.yml carries a job named for accessibility that runs `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh a11y`. That leg runs
  `accessibility_hidden` (6), `accessibility_roles` (6) and `focusability_updates` (3) and none reads `running 0
  tests`, and a11y-plan §9's own search over ci.yml finds the job (per a11y-plan §9 CI Integration; §3 Bootstrap
  phases `a11y-ci-gate-wire`).

- (tests / obs) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh coverage` writes a non-empty `target/coverage/lcov.info` and prints
  a summary with no threshold. ci.yml uploads `target/coverage/` as its own `coverage-report` artifact, kept 7 days,
  never inside `ci-log-*` (per test-plan §3 Bootstrap phases `coverage-tooling-install`; obs-plan §9 Telemetry
  artifact handling).

- (arch / tests) Each new job runs its leg through `ci-leg.sh`, `needs` the four fast jobs, and carries the
  failure-only `ci-log-{job id}` upload. The fast/slow split and the upstream repository guards stay green under
  `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts` (per architecture §Standard Contracts → CI contracts; test-plan
  §9 Pipeline facts).

- (arch) No new cache entry: `a11y` restores the test job's shared key with `save-if: false`, and `coverage` and
  `audit` carry no cache step. The root Cargo.toml is untouched (per architecture §Occupied Resources → CI
  infrastructure; §Established Decisions → [Dependency pinning]).

- (CI) The fork's CI run on the pushed chunk sha reads `verdict: green` through `ci.py conclusion` (entry 17), the
  three new jobs included. Its run id and per-job timings are recorded in `evidence/` (per test-plan §9 Pipeline
  facts).

- No verification-matrix capability is claimed: none of the 15 escher-0.1.0 capabilities (all stand/driver
  outcomes, `matrix.py show --unclaimed`) is made verifiable by CI gate legs.

- Spec anchors: architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD · §Standard Contracts → CI contracts · §Occupied
  Resources → CI infrastructure / Names · §Established Decisions → [Dependency pinning] · §Conventions →
  Documentation · security-plan §Dependency Security (Pinning, Supply chain integrity) · §Authentication &
  Authorization · §Bootstrap phases · test-plan §3 Bootstrap phases · §4 · §9 · a11y-plan §1 · §3 · §9 · obs-plan
  §2 · §9.

- History: the 2026-10-05-as-built-baseline arch/test entries (the CARRY's origin) and the 2026-10-05-fork-ci-reached
  arch/security/test/obs entries (the leg-script shape, the cache budget, the repository guards, the citation
  re-point precedent).

- Research: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh`, `.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py`,
  `apps/browser/Cargo.toml`, the 4 rustdoc-error files, `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`.

- Forks, decided at P4 by the overseer on the founder's standing delegation of technical forks (2026-10-05,
  «на технические вопросы ты отвечаешь сам»): audit tool **cargo-deny**; coverage leg **uncached**, with any
  pipeline wall-clock growth recorded and the shared-cache-key lever left to a later chunk.

- P5 review (overseer, same delegation, 2026-10-05): cargo-deny stands after the correction that its default graph
  fires on ttf-parser alone, and the real ignore list is measured at implement (step 5). The `coverage-report`
  upload is ratified (see the obs-plan Expected amendment). `rustup component add llvm-tools-preview` on the dev
  host is approved (step 8).

- Leaned, decisive: ci.yml only is pinned, per the 2026-10-05-fork-ci-reached arch entry (the upstream-only
  workflows run only in `DioxusLabs/blitz` and were kept for small upstream merges). A workflow-level
  `permissions` block, because GitHub jobs inherit it and each job uses only `contents: read`. The audit job goes in
  the slow tier, so an External-decay red (playbook) cannot block every slow leg through the fast set.

- cargo-audit as the gate — rejected at the P4 fork (overseer): it fails on vulnerabilities only, so unmaintained
  and unsound findings would stay unowned.

- A rust-cache entry for the coverage job — rejected at the P4 fork (overseer): an instrumented target over a
  ≈ 9.73 / 10 GB cache evicts the other legs' entries.

- `-p blitz-tests` for the a11y leg — rejected: it resolves features differently from the `test` leg, so the
  restored shared cache would not match. Use `--workspace --test …`.

- A new job in `FAST_JOBS` — rejected: every slow job `needs` the fast set, so an advisory-DB red would block them
  all, and `test_c` pins the set.
- Renaming the browser bin `blitz` — rejected: §Occupied Resources → Names. `doc = false` resolves the collision.
- `--keep-going` in the doc leg — rejected: the gate must stop red. `--keep-going` is a diagnostic only.

- A blanket advisory allow, or `unmaintained`/`unsound` set to none — rejected: it empties the gate (security-plan
  §Dependency Security). Use per-ID ignores with reasons.

- Bumping one side of a coupled pin to clear an advisory — rejected (CLAUDE.md, arch §Established Decisions →
  [Dependency pinning]). Record such an advisory as a reasoned ignore.

- Pinning or adding `permissions` to publish-browser.yml / wpt.yml / wpt-post-results.yml — not this chunk. They never
  run on the fork, and a ref-only `if:` would re-arm them (UpstreamGuardTest keeps the guard).

- Per-job `permissions` blocks duplicating the workflow-level one — rejected: inherited, and the duplication adds no
  narrowing.

- `test_b` matches `uses == "Swatinem/rust-cache@v2"` exactly (`.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py:76`), so the SHA
  pin and the matcher change land together. Otherwise every compiling job fails `test_b`.

- `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` (ci.yml:58, :77, :97, :196) selects the toolchain by branch name. A SHA pin with no

body: - The CARRY's measurements hold exactly at HEAD under the new `line-tables-only` profile. `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked --keep-going` exits 101 with 3 crates failing: blitz-vibey-script 3 errors, blitz-dom 5, transparent 1, so 9 in all. The `target/doc/blitz/index.html` filename collision warning is present too. Without `--keep-going`, cargo stops at the first failing crate and lists only blitz-dom's 5. Every error is doc-text-only (unresolved, private or redundant links, and a bare URL). The collision is the `blitz` bin of `apps/browser`, and a `doc = false` key on that bin resolves it without a rename.

- The docs job today runs `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc`, whose leg is `cargo doc --locked` (ci-leg.sh:32): no `--workspace`, so it documents only the lib-less root package `blitz-examples`. Verified.

- Choosing the audit tool (cargo-audit vs cargo-deny `advisories`, and whether bans/sources/licenses come too) is a P4 fork. security-plan names both candidates, and both are on the dev host (cargo-deny 0.20.2, cargo-audit 0.22.2). In CI the tool is installed at a pinned version.

- [premise-corrected: `cargo audit --json` at HEAD returned 1 vulnerability + 3 warnings, so "unknown until the first run" is false] The advisories firing today are **RUSTSEC-2026-0285** `rustls 0.23.43` (vulnerability; patched `>=0.23.45`; via reqwest/hyper-rustls ← blitz-net), **RUSTSEC-2024-0436** `paste 1.0.15` (unmaintained; via rav1e), **RUSTSEC-2026-0192** `ttf-parser 0.25.1` (unmaintained; via ab_glyph ← sctk-adwaita) and **RUSTSEC-2026-0186** `memmap2 0.5.10` (unsound; via cacache ← http-cache, blitz-net's optional `cache` feature). None sits on a coupled pin. [premise-corrected at P4: cargo-deny 0.20.2's default graph fires on ttf-parser alone and logs rustls/paste/memmap2 as `filtered`; no build graph reaches rustls (`cargo tree --workspace --all-features --target all -e all -i rustls` → nothing to print), so it is a lockfile-only entry] rustls is still bumped by a semver-patch lockfile update, which takes the vulnerable version out of Cargo.lock for every lockfile-wide scanner. Whatever the committed `deny.toml` graph fires on is either an upgrade or a recorded per-ID ignore with a reason. There is never a blanket allow.

- The coverage tool is a P4 lean: cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1 is on the host and tarpaulin is absent. cargo-llvm-cov needs the `llvm-tools-preview` rustup component, which is NOT installed on the host's stable toolchain, so it is a stated host prerequisite and a CI toolchain component. The instrumented build is a separate compile, so its cache policy against the ≈ 9.73 / 10 GB Actions cache is a P4 fork.

- The a11y leg runs tests that already exist: `tests/blitz-tests` `accessibility_hidden` (6), `accessibility_roles` (6) and `focusability_updates` (3), 15 tests with no font-dependent skip. `-p blitz-tests` keeps `accessibility` on through blitz-tests' own dev-dependency features (`tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml:16`). The leg adds no new a11y assertions. "Stand a11y assertions" (Epoch 6) fills it later.

- Pinning covers the fork-active workflow, ci.yml. The three upstream-only workflows are repository-guarded, and their `permissions:` are already explicit (wpt-post-results.yml:8-11, wpt.yml:18-21, publish-browser.yml:38-39). Whether to also pin their `uses:` is a P4 lean.
- A SHA-pinned `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` loses the toolchain its `@stable` branch name selected, so every SHA-pinned use carries an explicit `toolchain:` input (research.md, action refs).

- Each workflow-invariant change (SHA pins, `permissions:`, the new legs, the doc-leg form) is pinned in `.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py`. Its `test_b` matches the cache step by the exact string `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2` (:76), so SHA-pinning requires reworking that matcher. Its `test_d` requires every new linux job in `LINUX_JOB_LEGS`.

- No new workspace crate, env var, listener or secret. A new CI tool (audit, coverage) is CI infrastructure, registered under arch §Occupied Resources → CI infrastructure if it occupies anything (cache budget).
- No new accessibility assertions on stand controls ("Stand a11y assertions"). No coverage threshold or quality gate ("Quality gates", Epoch 6).

- **Forks decided (P4 round, answered by the overseer under the founder's delegation — authority: founder, 2026-10-05, explicit delegation in his own words, 'сам решай', given in the overseer session before the overseer answered; relayed verbatim by the operator, 2026-10-05, at the P5 review, which records these answers as NOT provisional · the earlier record "delegate overseer — provisional per gate-contract.md §Scope, *Whose word*" superseded 2026-10-05):** debuginfo in a workspace `[profile.dev]` stanza (one debuginfo level for host and CI) · slow legs wait on the fast legs (`needs:`) · the 59 blitz-tests binaries are NOT consolidated here (measure after cache + debuginfo; a later chunk if linking still dominates)

Make the fork's GitHub Actions pipeline run on escher's build branch and give fast feedback without rebuilding the
dependency graph on every push — the founder's concern ("надеюсь ci не будет все это каждый раз пересобирать",
inputs#I1). Today a push to `build/escher-0.1.0` triggers nothing (ci.yml:3-8; 0 runs on the fork), 7 of the
compiling jobs carry no cache, and the one cache that exists never saves off `main` (ci.yml:205) — so every
build-branch run would be fully cold; debuginfo is 82 % of a test binary's bytes (research.md §Measured facts).

1. **`Cargo.toml` — the debuginfo level.** Add one stanza, `[profile.dev]` with `debug = "line-tables-only"`,
   placed with the other `[profile.*]` stanzas (Cargo.toml:195-235). Nothing else in the file changes: no
   `[workspace.dependencies]` pin, no other profile (`production` stays byte-identical). The `test` profile inherits
   `dev`, so test builds take the same level.

2. **`.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh` — the one definition of every linux leg.** A bash script (`set -euo pipefail`)
   taking one leg name. It exports `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings"` (the workflow-wide value at ci.yml:14-15, so a
   local doctest compiles as CI's does), creates `target/ci-logs/`, and runs the leg's command with its merged
   output written to `target/ci-logs/{leg}.log` — truncated at the start of the leg, never appended — exiting
   with the command's own status. The legs and their exact commands:
   - `fmt` — `cargo fmt --all --check`
   - `clippy` — `cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings`
   - `test` — `cargo test --workspace --locked`
   - `ci-scripts` — `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts`
   - `build` — `cargo build --workspace --locked`
   - `msrv` — `cargo +1.91 build --workspace --locked`
   - `counter` — `cargo build -p counter --locked`
   - `wasm` — `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` run in `examples/wasm_hello` (no `--locked`: that
     directory carries no `Cargo.lock`), then `cargo build -p seven_guis --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
     --no-default-features --features hybrid --locked` and the same for `todomvc` (ci.yml:79-85's commands)
   - `doc` — `cargo doc --locked` (bare, as ci.yml:124 — the real rustdoc gate is "CI gate legs"' CARRY)
   - `fast` — the local pre-push gate: `fmt`, `clippy`, `test`, `ci-scripts` in that order, stopping at the
     first red and exiting with its status
   An unknown or missing leg name prints the leg list to stderr and exits 2.

3. **`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — trigger.** Add `build/**` to `on.push.branches` beside `main` and `v0.*`. Keep
   `pull_request`, the per-ref `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress` and the workflow `env` as they are.

4. **`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — fast legs.** Jobs `fmt`, `clippy`, `test-features-default` and `ci-scripts`
   each run their leg through `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh {leg}` (legs `fmt`, `clippy`, `test`, `ci-scripts`)
   in place of the inline command. Each compiling one (`clippy`, `test-features-default`) installs
   `libfontconfig1-dev` as today and adds `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2` after the toolchain step with
   `save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/build/') }}`. `ci-scripts`
   ensures PyYAML before its leg: `python3 -c 'import yaml' || (sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y
   python3-yaml)`. The `perl … 's/opt-level = 2/opt-level = 0/g'` steps are removed from every job — they rewrite
   only `[profile.p2]` (Cargo.toml:210) and leave a dev/test build unchanged (baseline.md:57-59; research.md).

5. **`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — slow legs.** Jobs `build-msrv`, `build-features-default`, `build-counter`,
   `build-wasm-examples`, `doc` and `matrix_test` each declare `needs: [fmt, clippy, test-features-default,
   ci-scripts]`. The five linux build jobs run their leg through `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh {leg}` (legs
   `msrv`, `build`, `counter`, `wasm`, `doc`) and each adds the same `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2` step and `save-if`
   rule as step 4 (`build-msrv` keeps `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master` with `toolchain: 1.91`, so `cargo +1.91`
   resolves). `matrix_test`: drop the `linux` platform entry (its `cargo test --all --tests --target
   x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` duplicates `test-features-default`'s compile in a separate target tree —
   research.md §Measured facts; linux stays tested by the fast `test` leg, doctests included); widen its existing
   `save-if` to the step-4 rule; append `--locked` to its test/build command; run that command with `shell: bash`,
   its merged output written to `target/ci-logs/matrix-${{ matrix.platform.name }}.log`.

6. **`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — failure artifacts.** Every job that runs a leg ends with
   `actions/upload-artifact@v7`, `if: failure()`, `name: ci-log-{the job id}` (matrix:
   `ci-log-matrix-${{ matrix.platform.name }}`), `path:` the ONE log file its own leg writes
   (`target/ci-logs/{leg}.log`), `retention-days: 7`, `if-no-files-found: ignore`. No upload path names anything
   outside `target/ci-logs/`.

7. **Upstream-only guards.** `.github/workflows/publish-browser.yml` job `release-cli` gains
   `if: github.repository == 'DioxusLabs/blitz'`; `.github/workflows/wpt.yml` job `wpt` gains the same `if`, and
   job `trigger-archive`'s existing condition becomes `github.repository == 'DioxusLabs/blitz' && github.ref ==
   'refs/heads/main'`; `.github/workflows/wpt-post-results.yml` job `post-results`'s existing condition gains
   `github.repository == 'DioxusLabs/blitz' && ` in front. No step, trigger, secret reference or
   write/`always()`-remove pair inside these workflows changes.

8. **`.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py` — the invariants, as `unittest` (one `TestCase` per concern,
   per arch §Conventions Tests).** It loads the four workflows with PyYAML (YAML's `on:` key reads as `True` —
   handle it) and asserts: (a) ci.yml's push branches include `build/**`; (b) every ci.yml job that runs a cargo
   leg has a `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2` step whose `save-if` names both `refs/heads/main` and `refs/heads/build/`;
   (c) the fast set is exactly `fmt`, `clippy`, `test-features-default`, `ci-scripts` with no `needs`, and every
   other ci.yml job `needs` all four; (d) every linux ci.yml job's leg step runs `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh
   {leg}` and each named leg exists in the script's leg list; (e) every leg job has an `if: failure()`
   `actions/upload-artifact` step whose path lies under `target/ci-logs/`; (f) every job of publish-browser.yml,
   wpt.yml and wpt-post-results.yml carries `github.repository == 'DioxusLabs/blitz'` in its `if`; (g) no ci.yml
   step references `secrets.`; (h) no `perl` rewrite remains in ci.yml; (i) the matrix has no `linux` entry and
   still lists windows, macos, ios and android. A second TestCase runs `ci-leg.sh` in a temporary directory with a
   `cargo` shim on `PATH` that prints a marker line and exits 1, and asserts the script exits non-zero and wrote
   `target/ci-logs/{leg}.log` containing the marker — the producer of the failure artifact, proved on the host —
   and that an unknown leg exits 2.

9. **Re-measure the test-plan §9 local baseline under the new profile** (the "dev profile" condition moved, per
   test-plan §9 Local baseline): `cargo clean`, then the baseline's own method — entries 1 (`cargo build
   --workspace --locked`), 2 (`cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked`) and 4 (`cargo test --workspace --locked`) cold
   in sequence in one `target/`, then the immediate warm re-run — recording wall-clock, the pass/fail/ignore
   counts and `du -sh target/debug` in `chunks/2026-10-05-fork-ci-reached/evidence/baseline-rerun.md`, beside the
   prior figures (120.26/5.54 s · 486.45/7.41 s · 1632.88/13.08 s, baseline.md:72-75; 85G). Predicted: every
   cold figure and the target size fall — record what the re-run measures.
- `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh` — the leg commands (step 2)
- `.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py` — workflow invariants + the leg-script producer test (step 8)
- `Cargo.toml` — `[profile.dev] debug = "line-tables-only"` (step 1)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — trigger, fast/slow split, caches, leg script, failure artifacts, linux-matrix dedupe, `--locked` (steps 3-6)
- `.github/workflows/publish-browser.yml` — upstream-only guard (step 7)
- `.github/workflows/wpt.yml` — upstream-only guard (step 7)
- `.github/workflows/wpt-post-results.yml` — upstream-only guard (step 7)

Host gates first (entries 1-9), then the operator pass (entries 10-15). No boot path and no live leg: the chunk

fast`; it rides inside the push entry (11), so the operator pass re-runs it before every push and fix push. The

hygiene, the fast leg + clean-tree guard, the pre-CI commit, the push, the cold and warm `ci.py` reads (via `gh run
rerun`) and the timings. `--wait 6000` covers a cold first run (fast legs, then the uncached
windows/macos/ios/android legs behind them; the fork has no prior CI wall-clock — phase Setup 5a read `none
recorded`). Entry 13 re-runs that same run once its caches are saved, so entry 14 reads the WARM verdict on the
same sha; entry 15 records both runs' job timings — the cache's effect is recorded, not forecast as a pass/fail.
Two criteria have no listed producer by design. Step 9's baseline re-measure (`evidence/baseline-rerun.md`)

The failure log `target/ci-logs/{leg}.log` is produced inside the unit entry's own temporary directory (step 8's

title: Detailed scope (P3 premise closure applied — see research.md for each derivation)

data.head: ## Detailed scope (P3 premise closure applied — see research.md for each derivation)

body: - `ci.yml`'s `on:` gains the build-branch pattern (`build/**`). Verified: today it fires only on `pull_request` and on push to `main`/`v0.*` (ci.yml:3-8), and the fork has run 0 workflows (`gh api …/actions/runs` → 0). I1 fact (2) holds (inputs#I1).

- [premise-corrected: the signing workflow is armed by ref, not by branch name — publish-browser.yml:2-7/:40 fires on the fork's `main` and on its existing `ci-test/sign-android-builds` branch, and the fork holds 0 secrets and 0 environments] "Signing-secret jobs excluded" means no FORK ref fires publish-browser.yml's signing jobs: a repository guard (upstream-only), not just keeping it off `build/**`, which already does not trigger it.

- [premise-corrected: wpt.yml runs on the upstream-only `warp-ubuntu-latest-arm64-16x` runner (:26), deploys Pages and dispatches to `DioxusLabs/blitz-wpt-results` on main (:94-118), and diffs against upstream's published report (:75-76); wpt-post-results.yml writes PR bodies with `GITHUB_TOKEN`] WPT on the fork is classified EXCLUDED (upstream-only guard on both WPT workflows), not fast or slow. WPT stays host-reproducible through `cargo run -rp wpt css svg` / `just wpt`.

- [premise-corrected: 7 compiling jobs are uncached, not 5 — build-counter and build-wasm-examples too; and `save-if` is main-only (ci.yml:205), so even matrix_test never saves a build-branch cache] Every compiling job gets a dependency cache whose save rule covers the build branch, so a second push restores what the first saved.

- A reduced debuginfo level for dev/test builds. Verified: there is no `[profile.dev]`/`[profile.test]` (Cargo.toml profiles: profile, production, p2, small, small-panic, tiny), and debuginfo is 82 % of a blitz-tests binary (`accessibility_roles` 402 MB, 331 MB `.debug_*`; 140 executables > 100 MB in target/debug/deps). [inferred] I1's "link I/O-bound" PSI reading ("io full avg60≈48 % with 32 rust-lld at 4–6 % CPU", inputs#I1) is overseer-measured on a past cold run and not reproduced at P3. The byte share supports it. Where the change lives (workspace profile vs CI-only env) is a P4 fork.
- I1 fact (4) verified at baseline.md:72-75: 120.26/5.54 s · 486.45/7.41 s · 1632.88/13.08 s (inputs#I1 rounds to 1633).

- I1 hypothesis "a cache on every job plus a reduced debuginfo level are the two largest levers" (inputs#I1). Partly re-derived: the cache is necessary (no build-branch save means every run is cold), and debuginfo is the dominant byte share. "Largest" was not measured against the other two levers research found: the duplicate linux test compile (test-features-default and matrix linux build the workspace twice, ci.yml:56/:221) and the 59 separate test binaries.

- Consolidating the 59 `tests/blitz-tests` test binaries is NOT in scope by default (I1: "a code-structure call for you and the founder, not a directive", inputs#I1). Research shows 59 binaries × ~400 MB of links, so P4 asks it as a fork.
- The founder's stated concern frames the chunk's success: CI must not rebuild everything on every run ("надеюсь ci не будет все это каждый раз пересобирать", inputs#I1).

- "Green" is proven on a real pushed sha. Verified lifecycle: `gate.py run` never fires a history-moving step (gate-contract.md:88-100). A push plus `ci.py conclusion` read is an `operator` leg, driven at the operator pass before `chore({marker}): operator pre-CI commit` (gate-contract.md:76, :293), with its result recorded in `evidence/`.

- [premise-corrected: `just` is absent on the dev host (`command -v just` → absent), and the justfile has no CI-leg recipe] The local-reproduction surface is one script both the workflow steps and the host call (`.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh {leg}`), so "same command" holds by construction with no new tool. A justfile wrapper is optional sugar. No new env var or workspace crate is minted.
- Workflow invariants are pinned by a `unittest` in `.github/scripts/` (`test_ci_workflows.py`), so the existing CI-scripts leg guards the trigger, the cache, the guards and the leg-script wiring.

- **Marker:** 2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-06T12:16Z

Every AccessKit node that stands for a stand element carries that element's stable id, and every interactive control on the stand carries a role and a non-empty accessible name. intent §Findings 1 asks for "the same id in the snapshot, the accessibility tree and the driver". This chunk builds the accessibility-tree leg; the snapshot (Epoch 3) and the driver (Epoch 4) do not exist yet.

The id keeps one source, `DioxusDocument::element_id` / `element_ids` (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge; security-plan §Input Validation `id` row). It reaches the tree through a new `accessibility`-gated `Document` trait method. The method's default builds the tree exactly as `BaseDocument::build_accessibility_tree` does today. `DioxusDocument` overrides it to set AccessKit's `author_id` on each element node from `element_ids()`. The shell builds its platform tree through the trait method rather than from the inner `BaseDocument`. So the windowed app, the harness and any test all see the same carried id. Nothing is written into the DOM or the vdom, and the AccessKit `NodeId` keying stays `NodeId::as_u64()` (per architecture §Established Decisions → [Node identity]; a11y-plan §1 · §3).

The engine also gains two accessible-name sources: `aria-label` (accname-1.2 step 2C) and `<label>` association (HTML-AAM: a `for`-target or nested input labelled by its label). This was leaned by the operator at P4, 2026-10-06. The stand's six nameless inputs are named with attributes only: `for` on the four existing visible labels and `aria-label` on the two unlabelled flight-booker inputs. No element, class, style or order changes (per layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens; a11y-plan §2 → Role derivation, §4 · §5).

1. **Trait method.** In `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs`, add to `trait Document` a defaulted method `accessibility_tree(&self) -> accesskit::TreeUpdate`, under `#[cfg(feature = "accessibility")]`. Its default body returns `self.inner().build_accessibility_tree()`, and its rustdoc says that a wrapper may override it to enrich nodes, as `DioxusDocument` does with stable ids. The inherent `BaseDocument::build_accessibility_tree` keeps its name and signature, so its 10 callers are unchanged (research.md §Graph impact). No implementor other than `DioxusDocument` overrides it.

2. **Name sources in the tree build.** In `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs`, `build_accessibility_node`:
   - for an element whose `aria-label` attribute, trimmed, is non-empty, call `set_label` with the attribute value, citing accname-1.2 §2C in a comment;
   - after the visit, for every built `<label>` node, resolve `label_bound_input_element` (document.rs:627-660). When the bound input has a built node, `push_labelled_by` the label's AccessKit `NodeId` onto that input's node, citing HTML-AAM's input accessible-name computation. The pass runs after all nodes are built, because a label may precede or follow its input.
   - Nothing else about roles, `hidden`, `TextRun` or keying changes.

3. **Stable ids on the Dioxus tree.** In `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs`, implement `accessibility_tree` for `DioxusDocument` under `#[cfg(feature = "accessibility")]`:
   - build the base tree through `self.inner.borrow().build_accessibility_tree()`;
   - build a map from `element_ids()` keyed by `NodeId::as_u64()`;
   - for each `(accesskit::NodeId(raw), node)` in `tree.nodes` whose `raw` is in the map, call `set_author_id(id)`.
   - Nodes with no element id get no author id: `TextRun`s, the document root and the synthetic `Window` (`u64::MAX`).
   - The method never indexes the slab with a tree id.
   - In `packages/dioxus-native-dom/Cargo.toml`, add `accesskit = { workspace = true, optional = true }` and make `accessibility = ["blitz-dom/accessibility", "dep:accesskit"]`, following blitz-shell/Cargo.toml:15-17, 37. The only `Cargo.lock` change is `"accesskit"` added to dioxus-native-dom's dependency list.

4. **Shell builds through the document.**
   - In `packages/blitz-shell/src/accessibility.rs`, change `AccessibilityState::update_tree` to take `doc: &dyn Document` (blitz-dom's trait) and build with `doc.accessibility_tree()`.
   - In `packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs`, its two callers `View::poll` (379) and `View::build_accessibility_tree` (523) pass `&*self.doc`. `poll` keeps its `has_changes()` guard, read through `self.doc.inner()` and dropped before the build.
   - `application.rs:82` is unchanged.

5. **Stand names, attributes only.**
   - `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs`: `for: "timer-duration"` on `label.timer-label`.
   - `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs`: `for: "crud-filter"` / `"crud-name"` / `"crud-surname"` on the three existing labels.
   - `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/flight_booker.rs`: `aria-label` on `#flight-start` ("Departure date") and `#flight-return-date` ("Return date").
   - Use Dioxus's attribute spellings, `r#for` and `aria_label` (implement confirms each renders as the HTML attribute named here).
   - No other line of those files changes, and counter.rs, app.rs and stand.rs are untouched.

6. **Measure the pre-change Tab order.** Before step 5's edits land, boot each lean task on the untouched markup. Collect the focus sequence as element ids: `focus_next_node` from the root element (document.rs:606-609, 1634-1639), each focused node read through `element_id`, until it returns `None` or repeats. Record each task's list in `chunks/2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity/evidence/tab-order-base.md`. Step 8 pins those lists.

7. **Engine name check**, new file `tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_names.rs`. It opens with a `//!` doc, builds HTML documents through `Harness::from_html`, resolves them, and reads `build_accessibility_tree()` in the `accessibility_roles.rs` style. Five tests:
   - `aria_label_names_a_control`: an `<input aria-label="X">` node's `label()` reads `X`.
   - `empty_aria_label_is_ignored`: a whitespace-only `aria-label` sets no label.
   - `label_for_names_its_input`: `<label for="a">A</label><input id="a">` makes the input's `labelled_by` contain the label's node, and the label's `labelled_by` holds a `TextRun` whose value is `A`.
   - `nested_label_names_its_input`: the same result for `<label>A <input></label>`.
   - `plain_html_tree_carries_no_author_id`: through `Document::accessibility_tree`, the HTML document's tree is node-for-node equal to `build_accessibility_tree()`, and no node has an `author_id`.

8. **Stand identity check**, new file `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_accessibility_ids.rs`. It opens with a `//!` doc, boots each `LeanTask` through `stand::boot` / `boot_timer` with `stand::options(incremental)`, uses `for incremental in [false, true]`, and uses `#[track_caller]` helpers. A helper `name(tree, node)` reads `label()` when non-empty, else the joined names of its `labelled_by` nodes, where a `TextRun`'s name is its value. Five tests:
   - `element_nodes_carry_their_stable_id`: every tree node whose `NodeId` raw value is in `element_ids()` has `author_id` equal to that id, and every other node has none. The carried ids are pairwise distinct. Their count is non-zero, and it includes `back-btn` plus every control id of the task (research.md §Patterns detected table).
   - `non_elements_carry_no_id`: every `TextRun` node, the `NodeId(u64::MAX)` window and the document-root node carry no `author_id`.
   - `controls_carry_role_and_name`: each of the 15 controls, found by `author_id`, has its expected role (Button · TextInput · Slider, per research's table; never `Unknown`) and a non-empty `name`. The six inputs read "Departure date", "Return date", "Duration:", "Filter prefix:", "Name:" and "Surname:" after trimming.
   - `ids_hold_after_a_rerender`: after a counter click and after a CRUD Create then a Delete, each via harness input helpers that pump, a rebuilt tree again satisfies the first test's equality. The created row's carried id is `TaskShell/Crud/div:0/div:1/div:0/div[3]`. A row's dropped pre-delete `NodeId` raw value appears in no node, and no build panics.
   - `tab_order_is_unchanged`: each task's focus sequence, collected as in step 6, equals the list recorded in `evidence/tab-order-base.md`.
9. **Gates.** Run the `## Test Commands` entries in order and record the workspace and stand counts they print.
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_names.rs` — the engine's `aria-label` and `<label>` name sources, plus the default-path no-author-id proof (step 7)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_accessibility_ids.rs` — the stand accessibility-identity, role/name and Tab-order checks (step 8)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` — the defaulted, gated `Document::accessibility_tree` (step 1)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs` — `aria-label` → `label`; label → input `labelled_by` (step 2)
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs` — the `author_id` override (step 3)
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/Cargo.toml` — the optional accesskit dependency behind `accessibility` (step 3)
- `Cargo.lock` — `"accesskit"` in dioxus-native-dom's dependency list, and nothing else (step 3)
- `packages/blitz-shell/src/accessibility.rs` — `update_tree(&dyn Document)` (step 4)
- `packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs` — the two `update_tree` callers at 379 and 523 (step 4)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs` — `for` on the duration label (step 5)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs` — `for` on the three labels (step 5)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/flight_booker.rs` — `aria-label` on the two date inputs (step 5)

No live leg runs this chunk. The agent-run entries drive the in-process stand through `scripts/agent-run.sh`, and no external process is started, so there is no liveness probe and no `stop`. There is no headful self-verify, because the stand is headless (`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`). There is no `smoke` entry: test-plan declares no boot-smoke trigger list, the stand boot (`stand.rs`, `app.rs`) is untouched as the diff guard checks, and every stand check boots it. The one windowed-runtime file this chunk touches, `packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs` (step 4's two `update_tree` callers), has no headless boot. Its gates are the workspace compile, clippy and tests in `ci-leg.sh fast`, and its real boot (`just seven_guis`, the windowed app building its tree through `Document::accessibility_tree`) is /implement P3's smoke, not a gate here.

`evidence/tab-order-base.md` has no listed producer, by construction. It is step 6's ONE-SHOT measurement on the base markup at implement, before step 5 lands, and its reading is recorded there. Once step 5 lands, the base markup no longer exists in the tree, so no re-runnable entry can produce it. The listed non-mutating guard that re-runs is `--test stand_accessibility_ids`, whose `tab_order_is_unchanged` pins the recorded lists.

body: - (arch) On each lean task, in both layout modes, every AccessKit node whose `NodeId` is an element's carries `author_id` equal to `DioxusDocument::element_id(node_id)`. The carried ids are pairwise distinct, and nodes stay keyed by `NodeId::as_u64()`. Proved by `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_accessibility_ids` (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge / → Mutation, query and CSSOM).

- (arch) blitz-dom gains no dependency on any dioxus crate. A non-Dioxus document's tree through `Document::accessibility_tree` equals `build_accessibility_tree()` node for node and carries no author id (`--test accessibility_names`). No new crate, env var or port is added (the root-manifest diff guard) (per architecture §Design Philosophy → Embedder services are injected; §Occupied Resources).

- (arch) `cargo build -p blitz-dom --no-default-features --locked && cargo build -p dioxus-native-dom --no-default-features --locked` exits 0, and `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` passes (per architecture §Established Decisions → [Default features]; §Conventions → Formatting and lints).

- (a11y) Each of the 15 stand controls (`back-btn`; `counter-increment`; `flight-one-way`, `flight-return`, `flight-start`, `flight-return-date`, `flight-book`; `timer-duration`, `timer-reset`; `crud-filter`, `crud-name`, `crud-surname`, `crud-create`, `crud-update`, `crud-delete`) has its HTML-AAM role (never `Role::Unknown`) and a non-empty accessible name, in both layout modes (per a11y-plan §4 → Per-component pattern catalog; §2 → Role derivation).
- (a11y) No `TextRun`, no document root and no `Window` (`u64::MAX`) node carries a stable id (per a11y-plan §7 → Accessibility tree output; security-plan §Error Handling → Graceful degradation).

- **Forks ruled at P4** (one AskUserQuestion round, all three under the playbook's "Boundary widening" pattern,
  `.andromeda/playbook.md:35-38`, `verdict: escalate`). The answers came from the overseer under the founder's standing
  delegation. All three widenings are PROVISIONAL and listed for the founder's review (FOR DISCUSSION 7):
  1. agent client = Claude Code `claude -p` on the operator's own claude.ai login. No API key, and escher reads no secret.
  2. stub = a stdlib-only python MCP server over stdio, with no port.
  3. the live run happens on the operator host only, ONCE, with its token usage recorded. No CI secret and no recurring

Build the Foundation reachability pipe for the cold-agent gate (route 1A tree, `1a-tree.md:8`; `[GATE_REACHABILITY]`).
One command starts a fresh, isolated agent session whose only tools are a stub's. It gives the session a small task,
captures the whole session as a transcript, counts the session's wrong calls from the stub's own log and cross-checks
them against the transcript, and writes a machine-readable verdict. The pipe is proven twice:

- by contract tests that replace the agent client with a scripted shim, so no live model is involved
  (test-plan §4 shim pattern);

- by ONE live run on this host whose passing verdict, transcript and token usage are committed as evidence
  (test-plan §3 Proof).

The Epoch 6 "Cold-agent test" (v010-15) will drive the real driver and a stand task through this same pipe. So the
client invocation, isolation check, transcript capture, wrong-call count and verdict are built as reusable plumbing.
The stub tool and its task are the swappable parts. This chunk claims no capability: v010-15 needs the real tool and a
stand task (`matrix.py show --id v010-15`).

The pipe follows the stand test contract's grammar, which arch §Standard Contracts → CI contracts and test-plan §3
spell out:
- one verb script with python3-encoded JSON lines on stdout;
- exits 0/1/2/3, with usage checked before any precondition;
- state confined to its own `target/` directory, disjoint from `target/agent-run/`;
- a no-logic `.ps1` pass-through.

Two isolation rules follow from research. Isolation is checked in every run, never assumed. And the session runs from a
working directory whose path does not name the project, because research probe 1 showed the cwd path reaching the
session (research.md §Live probe; scope.md premise correction).

1. **The stub tool — `scripts/cold_agent_stub.py`.** A python3 stdlib-only MCP server speaking newline-delimited
   JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout. It opens with a module docstring stating what it is (arch §Conventions →
   Documentation).
   - **Protocol.** It answers `initialize` with its protocol version, `capabilities.tools` and `serverInfo` name
     `stub`. It accepts `notifications/initialized`. `tools/list` returns exactly three tools, `list`, `read` and
     `press`, each with an `inputSchema`. `tools/call` dispatches them. Any other method gets a JSON-RPC error. Nothing
     but protocol frames goes to stdout; any diagnostic goes to stderr.
   - **Model.** A toy counter held in memory: a display `count` (starts at 0), buttons `inc`, `dec` and `reset`. `dec`
     is disabled while the count is 0.
     - `list` takes no arguments and returns every element as id · role · enabled.
     - `read {id}` returns the display's number, or a button's label and enabled state.
     - `press {id}` acts on an enabled button.
   - **Refusals.** Each is a tool result with `isError: true` and a cause token as the first word, and none changes
     state:
     - `not-found`: the id is unknown;
     - `disabled`: the button is disabled;
     - `not-pressable`: `press` on the display;
     - `malformed`: a missing, extra or non-string argument.
   - **Call log.** Every `tools/call` appends one JSON line to the call-log file named by `--calls`: seq · tool · ok |
     refused · cause. It never records the argument values. After every call the stub rewrites the state file named by
     `--state` with the current count. Both paths come from argv; the stub reads no env var.

2. **The pipe — `scripts/cold-agent.sh`.** A bash script with the agent-run layout: a `VERBS` array, `usage()` to
   stderr exiting 2, and an embedded python3 program in a quoted heredoc that does every JSON read and write. Verbs:
   - `run <task>`: the only task is `counter`, checked against an allowlist before anything else.
   - `status`, `logs` and `cleanup`: each takes no argument.
   State lives in `STATE_DIR=target/cold-agent` only. Run it from the repository root.
   - `run counter`, in order:
     1. **Usage** (exit 2): a bad verb, a wrong argument count, or a task outside the allowlist.
     2. **Preconditions** (exit 3, with a stderr message): `claude` and `python3` on PATH.
     3. Recreate `target/cold-agent/` (`rm -rf` then `mkdir`).
     4. Make a per-run session directory with `mktemp -d`. Copy the stub into it and write the MCP config JSON there:
        one server, `stub`, whose command runs `python3` on the copied stub with `--state` and `--calls` pointing
        into the session directory.
     5. Emit `run.start` (task, ts).
     6. Run the client from the session directory, with stdout to `target/cold-agent/transcript.jsonl` and stderr to
        `target/cold-agent/client.log`:
        `claude -p "{the counter task prompt}" --output-format stream-json --verbose --tools "" --strict-mcp-config
        --mcp-config {session dir}/mcp.json --allowedTools mcp__stub --setting-sources "" --disable-slash-commands
        --no-session-persistence --max-budget-usd 1`.
        Bound the client with `timeout 600`. A timeout or any non-zero client exit becomes a `failed` outcome with
        exit 1, never a propagated 124.
     7. Copy the stub's call log and state into `target/cold-agent/` as `calls.jsonl` and `stub-state.json`. Remove the
        session directory.
     8. Compute the verdict (step 3) and write `target/cold-agent/verdict.json`.
     9. Emit `run.end` carrying the verdict's fields. Exit 0 on `passed`, 1 on `failed`.
   - **The task prompt.** It names only the goal: operate the counter through your tools until its display reads 3,
     then reply with the display's final reading. It names no element id, so the session must discover the ids
     through `list`.
   - `status`: prints the last verdict as one `status` event. Exit 0 when a verdict exists, 3 when none does.
   - `logs`: prints `target/cold-agent/events.jsonl`. Exit 3 when it is absent.
   - `cleanup`: `rm -rf target/cold-agent`, emits `cleanup`, exits 0, and is idempotent. It touches nothing else under
     `target/`. `target/agent-run/` and `target/ci-logs/` survive it.
   - Every event is printed and appended to `target/cold-agent/events.jsonl`, except `status` and `cleanup`, which are
     printed only (as in agent-run).
   - No event, and no verdict field, takes a scrub-set name (`url href src html text value attrs path request error
     panic.payload`, test_agent_run.py:15 plus obs-plan §8).
   - No transcript text, tool argument, tool result or the session's final reply is ever copied into an event or the
     verdict.

3. **The verdict** (computed by the embedded python from `transcript.jsonl`, `calls.jsonl` and `stub-state.json`;
   field names fixed here):
   - **`isolated`** is true only when all of the following hold in the transcript's `system/init` event:
     - `tools` is exactly the stub's three tools, `mcp__stub__list`, `mcp__stub__read` and `mcp__stub__press`, in any
       order;
     - `mcp_servers` is exactly one server named `stub`, with status `connected`;
     - `skills` and `slash_commands` are empty;
     - `apiKeySource` is `none`;
     - neither `cwd` nor any `memory_paths` value contains the repository root's directory name, compared
       case-insensitively. That name is `basename` of `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, falling back to the basename of
       the root the script runs from.
     `session_tools` (the init tool list) and `client_version` (`claude_code_version`) and `model` are recorded beside
     it.
   - **`tool_calls`** is the number of `tool_use` blocks in `assistant` events.
   - **`wrong_calls`** is the stub call log's `refused` count, plus the transcript's `tool_use` blocks naming a tool
     outside `mcp__stub__*`, plus the `result` event's `permission_denials` entries.
   - **`transcript_errors`** is the transcript's `tool_result` blocks with `is_error: true`.
   - **`counts_agree`**: the `tool_result` errors on stub tool_use ids equal the stub log's `refused` count, and the
     transcript's stub `tool_use` count equals the stub log's call count. A disagreement means a call the stub never
     saw, such as a client-side denial.
   - **`final_count`** is read from `stub-state.json`. It is the stub's state, never the agent's reply.
   - **Usage** comes from the `result` event: `num_turns`, `duration_ms`, `cost_usd` (from `total_cost_usd`),
     `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.
   - **`transcript_file`** is `target/cold-agent/transcript.jsonl`.
   - **`outcome`** is `passed` only on positive evidence: the client exited 0, the `result` event has `subtype`
     `success` and `is_error` false, `isolated`, `counts_agree`, `tool_calls` ≥ 1, and `final_count` == 3. Anything
     else is `failed`, with `reasons` listing each failed condition by a fixed token (`client-exit`, `no-result`,
     `not-isolated`, `counts-disagree`, `no-tool-call`, `task-unmet`).
     - A missing or unparsable transcript reads `failed` (`no-result`), never passed.
     - `wrong_calls` does not decide the outcome. It is a count the gate records (v010-15 "wrong calls counted").

4. **`scripts/cold-agent.ps1`** — a 4-line pass-through, the `scripts/agent-run.ps1` shape (comment lines, then
   `& bash "$PSScriptRoot/cold-agent.sh" @args` and `exit $LASTEXITCODE`). It holds no logic.

6. **The one live run — operator host, ONCE** (the `leg = 'operator'` entry in Test Commands, fired once by /implement
   and never re-run by the wrap). After `bash scripts/cold-agent.sh run counter` reads `passed`:
   - copy `target/cold-agent/{verdict.json,transcript.jsonl,calls.jsonl,events.jsonl}` into this chunk's `evidence/`
     as `live-verdict.json`, `live-transcript.jsonl`, `live-calls.jsonl` and `live-events.jsonl`;
   - record in `evidence/live-run.md` the command, exit, outcome, `wrong_calls`, `tool_calls`, the usage numbers
     (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, the two cache counts, `cost_usd`), `client_version`, `model` and wall-clock.
   The founder's budget ruling is that the run happens once and its token cost is recorded from the session's own
   usage report. A red live run is a finding, read from its own transcript. It is fixed and re-run only on the
   operator's word, never looped.
- `scripts/cold_agent_stub.py` — the stub MCP stdio server (step 1)
- `scripts/cold-agent.sh` — the pipe (steps 2–3)
- `scripts/cold-agent.ps1` — the Windows pass-through (step 4)
- `.github/scripts/test_cold_agent.py` — the contract tests (step 5)
- `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-cold-agent-run-pipe/evidence/` — the live run's record (step 6)

- none — `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}`, `test_agent_run.py`, `ci-leg.sh`, `ci.yml`, `Cargo.*` and every Rust crate stay

- (tests) The stub and the pipe pass their contract tests with no live model and no credential:
  `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -p 'test_cold_agent.py' -v` reads OK, and the cases cover pass,
  counted wrong calls, task unmet, empty session, isolation breach, client failure, usage (2) and precondition (3)
  (per test-plan §4 Agent-run contract; test-plan §3 `run` "an empty run is never a pass").

- (tests) The agent-run contract is untouched: `test_agent_run.py` still runs 14 tests OK, and the `git diff --quiet`
  guard from `d73df1a4` reads clean (per test-plan §3 Agent-run contract; arch §Standard Contracts → CI contracts).

- (tests) One live run of `bash scripts/cold-agent.sh run counter` on the operator host reads `passed`, with
  `isolated` true, `counts_agree` true and `final_count` 3. Its verdict, transcript, call log and events are committed
  under `evidence/`, and `evidence/live-run.md` records wrong calls and token usage (input and output tokens, the cache
  counts and cost_usd) from the session's own `result` event (per test-plan §3 Proof; founder budget ruling,
  2026-10-06).

- (security) The pipe and stub read no env var, open no socket and name no API key (census entry). The committed
  evidence holds no key, auth header, credential-file name, token field or e-mail address (evidence census). The
  session reports `apiKeySource` `none` (per security-plan §Secret Management).

- (security) The stub refuses an unknown id, a disabled button, a press on the display and a malformed argument. Each
  refusal names its cause, has no side effect, and is asserted by a contract test (per security-plan §Input Validation,
  the agent-run.sh row as precedent).

- (obs) Every stdout line of every verb, and every `logs` line, parses as one JSON object. No event, and no verdict
  field, carries a scrub-set key or any transcript text, and the shim's marker string never reaches them (per obs-plan
  §3 Agent-run harness log; §8 Scrubbing).

- (obs) Pipe state lives only in `target/cold-agent/` (gitignored). `cleanup` removes only that directory, is
  idempotent, and leaves `target/agent-run/` intact (per obs-plan §9 Telemetry artifact handling).

- (arch) The stub is reached over stdio only, and the session runs from a per-run `mktemp -d` directory that is removed
  after the run and whose path, as the session's own `init` event reports it, does not contain the repo root's name
  (per arch §Occupied Resources → Network ports and listeners; scope.md premise correction).

- (layouts) A malformed invocation prints usage to stderr, nothing to stdout, and exits 2. The usage line follows the
  `<script> <verb> [selection]` shape (per layout-templates §Surface: cli §Primary screens).

- (ci) The pushed sha's CI run reads `verdict: green`, and its `ci-scripts` job runs `test_cold_agent.py` on the
  runner (per test-plan §9; arch §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD).

- No matrix capability is claimed. v010-15 stays pooled for Epoch 6, which drives the real tool and a stand task through
  this pipe (`matrix.py show --id v010-15`).

- Spec anchors (from the extracts):
  - arch: §Occupied Resources (Network ports and listeners · Environment variables · Outbound hosts · Filesystem ·
    Names · Process-wide state), §Standard Contracts → CI contracts, §Conventions → Documentation / Tests,
    §Inherited Defaults → API style.
  - security-plan: §Secret Management, §Input Validation (CLI arguments (agent-run.sh)), §Logging & Monitoring,
    §Dependency Security.
  - test-plan: §3 Agent-run contract (Exit grammar · Events · State · `run` · Invocation · Proof), §4, §8, §9.
  - obs-plan: §3, §6, §8, §9.
  - layout-templates: §Surface: cli §Primary screens.

- Research inspected: `scripts/agent-run.sh`, `scripts/agent-run.ps1`, `.github/scripts/test_agent_run.py`,
  `.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py:151`, `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`, `.claude/rules/testing.md`,
  `.andromeda/playbook.md:35-38`, `claude --help` (2.1.288), research probe 1 (`system/init` + `result` fields).

- Graph impact: the chunk changes no existing symbol. `boot` @ `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs` has 11 callers, all
  stand checks (trace `tree-query-2026-10-06-cold-agent-run-pipe.json`), and stays untouched because the stub task
  does not use the stand.

- `claude --bare` — rejected: it authenticates only by `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` (`claude --help`), and the host has an OAuth login with no key. Adding one is a credential path the operator ruled out at P4.
- A direct Messages-API driver loop — rejected at P4: it needs an API key and puts egress code in escher's own scripts.

- A stub CLI behind a Bash allowlist — rejected at P4: the session would hold a shell tool, which is not "only the
  tool".

- A fork-CI live job — rejected at P4: it would need the fork's first secret, against the `test_ci_workflows.py:151`
  pin, and an API key. CI runs only the shim tests.

- A new `agent-run.sh` verb — rejected: it would change the measured 14-test contract. arch §Standard Contracts → CI
  contracts says a separate script following the same grammar leaves that contract unchanged.

- An MCP SDK or any new dependency — rejected: the stub is stdlib python, and nothing enters `Cargo.lock` or a
  requirements file.

- Do not run the live session from the repository, the session scratchpad or any path naming the project: probe 1
  showed the cwd path reaching the session (research.md §Live probe).
- Do not take the outcome from the agent's reply: `final_count` is the stub's own state.

- Do not loop the live run. Once is the founder's budget. A red is read from its transcript and re-run only on the
  operator's word.

- Do not print the transcript, tool arguments, tool results or the final reply to stdout or into any event. The
  verdict carries counts and identities only.

- `--allowedTools mcp__stub` (server-wide allow) is the intended permission for the stub's tools in `-p` mode. It is
  NOT measured: research's probe had no MCP server, and the second probe was denied. If the live run shows the stub's
  calls denied, they surface as `permission_denials` and as `counts-disagree`, so the verdict reads red rather than
  silently green. Read the transcript, fix the flag (for example the per-tool form `mcp__stub__list,mcp__stub__read,
  mcp__stub__press`), and re-run on the operator's word.

- Whether the probe-1 "escher: YES" came only from the cwd is unmeasured. The live run's `isolated` check measures the
  cwd and memory paths structurally from `init`. A `YES` from any other source is not measurable structurally, and the
  live run records `isolated` as the structural claim only.

- The MCP protocol version the stub answers with: echo the client's requested `protocolVersion` from `initialize`. The
  client's version is a host reading (Claude Code 2.1.288, research), recorded in the verdict as `client_version`.

- The `mktemp -d` default template (`tmp.XXXXXXXXXX` under `$TMPDIR` or `/tmp`) names nothing. `TMPDIR` is unset on
  this host (research `echo`). If an operator's `TMPDIR` names the project, the `isolated` check fails the run instead
  of passing it.

Give the snapshot its first text form and a recorded size budget — the second half of intent §Findings 2 and of
v010-04 ("readable whole in one tool result"). `Snapshot::to_text()` turns the model built by
`DioxusDocument::snapshot` into one compact text: one line per node, nested by indent, each line carrying the
node's role, name, id, state and bounds (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge; a11y-plan §7
Accessibility tree output). `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` states the ceiling one screen's text must stay under, anchored to
the agent client's own tool-result limits, and a stand check proves each lean task's screen whole, deterministic
and inside it (per test-plan §3; layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native / Primary screens).

Three decisions shape the chunk, each answered at P4's question round (the operator, 2026-10-06 — authority per
gate-contract.md §Scope, *Whose word*): the form is hand-written indented text, no dependency; the text leaves the
process through nothing but the returned value (asked as the playbook's `Boundary widening` pattern — no exit is
built here; **PROVISIONAL**, so marked by the answerer at the P5 review, 2026-10-06, for the founder's own word in
the Epoch 3 boundary batch — the work proceeds on it); and a file input's value reads the fixed mask, like a
password's (per security-plan §Input Validation; §Data Protection). The format and the mask stand as recorded.

v010-04 is advanced, not claimed (the operator, 2026-10-06, P5 review): its acceptance says "one snapshot
command", and an in-process call is not a command an agent can run — the first real one is the Driver CLI's. This
chunk builds and proves the cap's other legs, the text form and the budget. Leaned, per artifact: the serializer lives in a sibling module `snapshot_text.rs` (leaned per
arch-history — the masters cite eight `snapshot.rs` ranges a code insert there would move); "a fresh boot" is a
second boot in the same process (leaned per architecture §Occupied Resources — a re-exec is a third registration);
the budget is 10,000 bytes (leaned per the client's fetched limits, research.md §Scope).

1. **The serializer** — new module `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs`, opening with a `//!` doc.
   It adds one inherent method, `Snapshot::to_text(&self) -> String`, a pure function of the `Snapshot`: no document
   access, no failure path, no panic on any content, no log or print. It walks the roots and their children
   depth-first in the stored order — the order `Snapshot::nodes()` yields — and writes exactly one line per node,
   each ended by `\n`; a snapshot with no roots is the empty string. The line, left to right:
   - indent: two spaces per depth (a root is depth 0);
   - role: the model's `role` in its `Debug` spelling (`Button`, `TextInput`, `GenericContainer`) — no table;
   - one space, then the name as a quoted string: `"`, the name through `str::escape_debug`, `"` — `""` when empty;
   - ` id=` and the id quoted the same way;
   - state, each token preceded by one space, in this fixed order, a token absent when the model holds nothing
     for it: `enabled` / `disabled` for `enabled` `Some(true)` / `Some(false)`; `checked` / `unchecked` for
     `checked` `Some(true)` / `Some(false)`; `value=` and the value quoted the same way for `Some(v)` (so
     `Some("")` writes `value=""`); `focused` when `focused` is true;
   - ` @{x},{y} {width}x{height}`: the four bounds numbers, each written with `f64`'s `Display` (`8`, `12.5`,
     `12.515625`, `-4`).
   Every value comes from the `SnapshotNode` it is given; nothing is read from a control. There is no `Display`
   impl and no second entry point.

2. **The budget** — in the same module, `pub const SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET: usize = 10_000;` with a `///` doc that
   states the unit (bytes of `to_text`'s result) and the rationale: the agent client warns above 10,000 tokens,
   caps a tool result at 25,000 tokens and saves one over 50,000 characters to a file; a text of N bytes holds at
   most N characters and at most N tokens, so a text inside the budget is inside all three whatever the tokenizer.
   `to_text` never truncates or pages — the budget is a ceiling a caller compares against, not a behaviour.
   `to_text`'s own doc states the line grammar and shows a small example in a `text` fence (a synthetic snapshot,
   not compiled as a doc-test).

3. **The crate root** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs`: declare `mod snapshot_text;` under
   `#[cfg(feature = "accessibility")]` directly after `mod snapshot;`, re-export `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` under the
   same gate directly after the `pub use snapshot::…` line, and name the text form in the `accessibility` line of
   the feature-flag doc (:7-9).

4. **The file-input mask** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs`, in `value` (:184-208): an `input` whose
   `type` is `file` (compared ASCII-case-insensitively, as `password` is at :193) is masked exactly as a password
   is — a non-empty value reads `MASKED_VALUE`, an empty or absent one reads as it does today. Reword the two doc
   comments that state the mask (`MASKED_VALUE`, :11-12; `NodeState::value`, :55-57) to name both types. No field
   is added and no type changes.

5. **Unit tests** — one in `snapshot.rs`'s `mod tests`: `a_file_input_reads_a_masked_value` (an input authored
   with `type: "file"` and a synthetic path as `value` reads `Some(MASKED_VALUE)`; the path occurs in no id, name
   or value of any node; a file input with no `value` reads `None`). Seven in `snapshot_text.rs`'s own
   `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, the first six over hand-built `Snapshot` values with inline expected literals:
   `a_node_writes_role_name_id_and_bounds` · `state_tokens_follow_the_model` (each token, the fixed order, and one
   node that is both `disabled` and `focused`) · `children_are_indented_in_pre_order` (two roots, three depths) ·
   `strings_are_quoted_and_escaped` (a quote, a backslash, a line break and a tab in a name, an id and a value stay
   on one line; an id holding `/`, `//`, `:`, `[`, `]` and a space is written whole; `MASKED_VALUE` passes
   unchanged; `Some("")` writes `value=""`) · `bounds_print_the_shortest_decimal` (an integral, a 1/64 multiple, a
   negative) · `an_empty_snapshot_is_the_empty_text` · and `the_text_of_a_document_has_one_line_per_node` (a
   document built with the unit helper of snapshot.rs:216-221, copied into this module: line count equals
   `nodes().count()`, two calls are equal).

6. **The stand check** — new file `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_text.rs`, opening with a `//!` doc,
   booting through `stand::boot(task, stand::options(incremental))` for every `LeanTask::ALL` in both layout
   modes. Six tests:
   - `every_node_is_one_line_with_its_five_fields` — the text has as many lines as the snapshot has nodes; the
     i-th line belongs to the i-th node of `nodes()`: it is indented two spaces per the node's depth, opens with
     the node's role spelling, and holds the node's quoted name, `id=` with its quoted id, and the bounds token
     built from `node.bounds`; every id occurs on exactly one line; each author id `stand_snapshot`'s `rendered`
     list names for the task (stand_snapshot.rs:61-98 — copied into this file, since one test file imports nothing
     from another) is among them, and CRUD's three `crud-person-{0,1,2}` lines sit deeper than, and after,
     `crud-list`'s.
   - `state_reads_as_the_model_holds_it` — at boot no line holds the `focused` token; on the flight booker
     `flight-return-date`'s line holds `disabled`, `flight-start`'s holds `enabled` and `value=` with the fixture's
     date; after `press(Key::Tab)` on a fresh boot exactly one line holds `focused` and it is `back-btn`'s; after a
     click on `counter-increment` the `counter-value` line's name reads `"1"`.
   - `the_text_is_deterministic` — two calls on one document, the two layout modes, and a second boot of the same
     task each give the same text.
   - `every_screen_fits_the_budget` — each screen's byte length is at most its recorded ceiling (an in-file table,
     one entry per lean task) and each ceiling is at most `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET`; CRUD after one click on
     `crud-create` is longer than at boot and still inside the budget. The failure message names the task, the
     mode, the measured length and the ceiling — numbers only.
   - `a_masked_password_stays_masked_in_the_text` — on an in-file fixture (a labelled password input, booted with
     the stand's options) an empty password's line holds `value=""`; after a click and `type_text` of a synthetic
     literal the line holds `value=` with `MASKED_VALUE` quoted, and the literal occurs nowhere in the text.
   - `a_masked_file_input_stays_masked_in_the_text` — on an in-file fixture whose file input is authored with a
     synthetic path as `value`, its line holds the quoted mask and the path occurs nowhere in the text.
   The crossing rule binds this file: the serialized text is bound only to variables whose names start `text`, no
   format string interpolates one, the file uses `assert!` with an authored message throughout and never
   `assert_eq!` / `assert_ne!` (both print their operands), and it prints nothing.

7. **The size record** — before the ceilings are written, run the budget test once with every ceiling at `0` and
   read each screen's length from the failure messages (numbers only); record the readings, per task and mode, in
   `chunks/2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization/evidence/sizes.txt`. Then set each task's ceiling to the
   larger of its two readings rounded down to a multiple of 256, plus 512, and re-run green. The red run is also
   the control that the assertion bites.

8. **Gates** — run the entries of `## Test Commands`; the new test files are seen red before the code lands
   (their baselines are in the fence), and every forecast below is re-counted from the run's own listing.

- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs` — the serializer, the budget constant, seven unit tests (steps

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_text.rs` — the stand check and its two in-file fixtures (steps 6, 7)

- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs` — the file-input mask in `value`, two doc comments, one unit test

  are tests (research.md §Graph impact), and no caller reads a file input's value (`grep -rn 'type: "file"'
  tests/blitz-tests packages/dioxus-native-dom` → 0 hits)

It is the snapshot's FIRST AND ONLY text form. A pure function of the `Snapshot`: no document access, no failure path, no log, no print. It writes one line per node in pre-order (the order of `Snapshot::nodes()`), each ended by `\n`, a child indented two spaces deeper than its parent; a snapshot with no roots is the empty string.   - NEW public constant: `dioxus_native_dom::SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET: usize = 10_000` (`snapshot_text.rs:16`), exported under `accessibility` (`lib.rs:32-33`); `dioxus-native` re-exports the crate whole (`pub use dioxus_native_dom::*`). Rationale stated in its doc: the agent client warns above 10,000 tokens, caps a tool result at 25,000 tokens and saves one over 50,000 characters to a file; N bytes hold at most N characters and at most N tokens. It is a ceiling a caller compares against; `to_text` does not enforce it.
