data.head: ## Graph impact (from the code-graph query; rust plane, trace `tree-query-2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization.json`)

body: - **`snapshot`** (fn, `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs`) — 40 call sites in 4 files, every one a test: `snapshot.rs` 13 (its own unit tests), `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot.rs` 14, `stand_snapshot_state.rs` 11, `dioxus_falsy_boolean_attrs.rs` 2. No library, binary or script calls it. This chunk changes no signature: the serializer is an addition beside it, so the caller set is not a boundary.

- **References from outside `snapshot.rs`** — 27 `snapshot` call sites in 3 files, and field reads of `id` (19) · `state` (15) · `name` (8) · `bounds` (7) · `role` (6) · `value` (5) · `enabled` (5) across the two stand files; `MASKED_VALUE` 3 sites in 2 files. The model's fields are read by tests only; none changes type here.

- **Crate edges** — `dioxus-native-dom` → `blitz-dom`, `blitz-traits`; inbound from `dioxus-native`, `blitz-test-harness`, `blitz-tests`, `seven_guis`, `browser`, `blitz-examples`, `wgpu_texture`. A new public item reaches all seven; an additive one breaks none.

- **Name collisions** — `to_text`, `to_compact`, `snapshot_text`, `SNAPSHOT_BUDGET`, `SIZE_BUDGET`: 0 symbols on the plane (existence query, `kind <> 'meta'`); `serialize` and `render` are taken elsewhere (blitz-dom's `node/serialize.rs` module, blitz-traits `net.rs`, `element_id.rs:385`), so neither is the new item's name.

- **One line per node, indented by depth** (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/inspect.rs:117-131): the harness's `dom_string` already serializes a tree this way, text escaped with `{:?}`. A snapshot text in that shape needs no dependency.

- **String escaping is needed and std supplies it** (snapshot.rs:33, :57; element_id history): an author key is any non-empty `/`-free string, a name is parsed text (trimmed, inner whitespace kept), a `textarea`'s value can hold a line break. `str`'s `Debug` form (`{:?}`) quotes the string and escapes `"`, `\`, line breaks and control characters while leaving printable non-ASCII — the mask's U+2022 included — as is; a quoted field can therefore never read as a second field or line.

- **Role spelling without a second mapping** (accesskit-0.25.0 `src/lib.rs:62`): `Role` offers only `Debug`; writing `{:?}` (`Button`, `TextInput`, `GenericContainer`) is a one-to-one rewrite of the model's value with no table in the serializer. It ties the spelling to the accesskit pin — the same pin the model's `role` field already exposes.

- **The size is small against every limit** (estimate, not a measurement): the lean tasks declare 5 · 11 · 12 · 18 rsx elements (`grep -c -E '^\s*[a-z][a-z0-9]*\s*\{' examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/{counter,flight_booker,timer,crud}.rs`), the shell and skeleton add about eight nodes, and CRUD renders three rows — roughly 13 to 30 nodes a screen. At about 100 bytes a line that is 1.5–3 KB a screen, against 50,000 characters and 10,000 tokens. The real figures are measured by the check, not carried from here.

- **File-input reach** (snapshot.rs:184-208; pointer.rs:768-777): `type="file"` is not among the six excluded input types, so the reader returns the `value` attribute, which the click branch fills with a host path. The feature is off for `cargo test -p blitz-tests` and on under `cargo test --workspace` (`cargo tree --locked --offline --workspace -e features -i blitz-dom` lists `blitz-dom feature "file-input"` under `feature "default" (command-line)`; the `-p blitz-tests` tree has no such line). No headless run yields a path (the default dialog returns no file); an authored `value` on a file input is read as written under either build — the equality a fix is provable on: `input { r#type: "file", value: "/x/y.txt" }` reads `Some("/x/y.txt")` today.

- **Stand checks print nothing** (`grep -n -E 'println!|eprintln!|dbg!' tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_*.rs packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs` → 2 hits, both `stand_id_persistence.rs:315, :318`, the registered re-exec child): a check that prints a serialized screen would be the second exception to obs-plan §3's headless-stand bullet.

- **Assertion messages are an exit** (stand_snapshot.rs:109, snapshot.rs:227): the existing helpers already format ids — and, in the unit helper, a whole `{snapshot:#?}` — into panic messages; a failing `assert_eq!` on two serialized texts prints both into `target/agent-run/run.log` and, in CI, the per-leg failure log artifact.

- **Unit tests inline, at the end of the source file** (snapshot.rs:210-221): `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` with the `build` helper; a sibling module carries its own copy of the helper or builds `Snapshot` values by hand — the serializer is a pure function of a `Snapshot`, so most cases need no document at all.

- **Stand check shape** (stand_snapshot.rs:1-5, :100-110, :156-178): a `//!` doc naming the behaviour, `boot(task, incremental)`, `#[track_caller]` helpers, the fixture's own condition asserted first, both layout modes.
- **Public items documented, constants with their rationale** (snapshot.rs:11-13): `MASKED_VALUE` is the precedent for a public re-exported constant; `ci-leg.sh doc` runs rustdoc `-D warnings`.
- **MSRV 1.91 std only** (Cargo.toml:41): the host compiles on a newer stable; the `msrv` CI leg is outside `ci-leg.sh fast`.
- **No platform-bound key in a stand check** (.claude/rules/testing.md, Session Additions): typed characters and clicks only.
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs` — the serializer, the budget constant and their unit tests
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_text.rs` — the stand check: each lean task's serialized screen, complete, deterministic and under the budget
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs` — the gated module line, the re-export and the feature-flag doc line

- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs` — the value reader masks a file input, the two doc comments that state the mask, one unit test
<!-- The format fork closed on the hand-written text, so no manifest and no lockfile is in the write set (the
JSON-through-serde branch, rejected at P4, would have added three). -->
All three were plan-decision questions and were closed at P4's question round before synthesis (the operator, 2026-10-06):

- Which form does the text take — an indented line per node, or a JSON document? → blocks: plan-decision. **Answered: indented text, hand-written** — one line per node, two-space indent per depth, strings quoted with Rust escaping, no dependency. The Driver CLI, which must print JSON (v010-12), carries the text as a string field or adds a JSON view of the same model at its own chunk.

- Through what may the serialized text leave the process in this chunk? → blocks: plan-decision; asked as the playbook's `Boundary widening` pattern (`verdict: escalate`), never leaned. **Answered: the returned value only** — the stand check asserts on the text and never prints it or embeds it in an assertion message; the budget record is numbers only; the doc example and the unit-test literals use synthetic snapshots. No exit is built here; the driver's entries ask again. Marked PROVISIONAL at the P5 review (2026-10-06) for the founder's Epoch 3 boundary batch; the other two answers stand as recorded.

- What does the snapshot read as a file input's value? → blocks: plan-decision. **Answered: the fixed mask** — a file input holding a non-empty value reads `MASKED_VALUE`, the password rule extended to one more type. Provable without the feature or a file dialog: `type="file"` gets no text editor (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs:451 lists `text | password | email | number | search | tel | url` and no type at all), so an authored `value` reaches the reader through the attribute branch.

**Working entry (verbatim):** Compact snapshot serialization — whole stand screen readable in one tool result, size budget recorded (v010-04)  CARRY: first wire form (from 2026-10-06-snapshot-model) — the snapshot is in-process only today: no serialized form, log or event carries its ids, names or a text control's current text (security-plan §Input Validation, the `id` and accessible-names rows); a serialization that leaves the process is a new crossing for all three — a boundary widening, escalated to the operator at that chunk, with the two rows re-read; a password input's `value` reads the fixed mask `MASKED_VALUE`, never its text or its length (measured at 2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity, `stand_snapshot_state`; security-plan §Input Validation, the password row); hypothesis: a file input's `value` attribute holds the chosen file's host path under the `file-input` feature and the snapshot's value reader reaches it (read from the code at that chunk's phase, pointer.rs:769-777; not measured — blitz-tests does not enable `file-input`)

**Epoch:** Epoch 3 — Observation model, its fifth entry (after Snapshot state fidelity; Change tracking and diff follows) · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Freight on the entry:** one `CARRY:` block (`route.py pins` row 45, 910 chars) — the only block on this line; no `BLOCKED-ON`, `PREREQ` or `WATCH`.

The **serialized form of the snapshot** and its **recorded size budget**: the second half of intent §Findings 2 ("readable whole in one tool result") and of requirements v010-04. The data model (`DioxusDocument::snapshot`, 2026-10-06-snapshot-model) and the truth of its state (2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity) are built; today the snapshot is a Rust value with no text form at all.

- **A compact text form of the whole tree** — one call turns a `Snapshot` into one text that carries every node's id · role · name · state · bounds and the tree's parent/child structure (the entry's title; `matrix.py show --id v010-04`: "every node carries id, role, name, state and bounds").

- **The format** — the entry says "compact" and names no format. Candidates are an indented line-per-node text and a JSON document; which one, and how a node's absent state (`None` for enabled / checked / value, `focused: false`) and its bounds (floats snapped to 1/64 px) are written, is P4's — a contestable fork. Whatever the form, compaction never drops one of the five fields from a node that has it. Verified: no artifact fixes a format — the one in-repo precedent is the harness's one-node-per-line `dom_string` (inspect.rs:117-131), and JSON through serde would need two new manifest edges (research.md §Patterns detected).
- **The whole stand screen in one tool result** — each stand screen serializes whole: no truncation, no paging, no second call (the entry; intent §2).

- **"Stand screen" = the four lean tasks** — counter, flight booker, timer and CRUD, each booted headlessly through `seven_guis::stand` at its pinned viewport, the population `stand_snapshot` and `stand_snapshot_state` already cover (intent §Principles, "The stand is the proof"). Verified: `LeanTask::ALL` is those four (stand.rs:24-29) and `stand_snapshot` iterates it in both layout modes (stand_snapshot.rs:158-159). A screen is the whole document — the `html` root, the shell and the task body, nodes scrolled out of view included, since the snapshot keeps every element the accessibility tree keeps (snapshot.rs:112-158).

- **A size budget, recorded** — a stated ceiling for one serialized screen, written where a later check and the driver's command schema can read it, with each stand screen's measured size recorded against it and asserted under it by a stand check (the entry: "size budget recorded").

- **What the budget is anchored to** — "one tool result" is a property of the agent client, not of this repository, and the budget records both the limit it rests on and the headroom the stand screens leave. `[premise-corrected: the client states three limits, not one cap — Claude Code warns when an MCP tool's output exceeds 10,000 tokens, its default maximum is 25,000 tokens, and a result longer than 50,000 characters, or over the token maximum, is saved to a file and replaced in the conversation by a path (code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp, fetched 2026-10-06; the host's client reads 2.1.289). The units are tokens and characters; a Rust check can count bytes and characters, never tokens, so the ceiling is stated in bytes with its conversion written beside it (research.md §Scope, Platform issues consulted)]`

- **Deterministic** — the same screen serializes to the same bytes: across two calls, across `incremental in [false, true]` (CLAUDE.md invariant: the two layout modes stay identical) and across a fresh boot. Verified for the model: `stand_snapshot::snapshot_is_deterministic` proves two reads and the two layout modes equal as `Snapshot` values (stand_snapshot.rs:393-408), so a serializer that is a pure function of the `Snapshot`, walking `Snapshot::nodes()`' pre-order with one fixed number rule, inherits it. `[premise-corrected: "a fresh boot" is a second boot in the same process — a fresh-process proof would re-execute the test binary, a third registration under arch §Occupied Resources and one more ignored test (stand_id_persistence is the only mechanism); and byte equality is claimed on one platform at a time — no check proves a stand screen's bounds equal across the linux, windows and macos legs, so no expected text carries a stand screen's bounds as a literal]`

- **Entry point** — an in-process Rust API beside the model in dioxus-native-dom, under its `accessibility` feature like the model itself. The "one snapshot command" of v010-04's acceptance is, in this chunk, that API driven by a stand check; the driver, CLI and MCP command that expose it are Epoch 4–5. Verified: the `snapshot` module and its re-export are both `#[cfg(feature = "accessibility")]` (lib.rs:20-21, :28-29), and blitz-tests names `dioxus-native-dom/accessibility` (tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml:21).

- **CARRY, folded (first wire form — from 2026-10-06-snapshot-model).** Coordinates re-verified against the artifacts at take-up:
  - "the snapshot is in-process only today: no serialized form, log or event carries its ids, names or a text control's current text" — security-plan.md:107 (the `id` row: "the snapshot has no wire form, no log, event, socket or file carries it") and :108 (the accessible-names row: "the snapshot has no wire form and reaches no log or event") both read so at HEAD; snapshot.rs has no `Display`, no serde derive and no text-producing function (its outline, 527 lines).
  - "a serialization that leaves the process is a new crossing for all three — a boundary widening, escalated to the operator at that chunk, with the two rows re-read" — **the escalation is this chunk's**: whether, and through what, the serialized text leaves the process here (a returned `String` only · a test's stdout · a committed evidence or budget record carrying stand content) is asked of the operator at P4 as a fork, never leaned, and rows :107 and :108 are re-read for it. The text carries three content classes: ids, accessible names, and a text control's current text (`NodeState::value`).
  - "a password input's `value` reads the fixed mask `MASKED_VALUE`, never its text or its length (measured at 2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity, `stand_snapshot_state`; security-plan §Input Validation, the password row)" — the row is security-plan.md:109; the mask is snapshot.rs:11-13 and :184-208; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_state.rs exists. The serialized form takes its values from the model, so it carries the mask and never a second reading of the control.
  - The file-input hypothesis ("a file input's `value` attribute holds the chosen file's host path under the `file-input` feature and the snapshot's value reader reaches it … not measured — blitz-tests does not enable `file-input`"). `[premise-corrected: re-derived from the code at HEAD, still not measured by a run. The reach holds — the value reader treats `type="file"` as value-bearing (snapshot.rs:184-208 excludes only checkbox, radio, button, submit, reset, hidden), a file input holds no text editor (`text_input_data` answers for `TextInput` data only, element.rs:558-563), so it reads the `value` attribute; and a click on a file input writes the first chosen file's whole path there (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:768-777). Two corrections: (1) the feature is OFF for `cargo test -p blitz-tests` but ON under `cargo test --workspace` — a workspace member enables blitz-dom's defaults and cargo unifies features (`cargo tree --workspace -e features -i blitz-dom` lists `file-input`; the `-p blitz-tests` tree does not) — so the local gate and CI compile the branch in; (2) no headless route produces a path today — the default `ShellProvider::open_file_dialog` returns no file (blitz-traits/src/shell.rs:35-43) and only blitz-shell overrides it — while an authored `value` on a file input is read as written, with or without the feature. So a serialized stand screen carries no host path today; a windowed app's snapshot would, once a driver reads one]` What the snapshot reads for a file input is a P4 question for the operator, beside the crossing.
- In: the serializer and its unit tests; the size budget's record; the stand check that serializes each lean task's screen and asserts completeness, determinism and size.

- In, on the operator's ruling at P4: the snapshot's value reading for a file input. Verified: the reach holds by code (the CARRY bullet above), and the reading is provable without the feature or a file dialog — an authored `value` on a `type="file"` input goes through the same reader.

- Out: change tracking and the diff (v010-06, the next entry) — though the form chosen here is the one a diff will be written in; the driver session, the command and refusal schema, the CLI and the MCP surface (Epoch 4–5); the actionable-key check's wire form (its own CARRY, on Driver CLI); the screenshot.

- Out: parsing the text back into a `Snapshot` — nothing in 0.1.0 reads a serialized snapshot but an agent. Verified: `DioxusDocument::snapshot` is called from tests only — 40 call sites in 4 files, none in a library, a binary or a script (research.md §Graph impact).

- No new workspace crate, port, socket, listener or env var (CLAUDE.md invariant). A new dependency edge is not assumed. Verified: `serde = "1"` is a workspace dependency (Cargo.toml:163) that dioxus-native-dom and blitz-tests do not name; `serde_json` is no workspace dependency — only wpt/runner's own manifest names it (wpt/runner/Cargo.toml:50); accesskit 0.25.0's `Role` derives serde only under its `serde` feature, which the workspace leaves off. - **Marker:** 2026-10-06-headless-stand · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-06T02:07:41Z

The 7GUIs stand boots headless. A check calls one stand function to mount counter, flight booker, timer or CRUD inside
the stand's own `TaskShell` chrome. The boot uses no window and no GPU, one pinned viewport, the stand's bundled DejaVu
Sans and no network, and builds a fresh document per call. The check then drives the task through `blitz-test-harness`'s
input helpers. This is the boot every later 0.1.0 capability is proven on: stable ids, snapshot, settle, driver,
screenshot and the cold-agent test (intent §Principles, "infrastructure ahead of the queue"; arch §Design Philosophy
"Headless, measurable, testable").
Research grounded four design facts (research.md §Patterns detected):
- The stand is offline already, because a document with no net provider falls back to `DummyNetProvider`.
- Host fonts cannot leak once a font context is supplied, because `build_single_font_ctx` turns system fonts off.

- The bundled woff2 decodes only under blitz-dom's `woff` feature, which a package-alone build of the stand or its
  checks leaves off today. That would be the vacuous 0×0 trap the design and test plans warn of.
- The timer ticks on wall-clock time the harness cannot reach.

So this chunk adds a font context and an incremental switch to `HarnessOptions`, turns `woff` on for the stand, and
gives the timer a stand-side tick seam. The windowed app's behaviour stays unchanged.

1. **`HarnessOptions` gains two fields** (`packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs`). The first is `font_ctx:
   Option<FontContext>`, passed into `DocumentConfig.font_ctx` (config.rs:49). `FontContext` comes from blitz-dom's
   re-export. The second is `incremental: Option<bool>`, passed into `DocumentConfig.incremental` (config.rs:61).
   `Default` keeps both `None`, so every existing construction is unchanged: the 3 struct-literal sites
   `dir_attribute.rs:23`, `pointer_events.rs:11` and `touch_events.rs:28` all end in `..Default::default()` (research.md
   §Graph impact, re-derived by `grep -rn "HarnessOptions {" --include=*.rs`). Each new field carries rustdoc (the
   `doc` leg runs `-D warnings`).

2. **Shared task mapping in `app.rs`** (`examples/seven_guis/src/app.rs`). Make the task enum public with the seven
   variants unchanged. Factor the `Some(task) => TaskShell { title, on_back, <Task> {} }` arm of `app()` (app.rs:68-112)
   into one public function or component that renders a given task inside `TaskShell`. `app()` calls it for the
   windowed flow, and the stand root (step 4) calls it headlessly. The rendered element tree, class names, ids, CSS
   constants and the Home → TaskShell flow stay byte-for-byte what `app()` renders today. `TaskShell` itself may stay
   private if the shared function lives in `app.rs`.

3. **Timer tick seam** (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs`). The `Timer` component reads an optional tick source
   from the Dioxus context.
   - **Absent** (the windowed and wasm app): the coroutine is today's loop, `futures_timer::Delay::new(100 ms)` then the
     `+0.1` capped at `duration` arithmetic, unchanged.
   - **Present** (the headless stand): each tick the source delivers runs the same `+0.1`-capped arithmetic once, with
     no `Delay` awaited.
   The tick source type is defined in seven_guis (in `stand.rs` or `timer.rs`) and uses only crates already in
   seven_guis' graph (the dioxus prelude's signals, channels or coroutines). No registry crate is added. The timer's
   markup is unchanged.

4. **Headless stand module** (`examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs`, new, declared `pub mod stand;` in `src/lib.rs`
   behind `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`). It names the stand configuration once and provides:
   - **The lean four**: a public enum of counter, flight booker, timer and CRUD, mapping onto step 2's task enum.
   - **The pinned viewport**: one set of public constants, 800 × 600, hidpi scale 1.0, `ColorScheme::Light`.
   - **The bundled font**: a public function returning `build_single_font_ctx` over `include_bytes!` of
     `assets/DejaVuSans.woff2`. The wasm entry in `lib.rs` shares the same byte constant, with no second `include_bytes!`
     of the file.
   - **The stand's `HarnessOptions`**: a public builder taking an `incremental: bool`. It sets the pinned viewport and
     the bundled font, and leaves `net_provider: None`, which is offline by `DummyNetProvider`. A caller may replace
     fields with `..` to inject a recording net provider.
   - **Boot**: a public boot function per task that builds a fresh `VirtualDom` over a stand root component. The root
     renders step 2's TaskShell mapping for the named task with a no-op back handler, and for the timer it provides the
     tick source from step 3 in context. The function hands that root to `Harness::from_vdom` with the stand's options
     and returns the harness. For the timer it also returns a handle whose method delivers N ticks; the check then
     calls `pump`.
   - Nothing in the module installs telemetry, reads an env var, or touches `blitz_net`.

5. **Manifests**:
   - `examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml`: add `blitz-test-harness = { workspace = true }` under the
     `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]` table, and add `"woff"` to the native `dioxus-native`
     features (`system-fonts` → `system-fonts`, `woff`). The woff2 then decodes in every build that includes the stand
     (research.md §Patterns detected, "Bundled font only under woff").
   - Root `Cargo.toml`: add `seven_guis = { path = "./examples/seven_guis" }` to `[workspace.dependencies]`. It keeps
     default features, because `dioxus-native` refuses to compile with no renderer (`dioxus_renderer.rs:27`).
   - `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml`: add `seven_guis = { workspace = true }` to `[dev-dependencies]`.
   - `Cargo.lock` updates its dependency lists only. No new package stanza appears: `wuff` is already locked, and both
     added edges are path crates already in the lock.

6. **Proof checks** (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_*.rs`, one file per behaviour, each opening with a `//!` doc, in
   snake_case behaviour names with `#[track_caller]` helpers; `.claude/rules/testing.md`). Each check builds its own
   harness with the stand boot, asserts the fixture first, and asserts unconditionally: no font-skip early return, no
   `if` on measured size, no sleep, no `dispatch_recorded`.
   - `stand_boot.rs`:
     - For each of the four tasks, the document holds `main#main > #task-shell`, with `#task-header` holding
       `#back-btn` and `#task-title` (text = the task's title) before `#task-body`.
     - `#task-title`'s layout rect has width > 0 and height > 0 under the bundled font.
     - For each task, two fresh boots give equal `dom_string()` (the geometry-bearing serialization).
     - Boots with `incremental` false and true give equal `dom_string()`.
     - A boot with a file-local recording `NetProvider` injected into the stand's options records zero requests across
       boot plus one click.
   - `stand_counter.rs`: `.counter-display` reads `0`; `click(".counter-btn")` → `1`.
   - `stand_flight_booker.rs`: initially `.flight-btn` carries no `disabled` attribute and the first `.date-input` class
     has no `invalid`. Click that input and `type_text` a character that breaks `dd.mm.yyyy`. Its `class` then contains
     `invalid` and `.flight-btn` carries `disabled`. The check asserts no colour.
   - `stand_timer.rs`:
     - Initially `.timer-elapsed` reads `Elapsed: 0.0s`.
     - Deliver 3 ticks and pump: `Elapsed: 0.3s`, and `.progress-fill`'s `style` reads `width: 2.0%;` (0.3 / 15 s ×
       100).
     - Click `.timer-reset-btn`: `Elapsed: 0.0s`.
     - Ticks past `duration` cap at it: the duration is unchanged at 15, and 151 ticks read `Elapsed: 15.0s`.
   - `stand_crud.rs`:
     - Initially the list's item count is read.
     - Click the first field input and `type_text` a name, then the second and type a surname, then click the create
       button. The list gains exactly one item whose text contains both strings.
     - The update and delete buttons carry `disabled` before a selection.
- `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs` — headless stand: lean-four enum, pinned viewport, bundled font, stand `HarnessOptions`, boot functions, timer tick handle
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_boot.rs` — TaskShell mount, bundled-font non-zero text, two-boot and two-mode `dom_string` identity, zero net requests
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_counter.rs` — counter proof check
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_flight_booker.rs` — flight-booker invalid-date proof check
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_timer.rs` — timer tick-seam proof check
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_crud.rs` — CRUD create proof check
- `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs` — `HarnessOptions.font_ctx` + `.incremental`, threaded into `into_config`
- `examples/seven_guis/src/app.rs` — public task enum + shared TaskShell mapping; windowed tree unchanged (`app` called only from `main.rs:8` and the wasm entry — research.md §Graph impact)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/lib.rs` — `pub mod stand` (native only); shared DejaVu byte constant
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs` — optional context tick source; default path unchanged
- `examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml` — native `blitz-test-harness` dependency; native `dioxus-native` feature `woff`
- `Cargo.toml` — `seven_guis` in `[workspace.dependencies]`
- `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml` — `seven_guis` dev-dependency
- `Cargo.lock` — dependency lists of blitz-tests and seven_guis
The gates below run in /implement P2 and the wrap's light gate.

- The first entry is the chunk's witness. It builds `-p blitz-tests` alone, without the workspace's feature unification,
  so it proves the bundled woff2 decodes in the stand's own build and not only when `blitz` happens to turn `woff` on.

- The census probes keep network, env and telemetry calls out of the stand, keep sleeps and recorded dispatch out of the
  checks, keep `Cargo.lock` free of new packages, and keep the windowed `main.rs` untouched. Their base is `d57a6c69`,

- The boot smoke runs the windowed stand. `app.rs`, `lib.rs` and `timer.rs` change what `seven_guis_native` launches,

The stand gets a headless boot: a check can mount any of the four lean 7GUIs tasks (counter, flight booker, timer, CRUD; intent §Principles "the stand is the proof") inside the stand's own `TaskShell` chrome with no window and no GPU. It can then pump, read and drive the task through `blitz-test-harness`. intent §Principles places this right after "the as-built baseline green on this host and the fork's CI reached": every later capability (stable ids, snapshot, driver, screenshot, cold-agent test) is proven on this boot, so it is the abstraction they rest on.

- **Headless mount in TaskShell** — each of the four tasks can be built headlessly wrapped in the same `TaskShell` (header, back button, title, body) the windowed app shows. A check sees the real stand chrome, not a bare task component. Verified (research.md §Files inspected: `app.rs:6`, `:68`, `:146`): `app()` always starts on `Home`, and `TaskShell` and the `Task` enum are private to `app.rs`. An entry point that starts on a named task is needed, and the windowed app must render the same tree it does today. `app` has no caller beyond `main.rs` and the wasm entry (research.md §Graph impact).
- **No display** — the boot runs through `Harness` (`DioxusDocument`, no winit, no renderer, no `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`), so it runs on the CI runner and in an agent's shell.

- **Fixed viewport** — every check boots at one pinned viewport size, scale and colour scheme, named once and shared by every check, so layout is identical run to run. Verified (`harness.rs:23-33`): `HarnessOptions::default()` is 800×600 · scale 1 · light today. Whether that is the pinned value or a stand-specific one is a P4 decision.

- **Bundled fonts** — text shapes and measures with the stand's bundled `assets/DejaVuSans.woff2` (the font the wasm build already ships), not the host's system fonts. Layout is then the same on the dev host and the CI runner. Verified: `blitz-test-harness` enables `blitz-dom/system-fonts` and `HarnessOptions` has no font-context field (`harness.rs:12-21`). `DocumentConfig.font_ctx` exists (`config.rs:49`), and a supplied context replaces system-font discovery (`document.rs:370-376`). Supplying it headlessly is new harness or stand surface. `[premise-corrected: decode_font_bytes decompresses woff2 only under blitz-dom's woff feature (util.rs:22-37); cargo tree shows woff off for both -p blitz-tests and -p seven_guis]` The bundled `DejaVuSans.woff2` registers no face unless `woff` is on in the build that runs the check. That feature is unified on only by `cargo test --workspace`, through `blitz`, so the stand must enable `woff` itself. Otherwise text has no face and font-dependent assertions pass vacuously.

- **No live network** — the boot never reaches a network. A check uses no net provider, or one that refuses every fetch, so no stand check depends on or emits outbound traffic (security rules §Untrusted input: `blitz-net` has no timeout or size cap).
- **Fresh per check** — each check builds its own document from scratch. No state leaks between checks: no shared `VirtualDom`, no global signal, no reused harness, and check order does not matter.

- **The timer task is deterministic headlessly** — verified (`timer.rs`, `dioxus_document.rs:220-238`, `harness.rs` `tick`): the timer's `use_coroutine` ticks on `futures_timer::Delay`, 100 ms of real wall-clock time from its own timer thread. `Harness::pump` polls with a noop waker, and `Harness::tick` advances only the animation clock passed to `resolve`. No harness knob moves `elapsed`, so a deterministic elapsed advance needs a **stand-side** tick seam (the shape is a P4 fork). Settle detection proper (v010-10) is a later chunk and is out.

- **Proof checks** — at least one check per task boots it headlessly in TaskShell, reads its initial state, and drives one real interaction through the harness's input synthesis. Examples: the counter increments; the flight booker flags an invalid date; CRUD creates an entry; the timer's elapsed state moves. The checks run under the workspace test leg (`ci-leg.sh fast`).
- In: the headless boot entry point(s), the pinned viewport/font/net configuration, the four tasks, and the per-task proof checks.
- Out: the agent-invocable boot/run/status/cleanup commands and JSON-line logs ("Stand test contract", the next entry — it owns `scripts/agent-run.*`).
- Out: stable ids (Epoch 2), the snapshot (Epoch 3), settle detection (Epoch 4), screenshots ("Headless screenshot"), and the stand's a11y/contrast/keyboard harnesses (Epoch 6).
- Out: temp converter, circle drawer and cells. They stay in the app untouched. The lean four are intent's named set.
- The windowed stand (`seven_guis_native`, `just seven_guis`) and the wasm entry keep working and render the same Home → TaskShell flow.

- `examples/seven_guis/src/{app,lib}.rs` — a headless-reachable entry for a named task in TaskShell (verified, research.md §Graph impact). Plus `tasks/timer.rs` for the tick seam and the seven_guis manifest for `woff`.

- `packages/blitz-test-harness` — possibly a font-context option on `HarnessOptions` (P4 fork; the alternative is `Harness::wrap` over a stand-built `DocumentConfig`). arch §Standard Contracts lists the harness API, so a public addition there is an architecture amendment at wrap. `[premise-corrected: net_provider None already falls back to DummyNetProvider, document.rs:421-423]` No net option is needed for "no live network". All 3 `HarnessOptions { … }` literal sites use `..Default::default()`, so a new field breaks no caller.

- Where the stand checks live: verified, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/`, one file per behaviour (test-plan §2/§5, `.claude/rules/testing.md`). This adds a new `blitz-tests → seven_guis` dev-dependency edge, with no inbound edge to seven_guis today (graph query 2). It is an arch §Occupied Resources / crate-graph fact and needs a root `[workspace.dependencies]` entry. seven_guis keeps its default `hybrid` feature, because `dioxus-native` refuses to compile with no renderer (`dioxus_renderer.rs:27`).

- Incremental-layout invariant: where the stand checks assert layout, they run under the pipeline's `for incremental in [false, true]` discipline (CLAUDE.md warning). `[premise-corrected: HarnessOptions has no incremental field; DocumentConfig.incremental exists, config.rs:61]` The two-mode run needs the same configuration seam as the font context (the P4 fork above).

- Fresh per check: verified safe under parallel `cargo test`. `StyleThreading`'s `#[default]` is `Sequential` (`config.rs:19-28`), so harness documents never share Stylo's global pool. The field doc at `config.rs:54` saying "Parallel" is upstream doc drift, not this chunk's to fix.
- a11y surface: TaskShell's back button and the tasks' controls are focus surface (a11y rules). This chunk changes no markup the windowed app renders.

title: Plan — 2026-10-06-id-persistence: "Id persistence — same id across re-render, remount and fresh process on the stand (v010-02)"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-06-id-persistence: "Id persistence — same id across re-render, remount and fresh process on the stand (v010-02)"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-06-id-persistence · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-06T10:05Z
- **Base sha:** `065295540ec0b80c0e40b7b186c7aecfba6f6121`, the commit this chunk starts from (HEAD at P4). The diff guards below compare against it.

Prove that the stable element id built by `2026-10-06-stable-element-ids` persists on the stand. Every lean-task element keeps its id across a re-render, a remount, and a restart in a new process (`verification-matrix.json#v010-02`).

Research found that persistence holds by construction. The id is a pure function of the rendered component chain, Dioxus keys, tag structure and HTML `id` attributes. No runtime identity enters it, and no output depends on hash order (research.md §Patterns detected; per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge). So the chunk's work is mostly proof: three stand checks, each built so that it fails unless its event really happened.

One code change closes the folded CARRY. CRUD rows are keyed by their list index, so after a Delete a person's row takes another person's id. Rows are re-keyed on a stable person id from `crud.rs`'s own model. Then a person's row id follows the person, which is what Epoch 4's act-by-id will rely on.

The remount runs through the app's own Back → Home → task-card navigation. The test boots `seven_guis::app::app` with the stand's pinned options, so `seven_guis` needs no new API and the remount is one a user can perform.

The fresh-process proof re-executes the test binary as a child. This is the in-repo precedent at `tests/blitz-tests/tests/telemetry_stdout_silent.rs:10-11` (per test-plan §1, the escher-telemetry process-global files).

1. **Re-key CRUD rows by person** (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs`).
   a. `Person` (crud.rs:3-7) gains an `id: u64` field. The three fixture people take ids `0`, `1`, `2`, in their current order: Hans Emil, Max Mustermann, Roman Tisch.
   b. A `next_id` signal in `Crud` starts at `3`. **Create** (crud.rs:97-103) pushes the new person with `id: next_id()` and then increments `next_id`.
   c. **Update** (crud.rs:108-115) keeps the edited entry's `id`. It replaces only `first` and `last`.
   d. The row's Dioxus key (crud.rs:63) becomes `key: "{person.id}"`. Selection, Update and Delete stay index-based, unchanged (crud.rs:27, 64-69, 122-130). No `class`, `style`, element, `CSS` text or `id:` attribute changes.
   e. Because the fixture ids equal the old fixture indices, the first row still reads `TaskShell/Crud/div:0/div:1/div:0/div[0]`. The pin at `stand_element_ids.rs:227-231` holds unchanged.

2. **New stand check file** `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_id_persistence.rs`.
   - It opens with a `//!` doc naming the behaviour: a lean-task element's stable id survives a re-render, a remount and a fresh process.
   - It boots through `seven_guis::stand::{boot, boot_timer}` with `stand::options(incremental)`, for each `incremental` in `[false, true]` (per architecture §Conventions → Tests; test-plan §3 Construction).
   - It holds three `#[test]`s plus one `#[ignore]` child, as steps 3–5 describe.
   - Input goes only through harness helpers (`click`, `type_text`); timer ticks go through `TimerTicks::deliver` + `pump`.

3. **Test `ids_hold_across_rerenders`.** For each lean task and both modes, read `doc.element_ids()` before (`B`) and after (`A`) the task's scripted re-renders. Then assert all of the following.
   - The re-render happened: `harness.dom_string()` after differs from before.
   - Every `NodeId` present in both `B` and `A` reads the same id in both.
   - The scripted re-renders:
     - **Counter:** click `#counter-increment` twice.
     - **Flight booker:** click `#flight-return`, which toggles `disabled` on `#flight-return-date`. Then click `#flight-book`, which inserts `p#flight-booked`. Assert the inserted node reads `flight-booked` and the ids of all earlier elements are unchanged.
     - **Timer** (via `boot_timer`): `deliver(5)` + `pump`. `#timer-elapsed` text changes and the ids are unchanged.
     - **CRUD:** the four scenarios below.
   - **CRUD scenarios.** Map each row's text (`"{last}, {first}"`) to its id before and after each scenario.
     - Filter: click `#crud-filter`, type `M`. One row remains, and `Mustermann, Max` reads the same id it read before the filter.
     - Delete: on a fresh boot, click the `Emil, Hans` row, then `#crud-delete`. `Mustermann, Max` and `Tisch, Roman` read the ids they read before, `…/div[1]` and `…/div[2]`. No row reads `…/div[0]` any more.
     - Create: type a name and surname, click `#crud-create`. The new row reads `TaskShell/Crud/div:0/div:1/div:0/div[3]`, and every earlier row reads its earlier id.

4. **Test `ids_hold_across_a_remount`.** Boot a test-side root in both modes: a `fn` component that provides `seven_guis::tasks::timer::TimerTicks::default()` as context and returns `seven_guis::app::app()`. Boot it with `Harness::from_vdom(VirtualDom::new(root), stand::options(incremental))`. Then, for each lean task's card in `#task-grid` (Counter 1, Flight booker 3, Timer 4, CRUD 5 by `:nth-child`, app.rs:24-67):
   a. Click the card and read `before = element_ids()`. Assert `#task-shell` is present. Also assert `before`'s id strings equal, in order, the id strings of `stand::boot(task, stand::options(incremental))`. This is the app-root/stand-root equality from research.md §Patterns detected.
   b. Click `#back-btn`. Assert `#task-shell` is absent and `#home` is present, so the task really unmounted.
   c. Click the same card again and read `after = element_ids()`. Assert:
      - `after`'s id strings equal `before`'s, in order.
      - No `NodeId` in `after` appears in `before`, so the remount minted fresh nodes.
      - `doc.element_id(n)` is `None` for every `NodeId` `n` in `before`, with no panic.
      - `harness.focused()` is not any `NodeId` of `before` (per a11y-plan §5 → Focus restoration).

6. **Leave everything else unchanged.** That covers the manifests and `Cargo.lock`, `packages/` (`element_id.rs` included), `app.rs`, `stand.rs`, `counter.rs`, `flight_booker.rs`, `timer.rs` and `scripts/` (the diff-guard entry). The new file picks up its `stand_` prefix for `run stand` with no script change (per test-plan §3 `run {selection}`).
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_id_persistence.rs` — the re-render, remount and fresh-process checks, plus the ignored child (steps 2–5)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs` — `Person.id`, a `next_id` source, Create assigns ids, and the row key is `person.id` (step 1). Model and key only; no markup, class, style or CSS change.

No live leg runs this chunk. The agent-run entries drive the in-process stand through `scripts/agent-run.sh`, and the fresh-process check spawns its own test binary inside `cargo test`. No external process is started, so there is no liveness probe and no `stop`.
No headful self-verify exists in this project, because the stand is headless (`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`). So no `self-verify` entry is listed.

No `smoke` entry either. test-plan declares no boot-smoke trigger list, and the stand boot (`stand.rs`, `app.rs`) is untouched, as the diff-guard entry checks. The boot itself runs under every stand check.
The base sha in the diff guards is `065295540ec0b80c0e40b7b186c7aecfba6f6121`.

- **boot / boot_timer** — 13 call sites in 6 stand files (`stand_boot.rs` 50-113, `stand_counter.rs:9`, `stand_crud.rs` 16, 27, `stand_element_ids.rs:70`, `stand_flight_booker.rs:16`, `stand_timer.rs` 10, 26, 38). Each `line + 1` is from the trace's 0-indexed `line`. An additive function in `stand.rs` leaves them unchanged.

- **task_in_shell** — 2 callers: `app::app` @ `app.rs:77` and `stand::stand_root` @ `stand.rs:102`. Both render it as the root component's only child, so its `TaskShell` instance sits under the same `ScopeId::APP`-owned chain in both.
- **Person / crud.rs** — no symbol outside `crud.rs` names `Person`. Its only external pins are the `stand_element_ids.rs` row id (229) and `stand_crud.rs` selectors.

- **Ids carry no runtime identity** (`element_id.rs:14-15`, 153-228): an element's id is a pure function of the rendered component chain, the keys, the tag structure and the `id` attributes. Equality: the same rendered tree yields the same id list, in any process and after any remount that re-renders the same tree. This was verified by reading every input and the iteration order above. The chunk's checks are its empirical proof.

- **App root and stand root give the same task ids** (`app.rs:77`, `stand.rs:102`): `app` and `stand_root` are both the `ScopeId::APP` root, and that scope adds no path segment (`element_id.rs:47-54`). `task_in_shell` renders `TaskShell` as its direct child in both, so a task's ids under `app` after Home → task equal its ids under `stand::boot`. This holds by construction. The remount check can assert it outright.

- **Remount mints fresh nodes** (`mutation_writer.rs:290-303`, `mutator.rs:533`, `document.rs:844-855`): unmounting detaches, and remounting deep-clones templates into newly created slab nodes. Equality: for every element, the post-remount `NodeId` differs from its pre-remount `NodeId`. The check must assert this, so it cannot pass vacuously. The pre-remount `NodeId` then reads `element_id == None`, because a detached node is unreachable from the root, or because a dropped one is stale (`element_id.rs:237`; `doc.get_node` → `None`).

- **Re-exec the test binary as the child** (`telemetry_stdout_silent.rs:10-11, 32-33`): the parent runs `current_exe()` with `--ignored --exact {child} --nocapture` and reads the child's output. The child is an ignored test in the same file.

- **Index keys follow position, not entity** (`crud.rs:57-63`, 126): after `Delete` at index `k`, every person after `k` moves to key `k…`. Dioxus's keyed diff keeps the DOM nodes of keys `0..len-1` and drops the last key's node. A person's row therefore changes id, and the surviving DOM node at a key now shows another person. This re-derives the CARRY's measured claim at HEAD, by reading `crud.rs` plus the keyed-diff rule. The existing `stand_element_ids.rs:236-271` test is its witness.

The stable element id built by `2026-10-06-stable-element-ids` (`DioxusDocument::element_id` / `element_ids`) is proved to **persist**: an element keeps the same id across a re-render, a remount, and a fresh process. intent §Findings 1 names the gap this closes. A `NodeId` is a versioned slot that a remount re-mints, so an agent holding one between actions aims at nothing. An id that survives re-render and remount is what snapshot diffs (Epoch 3) and act-by-id (Epoch 4) rest on. Capability v010-02 (`verification-matrix.json#v010-02`, method `e2e`): "For each stand element, the id read before and after a re-render, a remount, and a restart in a new process is the same."

- **Re-render** — a state change that re-renders a task's components without unmounting them (counter increment, flight-booker field edit, timer tick, CRUD filter or selection) leaves every surviving element's id unchanged. The id is a pure function of the rendered component chain, keys, tag structure and `id` attributes, with no runtime identity and no hash-ordered output (research.md §Files inspected, element_id.rs:153-228). It is therefore persistent by construction for every element whose own path survives. `[premise-corrected: a disabled toggle is an attribute change, not a shape change (flight_booker.rs:89, 96; crud.rs:107, 121); the lean four's shape-changing re-renders are flight booker's p#flight-booked inserted as the last, author-keyed child (flight_booker.rs:107-109) and CRUD's keyed rows filtered, created and deleted (crud.rs:57-63) — research.md §Files inspected]` The re-render checks cover those shape changes as well as the text- and attribute-only ones.

- **Remount** — the same element, unmounted and mounted again, reads the same id. Verified (research.md): the stand has no remount path today. `stand::boot` mounts one task through `task_in_shell` with a no-op `on_back` (stand.rs:100-102). `seven_guis::app::app` is `pub` (lib.rs:1; app.rs:69-79) and navigates Home ⇄ task through `#back-btn` and `button.task-card`. Its task ids equal `stand::boot`'s by construction, because both roots are `ScopeId::APP` and render `task_in_shell` directly (app.rs:77, stand.rs:102, element_id.rs:47-54). Unmount detaches, and remount deep-clones templates into newly created slab nodes (mutation_writer.rs:189-193, 290-303; mutator.rs:533; document.rs:844-855). So every post-remount `NodeId` differs from the pre-remount one, and the check asserts that difference. Whether the remount goes through the app's own Back → Home → task-card path or through a stand-side handle is a P4 fork.

An element left in place keeps its stable id when the app's code around it changes (v010-16; intent §Findings 1).
The founder settled what that means at this phase (inputs#I1, inputs#I2, inputs#I3), as two rules:

1. **Anchored paths.** An unkeyed element under an element of its own component that reads an author key takes
   its path from that element: `{key}//{relative path}`. A component's template root keeps starting at its
   component names, as today, so the anchor acts inside one component only. An edit outside the keyed element
   then no longer renames what is inside it (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge, amended
   at wrap on the founder's ratification).

2. **Actionable elements are keyed.** Every element an agent can act on — focusable, or carrying an interactive
   role, or carrying an event listener — reads an author key. The rule is for app authors, so its check is a
   public function of `dioxus-native-dom` that returns the actionable elements reading a positional path, each
   with the element and the remedy; the later CLI and driver reuse it (inputs#I3). The stand check asserts it
   returns nothing.

The chunk changes the id grammar in one place (`element_id.rs`), adds the library check as a new gated module,
keys the two kinds of stand element the check finds — CRUD's person rows and Home's seven task cards — measures
the three non-lean tasks with the same function, adds two stand checks (the edit proof and the actionable-key
check) and re-pins the five places that spell a row's id. No engine change and no new dependency
(research.md §Graph impact; security-plan §Dependency Security).

1. **Anchor rule** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs`, `element_ids` and `place_children`
   (`place_children` @ `element_id.rs:163` and `:175` are its only call sites, research.md §Graph impact). Where
   an element reads its author key (the existing predicate at 170-174: HTML `id`, non-empty, no `/`, first
   claim), each child that continues the same owner's path reads `{key}//{segment}` in place of
   `{parent path}/{segment}`; deeper same-owner descendants extend that path with `/` as today. A child that is
   a template root of another owner still restarts at its component chain (217-220), unchanged. An element
   whose `id` fails the predicate anchors nothing. The precedence becomes: author key → anchored path →
   component path → document path. Nothing else about the walk changes: ids stay computed on demand, written
   to neither tree, and free of `NodeId`, `ElementId`, `ScopeId` and pointers.

2. **Grammar docs** — the module `//!` of `element_id.rs` (1-15) and the `DioxusDocument::element_id` doc comment
   in `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs` (185-199) state the four tiers and the `//` spelling,
   and the sentence "Paths always contain `/` and keys never do" is extended with why an anchored path equals no
   other id (a key holds no `/`; a component path has no empty segment; a document path starts with `/`).

4. **The library check** — new module `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/actionable.rs`, compiled only under the
   crate's `accessibility` feature (it reads the accessibility tree's role), wired in
   `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs` the way `snapshot` is (`lib.rs:17-18`, `23-24`): a gated `mod` and a
   gated `pub use`. It adds:
   - `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable(&self) -> Vec<UnkeyedActionable>` — every actionable element whose id
     holds a `/`, in document pre-order; empty when every actionable element reads its author key. It takes no
     argument, writes nothing, logs nothing and never panics: a node that does not resolve is skipped.
   - `UnkeyedActionable` — public, with rustdoc on every item: the element (its `NodeId`, the positional id it
     reads, its tag and its role), which of the three readers matched, and `remedy()`, text that names the fix —
     an HTML `id` that is non-empty, holds no `/` and is unique in the document. No field or text carries the
     element's text content, accessible name or an attribute value.
   - An element is actionable when any of three existing readers says so: `Node::is_focussable()`
     (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:546`); its accessibility node's role is in the closed list Button,
     Link, CheckBox, RadioButton, Slider, SpinButton, ScrollBar, ComboBox, ListBox, ListBoxOption, MenuItem,
     MenuItemCheckBox, MenuItemRadio, Tab, TreeItem, DisclosureTriangle, MultilineTextInput, plus every role
     `role_from_element_data`'s `input` arm returns (`packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:260` onward); or it
     carries the `data-dioxus-id` attribute, which the bridge writes for every listener but `onmounted`
     (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/mutation_writer.rs:309-323`). Ids come from `element_ids()` and roles from
     `accessibility_tree()` — no second id or role computation. An element the accessibility tree leaves out
     (hidden) is still held by the other two readers.

6. **Key the CRUD row** — `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs`, the row `div` at 67-78: add the attribute
   `id: "crud-person-{person.id}"`. The `key: "{person.id}"` stays on the same element; no class, style,
   wrapper, order, `tabindex` or handler changes.

7. **Key Home's task cards** — `examples/seven_guis/src/app.rs`: `TaskMeta` (17-22) gains a
   `slug: &'static str` field, each of the seven `TASKS` entries (24-67) a kebab-case value (`counter`,
   `temp-converter`, `flight-booker`, `timer`, `crud`, `circle-drawer`, `cells`), and the card `button` (135-144)
   the attribute `id: "task-card-{meta.slug}"`. No class, style, wrapper, order or handler changes, and no Home
   or shell CSS rule is added or edited.

8. **Re-pin the row** — the five places that spell a row's id read the author key instead:
   `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_element_ids.rs` (231, and the `keyed ||` test at 203-207 so a row counts as
   keyed; its `//!` head names the four tiers), `stand_id_persistence.rs` (`ROW_PATH` at 15 and `row_path` at
   58-60), `stand_accessibility_ids.rs` (271), `stand_snapshot.rs` (the row lookups at 286-294 and 421). Every
   property those tests assert stays asserted — uniqueness, a row following its person under filter, Create
   and Delete, the same ids across a re-render, a remount and a fresh process, `author_id` on every element
   node. The child test keeps its name `ids_in_a_child_process` and its `stand-id` line shape.

9. **Edit proof** — new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_id_edits.rs`, booted with
   `Harness::from_vdom(vdom, stand::options(incremental))` in both layout modes, each test first asserting its
   fixture differs between before and after. Before/after variants are components of the same name in two
   modules, so a rename never stands in for the edit. Five tests:
   - `a_task_keeps_every_id_when_the_code_around_it_changes` — each lean task component (`Counter`,
     `FlightBooker`, `Timer` with a `TimerTicks` context, `Crud`) rendered in a plain shell and in an edited
     shell (an earlier sibling of the task's root tag, a wrapper around the task, the task one level deeper):
     the task's elements read the same ids, in order;
   - `keyed_elements_keep_their_ids_under_every_edit` — in a small form fixture, each keyed element reads the
     same id after an earlier same-tag sibling is added, a sibling is removed, and an ancestor is wrapped;
   - `anchored_elements_keep_their_ids_under_edits_outside_their_anchor` — an unkeyed element under a keyed
     element of the fixture reads `{key}//…` and keeps it when a sibling is added before the keyed element and
     when the keyed element is wrapped;
   - `a_behaviour_edit_changes_no_id` — text, an attribute, a class and a handler changed: the id list is equal;
   - `edits_inside_the_anchor_change_only_positional_ids` — the measured negatives: an earlier same-tag sibling
     and a wrapper inserted between an unkeyed element and the point its path starts at change that element's
     id, change no keyed element's id, and an unkeyed element with no keyed ancestor in its component changes
     under an earlier-sibling edit.

10. **Actionable-key stand check** — new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_actionable_keys.rs`, calling
    `harness.doc.unkeyed_actionable()`, in both layout modes. Three tests:
    - `every_actionable_stand_element_reads_an_author_key` — the four lean tasks through `stand::boot`, and
      Home through `seven_guis::app::app` with the stand's options: the function returns nothing, and each
      screen has a non-zero count of actionable elements (read from the same three readers, so an empty result
      is not vacuous);
    - `the_verdict_does_not_change_with_state` — the flight booker with Book enabled and disabled, the flight
      booker after Book (so `#flight-booked` is mounted), CRUD after Create and after a row is selected: the
      function returns nothing in each state;
    - `the_non_lean_tasks_are_measured` — the temp converter, the circle drawer and cells, each opened from
      Home by its card's author key: the number of entries the function returns is asserted equal to a constant
      per task, written from this test's first run (predicted: unknown — record what the run measures). The
      test's doc comment names the CARRY that owns keying them.

11. **Record for the wrap** — the report carries: the measured id list of each lean task after the change (the
    `ids_in_a_child_process` output); the anchored ids the children of Home's task cards now read; the three
    non-lean counts; the new public surface (`DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable`, `UnkeyedActionable`,
    re-exported through `dioxus-native`'s `pub use dioxus_native_dom::*`, `packages/dioxus-native/src/lib.rs:27`);
    and a line map for each edited file the masters cite by line (`app.rs`, `crud.rs`, `lib.rs`, `element_id.rs`,
    `dioxus_document.rs`, the four stand checks).
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/actionable.rs` — the library check and its unit tests (steps 4-5)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_id_edits.rs` — the edit proof (step 9)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_actionable_keys.rs` — the actionable-key stand check (step 10)
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs` — the anchor rule, its docs and seven unit tests
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs` — the grammar in the `element_id` doc comment
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs` — the gated `mod actionable` and its gated re-export
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs` — the row's author key
- `examples/seven_guis/src/app.rs` — the task cards' author keys and the `slug` field behind them
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_element_ids.rs` — the row pin and the keyed test
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_id_persistence.rs` — `ROW_PATH` and `row_path`
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_accessibility_ids.rs` — the created row's id
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot.rs` — the row lookups

No live leg runs this chunk: the agent-run entries drive the in-process stand through `scripts/agent-run.sh`, and
no external process is started, so there is no liveness probe and no `stop`. No headful self-verify exists in this
project, because the stand is headless (`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`). Test-plan declares no boot-smoke
trigger list, so the boot path is read by shape as earlier plans read it (`stand.rs`, `app.rs`, `main.rs`): `app.rs`
is touched, so the block carries the windowed boot smoke the headless-stand plan used after its `app.rs` change,
behind the display handle `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` (unset reads `not run`, never red). `stand.rs` and `main.rs` are
untouched as the diff guard checks, and the two markup probes hold `crud.rs` and `app.rs` to attributes and one
data field. The CI acceptance follows the operator pass (pre-CI commit, push, CI read) like every prior chunk.

- (v010-16) On the stand — the four lean tasks and the edit fixture beside them, in both layout modes — an
  element left in place reads the same id after the code around it changes: every element of each lean task
  when its shell is edited; every keyed element under a sibling added or removed before it and under a wrapped
  ancestor; every anchored element under an edit outside its anchor; every element under a behaviour edit.
  Proved by `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_id_edits` (cites
  `verification-matrix.json#v010-16`; per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge).

- (v010-16) The edits the contract says may change an id are measured, not assumed: an earlier same-tag sibling
  or a wrapper between an unkeyed element and the point its path starts at changes that id and no keyed id
  (`edits_inside_the_anchor_change_only_positional_ids`) (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM
  bridge).

- (v010-16 · a11y) `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable()` returns nothing on the four lean tasks and on Home,
  in the boot state and after Book, Create and a row selection, with the Book button held to the rule enabled
  and disabled. Proved by `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_actionable_keys` (per a11y-plan §5
  Focus order per layout; §7 Accessibility tree output).

- (arch · a11y · security) The library check reports an unkeyed actionable element — a button, a disabled
  button, a `div` with a click handler, a button with a repeated `id`, a hidden button with a handler — with
  its element, the reader that matched and the remedy, reports no keyed or inert element, and carries no text
  content, accessible name or attribute value. Proved by `cargo test -p dioxus-native-dom --locked --lib
  actionable::` (per a11y-plan §7 Accessibility tree output; security-plan §Logging & Monitoring; architecture
  §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge).

- (tests) The three non-lean tasks are measured with the same function and their counts pinned by
  `the_non_lean_tasks_are_measured`; the report states the three counts and names the CARRY owed at wrap (per
  test-plan §1 Coverage scope).

- (arch · security) Under the new grammar `element_ids()` is pairwise distinct on each lean task and on the
  fixtures; an `id` that is empty, holds a `/` or repeats an earlier one neither reads as a key nor anchors a
  child; a key spelled like a component name reads a different id from that component's path. Proved by
  `cargo test -p dioxus-native-dom --locked --lib element_id::` (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus
  DOM bridge; security-plan §Input Validation).

- (arch · tests) The persistence properties still hold after the re-pin: the same id across a re-render, a
  remount and a fresh process on each lean task in both modes, the `#[ignore]` child still run by its parent,
  and a CRUD row following its person under filter, Create and Delete — the re-pinned
  `stand_id_persistence` and `stand_element_ids` pass (per test-plan §1 Coverage scope; layout-templates
  §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens).

- (a11y) Every element node of each lean task's accessibility tree carries an `author_id` equal to its
  element's id and no `TextRun`, document-root or `Window` node carries one; the 15 controls keep their roles
  and names and each task keeps its focus sequence — the re-pinned `stand_accessibility_ids` and
  `stand_snapshot` pass (per a11y-plan §7 Accessibility tree output; §5 Focus order per layout; §8 Error
  recovery).

- (layouts · design) The stand's markup changes by attributes only: the `crud.rs` diff is one added
  `id: "crud-person-{person.id}"` line; the `app.rs` diff is the `slug` field, its seven values and one added
  `id: "task-card-{meta.slug}"` line; no other file under `examples/` changes — the `added=1 other=0` entry,
  the `field=1 slugs=7 id=1 other=0` entry and the `git diff --quiet` entry (per layout-templates §Surface:
  desktop-native → Primary screens; design-system §Color Palette → Core Colors).

- (arch · security) No manifest, lockfile, engine, harness, telemetry, script or CI file changes: the
  `git diff --quiet` entry exits 0, and `cargo build -p dioxus-native-dom --no-default-features --locked`
  succeeds with the new module compiled out (per architecture §Occupied Resources → Names; §Cross-cutting
  Patterns → Config management; security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (obs · security) The id module, the library check and the two new stand checks hold no log site, print, env
  read or listener, and no agent-run event carries a content-named key (the census entry reads 0; the events
  entry reads 0) (per obs-plan §2 Telemetry Strategy → Telemetry mechanism; §8 PII Scrubbing & Compliance →
  Scrubbing; security-plan §Logging & Monitoring).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run stand` exits 0 with 41 stand tests `ok` (predicted — record what the
  run measures), and `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast`, `doc` and `a11y` exit 0 (per test-plan §3
  Agent-run contract; §9 Pipeline facts → Local pre-push gate).

- (tests · obs) The windowed stand still boots with Home's cards keyed: the smoke entry reads
  `service.name=seven_guis` from a stand up for 10 s, where a display is present (per test-plan §3 Runners and
  invocation; obs-plan §3 Observability Harness Contract → Logging stack).

- (tests) The fork's CI reads `verdict: green` on the pushed sha; the report names the run id the
  `ci.py conclusion` entry read (per test-plan §9 Pipeline facts → Legs).

- Spec anchors the plan rests on (from the extracts): architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge ·
  §Standard Contracts → Headless stand · §Cross-cutting Patterns → Config management · §Occupied Resources ·
  §Conventions → Tests · §Conventions → Documentation; security-plan §Input Validation · §Logging & Monitoring ·
  §Dependency Security; a11y-plan §5 · §7 · §8 · §9; test-plan §1 · §2 · §3 · §9; obs-plan §2 · §3 · §6 · §8;
  layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens; design-system §Color Palette · §Typography →
  Loading.

- The founder's rulings: inputs#I1 (both rules in this chunk; the ledger's gap text corrected before the
  claim), inputs#I2 (the anchor acts inside one component; a listener-bearing element is actionable; the
  spelling `key//segment`) and inputs#I3 (the check is a public library function, a contract addition recorded
  for the wrap; Home's seven task cards are keyed here; the three non-lean tasks are measured and carried).

- Leaned, not asked: the edit fixture lives in the stand check file and boots through `Harness::from_vdom` with
  `stand::options`, per `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:90-91` (`TaskShell` is private, `app.rs:153`); the
  three non-lean counts are pinned by a test rather than only written into the report, so the wrap's light
  gate re-measures them.

- Research files inspected: `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs`, `dioxus_document.rs`, `snapshot.rs`,
  `lib.rs`, `mutation_writer.rs`; `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs`, `accessibility.rs`;
  `packages/dioxus-native/src/lib.rs`; `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs`, `app.rs`, `tasks/crud.rs`; the four
  stand identity checks.

- A leading `#` on the anchor key — rejected by the founder: it starts a comment in bash and zsh, and intent
  §Findings 7 wants stand flows scriptable in shell alone (inputs#I2).

- A bare `key/segment` — rejected: a key spelled like a component name would read that component's path
  (`Item/b:0`, the pin at `element_id.rs:347`).

- Anchoring across component boundaries — rejected by the founder (inputs#I2): every lean task's root would
  read the same id under `task-body` on four screens, and component names would leave task ids.

- A test-local check with no library entry point — rejected by the founder (inputs#I3): the rule is for app
  authors, and the later CLI and driver reuse the function.

- A second id or role computation inside the library check — not done: ids come from `element_ids()` and roles
  from `accessibility_tree()` (a11y-plan §7; architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge).

- Adding `tabindex`, a `role` or a focusability change to the CRUD row to make it satisfy the check — not done:
  it changes the Tab order a11y-plan §5 pins; the row is keyed, nothing else.

- Deriving a key from text, a name or a list index — not done: security-plan §Input Validation bars a list
  index, pointer, hash, clock or process-local value from an id; a row's key is the person's model id and a
  card's key is a fixed slug.
- Keying the three non-lean tasks — not in this chunk: they are measured and carried (inputs#I3).

- Any print or log of an id in the id module, the library check or the stand checks — not done: the library
  returns data and the stand check's failure text travels as a test assertion message only (obs-plan §3; §6).

- The `//` spelling was checked for collisions before planning, as the founder asked (inputs#I2): an author key
  holds no `/` (`element_id.rs:173`); a path that is not anchored either starts with `/` (document and app-root
  paths, `element_id.rs:163` with an empty base) or is a component chain of non-empty names followed by
  non-empty `{tag}:{n}` / `{tag}[{key}]` segments (`element_id.rs:103-114`, `210-215`), so it holds no `//`;
  and a tag cannot hold a `/` — measured on dioxus-rsx 0.7.10: `ElementName::parse` accepts only identifiers
  joined by `-` (`src/element.rs:349-365`). No collision case was found.

- The skeleton's `main` reads an author key but anchors nothing: its children are template roots of another
  owner, which restart at their chain (`element_id.rs:217-220`; `dioxus_document.rs:126-131`).

- Predicted, to be measured: after the change no lean-task element reads an anchored path at boot (the rows,
  the only unkeyed children of a keyed same-component element in the measured lists, become keyed); the
  children of Home's keyed task cards do (`task-card-counter//div:0` and below), which
  `ids_hold_across_a_remount` compares without pinning a spelling. Record both in the report.

- `ids_hold_across_a_remount` opens a task with `#task-grid > .task-card:nth-child(n)`
  (`stand_id_persistence.rs:199`); the selector still matches a keyed card.

- `stand_snapshot.rs` finds rows by `id.contains("/div[")` (289) and `ends_with("div[n]")` (292, 421); a keyed
  row matches neither, so those lookups change with the pin, not only the string.

- The persistence parent parses the child's `stand-id {task} {mode} {id}` lines by whitespace
  (`stand_id_persistence.rs:296-300`); no id holds a space under either rule.
- The new public type exposes `accesskit::Role`, as `SnapshotNode.role` already does (`snapshot.rs:26`).

- Counts the wrap re-measures: dioxus-native-dom unit tests 18 → predicted 29 (test-plan §1, as counted by
  2026-10-06-snapshot-model); stand `ok` 33 → predicted 41; workspace 471 · 0 · 5 → predicted 490 · 0 · 5.

- Owed at wrap (route-resolve, on the founder's word, inputs#I3): a CARRY for the three non-lean tasks — the
  temp converter, the circle drawer and cells — carrying each task's measured count of unkeyed actionable
  elements and the test that pins it; the wrap chooses the entry that owns keying them.

- Expected amendments (wrap):
  - architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge — the grammar gains the anchored tier (`key//segment`,
    same-owner children of a keyed element, component roots still restart), and the bridge gains
    `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` with `UnkeyedActionable` under `accessibility`; both on the founder's
    word (inputs#I1, inputs#I2, inputs#I3), recorded as ratified, never as PROVISIONAL
  - security-plan §Input Validation — the `id` row's grammar text, its uniqueness argument (`//`) and its line
    anchors into `element_id.rs`; the new in-process reader added where the row lists who reads the id
  - layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens — a CRUD row's id is its author key
    `crud-person-{person.id}`; the author-id list gains the rows and Home's seven `task-card-{slug}` keys
  - a11y-plan §7 Accessibility tree output — the `author_id` values re-spell with the grammar; the actionable
    rule and its library check
  - test-plan §1 · §3 · §9 — the unit and stand counts, the two new stand files, the local baseline link
  - design-system — coordinates only: `app.rs` holds 12 design citations (the design history file) and nine
    lines are inserted above most of them; no value changes
  - obs-plan — coordinates only if a cited line in `lib.rs` moved (it cites `examples/seven_guis/src/lib.rs`,
    not the bridge's); no log site and no printing child is added
  - matrix#v010-01 notes — its acceptance says "every other element reads its component path"; after this
    chunk an unkeyed element under a keyed element of its own component reads an anchored path
    (`key//segment`) instead, and CRUD's rows read author keys. A premise correction on the founder's ruling
    (inputs#I1), the outcome unchanged: every element reads exactly one unique id.

An element's id is now, in order of precedence, one of FOUR tiers:
    1. the **author key** — unchanged: the HTML `id`, verbatim, when non-empty, `/`-free and the first in document pre-order to claim it;
    2. the **anchored path** (NEW) — for an element under an element of its own component instance that reads an author key: `{key}//{segment}`, then `/{segment}` per further DOM level (`box//p:0/b:0`). The nearest such keyed element anchors. Mechanism: when an element reads its author key, `element_ids` passes `{key}/` instead of the element's own path as the base its children extend (element_id.rs:181-187), so a child that continues its parent's path reads `{key}/` + `/{segment}`; a segment is still `{tag}[{key}]` for a template root of a Dioxus-keyed VNode, else `{tag}:{n}`;
    3. the **component path** — unchanged in form. A template root owned by ANOTHER component instance still restarts at that component's chain (element_id.rs:231-234), so the anchor acts inside one component only: `div#slot { Item {} }` leaves Item's root at `Item/b:0`, and `TaskShell/Counter/div:0` is unchanged under the keyed `main#task-body`;
    4. the **document path** — unchanged.
    An `id` that fails the author-key predicate (empty, `/`-bearing, a later duplicate) anchors nothing. The skeleton's `main` reads its key and anchors nothing in a Dioxus app, because its children are template roots of another owner.
    Uniqueness argument, now three-way: an author key holds no `/`; an anchored path is the only id holding `//` — a component path is a chain of non-empty names and non-empty segments, and a document or app-root path starts with one `/` and has no empty segment after it; so no id of one tier equals an id of another. A key spelled like a component name stays distinct: `div#Item { b {} }` beside `Item {}` reads `Item//b:0` and `Item/b:0` (unit test `a_key_spelled_like_a_component_stays_distinct`). Ids stay computed on demand, written to neither tree, and free of `NodeId`, `ElementId`, `ScopeId` and pointers. Ratified by the founder at /andromeda-phase (inputs I1 · I2): both rules, the `key//segment` spelling, and the one-component reach.

Read-only, takes no argument, logs nothing, never panics: a node that does not resolve through `BaseDocument::get_node` is skipped.
    - `UnkeyedActionable { pub node: NodeId, pub id: String, pub tag: String, pub role: Option<accesskit::Role>, pub focusable: bool, pub interactive_role: bool, pub listener: bool }` (actionable.rs:15-34; `Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`) with `remedy(&self) -> String` (36-44): "give the `{tag}` element reading `{id}` an HTML `id` attribute that is non-empty, holds no `/` and is unique in the document". `role` is `None` when the accessibility tree leaves the element out (hidden).
