- **Marker:** 2026-10-06-stand-test-contract · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-06T03:20:00Z

An agent gets one fixed, machine-readable way to drive the stand checks and blitz-tests: `scripts/agent-run.sh` with
five verbs, `boot · run · status · cleanup · logs`. Each verb has a closed exit grammar and JSON-line output, and
`scripts/agent-run.ps1` delegates to it on Windows. This is the 5-command discipline that test-plan §3 leaves NOT YET
MEASURED, and the harness that health check 13 reports missing for an agent-driven project. The design follows the
stand as it is built. The stand is an in-process library boot, with no daemon, socket or window (architecture
§Standard Contracts → Headless stand; research.md §Files inspected). So boot builds the test binaries and opens a
state area under `target/`, and nothing is started or polled. Per-test results come from libtest's pretty output,
because its JSON format is nightly-only on this toolchain (measured at P3, research.md §Patterns detected).

The JSON-line log is harness-level. The script writes one event per verb and per test. It never carries captured
test output, and its field names stay off the scrub's content-named set (security-plan §Logging & Monitoring;
obs-plan §8 Scrubbing). The stand installs no escher sink, so no telemetry stream exists in a stand-check process for
it to carry (obs-plan §3 Logging stack). The chunk changes no Rust signature, no `Cargo.lock` and no CI job. Its
contract tests run in the existing `ci-scripts` leg through a cargo shim, the `LegScriptTest` precedent (test-plan §4).

The chunk also discharges its PREREQ. It corrects the `//!` doc of `tests/blitz-tests/tests/dioxus_falsy_disabled.rs`
so that the doc claims only the defect the falsy-`disabled` fix removed: the literal `"false"` matched `:disabled` and
DISABLED state. It drops the focus-order and focusability clauses. Re-verified at HEAD, focusability parses the value
as a bool (`element.rs:629`), and presence keys the state (`element.rs:449`) and the click target (`pointer.rs:330,457`).
The test body asserts no focusability (a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation, §8 Cognitive Accessibility; security-plan
§Input Validation `disabled` row).

1. **PREREQ — rewrite the `//!` doc of `tests/blitz-tests/tests/dioxus_falsy_disabled.rs` (lines 1-6) and nothing else.**
   The new doc states two things:
   - the behaviour: a Dioxus `disabled: false` leaves the element with no `disabled` attribute, so it does not match
     `:disabled`;
   - the guarded bug: dioxus-native-dom wrote a falsy `disabled` as the literal `disabled="false"`, and blitz-dom keys
     the DISABLED element state and `:disabled` on the attribute's presence, so every enabled Dioxus control was styled
     and stated disabled.

   It contains no word `focus` in any form. The test body (line 8 to the end) stays byte-identical.

2. **Create `scripts/agent-run.sh`, executable.** It follows `ci-leg.sh`'s shape: `#!/usr/bin/env bash`,
   `set -euo pipefail`, a `VERBS=(boot run status cleanup logs)` array, a `usage()` to stderr, one `case` per verb, and
   it is invoked from the project root (research.md §Patterns detected, `ci-leg.sh:8-64`).
   - State lives in `target/agent-run/` only: `status.json`, `events.jsonl` and `run.log`. It reads no env var of its
     own, and every cargo call carries `--locked`.
   - JSON is produced by a real encoder (`python3` and its `json` module, which the `ci-scripts` leg already requires),
     never by string concatenation (Constraints).
   - It keeps a no-op `ensure_fresh_artifacts` function with a comment, called first in `boot` (setup's hook, read by
     its U10 detector).

   The contract, fixed here because the wrap writes it into test-plan §3:
   - **Exit grammar, every verb:** `0` success · `1` the verb ran and failed (build failure, a failing or empty run) ·
     `2` usage (missing or unknown verb, unknown selection) · `3` a precondition is unmet (not booted, nothing to read).
   - **`boot`** — runs `ensure_fresh_artifacts`. Then it recreates `target/agent-run/` and truncates `events.jsonl`
     and `run.log`. Then it builds every blitz-tests test binary with `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --no-run`,
     merged output to `run.log`. It writes `status.json` (`booted`, `boot_ts`, `head` — `git rev-parse HEAD` or null
     outside a repository) and prints and appends one event: `{"event": "boot", "ts", "outcome": "ready"|"failed",
     "cargo_exit", "head"}`. Exit 0 on ready, 1 on failed (a failed boot leaves `booted` false).
   - **`run {selection}`** — requires a ready boot (else exit 3). `{selection}` is one of:
     - `stand` — every `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_*.rs` file present, each as `--test {name}`;
     - `all` — the whole blitz-tests package, no `--test`;
     - `{name}` — one blitz-tests file, with `name` matching `^[a-z0-9_]+$` and `tests/blitz-tests/tests/{name}.rs`
       existing.

     Anything else exits 2. It runs `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked [--test …]`. The merged output is written to
     `run.log`, truncated at the run's start. `status.json`'s run state is `running` during the run and `passed` or
     `failed` after it. It parses libtest's pretty lines (`Running {target} (…)`, `Doc-tests {crate}`,
     `test {name} ... ok|FAILED|ignored`) into events, each printed to stdout and appended to `events.jsonl`:
     - `{"event": "run.start", "ts", "selection", "files": [...]}`;
     - one `{"event": "test", "file", "test", "outcome": "ok"|"failed"|"ignored"}` per test line, where `file` is the
       target's stem (`stand_boot`) or `doc:{crate}`;
     - `{"event": "run.end", "ts", "selection", "passed", "failed", "ignored", "cargo_exit", "outcome": "passed"|"failed"}`.

     `outcome` is `passed` only when cargo exited 0, `failed` is 0 and at least one test event was parsed. Otherwise it
     is `failed` and the verb exits 1: an empty result is never a pass (test-plan history, 2026-10-05-ci-gate-legs,
     where `llvm-cov report` exited 0 on an empty table).
   - **`status`** — prints one JSON object, `{"event": "status", "booted", "boot_ts", "head", "run": {"selection",
     "state": "none"|"running"|"passed"|"failed", "passed", "failed", "ignored"}}`, built from `status.json`. Exit 0
     when booted and 3 when not (no `status.json`, or `booted` false). It never builds or runs anything.
   - **`cleanup`** — removes `target/agent-run/` if present and prints `{"event": "cleanup", "outcome": "done"}`. It is
     idempotent (exit 0 on a clean tree) and never touches anything else under `target/`.
   - **`logs`** — prints `events.jsonl` verbatim, one JSON object per line. Exit 3 when it is absent. Raw cargo output
     stays in `run.log` and is never printed by `logs`.

3. **Create `scripts/agent-run.ps1`, a thin wrapper.** A comment names it as the Windows entry and lists the five
   verbs. It passes every argument unchanged to `bash "$PSScriptRoot/agent-run.sh"` and exits with bash's exit code.
   It contains no contract logic (leaned per the operator's fork answer; Constraints).

5. **Run the new contract live once** through the gate entries below (cleanup → status → boot → status → run stand →
   logs checks → run all → a11y count → cleanup ×2). Record nothing by hand. The gate tool's trail is the record.
- `scripts/agent-run.sh` — the five-verb contract (step 2), executable
- `scripts/agent-run.ps1` — the Windows wrapper (step 3)
- `.github/scripts/test_agent_run.py` — the shim-driven contract tests (step 4)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/dioxus_falsy_disabled.rs` — the `//!` doc only (step 1)
The gates below run in /implement P2 and the wrap's light gate.

- The contract tests run first, under a cargo shim. Then the contract runs live against the real cargo, in block
  order: cleanup first, so a prior run's residue cannot satisfy a later status read. Every status read follows an
  entry of this block that set its state.
- No entry relies on a `timeout` exit (verification-harness.md Session Additions, 2026-10-06).

- The census probes set their base at `913f5918`, the commit this chunk starts from, so they survive the operator's
  pre-CI commit.
- Health check 13 itself is the witness that both scripts exist, the `.sh` is executable and both name the five verbs.
- No `audit` entry: `Cargo.lock` is unchanged, and an entry below guards that.
- No boot smoke of a binary: no binary changes.
- The operator entries push this chunk and read the CI run whose `ci-scripts` job runs the new tests on the runner.

body: - **No query run — no Rust symbol is created, changed or called anew.** The only Rust edit is a `//!` doc comment. The new surface is bash, PowerShell and Python, and the graph indexes only the `rust` plane. derived-without-graph for those files.
- **`seven_guis::stand::{boot, boot_timer, options}`** — unchanged and not called by the new scripts. The scripts drive cargo, which runs the existing `stand_*.rs` checks.

- **Shell-entrypoint tests through a cargo shim** (`.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py:204-260`). This proves exit and log contracts with no real cargo run. It runs in the `ci-scripts` leg, which discovers `.github/scripts/test_*.py` (`ci-leg.sh:22`).
- **Harness writes under `target/`.** `target/ci-logs/` and `target/coverage/` are the registered precedent (arch §Occupied Resources → Filesystem). `target/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:1,22`).
- **`--locked` on every cargo call** (`ci-leg.sh:19-39`; architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD).
- **One-file selection recipe**: `cargo test -p blitz-tests --test {name}` (`.claude/rules/testing.md` §Running tests). Several `--test` flags in one call are accepted (`ci-leg.sh:34`, the a11y leg).
- **Integration-test `//!` doc names the behaviour and the guarded bug** (`.claude/rules/testing.md` §File and naming conventions). The PREREQ rewrite keeps that form.
- **Python tests in `.github/scripts`**: one `TestCase` per function under test, stdlib `unittest`, a temp dir per case (`test_ci_workflows.py:204-260`; testing.md §Framework).

- `scripts/agent-run.sh` — the five verbs (boot, run, status, cleanup, logs), the JSON-line output, the state area under `target/`, and an `ensure_fresh_artifacts` hook (setup's U10 detector reads it).
- `scripts/agent-run.ps1` — the PowerShell counterpart. Its form is a P4 fork; every branch except dropping it creates this file.
- `.github/scripts/test_agent_run.py` — the shim-driven contract tests for `scripts/agent-run.sh`, discovered by the `ci-scripts` leg.
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/dioxus_falsy_disabled.rs` — the `//!` doc only (PREREQ).

- The PowerShell script cannot be run on this host. `pwsh` is absent: `command -v pwsh` printed nothing, while `jq`, `python3`, `timeout` and `flock` are present. Windows is tested in CI only through `matrix_test`'s direct cargo call. → blocks: plan-decision (the ps1's form, and how its contract is checked).

**Working entry (verbatim):** Stand test contract — agent-invocable boot, run, status, cleanup and JSON-line logs for stand checks and blitz-tests (per test-plan §3)  PREREQ: correct the `//!` doc of `tests/blitz-tests/tests/dioxus_falsy_disabled.rs` (from 2026-10-06-headless-stand) — it says a `disabled="false"` Dioxus control was "dropped from the focus order"; focusability parses the value as a bool and never excluded it, only the DISABLED state, `:disabled` and click targeting key on presence (measured at blitz-dom `element.rs:629` vs `:446-451`, that chunk's report and a11y-plan §5); the wrap touches no source

**Epoch:** Epoch 1 — Foundation · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Freight on the entry:** one block — line 21 `PREREQ:` (455 chars, `route.py pins`); the tail's other three blocks (line 35 `CARRY:` on "Snapshot state fidelity", line 52 `CARRY:` on "Driver command spans", line 72 `CARRY:` on "Quality gates") are not on this entry.

An agent gets one fixed, documented way to drive the stand checks and blitz-tests without knowing cargo's or the test harness's details: five commands (boot, run, status, cleanup, logs) whose outputs and exits are machine-readable, with JSON-line logs. This is the "5-command discipline" test-plan §3 records as NOT YET MEASURED, and `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` and `.claude/docs/tests-summary.md` assign it to this entry. It is also the harness health check 13 reports missing, since Development Style is agent-driven and `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` do not exist (new-session dashboard, 2026-10-06).

- **boot** — makes the stand ready to run headlessly: whatever has to exist before a check runs (built test binaries, a fresh per-invocation temp area) exists, and it reports ready or not-ready with a non-zero exit on failure. The headless stand is in-process: `seven_guis::stand::boot` runs over `Harness` with no daemon, socket or window, and `stand.rs` has 0 `escher_telemetry|env::var|println` hits (research.md §Files inspected). So "boot" cannot mean "start a daemon and poll its status endpoint", which is what the setup template's skeleton assumes. Concretely, boot builds the test binaries and opens the state area; P4 fixes the details.

- **run** — runs a named selection: the stand checks (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_*.rs`, 5 files), one blitz-tests file, or the whole blitz-tests suite. It returns an exit that distinguishes pass from fail and emits per-test outcomes an agent can parse. On stable, libtest's `--format json` exits 101 with "only accepted on the nightly compiler with -Z unstable-options" (measured at P3, research.md §Patterns). libtest's pretty output — `Running tests/{file}.rs`, `test {name} ... ok|FAILED|ignored`, `test result: …` — is the per-test channel, recorded at `evidence/p3-stand-run.log`. No test-runner crate is needed.

- **status** — reports whether a boot is ready and the state of the last run (running / passed / failed, with counts) without re-running anything. Non-zero when nothing is booted (the template's validation check 1).
- **cleanup** — removes everything boot and run created (temp area, status/PID files, any stray child process) and is idempotent: it succeeds on an already-clean tree.

- **logs** — returns the run's log as JSON lines, one object per line. escher's only sink writes a one-line TEXT format to stderr (obs-plan §3). The headless stand installs no subscriber: verified, `stand.rs` has 0 `escher_telemetry` hits, and arch §Standard Contracts → Headless stand requires that it keep installing none. So no escher sink is present in a stand-check process for a JSON format to reach. The JSON-line log is harness-level: the script writes one JSON event per test and per command. Its schema is P4's, its field names stay off the content-named scrub set, and it carries no captured test output (CLAUDE.md: add no new user-content log fields).

- **The script surface** — `scripts/agent-run.sh` (+ `agent-run.ps1`), the five verbs as words in both (health check 13's criterion). `[premise-corrected: setup Phase 4 is only-if-missing and calls the harness project-evolvable — andromeda-setup-project/SKILL.md:220-231]` The scripts are authored by this chunk's implement, not generated: setup preserves an existing `scripts/agent-run.*` and never re-renders over it. The rule's "then the scripts are generated" wording is a wrap amendment of `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`. The `.ps1`'s form is a P4 fork, because `pwsh` is absent on this host.

- **PREREQ — correct the regression test's doc.** `tests/blitz-tests/tests/dioxus_falsy_disabled.rs:1-6` (coordinates re-verified at take-up). Line 2 says the enabled control "stays focusable", and lines 5-6 say blitz-dom "keys disabled-ness on the attribute's presence, so every enabled Dioxus control was styled disabled and dropped from the focus order". The doc is corrected so that it claims only the defect the fix removed. A doc-only change; the test body is untouched.
  - The PREREQ's mechanism claim, kept verbatim with its marker: "focusability parses the value as a bool and never excluded it, only the DISABLED state, `:disabled` and click targeting key on presence (measured at blitz-dom `element.rs:629` vs `:446-451`, that chunk's report and a11y-plan §5)". VERIFIED at HEAD (research.md): `element.rs:629` uses `attr_parsed` with `unwrap_or(false)`, `:449` inserts `DISABLED` on `has_attr`, and `pointer.rs:330,457` check presence.
  - Found at P3: the test body asserts no focusability. It checks only attribute presence and `:disabled` matching. So the doc's line-2 "stays focusable" claims something the test does not prove, and it is removed along with the focus-order clause (a11y-plan §8: no test asserts a Dioxus control's focusability).

- In: the five commands, their output/exit contract, the JSON-line log, the scripts, the PREREQ doc fix, and the checks proving the commands work (at minimum: status non-zero before boot, boot → run → status → logs → cleanup round-trip on the stand checks, cleanup idempotent).
- Out: the stand checks' content (the headless stand, complete), new stand checks, and the stand's a11y/contrast/keyboard harnesses (Epoch 6).

- **Base commit:** 1ff57e3c4b282ef95fdfb2be7e0e2d564e609d48 (HEAD at P4; the commit this chunk starts from)

escher gets one telemetry bootstrap, a new library crate `escher-telemetry`, that every escher binary installs at
start. The stand (`seven_guis_native`) adopts it in this chunk. The driver CLI and MCP server adopt it when their
entries land. One init call installs a global `tracing` subscriber with these properties:
- it writes to **stderr, never stdout**, since stdout is reserved for the driver CLI's JSON and MCP's stdio;
- every line it writes carries the binary's **service identity** (`service.name` / `service.version`);
- a **panic hook** logs each panic as a `tracing` error event and then chains the previous hook;

- the **scrub** is an allowlist applied in the formatter. Events from engine targets keep only their level, target,
  location and known non-content fields, and content-named fields of any target are redacted.

This discharges obs-plan §3 Bootstrap phases `pii-scrubbing-wire` and security-plan §Bootstrap phases
`logging-redaction-wire`, and replaces the per-app stdout `fmt::init()` pattern for escher's own binaries (per
obs-plan §3 Logging stack, §7 Panic hooks, §8 PII Scrubbing; security-plan §Logging & Monitoring, §Error Handling).

**The working entry's "opt-in OTel export" is DEFERRED** (overseer, under the founder's standing delegation of
technical forks, 2026-10-06; scope.md). The exporter would add outbound egress, and it reads
`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` unconditionally (opentelemetry-otlp 0.33.0 `exporter/http/mod.rs:293-297`, research.md).
That is a boundary widening (playbook "Boundary widening", verdict escalate), so it reaches the founder before it
ships. This chunk adds **no** OTel crate, no network egress and no credential path. `otel-sdk-install` rides a route
CARRY to "Driver command spans" (§Implementation notes). The identity keys are the OTel resource keys, so a later
exporter reuses them unchanged.

1. **Create the crate `packages/escher-telemetry`.**
   - `Cargo.toml`: `name = "escher-telemetry"`, `publish = false`, every metadata key `*.workspace = true`, no
     `[features]` section.
   - Dependencies: `tracing = { workspace = true }`, `tracing-subscriber = { workspace = true, features =
     ["env-filter", "fmt", "registry", "std", "tracing-log"] }`, `tracing-log` (as the workspace already locks it,
     0.2.0) only if the `LogTracer` install needs a direct import. No other dependency.
   - Register it:
     - add `"packages/escher-telemetry"` to `[workspace] members` in the root `Cargo.toml`;
     - add `escher-telemetry = { path = "./packages/escher-telemetry" }` to `[workspace.dependencies]` beside
       `blitz-test-harness` (Cargo.toml:58), per architecture §Conventions → Manifests;
     - if `tracing-log` is a direct dependency, add a `tracing-log = "0.2"` entry to `[workspace.dependencies]`;
     - run `cargo update -p escher-telemetry --offline` or a plain build, so `Cargo.lock` records the path crate and
       nothing else changes (no registry version moves).
   - `src/lib.rs` carries `//!` crate docs, `///` on every public item, and `#![deny(missing_docs)]`. The `doc` leg
     denies warnings over every library crate.

2. **Service identity** (`src/lib.rs`):
   - a `ServiceIdentity { name: &'static str, version: &'static str }`;
   - a declarative macro `escher_telemetry::service_identity!()` expanding to
     `ServiceIdentity { name: env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME"), version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") }`. It expands in the
     CALLER's crate, so the values come from the binary's own manifest and are never hand-typed.

3. **Init API** (`src/lib.rs`):
   - `pub fn init(identity: ServiceIdentity) -> Result<InitOutcome, InitError>` installs the default sink, stderr.
   - `pub fn init_with_writer<W>(identity, writer: W) -> Result<InitOutcome, InitError>` takes a
     `tracing_subscriber::fmt::MakeWriter` for tests, or a caller that names a file it opened.
   - Both build a `Registry` with:
     - an `EnvFilter` from `RUST_LOG`, defaulting to `warn` when unset or unparsable;
     - one `fmt` layer using the formatter of step 5, `with_ansi(false)`, and the given writer.

     They call `set_global_default`, install `tracing_log::LogTracer` so `log`-facade records (e.g. `js_console`)
     reach the same scrubbed formatter, and install the panic hook of step 4.
   - Idempotence: a process-wide `OnceLock<ServiceIdentity>` records the first successful init.
     - A second call returns `Ok(InitOutcome::AlreadyInstalled)` without touching the subscriber or the hook.
     - A call that finds a global subscriber someone ELSE installed returns
       `Err(InitError::ForeignSubscriber)`.
     - `InitError` is an enum with `Display` and `std::error::Error`, per architecture §Conventions → Error
       handling, and never panics.
   - The first line written after a successful init is an `info` event at target `escher_telemetry` that reports
     the identity. It carries no argv, no path and no URL.

4. **Panic hook** (`src/panic.rs`):
   - `install()` takes the previous hook with `std::panic::take_hook()` and sets a new hook that:
     1. emits ONE `tracing::error!` event at target `escher_telemetry::panic`, with fields `panic.file`,
        `panic.line`, `panic.column` (from `PanicHookInfo::location`) and `panic.payload` (the `&str`/`String`
        payload, the shape `wpt/runner/src/panic_backtrace.rs:22-28` reads);
     2. then calls the previous hook with the same info.
   - The default hook's stderr output and the process exit code are unchanged.
   - `panic.payload` is a content field (step 5), so the sink shows its redaction marker. The chained default hook
     still prints the raw message to stderr: that is std's own output, not a log event.
   - Installed once, inside the idempotent init.

5. **Formatter and allowlist scrub** (`src/format.rs`):
   - A `FormatEvent` implementation writes one line per event: `{RFC 3339 UTC time} {LEVEL} {target}
     service.name={name} service.version={version} {fields}`.
   - A field visitor decides per field:
     - **(a) Engine target.** The event's target, or its `log.target` for a bridged `log` record, starts with one of
       the engine prefixes: `blitz`, `dioxus_native`, `stylo_taffy`, `accesskit_xplat`, `debug_timer`,
       `js_console`. Then only fields in the safe set print their value: `node_id`, `status`, `waiting_nodes`,
       `property`, `log.module_path`, `log.file`, `log.line`. Every other field, `message` included, prints as
       `{name}=[redacted]`.
     - **(b) Content field of any target.** For any target, a field whose name is in the content set prints as
       `{name}=[redacted]`. The content set: `url`, `href`, `src`, `html`, `text`, `value`, `attrs`, `path`,
       `request`, `error`, `panic.payload`.
     - **(c) Everything else** prints normally.
   - The two sets and the prefix list are `pub const` slices with `///` docs, so a reviewer reads them in one
     place. Their derivation is research.md §Patterns detected (the named-field sites) and obs-plan §8 "Values
     logged as-is".

6. **Stand adoption:**
   - `examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml`: add `escher-telemetry = { workspace = true }` under the existing
     `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]`.
   - `examples/seven_guis/src/main.rs`: inside the native `main`, BEFORE `dioxus_native::launch` (the one call site
     of `launch @ examples/seven_guis/src/main.rs:6` this chunk touches — research.md §Graph impact), call
     `escher_telemetry::init(escher_telemetry::service_identity!())`.
     - On `Err`, it reports the error with `eprintln!` and continues to `launch`. Telemetry failure never blocks the
       stand.
     - The wasm `main` and `lib.rs`'s wasm entry (`console_error_panic_hook::set_once()` at lib.rs:13) are not
       edited.
   - The stand's engine `tracing` features stay off: `dioxus-native/tracing` is not enabled.

7. **Integration tests**, one file per behaviour in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/`. Each file is its own process, which
   isolates the global installs (architecture §Conventions → Tests; test-plan §5).
   - Setup:
     - add `escher-telemetry = { workspace = true }` and `tracing = { workspace = true }` to
       `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml` `[dev-dependencies]`;
     - each file opens with a `//!` naming its behaviour;
     - every assertion is unconditional (test-plan §4 anti-pattern);
     - sentinels are literal fixtures such as `ESCHER-SENTINEL-7f3a`, never real PII.
   - The four files:
     - `telemetry_stdout_silent.rs` — a parent `#[test]` spawns `std::env::current_exe()` with args
       `--ignored --exact child_emits --nocapture`. The child `#[test] #[ignore] fn child_emits` calls `init` with
       the stderr sink and emits a `warn!` carrying the sentinel in an escher-owned target's non-content field. The
       parent asserts that the child exited 0, that its stderr contains the sentinel and
       `service.name=blitz-tests`, and that its stdout does NOT contain the sentinel. libtest's own harness lines
       are on stdout, so the assertion is "the sentinel is absent from stdout", not "stdout is empty".
     - `telemetry_scrub.rs` — `init_with_writer` with an in-memory `MakeWriter` (a hand-written recording writer,
       test-plan §8 pattern). It emits:
       - an event at target `blitz_dom::mutator` whose message interpolates the sentinel;
       - an event at target `blitz_net` with `url = sentinel` and `status = 404`;
       - an event at an escher target with `html = sentinel`;
       - a `log::debug!(target: "js_console", …)` record carrying the sentinel.

       It asserts that the captured output contains none of the sentinels, contains `[redacted]` for each, and
       still contains `status=404`. The filter is `RUST_LOG` unset → `warn`, so the test emits at `warn` or above;
       the `js_console` record is emitted at `warn` for the test.
     - `telemetry_panic_hook.rs` — install a sentinel previous hook first, which sets a static `AtomicBool`, then
       `init_with_writer` with a recording writer, then `std::panic::catch_unwind` around a `panic!("{sentinel}")`.
       It asserts:
       - exactly one captured line at target `escher_telemetry::panic`, with `panic.file` and `panic.line`
         present;
       - `panic.payload=[redacted]`, and the sentinel absent from the captured output;
       - the `AtomicBool` set, so the previous hook ran.
     - `telemetry_init_idempotent.rs` — the first `init_with_writer` returns `Ok(Installed)` and the second returns
       `Ok(AlreadyInstalled)`; neither panics. After the second call, an emitted event appears exactly once in the
       capture (no doubled subscriber).

8. **Unit tests** inline in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (architecture §Conventions → Tests):
   - `src/format.rs`: the decision function, given (target, field name), returns redact / print for each branch
     (a)–(c), plus a `log.target` bridge case;
   - `src/lib.rs`: `service_identity!()` expands to this crate's own `CARGO_PKG_NAME` and version.
- `packages/escher-telemetry/Cargo.toml` — the crate manifest (workspace-inherited metadata, no features)
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs` — identity, `init` / `init_with_writer`, `InitOutcome`, `InitError`
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/panic.rs` — the chaining panic hook
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs` — the event formatter and the allowlist scrub sets
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/telemetry_stdout_silent.rs` — the stderr-not-stdout proof
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/telemetry_scrub.rs` — the scrub proof
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/telemetry_panic_hook.rs` — the panic-hook proof
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/telemetry_init_idempotent.rs` — the idempotence proof
- `Cargo.toml` — workspace member + `[workspace.dependencies]` entry (the new crate; `tracing-log` only if a direct dependency)
- `Cargo.lock` — the path crate recorded; no registry crate added or moved
- `examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml` — native-target dependency on `escher-telemetry`
- `examples/seven_guis/src/main.rs` — the init call before `launch`
- `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml` — dev-dependencies `escher-telemetry`, `tracing`

- `examples/seven_guis/src/main.rs` (full). The native `main` calls only `dioxus_native::launch(seven_guis::app::app)` at line 6. It installs no subscriber and no panic hook. The wasm `main` is empty.

The workspace dep sets `default-features = false`, so **the stand does not turn on `dioxus-native/tracing`**: engine `tracing` call sites are compiled out of the stand by default (`cargo tree -p seven_guis -e features -i tracing` reaches `tracing` only through winit / winit-common, never through a blitz `tracing` feature).

- `Cargo.toml` (1-60, dependency lines). Members list (26, no escher crate). The workspace deps `tracing = "0.1.40"`, `tracing-subscriber = "0.3"` (line 184), `tokio = "1.42"`, `reqwest = { version = "0.13", default-features = false }` and `http = "1.1.0"`. Root dev-deps `env_logger = "0.11"` and `tracing-subscriber = "0.3"` (lines 285-286).

Locked versions: tracing 0.1.44, tracing-core 0.1.36, tracing-subscriber 0.3.23, tracing-log 0.2.0, log 0.4.34, reqwest 0.13.4, hyper 1.11.1, tokio 1.53.1, http 1.5.0, rustls 0.23.45. **No `opentelemetry*`, `tonic` or `prost` crate is locked** (re-derived: `awk` over `name = "…"` stanzas of Cargo.lock).

- `apps/browser/src/main.rs:74`, `apps/readme/src/main.rs:62`, `examples/todomvc/src/main.rs:17` — each calls `tracing_subscriber::fmt::init()` under its own `#[cfg(feature = "tracing")]`, with the default fmt writer (stdout). `wpt/runner/src/main.rs:458-459` calls `env_logger::init()` + `std::panic::set_hook(stash_panic_handler)` (re-derived: `grep -rn 'tracing_subscriber|set_global_default|env_logger::|LogTracer|set_hook|take_hook'` over apps packages examples wpt tests — 5 hits, no other install).

- `wpt/runner/src/panic_backtrace.rs` (1-40). This is the precedent hook. It captures message (from a `&str` or `String` payload), file, line, column and a forced backtrace into a thread-local. It **replaces** the hook rather than chaining it.

- `packages/blitz-net/Cargo.toml` (lines 14-38). blitz-net enables `reqwest` with `native-tls` (normal) and `native-tls-vendored` (target-specific). The stand does not pull blitz-net, since `dioxus-native/net` is off in the stand.

- `opentelemetry-otlp-0.33.0/src/exporter/http/mod.rs` (280-305, 780) and `src/exporter/mod.rs` (152-170, 299-301, 424-430). These are the exporter's implicit env reads, quoted under Patterns detected.

- **launch** (`dioxus-native/src/lib.rs`) has 19 callers. The one this chunk touches is `seven_guis main()` @ `examples/seven_guis/src/main.rs:6`. The bootstrap call goes before it, so no signature changes and no caller threading is needed.
- **crate_edges for seven_guis**: outbound to `blitz-dom` and `dioxus-native`, no inbound. The stand is a leaf, so adding a dependency on the new crate gives zero cross-crate blast radius.

- **Name collision** (`symbol WHERE name LIKE 'telemetry%' OR LIKE 'escher%' OR = 'scrub' OR LIKE 'init_tracing%'`): 0 rows on the rust plane. The rust plane built (db_state in the trace), and the names searched are new, so the rows count is a genuine "free" (trace: `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-06T00-14-27-phase/tree-query-2026-10-06-telemetry-bootstrap.json`).

- **Feature-gated subscriber install** (`apps/browser/src/main.rs:73-74`; `examples/todomvc/src/main.rs:16-17`): the app's own `tracing` feature gates `tracing_subscriber::fmt::init()`. `fmt::init()` writes to **stdout** by default (`fmt::Layer` writer is `io::stdout`). It also calls `try_init`, which installs `tracing_log::LogTracer` when the resolved `tracing-log` feature is on, and it is on in this workspace (`cargo tree --workspace -e features -i tracing-subscriber` lists `tracing-log`, `env-filter`, `fmt`, `ansi`, `registry`). So a `log`-facade record such as `js_console` reaches the subscriber.

- **The OTLP exporter reads env vars implicitly**, and that cannot be switched off through its API. `opentelemetry-otlp 0.33.0` `exporter/http/mod.rs:293-297` reads `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_{TRACES_}HEADERS` **unconditionally** at `build()`, after any explicit headers, and merges them in. `:780` reads `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` when no endpoint is set explicitly. `exporter/mod.rs:299-301, 424-430` read `…_INSECURE` and `…_TIMEOUT`. The headers variable is the standard place an OTLP auth token travels, so turning export on opens a **credential path**.

- **Process-global installs**: a global default subscriber can be set once per process (`set_global_default` errors on the second call), and `std::panic::set_hook` replaces whatever was there. Idempotence, and chaining via `take_hook`, are the bootstrap's to provide. Neither exists in-repo.

- **Workspace-inherited manifests**: in-repo crates are declared in `[workspace.dependencies]` with a `path` and consumed with `{ workspace = true }` (Cargo.toml:43-58). Package metadata comes from `[workspace.package]` (Cargo.toml:32-39; e.g. `examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml:5`).

- **Optional capability = Cargo feature** (`packages/dioxus-native/Cargo.toml:67`; `packages/blitz-dom/Cargo.toml:23`). OTel export goes behind a non-default feature of the new crate, and the stand's default build must not resolve it.

- **Engine `tracing` gating stays**: call sites are `#[cfg(feature = "tracing")]` with a no-op fallback (`packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs:131-139`). Any call site this chunk edits keeps its gate.

- **Integration tests** are one file per behaviour in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/` (59 files today, re-derived: `ls tests/blitz-tests/tests | wc -l`), each its own test binary. That gives process isolation for global-subscriber and panic-hook tests.

- **CI legs** go through `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh` (test leg `cargo test --workspace --locked` at line 21, default features; msrv leg `cargo +1.91 build --workspace --locked` at line 24). The leg list is pinned by `.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py`.
- `opentelemetry` / `opentelemetry_sdk` / `opentelemetry-otlp` 0.33.0, `tracing-opentelemetry` 0.34.0 — rust-version 1.75.0 each, ≤ the workspace's 1.91 (`cargo info`).

- `opentelemetry-otlp` requires `reqwest ^0.13.1` (locked 0.13.4 ✓), `http ^1.1` (1.5.0 ✓), `prost ^0.14`, `tokio ^1` (optional). `tracing-opentelemetry` requires `tracing-subscriber ^0.3.22` (0.3.23 ✓), `tracing-log ^0.2.0` (✓) (crates.io `/api/v1/crates/{c}/{v}/dependencies`). Newly locked crates: `opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry_sdk`, `opentelemetry-otlp`, `opentelemetry-proto`, `opentelemetry-http`, `tracing-opentelemetry`, `prost` (+ derive), and their small transitive helpers. **None touches a coupled pin** (html5ever family, skrifa, svgtypes, taffy/parley, winit).

- Transport: `http-proto` + `reqwest-blocking-client` posts over reqwest's blocking client, which runs its own internal runtime thread, so no ambient tokio runtime is needed before `launch`. The workspace's `reqwest` is `default-features = false`, so **with no TLS feature added, export reaches `http://` endpoints only**. `https` needs a reqwest TLS feature (blitz-net's choice is `native-tls`).
- `packages/escher-telemetry/Cargo.toml` — the bootstrap crate (lib), `otel` feature off by default
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs` — the init entry point, service identity, sink choice, typed init error
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/scrub.rs` — the scrub layer
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/panic.rs` — the chaining panic hook
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs` — the event formatter: identity prefix + the allowlist scrub applied per field
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/telemetry_stdout_silent.rs` — an emitted event reaches stderr, its sentinel never stdout
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/telemetry_scrub.rs` — sentinel values in engine-target messages and fields, and in content fields of any target, never reach the sink
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/telemetry_panic_hook.rs` — a panic logs one error event and the previous hook still runs
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/telemetry_init_idempotent.rs` — a second init is harmless
- `Cargo.toml` — workspace member + the new crate's `[workspace.dependencies]` entry
- `Cargo.lock` — the new path crate recorded (no registry crate added)
- `examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml` — depend on the bootstrap crate (native target)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/main.rs` — call the bootstrap before `launch`
- `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml` — dev-dependency on the bootstrap crate

- none. All three were decided at P4 (overseer, under the founder's standing delegation of technical forks, 2026-10-06). Scrub reach is the allowlist at the subscriber (no engine edits). OTel export is DEFERRED, so the transport and headers questions pass to the CARRY's owner, "Driver command spans", for the founder.
**Working entry (verbatim):** Telemetry bootstrap — tracing subscriber, opt-in OTel export, service identity, panic logging, scrub layer; logs never on stdout (per obs-plan §3 §8)

**Epoch:** Epoch 1 — Foundation · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Freight on the entry:** none (`route.py pins` — the only freight block on the markerless tail is line 72's `CARRY:`, on "Quality gates", not this entry)

escher gets one telemetry bootstrap that every escher binary — the stand, and later the driver CLI and MCP server — installs at start. Today each app calls `tracing_subscriber::fmt::init()` on its own, which writes to stdout. There is no OTel SDK, no service identity, no panic logging outside WASM and the WPT runner, and no scrubbing (obs-plan §3, §7, §8; the obs-plan bootstrap contract labels `otel-sdk-install` and `pii-scrubbing-wire`).
- **Tracing subscriber** — one init entry point that installs a global `tracing` subscriber with an env-filter level, idempotent and safe to call twice.

- **Logs never on stdout** — the subscriber writes to stderr (or a file the caller names), never stdout. Stdout belongs to the driver CLI's JSON (working-route "Driver CLI") and to MCP's stdio transport ("MCP surface").

- **Service identity** — every event the sink writes carries the service name and version (`service.name` / `service.version`, the OTel resource keys an exporter will reuse). The values are read from the binary, not hand-typed.
- **Panic logging** — a panic hook logs the panic message and location as a `tracing` error event, then chains the previous hook so the default output and exit code don't change.

- **Scrub layer** — log fields that carry user content are redacted before they reach any sink: URLs, attribute values, outer HTML, text content and CSS values (obs-plan §8's list). This closes the CLAUDE.md invariant "no scrub layer exists yet".

- **Opt-in OTel export — DEFERRED at P4** (overseer, under the founder's standing delegation of technical forks, 2026-10-06). The exporter's outbound egress and its unconditional `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` read are a boundary widening (playbook "Boundary widening", verdict escalate) that must reach the founder. Nothing in escher-0.1.0 needs an exporter. This chunk ships no OTel crate, no egress and no credential path. The obs-plan bootstrap item `otel-sdk-install` is carried as a route CARRY on "Driver command spans" (Epoch 4), the first entry whose spans an exporter would carry. The founder decides http-only vs TLS before that entry is taken up. The identity design below keeps `service.name` / `service.version` ready for an OTel resource.
- In: the bootstrap itself, its tests, and adopting it in this repository's escher-owned binary entry points — the stand (`seven_guis_native`) at minimum.

- Out: new instrumentation (spans or metrics at engine call sites — obs-plan §4/§5 record no coverage target), SLO budgets (§10 has no recorded intent), and the driver's own logging (the Driver CLI and MCP chunks adopt the bootstrap when they exist).
- Out: re-plumbing upstream `blitz` apps (browser, rdme) and the WPT runner's `env_logger`, unless research shows it's free.
- Engine crates keep the invariant that `tracing` call sites are `#[cfg(feature = "tracing")]` with a no-op fallback. The bootstrap adds no unconditional `println!`.

- A new workspace crate holds the bootstrap. No escher-owned crate exists, and the name is free on the rust plane (research.md §Graph impact). A new crate, an env var (the opt-in and filter switches) and an outbound host (the OTel endpoint) are each an architecture §Occupied Resources registration (CLAUDE.md critical warning). The outbound export is a security-plan amendment (security rules §Surfaces — "a new socket … is an arch §Occupied Resources + security-plan amendment first").

- `[premise-corrected: opentelemetry-otlp 0.33.0 exporter/http/mod.rs:293-297 reads OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS unconditionally at build()]` OTel crates (`opentelemetry` / `opentelemetry_sdk` / `opentelemetry-otlp` 0.33, `tracing-opentelemetry` 0.34) enter `Cargo.lock` behind an optional feature, so the default build resolves none of them. Each is MSRV 1.75 and fits the locked reqwest 0.13.4, http 1.5.0 and tracing-subscriber 0.3.23. No coupled pin moves. They pass the cargo-deny audit leg and a hand review (security rules §Dependencies). One correction: turning export on also opens a **credential path**, because the SDK reads the standard headers variable whatever the caller sets. That path is a security-plan decision, not a side effect. **After the P4 deferral, none of these crates enters `Cargo.lock` this chunk.** The facts stand for the CARRY's owner. This chunk's registrations are the crate and the filter env read only, with no outbound host.

- `[premise-corrected: ≥19 engine call sites interpolate user content into the message string — research.md §Patterns detected]` A subscriber-level scrub over field names covers only the named fields (`url`, `error`, `html`, `value`, `path`). It does **not** cover existing call sites without edits. URLs, attribute values, text and request dumps are also formatted into the event message at blitz-dom, dioxus-native(-dom), blitz and blitz-vibey-script sites, and `js_console` arrives through the `log` bridge. P4 fork, decided (overseer, under the founder's standing delegation of technical forks, 2026-10-06): **allowlist at the subscriber**. Events whose target is an engine crate or the `js_console` log target keep their level, target, location and allowlisted non-content fields. Their message and every other field value are redacted. No engine call site is edited. In the stand's default build, engine `tracing` call sites are compiled out (`dioxus-native/tracing` is off), so they reach the stand's sink only when that feature is turned on.
- obs-plan §2/§3/§7/§8 are the as-built record this chunk changes. Wrap amends them (obs-plan is read-only here).

- `1ff57e3c` (the last wrap's flip, HEAD) — CI#37392748770: **verdict not yet available** (in progress, 4/4 checks open, oldest running "Test [default features]" at 128 s when read at 2026-10-06T00:14Z). No red or not-green to disposition. It is re-read at P5.
- Re-read at P5 (2026-10-06T00:32Z): `1ff57e3c` — CI#37392748770 **verdict: green**, checks 16/16, wall 599 s.

title: Plan — 2026-10-06-upstream-sync-element-identity: "Upstream sync ahead of element identity"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-06-upstream-sync-element-identity: "Upstream sync ahead of element identity"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-06-upstream-sync-element-identity · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-06T08:05:00Z
- **Chunk start commit:** `ab936a9e46ee19365929465444725a0bc837dbbc` (HEAD at P4; every git-diff base below names it or a fixed upstream sha)
- **Upstream pin:** `2335458530518cdf167c55ce635fae99323e0789` (inputs#I1, re-measured at P1 and P3) · merge base `0f60502ea724ef703b34220b3847bb3483f70b5f`

Merge DioxusLabs/blitz `upstream/main` at `23354585` (11 commits) into `build/escher-0.1.0` as a true merge (both parents kept), and prove our logic survived it. This is the first of the epoch-boundary syncs that `escher-0.1.0/intent.md` §Principles ("Upstream stays in reach") asks for: small and often, with our changes kept additive.

The proof is the full local gate as CI runs it, re-read after the merge. Per test-plan §9 Pipeline facts and arch §Stack and Technologies (Code quality), that means `ci-leg.sh fast`, `doc`, `audit` and `a11y`. On top of the gate:
- the five `stand_*` checks, the four `telemetry_*` checks, `dioxus_falsy_disabled` and `incremental_oracle`, which run inside `fast`
- the agent-run `run stand` (test-plan §3)
- a windowed boot of the stand
- fork CI green on the pushed merge commit
The upstream half is pre-verified at P3:
- The in-memory merge is conflict-free (tree `aed58ca8`).
- The auto-merged `Cargo.lock` resolves under `--locked`, with no crate added and one skrifa 0.44.0 beside parley `e41dfea5` and vello 0.11.0.
- The merged root manifest keeps every escher entry.
- The delta adds no log site, no `unsafe` and one test (`wpt/runner` `attr_test.rs`).

That leaves this chunk's risk in what only compiling and running the merged tree shows: fmt and clippy under `-D warnings` on our 1.99.0 host toolchain, rustdoc `-D warnings`, the Taffy, Parley and alignment behaviour under the stand's pinned font and viewport, and the incremental oracle (per arch §Design Philosophy, test-plan §2 Differential oracle).

1. **Pre-merge baseline (on `ab936a9e`, before any merge).** Run `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh test`. Write the per-binary `test result:` sum (the same `awk` the count gate entry uses) to `evidence/pre-merge-counts.txt`, together with the HEAD sha and the date. This is the number the post-merge count is compared against. The recorded 430 · 0 · 4 (test-plan §9, 2026-10-06-headless-stand) is NOT copied.

2. **Confirm the pin.** Check that `git rev-parse upstream/main` still reads `2335458530518cdf167c55ce635fae99323e0789`. If upstream has moved, merge the PIN anyway (scope §What it builds), and record both shas in `evidence/merge.md`.

3. **Merge without committing.** Run `git merge --no-ff --no-commit 2335458530518cdf167c55ce635fae99323e0789`.
   - The tree then holds the merge staged, with `MERGE_HEAD` set. /implement never commits. The operator's pre-CI commit later records this as the two-parent merge commit (§Implementation notes).
   - Check that the worktree equals the P3 trial tree: `git diff --quiet $(git merge-tree --write-tree ab936a9e46ee19365929465444725a0bc837dbbc 2335458530518cdf167c55ce635fae99323e0789)` over the code paths. Record this in `evidence/merge.md`.
   - A conflict here contradicts P3's measurement. HALT, and do not resolve it by hand.
4. **Run the gate block** (`## Test Commands`) on the merged, uncommitted tree.

5. **On a red gate.** The fix is the minimal edit to the named file, in upstream-owned code only where the merged code itself fails our gate (for example a clippy lint our toolchain fires on new upstream code). Record each fix:
   - as non-additive in `chunks/2026-10-06-upstream-sync-element-identity/scope-record.md` when the file is outside research's list
   - and in the report

   Never fix a red by:
   - moving one side of a coupled pin
   - running `cargo update`
   - re-baselining a stand check's expectations, the viewport, the font or the task CSS
   - narrowing the `a11y` leg

   Those reds HALT for the operator (§Constraints & rejected approaches).

6. **Evidence** under `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-upstream-sync-element-identity/evidence/`. Record:
   - `merge.md`: the pin, merge base, upstream commit list (`git log --oneline 0f60502e..23354585`) and the worktree-equals-trial-tree reading
   - `post-merge-counts.txt` (the count entry's line), and the difference from step 1, each delta traced to an upstream commit. Predicted: +1 passed, from `3aa87bc1` (#1067), `subtest_names_include_nonempty_root_titles`. Record what the run measures.
   - the agent-run `run.end` line
   - the lockfile summary: crate set unchanged, 7 `source` lines moved
   - the additivity report entry's listing

7. **Record the upstream API changes for later chunks** in the report, not in code:
   - `Node::inline_fragment_boxes` (#1060)
   - `BaseDocument::inline_fragment_rects` now returning `Option<impl Iterator<Item = BoundingRect>>`, whose callers @ `document.rs` 2231/2276/2335 and `blitz-paint/src/debug_overlay.rs:19` iterate and are compatible
   - the JS-only `document.children` binding (#1069)
- `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-upstream-sync-element-identity/evidence/` — pre- and post-merge counts, merge record, agent-run `run.end`, additivity listing
All 17 come from the merge itself (research.md §Files to modify). None is hand-edited unless step 5 fires.

- `Cargo.toml` — upstream's taffy `4142c9d8` / parley `e41dfea5` revs, with the escher member, path entries, `tracing-log` and `[profile.dev]` kept (graph: no escher caller; manifest consumers are every workspace crate)
- `Cargo.lock` — 7 git `source` lines (parley-repo ×6, taffy ×1), crate set unchanged

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/{cssom.rs, document.rs, layout/inline.rs, node/node.rs, node/text.rs}`:
  - `inline_fragment_rects` @ `document.rs:2231/2276/2335`, `debug_overlay.rs:19` (iterator return)
  - our two `node.rs` rustdoc fixes kept (lines 129, 1616 of the merged file)
- `packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs` — upstream paint changes
- `packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/{dom/document.rs, dom/element.rs, dom/node.rs, dom/stylesheet.rs, runtime.rs}` — upstream script DOM changes, including the `document.children` binding

- `packages/stylo_taffy/src/{convert.rs, wrapper.rs}`:
  - `default_item_alignment` changes signature; its 5 call sites @ `convert.rs:912/916` and `wrapper.rs:277/581/586` are all inside this upstream rewrite
  - new `oof_item_alignment`
- `wpt/WPT_COMMIT`, `wpt/runner/src/test_runners/attr_test.rs` — upstream WPT pin and the +1 unit test
The gates below run in /implement P2 (on the merged, uncommitted tree) and in the wrap's light gate (on the committed merge).

- **Merge witness and guards.** The first entry is the merge witness. It is green when upstream's pin is MERGE_HEAD (before the operator's commit) or an ancestor of HEAD (after it), and red on the untouched tree. The next eight probe the merged manifest, the lock, `.github/`, the package manifests and stand sources, and the upstream delta:
  - Their git bases are the chunk start commit `ab936a9e` or the fixed upstream shas, so they survive the pre-CI commit.
  - The additivity entry is report-only. It lists every code path whose content differs from the clean auto-merge, re-derived by `git merge-tree`, which is deterministic. Each listed path must be a recorded step-5 fix.
- **Gate legs.** `fast` is the local pre-push gate, and its `target/ci-logs/test.log` feeds the count entry. Then `doc`, `audit` and `a11y`, then the agent-run proof.

- **Windowed boot smoke.** It runs because blitz-paint `render.rs` and the Taffy and Parley pins change what `seven_guis_native` renders. It declares `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and reads `not run — env unset` without one. It turns `timeout`'s 124 into exit 0 (verification-harness.md Session Additions, 2026-10-06), and its atom comes from test-plan.md's Stand log format reading, as in 2026-10-06-headless-stand's plan.

- **Not listed locally.** The `msrv` leg (`cargo +1.91`) and the wasm leg run on CI only: this host has no 1.91 toolchain or wasm32 target (measured in 2026-10-06-telemetry-bootstrap's plan). P3 read every new dependency's rust-version as ≤ 1.91.0 (parley 1.88, vello 1.89, taffy 1.71). The operator entries push the merge and read the CI run that covers both legs.
- **No live leg.** This chunk drives no external process.

- **The pre-merge count has no listed producer, by construction.** `evidence/pre-merge-counts.txt` is read on `ab936a9e` before the merge. No gate can re-run it on the merged tree, so implementation step 1 produces it once, as a one-shot reading. The count entry and the report compare it against the post-merge reading.

- **Rebase our 16 commits onto upstream:** rejected. The branch is pushed and shared, and the global rules forbid force-pushing.
- **`git merge --squash`:** rejected. It drops upstream ancestry, so every later sync would re-merge these 11 commits and conflict against itself. That breaks "small and often".

- **A `git merge` that commits inside /implement:** rejected. /implement never moves history (plan-template §Test Commands, `leg`). The merge is staged with `--no-commit`, and the operator's pre-CI commit records it.

- **Moving one side of a coupled pin, or running `cargo update`, to quiet a build or audit red:** banned per arch §Established Decisions [Dependency pinning] and security-plan §Dependency Security. Such a red HALTs for the operator.

- **Re-baselining a stand expectation, the viewport, the font or the task CSS to absorb an upstream layout or text shift:** banned per layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native and test-plan §2 Font-dependent tests. A shifted stand check is a halt to name.
- **Re-gating or narrowing the `a11y` leg, or "fixing" the two-way `disabled` keying during conflict resolution:** banned per a11y-plan §9 and §5.
- **Adopting `Node::inline_fragment_boxes` or the iterator-returning `inline_fragment_rects` in escher code now:** out of scope. They are recorded for Snapshot model.

- **Committing the merge (operator pass).** With `MERGE_HEAD` set, the operator's pre-CI commit is the merge commit. Its subject must be the pipeline's `chore(2026-10-06-upstream-sync-element-identity): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads`, and the body names `Merge upstream/main 2335458530518cdf167c55ce635fae99323e0789 (11 commits)`. The wrap's scope and hygiene base, "the oldest pre-CI commit's parent", resolves to its FIRST parent, `ab936a9e`. So the 17 upstream files read as this chunk's change, which matches research's list.

- **Keep the merge state intact until that commit.** Between step 3 and the operator's commit, nothing may run `git stash`, `git merge --abort`, `git reset` or `git checkout -- .`, because each one discards `MERGE_HEAD` or the staged merge. If the state is lost, re-run step 3; the merge-witness entry catches the loss.

- **Expect a cold first CI run.** The Cargo.lock change re-keys every rust cache, and the cache was already over budget (2026-10-05-ci-gate-legs). A slow or cold first wall-clock is cache churn, not a regression.

- **The additivity report is self-producing.** Its base `$(git merge-tree --write-tree ab936a9e… 2335458…)` re-creates the deterministic clean-merge tree at every run, so it never depends on the P3 object surviving gc.

- **The count forecast is a prediction.** Predicted +1 passed (`3aa87bc1`, a `#[test]` in `wpt/runner`, which is a workspace member at `Cargo.toml:22`). The basis is `git diff 0f60502e 23354585 | grep '^[-+][^-+].*#\[test\]'`, which gives +1 / −0. Record what the post-merge run measures, and trace every other difference.
- **Escalate patterns:** `.andromeda/playbook.md` has one `verdict: escalate` pattern, Boundary widening. No option here widens a boundary: no new crossing, input class or channel.

title: The upstream delta (11 commits, from `git log 0f60502e..upstream/main`)

body: - Layout and dependency pins: Taffy bumps (#1061 auto margins beside floats, #1070 cyclic percentage grid contributions), `align-content` for block, inline and table (#1059), self-alignment of absolutely positioned boxes (#977), Taffy's `normal` alignment keyword in `stylo_taffy` (#1063), Parley bumped to latest main (#1065).

- DOM API: inline fragment rect computation moved onto `Node` (#1062). `Node::inline_fragment_boxes` exposed, and `BaseDocument::inline_fragment_rects` now returns an iterator (#1060). The JS `document.children` binding in blitz-vibey-script (#1069).
- WPT: the pin is updated (#1068), and root titles are included in native checkLayout subtest names (#1067). Upstream's WPT workflows are upstream-only on the fork, guarded by `github.repository`.

- Files: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, blitz-dom (`cssom.rs`, `document.rs`, `layout/inline.rs`, `node/node.rs`, `node/text.rs`), blitz-paint `render.rs`, blitz-vibey-script (`dom/{document,element,node,stylesheet}.rs`, `runtime.rs`), stylo_taffy (`convert.rs`, `wrapper.rs`), `wpt/WPT_COMMIT`, and `wpt/runner/src/test_runners/attr_test.rs`. No `.github/` file changed.

- **Overlap**, meaning files both sides changed since the base: `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs`. At take-up an in-memory `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD upstream/main` exited 0 with tree `aed58ca8`, which means no textual conflict. Our `node.rs` delta is two rustdoc link fixes from the real-rustdoc-gate work. `[premise-corrected: the delta adds one intra-doc link, `[item_alignment]` on `pub fn oof_item_alignment`, which resolves to a `pub fn` in the same `pub mod convert`. Our two `node.rs` doc fixes survive the merge (research.md)]` No new rustdoc warning source is visible statically. The `doc` leg (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`) on the merged tree remains the proof.

- **Coupled dependency pins** (CLAUDE.md Critical Warnings): upstream moves taffy `49152ca2` → `4142c9d8` and parley `718dcb72` → `e41dfea5`, and leaves skrifa at 0.44. The merge takes upstream's pins as one set. The parley bump keeps the skrifa/vello coupling within 0.44. Verified at P3: the merged lock holds one skrifa 0.44.0 beside parley 0.11.0 (`e41dfea5`) and vello 0.11.0, and `cargo metadata --locked` on the merged tree exits 0. A failure here at /implement is a halt, never a one-sided fix.

- **Additivity**: the merge introduces no NEW edit by us to upstream-owned code beyond what a conflict or a gate failure strictly requires. Any such fix is named, minimal, and recorded as non-additive. Our pre-existing fork changes to upstream crates (blitz-dom `traversal.rs`, `layout/replaced.rs`, `node/node.rs`; blitz-test-harness; dioxus-native-dom `mutation_writer.rs`; blitz-vibey-script `document.rs`) are carried as they are.

- `Cargo.lock` is not regenerated. The auto-merged lock resolves under `--locked` as it stands, and its crate name+version set is identical to HEAD's, with only 7 git `source` lines moving (P3). Builds stay `--locked`. The dependency audit leg (`ci-leg.sh audit`) runs because new git revs enter the graph (security rules §Dependencies).
- No new crate, port, env var or listener (arch §Occupied Resources unchanged).
- Any element-identity work (Stable element ids and later entries).
- Bumping any dependency beyond upstream's own set. Sending our changes upstream. Upstream's WPT conformance numbers (the WPT runner is built and gated only as the workspace gates it).

- Adopting the new upstream APIs. `[premise-corrected: `children` (#1069) is a `pub(crate)` JS `document.children` binding in blitz-vibey-script, not a blitz-dom Rust API (`git show d3ced119`)]` The Rust-side candidate for Snapshot model bounds is `Node::inline_fragment_boxes` (and the iterator-returning `inline_fragment_rects`).    `accessibility` feature, unconditionally (the executor cannot be built without the snapshot — a11y-plan §2
   A11y Strategy, Feature exposure). No `[features]` table is added and no other manifest is edited. Before
   and after the edit, record in `evidence/feature-reach.md` the readings of the two `cargo tree` entries of
   `## Test Commands` and of `cargo tree -p seven_guis -e normal --locked -i accesskit`: predicted — the
   feature appears on `dioxus-native-dom` in the driver's and the stand's graphs, `accesskit` was already in
   both through blitz-dom, no platform adapter is in the stand's graph, and `Cargo.lock` is byte-identical
   (research.md §Patterns detected, "The feature adds no package") — record what the readings measure.

2. **Let the driver name a key** — `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/lib.rs` re-exports `keyboard_types::Key`
   and `keyboard_types::Modifiers`, the two types `Harness::press_with` takes. `escher-driver` gains no third
   dependency.

3. **Give the harness the delete binding** — `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs` gains one input helper
   on `Harness`, `apple_keybinding(command)`: it dispatches `UiEvent::AppleStandardKeybinding` carrying
   `command` and pumps, as every other input helper does (`input.rs:201-218`). No existing helper changes.

4. **Hand the session its time step** — in `packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs`, `Session` holds an
   optional time step, and a new method `Session::with_time(self, step)` returns the session carrying it. The
   step is a caller's closure taking the held harness and the milliseconds asked and returning the
   milliseconds the app actually moved. `Session::start`, `harness`, `harness_mut` and `act` keep their
   signatures and behaviour (`Session::start @ session.rs:35`, 10 outside reference sites; `Session::act @
   session.rs:70`, 7 call sites — research.md §Graph impact); a session started without `with_time` has no
   step. The library names no app, no Timer and no tick.

5. **Run a call** — new private module `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs`, re-exported from the crate
   root, holding:
   - the public result type `Outcome`, one variant per result shape of the verb table: `Screen` holding the
     snapshot `text`; `Acted` holding `settled`, `busy` (the `Busy` class, present only when not settled) and
     the `SnapshotDiff`, unchanged; `Advanced` holding those three and `advanced_ms`;
   - the public method `Session::run(&mut self, call: &Call) -> Result<Outcome, Refusal>`, the one entry
     point. It calls `validate(call)` first and returns its refusal before anything else runs; nothing public
     runs a `Command` that did not come from `validate`.
   Per verb:
   - `snapshot` — the text of `DioxusDocument::snapshot` through `Snapshot::to_text`; nothing is dispatched.
   - `click` — the id is resolved (below); then one settled step that clicks at the centre of the node's
     border box through `Harness::click_at`, the same arithmetic `Harness::click` applies to a selector
     (`input.rs:97-108`).
   - `type` — the id is resolved; then one settled step that clicks the node the same way, which focuses a
     text input (`pointer.rs:547`), and types the text through `Harness::type_text`.
   - `press` — one settled step that presses the key through `Harness::press_with`, with the shift modifier
     when `shift` is true. Each of the schema's twelve keys maps to one keyboard key. On macOS only
     (`target_os = "macos"`), a `backspace` press also dispatches `deleteBackward:` through step 3's helper —
     the binding a window delivers there, where the editor's own Backspace arm is compiled out
     (`text.rs:329-331`, `:430-433`).
   - `advance` — a session with no time step returns `Refusal::new(Cause::TimeUnavailable)` and runs nothing;
     otherwise one settled step that calls the time step with `ms`, and `advanced_ms` is the step's return,
     never above `ms` (the lesser of the two).
   A settled step is: the snapshot before, the step, `Harness::settle`, the snapshot after, and
   `before.diff(&after)`. A not-quiet instance is a result — `settled` false with its `Busy` class — never a
   refusal and never a `SessionError`; the step is not rolled back.
   Resolving an id: the first pair of `DioxusDocument::element_ids()` whose id equals the argument, its node
   read through `get_node`. An id no pair carries, or a node that does not resolve, returns
   `Refusal::new(Cause::NotFound)` with nothing run. Nothing resolved outlives the call; the session keeps no
   id and no `NodeId`. No path indexes a node, calls `Harness::layout_rect_of` (it panics on an unresolved
   node, `inspect.rs:59`), or uses `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!` or `unreachable!` on anything a call supplied.
   The module prints and logs nothing, reads no env var and no clock, and never formats a `Call`, a `Command`
   or an `ArgValue`.

7. **The stand's time step** — `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs` gains the public constant
   `TIMER_TICK_MS` (100) and the public function `timer_step(ticks)`, returning the closure step 4 takes: it
   delivers `ms / TIMER_TICK_MS` whole ticks through `TimerTicks::deliver`, returns that count times
   `TIMER_TICK_MS`, drops the remainder and leaves the harness's animation clock where it was. An inline unit
   test at the end of the file states the mapping as a table of five rows (1 → 0, 99 → 0, 100 → 100,
   250 → 200, 60000 → 60000), its row count asserted: the returned milliseconds for all five rows, and for
   the first four the `timer-elapsed` text of a booted Timer after the delivery and a pump.

8. **The host hands the step over** — in `examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs` the Timer's session is
   given `stand::timer_step` of the handle its boot returned, through `with_time`, before `serve`. The argv
   check stays first, no argument is added, nothing is printed, and the three other tasks get no step.

9. **The shared session helpers** — in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs`, `hold` attaches
   `stand::timer_step` to the Timer's session (it still returns the handle, so its five readers are
   unedited), and four small builders return the `Call` for `click`, `type`, `press` and `advance`.

10. **The checks** — six new files under `tests/blitz-tests/tests/`, each opening with a `//!` doc, each
    scenario `for incremental in [false, true]`, booted through `seven_guis::stand`, with no sleep, no clock
    read and no font skip; every assertion message names a mode, a task and a row index or class word only.
    - `stand_act_ids.rs` — for every node of each lean task's snapshot, the 15 controls of
      `common::controls` among them (that count asserted): the id is the snapshot node's id and its
      accessibility node's `author_id`, and a driver `click` naming it is accepted — not refused
      `not-found`. For the controls with an effect at boot, the driver's returned diff
      equals the diff a twin instance yields when the same control is clicked by selector — first asserting
      that diff is not empty. After the actions the mount still reads `main#main > #task-shell`.
    - `stand_act_diff.rs` — on each lean task, a driver step's result equals `before.diff(&after)` over the
      check's own two snapshots, and the nodes it names are stated per step; a CRUD Create names the new row
      `crud-person-3` in `added` and a Delete names it in `removed`; a `click` on a non-interactive element
      returns `settled` with an empty diff; the two layout modes return equal results. On an in-file fixture,
      a sentinel typed by the driver into a password input occurs 0 times in the result and the entry's value
      reads `MASKED_VALUE`.
    - `stand_act_timer.rs` — on the Timer: `click` on `timer-reset`, then `advance` 300, returns `settled`,
      `advanced_ms` 300 and `timer-elapsed` among `changed` reading `Elapsed: 0.3s`; `advance` 50 returns
      `advanced_ms` 0 and an empty diff; `advance` 250 returns `advanced_ms` 200; `Harness::time` reads the
      same before and after every `advance`. On the Counter (no step): `advance` is refused
      `time-unavailable` and the snapshots before and after are equal. On an in-file fixture with a running
      CSS animation: a `click` returns `settled` and `Harness::time` is unchanged.
    - `stand_act_refused.rs` — a table of refused calls (an unknown verb; a missing argument; an id of 1024
      bytes that names nothing; the id of a CRUD row the driver just deleted), its row count asserted: each
      returns its cause (`unknown-verb`, `malformed`, `not-found`, `not-found`), the snapshots before and
      after are equal, and the refusal's `Display` holds none of the bytes the call supplied.
    - `stand_act_keys.rs` — on CRUD: after a `click` on `crud-name`, `press` of `tab` and of `tab` with
      `shift` each return a diff naming exactly the two controls whose `focused` reading moved, and the one
      node reading `focused` is the accessibility tree's focus; `type` of three characters into `crud-name`
      then `press` of `backspace` leaves two — the one deleting-key check, whose macOS reading is the CI
      run's.
    - `stand_act_range.rs` — the measurement of step 11, pinned.

11. **Measure the range input** — drive the Timer's `timer-duration` slider through `Session::run` only, as
    an agent would: a `click` on its id, then `press` of `arrow-right`, `arrow-left`, `home` and `end`. Record
    in `evidence/range-input.md` the fixture (the stand's Timer task, the control's id, role and boot value,
    both layout modes), each call made and the value and `timer-duration-value` read after it. Predicted from
    the code read: the value reads the same after every call (research.md §Patterns detected, "No range
    interaction model") — record what the run measures; `stand_act_range.rs` then asserts the measured
    reading, whichever it is. No engine code is written for a range input and no owner is named here.

12. **Controls** — four mutations, each applied alone, shown to turn its named check red, reverted, and
    recorded in `evidence/controls.md`: the settle removed from a settled step (`stand_act_timer`); the diff
    replaced by an empty one (`stand_act_diff`); an unresolved id answered with the first element instead of
    `not-found` (`stand_act_refused`); `advanced_ms` returned as the `ms` asked (`stand_act_timer`).
- `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs` — the executor: `Outcome`, `Session::run`, the id lookup, the key mapping
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_ids.rs` — the three-way id check and the effect of an id-addressed click
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_diff.rs` — the returned diff, the empty diff, the masked value
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_timer.rs` — `advance`, the settled Timer flow, `time-unavailable`
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_refused.rs` — a refused call changes nothing
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_keys.rs` — `press`, focus moves, typed deletion
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_range.rs` — the range input's measured reading
- `packages/escher-driver/Cargo.toml` — the `accessibility` feature named on `dioxus-native-dom`
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` — the module, the `Outcome` re-export, the crate doc
- `packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs` — the optional time step and `with_time`
- `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/lib.rs` — the `Key` and `Modifiers` re-exports
- `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs` — the `apple_keybinding` helper
- `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs` — `TIMER_TICK_MS`, `timer_step` and its unit test
- `examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs` — the Timer's session carries the step
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs` — `hold` attaches the step; four call builders

No entry is a live leg: nothing here drives a process the launch environment names, so there is no liveness
probe and no `stop` key; the two seven_guis entries start and reap their own host. There is no headful
self-verify harness on this project and this chunk changes no screen. Two smoke entries: `host_binary` starts
the real `escher-session` binary, the one boot path this chunk edits; and the windowed stand is booted for
10 s, because the feature step 1 names changes what that binary compiles — it declares `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and,
unset, is not run and the report says so. **Not run locally:** the MSRV build and the windows, macos, ios and android matrix legs — the
fork's CI run is their one witness, and the only witness of the macOS reading of `stand_act_keys`; the CI
acceptance follows the operator pass (pre-CI commit, push, CI read). The preservation entry names its base as
the commit this chunk starts from, `3c58ce5c`.

`evidence/feature-reach.md`, `evidence/range-input.md` and `evidence/controls.md` have no listed producer, by
construction: they are implement's hand records of step 1's readings, step 11's measurement and step 12's
mutations, none of which an entry could re-produce at the wrap's light gate; what each records is asserted by
a listed entry (the two `cargo tree` entries, `stand_act_range`, and the checks the mutations turn red).

- **Files:** 15 source and test files (basis: `gate.py scope`, `changed 15 · listed 15`; `git diff --name-status 3c58ce5c`).
  - New (7): `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs` (209 lines) · `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_ids.rs` (206 lines, 2 tests) · `stand_act_diff.rs` (303, 6) · `stand_act_timer.rs` (213, 4) · `stand_act_refused.rs` (155, 2) · `stand_act_keys.rs` (127, 2) · `stand_act_range.rs` (107, 1) — 17 tests (basis: `grep -c '^#\[test\]'` per file).

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - **`escher_driver::Session::run(&mut self, call: &Call) -> Result<Outcome, Refusal>`** (`packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:60`) — new, public: the one entry point that runs a call on a held instance, **in process**. It calls `validate(call)` first and returns its refusal before anything else runs; nothing public runs a `Command` that did not come from `validate`. Per verb: `snapshot` returns `DioxusDocument::snapshot().to_text()` and dispatches nothing; `click` resolves the id, then clicks the centre of the node's border box (`Harness::click_at`); `type` resolves the id, clicks it the same way and types through `Harness::type_text`; `press` presses the key through `Harness::press_with`, with `Modifiers::SHIFT` when `shift` is true; `advance` hands `ms` to the session's time step. Each acting verb is one settled step: the snapshot before, the step, `Harness::settle`, the snapshot after, `before.diff(&after)` (`execute.rs:100-109`).
  - **`escher_driver::Outcome`** (`execute.rs:15`) — new, public enum, re-exported from the crate root, `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]`: `Screen { text: String }` · `Acted { settled: bool, busy: Option<Busy>, diff: SnapshotDiff }` · `Advanced { settled, busy, diff, advanced_ms: u32 }`. A step that ran and did not go quiet is a result (`settled` false, `busy` its class), never a refusal and never a `SessionError`; the step is not rolled back. The diff is `dioxus_native_dom::SnapshotDiff`, unchanged.
  - **`escher_driver::Session::with_time(self, step: impl FnMut(&mut Harness<DioxusDocument>, u32) -> u32 + 'static) -> Session`** (`packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:60`) — new, public: the session carrying a caller's time step, which is handed the held harness and the milliseconds asked and returns the milliseconds the app moved. `Session` gains one field, `time: Option<TimeStep>` (`session.rs:30`; `TimeStep` is a crate-private boxed `FnMut`, `session.rs:20`); its `harness` and `time` fields are `pub(crate)` so the sibling module `execute` reaches them. `Session::start`, `label`, `harness`, `harness_mut` and `act` keep their signatures and behaviour; `act` keeps its 7 call sites, all in `stand_settle.rs`, and `start` its 10 outside reference sites (research.md §Graph impact; none edited). A session started without `with_time` has no step.
  - **Refusals the executor returns** — the first two screen- and session-level causes any code returns: `Cause::NotFound` for an id no pair of `DioxusDocument::element_ids()` carries, or whose node does not resolve through `get_node` (`execute.rs:125-134`), with nothing run; `Cause::TimeUnavailable` for `advance` on a session with no time step (`execute.rs:80-82`), with nothing run. `stale`, `disabled`, `covered` and `off-screen` are still returned by nothing: a click on a disabled or covered target runs, and its diff says what changed.
  - **`advanced_ms`** — the lesser of what the caller's step returns and the `ms` asked (`step(harness, ms).min(ms)`, `execute.rs:85`). It is **the time delivered to the app, not what a counter inside the app gained**: on the stand's Timer, `advance` of 60000 reports 60000 while the Timer's elapsed display stops at its 15 s duration (the overseer's technical answer, 2026-10-07, `operator-rulings.md` R5 in this wrap's run dir; the stand's unit table states the row).

No step reads or drains the changed set.
  - **macOS arm of `press`** — under `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]`, a `backspace` press also dispatches `deleteBackward:` through `Harness::apple_keybinding` (`execute.rs:155-158`): the editor's own Backspace arm is compiled out there. This is the one `cfg` gate in `execute.rs`.
  - **`blitz_test_harness::Harness::apple_keybinding(&mut self, command: &str)`** (`packages/blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs:229`) — new input helper: dispatches `UiEvent::AppleStandardKeybinding(command)` to the focused element and pumps, as every other input helper does. No existing helper changes.
  - **`blitz_test_harness::{Key, Modifiers}`** (`packages/blitz-test-harness/src/lib.rs:26`) — new re-exports of `keyboard_types::Key` and `keyboard_types::Modifiers`, the two types `Harness::press_with` takes. `escher-driver` gains no third dependency.
  - **`seven_guis::stand::TIMER_TICK_MS: u32 = 100`** (`examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:86`) and **`seven_guis::stand::timer_step(ticks: TimerTicks) -> impl FnMut(&mut Harness<DioxusDocument>, u32) -> u32`** (`stand.rs:92`) — new, public: delivers `ms / 100` whole ticks through `TimerTicks::deliver`, returns that count × 100, drops the remainder per call and leaves the harness's animation clock where it was; the ticks apply on the next pass.
  - **`escher-session` host** (`examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:45-48`) — the Timer's session is given `stand::timer_step(handle)` through `with_time` before `serve`; the other three tasks get no step. Argv check still first, no argument added, nothing printed; exit codes 0 · 1 · 2 unchanged.

  - **No new** socket, port, listener, env var, IPC method, workspace crate or binary.

So **both seven_guis binaries — the windowed `seven_guis_native` and the `escher-session` host — now compile dioxus-native-dom's accessibility modules** (the `accessibility_tree` override, the snapshot model, its text and its diff), and still build no platform adapter.
