data.head: ## Graph impact (from the code-graph query; plane `rust`)

body: - **`Session::act`** — 7 call sites, all in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_settle.rs` (`:51`, `:58`, `:66`, `:94`, `:116`, `:173`, `:329`), none in a library or a binary. A new entry point beside it leaves them untouched; a change to `act`'s return type edits all seven.

- **`Session::start`** — 10 reference sites outside the crate in six files (query 5's row for the definition in `session.rs`; the crate's other `start`, the client's, has 9 in three) (`examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:36`, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs:41`, `stand_session_lifecycle.rs:101`, `stand_session_quiet.rs:93`, `stand_session_state.rs:61` · `:78` · `:105` · `:137`, `stand_settle.rs:171` · `:326`) and one unit test (`session.rs:96`). A time step added as a new parameter of `start` threads through all of them; an additive constructor or setter threads through none.
- **`Session::harness` / `harness_mut`** — 51 call sites in six test files; the checks drive the held harness by selector today. Nothing in this chunk needs them to change.
- **`validate`** — 7 call sites, all unit tests in `command.rs`, plus the re-export: nothing outside the crate calls it, and nothing calls it before running anything.
- **`serve`** — called by `session_host.rs:44` and two ignored host children (`stand_session_lifecycle.rs:103`, `stand_session_quiet.rs:101`).
- **Crate edges** — `escher-driver → blitz-test-harness`, `escher-driver → dioxus-native-dom`; inbound `seven_guis → escher-driver`, `blitz-tests → escher-driver`. No other crate reaches it.

- **External surface of escher-driver** (query 5) — `Session`, `harness_mut`, `harness`, `stop`, `attach`, `start` (both), `SessionError` with four of its variants, `act`, `serve`, and the `Hello` / `Started` fields. No schema item (`Command`, `Call`, `VERBS`, `validate`, `Refusal`, `Cause`) is referenced outside the crate: the executor is their first consumer.

- **A click by node is the selector click's own arithmetic** (`input.rs:97-108`, `inspect.rs:57-74`): `click(selector)` resolves a node, takes the centre of its border box and calls `click_at`. Resolving the node from a stable id instead of a selector and taking the same centre gives the same pointer events — the caller supplies an id and no coordinate. The centre must be read through `get_node`, not `layout_rect_of`, which panics on an unresolved node.

- **A click on a text input focuses it, and typing follows focus** (`pointer.rs:547`; `stand_session_state.rs:83-88`): `type` by id is a click on the element, then `type_text`. The standing check proves it for `crud-name` and `crud-surname`.

- **An id resolves through `element_ids()`** (`dioxus_document.rs:215`): it returns `(NodeId, String)` pairs in document pre-order, computed on demand; there is no stored index. The executor's lookup is a linear search for the first pair whose string equals the id; an id matching none is the `not-found` case, whose stated meaning is exactly that (`refusal.rs:60`).

- **The diff is two snapshots and one call** (`snapshot.rs:83`, `snapshot_diff.rs:60`): `harness.doc.snapshot()` before the step, the step through `Session::act`, `snapshot()` after, `before.diff(&after)`. `DiffNode` and `NodeState` together carry the schema's nine node fields with nothing to map.

- **The time step cannot live in the binary** (`host.rs:35`, `:48`, `:107-123`): `serve` owns the session and blocks, so whatever moves time is handed to the session before `serve`. The stand's mapping of milliseconds onto ticks therefore sits where both the host binary and an in-process check can reach it — `seven_guis::stand`, which already returns the tick handle (`stand.rs:79-83`).

- **The crate cannot name a key today** (`blitz-test-harness/src/lib.rs`, `input.rs:13`): `Harness::press_with` takes `keyboard_types::Key` and `Modifiers`, which neither of escher-driver's two dependencies re-exports. `click_at(f32, f32)` and `type_text(&str)` need no such type. Running `press` needs either a re-export from blitz-test-harness or a third dependency on the driver's manifest (`keyboard-types` is already a workspace dependency, so the lockfile gains no package either way).

- **Backspace has a platform-neutral path the harness does not use** (`text.rs:329-331`, `:368`, `:430-433`; `blitz-traits/src/events.rs:71`; `blitz-dom/src/events/driver.rs:197`, `:257`): on macOS the key arm is compiled out, while `UiEvent::AppleStandardKeybinding("deleteBackward:")` reaches `backdelete` on every platform (`target_os` occurs 0 times under `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/` and `packages/blitz-traits/src/` — `grep -rn target_os`). A `press backspace` that dispatches that binding on macOS deletes there with no edit to the engine's editor. The equality "the binding deletes one character on macOS" is not measurable on this host; its witness is the fork's macOS CI leg.

- **No range interaction model** (`construct.rs:441-459`; `grep -rn -i '"range"' packages/blitz-dom/src packages/dioxus-native-dom/src` → 2 hits: the Slider role at `accessibility.rs:272` and a snapshot unit-test fixture): a range input gets a role and a value reading and no input handling. Read from the code; no range input was driven.

- **The feature adds no package** (`cargo tree -p seven_guis -e normal --locked -i accesskit`; `-i accesskit_xplat`; `-i accesskit_winit`): `accesskit 0.25.0` is already in the graphs of `escher-driver` and `seven_guis` through `blitz-dom`, because blitz-test-harness names `blitz-dom/accessibility` (`packages/blitz-test-harness/Cargo.toml:15`). Naming `dioxus-native-dom/accessibility` in escher-driver turns on that crate's own `dep:accesskit` and compiles its snapshot modules into both seven_guis binaries; no platform adapter is in the stand's graph (`accesskit_xplat` and `accesskit_winit` "did not match any packages") and the feature forwards none — the adapter comes only through dioxus-native's and blitz-shell's own `accessibility` features, which seven_guis does not name (`cargo tree -p seven_guis -e features --locked -i dioxus-native-dom` lists `prelude`, `system-fonts`, `vello-hybrid`, `woff`).

- **Counts this chunk extends** — escher-driver unit tests 25 in six files (`grep -c '#\[test\]' packages/escher-driver/src/*.rs`: command 5 · error 3 · refusal 3 · schema 4 · session 2 · wire 8); `stand_*.rs` files 20 (`ls tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_*.rs | wc -l`).
- **Private module, re-exported at the root, every public item documented** (`lib.rs:27-49`, `#![deny(missing_docs)]`).

- **Fixed strings in every error and refusal; nothing a call supplied in any of them** (`error.rs:10`, `refusal.rs:46-99`); no `{:?}` of a `Command`, `Call` or `ArgValue` anywhere outside a test's own row index.
- **Unit tests inline at the end of the source file, each table with its row count asserted and a row index as the only assertion message** (`schema.rs:277-300`).
- **One behaviour per `stand_*.rs` file, `for incremental in [false, true]`, booted through `seven_guis::stand`, shared helpers from `session_common` and `common`** (`stand_settle.rs:40-43`).
- **The host binary checks its argv before anything boots and writes nothing to stdout** (`session_host.rs:24-32`).
- `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs` — the executor: a validated command run on a session, its typed outcome, the id lookup
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act*.rs` — the driver-action checks on the stand, one behaviour per file
- `packages/escher-driver/Cargo.toml` — the `dioxus-native-dom` feature named
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` — the new module, its re-exports, the crate doc
- `packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs` — the time step a caller hands the session
- `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/lib.rs` — the key types re-exported for the driver
- `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs` — a helper that dispatches the delete binding
- `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs` — the stand's mapping of milliseconds onto Timer ticks
- `examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs` — the host hands that step to its session

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs` — a held session that carries the time step

  The fork was answered "in process" (the operator, 2026-10-07, at the P4 forks), so the list was narrowed:
  the seven socket-branch files it first carried — escher-driver's wire, host, client and error sources,
  seven_guis' `host_log` check and its shared module, and `stand_session_lifecycle` — are read and left
  as they are. `Cargo.lock` is expected unchanged (no package enters the graph); a `--locked` build is its witness.
  Caller threading: no existing signature changes if the time step is additive — `Session::start`'s 10
  outside reference sites and `Session::act`'s 7 are left as they are (Graph impact).

- Where a command runs — in process on a `Session`, or across the session socket (scope's fork; the wire's 64- and 128-byte bounds hold neither an id of 1024 bytes nor a diff) → blocks: plan-decision. **Answered (the operator, 2026-10-07, at the P4 forks): in process.**

- What `advance` does with a remainder below one tick (100 ms): dropped per call, or carried to the next call → blocks: plan-decision. **Closed at P4 as a decisive lean, not asked:** the schema states `advanced_ms` is "never more than `ms`" (`schema.rs:189`), and a carried remainder makes a later call move more than it asked — so whole ticks per call, the remainder dropped.

- What this chunk does about a range input, which no input can change (CARRY 2, second half): measured and re-homed, or built → blocks: plan-decision. **Answered (the operator, 2026-10-07, at the P4 forks): measured through the driver as an agent would drive it, the reading recorded with its fixture; no owner named in the plan — the owner is decided at the wrap.**
**Working entry (verbatim):** Act by id — driver actions addressed by stable id, returning after settle with the diff (v010-09, v010-06)

**Epoch:** Epoch 4 — Driver core · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Freight on the entry:** seven `CARRY:` blocks (465 · 913 · 1062 · 922 · 504 · 1240 · 1293 characters), each folded below under "The carried freight" (`route.py pins`, trail in the run dir: 32 freight blocks on the markerless tail, all `CARRY:`, seven of them on line 62, and no abstention printed). No `BLOCKED-ON`, `PREREQ` or `WATCH` on the entry. No external input: every fact below is read from this repository or the route.

**Premise closure (P3):** every `[inferred]` bullet below was re-read against `research.md`: fourteen verified and their tags dropped, two corrected. A bullet with no tag is what the entry states or is verified; a corrected one carries `[premise-corrected: …]`.

The driver's fourth piece, after the session, settle and the schema: **the schema's verbs run on a held instance**. intent §5 states what it serves — "acting by id returns only once the UI has settled, so a stand flow with a delayed update passes with no sleep" — and intent §3 what comes back: "after an action the driver returns exactly the nodes that changed; an action that changes nothing returns an empty diff". At HEAD the crate says of itself "no command runs through a session yet" (`packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs:24-25`).
- **Driver actions addressed by stable id** — an action names its target by the element's stable id and takes effect on that element.

- **Which actions** — the schema's acting verbs, as the table states them: `click` and `type` take an `id`, `press` takes a `key` and an optional `shift`, `advance` takes `ms` (`packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:205-261`). `validate` already turns a `Call` into a typed `Command` (`command.rs:161`); this chunk gives a `Command` something that runs it.

- **The id an action takes is the element's `element_id`** — the string `DioxusDocument::element_id` / `element_ids` compute (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:209`, `:215`), the same one the snapshot and the accessibility node carry. How an id is resolved to the live node is the plan's.

- **"No coordinates or selectors" is the caller's side** — v010-09's acceptance reads "addressed by an element's stable id alone, with no coordinates or selectors". The harness's own helpers click by selector or at a point (`packages/blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs:97`, `:103`); what the executor dispatches inside the engine for a resolved node is the plan's, and the caller hands it an id only.

- **`press` names no element** — it carries a key, not an id, so it acts on whatever holds focus (the table's own help: "presses one key on the focused element", `schema.rs:238`). Found at P3: the crate cannot name a key today — `Harness::press_with` takes `keyboard_types::Key` and `Modifiers`, which neither of its two dependencies re-exports (research.md §Patterns detected). How that reads against v010-09's "every driver action … is addressed by an element's stable id alone" is settled at P4 against the cap, not assumed here.
- **Returning after settle** — an action returns once the instance has settled. The in-process step exists: `Session::act` runs a closure and settles (`session.rs:70-78`).

- **A step that ran and did not go quiet is a result, not a refusal** — the acting verbs' result carries `settled` and `busy` (`schema.rs:148`, `:155`), while `Session::act` returns `SessionError::NotSettled` today (`session.rs:77`); the executor reports the first shape.
- **With the diff** — the return names the nodes added, removed and changed.

- **The diff is `Snapshot::diff` over the snapshots taken before and after the step, returned unchanged** — `Snapshot::diff(&self, after: &Snapshot) -> SnapshotDiff` (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs:60`); the result fields `added` · `removed` · `changed` are the schema's (`schema.rs:163-178`).

- **The `snapshot` verb** — the table's fifth verb is a read, and the entry names actions. v010-04's command leg is a CARRY on "Driver CLI" (working-route.md:71), which also owns where the text first leaves the process. Whether one executor runs the whole table here, `snapshot` included, or leaves that verb unexecuted is the plan's; v010-04 is not claimable here either way.

- **What an id that names no element gets** — `[premise-corrected: the case has a cause whose stated meaning is exactly it — `not-found`, "no element on the screen reads the id", refusal.rs:60; ids resolve through `element_ids()` with no stored index, research.md §Patterns detected]` `validate` checks a call's shape and receives no `Session`, so it cannot know whether an id names anything; an executor that acts by id meets that case on its first unknown id. `Cause::NotFound` is named and worded, and "nothing returns the five yet" (the CARRY on working-route.md:64). Detecting the five screen-level causes is "Refusal detection" (Boundaries), which reserves two decisions — `stale` against `not-found`, and `off-screen` with no verb that scrolls. What this chunk returns for an id it cannot resolve, and for a target that cannot take the action, is the plan's, bounded by that entry.

title: The carried freight (the entry's seven CARRYs)

data.head: ## The carried freight (the entry's seven CARRYs)

body: Each is folded as a hypothesis: the artifacts it names were re-read at the take-up, and a mechanism it states keeps its own marker.

1. **v010-03's driver leg** (from 2026-10-06-snapshot-model). "its accessibility-tree leg and its snapshot leg are built and proven (`stand_accessibility_ids`, `stand_snapshot`…), and the remaining leg is the driver's — the id an action takes is that same id; this entry is where the three-way check can first pass". Re-read: both check files exist (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_accessibility_ids.rs`, `stand_snapshot.rs`); the cap reads `planned`, unclaimed, with two ledger notes saying the same (`matrix.py show --id v010-03`). Owed here: a check that the id the driver accepts for each stand element is the id in the snapshot and on the accessibility node.

2. **Input the engine cannot take headlessly** (from 2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity). Two engine defects, each with a route owner here:
   - (1), verified at HEAD for its code cause, with one finding added — the delete has a path that is not platform-gated: `UiEvent::AppleStandardKeybinding("deleteBackward:")` reaches `backdelete` on every platform (`text.rs:368`, `:430-433`), so a driver `press backspace` can delete on macOS with no edit to the engine's editor; that equality is witnessed only by the fork's macOS CI leg (research.md §Patterns detected). The CARRY's words: "on macOS the editor has no Backspace arm (text.rs:330-331 leaves the delete to the Apple standard key bindings), so a headless key press deletes nothing there (measured: CI#37539756517, `Test (macos)`); the driver needs typed deletion that works headless on every platform". Re-read at HEAD: `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/text.rs:329-331` — the comment "On macOS this is handled by the apple standard keybindings", `#[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]`, then the `Key::Backspace` arm. The schema's key set holds `backspace` (`command.rs:38`, `:80`). The measurement is that run's, not re-made here; no local gate runs macOS (the handoff).
   - (2), verified by code read at HEAD and still not measured by driving a range input — `"range"` occurs twice under `packages/blitz-dom/src` and `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src`, a role mapping and a snapshot test fixture, and in no input handling (research.md §Patterns detected). The CARRY's words: "the engine has no `select` or range interaction model, so the stand's `timer-duration` slider reads its value yet cannot be changed through input; hypothesis for (2): read from the code at that chunk's phase (construct.rs:440-459 gives special data only to text-entry inputs, textareas, checkboxes and radios), not measured by driving a range input". Re-read at HEAD: `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs:441-459` builds a text editor for `textarea` and the text-entry input types and a checkbox input for `checkbox` and `radio`, and nothing for `range`. Still a hypothesis: no range input was driven.
   - What this chunk does about each is the plan's: the first bears on `press` and `type` on every platform CI runs; the second on which stand controls an action can change. **Decided for the second (the operator, 2026-10-07, at the P4 forks):** measured, not built — "Drive it through the driver exactly as an agent would, and record the reading as a measurement with its fixture. Name no owner in the plan: the owner is decided at the wrap." No engine code is written for a range input here.

3. **v010-06's driver leg** (from 2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff; the operator's direction at that chunk's P5 review, 2026-10-07). "this entry's act returns that diff unchanged and claims v010-06". Re-read: `BaseDocument::has_changes` and `take_changed_nodes` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:1009`, `:1016`), `Snapshot::diff` (`snapshot_diff.rs:60`), `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_diff.rs`; the cap's ledger note says the same. Two constraints ride with it: "the engine's changed set is not the diff — it is engine-touched, and the flag true beside an empty diff is a designed case"; and "a diff carries ids, accessible names and a text control's value and leaves the process through the returned value only (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07; security-plan §Input Validation, the `id` row) — the first command that returns it asks the crossing question again". The second is the fork above.

4. **Typed text in a sink-installing host's log** (from 2026-10-07-driver-session; the founder's ruling, 2026-10-07). "when this entry gives the driver a command that types into a held instance, prove a typed sentinel occurs 0 times in the `escher-session` binary's stderr at `RUST_LOG=trace`… if another entry delivers a typing command first, the proof is that entry's". Re-read: both evidence files it cites exist (`escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-session/evidence/host-stderr-by-level.md`, `…/2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist/report.md`); the standing check is `examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs`, which spawns the binary with `RUST_LOG=trace` (`:79`) and searches its stderr for needles read from the stand (`:146-155`). The proof needs a typing command that reaches the binary's own instance — so whether it is owed in this chunk follows from the fork above; an in-process `type` reaches no sink-installing host.

5. **The session library's accessibility feature** (from 2026-10-07-driver-session). "`escher-driver` names no `dioxus-native-dom` feature, so nothing reads a snapshot or a diff through the library today; the entry that first reads the snapshot through a session decides the feature, and naming it in `escher-driver` reaches the windowed stand binary's own build through `seven_guis → escher-driver`". Re-read: `packages/escher-driver/Cargo.toml` names `dioxus-native-dom = { workspace = true }` and no feature; `DioxusDocument::snapshot` stands behind `accessibility` (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs:15-37`, `snapshot.rs:83`); `examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml:35` depends on `escher-driver`. A diff needs the snapshot, so this chunk is that entry: it decides the feature, and with it whether the windowed stand binary now builds AccessKit (the a11y plane's question — a CARRY on "Stand a11y assertions", working-route.md:86, says the stand binary builds none today).

6. **v010-10's driver leg** (from 2026-10-07-settle-detection; the operator, 2026-10-07, at that chunk's P5 review). "the remaining leg is the driver's — a driver action on the Timer returning settled with the delayed update present". 
   - the CARRY's measurement, its evidence pointer spot-checked at HEAD (the standing check still makes that step — a Reset click and three delivered ticks inside one `act`, `stand_settle.rs:66-70`), verbatim: "Measured at that chunk (escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-settle-detection/evidence/red-first.md): a step that clicks Reset and then delivers three ticks reads `0.0s` with no pass after the delivery and `0.3s` once settled, so the Timer check is red without the settle". The file exists; the reading is that chunk's, not re-made here.
   - The two reasons it gives for the cap standing unclaimed: "an in-process closure is no action an agent can run; under `escher-session` nobody delivers the ticks". Re-read: `examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:35-45` binds the tick handle, stores it and drops it after `serve` returns; nothing between delivers a tick.
   - "the leg now waits on that wiring, the next annotation" — CARRY 7.

- **Not Refusal detection** (working-route.md:64 — "not found, stale, disabled, covered by another element, off-screen named per action (v010-11)"). Telling which screen-level cause holds for an action is that entry's, with its minimal-fixture CARRY and its two reserved decisions. v010-11 is not claimable here.

- **Not Driver command spans** (working-route.md:66). This chunk adds no span and no event. Its CARRY binds this chunk all the same: "no `Command`, `Call` or `ArgValue` with `Debug`" in a log field — an executor that holds those values logs none of them (CLAUDE.md §Critical Warnings, "add no new user-content log fields").

- **Not Driver CLI, MCP surface or Self-description** (working-route.md:71 · 73 · 75). JSON on stdout, exit codes, MCP tools, argv parsing and serving the schema are theirs. If the fork above is answered "across the socket", what crosses is the wire's own form, registered first (arch §Occupied Resources, security-plan) — not the CLI's JSON.

- **Not Headless screenshot** (working-route.md:77) and **not the stand keyboard harness** (working-route.md:84): a `press` of Tab here is an action, not the focus-order check; the hypothesis carried there — "a click on a plain `button` clears focus instead of focusing it" — is not this chunk's to fix, and a check here that depends on focus after a click reads it first.

- **No new listener, port, env var or workspace crate.** The one listener stays the session socket. A change to what crosses it is the fork above; a new dependency or feature is CARRY 5's decision and is named in the plan.

  (:179-217) becomes a function, with the walk under `#task-body` (:195-217) a function of its own; the Counter and
  CRUD block (:221-238) becomes a function of `incremental`.

- `stand_id_persistence.rs` · `ids_hold_across_a_remount` (:189-251) — the `(incremental, task, nth)` body (:198-248)
  becomes a function, the kept/fresh/dropped accounting after the second mount (:217-247) a function of its own. The
  loop order (`incremental` outside the `cards`), the full-app boot through a Home card and the comparison with the
  stand's boot are kept. `ids_in_a_child_process`, its two `println!` and the parent's argv are not touched.

- `stand_snapshot_text.rs` · `every_node_is_one_line_with_its_five_fields` (:159-236) — the `(task, incremental)` body
  becomes a function, the per-line field assertions (:185-211) and the CRUD nesting block (:216-233) functions of their
  own. The text stays bound to `text`-named variables and no message formats it.

**Step 6 — format and measure.**
Run `cargo fmt --all` after the last edit (the write hook does not format a crate root whose module file did not
exist when it ran). Then the gates below. The mutation entry's untouched-tree reading (its `baseline`) is the red half
of the red-before-green record; its run on the finished tree is the green half. Record under
`chunks/2026-10-07-audit-corrections/evidence/` what each forecast in Implementation notes measured, and the mutation
run's last line.
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document_tests.rs` — the six tests of step 1
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs` — the three tables and six helpers of step 3
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs` — three `cfg(test)` lines appended after the last line; no function edited
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs` — `VdomWalk::walk` split into private helpers; the in-file tests untouched
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_element_ids.rs` — one test function restructured
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_id_persistence.rs` — one test function restructured
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_text.rs` — one test function restructured; reads the shared module
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot.rs` — reads the shared module
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_accessibility_ids.rs` — reads the shared module
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_state.rs` — reads the shared module
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_diff.rs` — reads the shared module
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_actionable_keys.rs` — reads the shared module

No live leg runs this chunk: the agent-run entries drive the in-process stand through `scripts/agent-run.sh` and start
no external process, so there is no liveness probe and no `stop`. There is no headful self-verify and no windowed boot
smoke — the chunk changes no rendered surface and no code a windowed binary runs differently (`walk` is restructured
with its output unchanged, and the stand binary names no `accessibility` feature). The mutation, complexity and
duplication entries run the audits' own tools on this host; none is a CI leg and none becomes one. The duplication
entry is report-only by disposition: its numbers are a forecast to be measured, and the asserted halves of that
criterion are the two definition censuses and the table comparison. The CI acceptance follows the operator pass
(pre-CI commit, push, CI read).

These are the guard of "every id unchanged".

- **`create_head_element`** — 1 caller: `packages/dioxus-native/src/dioxus_application.rs:98` (the windowed crate's `CreateHeadElement` handler). No headless caller; the function is `pub`, so a test calls it directly.
- **`flush_queued_mounted_events`** — 2 callers: `initial_build` (`dioxus_document.rs:154`) and `poll` (:283).

- **`handle_event` (the bridge's) · `Document::id` (the bridge's)** — 0 rows: both are reached by trait dispatch (`EventDriver` → `EventHandler`; `&dyn Document`), which the graph does not resolve. Not a leaf reading.

- **`propagation_is_stopped`** — 0 references on the plane; confirmed by a name sweep of `packages/`, `apps/`, `tests/`, `examples/` for `propagation_is_stopped|propagation_stopped`: 5 hits, all inside `blitz-traits/src/events.rs` (the field :16, the setter body :27, the getter :41-42, `merge` :54). Nothing reads the flag.

- **Every audit number reproduces on this host, same tools, same commands.** `rust-code-analysis-cli` 0.0.25 over the 302 files of `git ls-files '*.rs'` (the ledger's `commands.complexity`, the summarizer's rule: every space of kind `function`, closures included, cognitive > 15): **78** over the ceiling, source 75, test 3 — `walk` 26, `unkeyed_elements_read_their_component_path` 21, `ids_hold_across_a_remount` 17, `every_node_is_one_line_with_its_five_fields` 16. `jscpd` 5.4.0 over `packages apps tests examples wpt/runner` (the ledger's `commands.duplication`): 287 clones, **13** pairs with both sides a `stand_*.rs` check, **220** lines. `cargo mutants --list --workspace --file …/element_id.rs --file …/dioxus_document.rs`: **57** mutants, and seven name patterns select exactly the seven survivors, now at `element_id.rs:226:43`, `dioxus_document.rs:166:9`, `:220:9`, `:245:9` (twice), `:411:12`, `:414:12`.

- **The four functions under test are inherited unchanged.** `git diff 23354585 HEAD -- packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs` (the recorded sync base) has three hunks — two imports, the element-id methods after `create_head_element`, the `accessibility_tree` override — and none lies inside `create_head_element`, `flush_queued_mounted_events`, `Document::id` or `handle_event`.

- **Six of the seven mutants are killable through public surface; each kill is stated as the equality it needs.**
  - `&&` → `||` in `place_children` (:226): the filter is `!key.is_empty() && !key.contains('/')`. For a Dioxus key `a/b` the original reads `true && false` = reject, so the segment is positional (`li:0`); the mutant reads `true || false` = accept, so the segment is `li[a/b]`. For an empty key the original rejects and the mutant accepts (`li[]`). None of the 13 in-file tests carries a Dioxus key that is empty or holds `/` (they cover the HTML `id` filter at :179, a different line), which is why the mutant survived.
  - `create_head_element` → `()` (:166): after `create_head_element("title", &[], &Some(text))` the head element has one more element child, of that tag, with a text child; the mutant leaves `<head>` empty.
  - `flush_queued_mounted_events` → `()` (:220): an element with an `onmounted` listener has its handler called once by `initial_build`; the mutant never calls it. The listener is queued at `mutation_writer.rs:344-346`.
  - `Document::id` → `0` and → `1` (:245): for two documents built in one test, `Document::id(&doc) == doc.inner.borrow().id()` holds for both; inner ids come from a counter that starts at 1 and never repeats, so `0` fails on any document and `1` fails on at least one of two.
  - `!` deleted at :411: with a listener that does not call `prevent_default`, the original leaves the event state uncancelled and the mutant cancels it. The driver reads this flag (`driver.rs:316-317`), so it is observable through real input — a click on a checkbox carrying an `onclick` listener toggles it under the original and not under the mutant (`events/pointer.rs:645-649`) — and directly, as `EventState::is_cancelled()`.

- **The seventh is not observable outside its own module.** `!` deleted at :414 changes only `EventState::propagation_stopped`. No engine code reads that flag (see Graph impact), the driver builds the state and drops it, and Dioxus does its own bubbling inside `vdom.runtime().handle_event`. The one way to see the mutation is to call `DioxusEventHandler::handle_event` with an `EventState` the caller keeps — and the handler's two fields are private to the `dioxus_document` module, with no constructor (:316-319, built only at :289-292). So: a test that is a child module of `dioxus_document` kills it with one assertion (`propagation_is_stopped()` reads false after a plain listener, true after one that calls `stop_propagation`; the mutant inverts both); a test anywhere else cannot. The line executes on every handled event, so it is not unreachable — its effect is unread.

- **`walk`'s guard, as far as it is measured.** The mutation tool lists four mutants inside `walk` at HEAD (`walk` → `()`, the `!` at :80, `+=` → `-=` and `*=` at :115); none is among the Epoch 2 run's seven survivors. That run's six unviable mutants are counted, not named, in its record, so "all four were caught" is read from the survivors list and is not a named outcome per mutant. title: Revision — 2026-10-07 (the plan re-planned after /andromeda-implement stopped on it)

data.head: ## Revision — 2026-10-07 (the plan re-planned after /andromeda-implement stopped on it)

body: - The operator's word (`inputs#I1`, given in this session, 2026-10-07): /andromeda-implement stopped on this plan at the table-comparison entry of its Test Commands, and the plan is revised in what that stop falsified — the entry's pattern and whatever cites it; the promotion, the code already written and the evidence stay as they are. Verified against the stopped run's own record (run dir `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-07T03-27-51-implement/`, its gate trail; `evidence/implement-measurements.md`): one full run of the block read 21 green, 1 recorded, 1 red and 3 operator entries not run; the red is the table comparison, exit 1 with 33 unmatched lines, all on the base side.

- What the stop falsified is the entry, not a premise of this scope: the three tables are stated once and are the base copies line for line (re-derived at P3 of this revision, research.md §Patterns detected). No bullet above is corrected, the write set is the one research listed, and no boundary moves.

_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-07T00:48Z
- **Starts from:** `e616ec1c1ea20b7373eb5fab66687c87f5280f1c` (HEAD at P4; every git-reading gate names it as its base)

Build what intent §Findings 3 expects and its three observed defects deny: a changed-node set that is drained, a
change flag that tells the truth, and a diff that names exactly the nodes an action changed — empty for an action
that changed nothing (requirements v010-06).

Research found the engine's flag is not merely inverted but constant: the document's own constructor marks the set,
nothing drains it, and `has_changes()` answers `false` for every document at all times, so the windowed shell's
accessibility refresh has never run (research.md §Patterns detected). It also found that no per-node engine set can
equal "the nodes whose snapshot changed": a node's name is drawn from other nodes and its bounds from layout. So the
chunk is two parts with one seam between them. **The engine part** (blitz-dom, and the flag's one caller in
blitz-shell): the set is written where the engine writes something an agent reads as role, name or state — the
mutation writers, a focus or checked change, a typed character — and no longer by node creation, which layout also
performs; a drain takes it; the flag reads true exactly while the set is non-empty. **The observation part**
(dioxus-native-dom): the diff is a pure comparison of two `Snapshot` values, keyed by stable element id, exact by
construction and a reader of the model only (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge; a11y-plan §7).
The seam: the flag is the engine's cheap "something was written", the diff is the truth of what changed; a written
node whose reading did not move (an attribute re-written to itself, a further character in a masked password) reads
flag true, diff empty.

Both are proven on the stand in both layout modes through real input (intent §Principles, "The stand is the
proof"), with an in-file fixture for the cases the four lean tasks lack. The diff is an in-process Rust value
returned to its caller only — the CARRY's content rule, carried unchanged (security-plan §Input Validation, the `id`
row; PROVISIONAL, pending the founder at the Epoch 3 boundary).

1. **The set's contract in `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs`.**
   - `create_node` (`:854-865`) stops inserting into `changed_nodes`: the comment and the insert at `:862-863` leave.
     This is a direct change to an upstream line, named as one — layout creates anonymous blocks and pseudo-element
     nodes through the same function (`layout/construct.rs:142`, `:712`) and the constructor creates the root through
     it (`document.rs:514`).
   - `has_changes` (`:1009-1010`) returns whether the set is non-empty; its doc comment states the contract: true
     from the first tracked write of an in-document node until the next drain.
   - A new public `take_changed_nodes(&mut self)` beside it returns the set and leaves it empty. Its doc comment says
     a returned id may name a node dropped since it was written, to be read through `get_node`.
   - The field's doc comment (`:326`) is restated to match (it reads the same sentence twice today, on two fields).
   - `snapshot_node_and` (`:1540-1550`): when its `state` argument intersects `ElementState::FOCUS` or
     `ElementState::CHECKED`, `node_id` enters the set. Hover and active do not mark — they reach this helper on
     every pointer move and press.

2. **The mutation writers in `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs`.** At each of the 15 sites that set
   `mutations_occurred` (`grep -n 'mutations_occurred |=' packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` — lines 210, 242, 316,
   434, 497, 503, 509, 515, 522, 529, 544, 569, 613, 664, 674), when that site's own condition holds, the id of the
   node whose in-document flag the condition reads enters `changed_nodes`: `node_id` at the twelve sites guarded by
   `node_is_in_document`, the parent at `:613` and `:664`, the moved child at `:674`. No site outside those 15 is
   added and none of their existing behaviour changes.

3. **A typed character in `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs`.** In `apply_generated_text_input_event`, the
   `GeneratedTextInputEvent::Input` arm (`:119-126`) puts `node_id` into the set. The other arms do not mark.

4. **blitz-dom unit tests**, in an in-file `#[cfg(test)]` module of `document.rs`, documents built by hand through
   `BaseDocument::new(DocumentConfig { .. })` and `document.mutate()` (the shape at `mutator.rs:1379-1400`), each
   named with the prefix `changed_set_` — seven:
   a fresh document reads the flag false and an empty set · an attribute written on an in-document element reads
   the flag true, the drain returns that node, and after it the flag is false and a second drain is empty · a write
   to a node outside the document marks nothing · a focus move marks the node that lost focus and the node that
   gained it, and a hover-state change through `snapshot_node_and` marks nothing · a checked-state change marks its
   node · for `incremental in [false, true]`, a document whose layout builds an anonymous block, drained after its
   first `resolve`, is still empty after a second `resolve` with nothing written · an id drained after its node was
   dropped (`remove_and_drop_node`) reads `None` through `get_node` with no panic.
   **Control, once, recorded under `evidence/`:** with the tests written and only `take_changed_nodes` added, the
   attribute-write test reads red — the flag answers false after a write. That run measures research's by-code-read
   claim that the flag is constant; steps 1–3 then land and it reads green.

5. **The flag's caller in `packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs`** (`View::poll`, `:372-389`). Inside the existing
   arm that runs when `self.doc.poll(..)` reported work: the changed set is taken — outside the `accessibility`
   gate, so a shell built without the feature still drains — and, under `accessibility`, when the taken set was
   non-empty the platform tree is rebuilt through the existing `self.accessibility.update_tree(&*self.doc)` call.
   The call stays on the trait-method path (a11y-plan §2 Accessibility tree lifecycle); `build_accessibility_tree`
   (`:521-523`) and `application.rs` are untouched.

6. **The diff in a new `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs`**, crate-private module, compiled only
   under `accessibility`, its types re-exported from `lib.rs` beside the snapshot's and named in the crate doc's
   feature list (`lib.rs:7-9`, `:20-23`, `:30-33`).
   - `Snapshot::diff(&self, after: &Snapshot)` returns a `SnapshotDiff`: a pure function of its two arguments — no
     document access, no failure path, no log, no print.
   - `SnapshotDiff` holds three lists and an `is_empty()`: `added` and `changed` are `DiffNode`s, `removed` is ids.
     `DiffNode` is a node's reading after the step, flat: `id`, `parent` (the id of its parent snapshot node, `None`
     for a root), `role`, `name`, `state`, `bounds` — no children. Both types derive `Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`.
     (The entry shape is the operator's choice at P4's question round, 2026-10-07.)
   - A node is **added** when its id is in `after` and not in `self`; **removed** when in `self` and not in `after`;
     **changed** when in both and any of role · name · state · bounds · parent differs. A node whose own reading is
     equal is never named because a descendant's changed. `added` and `changed` follow `after`'s pre-order,
     `removed` follows `self`'s (`Snapshot::nodes()`).
   - No field of either type holds a `NodeId`, an `ElementId`, a `ScopeId`, an AccessKit id or a pointer, and the
     module names none of them; values come from the two snapshots only, so a password's or a file input's value is
     whatever the model holds — `MASKED_VALUE`.
   - Unit tests in the file's own `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, over `Snapshot` values built by hand from the model's
     public fields — eight: two equal snapshots give an empty diff · a changed name · a changed state · changed
     bounds — each naming that node alone, with its after-reading · an added subtree names every node of it, each
     with its parent's id · a removed subtree names every id of it in the before order · a node moved under another
     parent is changed · `added` and `changed` are in the after snapshot's pre-order.

7. **The stand check, a new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_diff.rs`** — opening with a `//!` doc naming the
   behaviour; `for incremental in [false, true]` in every test; boot through
   `stand::boot(task, stand::options(incremental))` / `stand::boot_timer`, fixtures through
   `Harness::from_vdom(VirtualDom::new(fixture), stand::options(incremental))` (`stand_snapshot_text.rs:387-389`).
   A **step** is: read the snapshot, drain the set through `harness.base_mut()`, perform one input helper (or
   deliver ticks and `pump`), read the flag through `harness.base()`, read the snapshot again, and diff the two.
   **Exactness is asserted two ways in every step**: the expected ids as literals, and an oracle of the check's own
   — for every id in either snapshot, the diff names it if and only if `Snapshot::get` finds it in one snapshot only
   or its role, name, state, bounds or parent's id — the parent read by the check's own walk of each tree — differ
   between the two. Nine tests:
   - a click on `counter-increment` names `counter-value`, whose name changed, and nothing in the shell's header;
   - CRUD's Create (the flow of `stand_crud.rs:25-36`) names the new row `crud-person-3` as added, and selecting it
     and pressing Delete names it as removed;
   - focus: a click on `crud-name`, a Tab press and Shift+Tab (the sequence of
     `stand_snapshot_state.rs:308-340`) each name exactly the controls whose `focused` reading moved, and the first
     Tab on a fresh boot names `back-btn`; the flag reads true after each;
   - a character typed into `crud-name` names it, its value changed, flag true;
   - the timer: after `deliver(3)` and a pump the diff names `timer-elapsed`, flag true; after a pump with nothing
     delivered the diff is empty and the flag false;
   - nothing changes: on each of the four lean tasks a pump with nothing pending gives an empty diff and a false
     flag, and a click on the disabled `crud-delete` at boot gives an empty diff (the flag after it is asserted
     false — predicted from the read of `events/pointer.rs:813-817`: nothing is focused, so no focus is written, and
     hover and active do not mark);
   - a fixture element hidden by a truthy `hidden` leaves the diff as removed with its descendants, and shown again
     returns as added, each with its parent's id;
   - a fixture password input: the first typed character names it with its value reading `MASKED_VALUE`; a second
     character reads flag true and an empty diff; the typed literal — synthetic — occurs in no `id`, `name` or
     `value` of any diff entry;
   - a fixture label whose text a click rewrites names the input it labels, by that input's id, and no text-run
     entry exists.
   In every test the diff of a step is equal across the two layout modes. **Content rule (the CARRY):** no diff,
   snapshot, name or value is printed or formatted into a message — assertions are `assert!(cond, "{mode}: …")`
   with mode and id labels; the file holds no `assert_eq!`, `assert_ne!`, `println!` or `dbg!`. Fixture controls an
   agent can act on carry an `id`. No deleting or platform-bound key is pressed (`.claude/rules/testing.md`).

8. **Counts, measured from the runs and recorded in the report**, never restated from this plan: blitz-dom
   `changed_set_` (predicted 0 → 7), dioxus-native-dom's unit census (predicted 41 → 49 in seven files),
   `stand_diff` (predicted 0 → 9), `run stand` (predicted 54 → 63), the workspace (predicted 518 · 0 · 5 over 130
   result lines → 542 · 0 · 5 over 131), `Ran 64 tests` unchanged.
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs` — `SnapshotDiff`, `DiffNode`, `Snapshot::diff` and their unit tests
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_diff.rs` — the stand check and its three in-file fixtures

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` — `create_node` no longer marks; `has_changes`; `take_changed_nodes`; the mark in `snapshot_node_and`; the unit tests (`has_changes @ packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:378` is its one caller; `create_node` has 7 non-test callers, none reads the set)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` — the mark at the 15 mutation-flag sites
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs` — the mark at a text control's input (`apply_generated_text_input_event @ events/keyboard.rs:97`, `events/ime.rs:24`)
- `packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs` — `View::poll` drains, and refreshes the platform tree when the set was non-empty
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs` — the gated `mod` and `pub use` lines and the crate doc's feature list

No live leg runs this chunk: the agent-run entries drive the in-process stand through `scripts/agent-run.sh` and no
external process is started, so there is no liveness probe and no `stop`. There is no headful self-verify — the stand
is headless (`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`). **Windowed boot smoke:** it runs because step 5 edits
`View::poll`, which every windowed app's event loop calls; the stand's windowed binary builds blitz-shell without
`accessibility`, so the smoke exercises the drain and proves the shell still boots and polls. It does not witness the
refresh — that branch is compiled out of this binary, and on this host AccessKit's `update_if_active` never runs the
tree build even where it is compiled in (`.claude/rules/a11y.md`, Session Additions) — so the refresh is proven at
the document level (the `changed_set_` tests), by the caller census and by both feature builds of blitz-shell, and
its windowed witness is an owed item (Implementation notes). The smoke declares `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`; unset, it is not
run and the report says so. The control of step 4 is implement's one-shot run, not an entry. The CI acceptance follows the operator pass (pre-CI commit, push, CI read).

What this chunk proves: on the stand, in both layout modes, a step being one harness input helper (or delivered timer ticks and a pump) on a booted lean task, read as `before.diff(&after)` over `DioxusDocument::snapshot` taken before and after it: the diff names a node, by its stable element id, exactly when its reading (role · name · state · bounds · parent) differs between the two snapshots or it is in one and not the other, and names no other; after a click on `counter-increment` it names `counter-value`; after CRUD's Create it names the new row `crud-person-3` as added and after its Delete as removed; after a click on a text input, a Tab press and Shift+Tab it names exactly the controls whose `focused` reading moved; after a typed character the text input; after delivered ticks `timer-elapsed`; and a step that changes nothing — a pump with nothing pending on each lean task, a click on the disabled `crud-delete` — returns an empty diff. data.head: ## Graph impact (from the code-graph query; rust plane, lines cited are the editor's)

body: - **`has_changes`** — 1 caller: `View::poll` @ `packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:378`. Its signature does not change; only what it answers.

- **`changed_nodes`** (field) — 3 references besides its definition (`document.rs:327`): the initialiser `:491`, the insert in `create_node` `:863`, the read in `has_changes` `:1010`. No reader drains it; no crate outside blitz-dom names it.

- **`create_node`** — 7 non-test callers: `BaseDocument::new` `document.rs:514` (the root node), `create_text_node` `:1016`, `deep_clone_node` `:1038`, layout's `create_anonymous_block` `layout/construct.rs:142` and `flush_pseudo_elements` `:712`, the mutator's `create_comment_node` `mutator.rs:135` and `create_element` `:148`. Two of the seven are layout, not mutation.

- **`snapshot_node_and`** (the element-state change helper) — 11 non-test call sites: focus (`clear_focus` `document.rs:1663`, `set_focus_to` `:1688`, `:1694`), active (`:1727`, `:1742`), hover (`:1882`, `:1885`, `:1911`), radio (`toggle_radio` `:700`), checkbox and radio clicks (`events/pointer.rs:647`, `:671`). `snapshot_node` (the attribute-change helper) — 2: `set_attribute` `mutator.rs:271`, `clear_attribute` `:399`.
- **`apply_generated_text_input_event`** — 2 callers: `events/keyboard.rs:97`, `events/ime.rs:24`. The one place a text control's editor change is announced.
- **`DioxusDocument::snapshot`** — 58 call sites, every one in a unit test or a `tests/blitz-tests` file; no library, binary or script calls it. A diff over two snapshots adds no caller threading.
- **`accessibility_tree`** — 3 callers: the shell's `update_tree` `blitz-shell/src/accessibility.rs:45`, `unkeyed_actionable` `actionable.rs:57`, `snapshot` `snapshot.rs:84`.
- **`update_tree`** — 2 callers: `View::poll` `window.rs:380` (behind the flag) and `View::build_accessibility_tree` `window.rs:523` (on `InitialTreeRequested`, `application.rs:81-82`).
- **Name collisions** — `diff`, `SnapshotDiff`, `snapshot_diff`, `take_changed_nodes`, `drain_changed_nodes`, `NodeChange`, `Change`: 0 rows on `symbol` — every candidate name is free.
- **Crate edges** — blitz-dom has 16 inbound crates, dioxus-native-dom 7. An additive public item on either breaks none; a changed answer from `has_changes` reaches blitz-shell only.

- **The flag is constant, not merely inverted** (`document.rs:514`, `:863`, `:1009-1010`): the constructor creates the root node through `create_node`, which inserts into `changed_nodes`; nothing removes from the set; `has_changes()` returns `changed_nodes.is_empty()`. So it reads `false` for every document from construction on, and the shell's `if has_changes { update_tree }` (`window.rs:378-381`) has never run. The platform accessibility tree is built once, on AccessKit's `InitialTreeRequested`, and never refreshed. By code read; no run measures it, and the dev host cannot (the a11y rule's addition: the AT-SPI bus reads inactive, so `update_if_active` skips the build).

- **The set is written by layout** (`layout/construct.rs:142`, `:712`): anonymous blocks and pseudo-element nodes are created through the same `create_node`. A set that keeps that write site reads "changed" after a resolve that only rebuilt boxes, and may differ between the two layout modes — non-incremental mode rebuilds boxes each resolve (architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns → Invalidation and state integrity). Not measured: whether an idle pump in non-incremental mode in fact creates nodes.

- **The mutator already tracks "did a rendered mutation occur"** (`mutator.rs:62`, `:69-76`): a per-mutator bool set at 15 write sites (`grep -n 'mutations_occurred |=' packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs`), each guarded by `node_is_in_document`, read once at `Drop` to request a redraw. Those 15 sites are exactly where a node-level mark would sit.

- **Element-state changes share one helper** (`document.rs:1540-1551`): focus, hover, active and checked all go through `snapshot_node_and(node_id, ElementState, cb)`; the state bits name which kind. Hover and active reach it on every pointer move and press — a mark there that did not select on the bits would make every click read as a change.

- **Writes that change a snapshot reading and bypass the mutator**: focus (`set_focus_to` / `clear_focus`, `document.rs:1660-1703` — `focused` on two nodes), checked (`events/pointer.rs:647-675`, `toggle_radio` `document.rs:686-703`), a text control's editor text (applied in the event handler, announced at `events/keyboard.rs:104-125`), scroll (`get_client_bounding_rect` subtracts `viewport_scroll()`, `document.rs:2249-2250` — a viewport scroll moves every node's bounds), a viewport resize.

- **A reading changes on nodes nothing wrote**: a node's `name` is its label, else the joined names of its `labelled_by` targets, a text run's name being its value (`snapshot.rs:160-179`) — a text node's edit renames its parent element and any input a `<label>` binds; `bounds` come from layout (`snapshot.rs:127`). So no per-node engine set equals "the nodes whose snapshot changed"; the equality the acceptance needs — the diff names node N **iff** N's reading differs between the two snapshots, or N is in one and not the other — is decided by comparing two `Snapshot` values, which `PartialEq` on `Snapshot` / `SnapshotNode` / `NodeState` (`snapshot.rs:17`, `:24`, `:45`) and the by-id reader `Snapshot::get` (`snapshot.rs:74-76`) support with no second reading of any control.

- **Equal snapshots are provable today**: `stand_snapshot::snapshot_is_deterministic` reads two snapshots of one screen equal, in both layout modes (called at `stand_snapshot.rs:398`, `:403`). A comparison of two readings with no step between them is therefore empty by construction.

- **The engine-touched, snapshot-unchanged case exists**: `set_node_text` writes only when the text differs (`mutator.rs:208-210`); `set_attribute` snapshots, damages and flags without comparing (`mutator.rs:268-316`). An attribute re-written to its own value touches the engine and changes no reading; so does a further character typed into a non-empty password input (the value reads `MASKED_VALUE` before and after, `snapshot.rs:207-210`).

- **A click that matches nothing clears focus** (`events/pointer.rs:813-817`): a click on a control the click handler does not match runs `clear_focus`. At boot nothing is focused, so the first click changes no `focused` reading; after a Tab press it can. Which controls match is not measured here — the stand check reads it from the diff rather than assuming it.

- **In-file fixtures boot with the stand's options** (`stand_snapshot_text.rs:387-389`): `Harness::from_vdom(VirtualDom::new(fixture), stand::options(incremental))` — the stand's pinned viewport and bundled font, not the harness default. The layouts extract's "harness default viewport" and the tests extract's "the stand's options" differ only in the font context; the existing fixtures settle it for the stand's.

- **Stand checks never format content into a message** (`stand_snapshot_text.rs:7`, `:117`, `:165-262`): content lives in `text`-named locals, assertions carry mode and id labels, nothing is printed. `assert_eq!` over two content values would print both on failure — the existing check uses `assert!(a == b, "{mode}: …")` for content.
- **Mutations through the mutator; marks beside the flag it already sets** — `DocumentMutator` (`mutator.rs:46-76`); never through `DocumentMutator::doc` from outside (CLAUDE.md invariant).
- **Stale ids read through `get_node`** — the snapshot's own reader does (`snapshot.rs:125-126`); a drained id may name a dropped node.

- **Feature gate and re-export** — a snapshot-level module is `#[cfg(feature = "accessibility")] mod …;` with a gated `pub use` and a line in the crate doc's feature list (`lib.rs:7-9`, `:20-23`, `:30-33`); module crate-private, types re-exported.

- **Tracing** — engine call sites sit under `#[cfg(feature = "tracing")]` (`document.rs:1681-1682`); the touched spans of `mutator.rs` hold 5 such sites (`:1147-1216`, image and iframe loading), `window.rs` 1 (`:835`), `snapshot.rs` and `snapshot_text.rs` none (`grep -n 'tracing::'`). The chunk needs none.

- **Unit tests** — blitz-dom: `BaseDocument::new(DocumentConfig::default())`, nodes through `create_node` / `document.mutate()` (`mutator.rs:1379-1400`). dioxus-native-dom: `build(app)` = `DioxusDocument::new` + `initial_build` + `resolve(0.0)` (`snapshot.rs:219-224`).

- **Stand checks** — `stand::boot(task, stand::options(incremental))` inside `for incremental in [false, true]`, input through the harness helpers, `#[track_caller]` on helpers (`stand_snapshot_state.rs:24-95`).
- **Public items documented** — the rustdoc gate runs `-D warnings` over every workspace crate; a new `pub fn` on `BaseDocument` and a new public type in dioxus-native-dom each carry `///`.
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs` — the diff over two snapshots and its unit tests
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_diff.rs` — the stand check: real steps on the lean tasks and the in-file fixtures, both layout modes
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` — the flag's answer, a drain, the set's write sites at node creation and at the focus and checked state changes
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` — the set's write sites at the mutation writers
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs` — the set's write site at a text control's editor change
- `packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs` — the flag's caller: what the poll does once the flag is truthful and who drains

- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs` — the gated `mod` and `pub use` lines and the crate doc's feature list

  The list is P4's fork as decided (the operator, 2026-10-07, at P4's question round): marks at the mutation writers, at focus and checked changes and at a typed character — so `packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs` is not written — and the diff is a pure function of two snapshots with no entry point of its own on `DioxusDocument`, so `dioxus_document.rs` is not written either. Sweeps: `has_changes` — 6 hits · 3 changed (the definition `document.rs:1009`, its caller's two lines `window.rs:378-379`) · 3 no-change (a local of the same name in `poll_subdocuments`, `document.rs:789`, `:799`, `:801`) — `grep -rn 'has_changes' --include=*.rs packages apps examples tests wpt`. `changed_nodes` — 4 hits · 3 changed or kept as the plan decides · 1 no-change (the initialiser) — same grep. `.claude/docs/services/blitz-dom.md:19` names the set as "the natural seed for snapshot diffs" — a derived doc, the wrap cascade's to re-derive.

- How far does the set's marking reach — every engine write an agent can read (mutations, focus, checked, typed text, scroll), so that the flag reading false means the snapshot did not change; or the mutation writers only, with a step's change flag read off the diff? → blocks: plan-decision

- What does the shell's poll do once the flag is truthful — refresh the platform tree when the set is non-empty and then drain it (the a11y plan's recorded intent, never yet the behaviour), with no windowed proof available on this host? → blocks: plan-decision
- Does this chunk give the diff a text form, or leave it a Rust value until the driver needs one? → blocks: plan-decision

**Working entry (verbatim):** Change tracking and diff — changed-node set drained per step, truthful change flag, empty diff for a no-op (v010-06)  CARRY: the snapshot's text form (from 2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization) — `Snapshot::to_text` exists: one line per node nested by indent, role · quoted name · `id=` · state tokens · bounds, strings in `str`'s `Debug` form (architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge), the form a diff can be written in; a diff carries the same content classes as that text (ids, accessible names, a text control's value), so the same answer binds it — it leaves the process through the returned value only (PROVISIONAL, pending the founder's word at the Epoch 3 boundary; security-plan §Input Validation, the `id` row), and a check never prints it or puts it into an assertion message (`stand_snapshot_text` is the shape)

**Epoch:** Epoch 3 — Observation model, its sixth and last entry (after Compact snapshot serialization; Epoch 4 — Driver core follows) · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Freight on the entry:** one `CARRY:` block (`route.py pins` row 47, 723 chars) — the only block on this line; no `BLOCKED-ON`, `PREREQ` or `WATCH`.

**Change tracking and the post-action diff**: intent §Findings 3 and requirements v010-06 — "after an action the driver returns exactly the nodes that changed; an action that changes nothing returns an empty diff". The snapshot model, the truth of its state and its text form are built (the three preceding entries); today nothing says what an action changed.

- **A changed-node set, drained per step** (the entry). The engine holds one today and it does not do the job: `BaseDocument::changed_nodes` (packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:327, a `HashSet<NodeId>`) is written at one site only — node creation (document.rs:863) — and is never read out or cleared anywhere in `packages/` (four mentions in the workspace: the field, its initialiser, that insert and the flag below). `[premise-corrected: the one write site is `BaseDocument::create_node` (document.rs:854-866), which the constructor calls for the root node (document.rs:514) and layout calls for anonymous blocks and pseudo-elements (layout/construct.rs:142, :712) — so the set is non-empty from construction and is written by layout, not by mutations alone; and writes that change a snapshot reading run beside the mutator — focus (document.rs:1660-1703), a checkbox or radio toggle (events/pointer.rs:647-675, document.rs:686-703), a text control's editor (events/keyboard.rs:103-125), scroll (bounds are viewport-relative, document.rs:2238-2254) (research.md §Patterns detected)]` "Drained per step" needs both halves built — the set written where the engine writes what an agent can read, and a reader that takes it and leaves it empty — but the set names engine nodes that were written, never the snapshot nodes that changed: a reading changes on nodes no write touched (a name drawn from a text child or a `<label>`, bounds moved by layout or scroll). Which write sites mark the set is P4's fork.

- **A truthful change flag** (the entry). `BaseDocument::has_changes` returns `self.changed_nodes.is_empty()` (document.rs:1009-1010) — inverted, as intent §3 observes. `[premise-corrected: no document is ever "untouched" to this flag — the constructor creates the root node through `create_node` (document.rs:514) and nothing drains the set, so `has_changes()` reads `false` for every document at all times, and the shell's poll-time accessibility refresh has never fired; the platform tree is built only on AccessKit's `InitialTreeRequested` (blitz-shell application.rs:81-82 → window.rs:521-523). By code read, not measured by a run]` Its one caller is the windowed shell, which gates its AccessKit tree update on it (packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:378-380; verified — the code graph's `calls` on `has_changes` returns that one row); making the flag truthful — and draining the set — changes when that update fires, which is accessibility surface (CLAUDE.md: `accessibility` is a default feature). What the shell does after the fix is this chunk's to state and prove or to leave provably unchanged, never a silent side effect.

- **The diff** (the entry: "empty diff for a no-op"; `matrix.py show --id v010-06`: "the returned diff names exactly the nodes whose snapshot changed and no others"). The diff is stated in the snapshot's terms, not the engine's: its subjects are snapshot nodes keyed by stable element id, and a node is in the diff when its snapshot reading (role · name · state · bounds) differs across the step, or when it appeared or disappeared. Verified: `Snapshot`, `SnapshotNode` and `NodeState` derive `PartialEq` (snapshot.rs:17, :24, :45) and `Snapshot::nodes()` / `get(&str)` read by pre-order and by id (snapshot.rs:64-76), so two readings compare with no second reading of any control. `[premise-corrected: of the three relations named at take-up only the before/after comparison can be exact — the engine's set holds `NodeId`s of text nodes and anonymous blocks, which read no stable id, and cannot name an element whose name or bounds moved because another node was written; the set is the flag's source, never the diff's (research.md §Patterns detected)]` How far the set's marking reaches is P4's design. "Exactly … and no others" binds both ways: no changed node missed, no unchanged node named.

- **An empty diff for a no-op** (the entry). A step that changes nothing — an action on a control that takes no effect, a pump with nothing pending — yields a diff with no entries and a change flag reading false; an action that re-writes a value to what it already was is the case that separates "the engine touched a node" from "the snapshot changed", and which of the two the flag reports is stated by the plan. Verified: the separating case exists in the engine — `set_node_text` writes only when the text differs (mutator.rs:208-210) while `set_attribute` damages and flags unconditionally (mutator.rs:268-316), so an attribute re-written to its own value is engine-touched and snapshot-unchanged. Not verified by a run: that a pump with nothing pending leaves the set empty in non-incremental mode, where layout re-creates anonymous blocks through `create_node` — the plan owes a check of it in both modes.

- **"Step"** — no driver exists yet (Epoch 4), so in this chunk a step is one harness action on a stand screen followed by the pump that resolves it, driven by a stand check; the driver session that owns a step, and settle detection that ends one, are Epoch 4's (Driver session · Settle detection). Verified: every harness constructor pumps once and every input helper pumps after its dispatch, `pump` being `poll(None)` then `resolve` (harness.rs:123-126; `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`); focus and editor text change at dispatch, vdom writes land at `poll` (dioxus_document.rs:256-286) — so a step's reading is taken after the helper returns.

- **Proven on the stand** — the four lean tasks booted through `seven_guis::stand` (intent §Principles, "The stand is the proof"), in both layout modes (`for incremental in [false, true]`, CLAUDE.md invariant): a diff after a real action names the nodes that changed (counter's count after a click is the plain case), and a no-op yields none. `[premise-corrected: the lean tasks do not lack a node added or removed — CRUD's Create and Delete add and remove a row keyed `crud-person-{id}` (crud.rs:103, :126; layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens), so those two are proven on the stand itself]` Where the lean tasks do lack a case — a value re-written unchanged, a node hidden and shown by attribute, a masked control — a minimal fixture beside the stand proves it (the founder's ruling, 2026-10-06), booted as the existing ones are: `Harness::from_vdom(VirtualDom::new(fixture), stand::options(incremental))` (stand_snapshot_text.rs:387-389).

- **A text form for the diff** — the CARRY says the snapshot's text form is "the form a diff can be written in"; whether this chunk writes the diff as text at all, or leaves it a Rust value until the driver needs one, is P4's. Verified open: v010-06's acceptance names a returned diff and no text, and `Snapshot::to_text`'s contract closes off a second entry point (architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge), so a diff text would be a new contract item.

- **CARRY, folded (the snapshot's text form — from 2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization).** Coordinates re-verified against the artifacts at take-up:
  - "`Snapshot::to_text` exists: one line per node nested by indent, role · quoted name · `id=` · state tokens · bounds, strings in `str`'s `Debug` form (architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge)" — `pub fn to_text(&self) -> String` is packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs:36, `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` is :16; the Dioxus DOM bridge bullet is architecture.md:134.
  - "a diff carries the same content classes as that text (ids, accessible names, a text control's value), so the same answer binds it — it leaves the process through the returned value only (PROVISIONAL, pending the founder's word at the Epoch 3 boundary; security-plan §Input Validation, the `id` row)" — the row is security-plan.md:107 (accessible names :108, the masked values :109). The answer is carried as written: the diff is returned to its caller and reaches no log, event, file or stdout in this chunk; its provisional standing is unchanged by this chunk and is not this chunk's to settle. A password's or a file input's value in a diff is the model's `MASKED_VALUE`, never a second reading of the control.
  - "a check never prints it or puts it into an assertion message (`stand_snapshot_text` is the shape)" — tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_text.rs exists; its header (:7) states the rule and its assertions carry mode and id labels only. The stand check this chunk adds follows it: no diff content in a `println!`, a `dbg!` or an assertion message.

- In: the engine's change tracking (the set written where the engine writes what an agent can read — how far is P4's fork — its drain, the flag); the diff over the snapshot and its unit tests; the stand check that drives real actions and asserts the diff; what the shell's accessibility update does once the flag is truthful.

- Out: the driver session and its per-command step, settle detection, the command and refusal schema, act-by-id, the CLI and the MCP surface (Epochs 4–5) — the diff is an in-process Rust API here, as the snapshot and its text are. Out: a mutation *stream* (an ordered log of operations) — intent §3 observes none exists and expects a diff, not a stream.

- Out: the founder's two provisional items at the Epoch 3 boundary (the bridge's 27-name falsy clear; the snapshot text's exit) — this chunk closes the epoch's entries, the boundary batch is the operator's.
- DOM mutations go through `DocumentMutator` (CLAUDE.md invariant) — tracking is added where the mutator and the document already write, never by reaching through `DocumentMutator::doc`.

- `NodeId` is a versioned slot id (CLAUDE.md invariant): a changed set can hold the id of a node dropped later in the same step — every read of a tracked id uses `get` / `contains_key`, never an index.

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` (the set, the flag, a drain; the focus and state setters) and `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` (where mutations are written). Verified: both exist; the mutator already records "a mutation that affects rendered output" per mutator lifetime at 15 write sites (`mutations_occurred`, mutator.rs:62 — `grep -n 'mutations_occurred |=' packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs`).
