- **Marker:** 2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-07T12:03:42Z

Give the driver its one definition of what can be asked of it and of how it says no. `escher-driver` gains, in
process and as `'static` data, a closed verb set with each verb's argument and result shapes; a validation that
turns a call into a typed command or a refusal before anything runs; and a closed set of refusal causes, each
with a fixed remedy. Every later surface reads this one table — the actions ("Act by id"), the detection of the
screen-level causes ("Refusal detection"), the span's cause field ("Driver command spans"), the CLI, the MCP
tools and the self-description (per intent §Principles, "the driver's command and refusal model as one schema";
architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session; security-plan §Input Validation).

Nothing here runs a command, reaches the socket or serves the schema. The verb set is the core five — `snapshot`,
`click`, `type`, `press`, `advance` — in a table the later entries extend with their own verbs when the questions
the route reserves for them are asked (the operator, 2026-10-07, at the P4 forks). `advance` is the answer to the
first carried question: time on a held instance moves when an agent asks for it, in milliseconds, through a step
the session's caller supplies. The second carried question is answered no: no driver command waits on a load.

The chunk claims no capability. v010-11 and v010-14 each need a surface a later entry builds and each is listed on
that entry (Implementation notes, "No capability is claimed").
Files and conventions are research.md's (§New files to create · §Files to modify · §Conventions to follow).

1. **The cause set — `packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs` (new).** A public closed enum `Cause` of eight
   causes, in this order, each with a `name` (lowercase, hyphenated — the stub's spelling where the two overlap),
   a one-sentence `meaning` and a `remedy`, all three `&'static str`; a constant listing all eight; `Display`
   printing the name.

   | variant | name | meaning | remedy |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `UnknownVerb` | `unknown-verb` | the call names no verb of the verb set | use a verb the verb list names |
   | `Malformed` | `malformed` | the call's arguments are not the ones the verb's schema states | pass exactly the arguments the verb's schema names, each of the kind and within the bound it states |
   | `NotFound` | `not-found` | no element on the screen reads the id | take a snapshot and use an id it lists |
   | `Stale` | `stale` | the id read an element earlier in this session and no element reads it now | the screen changed since the id was read: take a new snapshot and act on what it lists |
   | `Disabled` | `disabled` | the element carries the `disabled` attribute, which the snapshot reads as not enabled | the control is disabled: change the state that disables it, then act again |
   | `Covered` | `covered` | another element is hit at the point the action would land | another element covers this one: act on the covering element or dismiss it first |
   | `OffScreen` | `off-screen` | the element lies outside the viewport | the element is outside the viewport: bring it into view, then act again |
   | `TimeUnavailable` | `time-unavailable` | the app this session holds gives it no way to move its time | this session cannot move time: act without `advance`, or start a session whose host supplies a time step |

   The texts above are the stated ones; a rewording is recorded in the report, never silent.

2. **The fault and the refusal — same file.** A public closed enum `Fault` naming which rule a malformed call
   broke: an argument the schema requires is missing; an argument the schema does not name was passed; an
   argument was passed twice; an argument's value is not of its kind; an argument's value is outside its bound.
   Each variant that names an argument holds the SCHEMA's own argument name as a `&'static str` — never a name or
   a value taken from the call; the unnamed-argument variant holds nothing. A public struct `Refusal` holds a
   `Cause` and an optional `Fault` (present only with `Malformed`), with `Display` built from the cause's name,
   its remedy and the fault's fixed words, and `std::error::Error`. Neither type has a `String` field: nothing of
   a call can be in a refusal, by type.

3. **The verb table — `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` (new).** Public `'static` data, no serialization
   crate:
   - an argument kind with five members and the bound each states — `id` (1 to 1024 bytes of text; an author key
     is arbitrary text, so no character class), `text` (0 to 4096 bytes), `key` (one name of the closed key list),
     `flag` (true or false), `milliseconds` (a whole number, 1 to 60 000); the three bounds are public constants;
   - the closed key list, twelve names: `tab` · `enter` · `escape` · `backspace` · `delete` · `space` ·
     `arrow-up` · `arrow-down` · `arrow-left` · `arrow-right` · `home` · `end`;
   - an argument spec (name, kind, required or optional, help) and a result-field spec (name, kind, present always
     or only sometimes, help), the field kinds being text, flag, milliseconds, busy class (`render` · `layout` ·
     `loads`), a list of ids, and a list of nodes whose own fields are stated once (`id` · `parent` · `role` ·
     `name` · `enabled` · `checked` · `value` · `focused` · `bounds` — the diff node's fields, by name only);
   - a verb spec (name, help, argument specs, result-field specs), the constant table of the five verbs in the
     order below, and a lookup by exact name.

   | verb | arguments | result fields |
   |---|---|---|
   | `snapshot` | none | `text` |
   | `click` | `id` (id, required) | the acting fields |
   | `type` | `id` (id, required) · `text` (text, required) | the acting fields |
   | `press` | `key` (key, required) · `shift` (flag, optional) | the acting fields |
   | `advance` | `ms` (milliseconds, required) | the acting fields · `advanced_ms` |

   The acting fields: `settled` (flag) · `busy` (busy class, only when `settled` is false) · `added` (nodes) ·
   `removed` (ids) · `changed` (nodes). A step that ran and did not go quiet is reported here, as `settled: false`
   with its class — it is not a refusal, because the step is not rolled back. `advance`'s help states the unit in
   the schema itself: it moves the app's time forward by `ms` milliseconds and then settles; an app moves time in
   its own units, and `advanced_ms` is the time it actually moved, never more than asked. Help texts name no app,
   no stand type and no element of the stand.

4. **The call and its validation — `packages/escher-driver/src/command.rs` (new).** A call as owned data: a verb
   name and a list of named argument values, a value being text, a whole number or a flag. A public closed enum
   `Command` with one variant per verb carrying its validated values (the key as a member of a public closed
   `Key` enum mirroring the key list), a function from a call to `Result<Command, Refusal>`, and a way from a
   `Command` to its verb spec. The function receives no `Session`. Its order, so every call has ONE answer:
   (a) the verb is looked up by exact name — absent → `UnknownVerb`; (b) the call's arguments in the order given —
   a name the verb's spec lacks → `Malformed` with the unnamed-argument fault; a spec name seen a second time →
   the passed-twice fault; (c) the spec's arguments in the spec's order — a required one absent → missing; a value
   not of the kind → wrong kind; a value outside the bound, or a text that is no name of the key list → outside
   its bound. The first failure in that order is the refusal. No `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `unreachable!` or
   index on anything a call supplies.

5. **The crate root — `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs`.** Declare the three private modules, re-export every
   public item of steps 1–4, and add one paragraph to the crate doc: the schema is held in process, nothing of it
   crosses the socket, and no command runs through a session yet. Every public item carries `///`
   (`#![deny(missing_docs)]`, `lib.rs:21`). No other file of the crate is edited and no manifest.

6. **Unit tests, inline at the end of each new file** (built-in harness; every table stated in the test, never
   read back from the code under test; every row asserted unconditionally; each table's row count asserted):
   - `refusal.rs` — (T1) the eight names, in order, against a stated table; (T2) each cause's meaning and remedy
     against step 1's table, stated again in the test, and over all eight: names pairwise distinct, meanings and
     remedies non-empty, remedies pairwise distinct, no `/` in any text; (T3) a refusal's
     `Display` for every cause and every fault variant is non-empty, opens with the cause's name and holds no `/`.
   - `schema.rs` — (T4) the five verb names, in order, against a stated table; (T5) over every verb: help
     non-empty, argument names unique within the verb, every argument and result-field help non-empty, at least
     one result field; (T6) the lookup finds each stated name and refuses a name differing only in case or
     padding; (T7) each verb's arguments (name, kind, required) and result-field names against a stated table,
     and the twelve key names against a stated list.
   - `command.rs` — (T8) admitted calls, each to its expected `Command`: every verb, `press` with and without
     `shift`, and the bounds' edges (an id of exactly 1024 bytes, an empty `text`, `ms` 1 and 60 000); (T9)
     unknown verbs → `UnknownVerb`: the empty name, an upper-case name, a padded name, the lifecycle word `stop`,
     the later verb `screenshot`; (T10) malformed calls, one witness per rule per kind, each to its expected
     cause and fault: a missing required argument, an unnamed argument, an argument passed twice, each kind given
     a value of another kind, an empty id, an id of 1025 bytes, a text of 4097 bytes, `ms` 0, `ms` 60 001, a
     negative `ms`, a key name outside the list; (T11) a call breaking two rules returns the one step 4's order
     puts first, for two stated pairs; (T12) every verb of the table is reached by a row of T8 and the `Command`
     reached names that verb's spec — five of five.

7. **Controls, recorded in `evidence/controls.md`** (implement's hand record; each mutation applied, the named
   test read red, the mutation reverted): the passed-twice check removed → T10; the id bound compared with `<`
   where it reads `<=` → T8; two remedies swapped → T2; one verb dropped from the table → T4 and T12.
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` — the verb table, the argument and field kinds, the key list, the bounds
- `packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs` — `Cause`, `Fault`, `Refusal`
- `packages/escher-driver/src/command.rs` — the call, `Command`, `Key`, the validation
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` — three module declarations, the re-exports, one crate-doc paragraph

No entry is a live leg: nothing here drives a process the launch environment names, so there is no liveness probe
and no `stop` key. There is no headful self-verify harness on this project and this chunk changes no screen. No
smoke entry: the chunk adds no boot path and edits none — the `escher-session` binary and its sources are
byte-identical to the base, which the preservation entry asserts. The agent-run `stand` selection is not listed:
the chunk adds no `stand_*` check, so its count stands at 80 (test-plan §3, as the last wrap recorded it). The
audit leg is not listed: no manifest and no lockfile changes, which the preservation entry asserts. **Not run
locally:** the MSRV build and the windows, macos, ios and android matrix legs — the fork's CI run is their one
witness; the CI acceptance follows the operator pass (pre-CI commit, push, CI read). The preservation entry names
its base as the commit this chunk starts from, `294ff415`.

`evidence/controls.md` has no listed producer, by construction: it is implement's hand record of step 7's
mutations, each reverted, which no entry could re-produce at the wrap's light gate.

- (arch) No source file of `escher-driver` names an app, a stand type or `TimerTicks`, the `advance` verb's help included — the `seven_guis|LeanTask|TimerTicks` census reads 0 (per architecture §Established Decisions → [Driver session]).

- (security) Every row of the malformed-call table — a missing, an unnamed and a twice-passed argument, each kind given another kind's value, each bound crossed — is refused as a typed `Refusal` naming `malformed` and its fault, and every unknown verb as `unknown-verb`; none panics — T9, T10 and T11 under the `command::` entry (per security-plan §Input Validation, Cold-agent MCP stub row; security-plan §Error Handling, Error format (typed errors)).

- (security) A refused call changes nothing on a held instance by construction: the validation takes a call and returns a command or a refusal, and receives no `Session` — the signature of step 4, cited in the report with its `file:line` (per security-plan §Input Validation, Driver session label row).

- (security) Every cause's name, meaning and remedy is a non-empty fixed `&'static str` holding no path, and no field of `Refusal` or `Fault` can hold anything a call supplied — T1, T2 and T3 under the `refusal::` entry, and the two type definitions (per security-plan §Input Validation, CLI arguments (escher-session) row).

- (security) No verb of the set has a shape that waits on a load or reads a clock: the table holds five verbs and no argument or field of a wait — T4 and T7; question 2's answer is recorded as the operator's (per security-plan §API Security, Settle and loads in flight row).

- (tests) The three module entries each pass with at least one test and no failure, and `cargo test -p escher-driver --locked` passes whole; the crate's unit-test count is read from that run and recorded against the standing 13 (per test-plan §4 Unit Test Strategy — What unit tests cover → escher-driver).
- (tests) Each of step 7's mutations turns its named test red and is reverted — `evidence/controls.md` (per test-plan §4 Unit Test Strategy — What unit tests cover → Conditional assertions).

- (tests) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` and `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` pass; the workspace passed · failed · ignored counts are read from that run and recorded against 598 · 0 · 8, with the existing session checks green and unedited (per test-plan §9 CI Integration — Pipeline facts → Local pre-push gate).

- (tests) The fork's CI run on the pushed sha reads `verdict: green`, its run id named in the report — the only witness of the MSRV build and of the windows and macos legs of the new code (per test-plan §1 Test Scope Summary — Surfaces under test → Native platforms).

- (obs) The three new modules and the crate root install no subscriber, read no env var or clock and print or log nothing; `escher-driver` ends with no span, no event and no `tracing` or `log` dependency — the census entry reads 0 and the preservation entry holds the manifest (per obs-plan §3 Logging stack; obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage).

- (obs) A cause's name is a class word with no id, name or value in it, and no test's name or assertion message carries an argument value — T1's stated table and the test source (per obs-plan §8 Scrubbing).

- (a11y) The `disabled` cause's stated meaning names the presence reading — the attribute's presence, which the snapshot reads as not enabled — and no shape of the schema defines a role or a name set of its own: `role` and `name` are field names only (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support, Accessibility tree output; a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation, Focus order).

- (a11y) No result shape names a snapshot type, so `escher-driver`'s manifest names no `dioxus-native-dom` feature — the preservation entry; `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh a11y` passes with its three files (per a11y-plan §1 A11y Scope Summary, Dioxus crates; a11y-plan §9 CI Integration).

- (layouts) No element, id, class, style, wrapper or order changes on the lean tasks or the TaskShell mount, and `escher-session` keeps its two-argument argv, its exit codes and its empty stdout — the preservation entry holds `examples/seven_guis` byte-identical to the base (per layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens; layout-templates §Surface: cli → Primary screens).

- Spec anchors the plan rests on (from the extracts): architecture §Existing Scopes → escher-driver, §Standard Contracts → Driver session · → Test harness · → Dioxus DOM bridge · → CI contracts, §Established Decisions → [Driver session], §Occupied Resources → Network ports and listeners · → Names, §Conventions → Manifests · → Tests · → Error handling; security-plan §Input Validation, §API Security, §Error Handling, §Logging & Monitoring, §Dependency Security; test-plan §1, §3 → Session lifecycle, §4, §8 Time, §9; obs-plan §3, §4, §6, §8; a11y-plan §1, §5, §7, §9; layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native · §Surface: cli. design-system: no domain coverage.

- Research files inspected: `packages/escher-driver/src/{lib,error,session,wire,host,client}.rs` and `Cargo.toml`, `examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs` and `tasks/timer.rs`, `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/{settle,harness,input}.rs`, `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/{actionable,snapshot,snapshot_diff}.rs`, `scripts/cold_agent_stub.py`, `.github/scripts/test_cold_agent.py`, `escher-0.1.0/working-route.md` lines 62 · 64 · 71 · 73 · 75 · 77.

- The operator's three answers (the operator, 2026-10-07, at the P4 forks; `references/gate-contract.md` §Scope, *Whose word*):
  - **time** — a verb the caller steps; "the schema itself must say what one step is, so an agent learns the unit from the tool alone", and "an app with no time seam refuses the verb with a named cause and a remedy". Weighed as directed: a duration in milliseconds against a bare step count — milliseconds taken, because a step's size is the app's and the library names no app, so a count would need knowledge from outside the tool, while a millisecond needs none; the result's `advanced_ms` says what an app with a coarser unit actually moved.
  - **loads** — no: report and return; the cost is a residual (Implementation notes).
  - **verb set** — the core verbs in one table the later entries extend.

- Leans stated, each on an artifact:
  - **no capability is claimed** — v010-11's and v010-14's requirement lines each name a surface this chunk does not build, and each cap is listed on another markerless entry (working-route.md:64, :75).
  - leaned **no serialization crate** — a `'static` table is readable as data; the route gives JSON to "Driver CLI" (working-route.md:71) and architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge records that the snapshot has one serialized form and the diff none.
  - leaned **the refusal is its own type, and `SessionError` stays twelve** — architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session records the set as exactly its lifecycle edges, pinned by a hand-listed test (`error.rs:78-96`).
  - leaned **not settled is a result, not a refusal** — `Session::act` does not roll its step back (`session.rs:66-67`), and a refused call changes nothing.
  - leaned **a refusal carries nothing of the call** — security-plan §Input Validation (CLI arguments (escher-session) row): an error's text is a fixed message with no path, label, id or value; the caller holds the id it sent.
  - leaned **an unknown verb has its own cause** — security-plan §Input Validation (Driver session socket row): the wire already separates a known word from everything else, and a fixed remedy per cause is only useful when the cause is narrow.
  - leaned **result shapes name fields, not Rust types** — the `accessibility` feature on `escher-driver` is decided by "the entry that first reads the snapshot through a session" (working-route.md:62).
  - leaned **the cold-agent stub is left as it is** — it is a ratified toy model pinned by nine rows (`.github/scripts/test_cold_agent.py:163-171`); the schema takes its spelling for the three names they share.

- No `verdict: escalate` pattern of `.andromeda/playbook.md` is met by the option taken on any fork (its two: Boundary widening, Provisional discharge): the schema is held in process and nothing new crosses a boundary; the answers are the operator's own, so none is provisional.
- A bare step count for `advance` — rejected on the operator's criterion: its unit is the app's, which the library cannot name, so an agent would need knowledge from outside the tool.
- A verb or an argument that waits on a load, or any clock read in the schema's code — rejected (the operator, 2026-10-07).

- `screenshot`, a key-check verb, `help` and the lifecycle commands in this chunk's table — out: each joins the table at its own entry's promotion, where its reserved question is asked (the operator, 2026-10-07).
- A thirteenth `SessionError` variant, or `NotSettled` recast as a cause — rejected: see the leans.
- `serde`, `serde_json` or a JSON form of any result — rejected for this chunk: no manifest moves.

- Naming `Snapshot`, `SnapshotDiff`, `DiffNode`, `accesskit::Role` or `keyboard_types::Key` in a schema item — rejected: the first three need a feature this crate does not name, and the crate depends on neither of the last two.
- A `Session` method that takes a call, or any step run on a held instance — out: running a command is "Act by id".
- Editing `scripts/cold_agent_stub.py` or its tests — out: see the leans.
- An id, a name, a value or an argument name taken from the call inside a `Refusal`, a `Fault`, a test name or an assertion message — banned: a failing leg's log is uploaded as a CI artifact.
- Do not edit `wire.rs`, `host.rs`, `client.rs`, `session.rs`, `error.rs`, any manifest, `examples/seven_guis`, `tests/` or `scripts/` — the preservation entry fails on any of them.
- No std API newer than Rust 1.91: the dev host compiles on a newer stable and only the fork's CI builds the MSRV.
- **Order** — steps 1–2, then 3, then 4 (it reads both), then 5; step 6's tests are written with each file; step 7 last.

- **Mechanism the plan rests on** — *a validation that receives no session cannot change one*: the equality the "changes nothing" criterion needs is carried by the function's signature, not by a run; the report cites the signature. *One answer per call*: step 4's order is total — (a), then the call's arguments in call order, then the spec's arguments in spec order — and T11 is its control.

- **`backspace` is in the key list, and typed deletion is not solved here** — on macOS a headless Backspace deletes nothing (the CARRY on working-route.md:62); the name is a member of the vocabulary, its behaviour is "Act by id"'s.

- **Argument names against the sink's scrub set** — `text` is one of the eleven redacted field names; `id`, `key`, `shift` and `ms` are not (obs-plan §8 Scrubbing). A later span that fields an argument by its schema name would print an id. Owed to "Driver command spans" below.

- **No capability is claimed.** v010-11 (requirement: "an action that cannot happen is refused with its cause named") needs actions and their detection; "Refusal detection" lists it. v010-14 (requirement: "help and schemas served by the tool itself") needs both serving surfaces; "Self-description" lists it. Both stay pooled, each with a dated ledger note written at P5 step 4. /implement writes no `ref` and the report claims nothing.

- **Owed to the route (wrap's route-resolve) — "Act by id"** — the wiring of `advance`: the step a session's caller supplies at start, the stand host's mapping of milliseconds onto Timer ticks (one tick is 0.1 s, `timer.rs:57-60`), what it does with a remainder and reports as `advanced_ms`, whether the harness's own clock moves with it (`Harness::tick`, `harness.rs:152-155`), and `time-unavailable` for a session with no step. v010-10's driver leg has its route once this is wired; the CARRY's first question is answered and can be discharged from this entry's line.

- **Owed to the route — "Refusal detection"** — the five screen-level causes are named and worded here and detected there: what distinguishes `stale` from `not-found` needs the session to remember ids it has read; and the `off-screen` remedy says "bring it into view" while the core set has no verb that scrolls — that entry decides between a verb joining the table and an action that brings its target into view itself.
- **Owed to the route — "Driver command spans"** — the span's cause field takes a `Cause` name; no argument is fielded by its schema name (see the scrub-set note).
- **Owed to the route — "Driver CLI", "MCP surface", "Self-description", "Headless screenshot"** — each adds its verbs to this table at its promotion; none is pre-shaped here.

- **Residual (wrap's route-resolve, on the operator's word, 2026-10-07)** — no driver command waits on a load in 0.1.0, so an app that loads over the network must be polled by its caller; target: the version that first drives such an app.

- **Citations will move** — `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` gains lines above and inside the ranges the masters cite into it (grep `escher-driver/src/lib.rs:` over `.andromeda/*.md` at the wrap). A measured line map, not the plan's coordinates.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session — the schema's public items, the verb table and the cause set; the "not built" clause now reads a verb set built in process, none on the socket, no command run.
- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Existing Scopes → escher-driver — eight private modules where it names five.
- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan §Input Validation — a row for the schema's argument validation: the closed verb table, the five kinds and their bounds, refusal before any step.
- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan §API Security — question 2's answer beside "Settle and loads in flight": no driver command waits on a load (the operator, 2026-10-07).
- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan §Error Handling — the refusal type under Error format: a closed cause set, fixed texts, nothing of the call.
- Expected amendments (wrap): test-plan §4 Unit Test Strategy → escher-driver — the unit-test count and the three new pins; §9 Local baseline — the workspace link.

- Expected amendments (wrap): obs-plan §3 Logging stack — the crate's silence covers the three new modules; §4 Span / Trace Coverage — the cause set exists as the value domain the later span field reads.
- Expected amendments (wrap): a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support — the `disabled` cause is stated on the presence reading, beside the snapshot's `enabled`.

  - `refusal.rs` — `enum Cause` (8 variants, in order: `UnknownVerb`, `Malformed`, `NotFound`, `Stale`, `Disabled`, `Covered`, `OffScreen`, `TimeUnavailable`; `Copy`) with `const fn name(self) -> &'static str` (`unknown-verb` · `malformed` · `not-found` · `stale` · `disabled` · `covered` · `off-screen` · `time-unavailable`), `const fn meaning(self) -> &'static str`, `const fn remedy(self) -> &'static str`, and `Display` printing the name; `const CAUSES: [Cause; 8]`; `enum Fault` (5 variants: `Missing(&'static str)`, `Unnamed`, `Repeated(&'static str)`, `WrongKind(&'static str)`, `OutOfBound(&'static str)` — the `&'static str` is the schema's own argument name; `Copy`, `Display`); `struct Refusal` (private fields `cause: Cause`, `fault: Option<Fault>`; `const fn new(cause)`, `const fn malformed(fault)`, `const fn cause(&self)`, `const fn fault(&self)`; `Copy`, `Display` as `{name}: {remedy}` or `{name} ({fault}): {remedy}`, `std::error::Error`).   - `schema.rs` — `const MAX_ID_BYTES: usize = 1024`, `const MAX_TEXT_BYTES: usize = 4096`, `const MAX_MILLISECONDS: u32 = 60_000`; `const KEY_NAMES: [&str; 12]` (`tab` · `enter` · `escape` · `backspace` · `delete` · `space` · `arrow-up` · `arrow-down` · `arrow-left` · `arrow-right` · `home` · `end`); `const BUSY_CLASSES: [&str; 3]` (`render` · `layout` · `loads`); `const NODE_FIELDS: [&str; 9]` (`id` · `parent` · `role` · `name` · `enabled` · `checked` · `value` · `focused` · `bounds`); `enum ArgKind` (`Id`, `Text`, `Key`, `Flag`, `Milliseconds`; `name()`, `bound()`); `struct ArgSpec { name, kind, required, help }`; `enum FieldKind` (`Text`, `Flag`, `Milliseconds`, `Busy`, `Ids`, `Nodes`; `name()`); `struct FieldSpec { name, kind, always, help }`; `struct VerbSpec { name, help, args, fields }`; `const VERBS: &[VerbSpec]` (5 verbs, in order: `snapshot`, `click`, `type`, `press`, `advance`); `fn verb(name: &str) -> Option<&'static VerbSpec>` (exact name only).
  - `command.rs` — `enum ArgValue` (`Text(String)`, `Number(i64)`, `Flag(bool)`); `struct Call { verb: String, args: Vec<(String, ArgValue)> }`; `enum Key` (12 variants mirroring `KEY_NAMES`; `const ALL: [Key; 12]`, `const fn name(self)`, `fn from_name(&str) -> Option<Key>`); `enum Command` (`Snapshot`, `Click { id }`, `Type { id, text }`, `Press { key, shift }`, `Advance { ms: u32 }`; `const fn spec(&self) -> &'static VerbSpec`); `fn validate(call: &Call) -> Result<Command, Refusal>` at `packages/escher-driver/src/command.rs:161` — it receives no `Session`.

- **Two remedy precedents that differ** — `SessionError`'s messages are fixed strings (`error.rs:10`); `UnkeyedActionable::remedy()` interpolates the tag and the id (`actionable.rs:38-43`). Only the first is a fixed-text precedent.

- **A validation that takes no session cannot change one.** `Session::act` does not roll back (`session.rs:66-67`), so "a refused call changes nothing" holds only when the call is decided before any step runs. A function from a call to `Result<command, refusal>` that receives no `Session` holds it by construction; a held-instance check of it would assert nothing the signature does not already state.

- **The host cannot reach the tick handle while serving.** `serve` consumes the session and blocks in `accept` (`host.rs:48`, `:107-123`); the handle lives in `main`'s frame on the same thread (`session_host.rs:35-45`). A host that delivers ticks needs a change inside `escher-driver::serve` or a hook the caller hands the session — the binary alone cannot do it.

- **Two clocks, both the caller's.** The Timer's time moves by `TimerTicks::deliver` (`timer.rs:20-26`); animation time moves by `Harness::tick` (`harness.rs:152-155`), which `settle` reads and never advances (`settle.rs:145-148`, `:152`).

- Does the verb set hold the whole 0.1.0 vocabulary now, or the verbs whose shapes rest on what is built, in one table the later entries extend? → blocks: plan-decision (six shape decisions are reserved by later entries' freight)
**Working entry (verbatim):** Command and refusal schema — one verb set, argument and result shapes, malformed arguments refused, refusal causes each with a remedy (v010-11, v010-14)

**Epoch:** Epoch 4 — Driver core · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Freight on the entry:** one `CARRY:` block of 755 characters, folded below under "The carried questions" (`route.py pins`, trail in the run dir: 26 freight blocks on the markerless tail, all `CARRY:`, one of them on line 60, and no abstention printed). No `BLOCKED-ON`, `PREREQ` or `WATCH` on the entry. No external input: every fact below is read from this repository or the route.

**Premise closure (P3):** every `[inferred]` bullet below was re-read against `research.md`. A bullet with no tag is what the entry states or is verified; a corrected one carries `[premise-corrected: …]`.

The driver's third piece, after the session and settle: the **one definition of the driver's commands and of its refusals** that every later surface reads. intent §Principles orders it — "the driver's command and refusal model as one schema → its CLI, then its MCP surface" — and intent §9 states what it serves: "one consistent verb set, help and schemas from the tool itself, every refusal naming its remedy".
- **One verb set** — a closed list of the driver's commands, stated once.

- **Which verbs the set holds** is not on the entry. `[premise-corrected: six of the shape decisions are reserved by later entries' freight — research.md §Patterns detected, "Decisions the route reserves"]` The route's later entries name what the commands must cover: the lifecycle already built (`start` · `attach` · `stop`, and `hello` on the wire — `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs:31-33`, `wire.rs:25-28`); the snapshot read (v010-04's command leg, a CARRY on "Driver CLI", working-route.md:71); acting by stable id (working-route.md:62); the screenshot (working-route.md:77); the actionable-key check (a CARRY on working-route.md:71); and the self-description itself (working-route.md:75). Membership is not free for this chunk to settle whole: the route reserves for later promotions whether a command exposes the actionable-key check, how JSON carries the snapshot text, the orphaned-host answer that shapes the lifecycle commands (all three on working-route.md:71), the `accessibility` feature on `escher-driver` and typed deletion (working-route.md:62), and the screenshot's form (working-route.md:77). How much of the vocabulary the set holds now is a fork for the operator. **Decided (the operator, 2026-10-07, at the P4 forks):** the core verbs now — `snapshot`, `click`, `type`, `press` and `advance` — in one table the later entries extend with their own verbs at their promotions.
- **Argument and result shapes** — each verb's arguments and its result have a stated shape.

- **The shapes must be readable as data, not only as Rust signatures**: later entries serve them — "uncoloured JSON on stdout" (working-route.md:71), "driver commands as MCP tools" (working-route.md:73), "verb list, help and schemas served by CLI and MCP from the one schema" (working-route.md:75). `escher-driver` depends on two crates today, `blitz-test-harness` and `dioxus-native-dom`, and on no serialization crate (`packages/escher-driver/Cargo.toml`). A schema stated as `'static` Rust data is readable as data with no such crate; producing JSON from it is the serving surface's step (research.md §Patterns detected, "Serialization crates").
- **Malformed arguments refused** — a call the schema does not admit is refused with a named cause.

- **What "malformed" covers and what a refusal leaves behind**: an unknown verb, a missing, extra or ill-typed argument; a refused call changes nothing on the held instance. Two precedents exist in the repository and neither is this schema: the lifecycle wire's `RefusedMalformed` — "a request line over 64 bytes or outside the grammar is refused and changes nothing" (`.claude/rules/security.md` §Surfaces; `wire.rs:61-81`) — and the cold-agent stub, a toy counter whose causes are `not-found` · `disabled` · `not-pressable` · `malformed` (`scripts/cold_agent_stub.py:6`), pinned by nine rows of `.github/scripts/test_cold_agent.py:163-171`. Three of the stub's names have a counterpart here; `not-pressable` has none, and the stub refuses an unknown tool as `not-found`. Whether the stub is brought to the schema is the plan's.
- **Refusal causes, each with a remedy** — a closed set of causes; every cause carries a remedy.

- **The cause set**: the five intent §6 names — not found · stale · disabled · covered by another element · off-screen — and malformed. An instance that does not go quiet is today `SessionError::NotSettled(Busy)` (`packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs:35-36`), and `Session::act` does not roll its step back (`session.rs:66-67`): a step that ran and did not settle was not refused. Whether it is a cause is the plan's, read against that. **Amended at validation-1 (the plan surfaced two causes the entry does not list):** the set is eight — the six above, `unknown-verb` (a call naming no verb of the set, kept apart from malformed arguments so each has its own remedy) and `time-unavailable` (an app with no time seam refuses the time verb "with a named cause and a remedy" — the operator, 2026-10-07, at the P4 forks). Not settled is a result field, not a cause.

- **The remedy is a fixed text per cause.** `[premise-corrected: only one of the two precedents is a fixed text — actionable.rs:38-43 formats the tag and the id into its remedy]` The fixed-text precedent is `SessionError`: every message "is a fixed string: none carries a path, a label, an id or a value" (`error.rs:10`), pinned by a unit test that lists the variants by hand (`error.rs:78-96`). `UnkeyedActionable::remedy()` is the precedent for a remedy as a method on the typed value, not for its text being fixed. Whether a refusal also carries the id it was aimed at is the plan's; anything that does is returned to its caller only and is no log field (CLAUDE.md §Critical Warnings — "add no new user-content log fields").

- **Where the refusal type stands beside `SessionError`** — the lifecycle's one outcome type has twelve variants, each a lifecycle edge (`error.rs:12-37`); no site outside the crate matches it exhaustively (research.md §Graph impact). Whether a command's refusal joins that enum or is its own type is the plan's.

- **The check this chunk can make is over the schema itself**: every verb has an argument and a result shape; every cause has a remedy that is not empty; a table of malformed calls is each refused with its cause. `[premise-corrected: "leaves the instance as it was" needs no instance — a validation that receives no session cannot change one; research.md §Patterns detected]` Provoking the five screen-level causes on the stand is "Refusal detection" (Boundaries). Stated here as intent; the plan gives it its shape.

title: The carried questions (the entry's one CARRY, from 2026-10-07-settle-detection)

data.head: ### The carried questions (the entry's one CARRY, from 2026-10-07-settle-detection)

body: - **The mechanism the CARRY states, verbatim:** "settle is built in process only (`Harness::settle`, `Session::act`): it advances no time and waits on no load — time on a held instance moves only when its caller delivers ticks, and a load in flight is reported at once as `NotSettled(Loads)`." Re-derived at HEAD: `settle` takes the harness's clock value once and reads no other (`packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs:152`), returns `NotSettled { busy: Busy::Loads }` at once for a load in flight (`settle.rs:164-171`), and `Session::act` maps a not-quiet instance to `SessionError::NotSettled(busy)` (`packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:70-78`). One addition: a held instance has two clocks, both the caller's — the Timer's ticks (`TimerTicks::deliver`, `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs:20-26`) and the harness's animation clock (`Harness::tick`, `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs:152-155`).

- **Question 1 — how an agent moves the Timer's time through a driver session.** The CARRY: "the session host holds the tick handle and delivers nothing, examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:34-45". Re-read: the host binds `ticks` at line 35, stores the handle the Timer boot returns at line 39 and drops it after `serve` returns at line 45; nothing between delivers a tick. This chunk answers the question in the verb set — a verb, a host behaviour, or a recorded "not in this version" — and the answer is a fork for the operator, not a lean. Three constraints bear on it: intent §Out of this version lists "virtual time everywhere" (`escher-0.1.0/intent.md:77`); the tick handle is the stand's own seam, while `escher-driver` "names no app" (`lib.rs:4`); and the host cannot reach the handle while it serves — `serve` consumes the session and blocks in `accept` (`host.rs:48`, `:107-123`), so a host that delivers ticks needs a change inside the library or a step its caller hands the session. **Answered (the operator, 2026-10-07, at the P4 forks):** a verb the caller steps — and "the schema itself must say what one step is, so an agent learns the unit from the tool alone": a duration in milliseconds was weighed against a bare step count and taken, because a step's size is the app's and the library names no app. This chunk states the verb's shape; the wiring is "Act by id".

- **Question 2 — whether a driver command may wait on a load with a clock.** The CARRY: "a new decision for security-plan §API Security, not an extension of settle". The section exists (`.andromeda/security-plan.md:191`). The answer is a decision this chunk records, asked of the operator; it is never read off settle's present behaviour. **Answered (the operator, 2026-10-07, at the P4 forks):** no — a command that finds a load in flight reports it and returns; the cost, that an app loading over the network must be polled by its caller, is a residual for the version that first drives such an app.

- **What waits on question 1** — "v010-10's driver leg, carried on "Act by id", cannot be proven until the first is answered". Re-read: a `CARRY: v010-10's driver leg` block stands on working-route.md:62. This chunk answers the question; it does not build or prove that leg.

- **Not Act by id** (working-route.md:62 — "driver actions addressed by stable id, returning after settle with the diff (v010-09, v010-06)"). This chunk states the acting verbs' shapes; it runs no action on the held instance. That entry's six CARRYs stay on it.

- **Not Refusal detection** (working-route.md:64 — "not found, stale, disabled, covered by another element, off-screen named per action (v010-11)"). This chunk names the causes and their remedies; telling which cause holds for an action on a screen is that entry's, with its minimal-fixture CARRY.

- **Not Driver command spans** (working-route.md:66 — "one span per driver command covering settle wait, diff size and refusal cause"). The span's refusal-cause field reads this chunk's cause set; this chunk adds no span, no event and no `tracing` dependency.

- **Not Driver CLI, MCP surface or Self-description** (working-route.md:71 · 73 · 75). JSON on stdout, exit codes, MCP tools, and serving the verb list, help and schemas are theirs. This chunk builds what they serve.

- **No wire change.** The session socket stays `hello` and `stop`: "no element id, accessible name, control value, snapshot text or diff crosses it, and the first command that carries one is a new crossing question" (`.claude/rules/security.md` §Surfaces). A schema held in process crosses nothing. If the plan finds a verb must reach the wire in this chunk, that is an arch §Occupied Resources and security-plan question asked first, never a lean.

- **No new listener, port, env var or workspace crate — and no new dependency.** `[premise-corrected: the schema needs no serialization crate — research.md §Patterns detected, "Serialization crates"]` No manifest is edited, so no root-manifest citation moves and `Cargo.lock` is unchanged.

The claim decision is P4's and P5's against the matrix.
- **No sleep and no font skip in any check** (`.claude/rules/testing.md` §Determinism); a pipeline check runs `for incremental in [false, true]`.

- **Marker:** 2026-10-07-driver-command-spans · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-07T21:39:21Z

Every driver command leaves one span, and what that span says reaches a log only through escher's scrub. A
call handed to `Session::run` opens one span under the target `escher_driver`; the span carries, as its own
fields, which verb ran, how the settle wait went, how large the returned diff is and — for a refused call —
the cause's name (per obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage). Each field is a fixed word or a number: nothing of
a call's arguments and nothing of an outcome's content is fielded (per security-plan §Input Validation;
architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session).

As built the sink cannot show any of it: it prints events only, a span writes no line, and a span's fields
never pass the scrub (research.md §Patterns detected). So the chunk has a second half, decided at the P4
forks (`inputs#I1`): **escher's sink learns to print a closed span** — one line per closed span of an
admitted target, every field of it judged by the same `decide(target, field)` that judges an event's, with the
sink's own timing of the span. The driver therefore reads no clock, and every later escher span prints by the
same rule with no call site of its own (per obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing & Compliance → Scrubbing; §6 Log
Coverage → Log format).

That second half admits a new record class to the sink — the playbook's "Boundary widening" pattern
(`.andromeda/playbook.md:36-38`). It is recorded **PROVISIONAL**: the answer that chose it is not the
founder's own word (`inputs#I1`), so it is listed for the founder's batch at the Epoch 4 boundary, which this
chunk's wrap closes, and named in the handoff.

The proof is a stand check: driver commands run on stand tasks with the real sink installed over a captured
writer; one line per command; each reading held against what the call returned; and none of the ids, names,
typed text or values the commands handled anywhere in what the sink wrote (per test-plan §5 → Session ↔ held
instance; §5 → Session host ↔ what it writes).

`packages/escher-driver/Cargo.toml` gains `tracing` as a workspace dependency (`{ workspace = true }`, the
form `packages/escher-telemetry/Cargo.toml:14` uses), ungated: no `[features]` table is added (`inputs#I1`,
fork 2). `Cargo.lock` then gains exactly one line — `"tracing",` in the `escher-driver` entry
(`Cargo.lock:3084-3089`; `tracing 0.1.44` is already locked at `:8526-8527`) — produced by one cargo
resolution without `--locked`; every command after it runs `--locked`. The root `Cargo.toml` is not edited.

In `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs`, `Session::run` (`:82-141`) opens one span per call and holds it
entered from before `validate(call)` (`:83`) until `run` returns, so a refusal `validate` returns is inside
it. `run`'s signature and what it returns for any call are unchanged (`run @
tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs:151`, `:194` and seven direct test call sites —
research.md §Graph impact — see no difference).
- **Identity:** target `escher_driver`, name `command`, level INFO.

- **Fields — exactly eight, their names stated once in the module as a private table:** `verb` · `cause` ·
  `settled` · `busy` · `passes` · `added` · `removed` · `changed`. A field that does not apply to a call is
  left unrecorded, so it does not print.
  - `verb` — the table's own word for the call's verb: the `name` of the row `schema::verb(&call.verb)`
    returns (`packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:293-295`). Unrecorded when the table has no such verb. The
    caller's own text is never the value.
  - `cause` — on a refusal, `Cause::name()` of the refusal `run` returns
    (`packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs:43`), recorded at one site for every `Err` whichever of the two
    sources returned it. Unrecorded on a call that ran.
  - `settled` — for an acting verb that ran (`click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll`): whether
    the instance went quiet.
  - `busy` — when it did not: the class word, one of `BUSY_CLASSES`
    (`packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:30`), mapped from the `Busy` class by a private function of the
    module.
  - `passes` — when it did: `Settled.passes` (`packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs:32-39`), read where
    the settle's answer is read, `settled_step` (`execute.rs:257-267`, the one `harness.settle()` at `:264`,
    which keeps only the error half today). `Outcome` gains no field for it.
  - `added` · `removed` · `changed` — the lengths of the three lists of the diff the call returns.
  - `snapshot` records `verb` alone.

- **Nothing else is fielded:** not `in_view`, not `advanced_ms`, not the screen text or its length, not the
  session's label, not the record of ids or its size.

- **The span code reads only the call's verb and what the call returns.** It adds no snapshot, no settle, no
  pass and no dispatch; reads no document, no changed set and no clock; and puts nothing on `Session`.

- **Unit tests** in the module's `mod tests` (`execute.rs:316-346`), tables stated in the test with their row
  counts asserted: the field table has eight rows and none is an argument name of any verb in `VERBS`; the
  busy-class function returns the three rows of `BUSY_CLASSES`, one per `Busy` class.

`packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` (`:1-39`) gains one paragraph: a call run through `Session::run` leaves
one `tracing` span; what its fields are; that they hold fixed words and counts and nothing a call supplied or
a screen reads; and that the crate installs no subscriber — a caller that wants the record installs one. No
public item is added (`#![deny(missing_docs)]` at `:41`; the re-export list `:54-65` is unchanged).

title: 4. The sink prints a closed span

data.head: ### 4. The sink prints a closed span

body: In `packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs` and `packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs`.

- **The layer.** The sink's one fmt layer (`lib.rs:123-126`) turns the span-close record on — close only: no
  line when a span is created, entered or exited — and takes a field formatter of the sink's own in place of
  the default. The layer's construction is stated once and used by `init_with_writer` and by the unit
  tests' scoped subscriber (`format.rs:285-296` builds its own copy today), so the tests exercise the layer
  the binaries install.

- **The line.** For a closed span whose target the allowlist admits: the same head an event's line has
  (`{time} {LEVEL} {target} service.name=… service.version=…`), then `span` = the span's name, then the
  span's own fields, then the close record's own fields (`message`, `time.busy`, `time.idle` — the two
  timings are read by the layer's clock, `tracing-subscriber-0.3.23/src/fmt/fmt_layer.rs:938`, `:962`,
  `:990`). Every `name=value` pair on it, the `span` pair included, is printed as `decide(target, name)`
  says (`format.rs:93-107`): the value, or `[redacted]`. A value is spelled as an event's is (`format.rs:164-198`).

- **An outside target's span writes nothing** — at creation, on a recorded value, on enter, on exit and on
  close — as an outside target's event does (`format.rs:136-138`).

- **The mechanism the line rests on.** The layer hands a span's fields to its field formatter without the
  span's target (`tracing-subscriber-0.3.23/src/fmt/format/mod.rs:235-244`), so the judgment by target is
  made where the line is printed, `format_event` (`format.rs:128-155`), which reaches the closing span's
  stored fields through its context — the route the stock formatter takes (`format/mod.rs:985-995`); the
  close record arrives there with the span's own metadata (`fmt_layer.rs:851-865`, `:978-1015`). Two
  consequences bind the stored form: it keeps each field's name separable from its value whatever the value
  holds (a space, an `=`, a line break), and a content-named field's value (`CONTENT_FIELDS`,
  `format.rs:48-60`) is replaced before it is stored — that redaction needs only the name.

- **Events are unchanged.** An event's line reads as it does today, including an event emitted inside a
  span: it gains no span name and no span field.

- **Unit tests** in `format.rs`'s `mod tests`, through the scoped subscriber: (a) an escher-target span
  closes into exactly one line holding `span=`, its printable fields and both timings, and nothing is
  written before it closes; (b) a content-named span field — one given at creation, one recorded later —
  prints `[redacted]` and its value is nowhere in the output, and a printable field whose value holds a
  space, an `=` and a line break stays one pair on one line; (c) an outside-target span with fields writes
  no byte; (d) an engine-target span prints only safe fields and redacts the rest, `span` included; (e) an
  event inside an escher span prints exactly what it prints outside one.

- **Docs.** The crate doc (`lib.rs:1-18`) and `EscherFormat`'s doc (`format.rs:109-112`) say one line per
  printed event and one per closed span. `packages/escher-telemetry/Cargo.toml` and `src/panic.rs` are not
  edited.

New file `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_spans.rs`, opening with a `//!` doc naming the behaviour. It
declares `mod common;` and `mod session_common;` and keeps its capture writer in the file (the form of
`tests/blitz-tests/tests/telemetry_scrub.rs:12-24`); neither shared module is edited.

**Form.** The sink's level filter is read from the process's `RUST_LOG` at install
(`packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs:119`), and the span is INFO, below the default. So each reading is
made in a child: the test binary re-run on one `#[ignore]` test with `RUST_LOG` set or removed by its parent
(the form of `tests/blitz-tests/tests/telemetry_drop.rs:18-22`, not `cfg(unix)`-gated). The child installs
the real sink once over its capture (`escher_telemetry::init_with_writer`), drives the commands in both
layout modes and asserts in its own process; the parent reads it through `.output()` and asserts it
succeeded. Two parents, two children:

- **At `RUST_LOG=info` — the records.** In each layout mode the child drives, through
  `session_common`'s builders:
  - on **CRUD**: a `snapshot`; a `type` of the file's synthetic `SECRET` into `crud-name`; a `press` of a
    non-deleting key; twelve `click`s on `crud-create` (the count `stand_act_scroll.rs:24` uses), which put
    a row past the list box; a `click` on `crud-delete` while no row is selected, refused `disabled`; a
    `click` on the row past the list, refused `off-screen`; a `scroll` to it; a `click` on it, which
    selects it; a `click` on `crud-delete`, which removes it, then a `click` on the removed row's id,
    refused `stale`; a `click` on an id no screen read, refused `not-found`; a call whose verb is not in
    the table, refused `unknown-verb`; a `click` with no `id`, refused `malformed`; an `advance`, refused
    `time-unavailable` — in that order;
  - on **Timer** (held with its time step): an `advance` that moves time;
  - on **a minimal in-file fixture** booted with the stand's options — one button under one positioned
    overlay, the first pair of `stand_act_obstructed.rs:26-47`: a `click` refused `covered`, the case the
    stand lacks.

  For every call, by index: the capture grows by exactly one line; that line is at INFO under
  `escher_driver`, carries the service identity and `span` reading `command`; its `verb` is the table's word
  (absent for the unknown verb); and
  - a call that ran as an acting verb carries `settled`, with `passes` when settled, and `added` ·
    `removed` · `changed` equal to the list lengths of the diff the call returned — which the check first
    holds equal to its own `before.diff(&after)` (the form of `stand_act_diff.rs:54-66`) — and no `cause`;
  - a refused call carries `cause` equal to `Cause::name()` of the refusal it returned, and none of
    `settled` · `busy` · `passes` · `added` · `removed` · `changed`;
  - the `snapshot` carries none of those seven;
  - every line carries both timings, by presence only — no value of a timing is read or compared.

  All eight cause names are read back, each from its own refused call. Then, over the whole capture of
  that layout mode:
  - **field names** — every field name on every `escher_driver` line is one of `span` · the eight · `message`
    · `time.busy` · `time.idle`, and no value reads `[redacted]`;
  - **content** — zero occurrences of each needle: every stable id the driven screens read (from
    `element_ids` after the creates, so run-time `crud-person-…` ids are among them — the shared `rendered`
    table lists the boot screen only), every row's text and every label's text (the method of
    `examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs:42-60`), the fixture's ids, and `SECRET`; the needle lists are
    asserted non-empty and the capture non-empty first, so a zero is not vacuous.

- **With `RUST_LOG` removed — the default level.** The child drives one `click` and one refused call on a
  stand task in each layout mode and the capture holds no `escher_driver` line; both calls return what they
  return with no sink.

**Rules of the file.** No sleep, no clock read, no pass or tick of its own; no deleting key. A failure
message carries a layout mode, a task and a call index, or a kind and a count — never an id, a name, a
value, typed text or a captured line: with the sink installed the panic hook prints the raw message after
the scrubbed event (`packages/escher-telemetry/src/panic.rs`). The children print nothing of their own, and
no test name holds an id.

Each new test is turned red by a named mutation, reverted, and recorded in
`escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-command-spans/evidence/controls.md` (mutation · the test that turned
red · its message's kind and count):
1. the driver records `added` from the `changed` list → the records child red;
2. the driver records the cause of an executor refusal as the word of a different cause → the records child red;
3. the driver fields the typed text under a ninth name added to its table → the records child red twice over (field names, content) and the field-table unit test red (row count);
4. the busy-class function answers one class with another's word → its unit test red;
5. the span's level is raised to WARN → the default-level child red;
6. the sink also prints a line when a span is created → unit test (a) red;
7. the sink prints a span's stored fields without judging them → unit tests (b) and (d) red;
8. the sink stops dropping an outside-target span → unit test (c) red;
9. the sink adds the enclosing span's name to an event's line → unit test (e) red.

- The session host's stderr by level, with the sink's new setting: the standing instrument
  `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist/evidence/by-level.py host`, its table recorded in
  `evidence/by-level.md` beside the standing 0 · 1 · 1 · 1 lines at unset · `info` · `debug` · `trace`
  (obs-plan §8, as measured at that chunk) — predicted unchanged, since that host runs no command and opens
  no span of an admitted target; record what the run measures. The windowed stand's reading needs a display
  and is not re-measured by this chunk.

- The counts the masters carry, each from the run's own listing: escher-driver unit tests (27 at the base —
  predicted 29), escher-telemetry unit tests (10, 9 in `format.rs` — predicted 15), `run stand`'s `run.end`
  (107 passed, 0 failed over 29 files at the base — predicted 109 passed over 30 files, 2 more ignored),
  the workspace (647 passed · 8 ignored over 153 result lines — predicted one more result line, more
  passed, 10 ignored). Bases as recorded at 2026-10-07-refusal-detection (test-plan history), not re-run
  here; record what each run measures.
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_spans.rs` — the stand check of step 5
- `packages/escher-driver/Cargo.toml` — the `tracing` workspace dependency (step 1)
- `Cargo.lock` — one dependency line in the `escher-driver` entry (step 1)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs` — the span, its field table, the busy-class word, two unit tests (step 2)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` — the crate doc paragraph (step 3)
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs` — the closed span's line, the field formatter, five unit tests, the formatter's doc (step 4)
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs` — the layer's construction stated once with the span-close setting and the field formatter; the crate doc (step 4)

No entry is a live leg: nothing here drives a process the launch environment names, so there is no liveness
probe and no `stop` key. The project has no headful self-verify harness and this chunk changes no screen.
The sink both seven_guis binaries install at start is edited (`packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs`), so both
boots are read: the windowed stand by the smoke entry — it needs a display and opens a window for 10 s — and
the session host by `host_log`, `host_binary` and the by-level instrument. **Not run locally:** the
MSRV build and the windows, macos, ios and android matrix legs — the fork's CI run is their one witness, read
after the operator pass (pre-CI commit, push, CI read). **Not measured by this chunk:** the windowed stand's
stderr by level under the sink's new setting, beyond the smoke's one boot at `info`, and typed text in a sink-installing HOST's
log (no command reaches a host's instance — a CARRY on "Driver CLI", working-route.md:71). The preservation
entry and the lock entry name their base as the commit this chunk starts from, `b75ed30b`.

`evidence/controls.md` has no listed producer, by construction: it is implement's hand record of step 6's
mutations, which no entry could re-produce at the wrap's light gate; what it records is asserted by listed
entries (the new check and the telemetry unit tests the mutations turn red). `evidence/by-level.md` is
implement's record of the report-only by-level entry's output.

No capability of the verification matrix is claimed: the entry lists none, and each of the seven pooled ones
names a surface a later entry builds (see Provenance).

- (obs) Each of the six verbs run through `Session::run` leaves exactly one line in the sink's capture, at INFO under `escher_driver`, in both layout modes, and a refused call leaves one too — `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_act_spans` (per obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage)

- (obs) A refused call's line carries a cause equal to the name of the cause the call returned, all eight names read back, and none of the settle or diff fields; an acting call's line carries its settle reading and `added` · `removed` · `changed` equal to the list lengths of the diff the call returned; a call that ran carries no cause — `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_act_spans` (per obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage)

- (obs) With `RUST_LOG` unset no `escher_driver` line is written for a command, and with no subscriber installed nothing is written at all: the default-level child of `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_act_spans`, and `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_session_quiet` unedited (per obs-plan §6 Log Coverage → Log format (escher's sink))

- (security) The capture of the driven commands — a `type` of a known text, clicks, a `scroll`, a key press and refused calls naming ids — holds zero occurrences of every stable id, row text, label text and the typed text those commands handled, every field name on a driver line is one of the stated set, and no value reads redacted — `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_act_spans`, seen red under step 6's third mutation (per security-plan §Logging & Monitoring)

- (security) A closed span's fields reach the writer only as `decide(target, field)` says: an escher-target span prints a content-named field redacted whether it was given at creation or recorded later, an engine-target span prints only safe fields, and an outside-target span writes no byte — `cargo test -p escher-telemetry --locked`, seen red under step 6's seventh and eighth mutations (per security-plan §Logging & Monitoring)

- (security) The driver fields no `Command`, `Call`, `ArgValue`, `Outcome` or `Refusal`, instruments no function and gives no span field an argument's name: the unit test of step 2 in `cargo test -p escher-driver --locked`, and the census entry over `execute.rs`, `session.rs` and `lib.rs` reads 0 (per security-plan §Input Validation)

- (security) A refused call still changes nothing with the span in place — `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_act_disabled --test stand_act_obstructed --test stand_act_scroll` and the six-file driver-action entry pass with their files unedited, held by the preservation entry (per security-plan §Input Validation)

- (security) The lockfile gains one dependency line and no package, and the advisory audit passes — the `lock-one-edge` entry and `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh audit` (per security-plan §Dependency Security)

- (arch) The driver's manifest gains `tracing` alone as a workspace dependency, with no `[features]` table, no edge to `escher-telemetry` or an app and no new workspace crate; the root manifest, the schema modules, the session, the harness, the engine and the stand do not move — the preservation entry (per architecture §Established Decisions → [Driver session])

- (arch) An event's line is unchanged by the sink's new setting, an event inside a span included, and nothing is written to stdout — `cargo test -p escher-telemetry --locked`, the four-file `telemetry_*` entry and `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test telemetry_drop`, their files unedited (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Telemetry bootstrap)

**Date:** 2026-10-07
**Commits:** `44ad3887 chore(2026-10-07-driver-command-spans): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk verdict reads` — the one commit since the last wrap's flip `b75ed30b`; basis `git log --format='%h %s' b75ed30b..HEAD`, 1 line. Uncommitted at this report: `evidence/operator-pass.md` (the pass's entries 27 and 28, appended after the commit) and this wrap's run dir.

- **Files:** basis `git diff --name-status b75ed30b` (the parent of the oldest pre-CI commit) plus `git status --short`, run dirs aside — 7 source, manifest and test files, as `gate.py scope` reads them (changed 7 · listed 7).
  - Modified (6): `packages/escher-driver/Cargo.toml` · `Cargo.lock` · `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs` · `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` · `packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs` · `packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs`.
  - New (1): `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_spans.rs`.
  - Chunk records: `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-command-spans/{plan,research,scope}.md`, `inputs/` (1 copy, the manifest, `.gitattributes`), `evidence/{controls,by-level,operator-pass}.md`. `escher-0.1.0/verification-matrix.json` is not touched: the chunk claims no capability.
  - Not touched (the preservation probe, green): the root `Cargo.toml`, `deny.toml`, `packages/escher-driver/src/{wire,host,client,error,session,schema,command,refusal}.rs`, `packages/escher-telemetry/Cargo.toml`, `packages/escher-telemetry/src/panic.rs`, `packages/blitz-test-harness`, `packages/blitz-dom`, `packages/dioxus-native-dom`, `examples/seven_guis`, `scripts`, `.github`, `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml`, both shared test modules (`tests/common`, `tests/session_common`), the nine standing `stand_act_*` files, `stand_settle`, `stand_session_quiet` and the five `telemetry_*` files.

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - **The span of a driver command** (new; `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs`). Every call handed to `Session::run` opens one `tracing` span: target `escher_driver`, name `command`, level INFO. It is created and entered before `validate` and stays entered until `run` returns, so a refusal `validate` returns is inside it. It is built by hand with `tracing::info_span!` — no `#[instrument]`.
    - **Eight fields, each created unrecorded and recorded only where it applies:** `verb` · `cause` · `settled` · `busy` · `passes` · `added` · `removed` · `changed`. The list is stated once, in the private macro `command_span!` (`:64`, invoked at `:79`), which emits the span constructor `command_span()` and a table `SPAN_FIELDS` of the same names; the table is compiled only under `cfg(test)` — nothing but the unit test reads it.
    - `verb` — the `name` of the row `schema::verb(&call.verb)` returns: the table's own word, recorded for a known verb whether the call then runs or is refused; unrecorded for a verb the table lacks. The caller's verb text is never a value.
    - `cause` — `Cause::name()` of the refusal `run` returns, recorded at one site (`record_result`, `:183`) for every `Err`, whichever of `validate` and the executor returned it. Unrecorded on a call that ran.
    - `settled` (bool), `added` · `removed` · `changed` (the three list lengths of the returned `SnapshotDiff`) — recorded at the same site from the `Outcome` an acting verb returned (`Acted`, `Advanced`, `Scrolled`). `busy` — when the outcome carries a busy class, the schema's word for it, through the private `busy_word` (`:220`), which indexes `BUSY_CLASSES`.
    - `passes` — `Settled.passes`, recorded in `settled_step` (`:342`; the one `harness.settle()` at `:350`) when settle answered quiet. The span is handed to `settled_step` and `acted` as a parameter; `Outcome` gains no field.
    - `snapshot` records `verb` alone. A refused call records `verb` (when known) and `cause` and none of the other six.
    - **Never fielded:** `in_view`, `advanced_ms`, the screen text or its length, the session's label, the record of ids or its size, any argument, any `Command`, `Call`, `ArgValue`, `Outcome`, `Refusal` or `Fault`.
    - The span code reads the call's verb and what the call returned, plus settle's own answer where it is already read. It adds no snapshot, settle, pass or dispatch, reads no document, no changed set and no clock, and puts nothing on `Session`.
  - **`Session::run`** (`:108`, was `:82`) — signature and return unchanged for every call; its former body is the private `Session::execute(&mut self, call, span)` (`:119`). Its nine call sites (all tests) are unedited. With no subscriber installed the span is disabled and writes nothing.
  - **`escher-driver`'s crate doc** (`lib.rs:41-48`) gains one paragraph stating the span, its fields, that they hold fixed words and counts, and that the crate installs no subscriber. The re-export list is unchanged at 33 names (basis: the `pub use` lines of `lib.rs`, counted by script).
  - **The sink prints a closed span** (new record class; `packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs`, `lib.rs`). One line per closed span whose target the allowlist admits, beside the one line per printed event. No line when a span is created, recorded to, entered or exited.
    - **Line shape:** `{time} {LEVEL} {target} service.name=… service.version=…`, then `span={the span's name}`, then the span's own fields in the order recorded, then the layer's close fields `message`, `time.busy`, `time.idle`. Level and target are the span's.
    - **Every pair, `span` included, is printed as `decide(target, name)` says** — the rule that judges an event's field: under an escher target every field prints unless its name is in `CONTENT_FIELDS`, which prints `[redacted]`; under an engine target only `SAFE_FIELDS` print and the rest read `[redacted]` — `span`, `message`, `time.busy` and `time.idle` among them.
    - **An outside target's span writes no byte** at creation, on a recorded value, on enter, on exit and on close.
    - **Spelling:** as an event's field. A string value is Debug-quoted, so a driver line reads `span="command" verb="click" cause="off-screen"` and the close marker reads `message="close"`; a number or a bool is bare; line breaks in a value are written `\n` / `\r`. As read from a real capture: `… INFO escher_driver service.name=blitz-tests service.version=0.3.0-beta.2 span="command" verb="click" passes=1 settled=true added=1 removed=0 changed=1 message="close" time.busy=11.0ms time.idle=4.51µs`. The two timings are the layer's own (`Instant`, read inside `tracing-subscriber`); no escher code reads a clock for them.
    - **Mechanism:** `SpanFields` (`format.rs:200`, crate-private) is the layer's field formatter. The layer hands it a span's fields without the span's target, so it stores each field as its name and its spelled value, one line each (a spelled value holds no line break), and `EscherFormat::format_event` (`:138`) judges each by target when the close record arrives — that record carries the span's own metadata and the span as its parent. **The value of a field named in `CONTENT_FIELDS` is not stored at all** (the stored value is empty; the marker is written at print time). Every other field's value — of an engine span and of an outside-target span too — is held in the span's extensions, in process memory, until the span closes, and never written.
    - **`EscherFormat`** (`:124`) now implements `FormatEvent` for the sink's own field formatter only (`FormatEvent<S, SpanFields>`), not for any field formatter. Crate-private; no public item of `escher-telemetry` is added or changed (its five public constants, `init`, `init_with_writer`, `ServiceIdentity`, `InitOutcome`, `InitError`, `service_identity!` stand).
    - **`sink_layer(identity, writer)`** (`lib.rs:102`, private) is the one statement of the layer: `fmt::layer().with_span_events(FmtSpan::CLOSE).fmt_fields(SpanFields).event_format(EscherFormat::new(identity)).with_ansi(false).with_writer(writer)`. `init_with_writer` (`:130`) and the unit tests' scoped subscriber both build through it.
    - **An event's line is unchanged**, an event emitted inside a span included: it gains no span name and no span field.
    - **A named limit, read from the locked `tracing-subscriber 0.3.23`, not exercised:** when a field formatter returns an error at span creation, the layer itself `eprintln!`s the span's attributes with `Debug` to stderr (`fmt_layer.rs`, `on_new_span`). `SpanFields` writes into a `String` and returns no error.
  - **What reaches a log from a command, in a process that installs the sink at `info` or below:** one line per call, holding the eight fields' values where recorded — six verb words, eight cause names, three busy-class words, bools and counts — and the sink's timing. At the default level (`warn`) the span is filtered out before it is created: no line.
  - **Who runs a command with the sink installed today:** only the new check's two children. `escher-session` installs the sink and runs no command (its wire is `hello` and `stop`); `seven_guis_native` runs none. No surface carries a call out of the process yet.
