body: - **`centre_of`** — 2 callers, both in `Session::run`: `run @ packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:66` (`click`) and `:70` (`type`). The detection goes where they are; no other caller exists.

- **`Session::run`** — 8 call sites, all in blitz-tests: `act @ tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs:143`; `stand_act_diff.rs:272`; `stand_act_ids.rs:96`, `:108`; `stand_act_refused.rs:102`, `:142`, `:148`; `stand_act_timer.rs:106`. Its signature does not change, so none is a threading edit; the two files whose expectation changes are `stand_act_ids` and `stand_act_refused`.

- **`Cause::NotFound`** — constructed at one site, `centre_of @ execute.rs:126`; asserted at `stand_act_ids.rs:109` and `stand_act_refused.rs:69`, `:76`, `:143`. **`Cause::Stale` · `Disabled` · `Covered` · `OffScreen`** — 4 reference sites each, all in `refusal.rs` (the `CAUSES` list, `name`, `meaning`, `remedy`): constructed nowhere, asserted by no check.

- **`Command`** — 7 reference sites outside `command.rs`: the import and the five `match` arms of `Session::run` (`execute.rs:6`, `:62`, `:65`, `:69`, `:76`, `:79`) and the re-export `lib.rs:48`. A sixth variant adds one arm to that `match`, one to `Command::spec` (`command.rs:134-143`) and one to `validate`'s final `match` (`command.rs:185-203`); no site outside the crate matches on `Command`.

- **`VERBS`** — read outside `schema.rs` at `command.rs:568` (the unit test that reaches every verb) and re-exported at `lib.rs:55`; no check in blitz-tests reads it. The five verb constants are named at `command.rs:136-140`.

- **`element_from_point`** — 1 caller outside blitz-dom, `packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/document.rs:323`; **`get_client_bounding_rect`** — the snapshot at `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs:127` among 9 outside sites. Both are read here, not changed.

- **Every reading the detection needs exists and is reachable through the crate's two dependencies** (`execute.rs:133-136` already calls `harness.base()` and reads a node): the snapshot's `enabled` and `bounds` through `harness.doc.snapshot()` and `Snapshot::get`; the node hit at a point through `Harness::hit` (`inspect.rs:96-98`) or `BaseDocument::hit` (`document.rs:1564`); an anonymous box's element through `BaseDocument::nearest_non_anonymous_ancestor` (`document.rs:1638`, public); a node's parent through `get_node(..).parent` (`node.rs:91`, public); the viewport's size and scroll through `BaseDocument::viewport()`, `Viewport::logical_size` and `viewport_scroll()` (`document.rs:1980`, `:2223`; `shell.rs:120-127`). Methods are called on values, so the driver names no blitz-dom type for any of them. No engine edit and no feature line is needed.

- **Each of those readers takes `&self`** — `snapshot`, `hit`, `nearest_non_anonymous_ancestor`, `get_node`, `viewport`, `viewport_scroll`, `get_client_bounding_rect` — so a detection made of them dispatches nothing, moves no hover and marks nothing in the changed set. Hover is set by `set_hover_to` on a pointer event (`document.rs:1831`), never by a hit test.

- **A pointer event's target is the hit at its page point** — `click_at(x, y)` sends a pointer down and up at one point carried as page, client and screen coordinates alike (`input.rs:18-27`, `:103-108`); the engine sets hover from the event's PAGE coordinates (`events/driver.rs:51`), and `set_hover_to` subtracts the viewport's scroll only to remember the client position before it hit-tests the point as given (`document.rs:1835-1840`). The hit walk treats fixed-position children of the root apart by subtracting the viewport's scroll for them alone (`node.rs:1417-1425`). So the hit test and `click_at` both take page coordinates, and "another element is hit at the point the action would land" is the answer of the raw hit at that page point: positive z-index hoisted children first, paint children in reverse, negative z-index last, an element with `visibility: hidden` never hit and one with `pointer-events: none` transparent to hits (`node.rs:1304-1320`, `:1388-1480`).

- **`element_from_point` is the wrong reader once a viewport is scrolled** — it documents viewport coordinates, checks them against the viewport's size, and passes them unconverted to the page-coordinate hit (`document.rs:1575-1586`). At viewport scroll 0 the two spaces coincide; after a scroll they differ by the scroll. It is not edited here (one caller, blitz-vibey-script); the detection reads the raw hit at the page point and resolves the answer to its element itself, as `element_from_point` does at `:1592-1600`.

- **The raw hit does not stop at the viewport's edge** — a point outside the viewport can still be answered through a node's scrollable overflow (`node.rs:1356-1361`), so a click aimed outside the viewport can land today and `off-screen` has to be read explicitly, from the target's viewport-relative `bounds` against `Viewport::logical_size`.

- **The executor's click point is the centre of the layout box, which a non-atomic inline element does not have** — `centre_of` uses `absolute_position` and `final_layout().size` (`execute.rs:135-143`); `get_client_bounding_rect` says of such an element "Non-atomic inline elements have no layout box of their own" and answers the union of its line fragments (`document.rs:2250-2254`). The stand has one such id-bearing element, the `span` `timer-duration-value` (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs:93`). A `covered` reading at the layout-box centre would name it covered; at the centre of its client bounding rect — the snapshot's `bounds` — the hit is its own text. For an element with a box of its own the client rect is the unrounded absolute position less the viewport's scroll (`document.rs:2256-2263`), so the page point is the client centre plus the viewport's scroll, and on an unscrolled viewport it is today's point.

- **Which stand controls read not enabled at boot: 3** — `flight-return-date` (`disabled: !is_return`, `flight_booker.rs:91`), `crud-update` and `crud-delete` (`disabled: !has_selection`, `crud.rs:113`, `:128`); the fourth `disabled:` line, `flight-book` (`flight_booker.rs:98`), is enabled at boot (derivation: `grep -n 'disabled' examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/{counter,flight_booker,timer,crud}.rs` — 4 `disabled:` attribute lines and 2 CSS selectors — read against `stand_act_ids.rs:29-38`, whose doc names "the disabled controls" among the 7 of 15 a click does not change). A selector click on each already changes nothing, because the engine's click target keys on the attribute's presence (a11y-plan §5; `stand_act_ids.rs:137-142` asserts the empty diff).

- **A disabled stand control cannot hold focus** — the four are rendered through a Dioxus `disabled:` expression, which writes a truthy attribute or removes it (a11y-plan §5, Script and framework exposure), and focusability parses the value as a bool (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/element.rs:629`; `tests/blitz-tests/tests/focusability_updates.rs:63-76`). A `press` aimed at a focused disabled control has no case on a lean-task screen.

- **The stand has no off-screen element at boot, and its scrollers are nested** — `stand_snapshot` asserts for every id of `rendered(task)` a box of non-zero size with `x >= 0`, `y >= 0`, `x + width <= 800` and `y + height <= 600` (`stand_snapshot.rs:185-197`). The two stand elements that scroll are `#task-body` (`app.rs:196-197`, `overflow-y: auto`) and the CRUD list (`crud.rs:181-182`, `overflow-y: auto; min-height: 150px`); the document itself does not overflow the viewport. Rows created past the list's box are clipped by it; what a driver click on such a row reads is not measured here.

- **`scroll_into_view` scrolls the viewport only** — it computes the aligned offset from the target's absolute position and the viewport's size and calls `scroll_to` on the root element, which the engine resolves to the viewport (`scrolling.rs:619-651`, `:272-283`). A target clipped inside a nested scroll container is not brought into view by it. With `ScrollBehavior::Instant` the viewport's scroll is written at once: `fragment_navigation.rs:220-246` asserts the offset read back immediately after the call, for each alignment. `scroll_programmatically` dispatches no `scroll` event (a TODO at `scrolling.rs:574`).

- **The driver cannot name the scroll's two enums** — `scroll_into_view` takes blitz-dom's `ScrollBehavior` and `ScrollLogicalPosition` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs:103`); blitz-test-harness re-exports `Harness`, `HarnessOptions`, four event builders, `Rect`, `Key`, `Modifiers` and the settle names (`lib.rs:23-27`), and dioxus-native-dom re-exports `DocumentConfig` and `NodeId` of blitz-dom's (`lib.rs:30`, `:41`). A scroll therefore reaches the driver as a harness input helper, beside `apple_keybinding` (`input.rs:227-232`), which is how the harness gave the driver the delete binding at 2026-10-07-act-by-id. Whether an instant scroll made through such a helper and then settled reads `settled` in one step is not measured: no check drives a scroll through a session.

- **An id can resolve and still not be on the screen** — `element_ids()` lists every element reachable from the root, while a snapshot node needs an accessibility node and a client bounding rect (`snapshot.rs:122-129`); an element under `display: none` or `hidden` is in the first and not the second. Today a driver click on such an id resolves and runs. `not-found`'s fixed texts already describe it: meaning "no element on the screen reads the id" (`refusal.rs:60`), remedy "take a snapshot and use an id it lists" (`refusal.rs:82`).

- **Nothing stateless can tell `stale` from `not-found`** — a deleted element's id is in no `element_ids()` pair, and a detached node reads no id (architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge), so the two cases are identical to a lookup that keeps nothing: `stand_act_refused.rs:73-78` pins the deleted row as `not-found`. `stale` needs a record of ids an earlier screen of this session read; `Session` holds none (`session.rs:27-31`). Every acting call already takes the screen's snapshot before and after its step (`execute.rs:104-107`), so the ids such a record needs are already read.

- **What a sixth verb and a reworded remedy move, by count** — `VERBS.len()` is asserted 5 at `schema.rs:287`, `:294` and through `rows.len()` at `:352`, with the name list at `:283` and the shape table at `:333`; `command.rs` asserts 26 admitted rows (`:375`), 34 malformed rows (`:512`) and 5 table rows (`:569`); `refusal.rs:246-250` pins the `off-screen` meaning and remedy by text, with the remedies pairwise distinct and no `/` in any text (test-plan §4). Each moves in the same change as the text or table it pins (derivation: `grep -n 'fn \|len()' packages/escher-driver/src/{schema,command}.rs`).

- **The clean place for the nested scroll is the engine's `scroll_into_view`** (`inputs#I3`) — it is the engine's one implementation of the CSSOM View "scroll an element into view" steps, which scroll every scrolling box that holds the element, innermost first, and then the viewport; at HEAD it computes one offset from the target's absolute position and writes it to the root element only (`scrolling.rs:620-654`). Its three call sites outside the tests all mean the spec's steps: script `Element.scrollIntoView` (`packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/element.rs:1288`), Dioxus `MountedData::scroll_to` (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/events.rs:251`) and fragment navigation (`scrolling.rs:690`). Widening it changes what each does for a target inside a nested scrolling box — today the box does not move — and nothing for a target whose only scroller is the viewport, which is every case `fragment_navigation.rs:197-262` checks. The other places are worse: a second into-view method leaves the spec'd one wrong beside it, and a walk written in the harness puts a second copy of the alignment arithmetic (`aligned_scroll_offset`, private, `scrolling.rs:588-617`) in a test crate the driver ships on.

- **Everything the nested walk needs is already in the scroll module** — a programmatic scroll of one box is `scroll_to(node, x, y, behavior)`, clamped to that box's range and never chained to an ancestor (`scrolling.rs:551-586`); which boxes scroll is `scroll_state`'s rule — `overflow` `scroll` or `auto` on the axis, and `hidden` too for a programmatic scroll (`:479-485`); the root element's scroll is the viewport's (`:272-283`); the chain an element's position is computed along is `containing_block()` (`node.rs:1564-1568`). Both absolute-position readers subtract every ancestor's scroll offset on the way up (`node.rs:1571-1590`), so an element's client bounding rect — the snapshot's `bounds` — follows a nested scroll with no further change.

- **The engine holds one scroll animation at a time** — `scroll_animation` is a single `ScrollTo` state, and a new programmatic scroll interrupts it (`scrolling.rs:136-140`, `:512-526`). Two boxes cannot both travel smoothly, and an outer box's offset computed while an inner one is still travelling is computed from the wrong position.

- **A programmatic scroll dispatches no `scroll` event** (`scrolling.rs:574`, a TODO; `:584` passes a no-op), nested or not; a nested write does stamp the box's overlay-scrollbar activity with `Instant::now()` under blitz-dom's `scrollbars` feature (`document.rs:1793-1797`), which blitz-tests turns on through blitz-paint (`tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml:20`), so the document reads animating for the fade's length afterwards. `Harness::settle` reports that as `Settled { animating: true }` and neither waits on it nor advances it (design-system §Motion (Animation runtime)); whether the step still reads settled is not measured.

- **The hit walk does not clip at a scrolling box's edge** — a point outside a box is still passed to its children when it lies inside the box's scrollable overflow (`node.rs:1330-1363`: the four tests are the box, the overflow rect, the hoisted content and the scrollable overflow, and only all four failing returns `None`). A click at the centre of a row scrolled out of its list can therefore land on that row, or on whatever is painted at that point — on the CRUD screen the button row sits below the list (`crud.rs:100-140`). Predicted from the code, not measured. So "is the target in view" cannot be read from the hit; it is read from geometry: the action point against the viewport and against the scrollport of every box on the target's containing-block chain whose `overflow` is not `visible`. The driver cannot make that reading itself — it would have to name stylo's overflow values, and its two dependencies re-export none — so it is one read-only reader on `BaseDocument`, beside the scroll that shares its chain.

- **The CRUD list is the stand's reachable off-screen case** — `#crud-list` is `flex: 1; overflow-y: auto; min-height: 150px` inside `.crud-body` (`flex: 1; min-height: 0`) inside a root of `height: 100%` (`crud.rs:146-183`); a row is one line of 14px text with 6px padding and a 1px rule (`:185-190`), and `crud-create` appends a row on every click with whatever the two fields hold (`crud.rs:102-109`), so the driver can grow the list past its box with clicks alone. Each row reads its author key `crud-person-{n}` (`crud.rs:69`) and the list reads `crud-list` (`:57`), so both are snapshot nodes with bounds. Predicted: rows past the box are clipped by the list; how many clicks that takes, and that it is the list and not `#task-body` that clips, is the run's to measure.

- **A result field that says so has its shape already** — `FieldKind::Flag` exists (`schema.rs:94-95`), and `advance` is the precedent of an acting verb with a sixth field and its own `Outcome` variant (`schema.rs:185-190`, `:266`; `execute.rs:32-42`).

- **The fixture pattern for a driver check** — an `rsx!` component in the check's own file, booted by `Session::start` over `Harness::from_vdom(VirtualDom::new(fixture), stand::options(incremental))` (`stand_act_diff.rs:241-260`); author `id`s on every element an action names.

- **One behaviour per integration file, a `//!` doc first, both layout modes** — `for incremental in [false, true]` (`stand_act_refused.rs:1-7`, `:85`); the fixture's condition is asserted before the behaviour (`.claude/rules/testing.md` §File and naming conventions).
- **A failure message carries a mode, a task and a row index, never an id or what a screen reads** (`stand_act_refused.rs:6-7`, `:89`; `stand_act_ids.rs:8-10`).
- **Tables stated in the test with their row count asserted** (`stand_act_refused.rs:87`; `stand_act_ids.rs:113-116`, `:164-171`; `schema.rs:287`; `command.rs:375`).

- **A refused call is read from `Session::run` itself** — `act` answers `None` for every refusal (`session_common/mod.rs:140-143`), so a check that tells one cause from another matches on `session.run(&call)` (`stand_act_refused.rs:102-108`).

- **A verb is a `VerbSpec` constant listed in `VERBS`, a `Command` variant, and one arm each in `Command::spec`, `validate` and `Session::run`** (`schema.rs:204-270`; `command.rs:103-143`, `:185-203`; `execute.rs:61-94`).
- **An input the driver needs and cannot name is a harness input helper that dispatches and pumps** (`input.rs:227-232`).
- **No `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `unreachable!` or index on what a call supplies, no clock, no print or log in the crate** (`execute.rs:125-134` is the shape: a miss is `ok_or(refusal)`).
- **Every public item documented** — `#![deny(missing_docs)]` (`lib.rs:33`).
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_disabled.rs` — on the stand, a `click` and a `type` aimed at a control reading not enabled are refused `disabled`, and accepted once the app enables it

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_obstructed.rs` — on in-file fixtures booted with the stand's options, a covered target is refused `covered` and a target outside the viewport `off-screen`, each with its control

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_scroll.rs` — on the stand's CRUD list and on in-file fixtures, `scroll` brings an out-of-view target into view and a `click` on it is then accepted; a target it cannot reach is told in its result

- Which of the snapshot nodes of the four lean tasks turn refused under the detection besides the three disabled controls — `timer-progress` is 0 wide until a tick is delivered (`common/mod.rs`, the `rendered` doc) and has not been hit-tested at its own centre → blocks: implementation-scope (the restated table of `stand_act_ids` is written from the run's own listing; the file list above does not move with the answer)

- Does an instant scroll made through the harness helper and settled by `Harness::settle` read `settled` in one step, in both layout modes? → blocks: implementation-scope (the plan states it as a prediction for `stand_act_scroll` to measure; the file list does not move) — and the same question for a nested box, whose write starts the scrollbar fade

- How many `crud-create` clicks put a row past the list's box at 800 × 600, and is it `#crud-list` that clips it? → blocks: implementation-scope (the census measures it before the check is written; if no nested scrolling box clips a row on the stand the plan's stand criterion cannot be met as worded and the run stops and reports)

**Working entry (verbatim):** Refusal detection — not found, stale, disabled, covered by another element, off-screen named per action (v010-11)

**Epoch:** Epoch 4 — Driver core · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Freight on the entry:** three `CARRY:` blocks (433 · 1118 · 628 characters), each folded below under "The carried freight" (`route.py pins`, trail in the run dir: 35 freight blocks on the markerless tail, all `CARRY:`, three of them on line 64, and no abstention printed). No `BLOCKED-ON`, `PREREQ` or `WATCH` on the entry. Three external inputs: the operator's word on the CI red read at Setup (`inputs#I1`), cited under "CI verdict read at Setup"; the answers to the entry's two reserved decisions (`inputs#I2`), cited where each is decided; and the operator's directive at the P5 review of the first plan (`inputs#I3`), cited at the bullets it amends; every other fact below is read from this repository or the route.

**Amended at the P5 review (`inputs#I3`, the operator, 2026-10-07):** the first plan scrolled the viewport only, so on the stand — whose scrollers are nested — the `off-screen` remedy could not be followed. The directive, folded below as validation-1's intent-incomplete arm: `scroll` brings its target into view through nested scroll containers too, in the clean place; a change of what the engine's `scroll_into_view` does for every document is said at the review and is the founder's word; the proof is on the stand (a CRUD row past the list box is refused, `scroll` brings it into view, the click then acts); and where `scroll` cannot bring a target into view, its result says so.

**Premise closure (P3):** every bullet tagged `[inferred]` at the take-up — one the working entry did not state, or a mechanism claim that arrived in the freight — was re-read against `research.md`: eight verified and their tags dropped, one corrected. A bullet with no tag is what the entry states or is verified; a corrected one carries `[premise-corrected: …]`.

The driver's fifth piece, after the session, settle, the schema and the executor: **an action that cannot happen is refused, and the refusal names why**. intent §6 states it — "an action that cannot happen is refused with its cause named — not found · stale · disabled · covered by another element · off-screen" (`escher-0.1.0/intent.md:55-58`) — and the requirement repeats it (`requirements.md:17`, v010-11). At HEAD the eight causes are named and worded (`packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs:9-26`, `:56-101`) and the executor returns one of the five screen-level ones, `not-found` (`packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:125-134`); nothing returns `stale`, `disabled`, `covered` or `off-screen`.

- **Five causes, named per action** — a driver action aimed at a target that cannot take it returns a `Refusal` whose `Cause` is the one that holds: `not-found` · `stale` · `disabled` · `covered` · `off-screen`.

- **Which actions** — the two verbs that name a target by id, `click` and `type` (`execute.rs:65-75`); `press` acts on what holds focus and `advance` names no element, so neither has a target to refuse on. Whether a `press` aimed at a focused control that is disabled is this chunk's question is the plan's, bounded by the entry's words "named per action". Found at P3: no lean-task screen can hold one — the four controls the stand disables are rendered through a Dioxus `disabled:` expression (`flight_booker.rs:91`, `:98`; `crud.rs:113`, `:128`), which writes a truthy attribute or none, and a truthy `disabled` is not focusable (research.md §Patterns detected).

- **Where the detection sits** — in `escher_driver`'s executor, in front of the click: CARRY 3's words are "this entry's detection goes in front of that click, in `escher_driver`'s executor (packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs)". Today `click` resolves its id (`centre_of`, `execute.rs:125-144`) and clicks the centre of the border box (`:65-68`); `type` clicks the same way and then types (`:69-75`).

- **A refusal leaves the instance unchanged** — nothing is dispatched for a refused action; the snapshot before and after is equal, as `stand_act_refused` proves today for `unknown-verb`, `malformed` and `not-found` (CARRY 3; `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_refused.rs`).

- **A refusal still holds nothing of the call** — `Cause`, `Fault` and `Refusal` have no `String` field (`refusal.rs:8-26`, `:114-147`); a detected cause is one of the eight fixed names with its fixed meaning and remedy, and no id, name, value or coordinate enters a refusal, a test name or an assertion message (`.claude/rules/security.md` §Surfaces).

- **`disabled` is the snapshot's reading** — the cause's stated meaning is "the element carries the `disabled` attribute, which the snapshot reads as not enabled" (`refusal.rs:64-67`); it is told from `NodeState::enabled`, the presence reading, never from the attribute's value (CARRY 2).

- **`covered` is told at the point the action would land** `[premise-corrected: the executor's point is the centre of the target's layout box (`execute.rs:135-143`), and a non-atomic inline element has no layout box of its own (`packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:2250-2254`), so that point is not on such a target; the element's own box is its client bounding rect, the snapshot's `bounds` — research.md §Patterns detected]` — the cause's stated meaning is "another element is hit at the point the action would land" (`refusal.rs:68`). The engine's reading exists: `BaseDocument::element_from_point` answers the topmost element at a viewport point with text and anonymous boxes resolved to their element (`document.rs:1575-1600`), and a pointer event's target is that same hit. "Another element" is an answer that is neither the target nor one of its descendants; which point the action lands at is the plan's, from the correction above.

- **`off-screen` is told against the viewport** — the cause's stated meaning is "the element lies outside the viewport" (`refusal.rs:69`); the reading is the target's bounds, or its click point, against the viewport the instance holds. Wholly outside against partly outside, and a target inside a scrolled container, are the plan's from research. Found at P3: the viewport's size in CSS pixels is `Viewport::logical_size` (`packages/blitz-traits/src/shell.rs:120-127`), the snapshot's `bounds` are viewport-relative (`document.rs:2249-2264`), and the raw hit test does not stop at the viewport's edge — only `element_from_point` does (`document.rs:1582-1584`) — so a click aimed outside the viewport can land today. **Amended (`inputs#I3`):** an element inside the viewport and clipped out by a scrolling box that holds it — the directive's "a CRUD row past the list box" — is out of view the same way and is refused `off-screen`, the one cause whose remedy `scroll` answers. Found on the re-read: the hit walk descends into a box's scrollable overflow outside its own box (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:1330-1363`), so a click at such a row's centre can land on the clipped row itself or on whatever is painted there — the reading has to be made explicitly, from the scrollports of the boxes that hold the target, never from the hit.

- **One answer per call, in a fixed order** — where two causes hold at once (a disabled control that is also covered), the refusal names one, by a stated order, as `validate` answers the first failure in its order (`command.rs:161`). The order is the plan's.

- **Proven on the stand, with a minimal fixture where the tasks lack a case** — v010-11's acceptance opens "On the stand"; under the founder's ruling (CARRY 1) the covered case is proven on a minimal fixture beside the stand. Which lean-task elements give `not-found`, `stale` and `disabled`, and whether any lean-task screen holds an off-screen element at the pinned 800 × 600 viewport or `off-screen` needs a fixture too, is research's. Found at P3: three stand controls read not enabled at boot (`flight-return-date`, `crud-update`, `crud-delete`); every id the stand renders at boot lies inside the viewport, pinned by `stand_snapshot` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot.rs:185-197`), so the stand lacks an off-screen element at boot as it lacks a covered one. **Amended (`inputs#I3`):** the stand gains its off-screen case by the driver's own actions — CRUD rows created until one lies past the list box (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs:174-183`: the list is `overflow-y: auto`, `min-height: 150px`) — and the directive's proof runs on it: that row is refused, `scroll` brings it into view, the click then acts. A case scrolling cannot reach, and a viewport that itself scrolls, stay fixtures.

- **A sixth verb, `scroll`, joins the verb table** (decision 2, decided — `inputs#I2`) — a `scroll` naming its target by id brings that element into view and returns as the other acting verbs do; the `off-screen` remedy names it. Closed at P3 in the same pass: the engine's `BaseDocument::scroll_into_view` scrolls the viewport and nothing else (`packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs:619-651`), so a target clipped inside a nested scroll container — on the stand `#task-body` and the CRUD list — is not brought into view by it; the two enums its signature takes are blitz-dom's and neither of the driver's two dependencies re-exports them (`packages/blitz-test-harness/src/lib.rs:23-27`; `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs:29-41`), so the scroll reaches the driver as a harness input helper, not a third dependency; and the engine's pointer path hit-tests at page coordinates (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/driver.rs:51`; `document.rs:1831-1840`), so once a viewport can be scrolled the point an action lands at is the target's client centre plus the viewport's scroll (research.md §Patterns detected). `[premise-corrected: the first plan took the viewport-only scroll as the verb's reach and stated the nested case as a limit with no owner; the directive (inputs#I3) makes the nested case this chunk's — research.md §Patterns detected, "The clean place for the nested scroll"]` **The verb scrolls through nested scroll containers**: every scrolling box that holds the target is scrolled, innermost first, then the viewport. The clean place is the engine's `BaseDocument::scroll_into_view` itself — it is the engine's one implementation of the CSSOM View "scroll an element into view" steps, which scroll every scrolling box ancestor, and it has three callers that all mean that (script `scrollIntoView`, Dioxus `MountedData::scroll_to`, fragment navigation). That changes what the engine does for every document whose target sits inside a nested scrolling box — **the founder's word, asked at the review** (`inputs#I3`). **The verb's result says whether the target is in view after the step**, so a target scrolling cannot reach is told to the caller instead of sending it round the remedy again.
- **The session remembers the ids its screens read** (decision 1, decided — `inputs#I2`) — an id in that record that no element on the screen reads now is `stale`, any other unread id `not-found`.
- **The claim** — v010-11 is the one capability the entry lists; with both decisions made, each of its five causes has a detection this chunk builds.

- **Marker:** 2026-10-07-settle-detection · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-07T10:29:17Z

Give a held headless instance one call that runs every piece of work that is due now and then says, as a typed
value, whether anything is still outstanding — so a step taken through the driver's session returns with its
consequences already on the screen, and no check sleeps, waits or pumps on its own (intent §5; working-route.md:58).

Two layers, both additive. The harness gains `settle`: a bounded loop of the same poll-then-resolve pass `pump`
makes, which keeps poll's answer instead of dropping it (research.md §Patterns detected, "Poll's answer is the render
signal"), repeats while a pass still changed something, and ends in `Settled` or in `NotSettled` naming the busy
source class. The driver's session gains `act`: run a caller's step on the held instance, settle, return — the
entry point "Act by id" later addresses by stable id (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session;
test-plan §3 Pump semantics).

"Settled" means **no work is due**. Render and layout are driven to quiet. A load in flight is reported, never
waited on — settle reads no clock, so it cannot wait for the outside world (per security-plan §API Security, "Request
timeout"). A source only time moves — a timer not yet due, a running animation — does not hold settle open and is
not advanced by it: time on a held instance moves when its caller moves it (per test-plan §5 Session ↔ held
instance; design-system §Motion, Animation runtime). No engine crate, no Dioxus-bridge file and no stand source is
edited (research.md §Files to modify).

1. **Outcome types** — in the new `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs`, define and document:
   - `Busy` — a `Copy + Eq + Debug` enum of the source classes that can hold an instance unsettled: `Render`,
     `Layout`, `Loads`. It names a class only — no node id, element id, name, URL or value (per architecture
     §Standard Contracts → Driver session; security-plan §Threat Model Summary).
   - `Settled { passes: u32, animating: bool }` — how many passes ran, and whether the document's animating reader
     (`BaseDocument::is_animating`, `document.rs:2039-2056`) read true when it returned.
   - `NotSettled { busy: Busy }` — with `Display` (one fixed string per class) and `std::error::Error`.
   - `SETTLE_PASS_LIMIT: u32 = 64` — a public constant; never an env read or an option (per security-plan §Secret
     Management, "Environment values read").

2. **The load counter** — in the same file, a private counting wrapper around a `NetProvider`: it forwards `fetch`
   and `is_noop` to the provider it wraps, counts a request in flight from `fetch` until its handler is consumed by
   `bytes` or dropped unanswered, and keeps a second, only-growing count of handlers finished. It stores counts and
   nothing else — no URL, no request. Every request the engine issues crosses this seam (research.md §Patterns
   detected, "Every request crosses one seam": 7 fetch sites, sweep `net_provider.fetch|network_provider.fetch` over
   `packages/blitz-dom/src`), four of which the document itself does not track.

3. **The harness carries the counter** — in `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs`: `HarnessOptions::into_config`
   (`:43-60`) wraps a supplied provider that is not a no-op in the counter and hands the counter back beside the
   config; `Harness` gains one private field holding it (absent for a document built elsewhere and passed to
   `wrap`, and for an offline one); `from_html_with` and `from_vdom` (`:74-94`) store it. `pump`, `tick`,
   `dispatch`, `wrap`'s signature and every input helper stay as they are — `Harness::pump @ harness.rs:123` keeps
   its 44 callers untouched (research.md §Graph impact).

4. **`Harness::settle`** — in `settle.rs`, `pub fn settle(&mut self) -> Result<Settled, NotSettled>` on
   `impl<D: Document> Harness<D>`:
   - One **pass** is `doc.poll(None)` then `inner_mut().resolve(time)` — `pump`'s two calls, in its order, at the
     harness's own clock value. Around a pass it reads the hover node (`get_hover_node_id`, `document.rs:1951`) and
     the counter's finished count.
   - A pass is **quiet** when poll answered `false`, the hover node is the one it was before the pass, and the
     finished count did not move.
   - After a quiet pass: loads are outstanding when the counter has a request in flight or the document reads
     `has_pending_critical_resources()` (`document.rs:1264`) → `Err(NotSettled { busy: Loads })`; otherwise
     `Ok(Settled { passes, animating })`. It returns at once in both cases — it never spins on a load.
   - `SETTLE_PASS_LIMIT` passes with none quiet → `Err`, the class read off the last pass: `Render` when its poll
     answered `true`, else `Loads` when the finished count moved, else `Layout`.
   - It reads neither `has_changes` nor `take_changed_nodes`, logs nothing, and reads no clock but `self.time`.

5. **Exports** — `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/lib.rs`: declare the module, export `Busy`, `NotSettled`,
   `Settled`, `SETTLE_PASS_LIMIT`, and add settle to the crate doc's list beside the pump/tick line.

6. **Unit tests** — a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the end of `settle.rs` (the crate's first; its path carries
   `settle`, which the gate's filter selects), in two groups.
   - *The counter*, over a hand-written inner provider that keeps the handlers it is given: a fetch reads one in
     flight; `bytes` on the wrapped handler reaches the inner handler with the same url and bytes and reads none in
     flight; a handler dropped unanswered reads none in flight; the finished count grows by one each time and never
     falls; `is_noop` is the inner provider's.
   - *The loop's arithmetic*, over a scripted `Document` — a wrapper around an empty `BaseDocument`
     (`BaseDocument::new`, `document.rs:376`) whose `poll` answers from a script and counts its calls: `false` at
     once is one pass; `true` k times then `false` is k + 1 passes; `true` for ever is `NotSettled { busy: Render }`
     after exactly `SETTLE_PASS_LIMIT` polls; a request still in flight after a quiet pass is `Loads` after exactly
     one poll; a handler that finishes inside a pass costs one more pass. The harness for these is built in-crate
     with a counter attached, which the private field allows.
   - Each `NotSettled` message is non-empty, differs per class and holds no `/`.

7. **The driver's outcome** — `packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs`: a twelfth variant `NotSettled(Busy)` — "the
   instance did not go quiet" — whose message is a fixed string plus the class name, in the form the `Io(kind)` arm
   already uses (`error.rs:58`); add one value per class to the hand-kept list in
   `every_message_is_non_empty_and_holds_no_path` (`error.rs:71-86`). `SessionError` stays `Copy + Eq`.

8. **`Session::act`** — `packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs`: `pub fn act(&mut self, step: impl
   FnOnce(&mut Harness<DioxusDocument>)) -> Result<Settled, SessionError>` — runs `step` on the held instance,
   settles it, and maps `NotSettled` onto the new variant. A step that leaves the instance unsettled is not rolled
   back: the instance keeps what the step did. `harness()` / `harness_mut()` stay.
   `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs`: re-export `Busy` and `Settled` from the harness so a caller names them
   through the driver, and add one sentence on the settled step to the crate doc. The manifest gains nothing: no
   dependency, no feature, no `tracing`.

9. **The stand check** — the new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_settle.rs`, opening with a `//!` doc, declaring
   `mod session_common;`, every test `for incremental in [false, true]`, eight tests:
   1. `a_timer_step_returns_with_its_delayed_update_present` — on `session_common::hold(LeanTask::Timer, …)`: a step
      that delivers 151 ticks returns reading `Elapsed: 15.0s` (the timer has stopped at its duration — the count
      the standing check measures, `stand_timer.rs:41-45`); a step that
      delivers 3 more returns still reading `15.0s`; then ONE step clicks `#timer-reset` and delivers 3 ticks —
      inside the step, after the delivery, the elapsed text still reads `0.0s` (the update is delayed: delivered,
      not applied), and when `act` returns it reads `Elapsed: 0.3s`. Every step is `Ok`.
   2. `a_settle_on_an_idle_instance_changes_nothing` — for each of `LeanTask::ALL` on a held session: `act` with an
      empty step is `Ok(Settled { passes: 1, animating: false })`; the snapshot text is the same before and after;
      `has_changes()` reads false after it; no snapshot node reads focused; a first Tab afterwards focuses
      `back-btn`.
   3. `a_write_made_while_mounting_is_present_after_the_step` — an in-file Dioxus fixture booted with
      `stand::options(incremental)`: a keyed button reveals an element whose `onmounted` handler sets a signal a
      keyed status text shows. On the bare harness, one `click` leaves the status at its first text (one pump is
      not enough — the condition under test), and `settle` then returns `Ok` with `passes >= 2` and the status
      changed. On a second boot held by a `Session`, `act` with the same click returns with the status changed.
   4. `a_load_in_flight_reads_not_settled_until_it_is_answered` — an in-file HTML fixture through
      `Harness::from_html_with`, with `.test` URLs, the bundled font (`stand::font_ctx()`) and a hand-written
      provider that keeps every request for the check to answer (the shape at `render_blocking_stylesheet.rs:17-30`):
      a head stylesheet. `settle` is `Err(NotSettled { busy: Loads })` while the provider holds one request; the
      check answers it with a sheet that `@import`s a second sheet and sets a box's width; `settle` is `Loads`
      again (the import is in flight and on no list of the document's); the check answers the import, which sets
      the box's height; `settle` is `Ok` and `layout_rect` reads both the width and the height.
   5. `a_running_animation_is_reported_and_does_not_hold_the_step` — an in-file HTML fixture with an infinite
      `@keyframes` animation and no provider: `settle` is `Ok(Settled { passes: 1, animating: true })`.
   6. `an_instance_that_never_goes_quiet_ends_at_the_bound` — an in-file Dioxus fixture in which every render
      mounts a freshly keyed element whose `onmounted` handler bumps the key: on a `Session`, `act` returns
      `Err(SessionError::NotSettled(Busy::Render))`, the instance is still readable afterwards, and the error's
      message holds no `/`.
   7. `a_hover_that_moves_with_layout_is_resolved_before_the_step_returns` — an in-file Dioxus fixture booted with
      `stand::options(incremental)`: the pointer rests on a keyed upper box whose click handler removes it, so the
      keyed box below moves under the pointer; a `:hover` rule in the fixture's own style element resizes that
      lower box. After the one pump of `click`, `hovered()` names the lower box and its rect is still the
      un-hovered size (the condition under test); after `settle`, its rect is the hovered size.
   8. `a_hover_that_never_rests_ends_at_the_bound` — an in-file HTML fixture with the pointer on a box whose
      `:hover` rule removes it from layout: `settle` is `Err(NotSettled { busy: Layout })`.
   No test calls `pump`, `tick`, a sleep or a clock. Every element a fixture's check acts on or reads carries an
   author `id`. Tests 3, 4 and 7 each assert first that the fixture produces the condition under test.

10. **Red before green** — before step 4's loop exists, run test 3's bare-harness half with the `settle` call
    left out and record that the status reads its first text after one click; do the same for test 7's control and

    `evidence/red-first.md` — which were red, which were not. The Timer one is predicted NOT red (research.md §Open

- (arch) The workspace gains no crate, binary, feature, env var, listener, port or thread, and no manifest moves — the preservation entry exits 0 (per architecture §Established Decisions → [Driver session]).

- (arch) `escher-driver` names no stand type and no `dioxus-native-dom` feature, and its wire, host and client files are byte-identical to the base — the preservation entry; `stand_session_lifecycle` passes unchanged (per architecture §Occupied Resources → Network ports and listeners).

- (arch) Every settle check runs in both layout modes and reads the same state in each; `packages/blitz-dom`, `packages/dioxus-native-dom` and `packages/blitz-shell` are byte-identical to the base, so every `Document` implementor's `poll` and the shell's `View::poll` behave as before — the preservation entry (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Document core).

- (security) A fixture whose load is not answered reads `NotSettled(Loads)` with no sleep, no clock read, no panic and no hang, in both layout modes — test 4 and the census entries (per security-plan §API Security, row "Request timeout").

- (security) No env read beyond `RUST_LOG`: the census over `settle.rs`, `session.rs` and `error.rs` reads 0, and the host is untouched (per security-plan §Secret Management, "Environment values read").

- (security) The session socket still answers `hello v1` and `stop v1` only and no reply gains a field — `stand_session_lifecycle` and `stand_session_quiet` pass with no edit (per security-plan §Input Validation, row "Driver session socket (escher-driver)").

- (tests) `stand_settle` passes under `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_settle` with 8 passed, and under `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run stand` with no script change, `"failed": 0`, the ok count read from that run's `run.end` line and recorded against the standing 72 (per test-plan §3 `run {selection}`).

- (tests) Time on a held session still moves only with delivered ticks: `stand_session_state` and `stand_timer` pass with no edit, and their files are byte-identical to the base (per test-plan §8 Time (seven_guis timer); §5 Session ↔ held instance).

- (tests) The loads leg is proven on a fixture whose answers the check delivers itself through a hand-written provider — unanswered reads not settled, answered reads settled with the answer's layout — and issues no real fetch (per test-plan §8 Network).

- (tests) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` and `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` pass; the workspace passed · failed · ignored counts are read from that run and recorded against 579 · 0 · 8 (per test-plan §9 Local pre-push gate).
- (tests) The fork's CI run on the pushed sha reads `verdict: green`, its run id named in the report — the only witness of the MSRV build and of the windows and macos legs (per test-plan §9 Legs).

- (obs) The loop, the session step and the new check install no subscriber, read no env var and print or log nothing; `escher-driver` ends with no span, no event and no `tracing` dependency — the census entry and the preservation entry over its manifest (per obs-plan §3 Observability Harness Contract → Logging stack; §4 Span / Trace Coverage).

- (obs) `host_log` passes unchanged: the real `escher-session` at `RUST_LOG=trace` writes no stable id and no accessible name to stderr and 0 bytes to stdout (per obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing & Compliance → Scrubbing).

- (layouts) A held instance settled with no step reads as a fresh boot, and the Timer task's ids, the TaskShell mount, the pinned viewport and `escher-session`'s argv, exit codes and empty stdout are unchanged — test 2, `stand_session_fresh`, `host_binary` and the preservation entry (per layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens, seven_guis Home and TaskShell; §Surface: cli → Primary screens, `escher-session`).

body: - **`Harness::pump`** — 44 call sites: 28 in 12 `tests/blitz-tests/tests` files, 16 in the harness crate — `harness.rs:77` · `92` · `131` · `192` and the 12 input helpers at `input.rs:107` · `113` · `119` · `133` · `148` · `162` · `168` · `174` · `180` · `197` · `217` · `230`. Its signature and behaviour are not changed by anything listed below, so none of the 44 is threaded.

- **`Document::poll`** (trait, `document.rs:141`) — called from `poll_subdocuments` `document.rs:801`, `View::poll` `window.rs:375` and `Harness::pump` `harness.rs:124`; `DioxusDocument::poll` (`dioxus_document.rs:256`) from `dioxus_document.rs:457`, `dioxus_document_tests.rs:142`, `element_id.rs:415`; `ScriptDocument::poll` (`blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:423`) from two of its own tests and `wpt/runner/src/test_runners/mod.rs:158`. No change to the trait is needed: the answer settle wants is the one it already returns.
- **`has_changes` · `take_changed_nodes`** — outside blitz-dom's own unit tests: `stand_diff.rs:101` · `103` and `window.rs:376`. Settle is not added to either list.

- **`is_animating`** — `resolve.rs:161`, `window.rs:417`, `render_blocking_stylesheet.rs:81` and 13 sites in `fragment_navigation.rs`. **`has_pending_critical_resources`** — `resolve.rs:60`, `blitz-paint/src/render.rs:176`, `window.rs:418`, `render_blocking_stylesheet.rs:55` · `67`. Both are read-only additions of one more caller.

- **`Session::harness` · `harness_mut`** — 17 and 25 call sites, all in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/{session_common/mod.rs, stand_session_*.rs}` (5 further `harness` rows are a same-named local function in `pointer_events.rs`). Neither signature changes.

- **Names** — `settle` · `Settled` · `NotSettled` · `Settle` · `is_settled` · `SettleError` · `Busy` · `is_quiet` · `pending_work`: 0 rows on `symbol`; the names do not exist on the plane, so they are free, not "leaf".

- **Crate edges** — `escher-driver → blitz-test-harness, dioxus-native-dom`; `blitz-test-harness → blitz-dom, dioxus-native-dom, blitz-html, blitz-traits`; `seven_guis → escher-driver, blitz-test-harness`; `blitz-tests → blitz-test-harness, escher-driver`. A type defined in the harness is visible to the driver as a normal (non-dev) dependency; the driver re-exports nothing of the harness today.

- **`SessionError`** — sweep `SessionError::{Variant} =>` over `packages/escher-driver/src examples/seven_guis tests/blitz-tests/tests` outside `error.rs`: 0 hits · nothing to change — a twelfth variant breaks no `match` outside its own file. (`SessionError::` at large: 48 hits outside `error.rs`, constructions and `matches!` arms.)

- **Poll's answer is the render signal, and it is exact for "no work now"** (`dioxus_document.rs:267-276`): with nothing dirty and no task woken, `wait_for_work` is `Pending` and `poll` returns before rendering or delivering a `mounted` event. So a poll on an idle instance is inert, and "poll until it answers `false`" ends.

- **One pass is not always the last** — three places leave work behind: a `mounted` handler runs after the render inside `poll` (`dioxus_document.rs:283`) and anything it writes waits for the next poll; `resolve` returns unstyled while a head stylesheet is pending (`resolve.rs:60-62`); `refresh_hover` runs after damage is cleared and leaves its restyle "for the next resolve pass" (`resolve.rs:131-138`). The equality a settle loop needs: *a pass in which poll answered `false`, no load was answered and the hover node did not move leaves nothing a further pass would change* — the three writers above are the only ones found; the first and third are by code read, not measured.

- **Loads: the document sees three of seven request kinds** — sweep `net_provider.fetch|network_provider.fetch` over `packages/blitz-dom/src`: 7 sites — `mutator.rs:1156` (link stylesheet; tracked as critical only in the head), `mutator.rs:1216` and `layout/damage.rs:511` (images; `pending_images`), `iframe.rs:135` (iframe HTML; `iframe_loads`), `net.rs:225` (`@import`; untracked), `net.rs:503` (`@font-face`; untracked), `document.rs:1114` (stylesheet reload; untracked). A reader over the document's own collections would call an instance settled with a font or an import in flight.

- **Every request crosses one seam** — all seven sites call the document's `net_provider`, and each hands over a boxed handler that is consumed by `bytes` (`blitz-traits/src/net.rs:34-36`) and answers on the calling thread (`net.rs:116-125`). A provider wrapped at `HarnessOptions::into_config` (`harness.rs:44-59`) therefore sees every request issued and every handler answered or dropped, with no engine edit. The equality the loads leg needs: *handlers alive = requests in flight; an answered handler has already put its message on the channel when `bytes` returns, and the next `resolve` applies it* (`resolve.rs:49`).

- **An unanswered head stylesheet blocks layout for good** — a handler dropped without an answer sends nothing, so its id stays in `pending_critical_resources` and every later `resolve` returns early (`document.rs:1268-1269`; `resolve.rs:60-62`). Settle must read that as loads still busy, not as quiet.

- **Time-moved sources cannot be waited out without a clock** — `is_animating` (`document.rs:2039-2056`) is true for a canvas for as long as it exists, and its scrollbar-fade term reads the wall clock (`:1801-1806`); the only loop that waits on it sleeps (`fragment_navigation.rs:31-42`). The stand's styles have no transition, animation or keyframes (0 hits) but do have three scrollable regions (`app.rs:197` · `335`, `crud.rs:181`), so a scroll on the stand starts a wall-clock fade.

- **The stand's only delayed update is delivered ticks** — the Timer coroutine is the one asynchronous source on the four lean tasks, and one poll applies every delivered tick (`stand_timer.rs:41-45`: 151 ticks, one pump). By code read, an input helper's single pump after `deliver` therefore already shows the ticks; a settle check on the Timer is unlikely to be red before the fix. The case one pump does NOT cover has to come from a fixture (a `mounted` handler that writes state).

- **Time on a held session is pinned as caller-driven** — `timer_time_moves_only_with_delivered_ticks` (`stand_session_state.rs:132-169`) asserts a pump with no delivered tick leaves the time where it was.

- **One behaviour per integration file, `//!` doc first, both layout modes** — `stand_timer.rs:1-9`; a fixture the lean tasks lack lives in the check's own file and boots with `stand::options(incremental)` (`stand_diff.rs:89-94`).
- **A stand check names `mod common;` / `mod session_common;` and restates nothing** — `session_common/mod.rs:1-8`, `hold` at `:34-44`.
- **Typed, fixed-string, `Copy` outcomes in the driver** — `error.rs:6-33`; every public item documented (`lib.rs:20`).
- **Hand-written net fakes, private to their file** — `render_blocking_stylesheet.rs:17-30`, `stand_boot.rs:11-21`; no shared fake exists and none is needed for one more file.

- **Harness additions sit beside `pump`, not inside it** — `tick` and `set_viewport_size` call `pump` rather than changing it (`harness.rs:129-132` · `182-193`); the upstream-owned file stays additive.
- `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs` — the settle loop, its outcome types and the counting net provider
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_settle.rs` — the Timer proof on a held session, the idle readings, and the in-file fixtures
- `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs` — the harness keeps the load counter its options built
- `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/lib.rs` — the new module and its exports
- `packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs` — the session's settled step
- `packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs` — the not-settled outcome and its unit-test list
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` — the re-export and the crate doc

- Is the Timer flow red before the fix? By code read it is not (one pump applies delivered ticks), so the stand check alone cannot be seen red-first; the fixture carries the red. → blocks: implementation-scope — /implement measures both on the unfixed tree and records which was red.

- Does `wait_for_work` answer `Ready` for a task that was only woken (no dirty component), in every case the stand produces? `stand_timer` says yes for the coroutine; not read further in the dependency. → blocks: implementation-scope.

- How does time pass for an agent driving the Timer over the wire, once commands exist? Nothing in this chunk decides it (no wire, no command), and the recorded check pins caller-driven time. → a note for the route, not a question: no step here is blocked.
**Working entry (verbatim):** Settle detection — UI quiescence across render, layout, timers and pending loads; delayed stand update passes with no sleep (v010-10)

**Epoch:** Epoch 4 — Driver core · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Freight on the entry:** none (`route.py pins`, trail in the run dir: 24 freight blocks on the markerless tail, all `CARRY:`, on lines 62 · 64 · 66 · 69 · 71 · 73 · 77 · 84 · 86 · 88 · 90 · 92 — none on line 58, and no abstention printed). No external input: every fact below is read from this repository or the route.
**Premise closure (P3):** every `[inferred]` bullet below was re-read against `research.md`. A bullet with no tag is verified; a corrected one carries `[premise-corrected: …]`.

The driver's second piece, after the session: a way to know that a held headless instance has **gone quiet** after a step, and to reach that state without the caller sleeping, pumping or waiting on its own. intent §Principles orders it between change tracking (built) and the command and refusal model (next entry); intent §5 states the observed gap — "a check must pump or wait on its own" — and the expectation it serves: acting "returns only once the UI has settled, so a stand flow with a delayed update passes with no sleep anywhere in the check".

- **Quiescence is one answer over four sources** — the entry names them: render, layout, timers and pending loads. The instance is settled when none of the four has work outstanding; one source still busy means not settled.

- **Render** — the app's own pending work: a dirty component, a woken task, a queued mounted event. The signal is the one `Document::poll` already returns — `DioxusDocument::poll` returns `true` after a render pass and the sub-documents' answer when the VirtualDom has no work (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:256-286`); the trait default returns `false` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:141-145`); `Harness::pump` discards it (`packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs:123-126`). One poll is not always enough: a poll delivers `mounted` events after it renders (`dioxus_document.rs:283` · `219-239`), so a `mounted` handler that writes state leaves a dirty component only the next poll renders (by code read, not measured — the bridge test covers delivery, not a handler's write).

- **Layout** — style and layout resolved for everything the last render changed. `[premise-corrected: one resolve is not always enough — resolve.rs:60-62 · 131-138]` `resolve` returns before styling while a head stylesheet is still loading (`packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs:60-62`), and it ends by re-resolving the hover node against the fresh layout, leaving any restyle that causes "for the next resolve pass" and dropping the changed-or-not answer (`resolve.rs:131-138`; `refresh_hover` returns it, `document.rs:1942-1949`). A resolve never queues a device change itself — only `set_viewport` and the media setters do (`document.rs:1959-1963`) — and sub-documents are resolved inside their parent's pass (`resolve.rs:140-164`).

- **Timers** — a delayed update the app has scheduled. On the stand that is the Timer task's coroutine, which awaits the stand's tick seam (`TimerTicks`, `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs:10-41`): a delivered tick is applied only when the VirtualDom is next polled, so a tick delivered and not yet applied is outstanding work. The headless stand never takes the 100 ms wall-clock arm (`timer.rs:53-56`): `stand_root` always provides the tick context (`examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:100-103`). That coroutine is the only asynchronous source on the four lean tasks (grep `spawn(|use_effect|use_resource|use_future|onmounted|use_coroutine|async move` over `examples/seven_guis/src`: 5 hits, 2 in `timer.rs`, 3 in `circle_drawer.rs`, which is not a lean task).

- **What settle answers for a source that only time moves** is a decision this chunk makes and states, and the code narrows it: the engine's animating reader (`BaseDocument::is_animating`, `document.rs:2039-2056`) ORs in a canvas (always animating), a custom widget asking for redraw, a scroll animation and the overlay-scrollbar fade — and the last reads the wall clock (`scrollbars_animating`, `document.rs:1801-1806`, `Instant::elapsed`). The one existing loop that waits for it to read false sleeps 8 ms a turn under a 5 s timeout (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/fragment_navigation.rs:31-42`). So "wait until nothing is animating" cannot be built without a sleep; a periodic source never goes quiet on its own either. The stand's styles carry no transition, animation or keyframes (grep `transition|animation|@keyframes` over `examples/seven_guis/src`: 0 hits).

- **Pending loads** — a resource requested and not yet answered: an image, a stylesheet, a font, a sub-document. `[premise-corrected: the document tracks three of seven fetch sites, and one named collection is not a request list — research.md §Patterns detected]` The engine issues requests at seven sites (grep `net_provider.fetch|network_provider.fetch` over `packages/blitz-dom/src`) and tracks three kinds as pending: a head stylesheet (`pending_critical_resources`, `mutator.rs:1150-1154`, read by `has_pending_critical_resources`), an image by URL (`pending_images`, both image sites) and an iframe's HTML (`iframe_loads`, `iframe.rs:81-95`). A body stylesheet, an `@import` (`net.rs:225`), an `@font-face` source (`net.rs:503`) and a stylesheet reload (`document.rs:1114`) are in flight with no record on the document. `pending_style_image_nodes` is a work queue drained inside the same resolve (`layout/damage.rs:431`), not a list of requests. An answered load is applied by `handle_messages` at the start of `resolve` (`resolve.rs:49`; `document.rs:1243-1254`), never by `poll`. Every request does pass through the document's one `NetProvider` (`blitz-traits/src/net.rs:19-30`).

- **The loads leg needs a fixture** — the stand is offline (`net_provider: None`, `stand.rs:65`), so no lean task ever has a load pending: this leg is proven on a minimal fixture beside the stand (intent §Principles, "The stand is the proof" — the founder's ruling, 2026-10-06), with a hand-written net provider the check answers itself. The existing one (`ManualNetProvider`) is private to `tests/blitz-tests/tests/render_blocking_stylesheet.rs:17-30`.

- **A wait that ends** — settling is a bounded loop of polls and resolves, never a sleep and never a wall-clock read: `poll(None)` uses a no-op waker (`dioxus_document.rs:257-261`) and `resolve` takes the harness's own clock value (`harness.rs:125`). So the loop needs no clock, and its bound can be a count of passes. An instance that does not go quiet inside the bound ends in a typed outcome that says which source was still busy, rather than hanging the caller or returning as if settled — what this chunk builds, stated here as intent; the plan gives it its shape.

- **The check on the stand (the in-process leg of v010-10; the cap itself is not claimed here — Boundaries)** — a stand flow on the Timer task in which the update lands after the step through the async path, and the check holds the post-step state the moment the step returns: no `sleep`, no wait and no pump of its own anywhere in the check, in both layout modes. Today every such check pumps by hand after delivering ticks (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_timer.rs:13-14` · `27-28` · `41-42`; `stand_session_state.rs:150-151` · `162-163`; `session_common/mod.rs:51-54`).

- **Reachable from the session** — the held instance is already reachable: `Session` hands out the bare harness (`packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:53-61`), so anything the harness gains is callable through it with no session change; a session-level entry point is the plan's choice. The session host keeps the timer's `TimerTicks` handle alive for the session's life and does nothing with it (`examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:34-45`). The driver-session scope's forward note — "the later Settle detection entry advances it" — stays a hypothesis: a recorded check pins the opposite today, "timer time moves only with delivered ticks" (`stand_session_state.rs:132-169`).

- **Not Act by id** (working-route.md:62 — "driver actions addressed by stable id, returning after settle with the diff (v010-09, v010-06)"). This chunk builds what that entry returns *after*; it addresses nothing by stable id and returns no diff. Its five CARRYs stay on that entry.

- **Not the command and refusal schema** (working-route.md:60) and **no wire change**: settle is an in-process call on the held instance — nothing it reads lives across the socket. The session socket stays `hello` and `stop` only — a command that carries anything of the screen is a new crossing question (`.claude/rules/security.md` §Surfaces), and it belongs to the entries that define commands.

- **Not Driver command spans** (working-route.md:66 — "one span per driver command covering settle wait, diff size and refusal cause"). The span over the settle wait is that entry's. Neither crate the loop can live in carries a `tracing` dependency (`packages/blitz-test-harness/Cargo.toml`, `packages/escher-driver/Cargo.toml`: none), so this chunk adds no log call site at all.

- **No new listener, port, env var or workspace crate** — every reader the loop needs is public on a crate the harness already depends on (`poll`, `resolve`, `is_animating`, `has_pending_critical_resources`, `get_hover_node_id`, the `NetProvider` trait).

- **The windowed path is not changed** — `View::poll` (`packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:372-390`) is the shell's only caller of `Document::poll` and of `take_changed_nodes`; settle is a headless caller of the same methods and needs no change to the trait or to what `poll` returns.
- **Incremental and non-incremental layout stay identical** — every pipeline check here runs `for incremental in [false, true]`.
- **No sleep and no font skip in any check** (`.claude/rules/testing.md` §Determinism); the timer is driven only through its `TimerTicks` handle.

- **v010-10 is not claimed by this chunk** — decided at the P5 review (the operator, 2026-10-07). The requirement reads "acting returns only once the UI has settled" and its method is e2e; what this chunk builds is an in-process step, which is no action an agent can run; the Timer check is predicted green before the fix, so it cannot show the capability arriving; and in `escher-session` nobody delivers ticks, so an agent meets no delayed update yet. The Timer check stays, as a test of the in-process step. The cap's driver leg — a driver action on the Timer returning settled with the delayed update present — is carried to the route at the wrap; this entry was the only markerless one naming v010-10.

- **Code** — `[premise-corrected: no engine, Dioxus-bridge or stand source needs an edit — research.md §Files to modify]` `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/` (the loop, its outcome types, the harness's construction path) · `packages/escher-driver/src/{session,error,lib}.rs` (if the plan gives the session its own entry point) · `tests/blitz-tests/tests/` (a new stand check with its fixtures). Read and left as they are: `packages/blitz-dom/src/{document,resolve}.rs`, `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs`, `examples/seven_guis/src/{stand,session_host}.rs` and `tasks/timer.rs`.

- **architecture** — §Standard Contracts (the headless `Harness`, the driver session and its "Not built: … settle" clause), §Cross-cutting Patterns (Invalidation and state integrity — the changed set, which settle neither reads nor drains), the Architecture paragraph's "still to come — settle detection".

- **test-plan** — `[premise-corrected: the no-sleep rule is `.claude/rules/testing.md` §Determinism, not a test-plan section — tests extract]` §3 (Core · Pump semantics · Input helpers · the stand checks' drive surface; keyed contract `session-lifecycle`), §5 (Session ↔ held instance — the timer-time claim), §8 (Time — "applied on the next pump"; Network — the hand-written provider).
- **obs-plan** — §3 (the no-subscriber, no-env, no-print census over the new check) and §4 (escher-driver stays without a span, an event or a `tracing` dependency).

- **security-plan** — `[premise-corrected: "§Surfaces" is a heading of `.claude/rules/security.md`; in the plan the content sits under the three sections named here — security extract]` §Threat Model Summary (the local-IPC vector), §Input Validation (the driver-session rows — the wire stays two verbs), §API Security (no request timeout: the bound is what ends a wait).

- **a11y-plan** — none: a poll that finds no work returns before it delivers anything (`dioxus_document.rs:268-275`), so a settle on an idle instance moves no focus, and settle neither reads nor drains the changed set the tree refresh rests on.
- **design-system · layout-templates** — none: no style value and no markup is touched; §Motion's animating set is what the time-moved-sources decision answers for.

- `4ed27b535c6c` (the last wrap's flip, and HEAD) — **green**, checks 16/16, wall 560 s, CI#37596819847 completed/success, read from `Turbolet85/escher` by full sha (`ci.py conclusion`, trail `ci-no-marker.json` in the run dir). No red and no `not green` to disposition.
