title: 1a. The measured limits, said by the tool (`packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs`, `schema.rs`, `lib.rs`)

data.head: ### 1a. The measured limits, said by the tool (`packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs`, `schema.rs`, `lib.rs`)

body:
The option the founder chose for fork 9 has a second half: "the limits are stated where the tool describes `bounds`
and `covered`" (`inputs#I3`; the operator's review, `inputs#I4`). An agent reads the tool, not the masters, so each
limit is written into the text of the library an agent is served.

- **`covered`** — into the cause's own `meaning` sentence (`packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs:69`). It is the
  site an agent reaches first: the sentence is on stdout in every `covered` refusal's JSON from this chunk on.

- **`bounds`** — into the schema's help for the two result fields through which a node's bounds leave: `snapshot`'s
  `text` (`packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:204-209`) and the acting verbs' `changed` (`schema.rs:177-183`).
  No help text is served by this chunk's commands; the schema's help is what "Self-description" serves, so it is the
  first description of `bounds` an agent will be given. The crate doc (`lib.rs`) says the same for a library caller.

- **The words are step 1's readings, never the hypotheses.** Each sentence states what `evidence/engine-findings.md`
  measured: for `bounds`, that a box which is itself scrolled reads its bounds shifted by its own scroll offset and
  is named in `changed` though it has not moved, and what step 1 read of a `click` naming such a box; for `covered`,
  what step 1 read of a control lying where a scrolled-out row extends. A hypothesis step 1 read false is not
  written; the reading that stands is.

- **The check that holds the text** — the unit tests that pin these texts hold the new sentences word for word:
  `each_cause_states_its_meaning_and_its_remedy` (`refusal.rs:215`) for `covered`, and
  `every_verb_states_its_help_its_arguments_and_a_result` (`schema.rs:313`) joined by a row per amended help string;
  step 6's row for a `covered` refusal asserts the JSON carries the sentence. The cause set stays eight and every
  text stays a fixed string.

title: 2. The schema: three session-level rows, a sixth argument kind (`packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs`)

data.head: ### 2. The schema: three session-level rows, a sixth argument kind (`packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs`)

body: - `VerbSpec` gains a level — instance or session. The six standing rows are instance-level and keep their order.

- `VERBS` grows from six rows to nine: `start`, `status` and `stop` are appended as session-level rows, each with its
  help. `start` takes one required argument `app` of a new kind, **name** (1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`,
  the label's grammar, `packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:13-18`); `status` and `stop` take none.

- Result fields: `start` returns `label` (text), `pid` and `idle_expiry_s`; `status` returns `label`, `pid`,
  `served` and `idle_expiry_s`; `stop` returns `stopped` (flag). The three numbers need a new field kind, **count**
  (a whole number).
- `type`'s help is restated: it replaces what the control holds, and an empty text clears it.

- The table's unit tests are restated in the same change: nine rows in the stated order, each row's level, the six
  argument kinds with their bounds, the new field kind. The session address is not an argument of any row: it is the
  command line's own `--session` option.

- `validate` stays the check of what a session runs. A session-level verb handed to it is refused `unknown-verb`
  before its arguments are read — the standing fallback at `command.rs:208-209` ("a verb the table lists in a shape no
  command has is not one this function knows") made the first check, so the answer does not depend on the arguments.

- A second public check, `validate_session`, turns a call naming a session-level verb into a typed session command
  (`start` with its `app`, `status`, `stop`) or a refusal, by the same rules and the same fixed order `validate`
  uses; an instance-level verb handed to it is `unknown-verb`.

- Unit tests: every instance verb still reaches its command; each session-level verb is refused by `validate` and
  admitted by `validate_session`; one malformed witness per rule for `app`. The test
  `every_verb_of_the_table_is_reached_and_names_its_own_spec` (`command.rs:579`) is restated over the two levels.

- After the focusing click, when the snapshot read the target with a `value` (a control that holds one), the driver
  selects the control's whole content through the engine's own select-all — the key `a` with the engine's action
  modifier, the arm at `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/text.rs:244-248`; the modifier is Super on macOS and Control
  elsewhere (`packages/blitz-dom/src/util.rs:7-10`, crate-private, so the driver states the same two arms beside its
  standing macOS arm at `execute.rs:383-388`) — and then types, which replaces the selection.

- With an empty text the selection is deleted through the driver's own backspace path (`press`, which adds the macOS
  key binding), so the control reads empty.
- A target that reads no `value` is typed into as today: no extra key is pressed.

- `Session::run`'s doc and the crate doc say so. The new check `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_filled.rs`, in
  both layout modes: after `type` on the filled `flight-start` the control's value is exactly the text; `type` with
  an empty text leaves it empty; an empty control reads as before the change; the diff names the control. It types
  characters and clicks only — its one deleting step is the driver's own empty-text path. The same file holds the
  mask's JSON case on an in-file password fixture: the written form of a driver `type` into it carries
  `MASKED_VALUE` and no occurrence of the typed text.

title: 5. The record of ids is bounded in bytes (`packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs`)

data.head: ### 5. The record of ids is bounded in bytes (`packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs`)

body:
`SeenIds::record` does not record an id longer than `MAX_ID_BYTES` (`inputs#I2`): no call can name one, so `stale`
against `not-found` is never asked of it. One unit test beside the standing count test: an over-long id is not held,
an id of exactly the bound is.
A hand-written, output-only writer (`inputs#I2`): no dependency enters. Every form is exactly one line.

- **An outcome** — an object whose keys are the verb's result fields, in the table's order: the screen as
  `{"text":"…"}`; an acting verb as `settled`, `busy` (present only when not settled, one of `BUSY_CLASSES`),
  `added`, `removed`, `changed`, then `advanced_ms` or `in_view` where the verb has it.

- **A node** — an object with the fields `NODE_FIELDS` names, in that order: `id`, `parent` (left out when the node
  has none), `role` (the spelling `Snapshot::to_text` writes), `name`, `enabled` and `checked` (each left out when the
  node has none), `value` (left out when the node has none), `focused`, and `bounds` as an array of four numbers —
  x, y, width, height — each the shortest decimal that reads back the same; a number that is not finite is `null`.

- **A refusal** — `{"refused":{"cause":…,"meaning":…,"remedy":…}}` from the cause's three fixed strings, with
  `"fault"` (the fault's fixed sentence) beside a malformed one.

- **A session error** — `{"error":{"kind":…,"message":…}}`: a fixed kebab-case word per `SessionError` variant and
  its fixed message.
- **A session command's answer** — the fields step 2 names.
- **Strings** — `"` and `\` escaped, U+0000 to U+001F as `\n`, `\r`, `\t` or `\u00XX`, everything else as its UTF-8.

- Nothing is written by `Debug` of a `Call`, a `Command`, an `Outcome` or a `Refusal`. Unit tests over built values,
  each table stated with its row count: the escaping rows, one row per `Outcome` variant, per cause, per
  `SessionError` variant, a node with every optional field present and one with none, a masked value written as the
  mask.
- The version word becomes `v2` for every request; a known word with another version is still `refused version`.

- A third request: `call v2`, the verb, then one word per argument — the argument's name, `=`, a one-letter kind
  (`t` text, `n` whole number, `f` flag), `:`, the value. Verb, names and text values are escaped: every byte that is
  not an ASCII letter, a digit or one of `-`, `_`, `.`, `~` is written as `%` and two uppercase hex digits. A line
  that does not decode — a bad escape, bytes that are not UTF-8, a kind letter outside the three, a number or flag
  that does not parse — is `refused malformed` and changes nothing.

- Bounds: a request line at most 16,384 bytes (the widest validated call — a `type` with a 1024-byte id and a
  4096-byte text, every byte escaped — is 15,360 bytes of values); a lifecycle reply keeps a small bound, restated
  for its widest case; a call's answer at most 1,048,576 bytes.

- Replies: `ok v2 accepted` or `ok v2 refused` followed by the JSON line; `ok v2 oversize` when the answer is over
  its bound (the step ran and is not rolled back); `hello`'s reply gains the host's idle expiry in seconds. The
  answer's bound is on the JSON line alone, without the words in front of it, and framing an answer is one function
  of the wire that takes the line and returns the reply, so the bound is testable on a made value.

- **The answer bound's witness** (`inputs#I4`; no stand screen can reach it): unit rows on that function — a made
  answer of exactly 1,048,576 bytes is framed as an ordinary accepted answer and round-trips, one of 1,048,577 bytes
  is framed `ok v2 oversize`; and `ok v2 oversize` parses to its own reply.
- Read bounds: 2 s on each read and write as today; a client reads a call's answer under 30 s (`inputs#I2`).

- The eight unit tests are restated for the grown grammar and joined by: every request and reply round-trips; the
  escape table; a decoded call equals the encoded one for every argument kind, an id holding `/`, `:`, `[`, `]`, a
  space and a line break among them; the widest validated call fits its bound; each undecodable line is refused.

title: 8. The host runs calls and expires; the client sends one

data.head: ### 8. The host runs calls and expires; the client sends one

body:
- `packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs` — `serve` gains the idle expiry as a parameter and hands the session to its
  answer loop. A `call` request is decoded and run through `Session::run` and nothing else; the outcome or the
  refusal is written by step 6's forms and framed by step 7's replies. The loop waits on the listener without
  blocking, polling as the client does (25 ms), and when no request has been answered for the expiry it ends exactly
  as `stop` does: session dropped, socket file and state directory removed, `Ok`. An accepted connection is read and
  written under the standing 2 s bounds. A broken or undecodable connection changes nothing.

- `packages/escher-driver/src/client.rs` — a public `call` sends one call to the session in a state directory and
  returns its answer: whether it was accepted, and the JSON line as text, never decoded. `Hello` gains the expiry.

- `packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs` — a thirteenth variant for an answer over the wire's bound, with a fixed
  message; the standing message test covers it.

- The rest of the answer bound's witness: the client's reading of a reply is one function from the reply to the
  caller's result, and a unit row holds that the `oversize` reply reads as the thirteenth variant; step 9's ending
  table holds that this variant ends a command as a session error — the error object on stdout, its fixed message
  on stderr, status `3`.
- The crate exports `IDLE_EXPIRY`, 1800 s.

- Callers of the changed `serve`, from the graph (research.md §Graph impact): `main @ examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:49`,
  `session_host @ tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_session_lifecycle.rs:103`,
  `session_host_with_typed_text @ tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_session_quiet.rs:101`.

One public entry takes the arguments after the program's name, the names of the apps the binary boots, and a boot
function from an app's name to a `Session`; it writes the answer and returns the process status. It installs no
subscriber and reads no environment variable.

- **Reading a line**, in this order:
  1. No first word, or an argument that is not UTF-8: usage.
  2. `serve`: the host role, exactly `serve <app> --session <dir>`; anything else is usage. It boots the app, serves
     it with `IDLE_EXPIRY`, and returns `0` after a stop or an expiry.
  3. Any other first word is looked up in the verb table; a word the table does not hold is the refusal
     `unknown-verb`.
  4. `start` takes the app as its one positional word (the form the founder's fork 2 shows). Every other argument of
     every command is a named flag spelt as the table spells the argument: `--id`, `--text`, `--key`, `--ms` with
     one value, `--shift` bare. A flag the verb's row does not name, a flag given twice, a value that is missing or
     not of its kind and a stray word are the `malformed` refusal with the fault the schema already has for it.
  5. The call is checked (`validate`, or `validate_session`) before the session address is asked for: a refused call
     never touches a session.
  6. `--session <dir>` exactly once, else usage. For `start`, an app the binary does not boot is usage, naming the
     apps.

- **Running it**: `start` spawns the running binary itself in the host role with stdin, stdout and stderr closed,
  waits up to 30 s for it to answer (`client::start`), and prints the session's facts; `status` is `attach`; `stop`
  is `stop`; an instance verb is `client::call`.

- **The four endings**: accepted — the answer on stdout, status `0` (an instance that did not go quiet is accepted:
  `settled` reads false); refused — the refusal on stdout, status `1`; usage — one fixed usage line on stderr built
  from the table's words and the app names, stdout empty, status `2`; session error — the error object on stdout,
  its fixed message on stderr, status `3`. No ending echoes anything the caller typed.

- stdout is written as one line and a line break; a write to a closed pipe is not a panic. No path that reads argv
  can panic, index or unwrap on what the caller supplied.

- Unit tests over the argv reader alone (no session): one row per rule above, the rows counted; and over the
  endings as a table from a result to what is written and returned — an accepted answer, a refusal, each
  `SessionError` variant (the thirteenth among them), a usage error — the rows counted.

- `lib.rs`: the crate doc's sentences that this chunk makes false (`lib.rs:13-16`, `:32-33`) are rewritten to what
  is built; the new public items are re-exported (the count of re-exported names is read before and after — 33 at
  the base per architecture §Standard Contracts; record what the edit makes it).

`main` installs the sink first, as today, then hands argv, the four slugs and the stand's boot to step 9's entry.
The boot is today's: the Timer's session carries `stand::timer_step`, every task boots with `stand::options(true)`.
The two-argument form `<task> <state-dir>` is gone; the host role is `serve <task> --session <dir>`.

title: 11. Process checks on the real binary (`examples/seven_guis/tests/`)

data.head: ### 11. Process checks on the real binary (`examples/seven_guis/tests/`)

body:
All `cfg(unix)`, each starting and stopping its own host, every wait bounded, the host behind the kill-and-reap
guard, state directories under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR`, failures printing a kind, a row index and a count only.

- `host_binary.rs` — restated for the new argv: `serve counter --session <dir>` serves and stops with nothing on
  the host's stdout; a line with no command, `serve` with an unknown task and `start` with an unknown task each exit
  `2` with a usage line on stderr, nothing on stdout and no state directory.

- `cli_commands.rs` (new) — through the binary as a client:
  - `start`, `status`, `stop` on each of the four tasks: status `0`, one JSON line, `idle_expiry_s` 1800.
  - Each of the six verbs accepted at least once, the JSON line holding exactly the verb's fields.
  - `snapshot` on each of the four tasks: the stdout line equals the library's JSON form of the in-process
    snapshot text of the same task booted in the same layout mode, and is at most `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` bytes.
  - Refusals by status `1` with the cause in the JSON: `disabled` (`crud-delete`, `flight-return-date`),
    `not-found`, `stale`, `off-screen` then `scroll` reading `in_view` true (the standing twelve-Creates case),
    `time-unavailable` (`advance` on the counter), `unknown-verb`, `malformed` (a missing `--id`) — the last two with
    no session running.
  - A session error by status `3`: a command at a directory with no session prints the error object and the fixed
    message.
  - `press --key tab` on a fresh boot: the diff names exactly `back-btn` as gaining focus.
  - Streams: every stdout is one line, holds no ESC byte, and on an accepted command with `RUST_LOG` unset the
    client's stderr is empty.

- `host_timer.rs` (new) — boots `serve timer`, runs a hosted `advance --ms 250`, and reads `advanced_ms` 200 and the
  Timer's elapsed text one tick pair on (`examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:127-133`, the row 250 → 200); no sleep, no
  clock read.

- `host_log.rs` — extended: with the host at `RUST_LOG=trace`, a sentinel text is typed through a hosted `type`,
  beside a `snapshot` and a `click`; the sentinel, the id needles and the name needles each occur 0 times in the
  host's stderr; the lines whose target is `escher_driver` and whose span is `command` number exactly the calls
  sent; every line is stamped. Nothing is asserted on the total line count, which differs between the two builds.
- `tests/common/mod.rs` — the helpers these four share (running the client with bounded wait, the drained streams).

Two POSIX `sh` scripts, each taking the binary's path and a state directory, using no tool beyond the shell's own
`if`, `case` and `$(…)`, exiting `0` only when every step read as expected and printing the number of the failing
step otherwise:

- `counter.sh` — start; snapshot and match the counter's value; `click --id counter-increment`; match the changed
  value in the answer; a `click` on an id no screen reads must exit `1`; stop; a command after stop must exit `3`.

- `flight.sh` — start; `type` an unparsable text into the filled `flight-start`; `click --id flight-book` must exit
  `1` (`disabled`); `type` a valid date; `click --id flight-book` must exit `0` and the answer must name
  `flight-booked`; stop.
The strings each script matches are read from the stand as built, at implement. `cli_flow.rs` runs each script
under `sh` with a bounded wait and a kill guard, asserts status `0`, and asserts no session answers and no state
directory remains afterwards.

- `stand_session_lifecycle.rs` — its host child calls the changed `serve`; a second ignored child serves with a
  short expiry and the parent, polling `attach` under the standing bound, reads the session gone, the directory
  removed and the child's exit `0`; one hosted `call` through the library client is accepted and one is refused.

- `stand_session_quiet.rs` — its host child calls the changed `serve`; its doc is restated to what still holds: a
  host with no sink writes nothing of the screen to its stdout, its stderr or its state directory.
- `session_common/mod.rs` — only what the two need shared.

One-shot mutation controls at implement, each restored by writing the saved bytes back and comparing sha256 before
the green reading is taken, both readings in `evidence/controls.md`: the host fielding the typed text on a log line
(turns `host_log` red); the JSON writer leaving a quote unescaped (turns step 6's unit test and `cli_commands` red);
`type` skipping the select-all (turns `stand_act_filled` red); a flow script expecting the wrong value (turns
`cli_flow` red); the idle expiry never firing (turns the lifecycle check red at its bound); the answer bound's
comparison moved by one byte (turns step 7's two bound rows red); the sentence step 1a adds to `covered`'s meaning
removed (turns its pinning test and step 6's row red). The listed entries guard the same properties on every re-run.

- The host's stderr by level under both builds: this chunk's own instrument, `evidence/by-level.py`, adapted from
  `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist/evidence/by-level.py` to the new argv. It builds the host
  alone and workspace-wide in turn and, per build and per level (unset, `info`, `debug`, `trace`), drives a
  `snapshot`, a `click` and a `type` of a sentinel and prints counts only: stderr lines by target, command-span
  lines, id needles, name needles, sentinel occurrences, stdout bytes. Recorded in `evidence/by-level.md`.

- Counts: `cargo test -p escher-driver --locked` read 29 passed on the base (run at P4, 2026-10-10); the workspace
  leg stands at 158 result lines, 719 passed, 10 ignored and `run stand` at 110 passed, 5 ignored over 30 files
  (test-plan §9 Local baseline, the 2026-10-10 reading). Predicted: 158 → 162 result lines (three new seven_guis
  targets, one new blitz-tests target) and 30 → 31 stand files — record what the re-runs measure, every difference
  attributed to a named file.

The sentence at `README.md:36` that calls the agent driver planned is restated to what is built: the command line
exists; the MCP surface, the served help and the screenshot are still to come.
- `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs` — the written JSON forms
- `packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs` — the command line's entry, its argv reader, the four endings
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs` — every command through the real binary
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_flow.rs` — the check that runs the shell flows
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/flows/` — `counter.sh` and `flight.sh`
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/host_timer.rs` — the timer host booted and moved by a hosted `advance`
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_filled.rs` — `type` replaces what a control holds
- `packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs` — `covered`'s meaning states its measured limit
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` — levels, three session rows, the name kind, the count kind, `type`'s help, the measured limit of `bounds` in two help strings
- `packages/escher-driver/src/command.rs` — `validate` refuses a session-level verb first; `validate_session`
- `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs` — `type` selects the content of a value-holding control before typing
- `packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs` — an over-long id is not recorded
- `packages/escher-driver/src/wire.rs` — version `v2`, the `call` request, its replies and bounds
- `packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs` — `serve` runs calls and expires when idle
- `packages/escher-driver/src/client.rs` — `call`; `Hello` carries the expiry
- `packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs` — the thirteenth variant
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` — the crate doc and the re-exports
- `examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs` — `main` hands argv to the command line
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/host_binary.rs` — the new argv, streams and exit codes
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs` — the typed sentinel and the command-span lines
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/common/mod.rs` — shared helpers for the process checks
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_scroll.rs` — the scrolled box's click point, pinned as measured
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_obstructed.rs` — `covered` under a scrolled-out row, pinned as measured
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_session_lifecycle.rs` — the changed `serve`, the expiry, a hosted call
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_session_quiet.rs` — the changed `serve`, its doc
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs` — what the two session checks share
- `README.md` — the sentence that lists the driver as planned

No entry is a live leg: every process a check drives is one the check itself starts and stops, so there is no
liveness probe and no `stop` key. One boot path is edited, the `escher-session` binary's `main`, and its smoke is
the standing `host_binary` check, restated; the windowed binary's `main` and the sink are unedited, so the windowed
stand is not booted. The
project has no headful self-verify harness and this chunk changes no screen. No dependency enters and no manifest
changes, which the preservation entry holds; the audit leg is therefore not listed. **Not run locally:** the MSRV
build and the windows, macos, ios and android matrix legs — the fork's CI run is their one witness, read after the
operator pass. The unix-gated checks run on the macOS job by construction; no entry counts lines in a CI log (the
route's note on such counts binds nothing here).

`evidence/type-filled.md`, `evidence/engine-findings.md` and `evidence/controls.md` have no listed producer, by
construction: the first two are step 1's readings on the base commit, which no entry can re-produce once the tree
has moved, and the third is implement's record of step 14's one-shot mutations; what each records is asserted by a
listed entry (`stand_act_filled`, the two pinned readings, the checks the mutations turn red).
`evidence/by-level.md` is implement's record of the report-only by-level entry's output. That instrument grades no
criterion: the sentinel criterion is graded by `host_log` under the two builds.

It installs no subscriber and reads no environment variable. Its argv reader `read` (`cli.rs:106-146`) applies its rules in a fixed order: no first word → usage; `serve <app> --session <dir>` in exactly that shape, else usage; a first word the verb table does not hold → the refusal `unknown-verb`; the call the remaining words spell is built without judging (`read_arguments`, `cli.rs:148-199`) and checked by `validate` or `validate_session` **before** the session address is asked for; then `--session <dir>` exactly once, else usage; `start` on an app the binary does not boot → usage.
  - **Argument spelling** — an instance-level verb's arguments are flags spelt as the schema spells them (`--id`, `--text`, `--key`, `--ms` each followed by one value, `--shift` bare); `start` takes its app as one plain word; `--session <dir>` is the command line's own option, on every command. The word after a valued flag is its value whatever it is.
  - **Four endings, and the host role's quiet end** (`Ending`, `cli.rs:201-214`; `written`, `cli.rs:225-253`): accepted — the answer on stdout, status `0`; refused — the refusal on stdout, status `1`; usage — one fixed line on stderr built from `VERBS` and the app names (`usage`, `cli.rs:256-279`), stdout empty, status `2`; session error — the error object on stdout and its fixed message on stderr, status `3`; and `Served` — the host role ended after a stop or an expiry: nothing written, status `0`. No ending writes back anything the caller typed. A write to a closed pipe is dropped, not a panic (`write`, `cli.rs:281-294`).
  - **`start` spawns a process** (`cli.rs:326-340`): the running binary again (`std::env::current_exe()`), as `serve <app> --session <dir>`, stdin, stdout and stderr closed; it waits up to 30 s for the host to answer and drops the handle — the host is neither killed nor reaped by the command.
  - **The wire carries a call** (`wire.rs`): version `v2` for every request; a third request `call v2 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` beside `hello` and `stop`, kinds `t` text · `n` whole number · `f` flag; verb, names and text values percent-escaped byte for byte (`escape`, `wire.rs:82-93`; `unescape`, `wire.rs:95-115`, strict: uppercase hex only, no escape of a byte that needs none, the decoded bytes UTF-8, a number in its one spelling); replies `ok v2 accepted <json>` · `ok v2 refused <json>` · `ok v2 oversize`; `hello`'s reply gains `idle_expiry_s`. Bounds (added ranges `wire.rs:17-18`, `20-26`, `29-31`, `33-39`): a request line 16,384 bytes (was 64); a lifecycle reply 128 bytes (kept — the widest `hello` measures 122, was 87); an answer 1,048,576 bytes, on the JSON line alone; a call's answer is read under 30 s per read (`ANSWER_BOUND`), every other read and write under 2 s as before. `frame` (`wire.rs:216-226`) is the one function that turns an answer into its reply.
  - **The host runs calls and expires** — `pub fn serve(state_dir, session, idle_expiry)` gained its third parameter (signature change); `pub const IDLE_EXPIRY` = 1,800 s (added range `host.rs:9-14`). A `call` request is decoded and run through `Session::run` and nothing else. The accept loop is non-blocking, polled every 25 ms; with no request answered for the expiry the host ends exactly as on `stop`. Every answered request — a refused or malformed one included — counts toward `served` and restarts the expiry; a connection that breaks before its request is whole does neither. **Remaining callers of `serve`:** `command_line` (`cli.rs`, the host role), `session_host` and `session_host_with_a_short_expiry` (`stand_session_lifecycle.rs:242-243`, `:251-252`), `session_host_with_typed_text` (`stand_session_quiet.rs:113-114`); the stand's `main` no longer calls it directly.
  - **The client sends one** — `pub fn call(state_dir, &Call) -> Result<Answer, SessionError>` (`client.rs:68-90`) and `pub struct Answer { accepted, json }`. It runs `validate` first: a call the schema refuses is answered there with its refusal and reaches no session, so every call sent fits the request bound. `Hello` gained `idle_expiry_s` (a public struct grew a field). `read_answer` (`client.rs:92-107`) maps an `oversize` reply to the thirteenth error.
  - **Two levels of verb** — `pub enum Level { Instance, Session }` (`schema.rs:141-148`), `VerbSpec.level`; `VERBS` is nine rows (`schema.rs:382-386`): the six instance-level verbs in their order, then `start` (`schema.rs:348-359`, one required argument `app` of the new kind `ArgKind::Name` — 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`), `status` (`schema.rs:361-367`) and `stop` (`schema.rs:369-380`). New `FieldKind::Count`; new result fields `label`, `pid`, `served`, `idle_expiry_s`, `stopped`. `validate` refuses a session-level verb as `unknown-verb` before its arguments are read; `pub fn validate_session` (`command.rs:224-241`) and `pub enum SessionCommand` (`command.rs:154-167`) are the session-level check. A session-level verb handed to `Session::run` in process is `unknown-verb`, and its span still records the verb's table word.

data.head: ## Graph impact (from the code-graph query; plane `rust`)

body: - **serve** — 3 call sites outside the crate: `main @ examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:49`, `session_host @ tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_session_lifecycle.rs:103`, `session_host_with_typed_text @ tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_session_quiet.rs:101`. A changed signature or a `serve` that now runs calls reaches all three; the two test hosts are in-process `Session`s with no sink.

- **start · attach · stop** (the client's) — `the_binary_serves_and_stops @ examples/seven_guis/tests/host_binary.rs:37`/`:42`/`:46`, `the_host_logs_no_id_and_no_name_at_trace @ examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs:91`/`:105`, `start_attach_stop_and_each_edge @ tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_session_lifecycle.rs` (13 sites, `:44-93`), `nothing_of_the_screen_leaves_the_session_process @ tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_session_quiet.rs:49`/`:52`/`:65`. Additive client functions leave them untouched. The name `start` also resolves `Session::start` (`session.rs:95`), whose callers are the in-process checks.

- **run** (`Session::run`) — 12 call sites, every one under `tests/blitz-tests/tests/` (`session_common/mod.rs:151`, `:194`; `stand_act_{diff,ids,refused,spans,timer}.rs`); none in `examples/` or in the host: no code path outside a test runs a driver command today.
- **validate** — called from `execute @ packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:120` and the crate's own unit tests only.

- **crate edges** — inbound to `escher-driver`: `seven_guis`, `blitz-tests`; outbound: `dioxus-native-dom`, `blitz-dom`, `blitz-test-harness`, `blitz-traits` (usage-based; the manifest names three). No `packages/` crate names `seven_guis`.
- **Names free** — `json`, `cli`, `to_json`, `command_line`: 0 symbols (probe: `Request`, `Reply`, `SeenIds` found on the same query, so the plane built).

- **The crossing does not exist, and the built wire cannot hold one** (`host.rs:48`; `wire.rs:16`, `:20`, `:25-28`): the host is handed the label only; a request is two words in at most 64 bytes while an `id` argument admits 1024 bytes and `text` 4096 (`schema.rs:5`, `:8`), and a snapshot's text has a 10,000-byte ceiling that is compared, not enforced. Any form on this socket states a new version, new request and reply bounds and a way to carry arbitrary text (an id holds `/`, `:`, `[`, `]`; typed text holds spaces and line breaks) — research's answer to the extracts' "can the wire be extended": yes, at the one bind site, by a second request class beside `hello` and `stop`.

- **A hosted command meets the client's 2 s read bound** (`wire.rs:13`; `client.rs:165-173`): the reply to a command is read under the lifecycle's `IO_BOUND`. On the stand a command returns in milliseconds, but the bound is a wall-clock limit on the answer, so the plan states the bound a command's reply is read under and what a client that hits it exits with.

- **The schema already states the JSON's keys** (`schema.rs:33-35`, `:147-210`): each verb's result fields and each node's nine fields are named, kinded and helped in the one table. A JSON answer keyed by those names adds no vocabulary; a JSON form that names anything else is a second statement. `snapshot`'s one result field is `text` — "the screen as one text" — so a string field is what the table says today, and a JSON view of the tree would be a new field kind in it.

- **A refusal's JSON is a walk over fixed strings** (`refusal.rs:43-105`, `:119-130`, `:168-175`): cause name, meaning, remedy, and for `malformed` the fault with the schema's own argument name. Nothing of the call can enter it.

- **Three endings exist in the types** (`execute.rs:15-16`, `:108`; `error.rs:12-37`): `Ok(Outcome)` with `settled` true or false, `Err(Refusal)`, and a `SessionError` at the lifecycle. A command line adds a fourth, usage. The host's standing statuses are `0` · `1` · `2` (`session_host.rs:31`, `:51-56`); the repository's scripts use `0` · `1` · `2` · `3` (agent-run, cold-agent).

- **Typing into a filled control lands inside the value** — by code read, not measured: `type` clicks the centre of the control then types (`execute.rs:133-139`), a single click in a text input moves the caret to the click point (`pointer.rs:516-534`), and `type_text` presses one character key per `char` at the caret (`input.rs:222-226`). The Flight Booker's two date inputs are filled at boot (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/flight_booker.rs:84`, `:92`). What the value reads after a `type` there is unmeasured; the plan's first check measures it in process, in both layout modes.

- **A scrolled box's bounds shift by its own offset in both engine bodies** (`document.rs:2262-2267`; `writing_mode.rs:382-388`): the walk subtracts the node's own scroll offset, so the reading holds whichever body a build compiles. The driver derives its click point and its `off-screen` reading from those bounds (`execute.rs:259-266`, `:312-320`), so the freight's hypothesis follows from the code; it is still not measured.

- **The two builds differ in engine features** — re-derived: `cargo tree --workspace --locked -e features -i blitz-dom` names 16 distinct `blitz-dom feature "…"` (with `tracing` and `writing-mode`); `cargo tree -p seven_guis --locked -e features -i blitz-dom` names 5 (`accessibility`, `accesskit`, `custom-widget`, `system-fonts`, `woff`; neither `tracing` nor `writing-mode`). Counted with `grep -o -E 'blitz-dom feature "[a-z_-]+"' | sort -u` on each output; a first, line-anchored pattern read 0 on both and was discarded. The `escher-session` binary's stderr by level under the workspace build stays unmeasured.

- **A check reaches a real binary only as its own package's** (`host_binary.rs:15`, `host_log.rs:11`): `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*` names the binaries of the package under test. A command line carried by the stand's own binary is reachable by the stand's tests with what exists; a client binary in another package is not reachable from a seven_guis test, and a test in that package cannot name the stand's host (no `packages/` manifest names an example).

- **The host reads one layout mode** (`session_host.rs:39`, `:43`): `stand::options(true)`. `stand_snapshot_text` already holds each screen's text equal across the two modes in process, so a one-mode host proof can be held against either.

- **Shell alone can branch and match** — `sh` is the one interpreter a flow needs: a command's exit status drives `if`, and `case "$out" in *'…'*)` matches a substring of stdout with no `grep`, `jq` or `sed`. Whether the JSON is one line matters to that: a single-line answer is matchable and survives `$(…)` unchanged.
- **Closed argv, usage on stderr, exit 2 before anything runs** (`session_host.rs:24-32`; `host_binary.rs:83-102`).
- **Fixed-text errors with no path, label, id or value** (`error.rs:10`, `:76-101`); a JSON or stderr form of one renders the fixed text.
- **Tables stated in their unit test with the row count asserted; an assertion names a row index only** (`schema.rs:297-470`, `command.rs:243-594`).

- **Process checks**: `cfg(unix)`, own host started and stopped, every wait bounded, kill-and-reap guard, both streams drained from the spawn, failure prints kinds and counts (`host_log.rs:13-23`, `:125-158`; `tests/common/mod.rs:22-32`).
- **No panic path on what a call supplies** (`command.rs:159-241`): argv decoding and wire decoding are new input paths under the same rule; a panic message would reach stderr past the scrub.
- **Sink first in `main`, stderr only** (`session_host.rs:20-22`).

**Working entry (verbatim):** Driver CLI — every command with uncoloured JSON on stdout, diagnostics on stderr, accepted/refused exit codes, shell-scriptable stand flow (v010-12)

**Epoch:** Epoch 5 — Agent surfaces (its first markerless entry) · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Freight on the entry:** twelve `CARRY:` blocks and one `WATCH:` (13 blocks, 437 to 1891 characters; `route.py pins`, trail in the run dir: 43 freight blocks on the markerless tail, 13 of them on line 73). No `BLOCKED-ON`, no `PREREQ`. Each block is folded below under "The carried freight". One external input: the operator's directive given with the take-up (`inputs#I1`), which says who decides which fork; every other fact below is read from this repository or the route.

**Premise closure (P3):** every bullet tagged `[inferred]` at the take-up — one the working entry did not state, or a mechanism claim that arrived in the freight — was re-read against `research.md`: eleven verified and their tags dropped, none corrected. What was verified by reading code and is still not measured at run time says so in its bullet. A bullet with no tag is what the entry states or is verified.

The first surface of the driver: **a command an agent runs**. intent §7 states the gap and the expectation — "the headless harness is a Rust API in a test-only crate (`publish = false`) — no command an agent runs" → "every driver command runs from a CLI with JSON output and an exit code that means accepted or refused; a stand flow is scriptable in shell alone" (`escher-0.1.0/intent.md:60-63`). Everything a command needs is built and runs in process today: the session, settle, the verb table and its validation, the executor, refusal detection and the command span (`packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs:1-48`). No binary reaches any of it but the host `escher-session`, whose argv is `<task> <state-dir>` and which only serves (`examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:24-49`).

The founder's purpose for this surface, as the operator relayed it with the take-up (`inputs#I1`): "the CLI is the first surface an agent meets, and the founder stated the purpose again on 2026-10-09 — an agent sees, drives and verifies a UI and learns the tool from the tool."

- **Every command runs from the command line** — the six verbs of the one table (`snapshot` · `click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll`, `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:290`) and the commands of a session's life (bringing one up, reaching it, stopping it — today the library functions `start` · `attach` · `stop`, `packages/escher-driver/src/client.rs:37-64`).

- **Uncoloured JSON on stdout** — every command's answer is JSON on stdout and nothing else is written there: an accepted command's result (the screen for `snapshot`; for an acting verb whether the instance went quiet and the diff of the screen before and after, `scroll` adding whether its target is in view), a refused command's refusal (its cause and the cause's fixed remedy), a lifecycle command's answer. No colour, no escape sequence, in a terminal or out of one.

- **Diagnostics on stderr** — what is not a command's answer goes to stderr: usage, an error of the tool itself, the telemetry sink's lines (escher binaries install `escher_telemetry::init`, stderr only — CLAUDE.md §Critical Warnings).
- **An exit code that tells accepted from refused** — a script branches on the process status alone, without reading stdout.

- **A stand flow is scriptable in shell alone** — a shell script, with no other tooling, starts a session on a stand task, reads its screen, acts on ids the screen lists, checks what came back and stops the session; it is run as a check and passes (v010-12's acceptance: "a stand flow completes as a shell script with no other tooling").

- **A call reaches a held instance from another process** — verified at P3: `serve` takes the `Session` and hands its loop the label alone (`packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:48`), no code outside a test calls `Session::run` (12 call sites, all under `tests/blitz-tests/tests/` — research.md §Graph impact), and the built wire cannot hold a call: a request is two words in at most 64 bytes and a reply at most 128, read under a 2 s bound (`packages/escher-driver/src/wire.rs:13-20`, `:65-68`), while an `id` admits 1024 bytes and `text` 4096 (`packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:5`, `:8`) — a command-line process ends when its command returns, and a session is one instance held across commands, so the instance lives in a host process and each command's call and outcome cross between the two. Today "nothing of the schema, of a call or of an outcome crosses the socket: they are passed and returned as values" (`packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs:32-33`); the wire is `hello` and `stop` (`lib.rs:13-16`). Carrying a call in and an outcome out puts element ids, accessible names, control values, typed text and the snapshot's text on a process boundary for the first time. That is the playbook's "Boundary widening" (`.andromeda/playbook.md:36-37`, verdict `escalate`): the widening is asked, never leaned (decision 1 below). How it crosses — the session socket's grammar grows, or another form — is the plan's, from research.

- **JSON is produced from the one schema's data** — verified at P3, and the table already names every key an answer needs: each verb's result fields (`text`; `settled` · `busy` · `added` · `removed` · `changed`, with `advanced_ms` and `in_view`) and a node's nine fields (`NODE_FIELDS`), each with its kind and help (`packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:33-35`, `:147-210`); `serde` is a workspace dependency and `serde_json` is not, though the lock holds it for other packages (research.md §Files inspected) — the schema is `'static` Rust data and `escher-driver` depends on no serialization crate (`packages/escher-driver/Cargo.toml:13-16`: `blitz-test-harness`, `dioxus-native-dom`, `tracing`); an `Outcome`, a `Refusal`, a `SessionError` and a lifecycle answer each need a JSON form, and a call needs a form in which it arrives from argv. How (written by hand, or a dependency) is the plan's; a new workspace crate or dependency is registered, never silent (CLAUDE.md §Critical Warnings).

- **The cases that are neither accepted nor refused** — verified at P3 (`SessionError` has 12 variants, `packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs:12-37`; `Session::run` returns a not-quiet step as an `Outcome`, `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:15-16`; the host exits `0` · `1` · `2` today, `examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:31`, `:51-56`) — a command line has more endings than the entry's two: a session edge (`SessionError` — no session, a dead one, a timeout, an unsupported platform), a usage error, a client that waited past its bound for an answer (a command's reply is read under the lifecycle's 2 s bound as built, `packages/escher-driver/src/client.rs:165-173`), and an accepted acting verb whose instance did not go quiet (`NotSettled` naming the busy class — an outcome, not a refusal). What each exits with and what it prints is part of decision 4.

- **v010-04's command leg** — "one snapshot command returns each stand task's screen as a tree where every node carries id, role, name, state and bounds, and the whole result fits in a single tool result": the tree, its text form and its 10,000-byte budget are built and proven in process (`Snapshot::to_text`, `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET`, `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs:16`, `:36`; `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_text.rs`); the command is this chunk's (CARRY 2).

- **Two proofs the first hosted command owes** — a typed sentinel read absent from the host's stderr at `RUST_LOG=trace` (CARRYs 5 and 11), and a standing check that boots the timer host and moves its time by `advance` (CARRY 6).
- **The claim** — the entry names v010-12; CARRY 2 names v010-04. Whether each becomes fully verifiable here is read at P4 from the matrix; none is assumed.

The freight says of several things that they are "decided at this entry's promotion"; the entry's own words leave others open. Who decides is `inputs#I1`: "A fork that shapes what the agent meets (command and argument names, the shape of stdout, exit codes, how a session is started and addressed) is the founder decision: put it as a dialog with every option whole. He is away now; if a dialog expires, end your turn and wait for his words as text. Technical forks are mine." Each is asked at P4, after research has made its options whole; none is leaned here.

1. **The crossing** — a call and its outcome crossing the process boundary, and with them ids, names, values, typed text and the snapshot's text leaving the process on stdout (CARRYs 2 and 4; `.claude/rules/security.md` §Surfaces: "the first command that carries one is a new crossing question"). A boundary widening: the founder's.

2. **How a session is started and addressed** — what an agent types to bring a session up on an app, how a later command names that session (today a state directory the caller names), and what stops it. The founder's (`inputs#I1`).

3. **Command and argument names** — the verbs' spelling on the command line, how an argument is passed (the table's argument names are `id` · `text` · `key` · `shift` · `ms`), the lifecycle commands' names, and their place in the one verb table (CARRY 4). The founder's.

4. **The shape of stdout and the exit codes** — the JSON of an outcome, a refusal and an error; how the snapshot is carried — its text as a string field, or a JSON view of the same model (CARRY 2); which exit code means what, the cases of the bullet above included. The founder's.

5. **An orphaned session host** — a host whose client died without `stop` runs on; "an idle expiry, or a list-and-stop command" (CARRY 3). The freight names the operator; an answer that adds a command the agent meets is the founder's by `inputs#I1`.
6. **Whether a command exposes the actionable-key check** — `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable()` (CARRY 1); if one does, its output is a second crossing for ids.
7. **What `type` does to text already in a control** (CARRY 7) — measured first, then decided.
8. **A bound on the session's record of ids** (CARRY 10) — a byte bound, or an id past `MAX_ID_BYTES` left unrecorded. Technical: the operator's.

9. **The two engine findings whose output now leaves the process** (CARRYs 8 and 9) — each fix "changes … every document" and is "the founder's word"; this chunk measures the hypotheses they carry and asks what ships.

data.head: ## The carried freight (twelve CARRYs, one WATCH)

body: Each is folded as a hypothesis: the artifacts it names were re-read at the take-up (found unless said otherwise), and a mechanism it states keeps its own marker.

1. **The actionable-key check has no wire form** (from 2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits). `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable()` is public and exposed by no command (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/actionable.rs:55`); "the founder named the later CLI and driver as its reusers (2026-10-06, at that chunk's plan review); whether a command exposes it is decided at this entry's promotion; if one does, its output is a new crossing for stable ids, escalated to the operator then (security-plan §Input Validation, the `id` row), and it must leave `UnkeyedActionable.node` behind — a process-local `NodeId`" (`actionable.rs:16-18`). Decision 6.

2. **v010-04's command leg** (from 2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization). "this entry's snapshot command proves the cap with those two; it is also where the text first leaves the process — a new crossing for ids, accessible names and a text control's value, asked of the operator at this entry's promotion (the returned-value-only answer covered that chunk only — ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07; security-plan §Input Validation) — and where it is decided how the JSON stdout carries the text (a string field, or a JSON view of the same model)". The matrix's two notes on v010-04 say the same (`matrix.py show --id v010-04`). Decisions 1 and 4.

3. **An orphaned session host** (from 2026-10-07-driver-session). "a host whose client died without `stop` keeps running: a session has no idle expiry; this entry answers it at its promotion — an idle expiry, or a list-and-stop command — and the answer is the operator's (architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session; security-plan §API Security, the local session socket row)". `Started`'s own doc agrees: "dropping it neither stops nor reaps the host" (`client.rs:23-24`). Decision 5.

4. **One verb table** (from 2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema). "this entry adds its own commands to that table at its promotion — the lifecycle commands and, if it is exposed, the actionable-key check — and states no second table. The schema is `'static` Rust data with no serialization crate: producing JSON from it, and from a `Refusal`, is this entry's step, and the first command that reaches `validate` from outside the process is its own crossing question (security-plan §Input Validation, the Driver command schema row)". Re-read: `VERBS` holds six rows (`schema.rs:290`), `validate` takes a `Call` and no `Session` (`packages/escher-driver/src/command.rs:167`). Binding: no second table; decisions 1 and 3.

5. **Typed text in a sink-installing host's log** (from 2026-10-07-driver-session, moved on by 2026-10-07-act-by-id; the founder's ruling, 2026-10-07 — "the sink fix is proven with a typed sentinel once a command can type"). "this entry is the first whose command reaches the `escher-session` binary's own instance: when its `type` does, prove a typed sentinel occurs 0 times in that binary's stderr at `RUST_LOG=trace`; the standing check to extend is seven_guis' `host_log`" (`examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs`, which boots `crud`, `:77`). Owed here as soon as a hosted `type` exists.

6. **The timer host has no standing boot** (from 2026-10-07-act-by-id). `escher-session timer` is the one host branch whose session carries a time step (`session_host.rs:36-48`; `stand::timer_step`, `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:92`; `Session::with_time`, `packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:116`); `host_binary` boots `counter` (`examples/seven_guis/tests/host_binary.rs:30`) and `host_log` `crud`; "the first command that reaches the host's instance can move its time by `advance` — boot the timer host in a standing check there". Owed here.

7. **What `type` does to text already in a control** (from 2026-10-07-act-by-id; left undecided by its plan). Verified at P3 by reading the code, not by a run: `type` clicks the centre of the control and then types (`packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:133-139`), a single click in a text input moves the caret to the click point (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:516-534`), and typing presses one character key per character at the caret (`packages/blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs:222-226`); the two date inputs are filled at boot (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/flight_booker.rs:84`, `:92`). What the value reads after a `type` there is still unmeasured: the plan's first check measures it. The freight's words: "`type` focuses by a click at the centre of the control and then types, so in a text input that already holds text the caret lands where the click falls (hypothesis: the typed text is then inserted inside the old value — not measured; that chunk's checks type into empty inputs only); the stand's Flight Booker dates are pre-filled, so a shell-scripted flow that changes a date meets this first; the key list holds `home`, `end`, `backspace` and `delete`, and no verb clears a control" (the four keys: `schema.rs:18-26`). Measured at P3 or by the plan's first step; decision 7.

8. **A scrolled box's own bounds read shifted** (from 2026-10-07-refusal-detection; the wrap's placement, "on the first entry whose output carries bounds and a diff out of the process"). Spot-checked at P3: both bodies of the reader start their walk at the node itself and subtract its own scroll offset (`packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:2262-2267`; `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/writing_mode.rs:382-388`), so the shift holds in either build; the driver takes its click point and its `off-screen` reading from those bounds (`packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:259-266`, `:312-320`), so the hypothesis follows from the code and is still not measured. The freight's words: "a snapshot node's `bounds` is `BaseDocument::get_client_bounding_rect`, and for a box that is itself scrolled it reads shifted by the box's own scroll offset while the box has not moved: on the stand `crud-list` read y 112.796875 before a driver `scroll` and 94.796875 after it, and that step's diff names the list among its changed nodes (measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-refusal-detection/evidence/stand-census.md)"; "hypothesis: a driver `click` naming such a box lands off its centre by that offset, and its `off-screen` reading is made at the shifted point (not measured)"; "the fix lies in upstream-owned merge surface and changes a client bounding rect for every document — the founder's word — and the defect is upstreamable". Coordinates re-read: `get_client_bounding_rect` at `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:2273`, `physical_unrounded_geometry` at `document.rs:2257` and `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/writing_mode.rs:375`. Decision 9.

9. **The hit walk reaches a row scrolled out of its box** (same origin and placement). Spot-checked at P3: the walk's scroll-offset arithmetic stands (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:1387-1409`) and the driver's `covered` reading is a hit (`packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:324-337`); the hypothesis is still not measured. The freight's words: "the engine's hit passes a point outside a scrolling box to that box's scrolled-out children: on the stand, with the viewport unscrolled, the raw hit at the centre of a CRUD row lying below its list's box answers that row (measured at …/evidence/stand-census.md; the walk read at packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:1385-1418)"; "hypothesis: a control that sits where a scrolled-out row extends reads `covered`, and a pointer click there lands on the hidden row (not measured — the census clicked no control under a clipped row); clipping the walk at a scrolling box changes every pointer event of every document, so it is the founder's word, and the file is upstream-owned merge surface". The walk's scroll-offset arithmetic still stands at `node.rs:1387-1409`. Decision 9.

10. **The session's record has no bound on an id's length** (same origin and placement). Verified at P3 by reading the code: `SeenIds::record` stores the id whole with no length check, and its bound counts entries (`packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:48-65`). The freight's words: "at most `MAX_SEEN_IDS` 4096 ids, as text, for the session's life (packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:24-70); the bound counts ids, and the ids are the app's own, which `validate` never sees — one longer than `MAX_ID_BYTES` can be named by no call and is still recorded whole, so nothing bounds the record in bytes (read from the code, not measured; no test exercises it …); a byte bound, or leaving an id past `MAX_ID_BYTES` unrecorded, is decided at this entry's promotion (security-plan §Input Validation, the `id` row)". Re-read: `MAX_SEEN_IDS` at `session.rs:25`, `MAX_ID_BYTES = 1024` at `schema.rs:5`. Decision 8; it matters here because this is the first entry whose commands reach a hosted, long-lived session.

11. **The workspace build compiles the engine's `tracing` call sites in** (from 2026-10-07-driver-command-spans; the wrap's placement, "on the entry that owes the typed-text proof in a host's log"). Re-derived at P3 from cargo's feature graph: the workspace resolves blitz-dom with 16 features, `tracing` and `writing-mode` among them, and a `-p seven_guis` build with 5, neither among them (research.md §Patterns detected, with the two commands); the host's stderr by level under the workspace build is still not measured. The freight's words: "`cargo test --workspace` (CI's test leg, `ci-leg.sh fast`) resolves the whole workspace, where blitz's default `tracing` feature turns `blitz-dom/tracing` on through blitz-shell and blitz-html, while `cargo test -p blitz-tests` and a `-p seven_guis` build leave it off (measured at …/evidence/feature-unification.md)"; "not measured: the `escher-session` binary's stderr by level as the workspace build makes it"; "this entry's typed-sentinel proof … runs in that leg, so it reads a host built with the engine's call sites compiled in — hypothesis: that host prints engine lines at `trace`, scrubbed to their safe fields (not measured), and the sentinel has to be read absent from those lines too". Binding: CARRY 5's proof is read in the workspace leg's build as well as per package, and counts nothing by line where the two builds differ.

12. **A count over a fork CI log** (from 2026-10-10-upstream-sync-agent-surfaces). "a plan entry here that counts cargo lines in a CI log uses a pattern proven on a known positive from such a log (.claude/docs/session-learnings.md, the 2026-10-07 entry on reading a fork CI run, extended 2026-10-10)" — the earlier pattern "read 0 at exit 1 on a green 16/16 run whose log held the lines" (`escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-upstream-sync-agent-surfaces/evidence/ci.md`). Binding on the plan's operator entries.

- watch: a fork CI job hanging in its package-install step (1/3; since 2026-10-09-audit-corrections-agent-surfaces) — the install is bounded (`.github/scripts/apt-install.sh`: 3 attempts, 120 s per call; the job step `timeout-minutes: 10`) and no run has shown a bound fire; a recurrence is a job held in an install step past its bound, or a run red on the script's exit 1; a line `apt-install: attempt … failed in …` under a green run is the bound seen firing — recorded when seen. Retires at a recurrence or 3 green runs.
- **Not the MCP surface** (working-route.md:75) — no MCP tool, server or stdio protocol; what this chunk decides about names and shapes is what that entry mirrors.

- **Not Self-description** (working-route.md:77) — "verb list, help and schemas served by CLI and MCP from the one schema (v010-14)" is that entry's. Verified at P3: every verb, argument and result field already carries a help string as data (`packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:86`, `:131`, `:140`), served by nothing. What this chunk's commands say on a wrong call (a usage line on stderr, a refusal with its remedy) is this chunk's; where the line falls between that and served help is asked if it forks, given the founder's "learns the tool from the tool" (`inputs#I1`).
- **Not the screenshot** (working-route.md:79) and **not the cold-agent test** (working-route.md:96).

- **Unix only where a session crosses processes** — the socket is unix-only and `serve` · `start` · `attach` · `stop` return `Unsupported` elsewhere (`lib.rs:18-19`); a CLI over a hosted session inherits that.

- **No network port, no second listener** — the one listener is the session's Unix-domain socket in an owner-only state directory (CLAUDE.md §Critical Warnings); what crosses it is decision 1, and a new listener, env var or workspace crate is an arch §Occupied Resources registration first.

- **stdout is the answer, never a log** — ids, names, values and typed text may be in a command's JSON once decision 1 is given; none enters a log line, a span field, a test name or an assertion message (`.claude/rules/security.md` §Surfaces), and the command span stays eight fixed fields.

- **No upstream-owned engine file is edited without the founder's word** (CARRYs 8 and 9; the merge surface is a CARRY on working-route.md:82).

- **No sleep in any check; a pipeline check runs `for incremental in [false, true]`** (`.claude/rules/testing.md`). Verified at P3: the host boots its task with `stand::options(true)` (`session_host.rs:39`, `:43`; `stand.rs:58-69`), so a flow through the host binary reads one layout mode; `stand_snapshot_text` already holds each screen's text equal across the two modes in process. Whether the CLI's proof needs both is the plan's.

- **Code** — verified at P3 against the graph's caller sets (the full lists are research.md's): `packages/escher-driver/src/` (`wire` · `host` · `client` for the crossing, `schema` · `command` for the lifecycle commands in the one table, `execute` · `refusal` · `error` for JSON forms, `session` for decision 8, `lib` for the crate doc); a CLI binary and its manifest (where it lives is the plan's); `examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs` and `examples/seven_guis/tests/host_{binary,log}.rs`; a shell script for the stand flow and the check that runs it; `tests/blitz-tests/tests/` for what is proven in process; `Cargo.toml` · `Cargo.lock` if a crate or a dependency is added; `.github/scripts/` if the flow becomes part of a leg.

- **architecture** — §Standard Contracts (Driver session), §Occupied Resources (the socket's wire, names, any new crate or binary), §Existing Scopes, §Cross-cutting Patterns where the crossing is stated.

- **security-plan** — §Threat Model Summary (the local IPC vector), §Input Validation (the socket row, the `id` row, the Driver command schema row), §API Security (the local session socket row), §Error Handling.
- **test-plan** — §1 · §3 · §4 (the new checks, the session-lifecycle keyed contract), §9 (engine features by runner — CARRY 11).
- **obs-plan** — §2 · §4 · §8 (a host that runs commands: what its stderr carries, the typed-text measurement).
- **a11y-plan** — only if the actionable-key check is exposed (decision 6); **layout-templates · design-system** — no markup, style or token is touched; none expected.
Read from `Turbolet85/escher` by full sha (`ci.py conclusion`, trail in the run dir). The last commit that flipped a master record is HEAD itself, so one sha.

- `0493d26a82fb` (HEAD, the last wrap's flip, `chore(2026-10-10-upstream-sync-agent-surfaces)`) — **in progress: verdict not yet available.** CI#38018235072; at the read (2026-10-10T02:51Z) 4 of 4 created checks were read and `Test [default features]` had been running 212 s; no wall-clock yet. Not folded and not read as green; it lands here as read, unresolved. `git diff --stat 9462a7e4 0493d26a` over `packages`, `tests`, `examples`, `scripts`, `.github`, `apps`, `wpt` and the root manifests is empty, so the source this run reads is the source CI#38013740580 read green 16/16 on `9462a7e4` (the handoff's reading, not re-read here).

- Re-read at P4 (2026-10-10, the same call form, trail in the run dir): `0493d26a82fb` **verdict: green · checks 16/16 · wall 857 s** — CI#38018235072 completed/success. The row above is resolved: no red and no `not green` is carried into this chunk.

The nine decisions of "Decisions owed at this take-up" are given. The founder answered by question dialog in the overseer session on 2026-10-10, his chosen labels relayed by the overseer (`inputs#I3`); the operator answered the three technical forks through this session's dialog the same day (`inputs#I2`).

1. **The crossing — ratified by the founder: the socket carries commands.** The one registered socket gains a third request beside `hello` and `stop`; access stays the `0700` directory and the `0600` socket; a request up to 16 KiB, an answer up to 1 MiB, a 30 s read bound for an answer; ids, names, values (a password's and a file input's masked), typed text, the snapshot's text and the diff cross it and reach stdout; none enters a log line or a span field, and no `NodeId` crosses.

2. **App binary, path address.** The library carries the whole command line; the stand's binary `escher-session` hosts and drives; a session is the directory named with `--session` on every command. `start` · `status` · `stop` are the session's commands and `serve` the host role — his answer renamed none.
3. **Idle expiry**, 30 minutes with no request, each answered request restarting it; `start`'s answer states it.
4. **Named flags, the schema's own words** (`--id`, `--text`, `--key`, `--shift`, `--ms`).
5. **The snapshot's text as one string field**; every answer one line of JSON keyed by the schema's result fields.

own child and speaks MCP with it over the child's stdin and stdout, newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0, in the handshake

credential, so it is local to the invoking user. The server holds the app in its own process. All nine verbs of the
one table are tools: `start <app>` boots the app inside the server through the boot the binary hands over, and
`status` and `stop` act on that held session. Each `tools/call` leaves one `tool_call` span under `escher_driver`.
The driver's existing `command` span is its child by plain nesting, so the entry's "tool call parents its trace"
holds with no change to the executor.

A tool result is the driver's existing written form, except one case. A `snapshot` result's text block is

refusal and a session error carry `isError: true` (`inputs#I2`). Requests are read with `serde_json` as a reader only;
answers stay written by the crate's hand writer (`inputs#I3`, fork 2A). This crossing was ratified by the founder as
stated (`inputs#I3`, fork 1A): ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the mask),
the snapshot text and the diff out; an id and typed text in; the request's `id` echoed back within its bound.

v010-13 is claimed and proved three ways. A scripted MCP session completes a Counter flow by tool calls alone, both
in process in both layout modes and through the binary as a child process. One small live agent session on the dev
host, whose only tools are this server's, does the same in the operator pass (`inputs#I3`, fork 3A). Per

· §6 · §9.

1. **Measure first (evidence/controls.md, no source change).** Read and record, before any code moves:

   - No `[features]` table is added and no other manifest changes. `Cargo.lock` gains exactly one line,
     `"serde_json",` in `escher-driver`'s dependency list, and no package.
   - `serde_json` is used for reading only: no `to_string` or `to_writer` call and no derive anywhere in the crate.
     Answers stay written by `json.rs`.

3. **Make the hand writer reachable from a sibling module.** In `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs`, make `string`
   and `Object` (with its `new` · `text` · `flag` · `count` · `json` · `end`) `pub(crate)`. No behaviour changes; its
   seven unit tests stay as they are.

4. **A boot that can be called more than once.** In `packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs`:
   - Change `command_line`'s `boot` bound from `impl FnOnce(&str) -> Result<Session, SessionError>` to
     `impl FnMut(&str) -> Result<Session, SessionError>`, and `run`'s with it.
   - The one caller, `main` at `examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:24`, compiles unchanged: its closure builds
     every value it holds inside its own body.
   - The inline tests' three `run` call sites (`cli.rs:718`, `:721`, `:730`) pass closures that already satisfy the
     wider bound.

5. **The MCP server — new module `packages/escher-driver/src/mcp.rs`.** It opens with a `//!` doc and exposes one
   public function, re-exported at the crate root:

```
   serve_mcp(input: impl BufRead, output: impl Write, apps: &[&str],
             boot: impl FnMut(&str) -> Result<Session, SessionError>, idle_expiry: Duration)
             -> Result<(), SessionError>
   ```

It answers requests until the input ends (`Ok(())`); a failed read or write is `SessionError::Io`. It installs no
   subscriber, reads no environment variable and writes nothing but protocol lines to `output`.

- **The line reader.** Reads one request line of at most `MAX_MCP_REQUEST_BYTES` = 65,536 bytes, terminator not
     counted, from the one `BufRead` it holds for its whole life, never a fresh buffer per line. Read-ahead bytes must
     survive; `wire::read_line` builds a fresh buffer per call and is not reused (`wire.rs:287-289`).
     - A longer line is read to its terminator and dropped, and answered `-32700`.
     - An empty line is skipped.
     - A line that is not UTF-8 or not JSON (`serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>`) is answered `-32700`.
   - **The envelope.**
     - A JSON value that is not an object with `jsonrpc: "2.0"` and a string `method` is answered `-32600`.
     - A request with no `id` member is a notification and gets no reply, whatever its method.
     - An `id` that is not an integer (i64) and not a string of at most 128 bytes is answered `-32600` with `id: null`.
       Otherwise the reply echoes the `id`: an integer written back as an integer, a string through `json::string`.
       This echo is the one thing a client sent that is written back (`inputs#I3`, fork 1A).
   - **Methods.**
     - `initialize` answers `protocolVersion` with the client's requested version when it is one of `2025-06-18` ·
       `2025-03-26` · `2024-11-05`, and `2025-06-18` otherwise. It also answers `capabilities: {"tools": {}}` and
       `serverInfo: {"name": "escher", "version": <escher-driver's CARGO_PKG_VERSION>}`. Nothing the client sent in
       its `initialize` (its capabilities, its name or version) is read further, kept or written anywhere.
     - `ping` answers `{}`.
     - `tools/list` answers the nine tools (below), with no `nextCursor`.
     - `tools/call` (below).
     - Every other method is answered `-32601`. That includes `server/discover`, which tells a client of the current
       revision that this server speaks the handshake revisions.
     - Requests before `initialize` are served as after it; the handshake is not enforced.
   - **Protocol errors.** Each is a fixed `code` and a fixed `message` — `parse error` · `invalid request` ·
     `method not found` · `invalid params` · `unknown tool` — with no `data` and nothing of the request in it.
   - **The tool listing**, built from `VERBS` alone in the table's order. Each tool is `name` (the verb's name),
     `description` (the verb's `help`) and an `inputSchema`: `{"type":"object","properties":{…},"required":[…],
     "additionalProperties":false}`, with one property per `ArgSpec` in the table's order. Each property carries a
     `type` by kind, and a `description` written as the arg's `help`, then ` (`, then `ArgKind::bound()`, then `)`:
     - `id` · `text` · `name` → `"string"`; `key` → `"string"` with `"enum"` = `KEY_NAMES`; `flag` → `"boolean"`;
       `milliseconds` → `"integer"` with `"minimum": 1` and `"maximum": MAX_MILLISECONDS`;
     - `start`'s `app` gets `"enum"` = the `apps` the binary hands over;
     - `required` lists the args whose `required` is true.

No string is written that the table or `apps` does not hold.
   - **A tool call.** `params` must be an object with a string `name`; `arguments` is optional (absent reads as `{}`)
     and, if present, must be an object. Otherwise the call is answered `-32602 invalid params`. A `name` that is not
     a verb of `VERBS` is answered `-32602 unknown tool`. Otherwise the call becomes a `Call { verb, args }`, one
     argument per member in the object's order:
     - a JSON string → `ArgValue::Text`, an integer in i64 → `ArgValue::Number`, a boolean → `ArgValue::Flag`;
     - any other value (null, a non-integer number, an array, an object) refuses the call `malformed` before anything
       else, with `Fault::WrongKind(<the table's name>)` when the verb's table names the argument and `Fault::Unnamed`
       when it does not.

An instance-level verb then runs through `Session::run` on the held session. A session-level verb is checked by
     `validate_session` and answered by the server itself:
     - `start`: `boot(app)`, held; it is `AlreadyRunning` when one is held. Its answer is `json::started` of a `Hello`
       holding the app's name as label, `std::process::id()`, `served: 0` and `idle_expiry.as_secs()`.
     - `status`: `json::status` of the same, with `served` the count of tool calls answered on the held session
       before this one.
     - `stop`: drops the held session and answers `json::stopped()`.
     - An instance verb, `status` or `stop` with no held session is `SessionError::NoSession`.
   - **The tool result.** Every tool result is `{"content":[{"type":"text","text":…}],"isError":…}`:
     - an accepted `snapshot` → `text` is `Outcome::Screen`'s text itself, `isError: false`;
     - any other accepted call → the call's JSON line (`Outcome::to_json`, `json::started` · `status` · `stopped`),
       `isError: false`;
     - a refusal → `Refusal::to_json()`, `isError: true`;
     - a session error → `SessionError::to_json()`, `isError: true`.

A result whose `text` is over 1,048,576 bytes (`MAX_ANSWER_BYTES`, as on the socket) is replaced by
     `SessionError::AnswerTooLarge`'s result: the call ran and is not rolled back. Every reply is one line: the whole
     JSON-RPC object written through `json.rs`'s `Object` and `string`, a `\n`, then a flush.
   - **Idle expiry.** When a request arrives and a session is held, the server compares the time since the last
     answered tool call (or since `start`) with `idle_expiry`. At or past it, the session is dropped before the
     request is handled. No timer and no thread; the read blocks as before.
   - **The `tool_call` span** — the founder's fork 4A (`inputs#I3`). Each `tools/call` request, and nothing else,
     opens `tracing::info_span!(target: "escher_driver", "tool_call", tool = Empty, ending = Empty)` and enters it
     before its `params` are read; it stays entered until the result is written.
     - `tool` is recorded as `row.name` from `schema::verb` when the call names a verb of the table, and is absent
       otherwise.
     - `ending` is recorded as `accepted` (an accepted call), `refused` (a `Refusal`) or `error` (a session error or
       a protocol error).
     - No other field. Nothing the client sent is recorded, nothing of a result, no length.
     - The `command` span that `Session::run` makes (`execute.rs:74`, no `parent:`) then has `tool_call` as its
       parent.
   - **No panic path on what a client sends:** no `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `unreachable!` or index outside the
     `#[cfg(test)]` module, and no print.

7. **The `mcp` role.** In `cli.rs`:
   - `read` takes the first word `mcp` beside `serve`, before the verb table. `mcp` with no other word is
     `Line::Mcp`; any other shape is `Line::Usage`.
   - `run` maps `Line::Mcp` to `serve_mcp(stdin().lock(), stdout().lock(), apps, boot, IDLE_EXPIRY)`.
   - Its ending writes nothing on stdout in any case: `Ok` exits `0`, and `Err` exits `3` with the error's fixed
     message on stderr only. Stdout belongs to the protocol.
   - The usage line gains `; mcp role: mcp` after the host role.
   - The `command_line` doc names the role and its ending.
   - Inline tests gain the role's rows: `mcp` read as the role, `mcp x` and `mcp --session d` read as usage, the

8. **The binary.** `examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs`:

     process").
