9. **The shared test module for a child that speaks lines.** `examples/seven_guis/tests/common/mod.rs` gains:
   - `Speaker`: a spawned child with a piped stdin, its stdout read on a thread into a channel, its stderr drained
     from the spawn on, and kill-and-reap on drop. `send(line)` writes one line and flushes. `reply()` takes one
     stdout line under a 30 s bound; past the bound the check fails with a count only. `close()` closes stdin and
     waits under the same bound.
   - `string_at(json, key)`: the first string value under `key`, unescaped over exactly `json.rs`'s escape set
     (`\"` `\\` `\n` `\r` `\t` `\u00XX`) and nothing else.

   `host_binary.rs`'s reading of the usage line is updated for the role word.

11. **The log check — `examples/seven_guis/tests/mcp_log.rs`** (on the `host_log` pattern, not `cfg(unix)`-gated).
    It runs `escher-session mcp` with `RUST_LOG=trace`, both streams drained from the spawn on, over this flow:
    `start crud`, `snapshot`, `type` of a sentinel into `crud-name`, `click crud-create`, one refused call, `stop`.
    It asserts:
    - stderr holds 0 occurrences of the sentinel, 0 of the stable-id needles and 0 of the name needles, both read
      from the stand booted in the test's own process as `host_log` reads them;
    - exactly one line holding `span="tool_call"` per `tools/call` sent, each line's field names within
      `tool`/`ending` and the sink's own (`message`, `time.busy`, `time.idle`), each `ending` value one of the three
      words;
    - one `span="command"` line per instance-level call;
    - stdout holds protocol lines only.

    A failure message names a kind and a count, never a captured line. The workspace build of the same file is a
    separate gate entry.

12. **The in-process check — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_mcp_tools.rs`.** For each of `incremental` in
    `[false, true]`, it runs `serve_mcp` over an in-memory request buffer and a `Vec<u8>` writer, with a boot that
    boots the stand's lean tasks with `stand::options(incremental)` (and the Timer with its step, as the binary does):
    - the same Counter flow as step 10; the `snapshot` text block equal to `Session::run`'s `Outcome::Screen` text on
      a session booted the same way, byte for byte (`inputs#I2`); the second snapshot's block holding
      ` "3" id="counter-value" `; each `click`'s text equal to `Outcome::to_json` of the same click run directly on
      that parallel session;
    - a Timer flow, `start timer` then `advance` 1,000 ms, accepted with `advanced_ms` 1000, so a held Timer gets its
      step through `start`;
    - **the parent:** a hand-written `tracing` subscriber local to the file (installed with
      `tracing::subscriber::with_default`) that keeps a stack of entered spans and records, per new span, its name
      and its parent's name. Every `command` span's parent is a `tool_call` span; there is one `tool_call` per
      `tools/call` sent; the session-level calls' `tool_call` spans have no child; and each `tool_call` records
      `tool` as the verb's word and `ending` as the call's (`accepted` · `refused` · `error`), with no other field
      recorded;
    - the diff of each `click` is equal in the two layout modes.

    It is read under the per-package and the workspace build.

13. **The live trial — `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-mcp-surface/evidence/live-trial.py`** (written by /implement,
    fired once by the operator pass; `inputs#I3`, fork 3A). A stdlib Python script, run from the repository root.
    1. It builds a per-run `mktemp -d` session directory whose path names nothing, and removes it at exit.
    2. It writes there an `mcp.json` with one stdio server `escher`. The server runs `sh -c` with `exec`: stdin is
       tee'd to `target/mcp-trial/requests.jsonl`, the absolute path of `target/debug/escher-session` runs with the
       argument `mcp`, and its stderr goes to `target/mcp-trial/server.log`, under `RUST_LOG=info`.
    3. It runs, from that directory, `timeout 600 claude -p "Using only your tools, start the counter app, operate it until its display reads 3, take a snapshot, stop the session, then reply with the display's final reading." --output-format stream-json --verbose --tools "" --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <that mcp.json> --allowedTools mcp__escher --setting-sources "" --disable-slash-commands --no-session-persistence --max-budget-usd 1`
       (the pipe's flags, `scripts/cold-agent.sh:256-257`), with the transcript and the client's stderr in
       `target/mcp-trial/`.
    4. It prints one line, and nothing else to stdout:
       `trial: client_exit {n} · isolated {true|false} · tool_calls {n} · refused {n} · errors {n} · end_state {reached|unmet} · protocol_version {v} · discover {sent|not sent}`.
       - `isolated`: the transcript's `init` event lists exactly the nine `mcp__escher__*` tools and one connected
         server `escher`.
       - `tool_calls` · `refused` · `errors`: counts of `span="tool_call"` lines in `server.log`, all of them, and
         those with `ending=refused` and with `ending=error`.
       - `end_state`: `reached` when the last `mcp__escher__snapshot` tool result in the transcript holds
         ` "3" id="counter-value" `.
       - `protocol_version`: the version the client's first `initialize` request asked for, read from
         `requests.jsonl`, and whether any request's method was `server/discover`.

    Nothing of the transcript, the requests or a result is printed or committed. The operator pass copies the printed
    line into `evidence/live-trial.md`, with the run's date.

14. **Front page.** `README.md:48`: the MCP surface leaves the still-to-come sentence. One sentence says how it is
    run (`escher-session mcp`, spawned by an MCP client) and what it offers (the nine verbs as tools).

body:
- (matrix) **`verification-matrix.json#v010-13`** — the claim depends on all of the following:
  - `escher-session mcp`'s `tools/list` offers exactly the nine verbs of `VERBS` (every command the command line
    runs) in the table's order, each with the table's arguments, required set and help.
  - A scripted MCP session completes the Counter flow by tool calls alone, both in process in both layout modes
    (`stand_mcp_tools`) and through the binary as a child process (`mcp_server`): `start counter`, a `snapshot`,
    three clicks on `counter-increment`, a `snapshot` reading ` "3" id="counter-value" `, `stop`.
  - One live agent session on the dev host completes the same flow, its only tools this server's: the operator
    pass's trial line reads `isolated true` and `end_state reached`, recorded in `evidence/live-trial.md`.

  Proved by `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_mcp_tools`, `cargo test -p seven_guis --locked --test
  mcp_server --test mcp_log`, the same under `cargo test --workspace --locked --test stand_mcp_tools --test
  mcp_server --test mcp_log`, and the operator entry
  `cargo build --locked -p seven_guis --bin escher-session && python3 escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-mcp-surface/evidence/live-trial.py`.

- (operator, inputs#I2) A `snapshot` tool result's text block equals `Session::run`'s screen text byte for byte, in
  both layout modes, and equals the command line's `snapshot` `text` field unescaped on a fresh Counter. Every other
  accepted result is the call's JSON line; a refusal and a session error carry `isError: true` — `stand_mcp_tools`,
  `mcp_server`.

- (security) A non-JSON line, a 65,537-byte line, an unknown method and an unknown tool are each answered with a fixed
  JSON-RPC error. These, a refused call and a malformed call each run nothing: the next snapshot reads as before. No
  reply holds the refused id, the unknown tool's name or the over-bound bytes, and no path panics on them (per
  security-plan §Input Validation, the Driver command schema row and the Cold-agent MCP stub row) — `mcp_server`, the
  module's unit tables, the no-panic probe.

- (security) The request's `id` is echoed only as an integer or a string of at most 128 bytes; another form is
  answered `-32600` with `id: null` (`inputs#I3`, fork 1A) — the module's `id` table, 128 and 129 bytes the edges.

- (obs) Each `tools/call` leaves exactly one `tool_call` span under `escher_driver` with `tool` (the table's word,
  absent for an unknown tool) and `ending` (`accepted` · `refused` · `error`) and no other field. Each `command` span's
  parent is a `tool_call`, read by the check's own subscriber in both layout modes. The `command` span keeps its
  eight fields (per obs-plan §4) — `stand_mcp_tools`, `stand_act_spans`.

- (obs, security) With `RUST_LOG=trace`, the `mcp` role's stderr over a CRUD flow with a `type` holds 0 sentinel
  occurrences, 0 id needles and 0 name needles, built alone and built with the workspace. It holds one `tool_call`
  line per tool call, and stdout holds protocol lines only (per obs-plan §8 Values logged as-is; security-plan
  §Logging & Monitoring) — `mcp_log` under both entries.

- (design) Every stdout line of the role holds no ESC byte; no driver code asks whether a stream is a terminal (per
  design-system §Surface: cli → Component Patterns) — `mcp_server`, the terminal probe.

- (layouts) `escher-session mcp x` and `escher-session mcp --session d` end as usage, exit 2, with nothing on stdout.
  The nine verbs, `serve` and their four endings read as before (per layout-templates §Surface: cli) — the cli unit
  rows, `host_binary`, `cli_commands`, `cli_flow`.

- (arch, security) `serde_json` is named in `escher-driver` and the root `[workspace.dependencies]` only. The lock
  changes by that one line, no package enters, neither adapter enters the stand's graph, and the audit is green with
  no ignore added. The crate writes no JSON through `serde_json` (per architecture §Stack and Technologies;
  security-plan §Dependency Security) — the lock, adapter, no-panic and audit entries.

- (tests) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` and `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` pass, and the fork's CI run
  on the pushed sha reads `verdict: green` (per test-plan §9).

- **Spec anchors:**
  - architecture §Standard Contracts (Driver session; CLIs) · §Established Decisions ([Driver session]) ·
    §Occupied Resources (Network ports and listeners; Names; Process-wide state and threads) · §Stack and
    Technologies · §Conventions (Manifests; Tests)
  - security-plan §Threat Model Summary · §Input Validation (Driver command schema; Driver session socket; `id`;
    password and file `input` value; Cold-agent MCP stub; CLI arguments) · §Error Handling · §Logging & Monitoring ·
    §Dependency Security · §Secret Management
  - obs-plan §3 Observability Harness Contract (Logging stack) · §4 Span / Trace Coverage · §6 Log Coverage · §8 PII
    Scrubbing & Compliance
  - test-plan §2 Process-lifecycle checks · §3 Stand log format · §4 escher-driver · §5 Session ↔ held instance · §6
    Command line · §9 Engine features by runner
  - a11y-plan §1 (the Dioxus crates bullet) · §7 Screen Reader Support
  - design-system §Surface: cli → Component Patterns · §Typography → Loading · §Motion
  - layout-templates §Surface: cli (`escher-session`) · §Surface: desktop-native

- **Research files inspected:** `packages/escher-driver/src/{lib,cli,json,schema,execute,client,host,wire}.rs`,
  `packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs`, `examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs`,
  `examples/seven_guis/tests/common/mod.rs`, `scripts/cold_agent_stub.py`, `scripts/cold-agent.sh`; the MCP
  specification pages named in research.md §Scope.

- **Forks:** the operator's (`inputs#I2`): instance in process with nine tools · the handshake revisions only · a
  `snapshot` result as plain text. The founder's (`inputs#I3`): 1A the crossing ratified as stated · 2A `serde_json`
  as a reader only · 3A one small live trial now · 4A the `tool_call` span with `tool` and `ending`.

- **Playbook:** forks 1 and 4 match "Boundary widening" (`.andromeda/playbook.md:36-38`, verdict `escalate`), and both
  were answered by the founder at P4 (`inputs#I3`). Their wrap amendments carry the pattern and his words (below).

- **A client of a hosted session** — rejected by the operator (`inputs#I2`): it is unix only and it needs a trace
  identity on the socket. The wire stays `v2` and `wire.rs` · `host.rs` · `client.rs` are not edited.

- **The current MCP revision (2026-07-28), alone or beside the handshake** — not here (`inputs#I2`). Answer
  `server/discover` with `-32601` and nothing else; it is pinned on the route at the wrap, with what the host client
  sends, which the trial measures.

- **A snapshot result as the JSON line, or `structuredContent` on any result** — rejected by the operator
  (`inputs#I2`); no result carries `structuredContent`.

- **`rmcp`, an async runtime, or a hand-written JSON reader** — rejected by the founder (`inputs#I3`, fork 2A).
  `serde_json` reads; it never writes an answer.

- **A tenth verb, an MCP-only tool, or a tool description authored apart from `VERBS`** — do not (CARRY 2). The
  listing is built from the table and the binary's app names, and nothing else.

- **Fielding anything the client sent on `tool_call`** (the tool name as spelt, the request id, the method, an
  argument, a client's name or version), a result or its length, or a field named with the sink's scrub words — do not
  (obs-plan §4; `inputs#I3`, fork 4A, two fields only). A protocol-level rejection that is not a `tools/call` opens no
  span.

- **Printing a span's parent on the sink's line** — do not: that changes the ratified closed-span record. The parent
  is proved by a check's own subscriber.
- **Writing a log line, a diagnostic or a banner to stdout in the `mcp` role** — do not; its errors go to stderr only.

- **Changing the cold-agent pipe, its stub or its contract tests** — not here: swapping the stub for this surface is
  the Cold-agent test's (`working-route.md:100`). The trial is a separate one-shot script.

- **Committing the trial's transcript, requests file or server log, or copying any of their content into evidence**
  — do not; evidence holds the printed figures line only.

- **Re-running the live trial** — do not without a new word: the founder's word covers one run (`inputs#I3`). A
  failed run is recorded as read and reported.

- **A `tabindex`, markup, id or style added to the stand for the flows** — do not (layout-templates §Surface:
  desktop-native).

- **The parent equality:** `Session::run` makes `command` with `tracing::info_span!` and no `parent:`
  (`execute.rs:74`, `:111`), so its parent is the span current on the thread when it is made. With `tool_call`
  entered around the call, that is `tool_call`. Read from the code and from `tracing`'s rule for a span macro without
  `parent:`, and not run; step 12's subscriber runs it. A reading of `command` with no parent there is a defect in
  step 5's enter, never in the executor.

- **Why the sink cannot show it:** a closed span's line prints the span's own name and stored fields
  (`packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs:162-173`), so `mcp_log` counts lines and the in-process check proves the
  parent.

- **`serde_json` is already built:**
  - `cargo tree --locked -p escher-driver -e normal -i serde_json` reads
    `serde_json v1.0.151 ← dioxus-html v0.7.10 ← dioxus-native-dom` (research.md §Patterns detected);
  - naming it adds a line to the lock and no package.

- **The JSON escape set the tests unescape** is `json.rs:16-32`'s: `\"`, `\\`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\u00XX`.
  `string_at` handles exactly that set. A server reply holds a JSON-RPC envelope around the tool's text, so the text
  is escaped twice for a JSON-line result; `string_at` reads the outer layer only.

- **The counter's end-state atom** ` "3" id="counter-value" ` is the form `stand_snapshot_text.rs:260` asserts with
  `0` at boot.

- **Call sites a signature change reaches:**
  - `command_line` — one outside the crate (`session_host.rs:24`) and `cli.rs:73`;
  - `run` in `cli.rs` — `cli.rs:73` and the inline tests at `cli.rs:718`, `:721`, `:730`
    (research.md §Graph impact, `tree-query-2026-10-10-mcp-surface.json`).

- **Readers of `VERBS` outside the crate:** `stand_act_spans.rs`, `stand_act_scroll.rs`, `cli_commands.rs`
  (`grep -rln VERBS tests/blitz-tests/tests examples/seven_guis`). No row changes, so none changes.

Two fixes in the engine, each a direct change in the engine's own files, so that what the driver reads of a scrolling
box is true before any later surface carries it out of the process (the founder's ruling, 2026-10-10 — scope.md,
CARRY 1). **A box that is scrolled reads its own bounds where it shows:** the engine's geometry reader stops counting a
box's own scroll offset against the box itself. **A hit never reaches content scrolled out of its box:** the hit walk
tests a box's own area where the box stands and stops at the edge of every box that clips by `overflow`. Both follow
the shape the founder ratified for the nested into-view scroll: the function itself, for every document, no second
function beside it (per architecture §Established Decisions → Scrolling and input).

escher-driver's logic does not change (research.md §The driver): it takes a target's centre from the snapshot's
`bounds`, `off-screen` from the visible region and `covered` from the raw hit, so both fixes reach it through the
engine. What changes in the driver is text: the three sentences that state the two limits today, with every copy of
them, return to what is then true (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session; security-plan §Error
Handling). The three checks that pin the defects are restated to the true reading, and each fix gains an engine-level
check of its own. Every check is read in both layout modes and under both builds, because a workspace build and a
per-package build compile different bodies of the geometry reader (per test-plan §9 → Engine features by runner).

Decided, and by whom: the bounds fix sits in the shared reader (the operator, `inputs#I2`). The two forks written in
`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T13-07-20-phase/p4-founder-forks.md` were answered by the operator as technical forks — each
decides how far a fix the founder already ruled reaches, inside the principle he set (`inputs#I4`): **a hit stops at
every box that clips by `overflow`** (fork 1, option 1B), and **the second reader that carries the same shift,
`Node::absolute_position`, is measured and pinned here as it reads, its fix owned on the route** (fork 2, option 2B).
**A conformance reading is taken, report-only and bounded** (`inputs#I4`). The chunk claims no capability.

title: 1. The engine-level check of the bounds reader (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/scrolled_box_client_rect.rs`, new)

data.head: ### 1. The engine-level check of the bounds reader (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/scrolled_box_client_rect.rs`, new)

body:
In the shape of `scroll_into_view_nested`: parsed pages at 800 × 600, `for incremental in [false, true]`; a `//!`
header naming the behaviour and the bug it guards; no `cfg(unix)` gate, no `stand_` prefix, no sleep. Every box under
test carries a fixed CSS size — no assertion rests on a box sized by text. A rect is read through
`get_client_bounding_rect`; a box that is scrolled is never read through the harness's `layout_rect` or `center_of`,
which are built on the second reader (step 3). Each case first asserts that its fixture produces the condition (the
box is scrolled, by how much), then the reading. The cases, one test each:

- **A scrolled box's client rect is the rect it had before it was scrolled** — scrolled down its content, scrolled
  across it, and both.
- **A scrolled box inside a scrolled box** — the inner box's rect moves by the outer box's offset and not by its own.
- **An element inside a scrolled box** reads moved by the box's offset (as today).

- **An inline element inside a scrolling inline root** — its `node_client_rects` move with the root's scroll offset,
  the same figures before and after the fix (the caller at `document.rs:2379`).

- **An inline element whose offset parent is a scrolled, positioned box** — its `offset_rect` does not move when the
  parent is scrolled (the caller at `document.rs:2339`).

- **An element inside a scrolled box reads the same `visible_region`** before and after the box is scrolled, and that
  region is the box's padding box cut by the viewport (the caller at `scrolling.rs:776`).
The first two are the regression cases and are red on the engine as built; the other four hold before and after and
guard the three callers step 5 re-bases.

title: 2. The engine-level check of the hit (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/hit_clipped_at_scrolling_box.rs`, new)

data.head: ### 2. The engine-level check of the hit (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/hit_clipped_at_scrolling_box.rs`, new)

body:
Same shape and rules as step 1; a point is computed from client rects read before the box is scrolled, never from
`layout_rect` or `center_of` of a scrolled box. The cases, one test each:

- **A point above a scrolled box, over an earlier sibling, answers the sibling** — not the box, not a row scrolled out
  of it; and the hovered node after a pointer move there is the sibling.

- **A point below an unscrolled box, where its rows overflow and nothing else stands, answers what shows there** — not
  a row.
- **A point inside the box's own area answers the row showing there**, before and after the box is scrolled.
- **An `overflow: hidden` box scrolled by a program** reads as the first case does.
- **An `overflow: clip` box** — its clipped-out content is not reached by a hit.

- **A box clipped on one axis only** (`overflow-x: clip` beside `overflow-y: visible`, the fixture first asserting
  that both values compute as written): content overflowing along the visible axis is not reached — the hit stops at
  the box's whole padding box, as paint clips it. Pinned as it reads, and named in the report beside
  `visible_region`, which narrows per axis.
- **An `overflow: visible` box** — its overflowing content is hit outside the box, as today.
- **A scrolled box's overlay scrollbar thumb is still resolved** at a point on the thumb.

- **What this fix leaves, pinned as it reads:** a `contain: paint` box whose `overflow` is `visible` — paint clips its
  content, and a hit still reaches the clipped-out content. This is the one part of the remainder this chunk
  measures; an image's, a sub-document's and a text input's own box are not measured here.
The first, second, fourth, fifth and sixth are the regression cases and are red on the engine as built.

title: 3. The second reader, measured and pinned as it reads (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/scrolled_box_absolute_position.rs`, new)

data.head: ### 3. The second reader, measured and pinned as it reads (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/scrolled_box_absolute_position.rs`, new)

body:
Fork 2, option 2B (`inputs#I4`). Same shape and rules as step 1, one test: for a box scrolled by a known offset, in
both layout modes, `Node::absolute_position(0.0, 0.0)` is read before and after the scroll, and the reading is pinned
as measured. Hypothesis, read from the code and not measured (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:1626-1634`): the
reading after the scroll is the reading before it less the box's own scroll offset, though the box has not moved. The
file's header says the reading is pinned as measured on the engine as built, that the check turns red by design when
the reader is fixed and is then restated, and that the harness's `layout_rect` and `center_of` are built on this
reader. If the measurement does not show the shift, the test pins what it reads and the report says the hypothesis
read false. No engine line is edited for this step, and no caller of the reader is touched.
Report-only: it grades no criterion (`inputs#I4`). On the engine as built, before step 5 is written:

- fetch web-platform-tests at the commit `wpt/WPT_COMMIT` pins (`71b4d5f0eb7628a5d5f7cd2ee868ce1b1b5dc010`), at
  depth 1, into `target/wpt-checkout/` — `git init target/wpt-checkout`, then `git -C target/wpt-checkout fetch
  --depth 1 https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt.git 71b4d5f0eb7628a5d5f7cd2ee868ce1b1b5dc010` and
  `git -C target/wpt-checkout checkout FETCH_HEAD`;
- build the runner once — `taskset -c 12-15,28-31 cargo build --release -p wpt --locked`;

- run the CSSOM View tests — `WPT_DIR=target/wpt-checkout taskset -c 12-15,28-31 cargo run --release -p wpt --locked
  -- css/cssom-view`;

- keep the per-test results: the runner writes `wpt/output/wpt_expectations.txt` and `wpt/output/wptreport.json`
  (`wpt/runner/src/main.rs:831-844`) and deletes `wpt/output/` at the start of every run (`:492-496`), so both files
  are copied to `target/wpt-reading/before/` before anything else runs.
**The bound:** the wall clock is read when the fetch starts. If the fetch and the build together have not finished
30 minutes later, both are stopped, the measured figures (elapsed time, bytes fetched, how far the build got) are
written to `evidence/conformance.md`, the reading is recorded as "not taken, cost measured", step 10 is skipped, and
the chunk goes on — it does not wait on this reading.
**The footprint:** the release build and both runs are held to `taskset -c 12-15,28-31` — four physical cores; the
host is shared with three other builders.
**What stays out of the repository:** `target/wpt-checkout/`, `target/wpt-reading/` and `wpt/output/` are ignored by
git (`git check-ignore -q`, exit 0 for each, read at P5). No file of the checkout, no build output and no raw runner
log is copied into the repository or a run dir; `evidence/conformance.md` holds figures and test names, written by
hand.

title: 5. The bounds reader returns the box's own position (`packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs`, `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/writing_mode.rs`, `packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs`)

data.head: ### 5. The bounds reader returns the box's own position (`packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs`, `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/writing_mode.rs`, `packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs`)

body:
In **both** bodies of `BaseDocument::physical_unrounded_geometry` (`document.rs:2257-2270`; `writing_mode.rs:375-401`)
the node's own scroll offset leaves the sum on every path — the containing-block walk in both bodies, and the
vertical-chain path of the second (`writing_mode.rs:398-399`); every ancestor's offset stays. The reader's doc comment
says what it returns — the box's own position, not its content's origin — and cites CSSOM View's
`getBoundingClientRect` beside the change. The three callers that take a box as the origin of its content apply that
box's own scroll offset themselves, so each reads what it read before:
- `visible_region` drops its add-back (`scrolling.rs:774-780`) and takes the reader's position as the box's origin;

- `inline_fragment_rects` subtracts the inline root's own scroll offset from the origin it places fragments at
  (`document.rs:2379-2381`);

- `offset_rect` subtracts the offset parent's own scroll offset where it subtracts the parent's position
  (`document.rs:2338-2343`).
`get_client_bounding_rect` and the two layout-only callers in `resolved_style.rs` need no edit. No signature changes.
The six callers are research.md §Graph impact's list; no other caller exists (`calls`, `callee_name =
'physical_unrounded_geometry'`, 6 rows). `Node::absolute_position` is not edited.

title: 6. The hit walk stops where paint clips by `overflow` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs`)

data.head: ### 6. The hit walk stops where paint clips by `overflow` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs`)

body: In `hit_inner` (`node.rs:1350-1543`), two changes and nothing else:

- **The node's own area is tested where the box stands.** Today the test is made in scrolled coordinates as
  `0 ..= size + scroll_offset` (`:1386-1389`), which admits a point up to the scroll offset above or left of a scrolled
  box. The test becomes: the point, before the scroll offset is added, lies in the node's border box.

- **A node that clips by `overflow` stops the walk at its padding box.** The predicate is the overflow half of paint's
  own, as paint has it today and nothing of the hit's own: either axis of the node's computed `overflow` is not
  `visible`, the root element excepted (`packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:352-358`; fork 1, option 1B —
  `inputs#I4`). Paint does not tell the two axes apart (`render.rs:324` carries upstream's own note that it should),
  so a box clipped on one axis is stopped at its whole padding box, as paint clips it. For a point outside that node's
  padding box the walk reaches none of what the node draws as children — its positive and negative z-index hoisted
  children, its paint children and its inline content — and can still answer the node itself when the point lies in
  its border box. That is paint's own order of things: paint draws all four under the clip it pushes for a clipping
  node (`render.rs:546`, `:573`, `:1018-1069` — read at P4, not measured).
The other four classes paint clips — `contain: paint`, an image, a sub-document and a text input — are **not** stops:
the hit takes paint's overflow half only (fork 1, option 1C is not taken). Inside the padding box nothing changes: the
same order (positive-z hoisted, paint children last to first, negative-z hoisted, inline content, self), the
`visibility` and `pointer-events` rules, the transform handling, the thumb resolution inside the node's own area, the
canonicalization the callers do. No `layout_data` or `layout_style()` is newly reached on a node that may lack one, no
index on an id that may be stale, no log site. A spec citation sits beside the change (CSS Overflow, the clip of a box
whose `overflow` is not `visible`). No signature changes; `hit` and `hit_with_scrollbar` keep their callers
(research.md §Graph impact: 7 production call sites).

  0 failed · 11 ignored (test-plan §9 → Local baseline; predicted 165 lines, three new targets — record what the run
  measures).

- The stated tables in the blast radius are re-read, not assumed: `stand_act_ids` (70 accepted, 7 refused),
  `stand_act_diff` and `stand_diff`, `stand_snapshot`, `stand_act_spans`. P3 read none of them as pinning a scrolled
  box's bounds or a count on a scroll step (research.md §Sweeps); a row that moves is a finding for the report, with
  its cause, never an edit made to turn a gate green.

- Both fixes flagged upstreamable, with the base they are cut against (upstream `main` at `7832c177`); no upstream
  pull request is opened (scope.md, CARRY 5).
- The second reader's measured figures from step 3, for the route owner the wrap gives its fix (`inputs#I4`).

- The remainder under option 1B: what step 2's last case measured, and the three classes it did not measure (an
  image, a sub-document, a text input), for the wrap's route owner.

- The one-axis case as step 2 pinned it, named beside `visible_region`, which narrows per axis: a target lying
  outside such a box along its visible axis reads in view by the visible region while the hit stops at the box.
- The conformance reading: both counts and every moved test, or "not taken, cost measured" with the figures.

- Per new check file, which shared modules it declares (neither `common` nor `session_common` is expected — all
  three files are engine-level; record what is written).
- Every CI run of the operator pass with its id and verdict, for the `watch:` the scope carries.
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/scrolled_box_client_rect.rs` — the engine-level check of the bounds reader and its three re-based callers
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/hit_clipped_at_scrolling_box.rs` — the engine-level check of the hit walk
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/scrolled_box_absolute_position.rs` — the second reader, measured and pinned as it reads
- `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit/evidence/` — the red-then-green readings, the mutation controls and the conformance reading
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` — the reader's first body; `inline_fragment_rects` and `offset_rect` re-based
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/writing_mode.rs` — the reader's second body, both of its paths
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs` — `visible_region` drops its add-back
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs` — `hit_inner`: the own-area test and the stop where paint clips by `overflow`
- `packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs` — `Cause::Covered`'s meaning and its held copy
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` — the helps of `changed` and of `snapshot`'s `text`, and their held copies
- `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs` — the held copy of `covered`'s meaning
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` — the crate docs that state both limits
- `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs` — one private doc comment
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_scroll.rs` — two pinning tests restated, one comment, the header
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_obstructed.rs` — one pinning test restated, one comment, the header

No entry is a live leg: every check boots what it reads in process, so there is no liveness probe and no `stop` key.
No boot path is edited — the `escher-session` binary's `main`, the windowed stand's `main` and the sink are untouched
— so no boot smoke is listed beyond the standing hosted checks, which read what a call answers. The project has no
headful self-verify harness and this chunk changes no screen. No dependency enters and no manifest changes, which the
preservation entry holds; the audit leg is therefore not listed. **Not run locally:** the MSRV build and the windows,
macos, ios and android matrix legs — the fork's CI run is their one witness, read after the operator pass; the three
new check files carry no `cfg(unix)` gate, so the windows and macos jobs run them.

**The conformance reading has no listed entry, by construction** (steps 4 and 10; `inputs#I4`). It is report-only and
grades no criterion; it is a before and an after around steps 5 and 6, and the wrap's light gate re-runs entries
verbatim against a tree that no longer has a "before"; and it is bounded, so it may end as "not taken, cost
measured". Its readings are `evidence/conformance.md`, written by implement. The fact it rests on, read at P4 with no
clone and no build: the runner has no mode without a script engine — `blitz-vibey-script` is an unconditional
dependency of it (`wpt/runner/Cargo.toml:17`) and a test that loads `/resources/testharness.js` is run by executing
its JavaScript through that crate (`wpt/runner/src/test_runners/harness_test.rs:1-3`; classified at
`test_runners/mod.rs:325-327`) — and a suite is any path under the checkout (`wpt/runner/src/main.rs:239-244`). This
host held no checkout at P3 (`WPT_DIR` unset; none at `$HOME/dev/*/wpt`, `$HOME/dev/projects/wpt`, `$HOME/wpt`) and
the fork's CI runs no WPT job, so the cost of the fetch and of the release build is what step 4 measures.

`evidence/controls.md` has no listed producer either, by construction: it is implement's record of step 9's one-shot
readings — the red readings on the engine as built, which no entry can re-produce once the tree has moved, and the
mutation controls; what it records is asserted by listed entries (the three new check files and the restated pair,
under both builds).

- (arch) An element inside a scrolled box reads the same `visible_region` before and after the bounds fix, an inline element's fragment rects still move with its scrolling root, and an inline element's `offset_rect` still ignores its offset parent's scroll — the three callers re-based in step 5 — the same two entries, and `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test scroll_into_view_nested --test inline_fragment_rects --test scrollbars --test scrollbar_drag --test fragment_navigation --test paint_order --test touch_action --test text_selection_anonymous_block --test stale_dirty_descendants --test stand_snapshot --test stand_snapshot_state --test stand_accessibility_ids` (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Scrolling, selection, tree)

- (design) A point outside the padding box of a box that clips by `overflow` never answers that box's content — above a scrolled box, below an unscrolled one, for a hidden-overflow box scrolled by a program and for an `overflow: clip` box — and a box clipped on one axis is stopped at its whole padding box, pinned as it reads; a point inside the box's own area answers the same element as before, in stacking order, and `paint_order`, `scrollbars`, `scrollbar_drag` and `fragment_navigation` stay green unedited — the same two entries and the standing-checks entry above (per design-system §Depth Strategy, Engine depth behavior)

- **The frame that produces the shift.** Both bodies of `BaseDocument::physical_unrounded_geometry` walk from the node up its containing-block chain and add `location − scroll_offset` for every box on the walk, **the node itself included** (`document.rs:2263-2267`; `writing_mode.rs:383-388`, and again at `:398-399`). A box's own scroll offset moves its content, not the box, so that one term is the defect. `get_client_bounding_rect` returns the result less the viewport's scroll (`document.rs:2281-2289`), and the snapshot's `bounds` is that rect (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs:127`).

- **The equality the fix needs, on the readings already measured** (evidence file, both layout modes): `crud-list` after 12 Creates and a `scroll` naming the last row reads `(24, 94.796875, 393, 514)` where the box stands at `(24, 112.796875, 393, 532)` — the difference is the list's own scroll offset, 18; at 14 Creates it is 76; the fixture's `fx-box` reads `(8, -269, 792, -169)` at scroll offset 300 where it stands at `(8, 31, 792, 131)`. With the node's own term left out of the sum, each reads the box's standing figures. Still true at HEAD: `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_act_scroll --test stand_act_obstructed` — 6 passed and 5 passed, exit 0, run at this step (the per-package build, so the `document.rs` body); the source tree is byte-identical to `177d1652`'s (`git diff --quiet 177d1652 HEAD -- packages tests examples wpt apps Cargo.toml Cargo.lock`, exit 0), whose workspace run is green (CI#38047227075 — the `writing_mode.rs` body).

- **Two bodies, two runners — re-derived** (`cargo tree -e features -i blitz-dom --locked`, counting `feature "writing-mode"` lines): `-p blitz-tests` 0 · `-p seven_guis` 0 · `--workspace` 1. `wpt/runner` names the feature (`wpt/runner/Cargo.toml:15`) and is a workspace member, so a workspace build compiles the `writing_mode.rs` body and a per-package build the `document.rs` body. The same check file runs over a different reader under each runner; a fix in one body alone reads green under one runner and red under the other.

- **Three callers lean on the shifted reading** — they take a box's geometry as the origin of that box's *content*, where the box's own scroll offset belongs:
  - `visible_region` adds the offset back: "A box's own scroll offset moves its content, not the box" (`scrolling.rs:774-780`). It is escher's own code and the one place that already compensates.
  - `inline_fragment_rects` places an inline element's fragments from its inline root's geometry (`document.rs:2379-2381`): fragments move with the root's own scroll.
  - `offset_rect` subtracts the offset parent's geometry from a fragment's viewport rect (`document.rs:2338-2343`): the parent's own scroll offset is in both terms and cancels.
  - Two more callers read only the layout half and are indifferent: `resolved_style.rs:509`, `:521`.

- **So the fix has two honest sites** — decision 1, asked at P4: in the shared reader (both bodies), with the three content-origin callers taking the offset themselves; or in `get_client_bounding_rect` alone, which adds the node's own offset back and leaves the reader and its callers as they are.

- **Who reads a client rect** (code-graph, `calls`, production callers): the snapshot (`snapshot.rs:127`), a script's `getBoundingClientRect` (`packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/element.rs:1333`) and `getClientRects` through `node_client_rects` (`element.rs:1352`), a Dioxus element's `get_client_rect` (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/events.rs:212`), and the pointer event's element-relative coordinates — client point less the target's rect (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/driver.rs:328-331`). For a target that is itself a scrolled box each of these reads shifted today and true after the fix. An inline element takes the fragment path and is not touched by a fix in `get_client_bounding_rect`.

- **The root.** The viewport's scroll is its own field (`tree.rs:55-64`), subtracted separately; a nested fix decides nothing for the root unless the root element carries a scroll offset of its own. Not measured: whether it ever does.
- **The accessibility tree reads no geometry** (`accessibility.rs` holds no bounds reader — grep `bound|layout|rect|position`: one hit, a label lookup). The bounds fix moves nothing there.

- **The frame that produces it.** `hit_inner` moves the point into the node's scrolled content space first (`node.rs:1376-1377`: `x − location.x + scroll_offset.x`) and then tests the node's own area as `0 ..= size + scroll_offset` (`:1386-1389`). For a box scrolled by `s` that range starts `s` above the box: a point up to `s` above a scrolled box matches the box itself. The walk then goes on into the node's paint children whenever the point lies in the node's own area, its scrollable overflow or its overflow rect (`:1391-1418`, `:1458-1485`) — with no test of whether the node clips.

- **The equality the fix needs**, on the fixture already measured: the button before the box reads `8, 8, 73, 31`, the box stands at `31 to 131` scrolled by 300, row 7 reads `11 to 51`; the hit at the button's centre answers `fx-row-7` today and must answer the button. Local to the box that point is `y = 19.5 − 31 + 300 = 288.5`, inside `0 ..= 100 + 300`, so both the own-area test and the descent admit it.

- **Why the button after the box is hit as itself today:** paint children are walked last to first (`node.rs:1458`), so a later sibling is tested before the box's overflowing rows. That reading is right by order, not by a clip.

- **Paint already holds the rule the walk lacks:** a node clips its children when it is not the root element and either overflow axis is not `visible` — and also for an image, a sub-document, a text input and `contain: paint` (`render.rs:349-358`); the clip is the padding box, the content box for a text input (`:442-451`). `visible_region` uses the overflow half of the same rule, per axis (`scrolling.rs:763-773`). Which of these the hit stops at is decision 2.

- **Who hits** (code-graph, production callers): pointer move and pointer down (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:299`, `:413`, `:423`), hover (`document.rs:1846`), text selection (`document.rs:2486`), a script's `elementFromPoint` and `elementsFromPoint` (`packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/document.rs:330`, `:347`), the harness's `hit` (`inspect.rs:96`) and through it the driver's `covered` (`execute.rs:338`). Overlay scrollbar thumbs are resolved in the same descent, inside the node's own area (`node.rs:1422-1429`).

- **Hoisted children** (positive and negative z-index) are hit from their stacking context, not from their scrolling ancestor (`node.rs:1440-1455`, `:1487-1502`); a clip in the child loop does not reach them. What a clipping box that is itself a stacking context does with its hoisted children is the plan's to state and the implementation's to measure.

- **No logic change is needed in escher-driver.** A target's centre is the centre of the snapshot's `bounds` (`execute.rs:270-278`); `off-screen` is read from `visible_region` (`:324-332`); `covered` from the raw hit at the page point (`:336-349`). Both fixes reach it through the engine.

- **`off-screen` does not move with the bounds fix, by construction:** `visible_region` narrows by the padding box of each clipping box on the chain, and under either site of decision 1 that box's origin is the same figure — today by the add-back, after by the reader. The check that holds it is `scroll_into_view_nested`'s `reader_holds_the_target` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/scroll_into_view_nested.rs:117-120`).

- **The three sentences and every copy of them:** `Cause::Covered`'s meaning (`refusal.rs:71-75`; copies `refusal.rs:254`, `json.rs:574`), the help of `changed` (`schema.rs:198-202`; copy `:435`), the help of `snapshot`'s `text` (`schema.rs:229-232`; copy `:427`). The crate's own docs state both limits (`lib.rs:56`), and a private doc comment gives the hit defect as its reason (`execute.rs:323`). Before the limits were added the three read (`git show e144b44d^`): "the elements on the screen before and after the step whose role, name, state, bounds or parent differ, as they read after it" · "the screen as one text: one line per element, nested by indent" · "another element is hit at the point the action would land".

- **Which of the three reaches an answer line:** `covered`'s meaning, in every `covered` refusal's JSON (`json.rs`, `Refusal::to_json`). The two help texts are in the table and are served by nothing yet.

title: How the open questions closed (P4 and the P5 review)

data.head: ## How the open questions closed (P4 and the P5 review)

body: - The bounds fix sits in the shared reader — the operator, `inputs#I2`.

- A hit stops at every box that clips by `overflow`, by the overflow half of paint's own predicate (`packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:352-358`; `:324` carries upstream's note that the two axes are not told apart) — the operator, `inputs#I4`. This phase had placed the fork with the founder; the operator answered it as a technical fork and said why.
- The second reader is measured and pinned in this chunk, its fix owned on the route — the operator, `inputs#I4`.

- A conformance reading is taken, report-only and bounded — the operator, `inputs#I4`, reversing `inputs#I2` on the fact read at P4: the runner carries its script engine unconditionally (`wpt/runner/Cargo.toml:17`, `wpt/runner/src/test_runners/harness_test.rs:1-3`), a suite is any path under the checkout (`wpt/runner/src/main.rs:239-244`), and only the checkout is missing. Read at P5 for it: the runner writes its results under `wpt/output/` and deletes that directory at the start of each run (`main.rs:492-496`, `:831-844`); `target/wpt-checkout`, `target/wpt-reading` and `wpt/output` are ignored by git (`git check-ignore -q`, exit 0 each); the host has 32 logical cores and `taskset` (`nproc`; `command -v taskset`); `contain: paint` is read by paint (`render.rs:327-336`).
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_actionable_keys.rs` · companion · serves step 6 · self

**Working entry (verbatim):** Scrolling-box bounds and hit — a box that is scrolled reads its own bounds where it shows, and a hit never reaches content scrolled out of its box (the founder's ruling, 2026-10-10)

**Epoch:** Epoch 5 — Agent surfaces (its first markerless entry) · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Freight on the entry:** five `CARRY:` blocks and one `WATCH:` (6 blocks, 244 to 1308 characters; `route.py pins`, trail in the run dir: 45 freight blocks on the markerless tail, 6 of them on line 75). No `BLOCKED-ON`, no `PREREQ`. Each block is folded below under "The carried freight". One external input: the operator's directive given with the take-up (`inputs#I1`), which says who decides which fork; every other fact below is read from this repository or the route.

**Premise closure (P3):** every bullet tagged `[inferred]` at the take-up — one the working entry did not state, or a mechanism claim that arrived in the freight — was re-read against `research.md`: fourteen verified and their tags dropped, four corrected and tagged `[premise-corrected: …]`; a fifth correction was made at P4, to who owns decision 2. What was verified by reading code and is not yet measured on a fixed engine says so in its bullet. A bullet with no tag is what the entry states or is verified.
Two fixes in the engine, each a direct change in the engine's own files, so that what the driver reads of a scrolling box is true before any later surface carries it out of the process.

- **A box that is scrolled reads its own bounds where it shows.** A snapshot node's `bounds`, for a box that is itself scrolled, is the box as it stands on the screen — the same before and after the box's content is scrolled.
- **A hit never reaches content scrolled out of its box.** A point outside a scrolling box's own area never answers a row of that box, whatever the row's layout position.

- **What follows for the driver, with no change in escher-driver's logic** — verified by reading: a target's centre is the centre of the snapshot's `bounds`, `off-screen` is read from `visible_region` and `covered` from the raw hit (`packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:270-278`, `:324-332`, `:336-349`). So with the two fixes: a step that scrolls a box no longer names the box among its `changed` nodes for that reason; a `click` or a `type` naming a scrolled box lands at the box's centre; a box in view is no longer refused `off-screen` at a shifted point; a control lying where scrolled-out content extends is no longer refused `covered`, and a pointer click there reaches the control. Each is measured on the fixed engine by the chunk's checks.

- **A regression check per fix, in both layout modes** (`incremental` false and true — CLAUDE.md §Critical Warnings: the two modes stay identical), on the stand and on a minimal fixture beside it where the stand lacks the case: no stand control reads the `covered` case in any state measured (`stand_act_obstructed`'s `no_stand_control_is_hit_through_by_a_row_scrolled_out_of_the_list`, green at HEAD), so that one is a fixture's. **And under both builds:** a workspace build and a per-package build compile different bodies of the bounds reader (research.md §The bounds defect), so each check is read under both.

- `[premise-corrected: stand_act_scroll.rs holds two tests that pin the bounds defect, :358-445 and :447-508, and the freight names one]` **Three checks pin the defects and are restated to the true reading** — `stand_act_scroll`'s `a_scrolled_box_reads_its_bounds_shifted_and_a_click_naming_it_lands_off_its_centre` and `a_click_naming_a_scrolled_box_is_refused_off_screen_while_the_box_is_in_view`, and `stand_act_obstructed`'s `a_button_where_scrolled_out_rows_extend_reads_covered_only_before_its_box`. Each asserts the defect as it reads today (all green at HEAD, run at P3). Both files also say the limit in their header and in one comment each (`stand_act_scroll.rs:11-13`, `:175-178`; `stand_act_obstructed.rs:13`, `:392-393`).

- `[premise-corrected: the sentences stand in more places than the three table rows and their unit tests — json.rs:574, lib.rs:56, execute.rs:323]` **The tool's three limit sentences are restated to what is then true** — `Cause::Covered`'s meaning (`refusal.rs:71-75`; held copies `refusal.rs:254` and `json.rs:574`), the help of the result field `changed` (`schema.rs:198-202`; held copy `:435`) and the help of `snapshot`'s `text` (`schema.rs:229-232`; held copy `:427`). The crate's own docs state both limits (`lib.rs:56`) and a private doc comment gives the hit defect as its reason (`execute.rs:323`); both are restated with them. Of the three, `covered`'s meaning is the one that reaches an answer line today, in every `covered` refusal's JSON. What each then says is decision 3.

- **Every other reader of the two engine functions is in the blast radius** — verified, the callers listed in research.md §Graph impact: a client rect is read by the snapshot, a script's `getBoundingClientRect` and `getClientRects`, a Dioxus element's `get_client_rect` and a pointer event's element-relative coordinates; a hit is read by pointer move and pointer down, hover, text selection, a script's `elementFromPoint` and `elementsFromPoint`, the harness and the driver's `covered`. The accessibility tree reads no geometry and is not among them.
- **The claim** — the entry names no capability, and CARRY 1 says it claims none. Read at P4 from the matrix; none is assumed.

- **Not built here:** no upstream pull request (CARRY 5); no MCP tool, no new verb, argument, result field or refusal cause; what a `changed` node says of *which* field differs (a `CARRY:` on "Self-description"); states a snapshot does not read (a `CARRY:` on "Stand requirement sweep"); a range input's interaction (its own entry).

- **Adjacent and not folded:** the handoff's "still owed" note that `Harness::scroll_into_view` has no check of its own is on no route entry and is not this entry's freight. Verified: neither fix changes what that function does — the into-view scroll reads `Node::absolute_position`, not the bounds reader, and the reader's caller in the scrolling code is `visible_region` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs:776`; research.md §Graph impact). An extract that reads the into-view scroll as a caller of the reader is overridden by this.

- **A second reader with the same shift, found at P3 and not on this entry:** `Node::absolute_position` also subtracts a node's own scroll offset (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:1626-1634`). The snapshot does not read it; the synthetic click's point, the IME cursor area, the event path's target position and the harness's `layout_rect_of` do. It is decision 4 — asked, never absorbed.

- **The merge surface grows by design.** The route entry "Upstream sync ahead of polish and ship" carries the fork's merge surface in the inherited files as CARRYs; this chunk's edits in upstream-owned files add to it, and the wrap's route-resolve re-measures those blocks.

- **The masters, CLAUDE.md and the crate notes state both limits as built** — verified by sweep: `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/docs/services/escher-driver.md` and `.claude/docs/services/dioxus-native-dom.md`, and the three sites the arch extract names. They are restated at the wrap, never by this phase.

Who decides is `inputs#I1`: "Technical forks of this entry are the operator own: ask them in your dialog and I answer. A fork that changes what an agent meets beyond restating the three limit sentences, or that widens a boundary, is the founder decision: put all such forks whole in one file with their dependences, as at the Driver CLI." Each was asked at P4, with its options made whole by research; how each stands is said beside it. The operator's answers are `inputs#I2` (P4) and `inputs#I3`, `inputs#I4` (the P5 review). Two forks were written whole in `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T13-07-20-phase/p4-founder-forks.md` as the founder's; the operator answered both as technical forks (`inputs#I4`).

1. **Where the bounds fix sits** — in the shared reader (both bodies), with the three callers that take a box as the origin of its content taking the box's own offset themselves; or in `get_client_bounding_rect` alone, which adds the node's own offset back and leaves the reader and its callers as they are (research.md §The bounds defect). The founder has ruled the direction (CARRY 1: a direct change, additivity a preference and never a goal); the site is technical — the operator's. **Answered: the shared reader** (`inputs#I2`).

2. **What "its box" means for the hit** — which boxes stop a hit at their edge: scroll containers alone (`overflow` `auto`, `scroll` or `hidden` — the entry's own words), every box that clips by `overflow` (adds `overflow: clip`), or everything paint clips; paint's own rule is the reference (research.md §The hit defect). Under every option a control clipped out of its own ancestor is already refused `off-screen` before the hit is read, so the options differ only in which other box's clipped-out content can still read as covering. `[premise-corrected: this phase placed the fork with the founder at P4; the operator answered it at the P5 review as a technical fork and said why — it decides how far a fix the founder already ruled reaches, inside the principle he set, and widens no boundary (inputs#I4)]` **Answered by the operator: every box that clips by `overflow`** — the overflow half of paint's own predicate, either axis not `visible`, the root excepted; a box clipped on one axis is stopped at its whole padding box, as paint clips it (`inputs#I4`).

3. **What the three sentences say after the fix** — each limit removed, the sentence back to its words before 2026-10-10-driver-cli (recovered at P3 from `git show e144b44d^`), or restated to a narrower truth where decision 2 leaves a remainder. Restating the three is the operator's remit by `inputs#I1`. **Confirmed at the review (`inputs#I3`): each returns to its earlier words; and by `inputs#I4` the `covered` sentence then says what remainder stands under decision 2's answer, only as far as this chunk measures it — content clipped by `contain: paint`.**

4. **The second reader with the same shift** — `Node::absolute_position` left as it reads and given a route owner, measured and pinned, or fixed here. **Answered by the operator as a technical fork (`inputs#I4`): measured here and pinned as it reads, in both layout modes, red by design when the fix lands; the fix is owned on the route. The harness helpers built on it are not used for a scrolled box in this chunk's own checks.**

5. **Whether the fix is proven beyond our own checks** — a conformance reading before and after. `WPT_DIR` is unset and no web-platform-tests checkout was found on this host; the fork's CI runs none; the cost of a clone and a release run here is not measured. Technical — the operator's. **Answered at P4: none taken (`inputs#I2`). Reversed at the P5 review on the fact read for it (`inputs#I4`): a reading of the CSSOM View tests is taken before and after the two fixes — report-only, grading no criterion, held to four physical cores, and bounded at 30 minutes for the fetch and the build, past which it is recorded as "not taken, cost measured".**

title: The carried freight (five CARRYs, one WATCH)

data.head: ## The carried freight (five CARRYs, one WATCH)

body: Each was folded as a hypothesis: the artifacts it names were re-read at the take-up (found unless said otherwise), and a mechanism it states was re-derived at P3.

1. **CARRY — the founder's ruling and what it sets** (2026-10-10, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the overseer; taken up at the 0-pending wrap of that day). Asked where the two defects are fixed, with three placements put to him whole, the founder chose a separate chunk before "MCP surface". His earlier words stand beside it: 2026-10-07, the engine function itself is fixed for nested scrolling; 2026-10-10, measure and state in the Driver CLI chunk while the fixes stay owned on the route. Each fix is a direct change in the engine's files — additivity is a preference, never a goal: where staying additive would bend the logic the upstream code is changed, and the next sync's conflict is the accepted price. The entry claims no capability — v010-04 and v010-11 read verified. *Re-read:* the relay as committed, `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T12-54-32-wrap/relay-1.md` — found, and it says what the block says.

2. **CARRY — a scrolled box's own bounds read shifted** (from 2026-10-07-refusal-detection, measured at 2026-10-10-driver-cli; moved here on the founder's ruling).
   - "a box that is itself scrolled reads its `bounds` shifted by its own scroll offset: a step that scrolls it names it among the changed nodes though it has not moved, and a `click` or a `type` naming the box lands off its centre by that offset or is refused `off-screen` while the box is in view — on the stand at 14 Creates a `click` naming `crud-list` selects `crud-person-7` while `crud-person-9` lies at the box's centre (shift 76), and on a fixture a `click` naming a box in view is refused `off-screen`, in both layout modes (measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-driver-cli/evidence/engine-findings.md; pinned as it reads by `stand_act_scroll`)" — still true at HEAD: the pinning tests assert exactly these readings and pass (`cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_act_scroll`, 6 passed, at P3; the workspace build's witness is CI#38047227075 on the same source).
   - "the elements inside the box read true bounds" — verified, asserted by the same tests (`stand_act_scroll.rs:411-420`, `:491-494`).
   - `[premise-corrected: the reader has two bodies, one per setting of the writing-mode feature, and a workspace build and a per-package build compile different ones]` the fix changes a client bounding rect for every document and lies in upstream-owned merge surface: `BaseDocument::physical_unrounded_geometry` at `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:2257` (compiled without `writing-mode`) and at `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/writing_mode.rs:375` (compiled with it). Both sum `location − scroll_offset` over the containing-block chain with the node's own offset included (`document.rs:2263-2267`; `writing_mode.rs:383-388`, `:398-399`). `visible_region`, escher's own, already adds that offset back (`packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs:774-780`).

3. **CARRY — the hit walk reaches content scrolled out of its box** (same origin; moved here with it).
   - "a control that comes before a scrolling box in the document and lies where a scrolled-out row extends is refused `covered`, the hit at its centre answering the row, and a raw pointer click there runs the row's handler; a control after the box is hit and clicked as itself; no control of the stand's CRUD reads it in any state measured, `crud-filter` at 14 Creates included (measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-driver-cli/evidence/engine-findings.md; pinned as it reads by `stand_act_obstructed`)" — still true at HEAD: 5 passed at P3, same witness for the workspace build.
   - "clipping the walk at a scrolling box changes every pointer event of every document, and the file is upstream-owned merge surface" — verified: the walk is `Node::hit` / `hit_inner` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:1342-1543`), reached by seven production call sites (research.md §Graph impact).
   - `[premise-corrected: the defect has two parts in hit_inner, not one]` the walk tests a node's own area in scrolled coordinates as `0 ..= size + scroll_offset`, so a point up to the scroll offset above a scrolled box matches the box itself (`node.rs:1376-1389`); and it goes on into the node's children whenever the point lies in the node's area or overflow, with no test of whether the node clips (`:1391-1418`, `:1458-1485`). A control after the box is hit as itself only because paint children are walked last to first (`:1458`).

4. **CARRY — what each fix brings with it** (from 2026-10-10-driver-cli's record; the overseer's relay). A regression check of each fix in both layout modes; the pinned checks restated to the true reading with their fix; the three sentences of the tool restated to what is then true. Verified, with the two corrections above (three pinning tests; five more sites that state a limit).

5. **CARRY — upstreamable, and no pull request yet** (the founder's standing ruling, relayed by the overseer). Both fixes are flagged upstreamable in this chunk's report; no upstream PR is opened until DioxusLabs/blitz#1083 gets a reaction. *Not read:* the upstream issue itself — the ruling is carried as relayed.

6. **watch: a fork CI job hanging in its package-install step (2/3; since 2026-10-09-audit-corrections-agent-surfaces)** — an observation, not an obligation: no criterion, no task, no gate entry. Its retire clause: a recurrence, or 3 green runs.
