_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-10-snapshot-states · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-10T16:40:31Z
- **Base commit:** `f0cb9dd733c00f8effec29b242abd152eed486f3` (HEAD at P4; its CI run CI#38066501931 reads green 16/16)

A snapshot reads which control is selected, pressed or invalid, from what the app states in its markup, and the
stand's tasks state all three — the founder's ruling of 2026-10-10 (`inputs#I2`), which brings the three states into
0.1.0 as their own chunk ahead of "MCP surface". Measured at P3 on the engine as built: the two flight-mode buttons
read byte for byte the same in both modes, a date's line differs between an invalid and a valid date in its value
alone, and the CRUD's row lines are the same before and after a row is selected (research.md §Measured first). An
agent reads each of the three only from a side effect today.

The change runs through four existing units and adds none (per architecture §Existing Scopes). The engine's
accessibility builder reads `aria-selected`, `aria-pressed` and `aria-invalid` on every element, by value, and writes
AccessKit's `selected`, `toggled` and `invalid` on the element's node — a direct change in the builder's own file, for
every document, flagged upstreamable (per architecture §Established Decisions → Scrolling and input, the precedent
form). The snapshot reads the three from that node, as it reads role, name and focus (per a11y-plan §7), into three
new fields of `NodeState`; its text form writes them as bare words and its diff names a node whose reading moved with
no new rule. The driver's one table gains three node keys and two of its help texts say the state words and the two
limits of the boolean model, so an agent learns them from the tool (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver
session). The stand states the three by attribute alone: the flight mode buttons as toggle buttons, the CRUD rows as
options of a listbox, the two date inputs as invalid or not (per layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary
screens).

How each fork was decided is scope.md §Decisions owed: the operator's answers at P4 are `inputs#I3` and `inputs#I4`.
Two boundary forks are the founder's and are written whole in
`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T16-12-10-phase/p4-founder-forks.md`; the plan takes the recommended option of each and
records both as the operator's reading awaiting the founder's word, never as his (`inputs#I4`).

Order matters: the checks are written and read red before the code they hold (steps 1 to 3), then the engine, the
model and its two readers, the driver, the stand (steps 4 to 9), then the controls and the readings (steps 10, 11).

1. **The engine's check, written first** — new file `tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_states.rs`, on the pattern
   of `accessibility_roles.rs` (a parsed HTML page, `HtmlDocument::from_html` with the fixed 800 × 600 light viewport
   and `HtmlProvider`, `resolve(0.0)`, then `build_accessibility_tree`), in both layout modes. It opens with a `//!`
   doc naming the behaviour and the three WAI-ARIA 1.2 anchors. One stated table per attribute, its row count
   asserted, each row an authored value and the node property it must read:
   - `aria-selected`: `true` reads `Some(true)`, `false` reads `Some(false)`; absent, empty, `undefined`, `TRUE` and
     an unrecognized word read `None`.
   - `aria-pressed`: `true`, `false` and `mixed` read `Toggled::True`, `Toggled::False`, `Toggled::Mixed`; absent,
     empty, `undefined` and an unrecognized word read `None`.
   - `aria-invalid`: `true`, `grammar` and `spelling` read `Invalid::True`, `Invalid::Grammar`, `Invalid::Spelling`;
     an unrecognized word reads `Invalid::True`; absent, empty and `false` read `None`.
   - Each attribute is carried by an element whose role supports it (a `button`, a `div role="option"`, an `input`)
     and by one whose role does not (a plain `div`): both read alike. A value padded with spaces reads as the value;
     a value of several thousand characters reads as unrecognized and builds without a panic. An `aria-checked`
     attribute on any of them sets nothing.
   Read red on the engine as built before step 4; the reading goes to `evidence/controls.md`.

2. **The stand's reading checks, written first** — three tests added to
   `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_state.rs`, in the file's own shape (the stand booted through
   `common::boot`, real input through the harness's `click` and `type_text`, `for incremental in [false, true]`, the
   reading taken from `node(&harness.doc.snapshot(), id).state`):
   - exactly the active flight mode reads pressed: at boot `flight-one-way` reads `pressed: Some(true)` and
     `flight-return` `Some(false)`; after a click on `flight-return` the two swap; after a click on `flight-one-way`
     they swap back; every other snapshot node reads `pressed: None` throughout;
   - exactly the selected row reads selected: with no row selected every `crud-person-` row reads
     `selected: Some(false)`; after a click on a row that row alone reads `Some(true)`; a click on another row moves
     the reading; a character typed into `crud-filter` that keeps the selected row listed clears it; after Create and a click on the new row, Delete
     leaves every remaining row `Some(false)`; no node outside the rows reads a `selected` at any point;
   - a date that is no date reads invalid: `flight-start` reads `invalid: false` at boot and `true` after a character
     that breaks the date is typed into it; with a return flight chosen `flight-return-date` reads the same way, and
     reads `false` again once the flight is one-way; no other node reads invalid.
   Each test asserts, beside the snapshot's reading, that it equals the accessibility node's — `is_selected()`,
   `toggled()` mapped as step 5 maps it, `invalid().is_some()` — through `common::tree_node`. The file's `//!` doc
   gains the three states. No deleting key is pressed (`.claude/rules/testing.md`).

3. **The stand's diff check, written first** — new file `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_states.rs`, through
   `Session::run` with `session_common`'s `hold`, `click`, `type_into` and `act`, in both layout modes, each returned
   diff compared with the file's own `before.diff(&after)` and across the two modes:
   - a `click` on `flight-return` returns `flight-one-way` with `pressed: Some(false)` and `flight-return` with
     `Some(true)` among its `changed` nodes; the click back returns both with the readings swapped;
   - a `click` on a CRUD row returns that row with `selected: Some(true)`; a `click` on another row returns both
     rows, the first `Some(false)` and the second `Some(true)`;
   - a `type` of a text that is no date into `flight-start` returns it with `invalid: true`, and a `type` of a date
     returns it with `invalid: false` (`type` replaces what the control holds, so the way back needs no deleting key).
   A failure message names a layout mode, a task and a row index only.

4. **The builder reads the three attributes** — `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs`, in
   `build_accessibility_node`'s element arm, after the `aria-hidden` read (`:96-99`). Each read sits under its
   WAI-ARIA 1.2 URL (`#aria-selected`, `#aria-pressed`, `#aria-invalid`), as the two reads above it do, and compares
   the attribute's value after trimming ASCII whitespace, exactly and in lower case:
   - `aria-selected`: `true` sets `selected` true, `false` sets it false, anything else sets nothing;
   - `aria-pressed`: `true`, `false`, `mixed` set `toggled` to AccessKit's matching value, anything else sets nothing;
   - `aria-invalid`: `true`, `grammar`, `spelling` set `invalid` to the matching value; an absent, empty or `false`
     value sets nothing; any other value sets `Invalid::True` — the specification's own rule, quoted in a comment:
     "Any value not recognized in the list of allowed values MUST be treated by user agents as if the value true had
     been provided."
   No role is consulted. `aria-checked` is not read. The added lines hold no log site, no print, no `unwrap`,
   `expect`, index or panic path (per security-plan §Input Validation, the `aria-label` · `<label for>` row).

5. **The model gains three fields** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs`. `NodeState` gains
   `selected: Option<bool>`, `pressed: Option<bool>` and `invalid: bool`, each with a rustdoc line; the type stays
   `Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`, `Default`. At the one construction site (`:140-147`) they are read from `tree_node`:
   `selected` is `is_selected()`; `pressed` is `toggled()` with `Toggled::True` reading `Some(true)` and both
   `Toggled::False` and `Toggled::Mixed` reading `Some(false)`; `invalid` is `invalid().is_some()`. The docs of
   `pressed` and `invalid` say the two limits — a mixed toggle reads not pressed, a grammar or spelling error reads
   invalid — and that the accessibility node keeps the full value. `SnapshotNode.state`'s doc line is restated.
   Unit tests, one per field, each over a document built as the file's others are: every value of step 1's table as
   the snapshot reads it; a Dioxus `bool` attribute holding `false` arriving as the text `false` and reading
   `Some(false)`, never absent (`mutation_writer.rs:439-445`); a native checkbox's `checked` unchanged with
   `pressed: None`; an `aria-checked` attribute moving neither `checked` nor `pressed`.

6. **The text form writes them** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs`, `write_line` (`:48-76`): after
   `value=` and before `focused`, `selected` or `unselected`, then `pressed` or `unpressed`, each only where the model
   holds a reading, then `invalid` only when true. The rustdoc of `to_text` (`:23-35`) states the new order and its
   example gains a line that shows it. `state_tokens_follow_the_model` gains a row per new token and one line that
   holds every token at once, pinning the order.

7. **The diff is pinned, not changed** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs`: no code line moves
   (`:76-81` compares the whole state). One unit test is added: two hand-built snapshots that differ in `selected`
   alone, in `pressed` alone and in `invalid` alone each name that node `changed` and no other.

8. **The driver's table, its written form and its served text** —
   - `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs`: `NODE_FIELDS` becomes twelve words — `id`, `parent`, `role`, `name`,
     `enabled`, `checked`, `value`, `selected`, `pressed`, `invalid`, `focused`, `bounds` — its doc line and its pin
     (`:570-575`) restated. The help of `snapshot`'s `text` (`:227`) becomes: "the screen as one text: one line per
     element, nested by indent; a line's state words, each written only where the element states it, are enabled or
     disabled, checked or unchecked, value=, selected or unselected, pressed or unpressed, invalid and focused; a
     mixed toggle reads unpressed, and a grammar or spelling error reads invalid". The help of `changed` (`:199-200`)
     becomes: "the elements on the screen before and after the step whose role, name, state, bounds or parent differ,
     as they read after it; `selected` and `pressed` are left out where the element states neither, `pressed` is
     false for a mixed toggle, and `invalid` is true for a grammar or spelling error". Both pins in
     `every_verb_states_its_help_its_arguments_and_a_result` (`:421`, `:425`) are restated word for word. No verb,
     argument kind, field kind or refusal cause is added.
   - `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs`: `NodeParts` gains the three parts; `node` writes `selected` and `pressed`
     only where present and `invalid` always, in the table's order; `nodes` fills them from `DiffNode.state`.
     `a_node_is_written_with_the_schema_fields_it_has` (`:412-446`) is restated: the full line with all twelve keys,
     the bare line now holding `"invalid":false`, its key list, the masked line.
   - `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs`: the crate docs' paragraph on what an element reads (`:51-56`) gains one
     sentence on the three states and the two limits.

9. **The stand states the three** — attributes only; no element, class, style, wrapper, key or order changes.
   - `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/flight_booker.rs`: `flight-one-way` and `flight-return` each gain `aria_pressed`,
     `"true"` on the active mode and `"false"` on the other; `flight-start` and `flight-return-date` each gain
     `aria_invalid`, `"true"` when the field's own validity flag is false (`start_valid`, `return_valid`, `:51-52`).
   - `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs`: `crud-list` gains `role: "listbox"`; each row gains `role: "option"` and
     `aria_selected`, `"true"` when it is the selected row and `"false"` otherwise. The row's `key` and `id` lines
     stay as they are (`:68-69`).
   - `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_diff.rs`: the three stated id sets are restated with the nodes each step now
     returns — the click on `flight-return` and the click back each name `flight-one-way`, `flight-return` and
     `flight-return-date` (`:124`, `:132`); the click on `crud-person-3` names `crud-person-3`, `crud-update` and
     `crud-delete` (`:198`) — and the `is_some_and` assertions beside them gain the new reading.

10. **Controls, one-shot, recorded in `evidence/controls.md`** — the red reading of steps 1 to 3 on the engine as
    built; then, with the code in place, one named mutation per new or extended test, each read red and restored
    (the file's bytes saved before the mutation and compared by sha256 after, `.claude/rules/testing.md`): each of
    the builder's three reads removed; each of the snapshot's three field reads replaced by its default; each of the
    three text tokens removed; each of the three JSON keys removed; `Toggled::Mixed` made to read `Some(true)`; the
    unrecognized-value arm of `aria-invalid` made to set nothing; one stand attribute removed per state.
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_states.rs` — the engine's reading of the three attributes on parsed HTML
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_states.rs` — the step that changes each state returns that node in its diff
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs` — the three reads in `build_accessibility_node` (step 4)
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs` — three fields, their reads and unit tests (step 5)
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs` — the tokens, the rustdoc, the token pins (step 6)
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs` — one unit test (step 7)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` — `NODE_FIELDS`, two help texts, their pins (step 8)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs` — the node's written form and its test (step 8)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` — one sentence of crate docs (step 8)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/flight_booker.rs` — four attributes (step 9)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs` — two roles and one state attribute (step 9)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_state.rs` — three tests (step 2)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_diff.rs` — three stated sets restated (step 9)

No entry is a live leg: every check boots what it reads in process, or starts and stops its own host, so there is no
liveness probe and no `stop` key. No boot path is edited — the `escher-session` binary's `main`, the windowed stand's
`main`, `seven_guis::stand` and the sink are untouched — so no boot smoke is listed beyond the standing hosted checks,
which run the binary and read what a call answers. The project has no headful self-verify harness; the stand's two
edited task files change no painted value, which the attributes-only entry holds. No dependency enters and no manifest
changes, which the preservation entry holds; the audit leg is therefore not listed. **Not run locally:** the MSRV
build and the windows, macos, ios and android matrix legs — the fork's CI run is their one witness, read after the
operator pass; neither new check file carries a `cfg(unix)` gate, so the windows and macos jobs run them.

`evidence/controls.md` has no listed producer, by construction: it is implement's record of step 10's one-shot
readings — the red readings on the engine as built, which no entry can re-produce once the tree has moved, and the
mutation controls, which mutate source and revert; what it records is asserted by listed entries (the two new check
files and the two extended ones, under both builds). Step 11's readings are the report's, taken from the listed
entries' logs and from one hosted `snapshot` per task driven by hand.

title: Measured first — each state seen absent on HEAD

data.head: ## Measured first — each state seen absent on HEAD

body: Taken through the stand's own binary, `target/debug/escher-session` built at HEAD `f0cb9dd7` (`cargo build -p seven_guis --bin escher-session --locked`), one command per run on a hosted session, 2026-10-10. Every snapshot answered exit 0.
| Reading | What the snapshot's text holds | Verdict |
| Flight booker, one-way (boot), 1269 bytes | `Button "one-way flight" id="flight-one-way" enabled @240,252 160x32` · `Button "return flight" id="flight-return" enabled @400,252 160x32` | — |

| Flight booker, after `click flight-return`, 1268 bytes | the same two lines, byte for byte | **the active mode reads nowhere**: the two mode-button lines are equal in both modes; the step's diff names `flight-return-date` alone |
| Flight booker, `type flight-start "next week"` | `TextInput "Departure date" id="flight-start" enabled value="next week" focused @239,297 322x36` | — |

| Flight booker, `type flight-start "24.12.2026"` | `TextInput "Departure date" id="flight-start" enabled value="24.12.2026" focused @239,297 322x36` | **invalid reads nowhere on the field**: the two lines differ in the value alone; the invalid step's diff names `flight-start` and `flight-book` (Book turning disabled — the side effect the first trial read) |
| CRUD at boot, 2034 bytes | `GenericContainer "Mustermann, Max" id="crud-person-1" @25,142.796875 367x29` (rows 0 and 2 alike; `crud-list` reads `GenericContainer ""`) | — |

| CRUD, after `click crud-person-1`, 2045 bytes | the three row lines, byte for byte | **the selected row reads nowhere**: the step's diff names `crud-name`, `crud-surname`, `crud-update`, `crud-delete` and no row |

The keys of every changed node in those answers were `bounds · enabled · focused · id · name · parent · role · value` — no key for any of the three states. The two boot sizes equal the figures architecture records (1269, 2034).

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs` (full, 281 lines) — `build_accessibility_node` (`:64-109`) sets, on an element node, the role (`role` attribute through `role_from_name`, else the element mapping, `:76-85`), the HTML tag, a label from a trimmed non-empty `aria-label` (`:88-94`) and the hidden flag from `aria-hidden == "true"` (`:96-99`). It writes no state property. The file holds no `cfg` line and no log site, so both builds compile one body. `role_from_name` maps `option` → `ListBoxOption`, `listbox` → `ListBox`, `button`, `radio`, `radiogroup`, `tab`, `tablist`, `row`, `gridcell` (`:127-189`); it holds no `switch`.

- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs` (full, 591 lines) — `NodeState` is four fields (`:46-60`), `Default`-derived; the reader builds it at `:140-147`, the one full literal: `enabled` and `checked` from the element, `focused` from the tree's focus. `tree_node` (an AccessKit `Node`) and `element` are both in hand at that site. 13 unit tests, built by `initial_build` then `resolve(0.0)`; an attribute the bridge never writes is set through `mutate().set_attribute` (`:518-528`).

- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs` (lines 1-200, 244-292) — `write_line` (`:48-76`) writes role, name, `id=`, then `enabled|disabled`, `checked|unchecked`, `value=`, `focused`, then bounds; the rustdoc of `to_text` states that order in prose and in an example (`:23-35`). Its tests build `NodeState` with `..NodeState::default()` or `..state()`, so a new defaulted field compiles into them unchanged; `state_tokens_follow_the_model` (`:142` on) pins the tokens one by one.

- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs` (lines 1-150) — a node is `changed` when `was.state != node.state` among five comparisons (`:76-81`); `DiffNode.state` is the whole `NodeState` (`:44`). Its tests build nodes with `NodeState::default()` (`:157`, `:236`).

- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/mutation_writer.rs` (`:14-42`, `:413-447`) — `BOOLEAN_ATTRIBUTES` is 27 names, none an `aria-*` name (`grep -n -i aria` over the file: 0 hits); a falsy value of a name outside the list is written by `set_attribute` as its text (`:439-445`). So `aria_pressed: false` reaches the DOM as `aria-pressed="false"`. The `set_attribute` trace site (`:421`) prints the attribute's name and value at debug behind the crate's `tracing` feature.

- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/actionable.rs` (`:1-120`) — the interactive role list holds `Button`, `ListBox` and `ListBoxOption`; an element is reported only when its id is a positional path (`:63`), so a keyed row or list that gains an interactive role is still not reported.

- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` (`:24-36`, `:192-235`, `:565-580`) — `NODE_FIELDS: [&str; 9]` = `id, parent, role, name, enabled, checked, value, focused, bounds` (`:33-35`), pinned word for word by a unit test (`:570-575`). The help of `changed` says "role, name, state, bounds or parent" (`:199-200`) and `snapshot`'s says "id, role, name, state and bounds" (`:221`): neither lists the state fields.

- `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs` (`:80-180`, `:404-462`) — `NodeParts` (`:94-105`) and `node` (`:109-137`) write a node's keys in `NODE_FIELDS`' order, an optional one left out when absent; `nodes` (`:152-173`) fills the parts from a `DiffNode`. `a_node_is_written_with_the_schema_fields_it_has` (`:412-446`) pins the full line, the bare line and `keys(&full) == NODE_FIELDS`.

- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/flight_booker.rs` (`:20-200`) — the two mode buttons (`:67-78`) are `button` elements with `id`, a class switched on `is_return`, and `onclick`; the two date inputs (`:80-94`) carry `aria_label` and a class switched on `start_valid` / `return_valid`. `return_valid` is true whenever the flight is one-way (`:52`). The styles select `.type-btn-active` (`:167`) and `.date-input.invalid` (`:193`).

- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs` (`:28-142`, `:183-200`) — a row is a `div` with `key: "{person.id}"`, `id: "crud-person-{person.id}"`, a class switched on `selected() == Some(i)` and `onclick` (`:67-79`), inside `div { id: "crud-list", class: "list" }` (`:57`). `selected` is an index into `people`, cleared by a filter edit (`:49`) and by Delete (`:135`). The style selects `.list-item.selected` (`:196`).
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/cells.rs` (`:350-393`, by grep) — a cell's class switches on `is_selected` (`:375`); Cells is not one of the four tasks `seven_guis::stand` boots.

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs` (full) — `controls(task)` lists the 15 controls with their roles; the CRUD rows and `crud-list` are in neither `controls` nor `INPUT_NAMES`, and `rendered(Crud)` lists `crud-list` by id only. A role on the rows or the list moves no row of these tables.

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_diff.rs` (`:100-225`) — states each step's exact `[added, removed, changed]` id sets: `click flight-return` → changed `flight-return-date` (`:124`); `click flight-one-way` → the same (`:131-134`); `click crud-person-3` → changed `crud-update`, `crud-delete` (`:197-200`). **Three tables move** once a mode button reads pressed and a row reads selected.

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_diff.rs` (`:225-345`) — its CRUD and counter steps assert `added` / `removed` sets and `keeps_every_node`, and compare each diff with the file's own reading of the two snapshots; no assertion states the changed set of a flight choice or a row selection.

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_ids.rs` (`:20-270`) — 77 nodes, 70 accepted and 7 refused; of the 15 controls 8 change the screen at boot (`changes_at_boot`, `:36-43`: `flight-return` among them, `flight-one-way` not — "the choice already made"). An attribute alone adds or removes no node, and a click on the already active mode still changes nothing.

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_text.rs` (`:31-38`, `:98-100`, `:150-330`) — ceilings 1024 · 1536 · 1536 · 2304 per task; a token is matched whole (`holds`); `text_start.contains(" value={date:?} ")` (`:252`) needs a space after the value, which bounds or any later token gives.

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_state.rs` (`:1-140`) — the per-control state check v010-05 names: state read through `node(&harness.doc.snapshot(), id).state`, real input through `click` and `type_text`, `for incremental in [false, true]`, an in-file fixture where the lean tasks lack a case.

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_spans.rs` (`:596-626`, by grep) — pins the call count (27) and one `diff.changed.len() == 1` on the counter; no count on a flight or CRUD step that this chunk changes.

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_flight_booker.rs` (`:1-24`, by grep) — the non-colour invalid cue check reads the `invalid` class of `.date-input` and Book's `disabled`; seven check files select rows by `.list > .list-item`. The three classes stay.

- `examples/seven_guis/tests/flows/flight.sh` (`:29`, `:36`, `:54`) and `counter.sh` (`:36`) — glob patterns over the answer: `id=\"flight-start\" enabled value=\"01.01.2026\"` then `id=\"flight-book\" enabled` in the text; `"id":"flight-start",`…`"value":"next week",`…`"id":"flight-book",`…`"enabled":false,` in the JSON. A token or key written after `value` leaves all four matching; one written between `enabled` and `value` on `flight-start` breaks `:29`.

- `examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs` (`:119-258`, by grep) — asserts each answer's top-level keys against the schema's fields, not a node's keys. `examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs` (`:35-62`, by grep) reads its id and name needles from the CRUD screen it boots in process (at least 15 ids).
- `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh` (`:34`) — the `a11y` leg names three test targets.

- AccessKit 0.25.1 (the locked version, `Cargo.lock:22-23`), `src/lib.rs` in the cargo registry — `Node::is_selected() -> Option<bool>` / `set_selected(bool)` (`:2449`, by `bool_property_methods!`, `:1743-1747`), `toggled() -> Option<Toggled>` / `set_toggled` (`:2467`), `invalid() -> Option<Invalid>` / `set_invalid` (`:2457`); `Toggled { False, True, Mixed }` (`:486-490`), `Invalid { True, Grammar, Spelling }` (`:465-469`). Its own doc: "ARIA uses separate states for checked and pressed controls, while this property is interpreted based on the node's role" (`:2459-2466`) — **one property serves `aria-pressed` and `aria-checked`**. For `selected`: "The absence of this flag (as opposed to a `false` setting) means that the concept of 'selected' doesn't apply" (`:2438-2439`).

- web_atoms 0.3.0 (`Cargo.lock:9319-9320`), `local_names.txt` — `aria-checked` (`:69`), `aria-invalid` (`:89`), `aria-pressed` (`:102`), `aria-selected` (`:112`) are atoms, so `local_name!("aria-pressed")` compiles as `local_name!("aria-label")` does.

- dioxus-html 0.7.10, `src/attribute_groups.rs` — `aria_invalid` (`:1608`), `aria_checked` (`:1625`), `aria_pressed` (`:1652`), `aria_selected` (`:1661`) and `role` (`:338`) are global attributes an `rsx!` element takes.

title: The value grammars (WAI-ARIA 1.2, read at P3)

data.head: ## The value grammars (WAI-ARIA 1.2, read at P3)

body: - **`aria-pressed`** — used in role `button`; tristate: `false` "supports being pressed but is not currently pressed", `mixed`, `true`, `undefined` (default) "does not support being pressed". "If the attribute is not present, the button is not a toggle button."

- **`aria-selected`** — used in roles `gridcell`, `option`, `row`, `tab`; inherits into `columnheader`, `rowheader`, `treeitem`; `true` / `false` / `undefined` (default) "The element is not selectable."

- **`aria-invalid`** — used in roles `application`, `checkbox`, `combobox`, `gridcell`, `listbox`, `radiogroup`, `slider`, `spinbutton`, `textbox`, `tree`; inherits into `columnheader`, `rowheader`, `searchbox`, `switch`, `treegrid`; token: `grammar`, `false` (default), `spelling`, `true`. "Any value not recognized in the list of allowed values MUST be treated by user agents as if the value true had been provided. If the attribute is not present, or its value is false, or its value is an empty string, the default value of false applies." The page notes the state "is being deprecated as a global state in ARIA 1.2".
- **`aria-checked`** — used in roles `checkbox`, `menuitemcheckbox`, `option`, `radio`, `switch`; tristate.
- **Not stated by the page:** whether a state's value is compared case-sensitively (its one case sentence is about role names). No browser was measured.

- **What follows for the stand:** a `button` supports `aria-pressed`, a text `input` (role textbox) supports `aria-invalid`, and a `div` with no role supports neither `aria-selected` nor any of the three — a row needs a role from the list above for `aria-selected` to be valid markup.

data.head: ## Read at P4, after the answers

body: - `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:409-440` — the unit test `every_verb_states_its_help_its_arguments_and_a_result` holds three help strings word for word, among them the help of `snapshot`'s `text` (`:421`) and of `changed` (`:425`), and asserts that the five acting verbs share one `changed` help. **Working entry (verbatim):** Snapshot states — a snapshot reads which control is selected, pressed or invalid, and the stand's tasks state all three (v010-17)

**Epoch:** Epoch 5 — Agent surfaces (its first markerless entry) · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Freight on the entry:** three `CARRY:` blocks (1412, 1329 and 402 characters; `route.py pins`, trail in the run dir: 48 freight blocks on the markerless tail, 3 of them on line 77). No `BLOCKED-ON`, no `PREREQ`, no `WATCH`. Each block is folded below under "The carried freight". Two external inputs: the operator's directive given with the take-up (`inputs#I1`), which says who decides which fork, and the overseer's relay of the founder's ruling (`inputs#I2`); every other fact below is read from this repository, the route, or a public specification read at P3.

**Premise closure (P3):** every bullet tagged `[inferred]` at the take-up — one the working entry did not state, or a mechanism claim that arrived in the freight — was re-read against `research.md`: fourteen verified and their tags dropped, two corrected and tagged `[premise-corrected: …]`; two bullets were added from what P2 and P3 found (the three stated id sets that move; decision 7). A bullet with no tag is what the entry states or is verified.
A snapshot that reads three more states of a control — selected, pressed and invalid — from what the app states in its markup, proven on the stand.

- **The engine reads the three ARIA states.** The accessibility builder reads `aria-selected`, `aria-pressed` (or `aria-checked` for toggles) and `aria-invalid` — the option as it was read to the founder (`inputs#I2`). The change is made in the builder's own file, `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs` (CARRY 3).

- **A snapshot carries the three states.** A snapshot node's state today is four fields — `enabled`, `checked`, `value`, `focused` (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs:46-60`); the three join it.

- **The stand's tasks state all three.** The flight booker's two mode buttons, the CRUD's rows and the flight booker's two date inputs state their state in markup, where today a CSS class alone carries it.

- **Checks through real input, in both layout modes** (`incremental` false and true — CLAUDE.md §Critical Warnings): the active flight mode reads pressed and the other not, the selected CRUD row reads selected and no other row, an invalid date reads invalid and a valid one not; each reading follows the app's state when it changes, and the step that changes it returns that node in its diff (v010-17's acceptance, `matrix.py show --id v010-17`).

- **Measured first** — "so each state is seen absent before it is seen read" (CARRY 2). Taken at P3 on HEAD `f0cb9dd7` through the stand's own binary: the two mode-button lines read byte for byte the same in both flight modes; a start date's line differs between an invalid and a valid date in its value alone; the three row lines read the same before and after a row is selected, and that step's diff names no row (research.md §Measured first).

- **The text form carries them.** `Snapshot::to_text` writes a node's state as tokens in a fixed order — `enabled` or `disabled`, `checked` or `unchecked`, `value=`, `focused` (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs:48-76`); the text is what a `snapshot` call answers, so a state the model holds and the text does not write would not reach an agent. Every stand screen stays under its in-file ceiling and `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` with the new tokens (boot today: 1269 bytes of 1536 on the flight booker, 2034 of 2304 on the CRUD). Which tokens, and whether a false reading is written, is decision 3.

- **The diff needs no new rule to name such a node `changed`.** `Snapshot::diff` compares a node's whole `state` (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs:76-81`), and a `DiffNode` carries the whole `NodeState` (`:44`). What a diff calls `changed` is decision 4.

- `[premise-corrected: no help text of the schema lists the state fields — the help of changed says "state" (schema.rs:199-200) and snapshot's "id, role, name, state and bounds" (:221) — so none is restated for the model's growth]` **The driver's written form and its one table change with the model.** A diff node is written as JSON by `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs` (`NodeParts` `:94-105`, `node` `:109-137`, `nodes` `:152-173`), and the schema's table names those keys as the diff node's shape — `NODE_FIELDS`, nine words (`packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:33-35`; pinned at `:570-575` and by `json.rs:412-446`). CARRY 2: "a result shape the driver's schema states is changed in the one table (`escher_driver::VERBS`)". Two help texts are restated all the same, on the operator's answer (`inputs#I3`, `inputs#I4`): the help of `snapshot`'s `text` and the help of `changed` say the state words and the two limits of the boolean model, so an agent reads them from the tool.

- **The engine change reaches every document, and the platform tree.** The builder has one caller, `build_accessibility_tree`; that tree is the trait's default `accessibility_tree`, the Dioxus override's base, and what the shell hands the platform adapter (`packages/blitz-shell/src/accessibility.rs:45`, `packages/blitz-shell/src/application.rs:82`; research.md §Graph impact). A state set on the accessibility node is therefore read by the snapshot and, in a windowed build with `accessibility`, by the platform adapter. The file is upstream-owned merge surface (CARRY 3).

- **The stand's new attributes are a11y surface.** By WAI-ARIA 1.2, read at P3, `aria-pressed` is used in role `button`, `aria-invalid` in `textbox` among others, and `aria-selected` in `gridcell`, `option`, `row` and `tab`: the mode buttons and the date inputs support their attribute as they are, and a CRUD row — a `div` with no role — supports none. Which role each stand control takes is decision 2.

- **Three stated id sets move.** `stand_act_diff` states the changed set of a click on `flight-return`, of the click back on `flight-one-way` and of a click on a CRUD row (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_diff.rs:124`, `:132`, `:198`); each gains the node whose state the step changes and is restated with it, never loosened (research.md §Sweep records).
- **The claim** — the entry names v010-17. Read at P4 from the matrix, with its `requirement` line and every route line that names it; none is assumed here.

- **Not built here:** no MCP tool and no new verb, argument or refusal cause; no upstream pull request (CARRY 3); what a `changed` node says of *which* field differs (a `CARRY:` on "Self-description", line 81); whether a clickable row reads a role or an action as an affordance (a `CARRY:` on "Stand requirement sweep", line 96 — "if 'Snapshot states' gives the rows a role on its way, this CARRY is re-read against what that entry's report measured"); a range input's interaction (its own entry); any state beyond the three.

- **v010-05 stays verified as worded** — enabled, checked, value and focused (CARRY 1; the ledger note of v010-17). A fork that would change what `checked` reads for a native checkbox or radio is outside this chunk.

- **intent.md is not rewritten.** Intent §Out of this version sets "complete accessibility names and states beyond what the snapshot needs" in later versions (`escher-0.1.0/intent.md:76-79`); the founder's ruling widens the version by his own word, and it stands on the route and in the ledger note (CARRY 1).

No colour, style, element, wrapper or order changes.

- **The Cells task also marks a selection by class alone** (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/cells.rs:375`, `cell selected`). The entry and the ruling name the flight mode, the CRUD row and the date; Cells is not one of the four tasks the stand boots headlessly, so no check of this chunk could read it. - **The masters, CLAUDE.md, the a11y rule and the crate notes state the snapshot's state as four fields, the node's keys as nine and the builder as reading two ARIA attributes.** They are restated at the wrap, never by this phase.

- **The merge surface grows by design** — the route entry "Upstream sync ahead of polish and ship" carries the fork's merge surface in inherited files as CARRYs; this chunk's edit in `accessibility.rs` adds to it, and the wrap's route-resolve measures it.

- **Proven at the document level only.** Neither stand binary builds a platform adapter and the shell's refresh has no windowed witness on this host; nothing here claims that an assistive technology reads the three states.

Who decides is `inputs#I1`: "Technical forks of this entry are the operator own: ask them in your dialog and I answer — how the engine reads the three ARIA states, which roles the stand rows and mode buttons take, where a snapshot and its text form carry the states. The founder decision is only a boundary widening or a fork that changes what v010-17 says; put such forks whole in one file." Each is asked at P4, with its options made whole by research.

1. **How the engine reads the three states** — the builder writes AccessKit's `selected`, `toggled` and `invalid` on the node (AccessKit 0.25.1 offers all three; research.md §Files inspected); open are: whether the snapshot then reads them from that node or parses the element's attributes itself, as it reads `enabled` and `checked` today (`snapshot.rs:140-147`); whether an attribute is read on every element or only on a role WAI-ARIA lists for it; whether `aria-checked` is read here — AccessKit holds one `toggled` property for both `aria-pressed` and `aria-checked`, "interpreted based on the node's role"; and what `mixed`, `grammar` and `spelling` read as. The spec settles two readings and they are not asked: an `aria-invalid` value outside its list reads true, and an absent, `false` or empty one reads false (research.md §The value grammars). The operator's. **Answered (`inputs#I3`): an attribute is read on every element, by its value; `aria-checked` is not read in this chunk, and an ARIA checkbox's or switch's reading gets a CARRY on "Stand requirement sweep" at the wrap; the model is boolean — `grammar` and `spelling` read invalid and `mixed` reads not pressed, the accessibility node keeping AccessKit's full value — with the limit said in a text an agent is served and each reading pinned on a fixture. Leaned from the standing rule that the snapshot maps nothing the tree already reads (a11y-plan §7), and stated on the question that followed (`inputs#I4`): the snapshot reads the three from the accessibility node.**

2. **Which roles the stand rows and mode buttons take** — the mode buttons as toggle buttons (`aria-pressed` on the `button` they are) or as another pattern; the CRUD rows with a role that supports `aria-selected` and their list with the matching container role, or with none. v010-17's acceptance says "pressed" and "selected"; an option under which the stand's mode reads `checked` or `selected`, not pressed, changes what v010-17 says and is the founder's. The operator's otherwise. **Answered (`inputs#I3`): the rows take `role="option"` with `aria-selected`, `crud-list` takes `role="listbox"`, the mode buttons stay the buttons they are with `aria-pressed`, and the date inputs take `aria-invalid` — attributes only. A row stays unfocusable, so the stand then shows a listbox option no keyboard reaches: stated in the report and left to "Stand keyboard harness".**

3. **Where a snapshot and its text form carry the states** — the fields of `NodeState` and their types, the text tokens and their place in the line's order, whether a false reading is written, and the JSON keys of a diff node in the one table. One fact bounds the order: a token or key written after `value` leaves the two shell flows matching as they are, one written between `enabled` and `value` breaks `flight.sh:29` (research.md §Files inspected). The operator's. **Answered (`inputs#I4`): `selected` and `pressed` are `Option<bool>` and `invalid` is a plain flag, as the accessibility node holds them (it has no "valid" value). The text writes `selected` or `unselected`, `pressed` or `unpressed` where the node states one, and `invalid` only when true — all three after `value=` and before `focused`. A diff node's JSON leaves `selected` and `pressed` out when the node states neither and always writes `invalid`, as it does `focused`. The state words and the two limits are said in the help of `snapshot`'s `text` and of `changed`; a help per node key is pinned at the wrap on "Self-description".**

4. **What a diff calls `changed`** — "whether the three join the snapshot's text form and what a diff calls `changed` is decided at this entry's promotion" (CARRY 2). The diff already compares the whole state and v010-17's acceptance requires that the step returns the node; no new rule is needed. **Confirmed by the operator at the P5 review (`inputs#I5`): no new rule.**

5. `[premise-corrected: the security plan names the crossing by carriers — the snapshot's text and the diff — and holds no rule for a field added inside one; and the states have a second exit the take-up did not name, the platform accessibility adapter, a crossing ratified for ids, text runs, labels and accessible names]` **Whether the three states are inside the ratified crossings.** Two exits: the session socket and the command line, where the states travel inside the snapshot's text and the diff as closed words or bools; and the platform adapter, which a state written on the accessibility node reaches in a windowed build. Each earlier widening at either exit was ratified by the founder one by one (the security extract and its history). Both are written whole in one file for the founder, as `inputs#I1` directs: `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T16-12-10-phase/p4-founder-forks.md`. **How they stand (`inputs#I4`): the plan takes the recommended option of each — the readings travel inside the snapshot's text and the diff, and the builder writes the states on the node — and both are recorded as the operator's reading awaiting the founder's word, never as his. The operator brings both to him by dialog; his answers are discharged at this chunk's wrap if they are in by then, else in the batch at the Epoch 5 boundary. The chunk does not wait.**
6. **Whether Cells states its selected cell** — see Boundaries. **Leaned at P4 and confirmed at the P5 review (`inputs#I5`): untouched here; the question is owed a route owner at the wrap.**

7. **Whether the engine's new accessibility check joins the `a11y` CI leg** — raised at P2, where the a11y plan's extract and the test plan's each name the other as deciding it. The leg is three named test targets (`.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh:34`); a fourth is a CI-contract change with its own pins. **Leaned at P4 on the precedent of `accessibility_names`, which rides the workspace test leg, and confirmed at the P5 review (`inputs#I5`): the leg stays three files. The same word confirmed two more leans of the plan: a state's value is compared in lower case after trimming, and the snapshot reads the three states from the accessibility node.**
Each was folded as a hypothesis: the artifacts it names were re-read at the take-up, and a mechanism it states was re-derived at P3.

1. **CARRY — the founder's ruling and what it sets** (2026-10-10, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the overseer; taken up at the 2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit wrap, where the operator approved this entry's line, its place and v010-17 by question dialog). Asked whether the states a snapshot does not read belong in 0.1.0, with three options put to him whole, the founder chose their own chunk in 0.1.0, after "Scrolling-box bounds and hit" and ahead of "MCP surface". The option as it was read to him: the engine reads `aria-selected`, `aria-pressed` (or `aria-checked` for toggles) and `aria-invalid`, a snapshot carries the three states, the stand's tasks state them, and checks run in both layout modes. The reasoning put to him: his own frontends are escher's first real users, selection, toggles and validation are in any real interface, and MCP's tools and the served help then describe the full state set from the start. v010-05 stays verified as worded; the three states are v010-17's. *Re-read:* the relay (`inputs#I2`) — found, and it says what the block says; the ledger note of v010-17 — says the same; intent §Out of this version — found at `intent.md:76-79`.

The P3 measurement reads the same side effects in each step's diff.

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-10-upstream-sync-agent-surfaces: "Upstream sync ahead of agent surfaces"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-10-upstream-sync-agent-surfaces · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-10T01:08:00Z
- **Chunk start commit:** `09f479b8b2e61d997a84f115ec8c8802c47769fb` (HEAD at P4; every git-diff base below names it or a fixed upstream sha)
- **Upstream pin:** `7832c177ff272128154bac58afe56c2b9164b417` (inputs#I1, re-read at P3) · merge base `2335458530518cdf167c55ce635fae99323e0789`

Merge DioxusLabs/blitz `upstream/main` at `7832c177` — 61 commits, 72 files — into `build/escher-0.1.0` as a true merge with both parents kept, and prove our logic survived it (`escher-0.1.0/intent.md` §Principles, "Upstream stays in reach"). Unlike the two syncs before it, this one merges something: four files conflict, one of our own calls stops compiling in a file with no conflict, and upstream restructures both the test crate and the CI workflow our contracts name.

The merge takes upstream's dependency set whole (per architecture §Established Decisions [Dependency pinning]) and keeps the fork's CI shape whole (per architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD; test-plan §4). Two forks were put to the operator at P4 and are settled (§Constraints & rejected approaches): every blitz-tests file stays its own test target, and upstream's license check is kept as configuration but gates nothing yet.

The proof is counted, not read off an exit code: the workspace gate, the a11y leg and the agent-run contract each pass, every one of our test files is shown by name to have run, upstream's single-binary target is shown absent from every leg's build set, and fork CI is read green on a run left to settle (per test-plan §3 and §9; a11y-plan §9; security-plan §Dependency Security).

1. **Pre-merge reading (on `09f479b8`, before any merge).** Run `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh test` and write the per-target table — one row per `Running …` line with its `test result:` counts, and the totals from the count entry's `awk` — to `evidence/counts.md` with the sha and the date. The last recorded figures (154 result lines, 657 passed · 0 failed · 10 ignored, test-plan §9) describe this tree — no code path moved since they were taken (research.md) — but the per-target rows are what the post-merge attribution is read against, so they are taken, not copied.
2. **Confirm the pin.** `git rev-parse upstream/main` reads `7832c177ff272128154bac58afe56c2b9164b417`. If upstream has moved, merge the PIN anyway and record both shas in `evidence/merge.md`.

3. **Merge without committing.** `git merge --no-ff --no-commit 7832c177ff272128154bac58afe56c2b9164b417`. The merge stops on conflicts with `MERGE_HEAD` set; /implement never commits. `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` must list exactly `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `Cargo.toml`, `deny.toml` and `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml`. Any other conflicted path contradicts P3's trial merge: HALT, do not resolve it by hand.

4. **Resolve `Cargo.toml`.** Both sides of the one region stay: upstream's five ICU4X workspace entries, then our `[profile.dev]` stanza with `debug = "line-tables-only"`. Everything else in the merged file is taken as merged — upstream's Taffy rev `7d33901c` and `parley = { version = "0.12", … }`, our workspace members, path entries and `tracing-log`.

5. **Resolve `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml`** (the operator's decision, 2026-10-10).
   - The conflicted dev-dependency lines keep both sides: our `escher-telemetry` line, and upstream's `blitz-dom` line with the features `accessibility`, `autofocus`, `floats`, `system-fonts`, `text-transform-icu`.
   - Upstream's `autotests = false` line is removed, so every `.rs` file under `tests/` is a test target as today.
   - Upstream's `[[test]]` table for `all` is kept with one added key, `test = false`, so `tests/all.rs` stays in the tree byte-identical to upstream's and is built by no `cargo test`.
   - A comment above that table states the difference where the next sync will meet it: what upstream's two lines do (#1123), that the fork declines them and by whose decision, what breaks if a merge takes them (the `a11y` leg's three `--test` names, `agent-run.sh run {name}`, the per-target baseline, and upstream's own `all_test_files_are_included` on our unlisted files), and the name of the check that guards it (step 8).

6. **Resolve `deny.toml`.** One file holding our header comment, our `[graph]` (the six targets, `all-features = true`), our `[advisories]` with its one per-ID ignore, and upstream's `[licenses]` table verbatim. The header gains one sentence: the license table is upstream's and no leg runs it yet.

8. **Add the standing check** `.github/scripts/test_blitz_tests_targets.py` — one `unittest.TestCase`, `BlitzTestsTargetsTest`, with one test reading `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml` through `tomllib`: `[package]` does not set `autotests` to false; exactly one `[[test]]` table exists, named `all`, with `path = "tests/all.rs"` and `test = false`. Helpers carry no `test_` prefix (`.claude/rules/testing.md` Session Additions). The `ci-scripts` leg discovers it, so a later merge that takes upstream's two lines turns that leg red on the fork and locally.

9. **Fix the one dangling call.** In `BaseDocument::visible_region` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs:776-778`, the `unrounded_absolute_position` call site the code graph lists @ `scrolling.rs:777`) read the clipping box through upstream's replacement, `self.physical_unrounded_geometry(box_id)`: its position with the box's own scroll offset added back on each axis is the origin the old call returned, and its returned layout replaces the separate `unrounded_layout()` read for border, size and scrollbar. No other line of the function moves, and the signature its two callers use (`execute::in_view` @ `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:316`, `reader_holds_the_target` @ `tests/blitz-tests/tests/scroll_into_view_nested.rs:120`) is unchanged. This is the chunk's one known non-additive edit; it is named as such in the report.

10. **Read the lock.** `cargo metadata --locked` on the resolved tree. If it refuses the merged `Cargo.lock`, let cargo re-resolve once (`cargo metadata` without `--locked`), then compare the lock's `name`+`version`+`source` set with the trial merge's (research.md: upstream's set plus our three entries): equal → record the changed stanzas in `evidence/lock.md`; any version moved or name added → HALT for the operator. Never `cargo update`.
11. **Run the gate block** (`## Test Commands`) on the merged, uncommitted tree.

12. **On a red gate.**
    - A build, fmt, clippy or rustdoc red on merged code: the minimal edit to the named file, recorded as non-additive in the report and, where the file is outside research's two lists, in `chunks/2026-10-10-upstream-sync-agent-surfaces/scope-record.md`.
    - A stand or fixture check that reads a new NUMBER under the new pins (a bound, a snapshot's byte size, an accepted/refused count): do not edit the expectation. Re-run that check's file with `--no-fail-fast`, collect every moved reading across both layout modes into `evidence/moved-readings.md`, and soft-exit ONCE with that table for the operator's word. The table holds EVERY number that moved, old → new, each row with the entry or check it was read by, where it is stated, and its CAUSE as one of two words (the operator's direction at the P5 review, 2026-10-10): `upstream tests added` — a tally (result lines, passed, ignored, the CI-scripts count, a per-target count) that moved because the delta adds or changes a test, the upstream commit or file named, with no expectation of ours touched; or `our check reads differently` — an assertion of ours that meets a new value from the merged engine, the check, its row and the layout modes named. A row is classed by reading it, never by where it sits: a tally delta no upstream test accounts for is the second class. Only rows of the second class wait on the word. On the word, each such value is restated where it is stated once (the shared tables of `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`, or the check's own in-file table), never widened into a tolerance, and the stand's markup, ids, CSS, viewport and font stay untouched. With no row of the second class there is no stop, and the table is still written.
    - A red that would need one side of a coupled pin moved, a `cargo update`, a narrowed `a11y` leg, a widened sink allowlist or a log field: HALT for the operator.

14. **Record for later entries, in the report and not in code:** upstream rewrote the bounds reader the "Driver CLI" CARRY cites (`physical_unrounded_geometry` replaces `unrounded_absolute_position`, the node's own scroll offset still subtracted); upstream's Selection API, innerText getters and `writing-mode` feature exist and escher uses none; upstream's own CI now lints blitz-dom with a named feature set and installs packages with a bare `apt-get` after evicting a corrupt apt cache (#1114) — facts for "Quality gates" and for the folded watch.
- `.github/scripts/test_blitz_tests_targets.py` — the standing check of the blitz-tests manifest's target shape (step 8)
- `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-upstream-sync-agent-surfaces/evidence/` — the seven records of step 13

- Fourteen files arrive by the merge (research.md §New files to create): `tests/blitz-tests/tests/all.rs` and three new upstream test files, `docs/licensing.md`, two WPT CI scripts, the engine's `text_transform.rs` and two `writing_mode.rs`, the script crate's `selection.rs`, `inner_text.rs` and `tests/selection.rs`, the WPT runner's `test_variants.rs`
- `Cargo.toml` — step 4; consumers are every workspace crate
- `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml` — step 5
- `deny.toml` — step 6
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — step 7

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs` — step 9: `visible_region`'s one call, of the five call sites of `unrounded_absolute_position` (`document.rs:2257`, `:2307`, `:2347`, `node.rs:1588`, `scrolling.rs:777` — the first four rewritten or removed by upstream in the same delta)
- `Cargo.lock` — by merge; rewritten only under step 10's rule
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs` — only under step 12's second rule, on the operator's word

- The other 53 files change by the merge alone (research.md §Files to modify, each listed), our hunks in them kept as merged: the 15 changed-set marks of `mutator.rs`, the changed-set lines of `document.rs` and `window.rs`, the two rustdoc lines of `node.rs`, the one line of `layout/replaced.rs`

The gates below run in /implement P2 on the merged, uncommitted tree and again in the wrap's light gate on the committed merge. Their git bases are the chunk start commit `09f479b8` or the two fixed upstream shas, so they read the same after the operator's pre-CI commit.

- **Merge witness and guards** — the witness is green when the pin is `MERGE_HEAD` (before the operator's commit) or an ancestor of HEAD (after it). The probes after it read: no conflict marker left; our root-manifest entries kept; upstream's pin set taken; the lock resolving as committed with one skrifa; the workflow one line from its chunk-start text; the fork's own scripts, stand, driver, telemetry and bridge sources untouched; `deny.toml` holding both sides; the 15 changed-set marks; no caller of the removed method; and a fixed-sha census of upstream's delta.

- **The `test = false` reading is three entries, not a note** (the operator's direction): the workspace build set lists no `tests/all.rs` executable, the workspace test log runs none, and the a11y leg's log runs none. The `coverage` leg selects the same default targets as the `test` leg and is not run locally; its witness is fork CI's "Coverage report" job, where a built `all` target would run upstream's guard test, fail on our unlisted files and redden the job.

- **By-name presence** — one entry walks `tests/blitz-tests/tests/*.rs` and counts the files, `all.rs` aside, whose `Running tests/{name}.rs` line is absent from the workspace test log. Named limit: a stem another package's test target shares would satisfy it from that package; none does today (the other packages' targets are `host_binary`, `host_log`, `dom`, `selection`).

- **Counts** — the workspace tally is asserted on `failed 0` and recorded; the CI-scripts tally is report-only because its number is a forecast (70 today; predicted 78 — four tests of upstream's new file, three more in `test_wpt_diff_to_pr.py`, one of ours); the a11y leg's 3 result lines and 15 passed are asserted, since the merge changes none of its three files.

- **Not run locally:** `msrv` (`cargo +1.91`) and the wasm leg — no 1.91 toolchain or wasm32 target on this host — and the windows, macos, ios and android legs. The operator entries push the merge and read the run that covers them; the last entry reads that our checks ran in the macOS and Windows jobs, which a conclusion alone does not show.

- **Windowed boot smoke** — listed because the merge changes layout, text shaping and paint under `seven_guis_native`. It declares `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, turns `timeout`'s 124 into its own exit 0 (`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` Session Additions) and reads `not run — env unset` without a display.

- **No live leg**: nothing here drives a process the launch environment names. **The evidence records have no listed producer, by construction**: `merge.md`, `counts.md`, `lock.md`, `features.md`, `licenses.md`, `moved-readings.md` and `ci.md` are /implement's and the operator pass's hand records of what the entries read, and `counts.md`'s pre-merge half is step 1's one-shot reading on `09f479b8`, which no entry can re-run on the merged tree. No entry carries one of them as `artifact`.

- **The mechanism the test-shape decision rests on is measured, not assumed**: on cargo 1.99.0, in a scratch crate, a `[[test]]` table with `test = false` beside auto-discovered files left `cargo test` and `cargo test --no-run` building and running the other files only, `--test {name}` still selected each of them, and naming the switched-off target explicitly still built and ran it; under upstream's shape (`autotests = false`) the same crate listed `tests/all.rs` alone and `--test {name}` failed with `no test target named`. The three entries re-read it on the real crate.

title: The upstream delta (61 commits, 72 files, +5672 −876; inputs#I1)

data.head: ## The upstream delta (61 commits, 72 files, +5672 −876; inputs#I1)

body: - Dependency pins: Taffy bumped 17 times (to `7d33901c`, still a git `rev`), Parley to 0.12 — a registry version now, no longer a git `rev` — accesskit_unix 0.24 and accesskit_android 0.9, comrak 0.56, libc pinned to 0.2.189, one `cargo update`. `Cargo.lock` moves by 988 lines.

- Layout and style: vertical `writing-mode`s behind a new `writing-mode` feature, three `text-transform` values, the Taffy tree trait impls moved from `BaseDocument` onto `LayoutPassState` (#1099), abspos inline roots, text-indent, percentage heights, offset dimensions, getComputedStyle used values, an `a` without `href` no longer styled as a link (#1134, the selector `a` → `a[href]`, its values unchanged), a bare `autofocus` attribute treated as enabled (#1085), a custom-widget tag override (#1081).
- Script: a JavaScript Selection API and innerText/outerText getters in blitz-vibey-script. Net: file URLs read through `Url::to_file_path`, a hintless `@font-face` source fetched.
- Tests and CI: the single test binary, the CI job changes above, a cargo-deny license table in `deny.toml` with `docs/licensing.md` (#1089), WPT runner and reporting changes.

- **Overlap**, files both sides changed since the base, 16: the four conflicted files, `Cargo.lock`, `apps/browser/Cargo.toml`, `packages/dioxus-native/Cargo.toml`, `packages/dioxus-native-dom/Cargo.toml`, the three upstream-only workflows (`publish-browser.yml`, `wpt.yml`, `wpt-post-results.yml`), and four engine sources — `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs`, `layout/replaced.rs`, `mutator.rs`, `node/node.rs` — plus `packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs` (inputs#I1). The engine sources carry escher's change tracking, the changed set and the shell's refresh; in the trial merge the changed-set lines read the same count as at HEAD in each (15 in `mutator.rs`, 37 in `document.rs`, 3 in `window.rs`), and the three upstream-only workflows keep every repository guard (research.md).

- **Coupled dependency pins** (CLAUDE.md Critical Warnings): the merge takes upstream's pins as one set — the Taffy rev, Parley 0.12 with its skrifa/vello coupling, the accesskit family. A pin that does not resolve as a set is a halt, never a one-sided fix. In the trial merge's lock skrifa stays one version, 0.44.0, beside parley and fontique 0.12.0 and vello 0.11.0, and the core `accesskit` moves 0.25.0 → 0.25.1. Still a hypothesis, /implement's to read: Parley 0.12 and the Taffy bumps move text metrics, so a stand check that asserts exact bounds or a snapshot's byte size may read a new value (not measured); a moved number is re-measured and recorded, never loosened to pass.

- **Engine behaviour our checks rest on.** `[premise-corrected: of the three take-up hypotheses one is measured, one is false for the stand and one is narrowed. Measured: upstream removes `Node::unrounded_absolute_position` (replaced by the crate-private `BaseDocument::physical_unrounded_geometry`), the one function name the delta removes outright, and our `visible_region` calls it (`packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs:777`). False for the stand: no stand source and no stand check carries an `autofocus` attribute (`grep -rn -l autofocus` over `examples/seven_guis`, `tests/blitz-tests/tests`, `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src`, `packages/escher-driver`: `dioxus_falsy_boolean_attrs.rs` and `mutation_writer.rs` only, the bridge's falsy clear), so #1085 moves no boot focus there. Narrowed: the accesskit bumps are the two platform adapters and a patch of the core crate (0.25.0 → 0.25.1); whether `set_author_id` / `author_id` still compile and read the same is /implement's reading.]` The a11y target (WCAG SC 2.1.1 · 1.4.3 · 2.4.3) is surface here: focus order and accessibility-tree identity are re-proven by their standing checks.

- **A new engine feature reaches the workspace build.** The WPT runner, a workspace member, turns `blitz-dom/writing-mode` on at `7832c177`; no other manifest of the default build does (`git grep writing-mode 7832c177 -- '*.toml'`). Hypothesis, from cargo's feature unification and not measured: `cargo test --workspace` builds blitz-dom with the writing-mode layout path compiled in while `cargo test -p blitz-tests` does not — the same by-runner split test-plan §9 records for `tracing`. The merge is proven under both.

- **`Cargo.lock`**: the textually merged lock carries no conflict marker and its package set is exactly upstream's set plus our three entries (research.md); whether it resolves under `--locked` cannot be read until the conflicted manifests are resolved, and is /implement's first reading. Builds stay `--locked`. Six crate names enter the graph and two leave, so the dependency audit (`bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh audit`) runs and the six are reviewed by hand; an advisory the audit fires on is fixed or ignored by ID with a reason (security rules §Dependencies).

- **`deny.toml`**: both sides created the file since the base — ours the six-platform `[graph]` and `[advisories]`, upstream a `[graph]` and a `[licenses]` allow list (#1089). The resolution keeps every advisory rule of ours; whether the license check runs in our CI is the operator's decision at the plan. **Decided at P4** (the operator, 2026-10-10, by question dialog): no gate yet — the table is kept, upstream's CI job is not taken, one `cargo deny check licenses` reading goes into evidence, and the gate question goes to the route's "Quality gates" entry at the wrap.
- **MSRV** stays 1.91: upstream's root `Cargo.toml` delta carries no `rust-version` line (inputs#I1); whether the updated dependencies still build on 1.91 is the MSRV job's reading.

- **Additivity**: the merge introduces no new edit by us to upstream-owned code beyond what a conflict or a gate failure requires; each such edit is named, minimal and recorded as non-additive. One is known before the merge: the call in `visible_region` moves to upstream's replacement reader. Where staying additive would force contorted logic, the upstream code is changed directly and said so (intent §Principles).

- No new crate, port, env var or listener of ours, and none in upstream's delta: 0 bind or listen sites added, no workspace member added, and the one added `env!` reads `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` at compile time, a name the registry already holds (research.md). `architecture.md`'s `Upstream sync:` line moves to the new pin and merge commit at the wrap.
- Any agent-surface work (Driver CLI and the later Epoch 5 entries).
- Sending our changes upstream, including the widened `scroll_into_view` flagged upstreamable; bumping any dependency beyond upstream's own set; upstream's WPT conformance numbers.
- Adopting the new upstream APIs (the Selection API, innerText, vertical writing modes); the chunk records what later entries could use and uses none.

- The engine defects carried on "Driver CLI" (a scrolled box's bounds, the hit walk): the merge does not fix them. Upstream rewrites the reader the first one cites — the new `physical_unrounded_geometry` still subtracts a node's own scroll offset — so that entry's cited lines move, which is recorded for it.

- **CARRY — our merge surface in the inherited `dioxus_document.rs`.** Re-measured at take-up against the merge base `23354585` at HEAD `09f479b8`: `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs` carries 4 hunks of ours, 58 added and 0 removed (`+2` at line 18, `+34` at 185, `+18` at 296, `+4` at 467) — the figures the CARRY states, unmoved. Upstream's 72 changed files do not include this file (inputs#I1), so this sync meets none of the four hunks.

- **CARRY — our merge surface in the inherited `scrolling.rs`.** Re-measured the same way: `packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs` carries 6 hunks of ours, 157 added and 6 removed, and `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs` 3 hunks, 21 added and 1 removed — unmoved. `[premise-corrected: upstream changed neither file (inputs#I1), and the in-place edit of `scroll_into_view` meets no upstream edit — but the take-up reading that this surface meets nothing in this sync is false. Our reader `visible_region`, added in the same file, calls `Node::unrounded_absolute_position` at `scrolling.rs:777`, and upstream removes that method (`git diff 23354585 7832c177 -- packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs`; the code graph lists five call sites, four of them inside upstream's own rewrite). The driver takes a screenshot with no display: the whole screen of the held instance, or one element by its stable id.
It is the eleventh verb of the one table, `screenshot`, served in process, on the command line and over MCP. The image
is a PNG of what blitz-paint paints, rasterised on the CPU (`VelloCpuImageRenderer`), the path the screenshot example and
the pixel tests already use (research.md, Files inspected). This is v010-07, and with the same pixels on a repeated run
on the same host, v010-08 (intent §4).
The founder ruled both forks of this chunk (`inputs#I1`, `inputs#I2`):

- **Fork 1, In-band.** The PNG travels base64 inside the one JSON answer on the socket and the command line's stdout, and
  over MCP as a native `image` content block. There is no new carrier, no new exit and no path argument. The
  1,048,576-byte answer bounds stay, and an image past them ends `oversize` / `AnswerTooLarge`.

- **Fork 2, Engine masks.** blitz-paint draws a password input's characters as U+2022 for every document, so a typed
  password never leaves as pixels and the windowed app stops painting it in the clear. The caret and selection follow
  the bullets.

The raster hangs off the held instance in `blitz-test-harness`, which owns the document. The intent names the gap
there: "the harness has no screenshot" (intent §4). The driver encodes the PNG and its base64 by hand, as it writes
every answer. "Fails, never skips, without fonts" becomes a typed refusal: an instance whose document has no usable
font is refused `fonts-unavailable` with nothing painted. The checks never skip; they assert that text paints (scope,
premise-corrected at P3).

1. **Measure the password on a frame before any fix.** Write `tests/blitz-tests/tests/password_painted_masked.rs` (step
   4 states what it asserts) and run it on the untouched engine. Its masking test is expected to read red: the code read
   at P3 shows the typed characters painted (scope, CARRY 1). Record the red reading, and the control that a `text` input
   with two different values paints different pixels, in `evidence/controls.md`. If the masking test reads green on the
   untouched engine, stop and report: the premise of fork 2 is false.

2. **A reading of whether a document can paint text** — `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs`. Add a public, read-only
   method on `BaseDocument` answering whether its font context resolves at least one font family for the sans-serif
   generic. It reads the context's collection through fontique's `generic_families` (fontique 0.12.0, Cargo.lock:3319).
   It changes no state and no behaviour. On the stand's context it reads true. On a context built from bytes that do not
   decode as a font (`build_single_font_ctx` over 16 zero bytes, which registers no family, `packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs:143-156`)
   it reads false. Add a unit test of both readings.

3. **A password input paints masked** — `packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs`, `draw_text_input_text` (render.rs:890-945).
   For an `input` whose `type` is `password`, paint one U+2022 per character of the editor's text, in the input's own
   text style, in place of the editor's layout. Paint the caret and the selection at the positions of the bullets that
   stand for the same characters. Every other input paints as today. The editor, the DOM value, the snapshot and the
   accessibility tree are untouched: the snapshot still reads `MASKED_VALUE`. This holds for every document and every
   renderer that goes through blitz-paint (founder fork 2, `inputs#I1`, `inputs#I2`). If the bullet layout needs state
   kept between frames, it lives beside `TextInputData` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/text.rs:64-75`).

4. **The engine check** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/password_painted_masked.rs`, in both layout modes. It renders through
   `paint_scene` into `VelloCpuImageRenderer`, as `background_size.rs:43-47` does:
   - Two documents differ only in a `password` input's value, two strings of the same length with no shared character.
     They paint byte-identical RGBA.
   - The same two values in a `text` input paint different RGBA. This is the control: the check can see characters.
   - The password input's content box holds painted pixels that differ from its background, so the bullets are drawn.
   - A focused password input paints its caret: the box differs from the same input unfocused.

5. **The harness raster** — `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/screenshot.rs`, re-exported from `lib.rs`. Add
   `blitz-paint`, `anyrender` and `anyrender_vello_cpu` as `{ workspace = true }` dependencies in the harness manifest,
   blitz-paint with `default-features = false`. Do not add `anyrender_vello_cpu`'s `multithreading`.
   - `Harness` gains a screenshot of its document: the whole viewport, or a pixel rectangle of it, as width, height and
     RGBA8 bytes.
   - The raster resolves the document at the harness's own time and does not tick or pump. It fills the frame with
     opaque white, then runs `paint_scene` at the harness's scale and the viewport's device size.
   - A rectangle outside the viewport is clipped to it, and an empty rectangle is an error.
   - A document whose step-2 reading is false returns a typed error with nothing painted.
   - No path panics, prints or logs (obs-plan §4: the harness writes no record).

6. **The image's written form** — `packages/escher-driver/src/image.rs`.
   - Encode RGBA8 as a PNG through `png` (`{ workspace = true }` in the driver's manifest; png 0.18, Cargo.lock:6324),
     with no time or text chunk, so equal pixels give equal bytes.
   - Write the base64 of those bytes by hand: RFC 4648 §4, the standard alphabet with padding.
   - Unit tests: the RFC 4648 §10 vectors, and a PNG that decodes back to the same width, height and pixels (`png`'s
     decoder, in the test module only).
   - Neither function panics on any input.

7. **The table** — `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs`.
   - Add the `screenshot` row, `Level::Instance`, after `scroll`. Its help reads: the screen, or the element an id names,
     as a PNG image.
   - It takes one optional argument, `id` (`ArgKind::Id`), whose help says it names the element to crop to, as a
     snapshot lists it, and that the whole screen is taken without it.
   - Its result fields are `width` and `height` (`FieldKind::Count`, always) and `png` (`FieldKind::Png`, a new kind,
     always), each with help.
   - The help states the measured limits: an element shot is cropped to the part of its bounds that can be seen; and in a
     build that paints overlay scrollbars, a thumb painted within 0.7 s of a scroll fades by wall time
     (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/scrollbar.rs:12-26`).
   - Move every count pin of the table to eleven verbs, seven instance verbs and ten field kinds (research.md, Sweeps).

8. **The cause** — `packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs`. Add `Cause::FontsUnavailable`, named `fonts-unavailable`.
   Its meaning: the app this session holds has no font it can paint text with. Its remedy: boot the app with a font it
   can decode. It takes the last place in the refusal order and holds nothing of the call. The causes go from eight to
   nine (`CAUSES` and its pins).

9. **The command** — `packages/escher-driver/src/command.rs`.
   - `validate` turns a `screenshot` call into `Command::Screenshot` with an optional id, bounded as every id is.
   - A wrong-kind or extra argument is refused `malformed`.
   - The eight sites that stand `screenshot` as the unknown verb take another name no verb has (research.md, Sweeps):

    - Without an id, it shoots the whole viewport.
