body:
- (matrix) **`verification-matrix.json#v010-07`** — with no display present, the driver returns an image of the whole
  stand screen and an image cropped to one element addressed by its id. Concretely:
  - On each of the four lean tasks, in both layout modes, `screenshot` is accepted as a PNG of 800 × 600. It decodes to
    the harness's own raster of that state, and text paints inside `#task-title` (`stand_act_screenshot`).
  - `screenshot --id crud-list` on CRUD at boot is 369 × 420, the bounds rounded outward, and equals that rectangle of
    the whole-screen shot (`stand_act_screenshot`).
  - The same verb answers through the binary (status 0, one JSON line whose `png` decodes to 800 × 600 — `cli_commands`)
    and over MCP (an `image` block, then a `text` block — `stand_mcp_tools`, `mcp_server`).
  - Proved by `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test password_painted_masked --test stand_act_screenshot --test stand_screenshot_repeat --test stand_act_spans --test stand_mcp_tools --test stand_act_scroll --test stand_mcp_masked`,
    `cargo test -p seven_guis --locked --test cli_commands --test mcp_server --test host_log --test mcp_log`
    and the workspace entry of the same files. The answer's in-band form is founder fork 1, `inputs#I1`, `inputs#I2`.

- (matrix) **`verification-matrix.json#v010-08`** — two screenshots of the same stand state, taken in separate runs on
  the same host, are pixel-identical. Concretely:
  - Two child processes of `stand_screenshot_repeat` each shoot the four lean tasks whole, `crud-list`, the counter's
    value display, and the flight booker with a focused date input, in both layout modes.
  - The two children print byte-identical PNGs, so the pixels are identical, and each equals the parent's in-process
    shot. This holds under the per-package build and under the workspace build, whose renderer runs `multithreading`.
  - Proved by the same three entries.

- (security, a11y) A typed password never leaves as pixels:
  - On the engine, two equal-length password values paint byte-identical RGBA, while the same values in a text input
    differ, the bullets are drawn and the caret paints when focused (`password_painted_masked`).
  - Through the driver, two equal-length sentinels typed into a password fixture give byte-identical PNGs, while a text
    fixture's differ (`stand_act_screenshot`).
  - Both hold in both layout modes. The snapshot still reads `MASKED_VALUE` (per security-plan §Input Validation, the
    password row; a11y-plan §7). Engine mask: founder fork 2, `inputs#I1`, `inputs#I2`.

- (tests, design) The no-font case fails, and nothing skips. A stand instance with a font context holding no family is
  refused `fonts-unavailable` with nothing run and its next snapshot unchanged. The stand checks hold no skip path and
  assert that text paints (per test-plan §2, Font-dependent tests; design-system §Typography, Loading) —
  `stand_act_screenshot`, the blitz-dom unit test.

- (security) Every refusal holds nothing of the call: `not-found`, `stale` and `off-screen` on an element shot leave the
  instance unchanged; on the command line `--id` on an unread id exits 1 and writes back nothing typed; `fonts-unavailable`
  is a fixed text with its remedy (per security-plan §Input Validation, the Driver command schema and CLI arguments rows)
  — `stand_act_screenshot`, `cli_commands`. Neither `image.rs` nor the harness raster prints, panics or logs outside its
  tests, per the no-panic probe.

- (obs) An accepted `screenshot` leaves one `command` line with `verb=screenshot` and no new field; a refused one adds its
  cause; over MCP its `tool_call` line reads `tool=screenshot` and parents it. The host's and the `mcp` role's stderr at
  `trace` hold 0 ids, 0 names, 0 typed sentinels and 0 image bytes under both builds (per obs-plan §4; §8) —
  `stand_act_spans`, `stand_mcp_tools`, `host_log`, `mcp_log`.

- (a11y, layouts) A shot changes nothing: no change is marked, `focused` and the tree's focus read as before, the diff
  across it is empty, and no stand markup moves (per a11y-plan §2; layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary
  screens) — `stand_act_screenshot`, the outside-write-set probe.

- (design, layouts) `screenshot` is listed in table order on both surfaces, with `help` last. Its answer is one
  uncoloured line with no ESC byte, and no driver code asks whether a stream is a terminal (per design-system §Surface:
  cli; layout-templates §Surface: cli) — `cli_commands`, `mcp_server`, the terminal probe.

- (arch, security) No package enters `Cargo.lock`, the audit leg is green, and the driver's dependencies become five
  (`png` added), the harness's three more (per architecture §Established Decisions → Driver session; security-plan
  §Dependency Security) — the lock probe, the audit entry.

- (tests, matrix) The verified v010-13 and v010-14 stay proved at eleven verbs and nine causes. Every check their `ref`
  lists passes under its renamed or moved pin (step 12, step 17). `fonts-unavailable` is served with its remedy over MCP,
  so the binary's seven and MCP's eight cover the nine causes together. This is per their restated acceptances, recorded
  as the dated notes under Implementation notes — `cargo test -p escher-driver --locked`, the per-package and workspace
  entries of `stand_mcp_tools`, `mcp_server` and `cli_commands`.
- (tests) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` and `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` pass, and `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run stand` ends failed 0.

- Spec anchors: architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session, Headless stand, Paint and shell; §Established
  Decisions → Driver session, Renderer backends; §Occupied Resources; §Conventions → Manifests, Error handling, Tests ·
  security-plan §Input Validation (Driver command schema, CLI arguments, MCP server, password and file `input` value);
  §API Security; §Error Handling; §Logging & Monitoring; §Dependency Security · test-plan §2 (Font-dependent tests, Pixel
  tests); §3 Session lifecycle; §4; §5; §9 · obs-plan §3; §4; §8 · a11y-plan §1; §2; §6; §7 · design-system §Typography
  (Loading); §Color Palette; §Motion; §Surface: cli · layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native (Primary screens, IA
  notes); §Surface: cli.
- The founder's answers: `inputs#I1` (the relay as received), `inputs#I2` (the overseer's record).

- Research files inspected: listed in research.md; the decisive ones are `examples/screenshot.rs`,
  `packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs`, `packages/blitz-dom/src/{lib,document,util}.rs`,
  `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs`, `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs`.

- A file written by the driver, or an `--out` path: rejected by the founder at fork 1 (`inputs#I1`). No path argument,
  no filesystem exit.
- Refusing a shot while a password holds a value: rejected by the founder at fork 2 (`inputs#I1`). The engine masks.

- The raster inside `escher-driver`: rejected. The harness owns the document, and the intent names the harness's gap.
  The driver keeps one new dependency, the encoder.

- A caller-supplied raster hook, as `with_time` supplies time: rejected. Painting is the engine's and is the same for
  every app, while time is the app's own.

- The `base64` crate, or `serde_json` writing the answer: rejected. The crate's answers are hand-written (security-plan
  §Input Validation, MCP server row).

- A span field for the image's size or dimensions: rejected. arch's driver-command-spans entry never fields the screen
  or its length, and a new field would need a ruling this chunk has not asked for.
- A host-font fallback, or a skip, when no font paints: rejected (test-plan §2; design-system §Typography).

- Moving the scrollbar fade onto the harness clock: out of scope. It is an engine change for every document that the
  founder has not been asked for. The limit is stated in the verb's help, and its owner is on the card.
- Pixel comparison across the CI matrix: not written (v010-08 is "the same host").

- Order: the measurement (1) before the mask (3). The font reading (2) before the harness (5). The harness and the
  encoder (5, 6) before the table and the executor (7-10). The executor before the surfaces (11, 12) and the checks
  (13-18).

- Basis of the numbers:
  - 800 × 600 at scale 1.0 (`examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:42-47`).
  - `crud-list` (24, 112.796875, 369 × 419.203125), from layout-templates history 2026-10-07-refusal-detection and
    re-read by step 14. Rounded outward: x 24 → 393, y 112 → 532, so 369 × 420.
  - Eleven verbs, nine causes and the eight unknown-verb sites: research.md, Sweeps (the grep patterns there).
  - The 131 / 34 stand count: the 2026-10-12-self-description wrap (tests history).

- The base64 of an 800 × 600 PNG is predicted far under 1,048,576 bytes; a flat UI PNG compresses well, but this is not
  measured. Step 19 records the largest. If it passes the bound, the answer is `oversize` / `AnswerTooLarge`, per fork 1.

- The masked paint's caret placement follows the bullets. Pointer placement inside a password field still maps through
  the editor's own text geometry (`render.rs:890-945`). That is unmeasured, and implement reads it and records what it
  finds.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session — eleven verbs, seven instance verbs;
  `screenshot` with its optional `id`, its fields `width`, `height` and `png`; `FieldKind::Png`; nine causes,
  `fonts-unavailable`; `Outcome::Shot`; the MCP image block. Also → Test harness: `Harness`'s screenshot.
  Also → Paint and shell: a password input paints masked.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Established Decisions → Driver session — the image crosses in-band on the
  socket, the command line's stdout and the MCP stdio. Pattern «Boundary widening», answered by the founder's own word,
  relayed verbatim by the overseer (fork 1, `inputs#I1`, `inputs#I2`), whose own answer makes the wrap halt on it once,
  as the answer card. The driver's dependencies are five, the harness's raster three.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Established Decisions — a password input paints masked in every document,
  an engine behaviour change ruled by the founder (fork 2, `inputs#I1`, `inputs#I2`).

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Existing Scopes — escher-driver's modules thirteen → fourteen (`image`);
  blitz-tests gains three files.

- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan §Input Validation — the Driver command schema row (eleven verbs, nine
  causes); the CLI arguments row (`screenshot`); the MCP server row (the image block); the password row (painted

  fresh `VelloCpuImageRenderer` yields the same RGBA bytes — holds on everything this research read: no paint input reads
  a clock except scrollbar opacity (`document.rs:1782-1793`, wall clock since the last scroll activity, painted only under
  the `scrollbars` feature) and the caret is static (`render.rs:927-940`). NOT measured: run-to-run identity of the CPU
  renderer itself, single-threaded (per-package build) and with `multithreading` (the root package's dev-dependency,
  `Cargo.toml:274`, unified into a `--workspace` build) — the plan's determinism check is that measurement, under both
  builds.

  text (`construct.rs:449-455`, `873-882`; `render.rs:890-945`) — code read at HEAD, not a frame. The plan measures it on a
  frame before any fix.

     given to `help` is refused `malformed`, `Fault::Unnamed`.
   - `validate` is unchanged: it admits `Level::Instance` alone (command.rs:200), so it refuses `help` `unknown-verb`,
     as it refuses `start`. `Session::run` therefore runs no `help`, and its command span records the table's word
     `help`, as for a session verb (execute.rs:113-115).
   - The command table test reads ten rows: six instance, three session and one tool (command.rs:789-797).

7. **The command line answers `help`** — `packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs`:
   - The reader takes `help`, with no word after it but at most one `--session <dir>`, which it does not read. The
     answer is `describe()`'s line on stdout with the accepted status. A word the schema does not name ends refused
     `malformed`, status 1, as for every verb.
   - The usage line lists `help` with the other verbs.
   - The four status constants are read from `EXIT_STATUSES`; no status number is a literal of the module but in its
     tests.
   - `command_line`'s doc comment names `help`.
   - Unit rows:
     - `help` and `help --session d` read as `help`;
     - `help x` reads as refused `malformed`;
     - `help --session` with no directory, or with it given twice, reads as usage;
     - the usage line names `help`;
     - the endings' statuses equal `EXIT_STATUSES`.

8. **The MCP server serves the same** — `packages/escher-driver/src/mcp.rs`:
   - **Revisions.** `PROTOCOL_VERSIONS` gains `2025-11-25`, the newest. It is answered to any revision the server does
     not speak, `2026-07-28` included (`inputs#I2`, Q1). The tools' argument schemas use `type`, `properties`,
     `required`, `additionalProperties`, `enum`, `minimum` and `maximum` only (mcp.rs:343-390). These read the same in
     the JSON Schema 2020-12 dialect that `2025-11-25` makes the default. That is read from the keywords, not measured
     by a validator, and the plan states the reading (Q1's note).
   - **`help` tool.** `tools/list` lists ten tools, `help` last. A `help` tool call is answered by the server itself,
     whether or not it holds a session: its text block is `describe()`'s line, accepted. Its `tool_call` span's `tool` is `help`, and it leaves no
     `command` child.
   - **Descriptions.** A tool's `description` becomes the verb's help, then `Returns:` and each result field as
     `{name} ({kind}): {help}`, joined by `; `, all read from the table's `FieldSpec`s (`inputs#I2`, Q4). The
     listing's byte size before and after is measured and written in `evidence/counts.md` (Q4's note).
   - **Unit tests:**
     - the listing is the ten verbs;
     - each description holds each of its fields' help;
     - the revision table gains its rows (`2025-11-25` → itself; `2026-07-28` and `2099-01-01` → `2025-11-25`);
     - `help` answers the document with `isError` false.
   - The four methods answered stay four, so `server/discover` still reads `-32601` (founder fork 4A).

9. **A changed node names what differs** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs`:
   - `DiffNode` gains `differs`: the list of what differs, in node-key order, from a closed enum of the eleven readings
     the diff compares: parent, role, name, enabled, checked, value, selected, pressed, invalid, focused, bounds. The
     enum is re-exported from `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs`.
   - `Snapshot::diff` fills it at the one site that decides `changed` (snapshot_diff.rs:73-79). An added node's list is
     empty.
   - Its unit test reads a bounds-only change as `[bounds]`, and a value and focus change as `[value, focused]`.
   - This is a closed-word field inside the ratified diff, under the founder's rule (`.andromeda/playbook.md:40-42`;
     `inputs#I2`, Q2).

10. **The written forms** — `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs`:
    - **Session errors.** `SessionError::to_json` writes `{"error":{"kind","message","remedy"}}`, the remedy from
      step 3's table (conditional, as step 3).
    - **Changed nodes.** A changed node is written with `differs` after `bounds`, its words the node-key names of step
      2. An added node is written without it.
    - **Pins.** The pin at cli.rs:739 and the json unit tests that write a session error or a changed node are
      restated. `examples/seven_guis/tests/flows/counter.sh:79` matches by prefix and is not edited (research.md,
      Sweeps).

11. **The crate's face** — `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs`:
    - re-exports `describe`, `EXIT_STATUSES` with its row type, and the node-key row type. The count read before and
      after is written in `evidence/counts.md`, against 41.
    - The crate doc says there are ten verbs in three levels and that the tool describes itself through `help`.
    - The stated limits are the boolean model's, now in the node keys' help, and the `contain: paint` reading.

12. **Checks through the binary** — `examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs`:
    - **`help`.** `escher-session help` ends `0` with one line of JSON on stdout, equal to `escher_driver::describe()`,
      no ESC byte, and stderr empty with `RUST_LOG` unset.
    - **Remedies.** Every refusal the file provokes reads a `remedy` equal to its cause's `Cause::remedy()`: the seven
      causes the binary reaches, all but `covered`.
    - **Session errors.** The `no-session` error reads a `remedy` equal to the table's.
    - **Linux bound** (`cfg(target_os = "linux")`). A state directory whose path, as given, is 94 bytes starts and
      stops a session. One of 95 bytes ends `state-dir-too-long`, status 3, its message naming 94 and its remedy the
      table's. If the absolute prefix would pass the bound, the path is given relative to the child's working
      directory, under the target directory.
    - The `VERBS.len() == 9` pin (cli_commands.rs:100) reads 10.

14. **Checks in process** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_mcp_tools.rs`:
    - **Remedies.** Every cause reachable through MCP is read on its served form, `serve_mcp` booting the lean tasks,
      in both layout modes. Each result's `remedy` must equal `Cause::remedy()`. The seven are `malformed`,
      `not-found`, `stale`, `disabled`, `off-screen`, `time-unavailable`, and `covered` on an overlay fixture defined
      in-file, the shape of `stand_act_obstructed`'s. Over MCP an unknown tool is a protocol error, so `unknown-verb`
      is read through the binary (step 12).
    - **`help` span.** The `help` tool's `tool_call` span holds `tool` = `help` and `ending` = `accepted`, with no
      `command` child.
    - The union of steps 12 and 14 covers the eight causes.

15. **The password over MCP** — new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_mcp_masked.rs` (CARRY 7):
    - `serve_mcp` in process boots a password fixture defined in-file, the shape of `stand_act_filled`'s
      `password_fixture()`, held by `Session::start` with the stand's options. The run is `start`, a `type` of a
      synthetic sentinel into the password input, then a `snapshot`, in both layout modes.
    - The sentinel occurs 0 times in both results' text. The `type` result's changed node reads `MASKED_VALUE` as its
      value, as does the snapshot's line for the input. The input reads role `PasswordInput` with a non-empty name.
    - A failure message names a layout mode and a call index only (test-plan §4).

16. **The diff reading on the stand** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_diff.rs`: on the flight booker, a click on
    `flight-book` answers one added node and eight changed, each reading `differs` = `[bounds]`, in both layout modes.
    This is the P3 measurement made a check. One existing value step reads `[value]` on its node.

17. **One more pin** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_scroll.rs:505`: `VERBS.len() == 9` reads 10. The sixth verb
    is still `scroll`, named by the `off-screen` remedy.

18. **The front page** — `README.md:48`: the help the driver serves about itself is built. It says how to ask for it on
    the command line (`escher-session help`) and through MCP (the `help` tool). The screenshot is still to come.
- `packages/escher-driver/src/describe.rs` — the self-description document, written from the table
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_mcp_masked.rs` — a password typed through MCP reads the mask
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` — `Level::Tool`, two field kinds, `help`, node keys with help, `EXIT_STATUSES`
- `packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs` — the session errors' table, remedies, the stated bound
- `packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs` — `Covered`'s doc comment
- `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs` — the session error's remedy; a changed node's `differs`
- `packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs` — `help`; statuses from the table
- `packages/escher-driver/src/mcp.rs` — `2025-11-25`; the `help` tool; descriptions with result fields
- `packages/escher-driver/src/command.rs` — `validate_session` takes `help`
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` — re-exports and crate doc
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs` — `DiffNode::differs`
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs` — its re-export
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_diff.rs` — the Book step's `differs`
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_scroll.rs` — the verb count
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_mcp_tools.rs` — remedies and `help` over MCP
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs` — `help`, remedies, the Linux bound
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/mcp_server.rs` — the listing, the revision, `help` equal across surfaces
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/common/mod.rs` — a shared reader, only if two checks need one
- `README.md` — the front page

`VERBS` impact (research.md, Graph impact): `cli.rs` 3, `command.rs` 2, `mcp.rs` 5, `schema.rs` 9, and outside the
crate `cli_commands.rs:100`, `mcp_server.rs:120`, `stand_act_scroll.rs:505`, `stand_act_spans.rs:391`. The last reads
instance rows only and is not edited, nor is `execute.rs:446`'s test, which reads argument names (`help` adds none).

No entry is a live leg. Nothing is driven against an external process; the only processes are the stand's binary,
which the checks spawn and reap themselves. The binary's boot path changes (a new answer, no boot), so its smoke is the
`role = 'smoke'` entry: the built binary answering `help`. The project has no headful self-verify harness, and nothing
painted changes. No dependency changes, so the audit leg is not listed; the lock probe proves the lock untouched.

**Not run locally:** the MSRV build and the windows, macos, ios and android legs; the fork's CI run is their witness.
The macOS figure of the state-directory bound is read, not measured: the Linux check is `cfg(target_os = "linux")`.

`evidence/controls.md` (step 1) and `evidence/counts.md` (step 19) have no listed producer by construction. They are
/implement's records of one-shot readings, asserted by the listed entries.

data.head: ## The carried freight (eight CARRY blocks, folded)

body:
1. **What is served is built, the serving is not** (from 2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema; the operator, 2026-10-07, at that chunk's P4 forks). The one schema is `VERBS`, the key list and `CAUSES`. v010-14 was not claimed there; its requirement needs both serving surfaces. "A `help` verb joins the table at this entry's promotion; no text is restated outside the table." The measured cost of unserved help (the first live agent trial, 2026-10-10, relayed by the overseer — a fresh agent given only the `escher-session` binary of `177d1652`): the agent inferred `settled`, `served`, `idle_expiry_s`, that `type` replaces, and the four exit statuses.
   - The first four have help in the table today, unserved; the exit statuses' meanings stand in no text of the table (read in `schema.rs` at the 0-pending wrap of 2026-10-10) — "the help served here covers them".
   - `[premise-corrected: the constants stand at cli.rs:21-27 and the meanings at cli.rs:60-71, not :25, :743 and :67]` The exit statuses are four private `cli.rs` constants, `ACCEPTED` · `REFUSED` · `USAGE` · `SESSION_ERROR` = 0 · 1 · 2 · 3 (`cli.rs:21-27`, pinned at `cli.rs:743`). Their meanings are stated only in `command_line`'s doc comment (`cli.rs:60-71`). Serving them from the one schema puts the meanings in the table.

2. **Whether the actionable-key check becomes a command** (from 2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits, moved on by 2026-10-10-driver-cli; the founder's answer, 2026-10-10, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the overseer — not in the Driver CLI chunk, carried here). `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable()` is a public library function no driver, CLI or MCP command exposes; if a command exposes it, its output is a new crossing for stable ids (security-plan §Input Validation, the `id` row), and it leaves `UnkeyedActionable.node`, a process-local `NodeId`, behind. A command that exposes it widens a boundary: the founder's fork (`inputs#I1`).

3. **What a session error does not say** (the operator's direction, 2026-10-10, as the arguments of the 2026-10-10-driver-cli wrap). A refusal carries its cause's meaning and remedy; a session error carries a `kind` and a fixed message and no remedy (`{"error":{"kind","message"}}`), and `state-dir-too-long` states no bound though a socket address leaves about a hundred bytes for the whole path. What the driver's help says of the thirteen session errors, and whether they gain remedies or a stated bound, is decided at this promotion. Measured cost (the first live agent trial, 2026-10-10, relayed by the overseer): `state-dir-too-long` on an absolute `--session` path caused 3 of the trial's 3 unintended failures in 49 calls; the agent got past it by guessing a relative path.
   - The thirteen are `SessionError`'s variants, each with a `kind` word (`packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs:12-60`).
     - `StateDirTooLong` is `std` refusing `{dir}/session.sock` as `InvalidInput`, on connect (`client.rs:243`) or on bind (`host.rs:130`).
     - The platform's `sun_path` is 108 bytes on Linux and 104 on macOS, NUL included, so a state directory of at most 94 bytes fits on Linux and 90 on macOS.
     - The path is used as given, so a relative path counts its own bytes, which is why the trial's relative path worked. Read, not run at the edge (research.md, Measured at P3).

4. **What a `changed` node does not say** (from the first live agent trial, 2026-10-10, relayed by the overseer; the operator's placement at the 0-pending wrap of that day). One `click` on the flight booker's Book answered 8 `changed` nodes and 1 `added`; by the agent's report the eight had only moved. A node is `changed` when its role, name, state, bounds or parent differs and is written as it reads after the step, naming no field that differs (`Snapshot::diff` and the driver's `json` module, read at that wrap), so a move and a change of state read alike to a caller holding no earlier snapshot. What the help of `changed` tells an agent, and whether a changed node names what differs, is decided here; a result shape that changes is changed in the one table.
   - The freight's hypothesis: "the eight moved because the task's card is centred and the booked line is added inside it (read from the task's CSS, not measured)". **Measured at P3 and holds.** Through the built `escher-session` binary on a fresh flight booker, `click --id flight-book` answered 1 added and 8 changed. Comparing snapshots before and after, each of the eight reads equal except for its bounds: each moved up 27 px, and the card's container grew 54 px (research.md, Measured at P3). It is not the reading "Scrolling-box bounds and hit" owns, since the flight booker holds no scrolling box.

5. **A help per node key** (from 2026-10-10-snapshot-states; the operator, 2026-10-10, by question dialog at that chunk's plan forks: not built there, pinned here). `NODE_FIELDS` is a list of twelve names with no help of its own; what `selected`, `pressed` and `invalid` mean, and the two limits of the boolean model — a mixed toggle reads not pressed, a grammar or spelling error reads invalid — are said only in the help of two result fields (`changed`, `snapshot`'s `text`) and in the crate docs (`schema.rs`, `lib.rs`). Whether the served schema gives each node key its own help, and the table its shape for it, is decided here.

6. **The current MCP revision** (from 2026-10-10-mcp-surface; the operator's answer at that chunk's P4 — pin it on the route with what the host client actually sends, measured first — placed here by the wrap: this entry serves what the server says about itself). The server speaks `2025-06-18` · `2025-03-26` · `2024-11-05` only (any other asked → `2025-06-18`) and answers `-32601` to every method but `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`; the current revision is `2026-07-28` (per-request `_meta`, `server/discover`; read from the specification pages on 2026-10-10, not re-fetched). Measured at that chunk's live trial (`claude` 2.1.296, `chunks/2026-10-10-mcp-surface/evidence/live-trial.md`): the client's first request was `server/discover`, answered `-32601`, then `initialize` asking `2025-11-25`, answered `2025-06-18`, and the client went on. Whether the server takes up `2025-11-25` or the current revision and answers `server/discover` with what it serves about itself is decided here.

     - The specification was re-read at P3 (research.md, Platform issues consulted). `2025-11-25` changes nothing in `initialize`, `tools/list` or `tools/call` that this server misses.

- **Marker:** 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-13T20:15Z

Give the engine a minimal range interaction model for every document with an `input type="range"`, as the founder
ruled on 2026-10-07 («Пусть будет а», relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option label; the English wording,
"a minimal range interaction model in the engine", is the overseer's). The model has four parts:
- The arrow keys step a focused range input by its `step`: right and up add one step, left and down take one away.
- Home goes to the minimum and End to the maximum.
- A pointer click sets the value by where it lands along the track, and the click focuses the control.
- Every change of value fires an `input` event, so an app's `oninput` runs with the new value.

The founder answered the three P4 forks himself (inputs#I2, inputs#I3; relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen
option labels, the English wording the overseer's):

- Q1 «Отдельное текущее значение»: the moved value is held as the control's own current value, apart from its `value`
  attribute (the default value).
- Q2 «Стрелки + Home/End (Рекомендую)»: all four arrows plus Home/End step the value.
- Q3 «Клик даёт фокус (Рекомендую)»: a click focuses the control.
Q1 was not the plan's recommendation, so the plan takes on its stated costs:
- a new `SpecialElementData` variant, a public type change (architecture §Standard Contracts → Nodes and widgets);
- construction seeds the value (`construct.rs`);

- a `value` attribute write re-seeds it, the reset a Dioxus re-render needs (the text input's precedent,
  `mutator.rs:359-368`);
- the snapshot and the form entry list read the current value;
- a larger upstream merge surface.

Today no key or click moves a range input. A key acts only on a focused node holding text-input data
(`events/keyboard.rs:68-100`). `handle_click` has no range arm, so a click on the slider matches nothing and clears
focus (`events/pointer.rs:614-817`). This was measured at 2026-10-07-act-by-id and is pinned by `stand_act_range`, which
this chunk rewrites rather than deletes. The value rules follow the HTML range state's sanitization and step rules,
cited at the code (per architecture §Design Philosophy, "Behave like a browser, and cite the spec"). Every markup number
is read fallibly to a finite value inside `[min, max]` on the step grid, with no panic path (per security-plan §Input
Validation, rows "Markup numeric attributes" and "Layout values"; §Error Handling, Graceful degradation).

The change stays off the driver and the app. The driver gains no verb, key name, cause or text: `click` already lands
at the centre of the bounds, and `press` already names the six keys (`packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:351-366`,
`command.rs`). The Dioxus bridge already carries an engine `Input`'s value to `oninput`
(`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:377-380`). The Timer's markup does not move (per layout-templates
§Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens). Nothing is painted differently: blitz paints a range input as the default
sheet's bordered box, with no track or thumb (`packages/blitz-dom/assets/default.css:76-81`). The accessibility node
gains no numeric value and no action; either would be a new class on the adapter crossing (per security-plan §Input
Validation; a11y-plan §2).

1. **The value rules, a new module of ours** — `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/range.rs`, exported from
   `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/mod.rs` as `RangeInputData`. It holds the current value, an `f64`, and the pure rules
   over the four attributes `min`, `max`, `step` and `value`, written against
   `https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#range-state-(type=range)` and its step rules (the URL at the code):
   - **Parsing:** each number is read with the HTML float parser's rules. A parse error, NaN or an infinity counts as
     absent.
   - **Bounds:** `min` defaults to 0 and `max` to 100. A `max` below `min` reads as `min`.
   - **Step:** `step` defaults to 1. A value ≤ 0 or unparsable reads 1. `any` sets no step constraint and steps by 1
     on a key.
   - **Step base:** `min` when it parses, else the `value` attribute when it parses, else 0.
   - **Default value:** `min` when `max < min`, else `min + (max − min) / 2`.
   - **Sanitize:** an unparsable value reads the default value. It is then clamped to `[min, max]` and rounded to the
     nearest step-grid value, the greater on a tie. The result never exceeds the greatest grid value ≤ `max`.
   - **Moves:** one step up or down from the current value, then sanitized. The minimum and the maximum, each
     sanitized. A fraction in `[0, 1]` along the track, mapped to `min + fraction × (max − min)`, then sanitized.
   - **Format:** the current value as a string — the shortest round-trip form, `-0` written `0`. It is rounded to
     the decimals of `step` and the step base, so that 0.1 stepped three times from 0 reads `0.3`.
   - **Tests:** an inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` holds each rule as a stated table with its row count asserted. The
     degenerate rows must read finite, inside `[min, max]` and on the grid: `step="0"`, `step="-1"`, `step="any"`,
     `min > max`, `value="abc"`, `value="1e308"`, `min="NaN"`. The module holds no print, log site, `unwrap`,
     `expect`, panic or env read outside its tests. Every public item carries `///`.

2. **The node data** — `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/element.rs`:
   - Add `SpecialElementData::RangeInput(RangeInputData)` and `SpecialElementType::RangeInput`; the latter enum is
     `#[non_exhaustive]` and has no reader.
   - Add arms to the two exhaustive matches here, the `Clone` impl (375-391) and the `Debug` impl (893-913).
   - Add the accessors `range_input_data()` / `range_input_data_mut()`, shaped like `checkbox_input_checked` (594-608),
     and `range_input_value() -> Option<String>`, the formatted current value.
   - The third exhaustive match, the removal walk at `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:1080-1103`, gets a
     `RangeInput(_) => {}` arm.

3. **Seeding at construction** — `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs`, in the input match at 437-458:
   - An `input` whose `type` is `range` (ASCII case-insensitive, as the match reads the other types) gets
     `RangeInputData` seeded from its sanitized `value` attribute.
   - The seed happens only when the element does not already hold it, as `create_checkbox_input` does (917-925), so
     a re-construction keeps a moved value.
   - Construction then continues exactly as today, with no early `return`, so the box built is unchanged.
   - An `input` that holds `RangeInput` but no longer reads `type="range"` has the data cleared to `None`.

4. **An attribute write re-seeds** — `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` `set_attribute`, beside the text input's `value`
   branch (359-368):
   - On an element holding `RangeInput`, a `value` write sets the current value to the sanitized new attribute.
   - A `min`, `max` or `step` write re-sanitizes the current value against the new bounds.
   - `clear_attribute` (411) does the same for a removed `value`, `min`, `max` or `step`.
   - The mutator's own in-document marking of the changed set is kept; nothing reaches past it.

5. **The keys** — `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs` `handle_key_or_input_event`, after the text-input branch
   (68-100). When the focused target is an element holding `RangeInputData`, it has no `disabled` attribute (presence,
   as `ClickTarget::Disabled` reads it), and the key event is pressed:
   - `ArrowRight` and `ArrowUp` step up, `ArrowLeft` and `ArrowDown` step down.
   - `Home` moves to the minimum and `End` to the maximum.
   - Every other key does nothing here.

   When the new value differs from the old one, the engine:
   - writes it into the data;
   - inserts the node into `changed_nodes`;
   - dispatches `DomEventData::Input(BlitzInputEvent { value })` carrying the formatted value;
   - requests a redraw, the shape of `keyboard.rs:119-127`.

   An equal value does nothing and fires no event. The node is resolved with `get`, never by index.

6. **The click** — `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs`:
   - **Pointerdown:** `handle_pointerdown` gains a `ClickTarget` arm for a hit element holding `RangeInputData`,
     taken after the `disabled` check (457), so a disabled range does nothing. On the main button its fraction is
     `(hit.x − (padding.left + border.left)) / content-box width`, clamped to `[0, 1]`; a content box of no width
     reads fraction 0. This is the frame the text input's caret mapping uses (459-462, 506-507), correct under
     scrolled boxes. The value set from the fraction then takes step 5's write, mark, `Input` and redraw when it
     changed.
   - **Click:** `handle_click` gains an arm for an `input` holding `RangeInputData`, placed after the `disabled`
     check (635-638). It focuses the control through `generate_focus_events` → `set_focus_to`, as the checkbox arm
     does (658-664), and breaks with `matched` true. It changes no value: a label's synthetic click focuses the
     slider and leaves its value alone.
   - The track is horizontal and left to right only.

7. **Form submission reads the current value** — `packages/blitz-dom/src/form.rs` `construct_entry_list`, in the entry
   at 316-319: an input holding `RangeInputData` submits its formatted current value before the `value` attribute
   fallback. Add an inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` that builds a form holding a range input through `DocumentMutator`,
   with `resolve(0.0)` (elements made with `qual_name!(…, html)`). It moves the value through the data and asserts
   that the entry list carries the moved value, not the attribute.

8. **The snapshot reads the current value** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs` `value` (198-225):
   - A range input reads `range_input_value()`, and an element without the data still reads its `value` attribute.
     The field's doc line (55-58) is updated to say so.
   - Rename the unit test `a_range_input_reads_its_value_attribute` (591-605) to
     `a_range_input_reads_its_current_value`; it still reads `15` at boot.
   - Add a unit test: an uncontrolled range input, with no `oninput`, focused and sent one `ArrowRight` key-down
     through the document's event handling, reads the moved value. Its `value` attribute still reads the boot value.

9. **The engine check** — new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/range_input_interaction.rs`. It opens with a `//!` doc and drives
   inline-HTML fixtures through `blitz_test_harness::Harness` in both layout modes (`for incremental in [false, true]`).
   It first asserts that the fixture holds a range input with the data seeded. It reads the current value through
   `ElementData::range_input_value` and the events through `dispatch_recorded`, and asserts unconditionally:
   - **Keys:** a stated table with its row count asserted. On `min=0 max=10 step=2 value=4`, focused:
     - right → `6`, up → `8`, left → `6`, down → `4`, End → `10`, Home → `0`;
     - Home again → no change and no `input` event;
     - each change → exactly one `input` event.
   - **Click:** `click_at` at content-box fractions 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1, and at a point in the left padding, reads the
     sanitized value each maps to, computed from the input's laid-out box. After each click the harness's focused
     node is the input.
   - **Degenerate attributes:** a stated table of the step 1 rows, each driven by a right arrow and a centre click,
     completes with no panic. Each reads finite, inside `[min, max]` and on its grid.
   - **Decimals:** `step="0.1"` stepped three times from 0 reads `0.3`.
   - **Disabled:** a disabled range takes neither keys nor a click. The value is unchanged and no `input` event fires.
   - **Attribute writes:** `doc.mutate().set_attribute(value)` re-seeds the current value, sanitized (`7` on the step-2
     fixture reads `8`). A `max` write below the current value clamps it.

   The file prints nothing, installs no subscriber and reads no env var. A failure message carries the mode and a row
   index, never a value.

10. **The stand check, rewritten** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_range.rs`. The `//!` doc is restated to the new
    reading. Each sequence holds the Timer through `session_common::hold` and runs every call through `Session::run` in
    both layout modes:
    - **Sequence A, from boot:**

      | # | call | value | display |
      |---|---|---|---|
      | 1 | `click` | `15` | `15.0s` (focus moves to the slider; the centre is the midpoint) |
      | 2 | right | `15.5` | `15.5s` |
      | 3 | up | `16` | `16.0s` |
      | 4 | left | `15.5` | `15.5s` |
      | 5 | down | `15` | `15.0s` |
      | 6 | End | `30` | `30.0s` |
      | 7 | Home | `0` | `0.0s` |
      | 8 | right | `0.5` | `0.5s` |
      | 9 | `click` | `15` | `15.0s` (the click sets the value by position) |

    - **Sequence B, from a fresh instance:** two Tabs focus the slider, then right reads `15.5`.

    Every call returns settled. Each returned diff equals the file's own `before.diff(&after)` and is equal across the
    two modes. Each diff names exactly the controls stated for its step: after step A1 the slider alone, its `differs`
    `focused`; after a value change the slider (`value`) and `timer-duration-value` (`name`). A failure message carries
    the mode, the sequence letter and the step index only.

11. **The pinned click** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_ids.rs`:
    - `changes_at_boot(LeanTask::Timer)` (40) becomes `&["timer-duration"]`, since a click now focuses the slider and
      its diff names that.
    - Its doc comments are restated: the file's opening paragraph ("The Timer has no changing control at boot …") and
      the list doc above `changes_at_boot` ("… the range input …").
    - The twin's selector click lands at the same centre, so the equality the file asserts holds.
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/range.rs` — `RangeInputData` and the range state's value rules, with their unit tables

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/range_input_interaction.rs` — the engine check: keys, click, degenerate attributes, disabled,
  attribute writes, both layout modes
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/mod.rs` — `mod range;` and `pub use range::RangeInputData`
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/element.rs` — the `RangeInput` variants, their `Clone` and `Debug` arms, the accessors
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs` — seed the range data once, no early return; clear it off a non-range
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` — `value`/`min`/`max`/`step` writes and removals re-seed; the removal walk's arm
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs` — the six keys on a focused range
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` — the position set at pointerdown; the focus at click
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/form.rs` — submit the current value; its inline test
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs` — read the current value; the renamed and the added unit test
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_range.rs` — rewritten to the new reading
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_ids.rs` — the Timer row: the slider's click changes its focus

Graph impact (research.md, Graph impact): `handle_click @ packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs:215` and its own label
arm `@ pointer.rs:731`; `handle_key_or_input_event @ events/mod.rs:218, :232`; `handle_pointerdown @ events/mod.rs:192`.
Each gains an arm or a branch inside, with no signature change.

No entry is a live leg: nothing is driven against an external process the operator brings up. Every check boots in
process. There is no boot smoke, because the chunk changes no binary and no boot path. The project has no headful
self-verify harness.

The `a11y` leg runs three fixed files, `accessibility_roles` and `focusability_updates` among them. Both are read here
in the standing-checks entry. The leg itself stays unchanged (a11y-history 2026-10-05-ci-gate-legs).
No manifest changes, so the audit leg is not listed. The `Cargo.lock` census stands in for it.
No mutation control is planned or run: the mutation tier stays unstarted (inputs#I1).

**Not run locally:** the MSRV build and the windows, macos, ios and android legs. The fork's CI run is their witness;
a key path compiled differently on macOS is read there (testing.md, 2026-10-06).

`evidence/range-readings.md` (step 12) has no listed producer by construction. It is /implement's record of one-shot
readings, asserted by the listed entries.

- (arch) The ruled behaviour holds in both layout modes:
  - with a range input focused, the right and up arrows step its value up by `step`, the left and down arrows step it
    down, and Home and End go to the minimum and the maximum;
  - a pointer click sets the value by its position along the content box and focuses the control;
  - every change fires one `input` event, and a step that changes nothing fires none.

  `range_input_interaction` asserts each row of its keys and click tables (per architecture §Design Philosophy, "One
  incremental pipeline, safe identities"; architecture §Standard Contracts → Events).

- (arch) The moved value is held as the control's current value, `SpecialElementData::RangeInput(RangeInputData)`, apart
  from its `value` attribute, as the founder answered Q1 (inputs#I2). A `value` write re-seeds it, and a `min`, `max`
  or `step` write re-sanitizes it. `range_input_interaction`'s attribute-write rows and the snapshot unit test of an
  uncontrolled input (whose attribute keeps its boot value) read both (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Nodes and
  widgets).

- (arch) The driver schema is unchanged: the preservation entry reads exit 0 over `packages/escher-driver`, so `VERBS`
  stays 11, `KEY_NAMES` 12, `Cause` 9 and `SessionError` 13 (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session).

- (arch) No workspace crate, listener, port, env var or package is added. The `Cargo.lock` census reads 0 and the
  preservation entry reads exit 0 over the manifests (per architecture §Occupied Resources).

- (security) Every degenerate-attribute row completes with no panic in both layout modes and reads a finite value
  inside `[min, max]` on its grid:
  - non-numeric text, `step="0"`, a negative step, `step="any"`;
  - `min` above `max`, a value of `1e308`, `min="NaN"`.

  So do `range.rs`'s unit tables (per security-plan §Input Validation, rows "Markup numeric attributes" and "Layout
  values"; security-plan §Error Handling, Graceful degradation).

- (security) The rules module outside its tests holds no print, panic path, log site or env read. No added line in the
  changed engine files prints, logs, reads env or adds an `unwrap` or `expect`. Both census entries read 0 (per
  security-plan §Logging & Monitoring; security-plan §Error Handling).

- (security) A disabled range takes neither a key nor a click: the value is unchanged and no `input` event fires
  (`range_input_interaction`, the disabled rows). The driver still refuses its click as `disabled` first (per
  security-plan §Input Validation, row "Markup attributes" / `disabled`).

- (tests) `stand_act_range` is rewritten, not deleted, and keeps its `stand_` prefix. Through `Session::run`, in both
  layout modes, sequence A reads every step of step 10's table and sequence B reads `15.5` after two Tabs and a right
  arrow. Each returned diff equals the file's own `before.diff(&after)` and is equal across the modes (per test-plan §5
  Session ↔ held instance; test-plan §3 Agent-run contract).

- (tests) `stand_act_ids` passes with the Timer row naming `timer-duration` as changing at boot. The fifteen standing
  checks of the standing-checks entry pass unchanged, `stand_snapshot_state`'s boot value `15` among them (per test-plan
  §1 Coverage scope; test-plan §2 Differential oracle).

- (tests) The new and rewritten checks pass under `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked` and under
  `cargo test --workspace --locked` (per test-plan §9 Engine features by runner).
  - `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run stand` reads failed 0; its totals are recorded against 141 · 0 · 7 over 37 files.
  - `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` and `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` pass; the workspace totals are
    recorded against 180 result lines · 900 passed (per test-plan §9 Pipeline facts, Local pre-push gate).

- (a11y) With `timer-duration` focused by two Tabs, its arrow step leaves it focused and still the tree's focus. It
  reads role `Slider` with its name before and after. The stand's forward focus sequence is unchanged: the standing
  entry's `stand_accessibility_ids` and `focusability_updates` pass (per a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation, Test harness
  pattern and Focus order per layout; a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support, Accessibility tree output).

- (a11y) A stepped or clicked value is named by the driver's diff on the slider's stable id, its `differs` `value`, and
  on the display it drives (per a11y-plan §2 A11y Strategy, Accessibility tree lifecycle).

- (a11y) `stand_contrast` reads its 18 rows unchanged, `timer-duration` `no-text` (per a11y-plan §6 Visual Design
  Verification, Color contrast).

- (design) No colour literal is added. The range paints as before; the preservation entry reads exit 0 over
  `packages/blitz-paint` and `packages/blitz-dom/assets`. A click returns settled in one step and adds no animation
  (per design-system §Color Palette, Token sets; design-system §Motion, Animation runtime).

- (layouts) The Timer's markup diff is empty: the preservation entry reads exit 0 over `examples`. After the range calls
  the stand mount reads as on a fresh boot: `stand_session_fresh`, in the standing entry (per layout-templates §Surface:
  desktop-native → Primary screens).

- (obs) No `tracing` span, event or field is added, and the driver's `command` span keeps its eight fields:
  `stand_act_spans` passes in the standing entry. The two new or rewritten checks are silent: their census entry reads

  (`python -X utf8 ~/.claude/skills/andromeda-tools/scripts/ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1800`).
- Research files inspected: listed in research.md, Files inspected and Resolved at P4.

- Leaned on the founder's answers to Q1, Q2 and Q3 (inputs#I2), not on the plan's own preferences: the value lives
  apart from the attribute, all six keys step, and a click focuses.

- Leaned "form submission reads the current value", per the founder's Q1: a separate current value is the control's
  value, and the HTML entry list submits "the value of the field element" (`packages/blitz-dom/src/form.rs:315`). A
  form left reading the attribute would submit a moved range's default.

- Leaned "an attribute write re-seeds the current value", per the overseer's record of the costs Q1 takes on (inputs#I3)
  and the text input's precedent (`packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:359-368`). Without it, the stand Timer's re-render
  could never move the slider. This differs from the spec's dirty-value flag, which ignores attribute writes once the
  user has moved the value.

- Leaned "the value is set at pointerdown, the focus at click", per browsers and the engine's own split: the caret moves
  at pointerdown (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:506-507`), and a checkbox focuses at click (658-664). A
  label's synthetic click therefore focuses without moving the value.

- Holding the moved value in the `value` attribute — rejected by the founder's Q1 answer (inputs#I2), though it was the
  plan's recommendation.

- A numeric value or Increment/Decrement/SetValue actions on the slider's accessibility node — rejected: a new class on
  the platform adapter crossing, a founder question (security-plan §Input Validation; a11y-plan §2).

- Painting a track or thumb, a drag, a `change` event, Page Up/Down, or a vertical or right-to-left track — rejected:
  outside the ruled minimal model. blitz-traits has no `change` event and the driver has no drag or Page key (scope,
  Boundaries).

- A new driver verb, key name, cause or help text — rejected: the six keys and the centre click already exist
  (`packages/escher-driver/src/command.rs`, `execute.rs:351-366`).

- Any edit to the Timer's markup, id, class or style, or a CSS selector on `timer-duration` — rejected (layout-templates
  §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens). A position other than the centre is proven by the engine check's
  `click_at`, and on the stand by clicking after a key step has moved the value.

- An early `return` in the range construction arm — rejected: it would skip the construction an input gets today and
  could change its box. Construction must stay identical.

- A log site, span field or print holding a range value, attribute or click position — rejected (obs-plan §8;
  security-plan §Logging & Monitoring).
- Any mutation control or mutation-tier run — rejected on the founder's standing word (inputs#I1).

- **Hypothesis to measure, never to assume:** a centre click on the Timer slider maps to its midpoint, 15. The basis is
  the default sheet's symmetric 1px border and 2px padding (`packages/blitz-dom/assets/default.css:76-81`) and
  `.timer-slider` setting neither (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs:164-167`), so the centre of the box is the
  centre of its content box. An `f32` error near 0.5 snaps to 15 on the 0.5 grid. Record the measured value and the
  content-box width in `evidence/range-readings.md`.

- **The Timer's display:** `{duration():.1}s` (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs:93`), so 16 reads `16.0s` and
  0.5 reads `0.5s`. The app writes `value: "{duration()}"`, which re-seeds the current value with what the event
  carried.

- **macOS:** the six keys are `keyboard_types::Key` values the driver maps on every platform
  (`packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:499-500`). Read the `#[cfg]` lines around the new keyboard branch; the macOS
  CI leg is the one witness of a platform-gated arm (testing.md, 2026-10-06).

- **Merge surface:** upstream/main at `434e0661` has no range interaction (`git log -i --grep=range upstream/main`).
  These upstream files change: `node/element.rs`, `node/mod.rs`, `layout/construct.rs`, `mutator.rs`,
  `events/keyboard.rs`, `events/pointer.rs` and `form.rs`. Keep each edit additive; the rules live in `node/range.rs`.

  - **The value rules** (`range.rs`), written against `https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#range-state-(type=range)`, cited at the code:
    - `min` defaults to 0 and `max` to 100. A `max` below `min` reads as `min`.
    - `step` defaults to 1. A step ≤ 0 or unparsable reads 1. `any` sets no grid and steps by 1 on a key.
    - The step base is `min` where it parses, else the `value` attribute where it parses, else 0.
    - The default value is the midpoint, computed `min/2 + max/2` so it cannot overflow.
    - Sanitizing clamps to `[min, max]` and moves to the nearest grid value inside them, the greater on a tie. The grid index is computed `value/step − base/step`, so the difference of two finite bounds cannot overflow.
    - The value is then rounded to the decimals of the step and the base, and formatted in its shortest round-trip form.

body:
- **handle_click** — callers `events/handle_dom_event()` at `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs:215` and itself
  (the label arm) at `pointer.rs:731`; no signature change is planned, so the change is a new arm inside it.

- **handle_key_or_input_event** — callers `events/handle_dom_event()` at `events/mod.rs:218` (`KeyDown`) and `:232`
  (`AppleStandardKeybinding`); a new branch inside it, no signature change.

- **handle_pointerdown** — caller `events/handle_dom_event()` at `events/mod.rs:192`; a new arm of its `ClickTarget`
  match, no signature change.

- **handle_dom_event** — called from `BaseDocument::handle_dom_event` (`document.rs:661`) and
  `EventDriver::run_default_action` (`events/driver.rs:425`); not changed.

- Harness `click` / `press` / `click_at` / `center_of` — 127 call sites over 27 files (trace query 2); the sweep below
  narrows them to the two checks that touch the slider.

- **Form-control default action in `handle_click`** (`pointer.rs:645-695`): set the state, dispatch `Input` with the new
  value as text, then focus the control through `generate_focus_events`.

- **Point-in-control from the hit** (`pointer.rs:459-462, 506-507`): `hit.x - (padding.left + border.left)` is the
  click's offset into the content box, already correct under scrolled boxes since 2026-10-10 (the hit stops at and
  reads each clipping box where it stands).
- **`input` event shape** (`keyboard.rs:119-127`): mark changed, dispatch `Input { value }`, request redraw.

- **Spec citation beside the code**: arch §Design Philosophy — cite the HTML "range state" value sanitization and the
  step rules (`https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#range-state-(type=range)`) at the implementation.

- **No panic on markup**: parse `min`/`max`/`step`/`value` fallibly to finite `f64`, defaults 0 / 100 / 1 / the
  midpoint (spec default value); `step` ≤ 0, non-numeric or `any` → 1 for a key step (spec: `any` steps by 1); `max <
  min` → the value is `min`.

- **Stale ids**: resolve the focused or hit node with `get`, never by index (arch §Standard Contracts → Scrolling,
  selection, tree).
- **Engine tracing**: none added; if one were, `#[cfg(feature = "tracing")]` with `node_id` only (obs-plan §8).

- **Tests**: one blitz-tests file per behaviour with a `//!` doc, `for incremental in [false, true]`, the condition
  asserted first; stand driver checks through `session_common` (`hold`, `act`, `click`, `press`).

- **Marker:** 2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-13T17:16Z
- **Base:** `198bf85cb674498549cd8f36721041680770e7ce` (HEAD at P4, the commit the chunk starts from)

Build the contrast verification harness that a11y-plan §3 records as observed absent and §6 records as NOT YET MEASURED,
and take its reading on every stand control. `blitz-test-harness` gains a `contrast` module: a WCAG 2.x contrast ratio,
and `Harness::text_contrast`, which reads a control's text colour and the background that text is painted on from the
engine's computed styles. The background is resolved up the ancestor chain to the canvas, by the rule blitz-paint paints
the canvas with. The module also states the SC 1.4.3 threshold the text's computed size and weight call for (per
a11y-plan §1, §3, §6; architecture §Standard Contracts → Test harness).

A new stand check, `stand_contrast`, boots each lean task through the stand in both layout modes. It measures every row
of the shared `controls(task)` table, 18 rows naming 15 controls, and records one result per row:
- **pass** or **fail** — the colours, the ratio, the size, the weight and the verdict against the threshold;
- **exempt-inactive** — the control reads not enabled;
- **no-text** — the range input, which paints no text.

The record is the check's own stated table: the check asserts the reading equals that table, row for row, in both modes.
A second test proves the measurement against what is painted: the pixel inside each measured control's left padding,
taken from the harness's raster, is the background the reader resolved (per test-plan §1, §3; a11y-plan §3, §7).

This chunk measures and records; it gates nothing and re-colours nothing. Asserting SC 1.4.3 on every control, and the
CI leg that gates merges on it, belong to "Stand a11y assertions" (working-route.md:94). The check runs in the workspace
`test` leg and per package, never in the `a11y` leg (per a11y-plan §9; test-plan §9). No engine crate changes. The
ratio is the harness's own, computed with the same `color` crate luminance blitz-paint's `pub(crate)` helper uses, so the
two agree by construction (per architecture §Conventions → Visibility and naming).

1. **Take the colour type into the harness.** Add `color = { workspace = true }` to `[dependencies]` in
   `packages/blitz-test-harness/Cargo.toml` (`Cargo.toml:132` declares `color = "0.3"` for the workspace; blitz-dom
   already takes it, `packages/blitz-dom/Cargo.toml:75`). `Cargo.lock` gains the dependency line in blitz-test-harness's
   entry and no `[[package]]`. Record the lock delta in `evidence/counts.md`.

2. **The ratio.** In the new `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/contrast.rs`, state
   `pub fn contrast_ratio(a: Color, b: Color) -> f32`. `Color` is `color::AlphaColor<color::Srgb>`, the engine's colour
   model, the type `blitz_dom::util::ToColorColor::as_color_color` returns (`packages/blitz-dom/src/util.rs:166-179`).
   - Compute WCAG 2.x's `(L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05)`, the larger over the smaller, with `L` from the `color` crate's
     `OpaqueColor::relative_luminance` after the alpha is split off. That is blitz-paint's formula exactly
     (`packages/blitz-paint/src/color.rs:29-35`).
   - The `///` doc names WCAG 2.x and Chrome's `GetContrastRatio`, and says the alpha is ignored. A caller composites a
     translucent colour first.

4. **The reader.** In the same module, add `impl<D: Document> Harness<D> { pub fn text_contrast(&self, node_id: NodeId) -> Option<TextContrast> }`,
   the impl-block shape of `inspect.rs` (`packages/blitz-test-harness/src/inspect.rs:26`). It reads, and changes nothing.

   **The text-bearing element** is one of:
   - `node_id` itself, when it is a text input (its element's special data is the text input's, which paints its value
     in its own computed `color` at its computed size, `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs:875-910`);
   - otherwise the parent element of the first text node, in tree order under `node_id`, whose text holds a character
     that is not whitespace. Paint strokes a glyph in the computed `color` of its brush node,
     `packages/blitz-paint/src/text.rs:616-638`, which reads the colour by `resolve_decoration_entry`, the node's
     inherited-text `color`, `packages/blitz-paint/src/text.rs:156-167`.

   No such element → `None`. The range input `timer-duration` is the stand's case.

   **The text colour and font** come from that element's primary styles:
   - its computed `color`, resolved to absolute and converted through `as_color_color`;
   - its computed `font-size` (the used size, in px);
   - its computed `font-weight`.

   **The background** walks from that element up its ancestors to the root. At each element, its computed
   `background-color`, resolved against its own `color` (`packages/blitz-paint/src/render/background.rs:334-336`), is
   gathered while it is not fully opaque, and the walk stops at the first fully opaque one. The gathered layers are
   composited source-over, the nearest on top, over the first opaque layer.
   - With no opaque layer before the root, the canvas follows `packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:193-219`: the root
     element's `background-color`, else `body`'s when the root's is transparent.
   - If the canvas is transparent too, the base is opaque white, the white `Harness::screenshot` composites over.

   **The text colour is composited** over the resolved background when its alpha is below 1.

   **An element on the walk returns `None`** when it lies between the text-bearing element and the first opaque layer,
   that element included, and it carries any of:
   - a background image layer that is not `none`;
   - an `opacity` below 1;
   - a `filter` that is not `none`.

   Colours alone do not determine such a pair, and the `///` doc says so. The stand has none (research.md, Sweeps).

   **Every node is reached through `get_node`.** No `NodeId` is indexed, and no `primary_styles()` result is unwrapped: a
   node without styles reads `None`. There is no `doc.mutate()`, no input, no pump and no settle. The reader prints, logs
   and panics on nothing (per security-plan §Error Handling, Panic paths; obs-plan §3, §4).

6. **Export.** In `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/lib.rs`, declare `mod contrast;` and add
   `pub use contrast::{TextContrast, contrast_ratio};`. Add one bullet to the crate doc's feature list naming
   [`text_contrast`](Harness::text_contrast), the screenshot bullet's form.

7. **The stand check.** Create `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_contrast.rs`.

   **The file:**
   - It opens with a `//!` doc naming the behaviour: every stand control's text/background pair, measured and recorded.
   - It declares `mod common;`.
   - It states the per-pair record as a table: one row per `controls(task)` row, in that table's order, with the task,
     the stable id and the expected result.

   **The expected result** is one of:
   - `NoText`;
   - `ExemptInactive { text, background, ratio, size, weight }`;
   - `Pass { … }` or `Fail { … }`, with the same fields.

   **The fields are stated as:**
   - colours as 8-bit `#rrggbb` hex, opaque;
   - the ratio rounded to two decimals;
   - the size in whole px;
   - the weight as a number.

   **The table's values are this chunk's measurement:** step 9 fills them from the first reading. No row is copied
   from the stylesheets.

8. **The check's two tests**, each `for incremental in [false, true]` over `LeanTask::ALL`, booting with
   `common::boot(task, incremental)`.

   **`every_stand_control_reads_its_recorded_pair`**
   - Assert first that the table has as many rows as the four tasks' `controls(task)` together (18,
     `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs:16-45`), and that its ids follow that table's order.
   - Assert that the snapshot lists every control id.
   - Then, per row:
     - resolve the node with `harness.query` on `#` plus the row's id;
     - read `text_contrast` and the snapshot node's `state.enabled`;
     - derive the result: `NoText` when `text_contrast` is `None`; `ExemptInactive` when `enabled == Some(false)`;
       otherwise `Pass` when `ratio >= required_ratio()`, else `Fail`;
     - compare the result field by field with the stated row: colours as 8-bit values, the ratio at two decimals.
   - Finally assert that the two layout modes produced identical records.

   **`the_painted_background_is_the_measured_background`**
   - For every row whose result is not `NoText`, take the one-pixel `PixelRect` at:
     - x: the box's left edge plus its left border plus half its left padding;
     - y: the box's vertical middle.

     The box is read through `layout_rect_of` and the control element's `final_layout()` border and padding. An
     element resolved by `query` always carries layout data, and the accessor is called on nothing else (per
     security-plan §Error Handling, Panic paths). Take that pixel from `screenshot_rect`.
   - Assert each RGB channel is within 1 of the measured background's 8-bit value (the renderer's rounding).
   - Assert first that every such box has a left padding of at least 2 px, so the pixel lies in padding. The stand
     sheets state 6–24 px (research.md, Files inspected).

   **Rules for both tests:**
   - No print, no subscriber, no env read, no sleep and no font skip.
   - Every assertion message names the layout mode, the task and the row index only, never an id, a colour or anything
     the screen reads (per test-plan §3, the 2026-10-07-act-by-id rule; `.claude/rules/security.md`, assertion messages).

9. **Take and record the reading.** Run the check once with the table's values left unknown, and read the measured
   record by any means that leaves no print in the committed file. One example: a temporary local assertion message,
   removed before the gates run.

   Then:
   - write the 18 rows into the table;
   - copy them, with each row's declared stylesheet value beside it and the per-verdict counts, into
     `evidence/pairs.md`;
   - record whether the scope's hypothesis held — five controls `#ffffff` on `#4a6cf7` at 4.39, `fail`
     (scope.md, Boundaries) — and every row where the measured value differs from the declared hex
     (per design-system §Color Palette).

   The record in `evidence/pairs.md` is this step's product. No listed gate produces it. The integration entries assert
   the same table.

10. **Counts.** Record in `evidence/counts.md`:
    - `run stand`'s `run.end` against the standing 139 · 0 · 7 over 36 files (test-plan history,
      2026-10-12-headless-screenshot). Predicted 37 files and 141 passed: record what the run measures.
    - The workspace test leg's totals against 179 result lines · 893 passed · 0 failed · 12 ignored
      (2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship). Predicted to move by exactly the new tests: record what
      `target/ci-logs/test.log` reads.
    - `mod common;` readers, recounted by `grep -l 'mod common;' tests/blitz-tests/tests/*.rs | wc -l`: 17 at P3,
      predicted 18.
    - The `Cargo.lock` delta from step 1.
- `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/contrast.rs` — `contrast_ratio`, `TextContrast`, `Harness::text_contrast`, and their unit tests
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_contrast.rs` — the stand check: the stated per-pair record and its two tests
- `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness/evidence/pairs.md` — the per-pair record as measured, beside the declared values
- `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness/evidence/counts.md` — run stand, workspace, `mod common;` readers, lock delta
- `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/lib.rs` — `mod contrast;`, the re-export, one crate-doc bullet
- `packages/blitz-test-harness/Cargo.toml` — `color = { workspace = true }`
- `Cargo.lock` — blitz-test-harness's dependency list gains `color`; no package enters

No entry is a live leg: nothing is driven against an external process the operator brings up. The checks boot the stand
in process. There is no boot smoke, because the chunk changes no binary and no boot path. The project has no headful
self-verify harness.

The `a11y` leg runs three fixed files that this chunk does not touch (a11y-history 2026-10-05-ci-gate-legs). The audit

body: - (a11y) Every row of `controls(task)` over `LeanTask::ALL` ends in exactly one recorded result: `pass`, `fail`, `exempt-inactive` or `no-text`. The stated table has 18 rows in that table's order, and `stand_contrast` asserts the reading equals it row for row. A measured row holds the colours, the ratio, the computed size and weight, and the verdict against the threshold SC 1.4.3 sets for its size and weight (per a11y-plan §1 A11y Scope Summary; a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support, Accessibility tree output).

- (a11y) A row reads `exempt-inactive` exactly when its snapshot node's `enabled` is `Some(false)`. At boot that is `flight-return-date`, `crud-update` and `crud-delete` (research.md). It is never decided from focusability (per a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation, Focus order per layout).

- (a11y) The harness's ratio is WCAG 2.x's, over the same `color` crate luminance blitz-paint's helper uses: black on white reads 21.0, a colour on itself 1.0, and `#777777` on white 4.48 in the unit table (per a11y-plan §6 Visual Design Verification, Color contrast).
- (a11y) The record is identical with incremental layout off and on (per a11y-plan §3 A11y Assertion Harness Contract).

- (design) Each measured pair's colours come from computed, post-cascade styles under the stand's Light boot. The background is resolved to the canvas by the root-else-body rule. `the_painted_background_is_the_measured_background` reads the painted pixel inside each measured control's left padding within 1 per channel of the measured background (per design-system §Color Palette, Color model and scheme).
- (design) `evidence/pairs.md` sets each measured colour beside the stylesheet value it was declared as, and names every difference (per design-system §Color Palette).

- (layouts) Every pair is measured on the lean task as the stand mounts it, at the pinned 800 × 600, scale 1, Light viewport, keyed by its stable id, `back-btn` once per task. The chunk's diff touches nothing under `examples/`, read by the preservation entry `git diff --quiet 198bf85cb674498549cd8f36721041680770e7ce -- … examples …` (per layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens).

- (tests) `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_contrast` and `cargo test --workspace --locked --test stand_contrast` both pass (per test-plan §9 Pipeline facts, Engine features by runner).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run stand` picks up `stand_contrast` with no script change and reads failed 0, its totals recorded against 139 · 0 · 7 over 36 files (per test-plan §3 Agent-run contract).

- (tests) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` and `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` pass, the workspace totals recorded against 179 result lines · 893 passed (per test-plan §9 Pipeline facts, Local baseline).

- (arch) No engine crate changes: the preservation entry reads exit 0 over `packages/blitz-paint`, `packages/blitz-dom` and the other crates, so `contrast_ratio` in blitz-paint stays `pub(crate)` (per architecture §Conventions → Visibility and naming).
- (arch) Every new public item of `blitz-test-harness` carries `///`, and the doc leg passes (per architecture §Conventions → Documentation).

- (security) No package enters `Cargo.lock`: `git diff 198bf85cb674498549cd8f36721041680770e7ce -- Cargo.lock | grep -c '^+\[\[package\]\]'` reads 0. The audit leg reads `advisories ok` with `deny.toml` unchanged (per security-plan §Dependency Security).

- (security) The reader outside its tests holds no print, panic path, log site, mutation or env read. The check holds no print, subscriber, env read or listener. Both census entries read 0 (per security-plan §Error Handling, Panic paths; security-plan §Secret Management).

- (obs) No `tracing` span or event, and no subscriber, is added: the two census entries read 0 over `contrast.rs` outside its tests (`tracing::`) and over `stand_contrast.rs` (`escher_telemetry`, `tracing_subscriber`). blitz-test-harness's manifest gains no `tracing`: `grep -c -E 'tracing' packages/blitz-test-harness/Cargo.toml` reads 0 (per obs-plan §3 Logging stack; obs-plan §4).
- (ci) The operator's CI read on the pushed sha reads `verdict: green` (`python -X utf8 ~/.claude/skills/andromeda-tools/scripts/ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1800`).
- External input: inputs#I1 (no mutation runs).

- Leaned "states beyond boot are not measured here" per the working entry's own wording, "text/background pair of every stand control": one pair per control, at the state the stand boots in. The colour-changing states are named for their owner on the review card.

- Leaned "the CRUD rows stay out" per test-plan §3 and a11y-plan §7. `controls(task)` is the one stated control set, and a second mapping beside it is banned; extending the table would move the six standing checks that read it (research.md, Graph impact).

- Leaned "computed styles, with a painted-pixel witness of the background", per research's verified equality: paint's colour sources are computed styles (`packages/blitz-paint/src/text.rs:156-167, 616-638`, `packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:193-219`, `packages/blitz-paint/src/render/background.rs:334-336`). A raster-sampled text colour is anti-aliased (design-system §Typography).

- Leaned "the harness's own ratio, no blitz-paint change", per architecture §Conventions → Visibility and naming and the upstream merge surface. The helper's four call sites are all inside blitz-paint (research.md, Graph impact).
- Leaned "home in blitz-test-harness", per a11y-plan §3 ("Contrast verification harness") and the `screenshot` module's precedent.
- Making blitz-paint's `contrast_ratio` public — rejected: a public-API widening of an upstream engine crate, a merge surface at the next sync, for one consumer.
- Reading the text colour from the raster — rejected: glyph edges are anti-aliased and, under `font-embolden`, thickened (design-system §Typography). The raster witnesses the background only.
- Adding `stand_contrast` to the `a11y` leg, or asserting `pass` on any row — rejected: gating SC 1.4.3 is "Stand a11y assertions" (working-route.md:94). This chunk records a `fail` as a `fail`.

- Re-colouring a stand control, or adding an id, class, style or wrapper under `examples/` — rejected: the stand's markup and colours are measured, not edited (layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens).
- Extending `controls(task)` with the CRUD rows, or stating a second control list — rejected: one stated table, read by six standing checks (test-plan §3).

- A record written to a file at run time, a printing child, or a `tracing` field carrying a pair — rejected: the stand checks print and log nothing (obs-plan §3), and ids and readings never ride a log (obs-plan §8). The record is the check's stated table, copied into evidence by hand.
- Any mutation control or mutation-tier run — rejected on the founder's standing word (inputs#I1).

- **Large text:** none is predicted. The stand sheets declare control text at 13–16 px with weight 400–600 (research.md, Files inspected), so every measured row's threshold is predicted 4.5. Record what is read.
- **Selectors:** the check's selectors are `#` plus a stable id from the stated tables, test-authored constants (security-plan §Input Validation, Test harness queries).

- **The pixel witness:** the 1-per-channel tolerance is the renderer's rounding (vello_cpu's premultiplied paint versus the `color` crate's 8-bit conversion). If a reading differs by more, the measurement is wrong: stop and record it, and do not widen the tolerance. An input's caret paints only while it is focused, and no stand control holds focus at boot. Assert that the harness's `focused()` is `None`, or not one of the measured controls, before taking pixels.
- **The `back-btn` box** lies in `#task-header` (white) and paints its own `#f0f0f0`. Its background stops at itself, so the canvas rule is exercised only by the unit fixtures.

- Expected amendments (wrap): a11y-plan §3 — the contrast verification harness built (`contrast_ratio`, `TextContrast`, `Harness::text_contrast`, its reading rules), and the keyed contract `contrast-verification-harness-setup` discharged.

- Expected amendments (wrap): a11y-plan §6 — Color contrast: the stand's 18 rows as measured, counted by verdict, the record's home `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_contrast.rs` and `evidence/pairs.md`.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Standard Contracts — Test harness: the `contrast` module and its exports; §Existing Scopes, blitz-test-harness's module count; the crate's `color` dependency.
- Expected amendments (wrap): test-plan §1, §2, §3, §4, §9 — the new target, its two tests, the harness's new unit tests, `mod common;` readers, `run stand` and workspace totals as measured.
- Expected amendments (wrap): obs-plan §3 — `stand_contrast` joins the silent census by name; obs-plan §4 — the contrast reader opens no span.
- Expected amendments (wrap): design-system §Color Palette — the measured pairs beside the declared stand values.
