    lighter over darker, with `L` from the `color` crate's `OpaqueColor::relative_luminance` after `split()`. The alpha
    is ignored. Its doc names Chrome's `GetContrastRatio`.
    - The body is blitz-paint's `pub(crate) contrast_ratio` (`packages/blitz-paint/src/color.rs:29-35`), restated in
      the harness. blitz-paint is untouched, and its helper keeps its four in-crate callers.
  - `pub struct TextContrast { text, background, ratio, font_size_px, font_weight }` (`contrast.rs:25-41`). It derives
    `Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq`. `text` and `background` are `color::AlphaColor<Srgb>`, opaque.
    - `is_large_text()` (`:44-48`): true at `font_size_px >= 24.0`, or at `>= 56/3` (14 pt) together with
      `font_weight >= 700`.
    - `required_ratio()` (`:50-53`): 3.0 for large text, else 4.5.
  - `impl<D: Document> Harness<D> { pub fn text_contrast(&self, node_id) -> Option<TextContrast> }`
    (`contrast.rs:56-91`, head `:70`). It reads and changes nothing: no `doc.mutate()`, no input, pump or settle, and
    every node is reached by `get_node`.
    - **The text-bearing element** is `node_id` itself when it is a text input (its element's `text_input_data()`).
      Otherwise it is the parent element of the first text node, in tree order under `node_id`, that holds a character
      other than whitespace (`:93-119`).
    - **The text** is that element's computed `color` (`clone_color().as_color_color()`), `font-size`
      (`clone_font_size().computed_size().px()`) and `font-weight` (`clone_font_weight().value()`).
    - **The background** (`background_behind`, `:121-147`) walks from that element through its element ancestors. Each
      element's `background-color` is resolved against its own `color`. Translucent layers are gathered until the
      first opaque one; with none before the root, the base is the canvas over opaque white. The canvas
      (`:168-187`) is the root element's background, else `body`'s when the root's reads `Color::TRANSPARENT`. The
      layers are composited source-over (`over`, `:189-198`) and the text is composited over the result.
    - **`None` cases:** no such text; an element on the walk without primary styles; or an element on the walk, up to
      and including the first opaque one, whose `opacity` is below 1, whose `filter` list is not empty, or whose
      `background-image` holds a layer other than `none` (`paints_more_than_colour`, `:149-156`). The image layers are
      read through `BaseDocument::resolved_style_value(node, "background-image")`, split on `,`, because the harness
      takes no `style` crate.
  - The crate-doc gains one bullet naming `text_contrast` (`lib.rs:16-17`).
  - No other symbol changed. `contrast_ratio` and `TextContrast` have their two first callers in
    `stand_contrast.rs`, beside the crate's own unit tests.

edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-13T22:40Z

- **Forks:** F1–F4 answered by the founder, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option labels (inputs#I2,
  inputs#I3): F1 «Клавиши нажимают (Рекомендую)», F2 «Клик даёт фокус (Рекомендую)», F3 «По наличию (Рекомендую)»,
  F4 «Отложить (Рекомендую)». F5 answered by the operator (inputs#I4): "List takes focus", on the condition that the
  plan states the gap below plainly.

- **Matrix:** no capability is claimed — the one unclaimed id, `v010-15`, is listed by the markerless "Cold-agent
  test" entry (escher-0.1.0/working-route.md:100), so it is not provable by this chunk.

Make the stand operable and readable by keyboard alone, and prove it headlessly. Today no key activates anything:
measured through the driver at P3, Tab focuses `counter-increment` and `press enter` / `press space` each return an
empty diff while a click counts (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-13T22-07-35-phase/probe-counter.txt`), so SC 2.1.1 is not met
on any stand button (per a11y-plan §1, §5). The chunk lands four rulings and a harness that proves them:
three direct engine changes for every document, ratified by the founder — Enter and Space run a focused control's
click (F1), a click on a button focuses it (F2), any `disabled` attribute removes focusability (F3) — and one stand
markup change by the operator's answer — the CRUD list takes focus and its arrows move the selection (F5). The fifth
fork, `Node::absolute_position`, is deferred by the founder's word (F4) and re-homed.

The harness is one new blitz-tests target, `stand_keyboard`, booted through `seven_guis::stand` in both layout modes:
each lean task's whole Tab sequence forward and back with wrap-around, the three focus readings agreeing at every step
(the stable id, the snapshot's one `focused` node, the accessibility tree's focus `author_id`), a stated activation
table whose keyboard outcome equals the pointer outcome row for row, the click-focus reading, the disabled-attribute
skip, the list's arrow keys, and the every-OS witness of the Apple delete binding (per a11y-plan §3, §5; test-plan §1,
§3; arch §Conventions → Tests). Telemetry is untouched: no log site, field or span is added (per obs-plan §2, §3, §4).

**The known gap, stated plainly (the operator's condition, inputs#I4):** with F5 the keyboard focus sits on the list
(`crud-list`), never on a row; the engine's accessibility builder does not read `aria-activedescendant`, so the tree's
focus is the list, not the option, and an assistive technology learns the current row only from its `selected`
reading. The fix is owned by a new CARRY on "Stand a11y assertions" (escher-0.1.0/working-route.md:94), beside the
listbox-name CARRY already there (`## Beyond the plan` on the review card).

1. **F3 — focusability reads `disabled` by presence** (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/element.rs:702-734`,
   `flush_is_focussable`). Replace the `attr_parsed` read at :703 with the attribute's presence, for every element —
   leaned per the founder's option as put (inputs#I3: "any `disabled` attribute removes focusability") and matching
   `handle_click`'s own presence read on every element (`pointer.rs:661-664`), and confirmed by the operator to keep
   today's reach, any element (inputs#I5). A known limit, named here and in the wrap's a11y-plan §5 text: a non-form
   element with a `disabled` attribute and a `tabindex` (`<div disabled tabindex=0>`) is no longer focusable, where
   browsers apply `disabled` to form controls only and focus it. The recompute on a `disabled` write or
   removal is already wired (`mutator.rs`, a11y-plan §5 Focus order) and is not touched. Readers that move with it
   (research.md §Graph impact): the Tab walk `document.rs:1741`, `:1749`; autofocus `mutator.rs:1042`;
   `unkeyed_actionable` `actionable.rs:70`.

2. **F3 — the three pins restated**: `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs:552-575` (the falsy and bare forms now
   read `is_focussable()` false, `enabled: Some(false)` unchanged, the test renamed to say both);
   `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_state.rs:233-249` (the parsed-markup `fx-falsy` / `fx-bare` read not
   focusable); `tests/blitz-tests/tests/focusability_updates.rs:58-76` (the doc note restated, and one added test: a
   bare `disabled=""` set after creation takes focusability away).

3. **F1 — Enter activates on keydown** (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs:71-118`). In the focused-target
   branch, after the text-input arm and the range arm, a pressed `Key::Enter` on a focused control with no `disabled`
   attribute (presence) dispatches `DomEvent::new(node_id, DomEventData::Click(…))` through `dispatch_event`, its data
   from `Node::synthetic_click_event_data(modifiers)` (`node.rs:1923-1953`) — the pointerup's own route
   (`pointer.rs:628`): a default action's dispatched event is queued (`events/driver.rs:423-426`) and `process_queue`
   runs its handlers, the app's `onclick` among them, then its default action (`events/driver.rs:350-357`), which for a
   `Click` is `handle_click` (`events/mod.rs:214`). Enter
   activates: a `button`; an `input` whose `type` is `submit`, `reset` or `button`; an `a` with `href`; a `summary`.

4. **F1 — Space activates on keyup** (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs:228` routes `DomEventData::KeyUp` to a new
   keyboard-module function; `keyboard.rs`). A released `Key::Character(" ")` whose target is the focused node, with no
   `disabled` attribute, dispatches the same `Click` on: a `button`; an `input` of type `submit`, `reset`, `button`,
   `checkbox` or `radio`; a `summary`. A link takes no Space. A text input and a range input take neither key here
   (their own arms run first and are unchanged). No other key changes.

5. **F2 — a click on a button focuses it** (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:640-866`, `handle_click`). When
   the walk reaches a `button` element or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or `button`, it focuses that element
   through `generate_focus_events` / `set_focus_to` (as the checkbox arm does, :697-704), still submits the form owner
   for a submit button as the arm at :800-806 does today, and ends the walk matched — so the unmatched clear at
   :853-856 no longer runs for it. A `disabled` attribute still stops the walk first (:661-664). Any other element's
   click is unchanged: a click on a CRUD row or on `crud-list` still clears focus (not ruled — `## Constraints`).

6. **F5 — the CRUD list takes focus** (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs:56-82`). `crud-list` gains `tabindex:
   "0"` and an `onkeydown` in the CRUD's own markup, following Cells' handler shape (`cells.rs:390-395`): ArrowDown
   selects the next visible row (the first when none is selected), ArrowUp the previous, Home the first, End the last;
   each selection does what a row's `onclick` does (`selected`, `first_field`, `last_field`); a key at the end of the
   list changes nothing. The list gains no class, style, element or wrapper; its rows gain nothing.

7. **The shared tables** (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`): move `tab_order` from
   `stand_accessibility_ids.rs:18-38` and `focused()` from `stand_snapshot_state.rs:61-77` line for line into the shared
   module, CRUD's sequence restated to `back-btn`, `crud-filter`, `crud-list`, `crud-name`, `crud-surname`,
   `crud-create`; both files read them through `mod common;` and keep no copy.

8. **The new target** `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_keyboard.rs` (`//!` doc naming the behaviour; every scenario `for
   incremental in [false, true]`; each fixture's condition asserted first; failure messages name a layout mode, a task
   and an index, never an id or screen text). Its tests:
   - **Tab walk** — per `LeanTask::ALL` on a fresh boot: nothing focused; Tab `n + 1` times reads the stated sequence
     then wraps to its first; Shift+Tab from there reads it in reverse, wrapping to the last; at every step `focused()`
     returns exactly the expected id.
   - **Activation equals a click** — a stated table, its row count asserted: for every button in the four sequences
     (10 controls, `common::tab_order`), Enter and Space each (20 rows): boot A, Tab to the control, press the key,
     read the snapshot text; boot B, Tab to the control, `click` it, read the snapshot text; the two texts are equal,
     and each row states whether the click changes the screen beyond focus — predicted true for `counter-increment`,
     `flight-return`, `flight-book` and `crud-create`, false for the rest (record what implement measures); at least
     one row reads changed.
   - **Keys that do not activate** — Space on each focused text input (`flight-start`, `crud-filter`, `crud-name`,
     `crud-surname`) inserts a space and Enter changes nothing visible; Enter and Space on `timer-duration` change
     nothing (10 rows).
   - **A minimal fixture beside the stand** (booted with `stand::options(incremental)`): Space toggles a checkbox and a
     radio and Enter does not; Enter fires a link's `onclick` and Space does not; Enter and Space each toggle a
     `details` open through its `summary`; Enter and Space fire an `input type="button"`'s `onclick`; a button
     disabled after it took focus dispatches no click on either key; a button that is itself a scrolled box (its scroll
     offset asserted non-zero first, scrolled by `BaseDocument::scroll_to` as `scrolled_box_absolute_position.rs:63`
     scrolls its box) fires its own
     `onclick` on Enter — the target is right while F4 stands; its event coordinates are not asserted.
   - **A click focuses a button** — per stand button: `click` it on a fresh boot, `focused()` reads that id, and the
     next Tab reads the control after it in the stated sequence.
   - **A disabled attribute of any value is skipped** — parsed markup `a`, `b disabled=""`, `c disabled="false"`,
     `d disabled="true"`, `e` (each attribute asserted present first): Tab from `a` reaches `e`, Shift+Tab back to `a`;
     and a `div disabled tabindex="0"` between them is skipped too — the known limit of step 1, pinned (inputs#I5).
   - **The list takes focus** — on CRUD: Tab three times focuses `crud-list`; ArrowDown selects the first row
     (`selected` true on it alone, the name fields filled as a click fills them), ArrowDown the second, ArrowUp the
     first, End the last, Home the first; `focused()` reads `crud-list` after every key — the gap of `## Goal`, pinned.
   - **The delete binding on every OS** — on CRUD: click `crud-name`, type `Ada`, `apple_keybinding("deleteBackward:")`,
     `editor_text` reads `Ad` (no `press`, so testing.md:52 holds).
   - **`inert` is not honoured** — a fixture with a button under a Dioxus `inert: true` and one under `inert: false`:
     Tab reaches both — the engine implements no `inert` (research.md §Sweeps), pinned and red by design when it does.

9. **The falsy `inert`** (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/dioxus_falsy_boolean_attrs.rs`): `inert` joins the file's table as
   its 28th name, read on both attribute paths: `inert: false` writes no attribute, `inert: true` writes it.

10. **The driver surface** (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_keys.rs`): on Counter, through `Session::run` and
    `session_common`'s `press` builder, Tab twice, then `press enter` names `counter-value` changed with `differs`
    `["name"]`, then `press space` does again — the P3 probe made a standing check.

11. **F2's restated pins**: `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_obstructed.rs` (the plain-button reading: after an accepted
    `click` the button reads `focused` and is the tree's focus); `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_diff.rs` (the Create
    step names `crud-create` gaining focus); then run `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --no-fail-fast` and
    `cargo test -p seven_guis --locked --no-fail-fast` and restate, one by one, each further check whose recorded
    reading was "a button click leaves nothing focused" or a button click's diff — the derived rows of research.md
    §Files to modify; any red with another cause stops the run and is reported.

12. **The gates** of `## Test Commands`, in order; the counts read for the report (workspace result lines, blitz-tests
    files and targets, `common` readers, `run stand`), each measured, never added to the last link.
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_keyboard.rs` — the stand keyboard harness (step 8)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/element.rs` — F3 (step 1)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs` — F1 (steps 3, 4)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs` — F1, the KeyUp routing (step 4)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` — F2 (step 5)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs` — F5 (step 6)
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs` — F3 pin (step 2)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs` — the moved tables (step 7)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_accessibility_ids.rs` — the moved sequence, CRUD restated (step 7)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_state.rs` — the moved helper, F3 pin (steps 2, 7)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/focusability_updates.rs` — F3 (step 2)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/dioxus_falsy_boolean_attrs.rs` — `inert` (step 9)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_keys.rs` — the driver's Enter and Space (step 10)

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_obstructed.rs`, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_diff.rs`, and the derived rows —
  F2 (step 11)

No mutation runs — the founder's word (inputs#I1). A check's power to fail is shown instead by the baselines P5 reads
on the untouched tree (the new target absent; `stand_act_keys`, `stand_accessibility_ids` and the restated pins green
on the old readings that steps 1–6 turn red by design) and by the fixtures' preconditions. No live leg and no
boot-path smoke: the stand boots in process in every check; the windows, macos, ios and android legs and the MSRV
build are read only through the pushed sha's CI run.

- (a11y) On each of the four lean tasks, in both layout modes, Tab walks the stated sequence and wraps, Shift+Tab walks
  it back and wraps, and at every step the stable id, the snapshot's one `focused` node and the tree focus's
  `author_id` name the same control — `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_keyboard` (per a11y-plan §5 Test
  harness pattern; a11y-plan §3).

- (a11y) Enter and Space on every focused stand button yield the same snapshot text as a pointer click on it, 20 rows
  stated and counted, at least one row changing the screen; the 10 non-activating rows read as stated — the same entry
  (per a11y-plan §5 Keyboard handling; a11y-plan §1, SC 2.1.1).

- (a11y) The fixture rows hold: checkbox and radio by Space, link by Enter, summary by both, `input type="button"` by
  both, no click from a control whose `disabled` attribute appeared after it took focus, and a self-scrolled button's
  own `onclick` on Enter — the same entry (per a11y-plan §5 Keyboard handling).

- (a11y) A click on each stand button focuses it, and the next Tab continues from it — the same entry, and the restated
  `stand_act_obstructed` and `stand_act_diff` in `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_accessibility_ids
  --test stand_snapshot_state --test focusability_updates --test dioxus_falsy_boolean_attrs --test stand_act_keys
  --test stand_act_obstructed --test stand_act_diff --test stand_actionable_keys` (per a11y-plan §5 Focus restoration).

- (a11y) Tab skips a control whose `disabled` attribute is bare, `"false"` or `"true"`, and the three restated F3 pins
  pass — `stand_keyboard`, `cargo test -p dioxus-native-dom --locked` and the restated-pins entry (per a11y-plan §5
  Focus order per layout; security-plan §Input Validation, the `disabled` row).

- (a11y) On CRUD, Tab's third stop is `crud-list`; ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End move `selected` and fill the name
  fields as a click does; `focused()` reads `crud-list` throughout — the stated gap — and `stand_accessibility_ids`
  reads the restated CRUD sequence (per a11y-plan §5 Per-surface keyboard shortcuts; layout-templates §Surface:
  desktop-native → Primary screens).

- (tests) `apple_keybinding("deleteBackward:")` deletes one character in `stand_keyboard` on the linux leg, and the
  windows and macos jobs of the pushed sha's run read green — `python -X utf8
  ~/.claude/skills/andromeda-tools/scripts/ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1800` (per test-plan §3 Input helpers).

- (tests) Through the driver, `press enter` and `press space` on a Tab-focused `counter-increment` each name
  `counter-value` changed with `differs: ["name"]` — `stand_act_keys` in the restated-pins entry (per test-plan §3).

- (tests) `dioxus_falsy_boolean_attrs` reads `inert` as its 28th name: absent under `inert: false`, present under
  `inert: true`, both attribute paths; and `stand_keyboard` pins Tab reaching content under either (per a11y-plan §5
  Script and framework exposure; security-plan §Input Validation, the falsy boolean row).

- (tests) Every entry of `## Test Commands` reads its `expect`, `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run stand` included, and
  `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` and `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` pass (per test-plan §9; CLAUDE.md
  Critical Warnings).

- (security) No package enters `Cargo.lock`, and no added engine, bridge or stand line prints, logs, reads env or adds
  an unwrap, expect or panic — the two census probes (per security-plan §Dependency Security; security-plan §Input
  Validation).

- (obs) `stand_keyboard` installs no subscriber, reads no env var and prints nothing — the silence probe (per obs-plan
  §3 Logging stack).

- Spec anchors: a11y-plan §1, §3, §5, §7 · test-plan §1, §3, §4, §9 · architecture §Conventions → Tests, §Standard
  Contracts (Events, Dioxus DOM bridge, Test harness, Headless stand), §Established Decisions ([DOM semantics],
  [Scrolling and input]) · security-plan §Input Validation (the `disabled`, `input type="range"` and falsy boolean
  rows), §Error Handling, §Dependency Security, §Logging & Monitoring · obs-plan §2, §3, §4, §6, §8 · layout-templates
  §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens, IA notes · design-system §Color Palette → Core Colors, §Typography →
  Loading, §Motion → Animation runtime.

- Research files inspected: research.md §Files inspected (24 reads); the P3 driver probe
  `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-13T22-07-35-phase/probe-counter.txt`.

- Leans: the reach of F1 and F2 to `input type="submit|reset|button"` — leaned per inputs#I3's F1 option text ("a
  submit button submits", which in HTML includes the submit input) and kept equal for F2 so a Tab-reachable input
  button behaves as a `button` does — confirmed by the operator at P5 (inputs#I5). F3 for every element — leaned per
  inputs#I3 ("any `disabled` attribute removes focusability") and `pointer.rs:661-664`, confirmed by the operator on
  condition that the `<div disabled tabindex=0>` divergence from browsers is named as a known limit (inputs#I5).

- The two extract claims built on falsified scope bullets are overridden here (codebase-research §Scope premise
  closure): "content under `inert: false` is reached by Tab" (a11y and security extracts) is replaced by the attribute
  check plus the pinned limit (step 9, step 8); "the target pin moves" (a11y, security, obs extracts) by "the pin is
  unchanged" (`test_blitz_tests_targets.py:18-30`).

- Fix `Node::absolute_position` here — rejected by the founder's word (F4, «Отложить (Рекомендую)», inputs#I3); its
  CARRY moves to "Stand requirement sweep" (the review card's `## Beyond the plan`).

- Activate by calling `handle_click` directly, as the label arm does — rejected: it runs the default action only and
  skips the app's `onclick` (research.md §Open questions).

- Space on keydown — rejected: HTML activates a button on Space's keyup; `press` and the driver send both, so nothing
  the harness drives depends on it.

- An engine listbox keyboard model, or reading `aria-activedescendant` in the accessibility builder — not this chunk
  (F5 is stand markup only, inputs#I4); the builder's read is the new CARRY's.

- A click that focuses every focusable element (a `tabindex` div, the CRUD list, a row) — not ruled: F2 covers buttons
  (inputs#I3); a click on a CRUD row still leaves nothing focused, recorded with the new CARRY.
- Implementing `inert` in the engine — not ruled; pinned as the measured limit and given a route owner.

- Narrowing F3 to the form controls `disabled` applies to (`button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`) — not this chunk:
  the operator kept today's reach, any element (inputs#I5); the narrowing is a CARRY on "Stand requirement sweep"
  (escher-0.1.0/working-route.md:96), and the divergence is a known limit until then.
- No `press(Key::Backspace)` in the new check (testing.md:52), no `dispatch_recorded`, no font skip, no sleep.
- No mutation run and no hand mutation control (inputs#I1).

- The CRUD sequence moves from 5 stops to 6 (`stand_accessibility_ids.rs:31-37`, plus `crud-list`); the other three are
  unchanged (`back-btn` first on each, read at `stand_accessibility_ids.rs:18-38`).

- 24 standing files click a stand button (research.md §Sweeps, `command grep -lE` over `tests/blitz-tests/tests/*.rs` and
  `examples/seven_guis/tests/*.rs`); predicted: only those that pin a focus reading or an exact `changed` list after a
  button click turn red under F2 — record which, by the step 11 runs.

- `back-btn` is a no-op in the headless stand (`stand.rs:117`, `EventHandler::new(|_| {})`), so its activation rows
  change nothing but focus.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Established Decisions → [Scrolling and input] — three direct engine changes
  for every document (keyboard activation in `events/keyboard.rs` and `events/mod.rs`; a click focuses a button in
  `events/pointer.rs`; focusability by `disabled` presence in `node/element.rs`), each ratified by the founder
  (2026-10-13, his labels verbatim, relayed verbatim by the overseer, inputs#I3) — the playbook's engine-change rule
  (`.andromeda/playbook.md:64`), each upstreamable against 434e0661, the merge surface owned by a CARRY on "Quality
  gates"; §Standard Contracts → Events (KeyUp gains a default action).

- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan §Input Validation — a new row for keyboard activation in every document,
  remote pages included (Enter and Space reach the click default actions: form submission, link navigation, `summary`
  toggling), gated on `disabled` presence, with no print, log site or panic path — the Boundary widening pattern
  (`.andromeda/playbook.md:36`), answered by the founder himself (F1, «Клавиши нажимают (Рекомендую)», relayed verbatim,
  inputs#I3), so the wrap halts on it once, as the answer card; the `disabled` row's split closed by F3.

- Expected amendments (wrap): a11y-plan §5 — Focus order (presence, on every element; a known limit stated in the text:
  a `<div disabled tabindex=0>` is not focusable, where browsers focus it, the narrowing owned by "Stand requirement
  sweep", inputs#I5), Focus restoration (a click focuses a button; a row
  or list click still clears focus), Keyboard handling (activation), Per-surface keyboard shortcuts (the CRUD list and
  its keys; the tree's focus is the list), Script and framework exposure (the engine honours no `inert`; the claim "so
  it no longer makes content inert" amended to the measured limit), Test harness pattern (`stand_keyboard`); §8 the
  restated CRUD sequence.

- Expected amendments (wrap): test-plan §1, §3, §4 — the new target, the restated pins, the file, target, `common`
  reader and `run stand` counts as measured; obs-plan §3 — `stand_keyboard` in the silent census, the `common` reader
  count; layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens — `crud-list` takes a `tabindex`, the CRUD Tab order
  moves.

**Chunk:** Stand keyboard harness — Tab, Shift+Tab and activation keys dispatched headlessly on the stand, the focused node read back per step
**Date:** 2026-10-13
**Commits:** since `last_wrap` 2026-10-13T21:44:39Z — `71af33d06 chore(2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk verdict reads` (`git log --format='%h %s' e40d9437..HEAD`)

- **Symbols / APIs:** (coordinates from `## New text, by line`)
  - **F3 — focusability by presence, in every document** (founder, «По наличию (Рекомендую)», inputs#I3):
    - `ElementData::flush_is_focussable` reads `disabled` by presence
      (`self.has_attr(local_name!("disabled"))`, packages/blitz-dom/src/node/element.rs:703), where it parsed a
      boolean through `attr_parsed`. Any `disabled` attribute — bare, `"false"`, `"true"` — on ANY element now removes
      focusability.
    - Known limit, pinned (operator's condition, inputs#I5): a `<div disabled tabindex=0>` is no longer focusable,
      where browsers apply `disabled` to form controls only and focus it.
    - Readers that move with it (research §Graph impact): the Tab walk `focus_next_node` / `focus_prev_node`;
      autofocus `mutator.rs` (a disabled-attributed autofocus candidate is now skipped);
      `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` (`actionable.rs`).
    - The recompute on a `disabled` write is unchanged.
  - **F1 — keyboard activation, in every document** (founder, «Клавиши нажимают (Рекомендую)», inputs#I3):
    - In `handle_key_or_input_event` (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs:118-123): a pressed `Key::Enter`
      whose target is the focused node, after the text-input arm and the range arm, dispatches
      `DomEvent::new(node, DomEventData::Click(..))` when `activates_on_enter` holds. It holds for an element with no
      `disabled` attribute (presence) that is a `button`, a `summary`, an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or
      `button`, or an `a` with `href` (keyboard.rs:150-165).
    - New `pub(crate) fn handle_key_up` (keyboard.rs:128-148): a released `Key::Character(" ")` targeting the
      focused node dispatches the same Click when `activates_on_space` holds (keyboard.rs:167-181). It holds for an
      element with no `disabled` attribute that is a `button`, a `summary`, or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset`,
      `button`, `checkbox` or `radio`. A link takes no Space; a text input and a range input take neither key here.
    - `dispatch_activation_click` (keyboard.rs:183-193) builds the event data from
      `Node::synthetic_click_event_data(modifiers)`. The Click is queued by the event driver, so the app's handlers
      (a Dioxus `onclick`) run, then its default action `handle_click`.
    - `events/mod.rs` routes `DomEventData::KeyUp` to `handle_key_up` (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs:12,
      :228-229). KeyUp had no default action before.
    - `synthetic_click_event_data` keeps its other callers (`handle_click`'s label arm, `Node::synthetic_click_event`);
      `absolute_position` is untouched (F4).
  - **F2 — a click focuses a button, in every document** (founder, «Клик даёт фокус (Рекомендую)», inputs#I3):
    - `handle_click`'s submit arm (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:800-821) became a button arm. It matches
      a `button` (any type) or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or `button`.
    - It focuses the control through `generate_focus_events` / `set_focus_to`, then submits the form owner when
      `is_submit_button()` or `type == "submit"`, and ends the walk matched.
    - Before: a submit button submitted without breaking the walk, and every other button fell through to the
      unmatched clear of focus.
    - A `disabled` attribute still stops the walk first. A click on any other element is unchanged: a CRUD row or the
      list still clears focus.
  - **F5 — the CRUD list takes focus** (operator, "List takes focus", inputs#I4), stand markup only
    (examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs:59-86, :91, :172-178):
    - `crud-list` gains `tabindex: "0"` and an `onkeydown`. ArrowDown selects the next visible row (the first when none
      is selected); ArrowUp the previous; Home the first; End the last. A key at the end of the list changes nothing,
      and so does ArrowUp with no row selected.
    - Each selection sets `selected`, `first_field` and `last_field` as a row's `onclick` does.
    - The filter predicate moved into a private `fn shown(person, filter_lower)` read by the render and the handler.
    - No class, style, element, wrapper or row change.
  - **Tests' shared module** (tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs:48-70, :72-92):
    - `pub fn tab_order(task)` moved from `stand_accessibility_ids.rs`. CRUD restated to `back-btn`, `crud-filter`,
      `crud-list`, `crud-name`, `crud-surname`, `crud-create` (6 stops, was 5).
    - `pub fn focused(harness)` moved from `stand_snapshot_state.rs`.
    - The module now imports `blitz_dom::Document`.

- **Crates / modules:** none added or removed. Changed: blitz-dom (`node/element.rs`, `events/{keyboard,mod,pointer}.rs`),
  dioxus-native-dom (a unit test in `snapshot.rs`), seven_guis (`tasks/crud.rs`), blitz-tests (one new target).
- **Dependencies:** none — gate `git diff e40d9437… -- Cargo.lock | grep -c '^+\[\[package\]\]'` reads 0.

- **Schema / config:** none. No driver schema, no `KEY_NAMES` change: `enter`, `space`, `arrow-*`, `home` and `end` were
  already in it (packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:14-27, unchanged — gate `git diff --quiet … packages/escher-driver …`).
- **Spec-master edits:** none (the masters are read-only to implement; this wrap's P2 owns them).

    `stand_keyboard` 11, `stand_act_keys` +1 and `focusability_updates` +1. Basis: `target/ci-logs/test.log` of

body: - **is_focussable** — read at `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:1741` and `:1749` (the Tab walk), `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:1042` (autofocus), `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/actionable.rs:70` (`unkeyed_actionable`), and pinned by `snapshot.rs:563`, `stand_snapshot_state.rs:240`, `focusability_updates.rs:38-75`, `stand_actionable_keys.rs:68` — a presence-keyed fix moves the Tab walk, autofocus and the actionable census for every document and rewrites three pins.
- **focus_next_node / focus_prev_node** — called by `keyboard.rs:34` / `:36` and by the checks `stand_accessibility_ids.rs:89` and `stand_snapshot.rs:226`.

- **absolute_position** — read by `handle_dom_event` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/mod.rs:109`), itself recursively (`node.rs:1689`), `synthetic_click_event_data` (`node.rs:1929`), `Node::focus` (`node.rs:732`, the IME cursor area), `scroll_into_view` (`scrolling.rs:720`), the harness's `layout_rect_of` (`inspect.rs:60`) and `write_node` (`inspect.rs:142`), and by three checks (`anonymous_block_restyle.rs:100`, `stale_dirty_descendants.rs:81-100`, `scrolled_box_absolute_position.rs:44-74`) — a fix moves seven engine and harness readers for every document.

- **synthetic_click_event_data** — called by `handle_click`'s label arm (`pointer.rs:769`), `Node::synthetic_click_event` (`node.rs:1925`) and the bridge's uncalled `synthetic_click_event` (`events.rs:662`): the one engine path a key activation would reuse.

- **apple_keybinding** — the graph returned no `calls` row for it though its `symbol` row stands (`input.rs:230`, a second query); grep finds its one caller, `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:483`, under `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]`, which the Linux-built index does not see — not a leaf: no standing check calls it on this host.

- **The focus read-back helper** (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_state.rs:61-77`): the snapshot's `focused` ids asserted equal to the tree focus's `author_id`, returned for the caller's assertion — private to that file today.
- **A stated sequence read by the engine's walk** (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_accessibility_ids.rs:18-38`): the expected order is a table, never computed from the engine.
- **Measured-and-pinned, red by design when fixed** (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/scrolled_box_absolute_position.rs`): the shape for every defect a fork leaves standing.
- **A row table with its count asserted** (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/range_input_interaction.rs:113-135`): the shape for an activation table, one row per control and key.

- **One behaviour, one target file**: `//!` doc, `for incremental in [false, true]`, fixture condition asserted first; shared tables in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs` only (testing.md:15, :21-23).

- **A `stand_` prefix puts a file under `run stand`** with no script change (`scripts/agent-run.sh`, verification-harness.md:18); `range_input_interaction` chose no prefix and runs on the `test` leg alone.

- **No platform-bound key through `press`** (testing.md:52): leaned — a direct `apple_keybinding("deleteBackward:")` is not `press` and is not platform-bound (`text.rs:372` has no gate), so it is the every-OS witness CARRY 5 asks for.
- **Failure messages name a layout mode, a task and an index, never an id or screen text** (tests-history, 2026-10-07-act-by-id).

title: Folded freight (the seven CARRY blocks at working-route.md:92)

data.head: ## Folded freight (the seven CARRY blocks at working-route.md:92)

body:
1. **Focus defects from 2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity.** (1) A control whose `disabled` attribute is bare or
   `"false"` reads not enabled in the snapshot yet stays focusable (measured: `is_focussable()` true beside
   `enabled: Some(false)`, in the dioxus-native-dom unit pin and `stand_snapshot_state`'s parsed-markup pin; the
   bridge itself writes neither form). A Tab and Shift+Tab key-press focus check already exists in
   `stand_snapshot_state`.
   - Whether this chunk fixes defect (1) is fork F3: `flush_is_focussable` reads `disabled` by `attr_parsed`
     (`element.rs:703`) for every document, read again by the Tab walk, autofocus and `unkeyed_actionable`, and pinned
     by three checks (`research.md` §Graph impact) — an engine change for every document (playbook :64, inputs#I1).

2. The CARRY's own hypothesis, kept verbatim: "(2) hypothesis: a click on a plain `button` clears focus instead of
   focusing it (read from the code at that chunk's phase — pointer.rs `handle_click` has no button arm; measured there
   only for a click on a heading)" — verified at HEAD: no arm matches a plain `button`, so the walk ends unmatched and
   focus is cleared (`pointer.rs:853-856`); measured on `counter-increment` (P3 probe above).

3. **A reading for the plain-button focus hypothesis (from 2026-10-07-act-by-id).** A driver click on `crud-create`
   while `crud-surname` held focus returned `crud-surname` among `changed` — it lost focus — and named no node as
   gaining it (measured at `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_diff.rs`, the Create step, both layout modes);
   `stand_act_keys` adds a driver-run Tab and Shift+Tab focus check on CRUD.

4. **The plain-button focus reading, measured (from 2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit).** After an accepted driver
   `click` on a plain `button` no node reads `focused` and the accessibility tree's focus carries no author id, in both
   layout modes and under both builds (the restated `stand_act_obstructed`; a11y-plan §5 → Focus restoration).
   "Whether a click should focus a button is decided at this entry's promotion."
   - That decision is fork F2: a click that focuses a `button` changes `handle_click` (`pointer.rs:640-866`) for every
     document — the founder's (playbook :64; inputs#I1) — and 24 standing check files click a stand button
     (`research.md` §Sweeps), each a candidate pin on that branch.

5. **The delete binding has one witness (from 2026-10-07-act-by-id).** `Harness::apple_keybinding` dispatches a macOS
   standard key binding to the focused element; its one standing check is the driver's `press backspace` in
   `stand_act_keys`, which reaches it on the macOS CI leg only (CI#37633611745, `Test (macos)`); on Linux and Windows
   no standing check calls it (read once on Linux through a deleted probe,
   escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-act-by-id/evidence/controls.md).
   - This chunk adds a standing check that calls `Harness::apple_keybinding` on every OS — feasible: the editor's
     `apply_apple_standard_keybinding` carries no platform gate (`text.rs:372`), and a direct call is not the
     platform-bound `press` testing.md:52 forbids.

6. **The second position reader reads a scrolled box shifted (from 2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit).**
   `Node::absolute_position` answers, for a box that is itself scrolled, the box's position less its own scroll offset
   ((40, 50) scrolled by (70, 120) reads (−30, −70)), both layout modes and both builds, pinned by
   `scrolled_box_absolute_position` (red by design when the reader is fixed — rewritten then, not deleted);
   `get_client_bounding_rect` reads where the box stands, so the two disagree. Built on the unfixed reader (re-derived
   by the graph at P3): `handle_dom_event`, `synthetic_click_event_data`, `Node::focus`'s IME area, `scroll_into_view`
   and the harness's `layout_rect_of` and `write_node`. The fix is an engine change for every document in
   upstream-owned merge surface (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs`), upstreamable.
   - Whether this chunk fixes the reader is fork F4 — an engine change for every document (playbook :64; inputs#I1).

7. The CARRY's own hypothesis, kept verbatim: "hypothesis: an activation key on a focused box that is itself scrolled
   clicks off its centre by that offset (read from the code, not measured — no stand control that takes a key is
   itself a scrolled box)". [premise-corrected: at HEAD no key synthesizes a click (`keyboard.rs:71-118`), so the
   hypothesis has no path; it gains one only if F1 activates through `synthetic_click_event_data`, whose point reads
   `absolute_position` (`node.rs:1929`) — the click's target is the node either way, only the event's coordinates
   would be off.]

8. **A listbox option no keyboard reaches (from 2026-10-10-snapshot-states).** Each CRUD row states `role="option"` in
   a `listbox` with no `tabindex`, so Tab never lands on a row and no key selects one (`crud.rs:56-82`: an `onclick`
   only); the CRUD's forward focus sequence is held by `stand_accessibility_ids`; a `tabindex` on the rows moves the
   Tab order that plan pins. "How an option is reached by keyboard — and the pinned Tab order restated with it — is
   decided at this entry's promotion."
   - That decision is fork F5; a stand-markup answer (a `tabindex` and a key handler in the CRUD's own markup) changes
     the app only and is the operator's, while an engine listbox keyboard model would change every document.

9. **A falsy Dioxus `inert` (from 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship).** The bridge clears a framework-written
   `inert: false` by upstream's 28-name `is_bool_attr` (`mutation_writer.rs:458`), so the content stays focusable; no

title: Plan — 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship: "Upstream sync ahead of polish and ship"

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship: "Upstream sync ahead of polish and ship"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship · **Version:** escher-0.1.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-13T14:50:00Z
- **Chunk start commit:** `a703136878e47c0cf583448bbac02f06f8365be5` (HEAD at P4; every git-diff base below names it or a fixed upstream sha)
- **Upstream pin:** `434e06615d5f47a3df92c0f94e916df088fdcf4d` (inputs#I1) · merge base `7832c177ff272128154bac58afe56c2b9164b417`

Merge DioxusLabs/blitz `upstream/main` at `434e06615` — 16 commits, 45 files — into `build/escher-0.1.0` as a true merge with both parents kept, and prove our logic survived it (`escher-0.1.0/intent.md` §Principles, "Upstream stays in reach"). The delta is small but reaches the bridge escher is built on: Dioxus-removed nodes are now dropped (#1185), Dioxus attributes move to the empty namespace (#1186), falsy boolean attributes are cleared upstream (#1188, the behaviour we carried), UA stylesheets are shared and passed as parsed sheets (#1189), and Taffy leaves its git pin for the registry's 0.15.

Two files conflict, both in dioxus-native-dom; the resolution takes upstream's falsy-attribute predicate and drops our copy of it — a de-fork (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge; scope). Research found three things a clean merge would hide (research.md; scope premise closure): one unit test of ours asserts the old detached-node lifetime and turns red, the textually merged lock refuses `--locked` until our two workspace crates read the new version, and #1186 makes the UA sheet's attribute selectors match Dioxus elements for the first time. The front page is brought to eleven driver verbs and the built screenshot (the folded README CARRY).

The proof is counted, not read off an exit code: the workspace gate, the per-package stand run, the a11y leg and the agent-run contract each pass; every test file is shown by name to have run, upstream's five new files among them as targets of their own; upstream's single-binary target is shown absent from every leg; our merge surfaces are read whole after the merge; and fork CI is read green on a run left to settle (per test-plan §3 and §9; a11y-plan §9; security-plan §Dependency Security; obs-plan §8). No mutation tier runs (the founder's word, inputs#I2).

1. **Pre-merge reading (on `a703136`, before any merge).** Run `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh test` and write the per-target table — one row per `Running …` line with its `test result:` counts, from the one merged stream — and the totals to `evidence/counts.md` with the sha and the date. The last recorded figures (174 result lines, 849 passed · 0 failed · 12 ignored, test-plan §9 at 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) describe this tree, but the per-target rows are what the post-merge attribution is read against, so they are taken, not copied.

2. **Confirm the pin.** `git rev-parse upstream/main` reads `434e06615d5f47a3df92c0f94e916df088fdcf4d`. If upstream has moved, merge the PIN anyway and record both shas in `evidence/merge.md` (scope: moving the pin is the operator's call).

3. **Merge without committing.** `git merge --no-ff --no-commit 434e06615d5f47a3df92c0f94e916df088fdcf4d`. The merge stops on conflicts with `MERGE_HEAD` set; /implement never commits. `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` must list exactly `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs` and `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/mutation_writer.rs` (the P3 trial merge, tree `2481e052`, inputs#I1). Any other conflicted path contradicts it: HALT, do not resolve it by hand. The phase's own uncommitted files (`.andromeda/`, `escher-0.1.0/`) are outside the merge's paths and stay as they are.

4. **Resolve `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs`.** Both sides stay: the events line reads `pub use events::{NodeHandle, synthetic_click_event, synthetic_form_event};`, and our three `#[cfg(feature = "accessibility")]` re-exports (`snapshot`, `snapshot_diff`, `snapshot_text`) follow it unchanged.

5. **Resolve `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/mutation_writer.rs`.** The region takes upstream's side, `if is_falsy && is_bool_attr(local_name) {`, and our `BOOLEAN_ATTRIBUTES` constant with its doc comment (`mutation_writer.rs:11-41` at the chunk start, its one reference the conflicted line, per the code graph) is deleted. Upstream's `is_bool_attr` (28 names: our 27 and `inert`) and its two unit tests arrive by the merge. `set_attribute_inner` remains the one site both attribute paths reach (`mutation_writer.rs:300-315` dynamic, `:396` static at the chunk start), so the clear still covers both. Record in `evidence/merge.md`: our constant retired in favour of upstream's predicate, and the one name it adds.

6. **Bring `a_removed_element_reads_no_id` to the dropped-node lifetime** (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs:396-431`). After `render(&mut doc, false)` the test asserts that the removed `p` no longer resolves (`get_node(removed)` is `None`), that `element_id(removed)` is `None`, and that `element_ids()` lists no pair with that node. The detached-parent assertion (`:421-422`) and the hand call to `remove_node_if_unparented` (`:425-428`, which after #1185 would be handed a dropped id) go; the comment above them says removal drops the node and its id with it (upstream #1185). The test name and the first assertions (`:409-410`) stay. This is a test of ours whose premise the merged engine changes, recorded as such in the report.

7. **Refresh the lock's two workspace entries.** `cargo update --workspace`, then compare the lock's `name@version` set against upstream's lock at the pin with our two `escher-*` entries set aside (the lock-set entry below): equal, with `escher-driver` and `escher-telemetry` now at `0.3.0-beta.3` → record the changed stanzas in `evidence/lock.md`; any other entry moved → HALT for the operator. Never a bare `cargo update`, never a version bump of a third-party crate (security-plan §Dependency Security, Pinning).

8. **Bring the front page current** (`README.md:48`, the folded CARRY). "gets the ten driver commands as tools" becomes "gets the eleven driver commands as tools", and the closing sentence "Its screenshot is still to come." becomes one sentence that the `screenshot` command returns the whole screen, or one element of it by `--id`, as a PNG, and that an MCP client receives it as an image. No other line of the README moves.
9. **Run the gate block** (`## Test Commands`) on the merged, uncommitted tree.

10. **On a red gate.**
    - A build, fmt, clippy or rustdoc red on merged code: the minimal edit to the named file, recorded as non-additive in the report and, where the file is outside research's two lists, in `chunks/2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship/scope-record.md`.
    - A check that reads a new NUMBER under the merged engine (a bound, a snapshot's byte size, a pixel, an accepted or refused count): do not edit the expectation. Re-run that check's file with `--no-fail-fast`, collect every moved reading across both layout modes into `evidence/moved-readings.md`, and soft-exit ONCE with that table for the operator's word. Each row holds old → new, the entry or check that read it, where it is stated, and its CAUSE as one of two words: `upstream tests added` — a tally that moved because the delta adds a test, the upstream commit or file named, no expectation of ours touched; or `our check reads differently` — an assertion of ours meeting a new value from the merged engine, the check, its row and the layout modes named. Only rows of the second class wait on the word. On the word, each value is restated where it is stated once (the shared tables of `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`, or the check's own in-file table), never widened into a tolerance, and the stand's markup, ids, CSS, viewport and font stay untouched. With no row of the second class there is no stop, and the table is still written.
    - A red in one of upstream's five new test files, or in upstream's new unit tests, under our build: upstream's test is never edited. Record the failing test, its assertion and the layout mode in `evidence/moved-readings.md` under the cause `upstream test meets our engine change`, and soft-exit for the operator's word with the table.
    - A red that would need one side of a coupled pin moved, a third-party lock change, a narrowed `a11y` leg, a widened sink allowlist or a log field: HALT for the operator.

12. **Record for later entries, in the report and not in code:** upstream's new APIs escher does not use (`synthetic_form_event`, `UserAgentStylesheet`, `UiEvent::PointerLeave`); that #1186 lets the UA sheet's and the stand's own attribute selectors match Dioxus elements — on the four lean tasks no rule is predicted to newly match, while Circle Drawer's `.cd-dialog input[type="range"]` (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/circle_drawer.rs:215`) applies for the first time — for "Stand requirement sweep"; and that a falsy `inert` is now cleared.
- `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship/evidence/` — the six records of step 11
- Five files arrive by the merge: `tests/blitz-tests/tests/{anonymous_block_restyle,button_alignment,checked_attribute,pointer_leave,ua_stylesheet_order}.rs` (research.md §Files to modify lists each)
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs` — step 4
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/mutation_writer.rs` — step 5; `BOOLEAN_ATTRIBUTES` @ mutation_writer.rs:439 is the constant's one reference (graph `refs`)
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs` — step 6
- `Cargo.lock` — by merge, then step 7's two entries
- `README.md` — step 8
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs` — only under step 10's second rule, on the operator's word

- The other 40 files change by the merge alone (research.md §Files to modify, each listed), our hunks in them kept as merged: the 15 changed-set marks of `mutator.rs`, the changed set, readers and bounds reader of `document.rs`, `hit_inner` in `node/node.rs`, the mask in `render.rs`, the refresh in `window.rs`, the four hunks of `dioxus_document.rs`

The gates below run in /implement P2 on the merged, uncommitted tree and again in the wrap's light gate on the committed merge. Their git bases are the chunk start commit `a703136` or the two fixed upstream shas, so they read the same after the operator's pre-CI commit.

- **Merge witness and guards** — the witness is green when the pin is `MERGE_HEAD` (before the operator's commit) or an ancestor of HEAD (after it). The probes after it read: no conflict marker left; our root-manifest lines kept; upstream's pin set taken, with no git Taffy left; the lock resolving as committed, our two entries at beta.3 and its third-party set equal to upstream's; the fork's own scripts, workflows, stand, driver, telemetry, harness and inherited-engine surfaces untouched; every merge surface of ours read present after the merge (changed-set marks, the mask's two functions, the two readers, both bodies of the bounds reader, `hit_inner`, the tree override and `bridge_tests`, the shell's refresh); the conflict resolutions in place; and a fixed-sha census of upstream's delta.
- **The `test = false` reading is three entries**, as at the last sync: the workspace build set lists no `tests/all.rs` executable, the workspace test log runs none, and the a11y leg's log runs none.

- **By-name presence** — one entry walks `tests/blitz-tests/tests/*.rs` and counts the files, `all.rs` aside, whose `Running tests/{name}.rs` line is absent from the workspace test log; upstream's five new files are among those it reads. A second entry reads the five by name.

- **Both builds** — `ci-leg.sh fast` runs the workspace build (blitz-dom's `tracing` and `writing-mode` compiled in); `agent-run.sh run stand` and `run all` run `-p blitz-tests`; `cargo test -p seven_guis` runs the two sink-installing hosts' needle checks (`host_log`, `mcp_log`) in the per-package build (test-plan §9 Engine features by runner; obs-plan §8).

- **Counts** — the workspace tally is asserted on `failed 0` and recorded against the prediction in step 11; the CI-scripts tally is report-only because its number is a forecast (78 today; predicted 79 — upstream's one added test in `test_wpt_area_changes.py`); the a11y leg's 3 result lines and 15 passed are asserted, since the merge changes none of its three files.

- **Not run locally:** `msrv` (`cargo +1.91`) and the wasm leg — no 1.91 toolchain or wasm32 target on this host, and `taffy 0.15.0` is not in the local registry, so its MSRV is the CI job's reading — and the windows, macos, ios and android legs. The operator entries push the merge and read the run that covers them; the last entry reads that our checks ran in the macOS and Windows jobs.

- **Windowed boot smoke** — listed because the merge changes layout and UA styling under `seven_guis_native`. It declares `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, turns `timeout`'s 124 into its own exit 0 (`.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` Session Additions 2026-10-06) and reads `not run — env unset` without a display.
- **No mutation entry** — the mutation tier stays unstarted on the founder's word (inputs#I2); no entry runs mutants.

- **No live leg**: nothing here drives a process the launch environment names. **The evidence records have no listed producer, by construction**: the six records of step 11 are /implement's and the operator pass's hand records of what the entries read, and `counts.md`'s pre-merge half is step 1's one-shot reading on `a703136`, which no entry can re-run on the merged tree. No entry carries one of them as `artifact`.

Additivity is a preference, not a goal: where staying additive would force contorted logic, the upstream code is changed directly (founder, 2026-10-06).

Upstream now carries the behaviour ours added, so the resolution takes upstream's predicate and drops our constant — a de-fork that shrinks our merge surface. Verified at P3 (research.md, both lists read whole): upstream's list holds all 27 of ours and one more, `inert`, so no name of ours is lost and a falsy `inert` is now cleared too; the 27-name contract becomes upstream's 28, read at the same one site, `set_attribute_inner` (mutation_writer.rs:413 at HEAD), which both attribute paths reach — the dynamic `set_attribute` arms (:300-315) and the static template path (`create_template_node`, :396) — and is recorded so at the wrap.

data.head: ## The upstream delta (16 commits, 45 files, +2147 −208; inputs#I1)

body: - Dependency pins: Taffy moves from a git `rev` (`7d33901c`) to the registry release `0.15` (`ec782197`); the workspace version 0.3.0-beta.2 → 0.3.0-beta.3 with its nine in-repo `=` pins; `blitz-vibey-script` gains `publish = false`; `tests/blitz-tests` gains the dev-dependency `cursor-icon`.

- Engine behaviour: nodes Dioxus removes are dropped in dioxus-native-dom (#1185); a `synthetic_form_event` and the empty namespace for Dioxus attributes (#1186); a checkbox or radio unchecked when its `checked` attribute is removed (#1187); falsy boolean attributes removed (#1188); parsed UA stylesheets and their cascade data shared across documents (#1189); hover ended when the pointer leaves the window or a sub-document's host (#1176); the cursor set after a sub-document handled the event (#1177); UA flex centering no longer leaking into author-styled buttons (#1175); anonymous box styles refreshed in incremental damage propagation (#1174); object-fit on SVG images and object-fit/object-position overflow clipped to the content box (#1194, #1195).
- Tests and CI: five new test files; `.github/scripts/wpt_area_changes.py` and its test (#1183); two WPT pin bumps (`wpt/WPT_COMMIT`).

    no family (a `FontContext` over an empty `Collection` with system fonts off — the shape of `build_single_font_ctx`,
    `packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs:134-150`, with no font) and a hand `NetProvider` that holds every request, offline.
    Assert, in both layout modes: exactly one font request is made and its URL is the `data:` source; before it is
    answered the element's text lays out with no width; answered with `seven_guis::DEJAVU_SANS` (`wOF2`), the text
    lays out with a width — the body was sniffed (`net.rs:310-331`), decompressed and registered under `Sniffed` by
    the family override, which invalidates the inline contexts so the next pass lays the text out again
    (`packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:1415-1451`); a second document
    answered with four bytes no sniff matches lays its text out with no width (`Resource::None`, `net.rs:368-371`). The
    first assertion of the file is the fixture's own condition (no width before the answer). It installs no
    subscriber and prints nothing (per obs-plan §3).

20. **The three stderr readings (CARRY 10).** Taken under both builds (`cargo build -p seven_guis` and the workspace
    build), each at `RUST_LOG` unset · `info` · `debug` · `trace`, line counts by target and the needle counts (0 id ·
    0 name · 0 typed sentinel · 0 of a shot's first 64 base64 characters — per obs-plan §8): (a) the `escher-session`
    client's own stderr on a start · snapshot · click · type · screenshot · stop flow; (b) the session host on the
    Counter and Flight booker flows (`examples/seven_guis/tests/flows/{counter,flight}.sh`'s commands), beside the
    CRUD reading already recorded; (c) the windowed `seven_guis_native` under the workspace build, Home for 10 s per
    level, each run started as `timeout 10 target/debug/seven_guis_native` so the `timeout` the step starts ends it
    (no process is signalled by name), as the 2026-10-07 reading of the build alone was taken; (a) and (b) end each
    session they start with `escher-session stop` on its own state directory. State directories relative, `target/tmp/qg-*`
    (host-linux rule, 94-byte bound). Record in `evidence/stderr-by-level.md`; a reading the host cannot take (no
    display for (c)) is written as not measured with its reason.

21. **Per-OS tallies (CARRY 8).** Write `evidence/per-os-tallies.md` from CI#38649787488's job logs (research.md,
    Readings), the 2026-10-10 gap restated with the same cause; host paths masked.

22. **The merge surface (CARRYs 11 and 12).** Write `evidence/merge-surface.md`: for the range model (seven upstream
    files plus `node/range.rs`) and the keyboard activation (four files), each file's lines changed against
    `434e0661` (one `git diff --stat 434e0661 eb5ba90c --` over each set's files), and upstream's movement since — `upstream/main` at
    `e72650a6`, three commits, none touching either set (`git diff --stat 434e0661 e72650a6` over the same files reads
    empty), re-read at this step after a `git fetch upstream main`; no upstream pull request is opened.

23. **Counts.** From the `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` entry's run at implement, the workspace's result lines · passed · failed · ignored against 185 · 951
    · 0 · 12, every delta attributed per target (`target/ci-logs/test.log`), and the `ci-scripts` leg's `Ran N tests`
    against its HEAD count; record in `evidence/counts.md`.

   RUSTSEC-2024-0436 (paste 1.0.15, unmaintained) and RUSTSEC-2026-0186 (memmap2 0.5.10, unsound) never reach the `audit`
   leg though both are in the build graph; close it — a lockfile-wide scan beside it, or a graph that reaches them
   (measured at 2026-10-05-ci-gate-legs evidence/audit.md; pinned on the overseer's word, delegate overseer).
   - The mechanism as the CARRY states it, kept verbatim: "cargo-deny 0.20.2's resolved graph prunes `http-cache`
     (blitz-net's `cache` feature) and `ravif`" — measured 2026-10-05, verified at HEAD at P3: `advisories ok` while
     `Cargo.lock` holds `paste 1.0.15` and `memmap2 0.5.10`, both reached by `cargo tree --workspace --all-features`.
     [premise-corrected: a graph that reaches paste exists — `cargo deny --locked --workspace --all-features check
     advisories` reads `advisories FAILED` on RUSTSEC-2024-0436 alone; memmap2's RUSTSEC-2026-0186 is an `unsound`
     informational advisory that no invocation tried reports at `deny.toml`'s defaults (research.md, Readings)]
   - Whether a scan that can turn the audit leg red on a pruned-graph advisory is a widening of an existing gate (the
     overseer's pinned word) or a new CI gate (the founder's) is a P4 fork (verified as open at P3).

2. **Release metadata.** The root `Cargo.toml` `homepage` and `repository` still read `https://github.com/dioxuslabs/blitz`
   and become escher's (`https://github.com/Turbolet85/escher`); the README is already escher's page (directed by the
   operator, 2026-10-06).

3. **Two blitz-dom unit tests assert nothing.** `hover_state_tests` in `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs`
   (`hovering_text_in_anonymous_block_reports_text_cursor`, `hovering_anonymous_block_whitespace_reports_default_cursor`)
   print "skipping: no usable font" and pass with system fonts on, while test-plan §1 lists "hover cursor" among
   blitz-dom's covered behaviours.
   - The CARRY's mechanism, kept verbatim with its marker: "hypothesis: their fixture builds its elements with the
     one-argument `qual_name!`, a no-namespace element the default stylesheet's type selectors do not match, so `body`
     and `div` lay out inline and the text never gets the height the skip tests for (that mechanism measured on that
     chunk's own `changed_set_` fixture, not on these two tests)". Verified at P3 as far as HEAD can show it without an
     edit: both tests print the skip and pass under `--features system-fonts`, the fixture is one-argument throughout

data.head: ## Folded freight (the twelve CARRY blocks at working-route.md:94)

body:
1. **`author_id` on the platform tree (from 2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity).** The operator ratified the stable
   element id leaving the process as AccessKit `author_id` through the platform accessibility adapter; assert that no
   `author_id` on the tree the shell hands the adapter carries a `NodeId`, `ElementId`, `ScopeId` or pointer form.
   Today's proof is headless: `stand_accessibility_ids` reads `DioxusDocument::accessibility_tree`, not the platform
   adapter (security-plan §Input Validation, `id` row).

2. **The stand binary builds no AccessKit (from 2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity).** seven_guis takes
   dioxus-native with `default-features = false` and names no `accessibility` feature, so `just seven_guis` compiles no
   platform adapter and no AT can read the windowed stand (measured at that chunk with `cargo tree -p seven_guis -e
   features -i dioxus-native`: prelude · system-fonts · vello-hybrid · woff; re-read at take-up: seven_guis'
   manifest names `prelude`, `system-fonts`, `woff`, and no `accessibility`). "Whether the stand enables it is decided
   at this entry's promotion." Enabling the platform adapter on the stand is a boundary widening (playbook :36) — the
   founder's fork, raised as a dialog (inputs#I1).

3. **Windowed witness of the refresh on change (from 2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff).** The shell's `View::poll`
   rebuilds the platform accessibility tree when its changed set was non-empty (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07,
   the witness owed); no windowed run witnesses it — the windowed binary builds blitz-shell without `accessibility`,
   and on the dev host AccessKit's `update_if_active` never runs the tree build (`.claude/rules/a11y.md:46`, the AT-SPI
   bus reads `IsEnabled` false); proven at the document level only (the `changed_set_` unit tests, both feature builds
   of blitz-shell). Witness here that a focus move and a rewritten accessible name reach the platform tree (a11y-plan §2).
   - [premise-corrected: `AccessibilityState` is built only from a live winit window and hands the adapter `doc.accessibility_tree()` inside `update_if_active` (`packages/blitz-shell/src/accessibility.rs`; `window.rs:150-151`, `:377-381`) — no in-process path reaches the adapter]
     A windowed witness on the dev host is blocked by the bus state, which the rule says to leave alone (the operator's
     desktop), and no path reaches the adapter without a window. What is reachable headlessly is the two halves the
     refresh composes: the tree the shell hands the adapter is exactly `Document::accessibility_tree` called through
     `&dyn Document` (the override for a `DioxusDocument`), and a focus move and a rewritten name each leave the changed
     set non-empty, which is the poll's rebuild condition. A witness at the platform tree itself keeps an owner.

4. **The tree override is compiled in, the adapter still is not (from 2026-10-07-act-by-id).** `escher-driver` names
   `accessibility` on dioxus-native-dom, so both seven_guis binaries compile the `accessibility_tree` override and the
   snapshot modules; `accesskit_xplat` and `accesskit_winit` are in neither graph (measured at
   escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-act-by-id/evidence/feature-reach.md); enabling the adapter is still this entry's
   decision (CARRY 2's fork).

5. **The stand's listbox reads no accessible name (from 2026-10-10-snapshot-states).** `crud-list` states
   `role="listbox"` (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs:57-58`) and its snapshot line reads the name `""`: an
   interactive-role element outside the 15 named controls `stand_accessibility_ids` asserts. "How the list is named is
   decided at this entry's promotion, with that check's table of named controls restated."
   - Naming it in the stand's markup (an `aria-label`) is a stand change, the operator's — no engine change. Verified:
     the builder takes a trimmed non-empty `aria-label` as the name (`.claude/rules/a11y.md`, Accessibility tree); the
     flight dates are named so (layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens); no check pins the list's
     name `""` (research.md §Sweeps); `host_log` and `mcp_log` take the rows' text as name needles, so the list's name
     joins that census.

6. **Windowed witness of the three states (from 2026-10-10-snapshot-states; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10,
   «Ратифицировать»).** In a windowed build with `accessibility` on, the platform adapter is handed `selected`,
   `toggled` and `invalid` on each element node whose markup states them; what an AT reads of them is not measured; they
   are proven headlessly only (`accessibility_states`; `stand_snapshot_state`). The witness rides the one owed for the
   refresh on change (item 3).

7. **Re-colour every pair the stand contrast check records `fail` (from 2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness; the
   operator's word at that chunk's P5 review).** `counter-increment`, `flight-one-way`, `flight-book`, `timer-reset` and
   `crud-create` read `#ffffff` on `#4a6cf7` at 4.39 against 4.5; SC 1.4.3 cannot be asserted green until they pass,
   and a re-colouring moves the record `stand_contrast` asserts row for row.
   - The accent `#4a6cf7` is a stand token used beyond the five buttons. Verified with the reach widened (research.md
     §Sweeps: 25 accent-family hits in 7 task files): white text sits on it also on `crud-update` and `crud-delete` once
     a row is selected (`crud.rs:139`, `:154`, `:261-270`), on the selected CRUD row (`crud.rs:230-233`), on the active
     flight toggle (`flight_booker.rs:170-174` — `flight-return` once chosen), and on the circle drawer's toolbar and
     dialog buttons (`circle_drawer.rs:150-163`, `:218-231`); it is a non-text border, outline or `accent-color` in
     timer, cells, temp converter and the flight dates. Its hover `#3a5ce5` and active `#2a4cd3` shades are declared
     beside it in counter, flight booker, timer, CRUD and circle drawer. White reads 4.39 on the rest shade, 5.47 on the
     hover and 6.83 on the active (research.md §Measurements). Which colour replaces it is the operator's (a stand
     change, no engine change).

8. **The colour-changing states not measured (same chunk, same word).** Hover and active on the primary buttons and
   `back-btn`, the flight booker's toggle in its other position, an invalid date (`#c53030` on `#fff5f5`), and the date
   and the buttons in their non-boot enabled state; each is SC 1.4.3 text, and `stand_contrast` reads each task at boot
   only.
   - `Harness::text_contrast` reads computed styles; hover and active are reachable headlessly by a pointer move and a
     pressed button through the harness's input synthesis, the other states by real input. The mechanism is verified:
     a `PointerDown` sets the hover node then `active_node()` (`driver.rs:182-190`), and `mouse_down_at` /
     `move_mouse_to` dispatch and pump (`input.rs:112-136`). That `text_contrast` then reads the `:hover` / `:active`
     background is not measured at P3 — implement measures it first (research.md §Open questions).

9. **The CRUD list rows (same chunk, same word).** `crud-person-{id}` (role `option`) lie outside `controls()` and are
   not measured; the CARRY's own hypothesis, kept verbatim: "hypothesis: a selected row reads `#ffffff` on `#4a6cf7` =
   4.39, a fail (predicted at that chunk's phase, not measured)". Re-derived at HEAD from the declaration:
   `.list-item.selected` is `color: #ffffff` on `background-color: #4a6cf7` (`crud.rs:230-233`), 4.39 over the declared
   hex; the harness reading is implement's.

10. **Text outside the controls (same chunk, same word).** Task titles, labels and value displays are SC 1.4.3 text
    too, and this entry names controls only.
    - Measuring them widens the record past "every stand control"; whether they are asserted here or recorded is a
      scope lean for P4 (the CARRY placed them here, so they are in scope at least as a record). Verified as a lean
      basis: every declared text pair off the accent passes 4.5 — `#task-title` 18.88, `.timer-label` 9.74, CRUD labels
      11.59, the inactive toggle 9.33, the invalid date 5.11, the success message 6.15 (research.md §Measurements, over
      the declared hex; the harness reading is implement's).

11. **The CRUD list's tree focus (from 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness; the operator's condition on fork F5).**
    `crud-list` takes focus and its ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End move the selection, but the accessibility tree's
    focus is the list, never the option: the builder reads no `aria-activedescendant`, so an AT learns the current row
    only from its `selected` reading; a click on a row or on the list leaves nothing focused (measured at that chunk:
    `stand_keyboard`). "How the current option reaches the tree is decided at this entry's promotion."
    - Two shapes: the builder reads `aria-activedescendant` and the tree's focus follows it — a new attribute read in
      every document, an engine change for every document and a new attribute crossing (playbook :64, :36; the
      founder's, inputs#I1); or the stand moves real focus onto the option (a roving `tabindex` in the CRUD markup, the
      operator's) — which moves the Tab sequence `common::tab_order` and `stand_keyboard` assert. Verified: the tree's
      `focus` is the engine's focused node or the `Window` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:62`), and no
      `aria-activedescendant` is read in `packages/` or the stand (0 hits, research.md §Sweeps).

12. **The engine honours no `inert` (from 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness).** A truthy `inert` takes no focusability
    away: Tab reaches a button under `inert: true` as under `inert: false`, both layout modes (pinned by
    `stand_keyboard::the_engine_honours_no_inert`, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_keyboard.rs:598`); whether an inert
    subtree still takes a hit is not measured; the bridge clears a framework-written `inert: false`
    (`dioxus_falsy_boolean_attrs`). "A fix is an engine change for every document, a founder's fork."
    - No stand task renders `inert` — verified: 0 hits for `inert` in `examples/seven_guis/src` (research.md §Sweeps).
      The stand's SC 2.1.1 / 2.4.3 do not turn on it; the fork is whether this chunk asks it at all.

- No mutation runs — the founder's word, relayed by the operator at take-up (inputs#I1): no mutation control is a

- Every founder fork is raised as a question dialog at P4 for the operator to take to the founder (inputs#I1): an
  engine change for every document (playbook :64 — items 11 and 12), a boundary widening (playbook :36 — item 2's
  platform adapter, item 11's attribute crossing), a new CI gate (the leg gating merges). Without his ruling the chunk
  asserts what the stand can meet by its own markup and records the rest with a route owner.

- Not this chunk: the three non-lean tasks' keys and requirement proof ("Stand requirement sweep"); the cold-agent test
  ("Cold-agent test"); coverage floors and flakiness budgets ("Quality gates").

- No new carrier, verb, field, log field or span: the work is stand markup and styles, test code over the existing
  `Harness`, snapshot and accessibility readers, and a CI leg's test list. Verified for the non-fork work: research.md
  §Files to modify names stand task files, blitz-tests files and two CI scripts, none an engine, driver or telemetry
