  pinned.
- A recorder at each surface: rejected in the dialog. Two taps that must agree would move 12 call sites.

- A `tracing` call site, span field or log line for any recording event, the check's path or a count of its steps:
  never (obs-plan §4; the founder's 2026-10-09 ruling allows a diff's sizes only).

- A truncated check left standing after a failure: never. The file is removed and the call answers
  `recording-failed`.

- **F3 may widen.** The founder's own word may widen F3 to **B**: each answer whole as the driver wrote it, a shot's
  pixels excepted. The form leaves room: B adds an `answer` key after `digest`, and the reader takes it then. Until his
  word, no answer text is kept.

- **Determinism the digest rests on.** A whole shot's PNG is byte-identical across processes (CLAUDE.md, the headless
  screenshot); `advance` moves the one clock by exactly `ms`; `scroll` is instant (`blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs:240`).
  So an unchanged app replays every digest, the shot's included. The CARRY's pan and fling are not reached by any
  driver call; their check is the engine's own proof (scope.md §Freight).

  - **`Session::run`** (signature, `command` span and its eight fields unchanged) now records each answered call
    when a recording is held.
    - A record is `{"tool","arguments",["masked":true],"accepted","digest"}`.
    - Arguments are written in the schema's argument order, not the order they crossed. That order makes the CLI's
      and MCP's checks byte-identical, and it is the order `validate` checks them in.
    - A call no record can spell is not recorded: a verb outside the seven instance verbs, or an argument the
      verb's schema does not name or passes twice.

      to none (refused `stale` or `not-found`). Otherwise its text is kept as it crossed.
    - When a write fails or a bound would be passed (400 records, 1,048,576 bytes), the recording ends: the check is
      removed, nothing further is recorded, and `recording_failed()` reads true. The call ran and is not rolled back.
    - A file the recorder did not create, such as a pre-existing temporary at its path, is never removed.

title: What it builds (stated by the entry)

data.head: ## What it builds (stated by the entry)

body:
- A driver session driven through the command line (`escher-session`, a hosted session) or through the MCP role
  (`escher-session mcp`) can be kept as a replayable check: the calls that crossed, in order, in a form a later run can
  replay.
- The kept check is owner-only at rest.

- It is never logged: no log record, span field or stderr line carries any of its content (the sink rule of CLAUDE.md's
  Critical Warnings and the two driver spans stand unchanged).
- Password handling follows the security plan.

- This chunk builds the RECORDING half of v020-04: what is kept, where, its file form, how a session turns it on and
  gets it back, and a reader of that form that a replay can trust. Running recorded checks as ordinary tests under
  agent-run, CI and stand-repeat, re-validating every step, and red-on-change / green-otherwise are the next entry's
  («Recorded-check replay», `escher-0.2.0/working-route.md:29`, which also names v020-04). (verified at P3)

- v020-04 is not claimable by this chunk: its matrix acceptance asks for replays in CI that pass on the unchanged app
  and fail on a changed one, and the next markerless entry carries that leg. (verified at P3: `matrix.py show --id
  v020-04`)

- A minimal in-process round trip — a recorded stand session read back and run again on a fresh session in a test —
  is the evidence that the form is replayable at all; whether it stays this chunk's or the next entry's is a P4
  technical fork. (verified open at P3: no reader of a kept check exists yet)

  `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `deny.toml` are unchanged (per security-plan §Dependency Security).

data.head: # Plan — 2026-10-19-upstream-sync-visual-lint-and-real-app-readiness: "Upstream sync ahead of visual lint and real-app readiness"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-19-upstream-sync-visual-lint-and-real-app-readiness · **Version:** escher-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-19T19:05Z
- **Base:** HEAD `67f17b9d632ceb66f6c01b347d9f9ba036dd29b6` (build/escher-0.2.0, 0 ahead of origin) — every git read of what this chunk changed names it.

Bring upstream's two commits past our last sync that carry no git dependency onto the branch, as the last sync did
with `fb8d6c15e`. The take is a no-commit cherry-pick of `38ca4e777` (#1226, `:focus-within`) and `17de049b1` (#1228,
the WPT pin), with the merge base staying `23b9b26a9`. The four Taffy-main commits wait for the next sync because
they put a git Taffy in the root manifest. This is the operator's answer to the P4 pin fork, given as delegate and
so PROVISIONAL (inputs#I2), on the facts measured at take-up (inputs#I1).
The take changes engine behaviour in every document, as upstream wrote it. Three things change:
- `:focus-within` matches the focused element and its DOM ancestors.
- A node outside the document is not focused.
- A focus set or cleared asks the shell for a redraw.

Upstream's two blitz-tests files come in as their own targets. The one textual conflict, in `mutator.rs`'s
`add_children_to_parent`, is resolved by keeping both sides. That is our changed-set insert and upstream's
`:focus-within` chain record, and it is recorded as the take's one non-additive edit.
Every escher proof must then pass:
- the fast and doc legs
- the audit
- the a11y leg
- the stand through agent-run
- the sink-installing hosts' capture checks under both builds
- the windowed build
- fork CI green on the pushed commit, with its per-OS tallies re-read
The four CARRYs are re-read and recorded:
- the Taffy commits, left out again
- `keyboard_compat.rs`, not retired
- the engine-debts merge surface, per row
- the document clock's merge surface

Nothing is sent upstream. Provenance: arch §Established Decisions ([Dependency pinning], [DOM semantics]) and §Cross-cutting Patterns (Invalidation and state integrity) · security-plan §Dependency Security, §Logging & Monitoring, §Input Validation · test-plan §2, §9, §10 · obs-plan §2, §3, §8 · a11y-plan §2, §5, §6, §9 · design-system §Color Palette · layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native.

1. **Record the tree before the take** in `evidence/before.md`:
   - `git rev-parse HEAD` must read the base. If HEAD has moved, stop and ask the operator.
   - `git status --short` covering the code paths.
   - The residue tallies of `target/ci-logs/test.log`. At P4 they read `lines 197 passed 1034 failed 0 ignored 12`, by the tally entry's awk.
   - The a11y log, and the stand-file and blitz-tests-file counts. At P4 there are 44 `stand_*.rs` files and 136 `.rs` files under `tests/blitz-tests/tests/`, by `ls … | wc -l`.
2. **Take `17de049b1`**: run `git cherry-pick --no-commit 17de049b11095808e0d093be2a8f0520e4dcbc0e`. It applies clean (inputs#I1: alone onto HEAD, tree `b1f50a45`) and changes `wpt/WPT_COMMIT` alone.

3. **Take `38ca4e777`**: run `git cherry-pick --no-commit 38ca4e777513607c7dcb659748380e7a650b018f`. A no-commit cherry-pick does not need the index to match HEAD.
   - It stops on one conflict in `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` (inputs#I1). The other hunks auto-merge: `document.rs`, `events/keyboard.rs`, `node/node.rs`, `stylo.rs`, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/all.rs`, and the two new test files.
   - Resolve it in `add_children_to_parent` as follows. Keep our three-line `if new_parent_is_in_document && !child_ids.is_empty() { self.doc.changed_nodes.insert(parent_id); }` first. Follow it with upstream's blank line, its three-line comment and `let mut focus_within_old_chain: Option<Vec<NodeId>> = None;`. Add or remove no other line.
   - `git add packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs`, then `git cherry-pick --quit`. The in-progress state clears, and the staged and worktree changes stay.
   - `git status` must show no cherry-pick in progress.
   - The exact-take entry proves that the chunk's code delta is upstream's added and removed lines and nothing else.

4. **Run the gates** of `## Test Commands` in order.
   - A gate red because of the take (a clippy lint on upstream's code, a `focus_redraw.rs` count, a moved stand reading) is fixed by the smallest edit that keeps upstream's behaviour. A red count may also be recorded as a measured reading where the behaviour is upstream's and our check is the reading that moved.
   - Each such edit is named in `evidence/take.md` as non-additive, with its file:line and why. The preservation guard's exclusions take its path, and that is recorded beside it.
   - An assertion is never loosened. A stand table, `tab_order`, `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER` or a `stand_contrast` row is never edited to pass.

5. **Record the take** in `evidence/take.md`:
   - the two shas and their subjects
   - the conflict and its resolution, quoted
   - the `git status` after `--quit`
   - the exact-take and preservation entries' lines
   - the commit trailers the operator's pre-CI commit carries: `(cherry picked from commit 38ca4e777513607c7dcb659748380e7a650b018f)` and `(cherry picked from commit 17de049b11095808e0d093be2a8f0520e4dcbc0e)`

6. **Record the lock** in `evidence/lock.md`:
   - `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `deny.toml` are byte-identical to the base, so no package enters, leaves or moves.
   - The four Taffy-main commits (`1a11761bc` · `4a5ab9cc9` · `510b592ab` · `1e5479ae6`) stay out because they put git Taffy `ea07c4c3` in the root manifest (inputs#I1). The reason and the answer are inputs#I2.
   - The audit verdicts `advisories ok` and `licenses ok`.

7. **Record the readings** in `evidence/readings.md`:
   - **CARRY 1:** the Taffy commits are left out again, and the CARRY moves to «Upstream sync ahead of polish and ship».
   - **CARRY 2:** `keyboard_compat.rs` is still listed at `17de049b1`, both coverage exclusions stand, and the CARRY moves.
   - **CARRY 3:** one row per engine-debts fix, F1–F8 of `escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-18-engine-debts/evidence/merge-surface.md`. Each row states whether `38ca4e777` touched its named functions, read from `git show 38ca4e777 -- {file}` hunk headers against the row's names. What research found:
     - F1, F4, F5 (`node.rs`): upstream adds three methods beside `is_hovered`/`focus`, none of `is_focussable`, `is_inert`, `hit_inner`, `absolute_position` or `position_in_containing_block`.
     - F7 (`events/keyboard.rs`): the Tab arm loses four lines, and neither `activates_on_enter` nor `activates_on_space` is touched.
     - F8 (`document.rs`): the hunks are in `clear_interaction_state_for_removed_node`, `clear_focus` and `set_focus_to`, none of F8's five functions.
     - F2, F3, F6: their files are untouched.
     Nothing is sent upstream.
   - **CARRY 4:** of the clock's files, upstream reaches `document.rs` alone, in focus functions. The no-wall-clock entry reads 0.
   - **Engine behaviour:** the three changes in every document, each with the upstream test that witnesses it, by test name from `focus_within.rs` and `focus_redraw.rs`.

8. **Record the sink** in `evidence/sink.md`, in the last sync's form (`escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-18-upstream-sync-determinism-and-traces/evidence/sink.md`):
   - the fixed-sha census of `38ca4e777`
   - `host_log` and `mcp_log` under the per-package build (the seven_guis entry) and the workspace build (inside `fast`)
   - `packages/escher-telemetry/` unchanged
   - the two upstream files' silence-census rows (env · print · subscriber: 0 · 0 · 0, research.md §Sweeps)
   - the `focussed node` INFO line's site, still inside `set_focus_to` under `#[cfg(feature = "tracing")]` after upstream's not-in-document gate

9. **Record the counts** in `evidence/counts.md`. Each moved count is attributed by name: the two new targets and their result lines, `run stand` and `run all` against step 1, and the stand selection count.

10. **Operator pass**, the four `operator` entries in order: hygiene; the pre-CI commit, its subject exactly `chore(2026-10-19-upstream-sync-visual-lint-and-real-app-readiness): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads`, its body carrying step 5's two trailers; the push; the CI read; the per-OS tallies. Each result goes in `evidence/ci.md`, every moved tally explained against CI#39302945352, the base's green run, read at P4 by the tally entry's own text. The 2026-10-19 chunks' moves since the last recorded reading, CI#39111579925 (test-plan.md:330), are attributed beside upstream's.
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/focus_within.rs` — upstream's, byte-identical, from `38ca4e777`: 7 tests of `:focus-within` and the not-in-document refusal
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/focus_redraw.rs` — upstream's, byte-identical, from `38ca4e777`: 4 tests of the redraw on a focus move, on a counting `ShellProvider` fake
- `escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-19-upstream-sync-visual-lint-and-real-app-readiness/evidence/` — `before.md`, `take.md`, `lock.md`, `readings.md`, `sink.md`, `counts.md`, `ci.md`

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` — upstream's hunks in `clear_interaction_state_for_removed_node`, `clear_focus`, `set_focus_to`, as written. Callers are kept, the signatures unchanged: `set_focus_to` @ `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:1746`, `:1754`, `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:964`, `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:574`, `:771`, `:980`, `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/events.rs:298` (research.md §Graph impact).
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs` — the Tab arm's `old_focus` and its redraw removed, as written

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` — upstream's `focus_within_old_chain` record and transfer in `add_children_to_parent`. The conflict is resolved per step 3; callers `append_children` @ `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:707` and `insert_nodes_before` @ `:714` are unchanged.
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs` — `add_focus_within`, `remove_focus_within`, `contains_focus`, as written
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo.rs` — `NonTSPseudoClass::FocusWithin` matches `ElementState::FOCUS_WITHIN`, as written
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/all.rs` — upstream's two `mod` lines; the file stays byte-identical to upstream's at `17de049b1`
- `wpt/WPT_COMMIT` — `9d8aceec…`, as written
Every gate is one entry of the fence below, in the order /implement runs it.
- No `leg = 'live'` entry: no external process is driven.

- The windowed smoke needs `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`; unset, it reads `not run`, and the windowed build stays proven by its `build` entry and CI. The smoke cannot see a focus ring or a `:focus-within` style. The windowed half of the redraw change is witnessed by upstream's `focus_redraw.rs` on its counting shell alone. That limit is recorded, not claimed.

- The coverage leg is not run locally: the take changes no line of the three floored crates (escher-driver, dioxus-native-dom, blitz-test-harness). Its `coverage floor: 3 of 3` reading is CI's "Coverage report" job, which the CI read's green covers, `keyboard_compat.rs` still excluded by the leg's own words (CARRY 2 entry).
- The CI-reading acceptance spans two runs by construction, so the operator's commit and push precede the CI read.
- Every git read of what this chunk changed names the base `67f17b9d632ceb66f6c01b347d9f9ba036dd29b6`.

One lint reads the current screen of a held instance and returns a finding for each element that overlaps another,
is clipped, has truncated text, lies off-screen, has zero size or fails text contrast. Each finding names the
element's stable id, one of six closed defect words, and the measured reason (intent §Findings 4, E1; v020-05). The
lint is read-only, like `screenshot`: no step, nothing dispatched, no time moved (arch §Standard Contracts → Driver
session). Contrast is read as `stand_contrast` reads it: `Harness::text_contrast` against `required_ratio`, a control
reading not enabled exempt, `None` not measured (a11y-plan §6 Color contrast).

The crossing is the founder's call. The operator answered F1 as delegate, «In process only (Most conservative)»,
PROVISIONAL until the founder's own word on `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-19T23-47-25-phase/founder-forks.md` (inputs#I2).
So this chunk builds the lint in process: `Session::lint` and the types it returns, a new read-only blitz-dom text
extent reader, and the fixture and stand proofs. Nothing new crosses the socket, the command line, MCP, a kept check
or a log. v020-05 asks for one command, so the in-process reader does not prove it on its own: the cap is claimed
GATED on the founder's F1 word (the operator's note, inputs#I2), as v020-03 was. The carriage his word sets is the
gated criterion (step 12), built only once his word is recorded.

The edge-case definitions are the operator's answers to three technical forks (inputs#I2). T1: `zero-size` only where
the element holds content. T2: `truncated` is text cut from view. T3: the lint itself reads `contain: paint` clips,
which `visible_region` does not.

1. **The text extent reader (blitz-dom).** Add `packages/blitz-dom/src/text_extent.rs` with a public read-only
   `BaseDocument::text_extent(node_id) -> Option<TextExtent>`, re-exported from `packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs`.
   `TextExtent` holds two `BoundingRect`s in CSS px, relative to the viewport like `get_client_bounding_rect`:
   - `content`: the element's content box (its client rect less border and padding).
   - `text`: the box the laid-out lines take. It starts at the content box's top-left, offset down by the inline
     layout's `block_offset`. It spans the lines' width and height at the layout's scale (Parley `Layout::width()` /
     `height()`, the reading `layout/inline.rs:884` takes as `content_width`).

   It returns `None` for an id that does not resolve (`get`, never an index), a node that is not an inline root
   (`Node::is_inline_root`, node/node.rs:65), or one with no inline layout data. It mutates nothing, has no log site,
   print, env read or panic path, and reads the same in both layout modes and under both builds (`writing-mode` on in
   the workspace build). Its rustdoc states its limit: right-to-left and vertical text are read as left-to-right,
   horizontal lines.

2. **The reader's check.** Add `tests/blitz-tests/tests/text_extent.rs`, three tests, each `for incremental in
   [false, true]`, over pages booted with the stand's options (bundled DejaVu Sans):
   - `a_line_that_cannot_wrap_reads_wider_than_its_box`: a `white-space: nowrap` paragraph 80 px wide, holding a line
     the bundled font lays out wider than 80 px. `text.width > content.width`, and `content.width` equals 80.
   - `a_wrapped_paragraph_reads_inside_its_box`: the same text with wrapping on. `text.width <= content.width`.
   - `an_element_with_no_inline_content_reads_none`: an empty block and a stale id both read `None`.

   Each test asserts its precondition (the line measured wider than its box), never branching on it (test-plan §4).

3. **The lint's types (escher-driver).** Add `packages/escher-driver/src/lint.rs`, its module and re-exports in
   `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs`:
   - `Defect` is a closed enum of six with `ALL` in this order: `Overlap`, `Clipped`, `Truncated`, `OffScreen`,
     `ZeroSize`, `Contrast`. `Defect::name()` gives the words `overlap` · `clipped` · `truncated` · `off-screen` ·
     `zero-size` · `contrast`.
   - `Finding` holds:
     - `id`: the element's stable element id, as its snapshot node lists it.
     - `defect`.
     - `bounds`: the snapshot node's `BoundingRect`.
     - `reason`, an enum of six variants carrying only measured numbers and stable ids:
       - `Overlap { other, area }`: the other element's id and the intersection.
       - `Clipped { visible }`: the part that can be seen.
       - `Truncated { text, visible }`: the text box and the part of it that can be seen.
       - `OffScreen`.
       - `ZeroSize`.
       - `Contrast { ratio, required }`: the measured ratio and `TextContrast::required_ratio`.

   Neither type holds a `NodeId`, page text, a colour or a value, and both derive `Debug`, `Clone` and `PartialEq`
   like `Outcome` (nothing prints, logs or fields them, per obs-plan §4).

4. **The six readings.** In `lint.rs`, `Session::lint(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<Finding>, Refusal>` reads the held
   instance's snapshot. It records its ids in the session's record of ids read, as `snapshot` does
   (`execute.rs:318-328`). It runs no step, no settle, no pump and no time move.
   - It refuses `Refusal::new(Cause::FontsUnavailable)` before any reading when `BaseDocument::can_paint_text` reads
     false, as `screenshot` does (`execute.rs:238-241`). That cause's meaning names no verb (`refusal.rs`), so no text
     changes.
   - Each element is a snapshot node, its box its `bounds`. Each node's **clip region** is `visible_region` (the
     viewport cut by every `overflow` clip on its containing-block chain, scrolling.rs:744). That region is cut further
     by the padding box of every ancestor whose computed `contain` includes `paint` (T3). This is the lint's own walk
     up the DOM parents; `visible_region` is unchanged.

   The readings, each over nodes whose `bounds` has positive width and height except `zero-size`:
   - **overlap**: two nodes, neither an ancestor of the other in the snapshot tree, whose boxes intersect with
     positive area. A pair is reported once, at the highest level it occurs: not when an ancestor of either, below
     their nearest common ancestor, already overlaps the other. The finding names the earlier node in document order,
     with `other` the later. Geometry only, never a hit (arch §Standard Contracts → Scrolling, selection, tree).
   - **clipped**: the box intersects its clip region with positive area but is not wholly inside it. `visible` is the
     intersection.
   - **off-screen**: the box has no positive-area intersection with its clip region.
   - **truncated** (T2): a node that `text_extent` reads, that is no text control (`ElementData::text_input_data` is
     `None`, so a password's or file input's value is never measured), and whose `text` box is not wholly inside the
     region its text can be seen through. That region is the node's clip region, cut by its own padding box when it
     clips by `overflow` or `contain: paint`. `visible` is the part of the text box inside it.
   - **zero-size** (T1): a node whose `bounds` width or height is 0 and which holds content. Content means a
     non-empty `name`, a `value` (`state.value` is `Some`), an `enabled` reading (`Some`: a form control), a focusable
     element (`Node::is_focussable`, node/node.rs:553), or a non-whitespace text node among its DOM descendants. An
     empty layout box reads nothing.
   - **contrast**: a node that holds a non-whitespace text node as a direct child, or is a text control. Not when its
     snapshot `enabled` reads `Some(false)` (exempt, inactive). Not when `Harness::text_contrast` reads `None` (not
     measured). Reported when `ratio < required_ratio()`.

   Findings come in document order (the snapshot's pre-order). One node's findings follow `Defect::ALL`'s order.

5. **The planted page and the fixture check.** Add `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_lint.rs`. It has one reader, so
   its page `lint_page` lives in the file (test-plan §3 Crate-local test helpers). The page is held through
   `fixtures::hold` in both layout modes. On an 800 × 600 root `fx-root`, at separate absolute positions:
   - **Planted:**
     - `fx-overlap-a` and `fx-overlap-b`, two sibling boxes intersecting.
     - `fx-clip-box` (`overflow: hidden`, 100 px wide) holding `fx-clipped` (200 px wide).
     - `fx-paint-box` (`contain: paint`) holding `fx-paint-clipped`, cut the same way.
     - `fx-truncated`, an 80 px `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden` paragraph holding a line wider than 80 px.
     - `fx-offscreen`, placed wholly right of the 800 px viewport.
     - `fx-zero`, a button labelled «Go» with zero width and height.
     - `fx-low-contrast`, text `#999999` on `#ffffff`.
   - **Negatives:**
     - `fx-spacer`, an empty zero-height box.
     - `fx-inert` (carrying `inert`) and `fx-hidden` (carrying `hidden`), each over `fx-overlap-b`'s box.
     - `fx-disabled`, a disabled button with `#999999` text on `#ffffff`.
     - `fx-faded`, low-contrast text under `opacity: 0.5`.
     - `fx-long-input`, a text input holding a value wider than its box.
     - `fx-wrapped`, a wrapping paragraph.

   Test `the_planted_defects_are_named_each_by_its_id_and_reason` asserts the findings equal exactly seven
   `(id, defect)` pairs, in document order:
   - `(fx-overlap-a, overlap)`
   - `(fx-clipped, clipped)`
   - `(fx-paint-clipped, clipped)`
   - `(fx-truncated, truncated)`
   - `(fx-offscreen, off-screen)`
   - `(fx-zero, zero-size)`
   - `(fx-low-contrast, contrast)`

   It also asserts each reason:
   - overlap: `other` is `fx-overlap-b`.
   - both clips: `visible` lies inside `fx-clip-box`'s and `fx-paint-box`'s boxes and is narrower than `bounds`.
   - truncated: `text.width > bounds.width`.
   - contrast: `ratio` equals `Harness::text_contrast`'s reading for that element and is below `required`, which is
     4.5.

   An assertion message names a layout mode and a row index, never an id (test-plan §3 `session-proof`, the
   2026-10-07-act-by-id rule).

6. **The stand at boot.** Test `the_stand_at_boot_reads_no_finding`: on each of the four lean tasks
   (`session_common::hold`), in both layout modes, `Session::lint` returns 0 findings. This is a prediction from the
   take-up's measurements (research.md §Measured: 0 overlapping pairs, 0 nodes outside the viewport, the CRUD rows
   inside `crud-list`; the five no-area nodes `task-header-spacer` ×4 and `timer-progress` hold no content under T1).
   Truncated text and the contrast of nodes outside `stand_contrast`'s rows are not yet measured. Record what the run
   measures in `evidence/readings.md`. A finding this reads is either a stand defect or a definition miss: stop and
   take it to the operator, never relax a reading to make it pass.

7. **Read-only.** Test `the_lint_reads_and_changes_nothing`, on the planted page and on CRUD, both modes. Drain the
   changed set first (`take_changed_nodes`), then lint twice. Each time `has_changes` reads false, the focused node is
   unchanged, `Harness::time` has not moved, the next `snapshot` equals the one before, and the two findings lists
   are equal (a11y-plan §7; arch §Standard Contracts → Test harness).

8. **Agreement with the per-action refusal.** Test `the_rows_cut_by_the_list_agree_with_off_screen`, CRUD, both
   modes. After twelve Creates through `Session::run` (`type` into `crud-name` and `crud-surname`, `click`
   `crud-create`, the stand's existing builders), the lint names the last row `clipped` or `off-screen`, measured
   against `crud-list`'s box. A `click` on that row is refused `off-screen` (layout-templates §Surface:
   desktop-native → IA notes).

9. **No font.** Test `an_app_with_no_font_is_refused_fonts_unavailable`, both modes. A session held with no font
   (system fonts off, none bundled, as `stand_act_screenshot`'s no-font case boots it) gets `Err` with
   `Cause::FontsUnavailable` from `Session::lint`, and the screen is unchanged.

10. **Unit tests in `lint.rs`.** `the_six_defects_are_named_in_order` pins `Defect::ALL` and its six words, with the
    row count asserted (`schema_tests.rs` style). `findings_follow_document_order_then_the_defect_order` pins the
    ordering over a hand-built list.

11. **Gates.** Fire the `## Test Commands` entries in order. Record the measured stand readings (step 6), the counts
    each entry forecasts, and the workspace tally in `evidence/readings.md` and `evidence/counts.md`.

12. **The gated criterion — after the block clears, in `/andromeda-implement`'s gated mode only.** The block is the
    founder's own word on F1 of `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-19T23-47-25-phase/founder-forks.md` (the operator's delegate
    answer «In process only (Most conservative)», PROVISIONAL, inputs#I2). Once his word is recorded:
    - Write `escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-19-visual-lint/evidence/founder-word.md` from it: one row
      `| F1 | {option number} | {his chosen label, verbatim, in its own script} | {date} |`, F2's row beside it, and
      the word cited by the snapshot implement takes of it (`--cleared-file`).
    - **His word is option 1** (a new instance verb `lint`, on every carrier, recorded), so build it:
      - `lint` is the eighth instance verb and twelfth verb in `VERBS` (`schema.rs:432`), after `screenshot`. It
        takes no argument. Its one result field is `findings`, of `FieldKind::Entries`, each keyed `id` · `defect` ·
        `bounds` and the reason's keys.
      - `Command::Lint` (`command.rs`) and `Outcome::Linted { findings }` (`execute.rs`), its arm calling the step-4
        reader. `record_result`'s early return covers it, so its span records `verb` and, refused, `cause` (F2).

      - It is recorded through the table (`recording.rs:92`).
      - The cold-agent pipe's twelve verb names (`scripts/cold-agent.sh:48`,

      - The pins and readers of research.md §Files to modify marked gated, each moved by the counts it states.
      - Test `the_lint_verb_answers_what_the_reader_reads` in `stand_lint.rs` asserts that a `lint` call through

- **Marker:** 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts · **Version:** escher-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-20T09:40:00Z

A screen whose snapshot text passes `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` (10,000 bytes) is read by an agent in parts it can walk.
Today `snapshot` answers such a screen whole on every carrier, held only by the 1,048,576-byte answer bound
(research.md §Measured). On the founder's word (inputs#I2 — F1 «Аргумент part, части по умолчанию (Рекомендую)»,
F2 «Пустая часть (Рекомендую)», relayed by the overseer), `snapshot` gains an optional `part` argument, a whole number
of a new argument kind. Over the budget, `snapshot` with no argument answers part 1. A paged answer adds two count
fields, `part` and `parts`. A part past the last answers an empty text with the same two fields, and no new cause is
added. A screen inside the budget, asked with no argument, answers exactly as today.

A part is a run of consecutive lines of `Snapshot::to_text`, cut at line boundaries, at most the budget in bytes. The
parts concatenated in order are the whole text, so each node's line appears exactly once and byte-equal to its line in
the whole snapshot (research.md §Measured; a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support). The cut is a pure reader of the
snapshot model in dioxus-native-dom beside `to_text` (arch §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge). The walk runs
through `Session::run` after `validate` like every instance verb (arch §Standard Contracts → Driver session;
security-plan §Input Validation, Driver command schema row). It therefore reaches the socket, the command line, MCP
and a kept check with no new verb, carrier, cause, exit or log field: the `command` span records `verb` alone for a
part read (obs-plan §4).

The proof is a fixture page over the budget, in both layout modes. It is driven through `Session::run` and through
`serve_mcp` in process, and its spelling is checked on every carrier on the lean stand (verification-matrix.json#v020-09).

1. **The part cut** — in `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs`, beside `Snapshot::to_text`, add a public
   pure method `Snapshot::text_parts(&self, budget: usize) -> Vec<TextPart>`. `TextPart` is a new public struct holding
   `text: String` and `ids: Vec<String>`: the lines of its nodes, then their ids in pre-order. Lines are written by the
   same `write_line` as `to_text`. A part takes consecutive nodes of `nodes()` pre-order while its text stays at most
   `budget` bytes. A node's line is never split: a line longer than `budget` is a part alone and stands over it (a
   stated limit, step 4). A snapshot with no nodes is one empty part, so there is always at least one part. The
   function has no document access, no failure path, no log and no print. Its doc states the equality the cut keeps:
   the parts' texts concatenated in order are `to_text()`. Amend `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET`'s doc, whose "never truncates
   or pages" stays true of `to_text`, to name `text_parts` as the reader that cuts the text into parts within it.

3. **The re-export** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs` re-exports `TextPart` beside `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET`
   (lib.rs:39), under the same `accessibility` gate as the snapshot model (arch §Cross-cutting Patterns → Config
   management).

4. **The schema** — in `packages/escher-driver/src/schema/spec.rs`, add `ArgKind::Part`, named `part` and bound "a
   whole number from 1 to 1000". In `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs`, add `pub const MAX_PART: u32 = 1000;`
   beside `MAX_MILLISECONDS` and give `SNAPSHOT` one optional argument `part` of kind `Part`. Its help: "the part of the
   screen to read, counted from 1; a screen over the budget is read in parts without it from part 1". Add two result
   fields after `text`: `part` (`FieldKind::Count`, `always: false`), "the part this answer holds, present when the
   screen is read in parts", and `parts` (`Count`, `always: false`), "how many parts the screen reads as, present with
   `part`". Rewrite `SNAPSHOT`'s help and `text`'s help to state:
   - a screen whose text is over 10,000 bytes is read in parts, each a run of whole lines of at most 10,000 bytes, and
     the parts in order are the whole text;
   - with no `part`, a screen over the budget answers part 1, and one inside it answers whole with no `part` or
     `parts`;
   - a part past the last is the empty text;
   - one element's line longer than 10,000 bytes is a part alone and longer than the budget;
   - each part is read from the screen as it stands, so a step between two reads gives parts of the new screen.
   `MAX_PART` is re-exported with the other bounds in `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` (:154-158).

5. **The schema pins** — `packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs`: `snapshot`'s row gains `("part", ArgKind::Part,
   false)` and its two fields. The kinds table (:295 on) gains `(ArgKind::Part, "part", "a whole number from 1 to
   1000")`, and any pinned count of kinds moves 6 → 7.

6. **Validation** — in `packages/escher-driver/src/command.rs`, `Command::Snapshot` becomes `Snapshot { part:
   Option<u32> }`. `validate` admits `("snapshot", [None])` and `("snapshot", [Some(Admitted::Part(n))])` in place of
   `("snapshot", [])`. `admit` gains `(ArgKind::Part, ArgValue::Number(number))` → `u32::try_from`, filtered to
   `1..=MAX_PART`, else `OutOfBound`; a value of another kind falls to `WrongKind` as for every argument. Add
   `Admitted::Part(u32)`. Update `Command::spec`, and every `Command::Snapshot` pattern in the crate's unit tests:
   command.rs:393 constructs `Command::Snapshot`, and command.rs:687's `snapshot` with an `id` stays `Fault::Unnamed`.
   Add unit tests: part 1, part 1000 and no part are admitted; part 0, part 1001, `-1`, `i64::MAX` and a text value
   are refused `malformed`, each with the fault the bound or the kind names.

7. **The read** — in `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs`, add `Outcome::Part { text: String, part: u32, parts:
   u32 }`, documented as what `snapshot` returns when the screen is read in parts. The `Command::Snapshot { part }` arm
   takes the screen once through `read_screen` (execute.rs:331), which records every id of the screen as today, then:
   - with `part` `None` and `to_text()` at most `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` bytes → `Outcome::Screen { text }`, exactly as
     today;
   - otherwise → `text_parts(SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET)`. Take `n` = `part` or 1, and `parts` = the parts' count. When `n`
     ≤ `parts`, answer `Outcome::Part` with part `n`'s text. When `n` > `parts`, answer `Outcome::Part` with the empty
     text.

   The record takes the whole screen's ids, as `snapshot` and `lint` do. Every acting call already records the whole
   screen before it resolves its id (execute.rs:378-382), so a part-only record would change no `stale` or `not-found`
   reading (see Provenance). The part count can pass `u32` only far beyond the 1,000-part bound, so it is converted with
   `try_from` and saturates rather than panicking. `record_result` (execute.rs:276) adds `Outcome::Part { .. }` to the arm that
   records nothing beyond `verb`. `Session::run`'s doc gains one sentence on the part read. A part read runs no step,
   settles nothing and waits on no load, as `snapshot` does (arch history 2026-10-20-load-wait).

9. **MCP** — no change to `packages/escher-driver/src/mcp.rs`: `Outcome::Part` reaches the generic arm (mcp.rs:234)
   and is answered as its JSON line, which is the form F1 chose. A whole screen is still the bare text (mcp.rs:230).
   `packages/escher-driver/src/mcp/listing.rs`'s `tool` gives `ArgKind::Part` the input schema `{"type":"integer",
   "minimum":1,"maximum":1000}`, plus its description as every argument's. `packages/escher-driver/src/mcp_tests.rs`:
   pin the `snapshot` tool's input schema and description; any listing byte-length pin moves.

10. **The command line** — in `packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs`, a flag of kind `Part` reads its value as a number,
    as `Milliseconds` does (cli.rs:253). The usage line then spells `snapshot [--part <part>]` from the table
    (cli.rs:352). `packages/escher-driver/src/cli_tests.rs`: pin the usage line's `snapshot` segment and argv
    `snapshot --part 2` → `Call { verb: "snapshot", args: [("part", Number(2))] }`; `--part x` reads a text value and is
    refused `malformed` at `validate`.

11. **The session-check helpers** — in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs`, add a builder `snapshot_part(n:
    i64) -> Call` and a reader `part(outcome) -> (String, u32, u32)` that panics with a fixed message on any other
    outcome, beside `snapshot()` and `shot`. The module stays silent (obs-plan §3 Logging stack).

12. **The fixture check** — new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_parts.rs`, with `//!` naming the behaviour, run
    `for incremental in [false, true]`. Its page is in this file (one reader): an `rsx!` component holding 400 keyed
    buttons with ids `item-001` to `item-400`, named "Item 001" to "Item 400", each counting its clicks into one keyed `output` `clicks` (author ids,
    test-plan §7 Fixture sources). Below them is a keyed password input `secret`. No actionable element on the page is
    unkeyed (`unkeyed_actionable()` empty, asserted). It is booted by `fixtures::hold` with the stand's options. The
    test asserts, each failure message naming the mode and an index only:
    1. **The condition first** — the whole `to_text()` of the session's own snapshot is over `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET`,
       and its text bounds are non-zero (a real font).
    2. **Default paging** — `snapshot` with no argument through `Session::run` answers `Outcome::Part` with part 1
       and `parts` ≥ 2, its text equal to `text_parts(SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET)[0].text` of a snapshot taken in the test.
    3. **The walk** — `snapshot_part(n)` for n in 1..=parts answers each part. Each text is at most the budget. The
       texts concatenated in order equal the whole `to_text()`. Every node id of the whole snapshot is on exactly one
       line across the parts, and each line equals its line in the whole text.
    4. **The end** — `snapshot_part(parts + 1)` answers the empty text with the same `parts`, and the screen is
       unchanged (a following whole read equal).
    5. **Addressable** — an id read only in the last part (`item-400`) takes `scroll` then `click`, both accepted. The
       diff names `clicks` changed, and after the click exactly one line across a fresh walk's parts reads `focused`.
    6. **Masked** — `type` of a sentinel into `secret`, then a walk: the sentinel occurs 0 times across the parts, and
       the `secret` line reads `MASKED_VALUE`.
    7. **MCP** — the same fixture held by `serve_mcp` in process (`stand_mcp_tools`' pattern at :517): a `tools/call`
       `snapshot` with no argument and with `{"part":2}` each return a text block equal to the JSON line
       `Outcome::to_json` writes for the same call through `Session::run`.
    8. **Inside the budget** — on the stand's Counter (`stand::boot`), `snapshot` with no argument answers
       `Outcome::Screen` byte-equal to before (no `part`), and `snapshot_part(1)` answers `Outcome::Part` with part 1
       of 1 whose text equals it.

13. **The span** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_spans.rs` drives one `snapshot` with `part` 1 per mode, beside its
    existing `snapshot` (:595). Its captured `command` line reads `verb="snapshot"` and no other field. The calls per
    mode move by one (the count the file states, 34 per mode since the lint: predicted 34 → 35, record what it
    measures).

15. **Docs** — rustdoc on every new public item (`TextPart`, `text_parts`, `Outcome::Part`, `ArgKind::Part`,
    `MAX_PART`), so `ci-leg.sh doc` stays clean.

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_parts.rs` — the over-budget fixture page and the walk, in process and over
  MCP, both layout modes
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs` — `TextPart`, `Snapshot::text_parts`, its unit tests, the budget doc
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs` — re-export `TextPart`
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema/spec.rs` — `ArgKind::Part`, its name and bound
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` — `MAX_PART`, `snapshot`'s argument, two fields, help
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs` — `snapshot`'s row and the kinds table
- `packages/escher-driver/src/command.rs` — `Command::Snapshot { part }`, admission, unit tests
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` — re-export `MAX_PART`
- `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs` — `Outcome::Part`, the part read, the record fed from the part, the span arm
- `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs` — the part's JSON line and its tests
- `packages/escher-driver/src/mcp/listing.rs` — the `Part` kind's input schema
- `packages/escher-driver/src/mcp_tests.rs` — the `snapshot` tool's listing pins
- `packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs` — a `Part` flag read as a number
- `packages/escher-driver/src/cli_tests.rs` — usage-line and argv pins
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_commands.rs` — `snapshot --part` through the binary
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs` — one part read at `trace`

- Smoke: none. The test plan declares no boot-smoke paths, and the stand's boot is untouched: no stand file changes,

- Live legs: none. Every check is in process or a spawned child of the workspace's own binary, offline.

body:
- (arch) On every stand screen, `snapshot` with no argument answers exactly as before: `stand_snapshot_text` and
  `stand_replay` pass unedited, and the committed Counter checks re-record byte-equal (`cargo test -p seven_guis --locked
  --test cli_commands --test host_log --test mcp_log --test recording 2>&1`) (per architecture §Standard Contracts →
  Driver session).

- (arch) The walk is reached only through `Session::run` after `validate`. `snapshot`'s `part` argument and its `part`
  and `parts` fields appear in `VERBS` with their help, and are listed by `help` and MCP `tools/list`. `VERBS` still
  holds twelve verbs and `CAUSES` eight, and describe's count row is unmoved (per architecture §Standard Contracts →
  Driver session).

- (security) `part` 0, 1001, a negative number, `i64::MAX` and a text value are refused `malformed` by `validate` with
  nothing run. The refusal's JSON on the command line holds no value the call supplied (per security-plan §Input
  Validation, Driver command schema row).

- (security) On the fixture, a sentinel typed into the password input occurs 0 times across a walk's parts, and its
  line reads `MASKED_VALUE` (per security-plan §Input Validation, password and file `input` value row).

- (a11y) Each part's lines equal their lines in the whole snapshot's text. After a click, exactly one line across a
  walk's parts reads `focused` (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).

- (obs) A part read writes one `command` span line holding `verb="snapshot"` and no other field. escher-driver keeps 2
  `info_span!` sites. `host_log` and `mcp_log` drive one part read at `trace` under both builds with 0 id and 0 name
  needles (per obs-plan §4; obs-plan §6, escher-driver logged events).

- (design) Each `snapshot --part` run through `escher-session` writes one uncoloured JSON line on stdout and exits 0
  accepted or 1 refused (per design-system §Surface: cli §Component Patterns).

- (layouts) No stand source, shared fixture module or stand table changes, and the four lean tasks mount as before
  (per layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens).

- (tests) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` and `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` pass, the a11y leg's six
  files keep their counts, and the CI run on the pushed sha reads green with the coverage floors and stand-repeat held
  (per test-plan §10 Coverage floors; test-plan §10 Flakiness budget).

- Spec anchors: architecture §Standard Contracts (Dioxus DOM bridge · Driver session) · §Cross-cutting Patterns
  (Config management) · §Occupied Resources; security-plan §Input Validation (Driver command schema row · password and
  file `input` value row · Recorded check row) · §API Security (Local session socket row) · §Logging & Monitoring;
  test-plan §1 · §2 · §3 (Session lifecycle) · §5 · §7 · §9 · §10; obs-plan §3 · §4 · §6 · §8 · §9; a11y-plan §7 ·
  §9; design-system §Surface: cli §Component Patterns · §Typography (Loading); layout-templates §Surface: cli →
  Primary screens · §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens.

- The founder's word: inputs#I2 (F1 «Аргумент part, части по умолчанию (Рекомендую)», F2 «Пустая часть (Рекомендую)»,
  his own answers relayed by the overseer); the fork routing inputs#I1.

- Graph impact: `Snapshot::to_text` @ `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:171` (its one production caller, research.md
  §Graph impact); `Outcome::Screen`'s two exhaustive matches @ `execute.rs:276` and `json.rs:325`.
- Research files inspected: listed in research.md §Files inspected.
- A new verb for a part — rejected by the founder's F1 (inputs#I2); `VERBS` stays twelve.
- A ninth refusal cause for a part past the last — rejected by the founder's F2 (inputs#I2); `CAUSES` stays eight.

- A held cut, or a cursor kept in the session between part reads — rejected. Each part read cuts the screen as it
  stands, because a `snapshot` read changes nothing (research.md §Measured), and a held cursor is state that a `NodeId`
  or a call-supplied token could leak through (security-plan §Input Validation, Driver command schema row).

- Repeating a part's ancestors at its head for context — rejected, because a node would then be read twice
  (v020-09's "exactly once"). A part's first line keeps its absolute indent.

- Changing `Outcome::Screen`'s fields — rejected for the new variant, since a changed variant moves 14 patterns
  (research.md §Sweeps).

- No field on the `command` or `tool_call` span for a part's number, count, size or text (obs-plan §4; security-plan
  §Logging & Monitoring).

- No stand task gains nodes, and Cells is not mounted in the lean boot (layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native →
  Primary screens).

- The fixture's size: 400 buttons named "Item nnn" with ids `item-nnn` write about 55 bytes per line. This is an
  estimate from the line form `snapshot_text.rs:57-92` writes, not a measurement, so step 12's first assertion reads
  the real size. Expect about 22 KB, three parts. The check asserts invariants, never a part count or a byte size: a
  part's bytes differ by runner, because `writing-mode` is on only in the workspace build and moves `bounds`
  (test-plan §9 Engine features by runner).

- `item-400` is below the 800 × 600 viewport, so its `click` alone would be refused `off-screen`; step 12 scrolls it
  first. That is the proof that an id read only in a later part is addressable as one read whole.

- The record of ids holds at most 4,096 (`session.rs:67`). The fixture's ~404 ids stay under it, and a screen past it
  forgets its oldest ids as today.

- Not paged, a stated limit: an acting verb's diff and a lint's findings have no budget of their own. On a large
  screen either can pass 10,000 bytes, held only by the 1,048,576-byte answer bound (research.md §Measured).

- Expected amendments (wrap):
  - architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge — `Snapshot::text_parts` and `TextPart`, the parts reader
    beside `to_text`.
  - architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session — `snapshot`'s optional `part` (`ArgKind::Part`, the seventh
    kind, 1 to `MAX_PART` 1000), `Outcome::Part`, the default paging over the budget, the empty part past the last, and
    a part read feeding the record of ids as `snapshot` does. Playbook «Boundary widening», answered by the founder's own word (inputs#I2, F1
    «Аргумент part, части по умолчанию (Рекомендую)» · F2 «Пустая часть (Рекомендую)»), so the wrap halts on it once,
    as the answer card.
  - security-plan §Input Validation (Driver command schema row) — the new bounded argument kind on `snapshot` and the
    paged answer on every carrier, with the same playbook pattern and word.
  - test-plan §3 → Session lifecycle (`session-binary`, `session-proof`) — `snapshot [--part <part>]`, the new check,
    and the counts the gates measure.
  - obs-plan §4 — a part read records `verb` alone.
  - design-system §Surface: cli §Component Patterns — a paged `snapshot` answers one line `{"text","part","parts"}`.
  - layout-templates §Surface: cli → Primary screens — the usage line's `snapshot [--part <part>]`.
  - a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support — the parts are one more reader of the snapshot model, each line equal to
    the whole text's.

**Date:** 2026-10-20T11:17:18Z
**Commits:** `191e66fdb chore(2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads`
(the one commit since `state.yaml.last_wrap` 2026-10-20T08:56:50Z; `git log --format='%h %s' c1a2e5b85..HEAD`)

- **Files:** 19 code and test files, from the pre-CI commit's parent `c1a2e5b85` to the tree (`gate.py scope`: `changed 19 · listed 19 ·
  recorded 0`). 18 modified · 1 new.
  - dioxus-native-dom: `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs` · `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs`.
  - escher-driver: `packages/escher-driver/src/{schema/spec,schema,schema_tests,command,lib,execute,json,mcp/listing,mcp_tests,cli,cli_tests}.rs`.
  - seven_guis tests: `examples/seven_guis/tests/{cli_commands,host_log,mcp_log}.rs`.
  - blitz-tests: `tests/blitz-tests/tests/{session_common/mod,stand_act_spans}.rs`, and the new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_snapshot_parts.rs`.
  - Pipeline files: `escher-0.2.0/verification-matrix.json` (v020-09 → implemented), the chunk folder and its `evidence/ci.md`, the
    phase, implement and wrap run dirs, and `.andromeda/friction-log.ndjson`.
  - `packages/escher-driver/src/mcp.rs` is unchanged: a part reaches its generic arm (`mcp.rs:234`).

- **Symbols / APIs:** coordinates are from `## New text, by line` below.
  - **dioxus-native-dom** (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs`):
    - `pub struct TextPart { pub text: String, pub ids: Vec<String> }` (`Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq`; 19-28). It is
      re-exported from the crate root under `accessibility` as `pub use snapshot_text::{SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET, TextPart}`
      (`lib.rs:39`), and the crate doc's feature list names `Snapshot::text_parts` (`lib.rs:8-9`).
    - `pub fn Snapshot::text_parts(&self, budget: usize) -> Vec<TextPart>` (59-81). It takes consecutive pre-order lines
      of `to_text` while a part stays within `budget` bytes, and never splits a line: a line longer than `budget` is a part
      alone. An empty snapshot is one empty part. It has no document access, failure path, log or print.
    - The parts concatenated are `to_text()`. `to_text` and `text_parts` share a private `each_line` pre-order walk with
      depth, and `to_text`'s output is unchanged.
    - `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET`'s doc now names `text_parts` as the reader that cuts the text into parts within it (15-16),
      while `to_text` "never truncates or pages" stands. Six unit tests: 493-609.
  - **escher-driver**:
    - `ArgKind::Part` (`schema/spec.rs:19-21`): name `part`, bound "a whole number from 1 to 1000"; the seventh argument kind.
    - `pub const MAX_PART: u32 = 1000` (`schema.rs:17-19`), re-exported from the crate root (`lib.rs:156-157`).
    - `SNAPSHOT`:
      - one optional argument, `part` (`ArgKind::Part`, `required: false`), help "the part of the screen to read, counted
        from 1; a screen over the budget is read in parts without it from part 1";
      - its fields are now `text`, then `part` and `parts` (`FieldKind::Count`, `always: false`; helps "the part this answer holds, present when the
        screen is read in parts" and "how many parts the screen reads as, present with `part`");
      - `SNAPSHOT.help` and `text`'s help are rewritten (`schema.rs:178-216`) to state the five paging rules.
    - `Command::Snapshot` is now `Snapshot { part: Option<u32> }`.
      - `validate` admits `snapshot` with no argument or with `Admitted::Part(n)`, `n` in `1..=MAX_PART` through `u32::try_from`.
      - Anything else of kind Number is `OutOfBound("part")`; a text or flag value is `WrongKind("part")`.
      - `Command::spec` is updated (`command.rs:139-144`, `:252-253`, `:362-366`).
    - `Outcome::Part { text: String, part: u32, parts: u32 }` (`execute.rs:32-41`).
      - The `Command::Snapshot { part }` arm reads the screen once through `read_screen`, which records every id of the whole
        screen (`execute.rs:188-204`).
      - With `part` `None` and `to_text()` at most `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` bytes, it answers `Outcome::Screen { text }` as before.
      - Otherwise it cuts `text_parts(SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET)`, takes `n` = `part` or 1 and `parts` = the count
        (`u32::try_from`, saturating), and answers `Outcome::Part` with part `n`'s text, or the empty text when `n` > `parts`.
      - `record_result` puts `Outcome::Part` in the arm that records `verb` alone (`execute.rs:308-313`).
      - `Session::run`'s doc gains the part read (`execute.rs:133-138`).
    - `Outcome::to_json` writes `Outcome::Part` as `{"text":…,"part":n,"parts":m}` (`json.rs:330-336`).
    - The MCP listing's `tool` gives `ArgKind::Part` `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":1000}` plus its description
      (`mcp/listing.rs:85-89`).
    - The command line reads a `Part` flag's value as a number, as `Milliseconds` (`cli.rs:253-257`). The usage line now
      spells `snapshot [--part <part>]`, built from the table.
    - Callers of the changed surfaces:
      - `Outcome` is a public enum matched exhaustively at `execute.rs`'s `record_result` and `json.rs`'s `to_json` (both
        updated), and outside the crate by `session_common::act` and `stand_act_spans::acting` (both updated).
      - Every other match is a `{ text }` or a wildcard pattern, which stands: the 14 `Outcome::Screen` patterns
        (research.md §Sweeps) are unchanged.
      - `Command::Snapshot` is matched only inside escher-driver.
  - **Test helpers** (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs`):
    - `pub fn snapshot_part(n: i64) -> Call` (68-71);
    - `pub fn part(outcome: Outcome) -> (String, u32, u32)` (73-80), which panics with the fixed message "the outcome is a part"
      on any other outcome;

  once.

- **Marker:** 2026-10-20-load-wait · **Version:** escher-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-20, between 01:51:21Z and 01:55:50Z (clock reads around P4)

An acting driver command that meets a load in flight waits it out within a stated bound. The acting commands are
`click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll` on every carrier: in process, the socket, the command line and MCP.
Today the instance settles once, and a counted request still in flight reads
`settled: false, busy: "loads"` at once (packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:461-466;
packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs:163-170), so a caller has to poll an app that loads over the network.
After this chunk the driver keeps re-settling while the only work outstanding is a load. It returns `settled` as
soon as the load is answered and the screen goes quiet. If `LOAD_WAIT` passes first, it returns with today's
`busy: "loads"` reading.

`LOAD_WAIT` is a fixed **5 s**, the operator's answer «5 s (Recommended)» at this P4. It is a public constant
re-exported beside `IDLE_EXPIRY`, and the `settled` field's help states it. That help is the program's own fixed
table text on the ratified carriers, per the playbook's fixed-text rule, set by the founder on 2026-10-12.

The wait moves no virtual time. It measures wall time between settles, sleeping a short poll. It never ticks the
harness, never runs the session's time step and never drains the changed set. So `advance` stays the one mover of
the session's clock, a rule ratified by the founder on 2026-10-18 (per arch §Standard Contracts → Driver session;
design-system §Motion §Animation runtime; a11y-plan §5).

`Harness::settle` is untouched: it still reports a load at once and reads no clock (per arch §Standard Contracts →
Test harness).

No verb, argument, result field, `Outcome` variant, refusal cause, session error, exit status, span field, env read,
listener or dependency is added. The bound sits well under every 30 s reply bound that reads a call's answer (per
security-plan §API Security, «Settle and loads in flight» and «Local session socket» rows).
The capability is proven on an in-file fixture held in a session, in both layout modes:

- a body stylesheet answered by a stand-in on its own thread after 200 ms ends the wait settled, with its styled
  box changed in the returned diff;
- the same request never answered (`fixtures::HeldNet`) ends the wait at the bound with `busy: "loads"`.

1. **The waiting settle, once, in `packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs`.**
   - Add `pub const LOAD_WAIT: Duration` (5 s) with a doc line saying what it bounds.
   - Add a crate-private function that settles the held harness through `Harness::settle` and, while the result is
     `Err(NotSettled { busy: Busy::Loads })` and the wall time since the function began is under `LOAD_WAIT`,
     sleeps a short fixed poll (a private const of 10 ms) and settles again.
   - It returns the first result that is not `Loads`, or the last `Loads` result once the next poll would pass the
     bound.
   - It stops at the deadline: it never sleeps past `LOAD_WAIT`, so the wait ends within one settle of the bound.
   - A `Render` or `Layout` result returns at once, unchanged.
   - Write the loop as a generic inner function over a settle closure, a bound and a poll, so its unit tests can
     drive it with a scripted closure and a short bound. The harness-facing function calls it with `LOAD_WAIT` and
     the poll.
   - The function reads `std::time::Instant` and calls `std::thread::sleep`. It does nothing else: no harness
     `tick`, no `advance_time`, no `TimeStep`, no `take_changed_nodes`, no print, no `tracing` call.

2. **`Session::act` settles through it** (packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:196-204). Its doc moves from
   «Settling moves no time» to say the step is settled, and that a load in flight is waited for up to `LOAD_WAIT`
   while no time moves.

3. **`settled_step` settles through it** (packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:453-470).
   - All five acting verbs reach it: `acted` and the `advance` and `scroll` arms (graph: `settled_step` has 3
     callers, all in `execute.rs`).
   - `passes` stays recorded on `Ok` only. On a waited step it is the passes of the settle that went quiet.
   - The doc at :126 moves from «Settling moves no time and waits on no load» to «Settling moves no time; a load
     in flight is waited for up to `LOAD_WAIT`».

4. **State the bound in the schema** (packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:117-122). The `SETTLED` field's help
   becomes: whether the app went quiet after the step, with a load in flight waited for up to 5 s. It is written as
   fixed text, as the double click's «within 500 ms» is (schema.rs:192-194).

5. **Pin text against value** in `packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs`. Add one unit test asserting:
   - the `settled` field's help names `LOAD_WAIT` in seconds as the text states it;
   - `LOAD_WAIT` is under `ANSWER_BOUND`, the client's 30 s read, which is crate-private in `wire.rs`, so the pin
     reads it in crate.

6. **Re-export `LOAD_WAIT`** in `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs`, in the `session` line beside `Session`. The
   crate root's re-exports go from 55 to 56.

8. **The check `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_load_wait.rs`**, both layout modes, every reading through
   `Session::run`. It declares `mod fixtures;` and `mod session_common;`.
   - **The fixture page, in-file:** one reader, so it stays in its check's file (test-plan §3 fixtures rule).
     - A button `fx-load` whose click renders a body `link` with `rel="stylesheet"` and
       `href="http://load.test/late.css"`.
     - A box `fx-box` whose height only that sheet sets; it reads zero height before the sheet.
     - Every element read carries an author `id` (layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native).
   - **The boot, in-file:** `Session::start` over `Harness::from_vdom` with `HarnessOptions { net_provider:
     Some(…), ..stand::options(incremental) }`. The stand's options are offline, and `fixtures::hold` takes no
     provider (research.md §Files inspected, stand.rs:57-65).
   - **The stand-in that answers on its own, in-file:** a `NetProvider` whose `fetch` spawns one thread per request.
     The thread sleeps 200 ms and then answers the handler with the sheet's bytes (`NetHandler` is
     `Send + Sync + 'static`, blitz-traits/src/net.rs:34). It overrides no `is_noop`, so the harness counts its
     loads. It holds no print, `tracing` call, env read, file, socket or listener.
   - **Arm 1, answered inside the bound:**
     - `click fx-load` returns `Acted` with `settled == true` and no `busy`;
     - its diff names `fx-box` changed with `bounds` in `differs`;
     - the next `snapshot` reads `fx-box` at the sheet's height;
     - the wall time the call took is under `LOAD_WAIT`;
     - `session.harness().time()` reads the same before and after the call.
   - **Arm 2, never answered** (`fixtures::HeldNet`):
     - `click fx-load` returns `Acted` with `settled == false` and `busy == Some(Busy::Loads)`;
     - the wall time the call took is at least `LOAD_WAIT` and under `LOAD_WAIT` plus 2 s;
     - `HeldNet::held()` reads 1;
     - the harness's `time()` is unchanged.
   - Failure messages name a mode and an arm only, never an id, a URL or a screen reading (security-plan §Input
     Validation, the rule on test names and messages).
   - The two wall reads are this check's own: `Instant::now()` around the call, and the stand-in thread's sleep.
     Test-plan §5 records `stand_virtual_clock`'s 800 ms sleep as the one sleep in a session check, so these are a
     second, narrowly stated exception, an Expected amendment below.

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_load_wait.rs` — the held-session check with its in-file page, boot and
  self-answering stand-in, both arms in both layout modes.

- `packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs` — `LOAD_WAIT`, the waiting settle with its generic inner loop and unit
  tests, and `Session::act` through it.
- `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs` — `settled_step` through the waiting settle, and its doc at :126.
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` — the `settled` field's help states the 5 s bound.
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs` — the help-against-value pin.
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` — re-export `LOAD_WAIT`.

body:
- (tests) v020-07 — on the in-file fixture of `stand_load_wait`, held in a session in both layout modes, through
  `Session::run` (verification-matrix.json#v020-07):
  - the stand-in answers on its own thread after 200 ms, so `click fx-load` returns `settled: true` with no `busy`,
    its diff naming `fx-box` changed with `bounds` in `differs`, and the next snapshot reads `fx-box` at the sheet's
    height, with the call's wall time under `LOAD_WAIT`;
  - with a `HeldNet` that never answers, the same click returns `settled: false`, `busy: "loads"`, no earlier than
    `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s) and less than 2 s after it.

  Gate: `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_load_wait 2>&1` reads 2 passed (per test-plan §5
  Integration Test Strategy).

- (arch) The wait moves no virtual time: `session.harness().time()` reads the same before and after each arm's call
  (per arch §Standard Contracts → Driver session; design-system §Motion §Animation runtime; a11y-plan §5).

- (arch) `Harness::settle` is unchanged, and blitz-dom gains no wall read. Gates: the `git diff` probe over
  `packages/blitz-test-harness packages/blitz-dom …` reads 0, and the blitz-dom `Instant::now|SystemTime::now`
  probe reads 0 (per arch §Standard Contracts → Test harness).

- (security) `LOAD_WAIT` is 5 s and under `ANSWER_BOUND` (30 s). The `settled` field's help states it, pinned by a
  unit test in `cargo test -p escher-driver --locked 2>&1` (per security-plan §API Security).

- (security) Nothing crosses that did not before:
  - no verb, argument, result field, refusal cause, session error, exit status or `Outcome` variant is added; the
    describe count row `[11, 13, 12, 3, 8, 4, 15]` is unmoved in the escher-driver unit gate;
  - no manifest or lock changes (the `git diff` probe);
  - the wall read lives in `session.rs` beside the three existing readers (the `Instant::now|thread::sleep`
    probe).

  (per security-plan §Input Validation, Driver command schema row)

- (obs) The `command` span keeps its eight fields and escher-driver its two span sites, with no event (the
  `info_span!` probe reads 2 and the event probe reads 0). On a waited step `passes` is the passes of the settle
  that went quiet (per obs-plan §4).

- (obs) The new check and its stand-in are silent: the census probe over `stand_load_wait.rs` reads 0 (per obs-plan
  §3).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run stand` passes with 0 failed, predicted 185 · 0 · 7 over 46 files. The CI
  run on the pushed sha reads `verdict: green`, its `stand-repeat` leg holding the new check three rounds under the
  zero-failure budget and the coverage job holding escher-driver at or above 97 % (per test-plan §10 Quality Gates
  & Coverage Targets).

- (a11y) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh a11y` stays green with its per-file counts unmoved (per a11y-plan §9 CI
  Integration).

- (tests) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` and `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` pass (CLAUDE.md
  invariants).

- Spec anchors: arch §Standard Contracts → Driver session, → Test harness · arch §Established Decisions [Driver
  session] · arch §Occupied Resources → Process-wide state and threads · security-plan §API Security («Settle and
  loads in flight», «Local session socket», «Request timeout») · security-plan §Input Validation (Driver command
  schema, MCP server, Cold-agent check) · obs-plan §3, §4, §8 · test-plan §3, §4, §5, §8, §10 · design-system §Motion
  §Animation runtime, §Surface: cli §Component Patterns · layout-templates §Surface: cli → Primary screens · a11y-plan
  §2, §5, §9.

- Amendment history: the settle-detection entry's standing rule says «a driver command that would wait on a load
  with a clock is a new decision for this plan» (security-plan sidecar). This chunk is that decision, taken on the
  version's requirement (intent §6, requirements.md:17).

- Research files inspected: `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs`, `packages/escher-driver/src/{execute,session,schema,lib,host,wire,client}.rs`,
  `tests/blitz-tests/tests/{fixtures/mod,stand_settle}.rs`, `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs`,
  `packages/blitz-dom/src/{mutator,net,resolve,document}.rs`, `packages/blitz-traits/src/net.rs`.

- Decisions taken at this P4:
  - **The bound, 5 s:** the operator's answer «5 s (Recommended)» to the one technical fork (dialog, 2026-10-20).
  - **A constant, not an argument:** leaned per security-plan §Input Validation, Driver command schema row. A
    caller-set bound is a new input on the validated surface.
  - **No span field:** leaned per obs-plan §4. A new `command` field lands only by a ruling, and the requirement
    asks for none.
  - **`passes`:** leaned to the passes of the settle that went quiet, which keeps the field's meaning.
  - **`Session::act` waits too:** leaned per research.md §Patterns detected, one settle seam per surface.
  - **A stylesheet load in the fixture:** leaned per research.md E1. It is the path `stand_settle` already proves on
    a harness, with no image decode.
  - **Playbook:** read before the round. No fork option ships what an escalate pattern names. No widening, no
    PROVISIONAL mark and no upstream-merge change are offered, so there is no founder fork this chunk.

- A wait inside `Harness::settle` — rejected. It would amend the test-harness contract (settle reads no clock and
  waits on no load) for every harness caller, where research found two production callers that both sit in
  escher-driver.

- A bound taken from the call, an env var or a file — rejected. That is a new input on the validated surface or a
  new env read (security-plan §Input Validation; §Secret Management).

- A wall read in blitz-dom, or moving the `VirtualClock`, the time step or the fade during a wait — rejected: it
  reopens the one-virtual-clock ruling, ratified by the founder on 2026-10-18.
- Draining or reading the changed set inside the wait — rejected (a11y-plan §2, the changed-set contract).

- A thread in the host or the `mcp` role for the wait — rejected. The wait runs on the calling thread
  (arch §Occupied Resources → Process-wide state and threads).

- Widening `fixtures::HeldNet` or adding the self-answering stand-in to `fixtures/mod.rs` — rejected. It has one
  reader, so it stays in its check's file (test-plan §3, the one-reader rule).

- An image as the fixture's load — rejected in favour of a stylesheet: no decode, and the same counted path
  `stand_settle` proves.

- A `has_changes()` witness of the load — rejected. A CSS or image load marks no changed node; the 6
  `changed_nodes.insert` sites are listed in research.md §Sweeps. The diff's `bounds` is the witness.
- A waited-time, «waited» or bound field on the `command` or `tool_call` span — not built: no ruling (obs-plan §4).

- **Race safety (E1, research.md):** `CountedHandler::bytes` posts the document's message before its `Drop`
  decrements `in_flight` (settle.rs:113-127). The settle after the answer therefore sees `loaded` and applies the
  sheet on its next pass.

- **Overrun:** a settle of the fixture is milliseconds, and the loop never sleeps past the deadline. The 2 s slack
  on the never-answered arm absorbs a loaded CI runner's slowest settle. The wait measures its own start, so the
  arm's reading includes the click's own pump.

- **Replay determinism:** a kept check whose app meets a load can now record `settled: true` where an offline replay
  would read `loads` after 5 s. The committed Counter checks meet no load (offline stand options), so `stand_replay`
  is unaffected. State the timing sensitivity in the wrap's Driver session amendment.

- **Coverage:** the four unit tests reach every branch of the inner loop in escher-driver's own unit run.
  escher-driver read 97.93 % against its 97 % floor at the last wrap (test-plan history). Predicted to stay at or
  above the floor; record what the coverage job measures.

- Expected amendments (wrap): architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session — an acting verb's settle waits on
  a load in flight up to `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s), moving no time. The statements «settling … waits on no load» and «no
  driver command waits on a load» retire. Re-exports become 56.

- Expected amendments (wrap): security-plan §API Security — the «Settle and loads in flight» row: the absent request
  timeout still cannot hang a command, because `LOAD_WAIT` ends every wait. Settle itself still never waits.
- Expected amendments (wrap): obs-plan §3 — session.rs joins the clock readers, for the wait and nothing else.

- Expected amendments (wrap): obs-plan §4 — the «settle wait» absent line, and `passes` on a waited step being the
  passes of the settle that went quiet.

- Expected amendments (wrap): test-plan §1, §3, §5, §9, §10 — `stand_load_wait` and its in-file self-answering
  stand-in. Its wall reads (`Instant::now()` around a call, the stand-in thread's 200 ms sleep) are the second
  recorded exception beside `stand_virtual_clock`'s sleep. The counts above move.

- Expected amendments (wrap): design-system §Motion §Animation runtime — the wait moves no clock, so a timer or an
  animation does not run during it.

- Expected amendments (wrap): layout-templates §Surface: cli → Primary screens — the `settled` help, and with it each
  acting tool's description, states the 5 s bound.
