   disabled gate stops a disabled select first, as it does a button.

8. **The `change` event** — `packages/blitz-traits/src/events.rs`: `DomEventKind::Change` (`from_str` "change",
   :190-210) and `DomEventData::Change(BlitzInputEvent)` with its `name` and `kind` arms (:268-310, :340-350).
   `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs` hands `Change` to the app as `NativeFormData`, as `Input`
   (:377-380). `packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime.rs` dispatches a real `Change` as its `change` event and keeps
   its own synthesized `change` for a checkbox or radio (:1671-1687) — never two for one choice. Every exhaustive
   match the new variant breaks gains its arm (the compiler names them).

9. **A `<label>` names every labelable element** — `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs`,
   `label_bound_input_element` (:678-703): both arms (`for`, and the first nested descendant) match HTML's labelable
   elements — `button`, `input` whose `type` is not `hidden`, `meter`, `output`, `progress`, `select`, `textarea` —
   in place of `input` alone; its name and signature unchanged. Its two callers move with it: the tree's label loop
   (accessibility.rs:53) and `handle_click`'s label arm (pointer.rs:860), which then focuses a select through step 7.

10. **The options in the tree** — `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs`: `is_hidden_from_accessibility_tree`
    (:244-257) keeps an `option` whose parent is a `select` although it computes `display: none` (`hidden` and `inert`
    still exclude it); such an option's node writes `selected` from its own `CHECKED` state, true or false, its
    `aria-selected` unread there (HTML-AAM: a native option's selectedness is its state). The role mapping stays
    (`ComboBox`, `ListBoxOption`, accessibility.rs:472-476).

11. **Form submission** — `packages/blitz-dom/src/form.rs`: the select step at form.rs:270-274, a named select's
    chosen option's value as its entry, the option not disabled.

12. **The snapshot** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs`:
    - the `value` reader (:238-262) gains a select branch, reading step 1's value through a public `BaseDocument`
      reader; its signature takes the node so `Builder::visit` (:170) can pass it;
    - an `option` whose parent is a `select` reads its select's client rect as its `bounds` (`Builder::visit`
      :142-147), so every option has the box an agent sees it in;
    - unit tests over stated tables: a select's value per row (a `value` attribute, text only, none chosen); its
      options listed under it with their labels as names, the chosen one `selected: Some(true)`, the others
      `Some(false)`; an option's bounds equal to its select's.
    No role or name is mapped here (a11y-plan §7: the tree's own).

13. **`type`'s help** — `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` (:207-208): one fixed sentence added — on a select,
    the text chooses the first option whose label starts with it. Its pin in
    `packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs` (:75-78) moves with it. No other driver line changes: `type` already
    clicks its target, presses select-all (a modified key step 6 ignores) where the snapshot reads a value, and types
    one character per key (execute.rs:171-189, :497-499; blitz-test-harness input.rs:222-226).

15. **The label rows** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_label.rs`: a `<label for>` and a wrapping `<label>`
    name a `select` and a `textarea`; a `<label for>` naming an `input type="hidden"` names nothing. Asserted with the
    file's own `verify_that!` form, both layout modes.

16. **The driver check** — new `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_select.rs`, both layout modes, a session held over
    an in-file fixture page through `fixtures::hold`: `button#fx-before`, `label[for=fx-pick] "Fruit"`,
    `select#fx-pick` (options `fx-apple` «Apple» `a`, `fx-banana` «Banana» `b` `selected`, `fx-cherry» «Cherry» `c`),
    `select#fx-named` `aria-label="Colour"` (`fx-red`, `fx-green`), `select#fx-off` `disabled` `aria-label="Off"`
    (`fx-x`), `button#fx-after`. Each option carries an author `id`, so `unkeyed_actionable` reads nothing:
    - at boot the snapshot reads `fx-pick` with role `ComboBox`, name `Fruit`, value `b`, its three options under it
      named by their labels, `fx-banana` selected;
    - `type --id fx-pick --text Cherry` is accepted and settled, its diff names `fx-pick` with `value` in `differs`
      and `fx-banana` / `fx-cherry` with `selected`, and the next snapshot reads `fx-pick` value `c`;
    - `click --id fx-named` then `press arrow-down` choose `fx-green`; `press home` chooses `fx-red`;
    - the Tab walk from boot reads `fx-before` → `fx-pick` → `fx-named` → `fx-after`, `fx-off` skipped, and reads the
      same after the choices;
    - `type --id fx-off --text X` is refused `disabled` with the snapshot unchanged; `click --id fx-apple` (an option
      not chosen) is refused `covered` with the snapshot unchanged.
    Its failure messages name a layout mode and a row index, never an id or a reading (test-plan §3 session-start).

17. **Sweeps and limits** — re-run the step-16 Tab walk, `stand_keyboard` and `accessibility_roles` unchanged (their
    files untouched); read the stated limits into the report: a `multiple` select and an `optgroup`'s options are
    not modelled; no popup is painted and an option is not clicked; a checkbox, radio or text input fires no engine
    `change` (vibey-script's own synthesis stays); an option with no author key reads in `unkeyed_actionable`.

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/select.rs` — a select's options, chosen option, value, the selectedness algorithm, steps
  and the typeahead match
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_interaction.rs` — the engine check, both layout modes
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_select.rs` — the driver check on an in-file fixture page
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/mod.rs` — declare the select module
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/element.rs` — seed `CHECKED` on an `option` from `selected`
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` — the typeahead buffer, the public select value reader, `label_bound_input_element` widened
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs` — `apply_select_choice` and the select key arm
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` — the select arm of `handle_click`
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` — re-seed on option and `selected` changes
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs` — keep a select's options, each `selected` by its state
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/form.rs` — the select's form entry
- `packages/blitz-dom/assets/default.css` — the select's box and its chosen option shown
- `packages/blitz-traits/src/events.rs` — `Change`
- `packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime.rs` — a real `Change` dispatched once
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs` — `Change` to the app
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs` — the select's value, an option's bounds, unit tests
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` — `type`'s help
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs` — its pin
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_label.rs` — the labelable rows

- Smoke: none — the test plan declares no boot-smoke paths, and by shape the stand's boot is untouched: its tasks hold
  no select, and the stylesheet rules this chunk adds match `select` and `option` alone. Every stand check boots the
  stand under `run stand`, the boot's witness.

- `evidence/checked-mechanism.md` is written by step 3's one-shot measurement, a step outside this block; no entry reads
  it, and the criterion that cites it is checked against it by the wrap.
- Live legs: none; both checks are in process and offline.

- CI: the per-OS run and `stand-repeat` are read in the operator pass through the seeded entries. `stand_act_select`
  joins `stand-repeat` by its prefix (.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh:48-59); `select_interaction` and
  `accessibility_label` run in the workspace `test` leg, not the a11y leg.

  session-start; a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation).

- (arch) The engine holds a select's choice as `CHECKED` on its chosen option and shows it as the select's content:
  the step-3 measurement in `evidence/checked-mechanism.md`, and `select_interaction`'s box rows (per arch §Established
  Decisions → [Scrolling and input]; arch §Cross-cutting Patterns → Invalidation and state integrity — a choice marks
  the changed set through `snapshot_node_and`, a no-change key marks nothing).

- (a11y) A focused select is operable by keyboard alone — the arrows, `Home`, `End` and a typed prefix — each change
  firing one `input` and one `change`, a no-change key firing none; a disabled select takes no key and no click and is
  skipped by Tab (`select_interaction`; per a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation, Keyboard handling).

- (a11y) A `<label>` names a `select` and a `textarea`, and an `input type="hidden"` nothing (`accessibility_label`;
  per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).

- (security) Nothing crosses the driver's surface that did not before: no verb, argument, key name, result field,
  refusal cause, session error or exit is added — the describe count row `[11, 13, 12, 3, 8, 4, 15]` unmoved in the
  escher-driver unit gate; option labels reach a client only as the `name` of their nodes and the value as `value`,
  inside the ratified crossings (per security-plan §Input Validation, Driver command schema row, Driver session
  socket row).

- (security) The select rules hold no print, log site, env read or panic path on page markup (the select.rs probe
  reads 0), and every gate reads `ElementData::is_disabled` (per security-plan §Input Validation, range-input row,
  `disabled` row).

- (obs) escher-driver keeps its two span sites with no field added, the new checks are silent, and blitz-dom gains no
  wall read (the `info_span!`, silence and `Instant::now` probes; per obs-plan §3, §4).

- A `SpecialElementData::Select` variant — rejected: the choice lives as `CHECKED` on the options, which the radio
  group already writes and `:checked` already reads; an enum variant is a source break for nothing.
- Special layout code painting a label — rejected: the user-agent rule shows the chosen option's own text.

- A popup, a windowed list or an option made clickable — not built (scope §Boundaries; F3 says an option is not
  clicked).

  F2 of 2026-10-14).
- A wall read for typeahead — rejected: the document's clock alone (arch, the document clock).

  bounds are read there.

  synthesis stays the checkbox's.

  what the executor reads.

- **`type`'s select-all:** `Ctrl`/`Cmd` + `a` reaches the select arm as a modified character and must change nothing;

- **Symbols / APIs** (coordinates from the `## New text, by line` listing below):
  - **The select's rules** — new module `blitz-dom::node::select` (`pub(crate) mod select`, node/mod.rs:10), cited to
    the WHATWG `select` element, unit-tested inline: `OptionReading` (17-26), `SelectStep` (`Next` · `Previous` ·
    `First` · `Last`, 28-39), `Typeahead` {select, text, at} (41-50), `TYPEAHEAD_TIMEOUT` = 1 s, `is_single_select`
    (55-58), `is_select_option` (60-68, an `option` whose parent is a `select`, read through `Node::with`),

    the `CHECKED` element state), `chosen_option` (94-100, the last chosen), `readings` (102-115), `option_label`
    (117-127, `label` attribute when not empty, else the text), `option_value` (129-139, `value` attribute when present,
    else the text), `option_text` / `strip_and_collapse` (141-153), `settled` (155-164, HTML's selectedness setting
    algorithm for a single-choice select: the last chosen, else the first option not disabled), `stepped` (166-181,
    next / previous / first / last not disabled; none chosen reads `Next` as `First`, `Previous` as `Last`), `matched`
    (183-193, the first enabled option whose label starts with the text, lowercase-compared; empty text matches
    nothing); `mod tests` (195-301, 4 table tests).

    HTML's `select.value` — the chosen option's value, `None` with none chosen or for a non-select; its non-test caller
    dioxus-native-dom's snapshot `value`, and `apply_select_choice`); `pub(crate)` `settle_select_choice` (730-743),
    `set_select_choice` (745-753, reads whether any option changed), `set_option_chosen` (755-775, the `CHECKED` write
    through `snapshot_node_and` for an in-document option, else a direct state write); new field
    `select_typeahead: Option<select::Typeahead>` (338-339, `None` at construction, 555); new private free fn
    `is_labelable` (3126-3140). **Changed:** `label_bound_input_element` — name and signature unchanged, both arms now
    match HTML's labelable elements (`button`, `input` whose `type` is not `hidden` ASCII-case-insensitively, `meter`,
    `output`, `progress`, `select`, `textarea`) in place of `input` alone; its two callers unchanged in code and moved
    in behaviour: the accessibility tree's label loop (a `<label>` now names a select, a textarea, a button…) and
    `handle_click`'s label arm (a click on a select's label re-dispatches to the select, focusing it).
  - **Keyboard** (events/keyboard.rs): a select arm in `handle_key_or_input_event` (108-113) — focused element
    `select::is_single_select`, `!ElementData::is_disabled()`, a pressed `KeyPress` — calling the private
    `press_select_key` (165-200): `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` next/previous enabled option, `Home`/`End` first/last, a

    released Space activates no select — `activates_on_space` unchanged). `BaseDocument::type_into_select` (private,
    248-269: the buffer starts afresh for another select or when `Clock::now() − at ≥ 1 s`) and
    `pub(crate) apply_select_choice(select, option, dispatch_event)` (271-297: the one write · mark · events · redraw
    path — `set_select_choice`; where a choice changed, the select joins `changed_nodes`, `Input` then `Change` are
    dispatched, each carrying `select_value`, and a redraw is requested; a choice of the chosen option fires nothing).
  - **Pointer** (events/pointer.rs:857-870): a `select` arm in `handle_click`'s walk — clears `select_typeahead` and

    `select` arm (1211-1215) — every tree entry point that calls it on the parent (`append_children`,
    `insert_nodes_before`, `insert_nodes_after`, `replace_node_with`, `remove_node`, `remove_and_drop_node`,

    `select` entering the document (1097-1101); `set_attribute` / `clear_attribute` of `selected` call the private

    single-choice select's other options not (exclusive), cleared sets it not chosen, its select recorded; `flush`

  - **Form** (form.rs:276-290): a named `select`'s entries — every chosen option that is not disabled, its

title: Measured (the residual's ask: a `select` under the driver's verbs first)

data.head: ## Measured (the residual's ask: a `select` under the driver's verbs first)

body:
A throwaway probe held a fixture page — `button#fx-before` · `label[for=fx-pick] "Fruit"` · `select#fx-pick` (Apple /
Banana `selected` / Cherry) · `select#fx-named` `aria-label="Colour"` (Red / Green) · `select#fx-off` `disabled`
`aria-label="Off"` · `button#fx-after` — in a driver session (`fixtures::hold`) and on a booted harness, in both
layout modes, and was removed after the run. Source and readings: `evidence/select-probe.rs.txt`,
`evidence/select-probe-readings.txt`. Every reading below is identical in both modes.

- **A `select` lays out as nothing.** Its computed display is `inline`, its layout `0×0`, and
  `BaseDocument::get_client_bounding_rect` returns `None` for it. Each `option` computes `display: none` (UA rule
  `option { display: none; }`, packages/blitz-dom/assets/default.css:146-148). With every child out of flow the inline
  box holds no fragment, so the select has no rect (the `label` beside it, holding text, reads 35.48×23).

- **The snapshot leaves it out.** `Builder::visit` keeps an element only when its client rect resolves
  (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs:142-147), so neither select is a snapshot node: the boot snapshot lists
  `fx-before`, the label and `fx-after` alone. Every id-addressed verb on a select is refused `not-found` with nothing
  run — `click fx-pick`, `type fx-pick …`, `click fx-named`, `click fx-off`, `screenshot --id fx-pick`.

- **The accessibility tree holds it, empty.** Each select is a `ComboBox` node with 0 children (the options are
  excluded as `display: none`, accessibility.rs:244-257); `fx-named` and `fx-off` read their `aria-label`; `fx-pick`
  reads no label — a `<label>` binds an `input` alone (`label_bound_input_element`, document.rs:678-703, matching
  `local_name!("input")` on both arms); no node reads a value.

- **It takes focus and no key.** Both enabled selects are focusable and the disabled one is not
  (`is_focussable`): Tab walks `fx-before` → `fx-pick` → `fx-named` → `fx-after` → `fx-before`, the two select stops
  showing in the diff only as `fx-before` losing focus (tab 2) and an empty diff (tab 3). On a focused select
  `press arrow-down`, `home`, `enter` and `space` each settle with an empty diff.

- **What an option change could reach.** blitz-traits has no `change` event kind (`DomEventKind`,
  packages/blitz-traits/src/events.rs:140-158 — `Input` the one form event); the Dioxus bridge hands `Input` to the app
  as `NativeFormData { value }` (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:377-380), so an `oninput` handler is
  the one a select change can reach, as the range model's does. Form submission skips a select (the WHATWG step is a
  `TODO`, packages/blitz-dom/src/form.rs:270-274).

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs` (10-90, 200-280, 320-345, 465-480) — the role mapping (`select` →
  `ComboBox`, `multiple` → `ListBox`, `option` → `ListBoxOption`), the label loop, the hidden-node exclusion
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` (678-710) — `label_bound_input_element`, `input` alone

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/element.rs` (480-490, 715-745) — `can_be_disabled` and default focusability both
  name `select`
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/range.rs` (1-60) — the range model: `RangeInputData` held apart from the attribute
- `packages/blitz-dom/assets/default.css` (75-100, 140-150) — `select` only in the font rule; `option` display none
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/form.rs` (255-285) — the select entry `TODO`
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs` (20-262) — the node model, the bounds gate, the `value` reader
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs` (355-395) — events handed to Dioxus
- `packages/blitz-traits/src/events.rs` (140-160, 240-260) — the event kinds

- `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs` (100-360) — `click` / `type` resolve through the snapshot; `type` clicks,
  selects all where the snapshot reads a value, then types
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` (18-31) — the twelve `KEY_NAMES`
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs` (1-60) — `boot`, `hold`, the shared pages
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs` (1-110) — the call builders
- `.andromeda/residuals.md` (line 11) — the absorbed residual

- **label_bound_input_element** — 2 callers: `build_accessibility_tree` @ packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:53
  and `handle_click` @ packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:860 — widening it to a `select` also moves what a click
  on its `<label>` does (focus moves to the select), in every document.

- **value** (snapshot.rs) — 1 caller, `Builder::visit` @ packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs:170 — a select
  branch in the reader reaches every snapshot through that one site.

- **apply_range_move** — 2 callers, `press_range_input_key` @ events/keyboard.rs:153 and `press_range_input` @
  events/pointer.rs:672 — the one write · mark · `input` · redraw path a select change would copy.

- **flush_range_input** — 1 caller, `collect_layout_children_with_wrap` @ layout/construct.rs:436 — where a control's
  special data is seeded at box construction.

- Trace: `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-20T03-46-58-phase/tree-query-2026-10-20-select-by-id.json` (rust plane rebuilt,
  8647 nodes / 52389 edges; every row count > 0).

- **The range interaction model** (node/range.rs:1-60, events/keyboard.rs:99-153, events/pointer.rs:449-672,
  layout/construct.rs:932-944, mutator.rs:357-507): a `SpecialElementData` variant holding the current value apart from
  the attribute, seeded at box construction, re-seeded on a `value` write, moved by key and pointer arms gated on
  `is_disabled`, every change through one write · mark · `input` path.

- **A test-only control on a fixture page** (`fixtures::password_named`, fixtures/mod.rs:38-45; the textarea on
  `stand_snapshot_state`'s page): named by `aria-label`, because a `<label>` binds an `input` alone.

- **Driver resolution through the snapshot** (execute.rs:333-357): `click` and `type` find their target as a snapshot
  node; an element the snapshot does not list cannot be acted on, whatever the engine holds.
- **Both layout modes**: every engine and fixture check runs `for incremental in [false, true]` (arch §Conventions).

- **Handler arms as private named functions**: `handle_click` / `handle_key_or_input_event` keep their signatures;
  a new arm is a private function (`press_range_input_key` precedent, events/keyboard.rs:140).

- **Key names**: the driver's are `arrow-up` · `arrow-down` · `home` · `end` (schema.rs:18-31) — `arrowdown` is
  refused `malformed` (measured).

title: The answered forks (inputs#I2) and where each lands

data.head: ## The answered forks (inputs#I2) and where each lands

body:
The operator answered every fork with its recommendation, as delegate, PROVISIONAL for the founder's word: F1 keys and
typeahead through the verbs there are; F2 the engine shows the chosen option's label; F3 options read as the select's
children; F4 a `change` event, and a `<label>` names HTML's labelable elements. The sites below are read at HEAD:

- **The chosen option as `:checked`** — the radio group already writes a choice as the `CHECKED` element state through
  `snapshot_node_and` (document.rs:735, `toggle_radio`), which restyles `:checked` (stylo.rs:470 reads the state) and
  marks the changed set (document.rs:1660-1662); `ElementData` seeds `CHECKED` from a markup attribute at creation
  (element.rs:443-452, a checkbox's `checked`). HTML says a chosen `option` matches `:checked`, so the select's choice
  can be that state on its options — and a user-agent rule `select:not([multiple]) > option:checked { display: inline }`
  lays the chosen option's own text out as the select's content, with no special layout code (F2).

- **Seeding and re-seeding** — the mutator's attribute hooks re-seed a range input on a `value` write
  (mutator.rs:367-378 `set_attribute`, :490-500 `clear_attribute`); its tree entry points are `append_children`
  (:707), `insert_nodes_before` (:713), `insert_nodes_after` (:841), `replace_node_with` (:857), `remove_node` (:590)
  and `remove_and_drop_node` (:614) — where an option's `selected` write and an option's insertion or removal re-run
  HTML's selectedness setting algorithm on its select.

- **Keys and typeahead** — `handle_key_or_input_event`'s arms (events/keyboard.rs:80-116): the range arm is gated on
  `range_input_data` and no `disabled` (:99-104) and calls `press_range_input_key` (:140-154), which hands a move to
  `apply_range_move` (:238). A select arm sits beside it. `Harness::type_text` presses one `Key::Character` per
  character (blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs:222-226), and the driver's `type` first presses select-all (`Ctrl`/`Cmd`
  + `a`, execute.rs:497-499) on a control the snapshot reads a value for — a modified key the select arm must ignore.
  So `type --id <select> --text <label>` reaches typeahead with no driver code change.

- **A click focuses it** — `handle_click`'s walk (events/pointer.rs:840-900) has a `label` arm that re-dispatches the
  click to `label_bound_input_element`'s target (:858-866) and a button arm that focuses (`click_button`); a select arm
  beside them focuses the select and starts typeahead afresh.

- **`change`** — `DomEventKind` (blitz-traits/src/events.rs:140-158, `from_str` :190-210) and `DomEventData`
  (:240-260, `name` :268-310, `kind` :340-350) gain `Change`; the Dioxus bridge counts listeners per kind index in a
  64-slot array (mutation_writer.rs:23, :349-358) and hands `Input` to the app as `NativeFormData`

- (a11y) The `a11y` leg runs the fourteen files of the founder's «Плюс проверки дерева (Рекомендую)» (inputs#I1):
  `accessibility_hidden`, `accessibility_roles`, `focusability_updates`, `stand_keyboard`, `stand_contrast`,
  `stand_accessibility_ids`, `accessibility_states`, `accessibility_label`, `accessibility_description`,
  `accessibility_merged_states`, `accessibility_active_descendant_unread`, `inert_subtree`, `select_interaction`,
  `stand_act_select`. Witnessed by the names probe reading those fourteen words in that order, by `bash
  .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh a11y` exiting 0, and by its tally probe reading `lines 14` and `failed 0`, its passed
  count recorded per file (predicted 84) (per a11y-plan §9 CI Integration).

- (a11y) Every added file witnesses an SC 2.1.1 or 2.4.3 requirement, or a tree reading the founder took into the
  leg, or pins a recorded gap. `inert_subtree` covers Tab skipping an inert subtree. `select_interaction` and
  `stand_act_select` cover the select by keys and through the driver. The five tree reads are `accessibility_states`,
  `accessibility_label`, `accessibility_description`, `accessibility_merged_states` and
  `accessibility_active_descendant_unread`, the last pinning the unread `aria-activedescendant`, a gap and not a
  closed requirement. The leg already ran the non-tier-0 `accessibility_hidden` and `accessibility_roles` (per a11y-plan
  §1, §3; inputs#I1).

- (a11y) The stand's Tab order, Enter/Space activation and contrast are re-read after 0.2.0. `stand_keyboard`,
  `stand_contrast` and `stand_accessibility_ids` read green in the widened leg (workspace build), in the per-package
  run of the fourteen and in `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh stand-repeat` (three rounds). The guard entry shows
  `common::tab_order`, `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER`, `controls`, `TEXT_ROWS` and `STATE_ROWS` unedited, so nothing is
  re-baselined. SC 1.4.3 holds on every non-exempt stand row, and the exempt class stays `enabled == Some(false)`
  (per a11y-plan §5 Test harness pattern, §6 Color contrast; layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary
  screens; design-system §Color Palette).

- (tests) `LegScriptTest`'s a11y tuple names the same fourteen words, and `python3 -m unittest discover -s
  .github/scripts -p test_ci_workflows.py` reads `Ran 33 tests` and `OK`. `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` is
  green (its `ci-scripts` leg at 100 tests). The workspace tally probe reads `failed 0` (predicted lines 206, passed
  1105, unchanged) (per test-plan §4 CI workflows and leg script, §9 Legs).

- (tests) `stand-repeat` comes through unchanged. The numstat probe reads `1 1` (one line of `ci-leg.sh` replaced).
  `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_requirement_sweep` passes. `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh
  stand-repeat` ends `stand-repeat: 3 of 3 rounds green` (per test-plan §10 Flakiness budget, §1).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh boot` reads ready, and `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run stand` reads `"failed":
  0` (per test-plan §3 Agent-run contract).

- (arch) The `ci.yml` "Accessibility (a11y) tests" job keeps its tier, its `needs`, its `workspace-test` restore with
  `save-if: false`, its failure-only `ci-log-*` upload and no required status check. The guard reads `guard: clean`
  with only the two scripts allowed, so `ci.yml` is byte-identical, and the chunk changes no repository setting (per
  architecture §Standard Contracts → CI contracts, §Occupied Resources → CI infrastructure; obs-plan §9).

- (security) The leg line keeps `--locked` (the names probe's anchor). `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `deny.toml`,
  `rust-toolchain.toml`, `packages/` and blitz-tests' manifest are unchanged, so the manifest probe reads `0` and no
  package, env read, dependency or engine line enters (per security-plan §Dependency Security, Lockfile verification;
  §Secret Management, Environment values read).

  graph holds no platform adapter (the `cargo tree` probe reads 0). escher-driver keeps its two `info_span!` sites,

body: Each commit cherry-picked with `-x`, then `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` (base: exit 0, 38.8 s warm).

- **Shape A — the cherry-pick take.** In upstream order: `28f848d3b` (one conflict, below), `9eeebb302`, `e4ca5b9b5`, `46d7cf993`, `fb297a38c`, `50bf2f235`, `f8723f495`, `21edc92d9`, `f102663b8`, `f9cbb2756` — every one picks clean but the first and checks exit 0 after each; then `cargo update -p tokio`. On that tree: `cargo fmt --all --check` 0 · `cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings` 0 · `cargo deny --locked --workspace --all-features check advisories licenses` 0, `advisories ok, licenses ok` · `cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast` 0: **206 result lines · 1099 passed · 0 failed · 12 ignored** against the base's 205 · 1098 · 0 · 12 (test-plan-detail/ci-integration.md:59) — +1 line and +1 passed, exactly upstream's new target `hit_test_dropped_nodes` (1 test); `stale_node_mapping` 4 unmoved; 0 `Running tests/all.rs` lines (`tally.py` over the merged stream). No stand number moved: every stand check, `stand_replay` and seven_guis `recording` (the committed Counter checks) green.

- **Not takeable on Stylo 0.22.0** — `3954ecb85` sets `layout.css.text-indent-keywords.enabled` and `layout.css.word-break.break-word.enabled`, neither in stylo_static_prefs 0.22.0's 57-line `preferences.toml` (its pick conflicts in `document.rs` on 0.23's renamed prefs); `1c5265a8b` implements `TElement::set_may_have_animations` and calls `has_active_animations_or_transitions`, neither in stylo 0.22.0 (`dom.rs:765` holds `may_have_animations` alone; `servo/animation.rs:1660-1668` holds `has_active_animations` and `has_active_transitions`) — its pick conflicts in `stylo.rs`. Both need `06ecec886` (Stylo 0.23-pre, git).

- **Shape B — A plus `286874cc1`** (Dioxus `0.8.0-alpha.3`, a crates.io pre-release, no git source): picks with `Cargo.lock` alone conflicting, every dioxus-native(-dom) file auto-merging; re-locked by cargo; `cargo check` exits 101 — dioxus-native-dom lib 10 errors, lib test 15, every site in escher's own `element_id.rs` (26-27, 78-127) and `dioxus_document_tests.rs` (12, 150-156): dioxus-core 0.8 reshaped `VNode` (`template`, `key`, `dynamic_nodes`, `mounted_root` now methods or gone), `DynamicNode::Placeholder`, `TemplateNode`, `DioxusState` (`node_id_mapping` gone, `stack` private), plus a `rustc_hash` import whose dependency the commit drops (inputs#I3 item 3). A port of the stable-id derivation onto Dioxus 0.8 — unmeasured past the compile errors.

- **Shape C — the whole merge of `f9cbb2756`.** `git merge` conflicts in `Cargo.lock`, `mutator.rs`, `scrolling.rs` and `construct.rs` (the last auto-resolved by rerere from shape A's pick — below); resolved as the take's resolutions plus: `scrolling.rs` upstream's `use stylo_taffy::CopyStyleGetters;` without its `web_time` line; `mutator.rs` ours (the conflict is the last sync's cherry-picked `38ca4e777` meeting upstream's own copy); the lock upstream's, re-locked. `cargo check` exits 101 on its first escher-owned line: blitz-dom 1 error, our `contain: paint` hit stop's `style.get_box().clone_contain()` (`node/node.rs:1531` at HEAD), absent under Stylo 0.23; no crate past blitz-dom reached, so shape B's dioxus-native-dom port is owed on top (inputs#I3 item 4). No `Instant::now()`/`SystemTime::now()` outside `clock.rs` on that tree.
- **Shape D — the audit fix alone.** The tokio lock move of shape A on HEAD; nothing of upstream taken.

- **Side effect, left standing:** git rerere is on (`~/.config/git/config`, `rerere.enabled true`) and recorded seven resolutions of these trials in the shared `.git/rr-cache` (`d3e70713…` `document.rs`, `46a43bbc…` `stylo.rs`, `4f8055e9…` `construct.rs`, `58a28736…` and `4439e693…` `Cargo.lock`, `ce4a55b6…` `mutator.rs`, `d2055d86…` `scrolling.rs`, 12:54–13:03 local); this host's guard refuses a recursive `rm`, so they stand. A pick of `28f848d3b` under /implement will apply `4f8055e9…`'s resolution — the intended one (upstream's import line plus `RangeInputData`) — and git says so ("Resolved … using previous resolution"); the trial worktree stays registered (`git worktree list`) until the operator removes it.

   4. README.md holds «the », the number word of the verb count, then « driver commands as tools» — «the twelve driver
      commands as tools» while `VERBS` holds twelve.

   No helper method takes a `test_` prefix (testing.md Session Additions, 2026-10-06). Every expected count is
   computed from what the module reads, never a literal beside it (testing.md Session Additions, 2026-10-15). It
   reads the files by path from the repository root (`Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]`), writes nothing, and reads
   no environment variable.

4. **Write the Viola pointer** — `../viola/viola-0.2.0-incubator/research/escher-capabilities.md`, outside this
   repository and untracked there (Viola's `.gitignore:6` ignores the incubator, inputs#I1). It holds a title, one
   sentence saying the file points at Escher's capability statement for Viola's 0.2.0 frontend planning, then these
   three lines at column 0:
   - `repository: Turbolet85/escher`
   - `path: docs/capabilities.md`
   - `commit: written by the operator pass after the pre-CI commit`

   The operator pass's pointer entry (Test Commands) rewrites the `commit:` line with the pushed sha. The file holds
   no copy of the statement, no host path and no e-mail address. Its full text is recorded in
   `chunks/2026-10-25-capability-statement/evidence/viola-pointer.md`.
5. **Run the gates** in the order of Test Commands, and record the counts in `evidence/counts.md`.

6. **The operator's confirmation (operator pass, after the pointer's commit line is written)** — the operator reads
   `docs/capabilities.md` at the pushed commit and the Viola pointer, and writes
   `chunks/2026-10-25-capability-statement/evidence/operator-confirm.md`. It holds one `confirmed: ` line with the
   pushed sha, the date and who confirmed, plus any correction asked. A correction is a fix commit on top, re-pushed
   and re-read as the operator pass's fix rule says, and the confirmation names the final sha. `/implement` writes no
   part of this file; the last operator entry reads it.
- `docs/capabilities.md` — the capability statement (step 1)
- `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py` — the drift pin (step 3)
- `README.md` — line 48's verb count and the statement link (step 2)

- `../viola/viola-0.2.0-incubator/research/escher-capabilities.md` — the untracked pointer (step 4, F1 A, inputs#I2);
  no other file of the Viola tree is touched

No live leg runs and no external process is driven. The chunk changes no Rust source, stand markup or boot path, so
there is no `smoke` or `self-verify` entry: no boot-path change, and no UI. The real boot smoke is `/implement` P3's.
The workspace gates still run as the done gate (CLAUDE.md). The chunk adds no OS-conditional site, since a markdown
file and a python unittest are read by the linux `ci-scripts` job alone. The acceptance needs the pushed commit, both
for the pointer's `commit:` line and for the CI run's verdict, so the plan carries the operator pass's hygiene, push,
CI read and pointer write. `evidence/operator-confirm.md` is produced by step 6, the operator's own read in the operator pass, by no entry here; its reader, the last entry, carries no `artifact`. The pointer entries read a path outside this repository (`../viola/…`), which exists on the
dev host alone; no CI job reads them.

body:
- (arch) `docs/capabilities.md` stands at the pushed commit with its five sections in order. Its verb list is the twelve
  of `VERBS` in three levels, its causes the eight of `CAUSES`, its session errors fifteen, its node keys thirteen and
  its exit statuses four, each read from the schema's tables and none hand-copied (per architecture §Standard
  Contracts → Driver session). The `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -p test_capability_statement.py
  2>&1` entry reads `Ran 4 tests` and `OK`.

- (arch) README.md says the MCP role gives «the twelve driver commands as tools», with no line reading «the eleven
  driver commands», and links `docs/capabilities.md`; only that one line changes (per architecture §Project Intent →
  Front page). Witnesses: the README entries above.

- (security) The MCP section names the trust boundary as the spawning client holding stdio, with no authentication. It
  lists what a result carries: ids, accessible names, control values with a password's and a file input's value as
  the fixed mask, snapshot text and diffs, a shot as an `image` block with a password painted masked, and a lint's
  findings. It names no description, since descriptions go to the platform adapter only. It states that what a client
  does with a result, a model provider included, is the client's (per security-plan §Threat Model Summary;
  §Authentication & Authorization).

- (security) The statement claims no authentication for the socket beyond its `0700` directory and `0600` socket, and
  none for MCP beyond holding the stdio (per security-plan §Authentication & Authorization). The committed text holds
  no credential, token, auth header or host home path (per security-plan §Secret Management); the secret-search entry
  above is the witness.

- (security) Nothing in the chunk adds a carrier, verb, field, exit, log field or span (per security-plan §Input
  Validation, the Driver session socket rows' widening rule). The guard entry above reads `guard: clean`.

- (design) The carriers' output is described as one JSON line, or JSON-RPC 2.0 lines, on stdout, with no colour or ESC
  byte and exit `0` · `1` · `2` · `3` (per design-system §Surface: cli). Any contrast claim names the stand accent
  `#3a5ce5` at 5.47 (hover 6.83, active 8.27) on the stand's accent controls alone (per design-system §Color Palette).

- (layouts) The stand reach is stated headless, at the pinned 800 × 600, scale 1.0, Light viewport with one bundled
  font, and the windowed stand as not measured. The lint's stand readings are 0 findings at boot on each lean task and
  `crud-person-14` `clipped` inside `crud-list` after twelve Creates (per layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native).

- (tests) Every limit called «pinned» names the check that pins it. The select's unmodelled parts are «asserted by no
  check». The boolean model's two limits are «pinned at unit and engine level only». The cross-OS shot limit cites
  CI#39225375577. The 2026-10-15 live cold-agent run is stated as measured at eleven tools and not re-fired since
  `lint` made twelve (per test-plan §1; §2; §3 Cold-agent run pipe).

- (tests) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` and `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` exit 0 on the tree that holds
  the statement, the README edit and the pin (per test-plan §9 CI Integration). The operator pass's
  `python -X utf8 ~/.claude/skills/andromeda-tools/scripts/ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1800` reads
  `verdict: green` on the pushed sha, and the report names the run id it read.

- (obs) Every telemetry claim names the two spans `command` and `tool_call` with closed-word, bool and count fields,
  stderr-only output, and no driver line at the default `warn`. The scrub's limits are named: the raw panic message,
  `log.file` on a bridged `js_console` record, the dropped third-party WARN or ERROR, and the unscrubbed upstream apps
  and WPT runner (per obs-plan §4; §8).

- (a11y) The accessibility reach names SC 2.1.1 · 1.4.3 · 2.4.3 as the tier-0 target and no other criterion as met. It
  names the `a11y` leg's fourteen files at 14 · 84 · 0 · 0 on CI#40134371519, with no required status check. It states
  the assistive-technology reading at a windowed run as unmeasured, since no stand binary builds a platform adapter,
  owned by its residuals line (`re-carried:0.2.0`, which this version does not reach). Among its limits are the unbuilt
  focus fixup, the unmodelled `multiple` and `optgroup` select parts, the unread `aria-activedescendant` and the
  native checked state absent from the tree (per a11y-plan §1; §5; §9).

- (v020-10) `verification-matrix.json#v020-10` — operator-confirmed (`manual`). The statement stands at the pushed
  commit, its pin green. README links it. Viola's pointer `viola-0.2.0-incubator/research/escher-capabilities.md`
  names `docs/capabilities.md` and that commit; the pointer entries and the operator's commit-line entry above are
  the witnesses. Before Viola's `viola-0.2.0/` exists, the operator confirms the statement is current with 0.2.0
  where that planning reads it, and the confirmation is recorded in
  `chunks/2026-10-25-capability-statement/evidence/operator-confirm.md`.

- Spec anchors: architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session, §Established Decisions → Driver session · Scrolling
  and input · DOM semantics, §Occupied Resources, §Project Intent → Front page, §Existing Scopes; security-plan §Threat
  Model Summary, §Authentication & Authorization, §Input Validation, §Data Protection, §API Security, §Secret
  Management, §Logging & Monitoring, §Error Handling; design-system §Surface: cli, §Color Palette, §Typography,
  §Motion, §Depth Strategy; layout-templates §Surface: cli, §Surface: desktop-native; test-plan §1, §2, §3, §6, §9;
  obs-plan §2, §3, §4, §6, §8, §9; a11y-plan §1, §2, §5, §6, §7, §9.

- Research files inspected: `README.md`, `packages/escher-driver/src/{schema,refusal,error,session,host,client,lib}.rs`,
  `.andromeda/security-plan-detail/threat-model-summary.md`, `.andromeda/residuals.md`, `escher-0.2.0/requirements.md`,
  `escher-0.2.0/intent.md`, `.andromeda/architecture.md` (Directory structure), `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh`; inputs#I1,
  inputs#I2.

- Code-graph: `VERBS` 36 reference sites over 14 files, `CAUSES` / `NODE_FIELDS` / `EXIT_STATUSES` read by
  `describe.rs` (trace `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-25T02-58-45-phase/tree-query-2026-10-25-capability-statement.json`). No
  symbol changes, so no caller is touched.

- Leaned «the scope's AT-witness owner reads `re-carried:0.2.0`» per `.andromeda/residuals.md:14` and
  requirements.md:42-43. This overrides the a11y, tests and security extracts' «target: next» (research.md, the scope
  premise closure).

- Paging the diff or the lint's findings — CARRY 2 asks the limit stated, not fixed; paging is a new argument on a
  ratified carrier (security-plan §Input Validation, the widening rule).
- A full copy of the statement in Viola's incubator — F1 chose a pointer; a copy drifts from escher (inputs#I2).
- Writing any tracked file in the Viola repository, or touching its other incubator files — the pointer alone, untracked.

- Restating the role, name or state mapping, or the stand's control tables — the statement points at the masters and at
  `help` (a11y-plan §7, «never a second role or name mapping»).

title: Statement content (each item required; the source after it)

data.head: ### Statement content (each item required; the source after it)

body: **What it can do**

- Driver: one held headless instance per `Session`, every call through `Session::run` after `validate`. It is carried
  four ways: in process, over a unix-domain socket (`start` · `attach` · `stop` · `call`, wire `v3`, idle expiry
  1,800 s), by the `escher-session` command line, and by the `escher-session mcp` stdio role. A kept check is a fifth
  medium, at rest (arch §Standard Contracts → Driver session).

- The twelve verbs in three levels, each named: `snapshot` · `click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll` ·
  `screenshot` · `lint`, then `start` · `status` · `stop`, then `help` (schema.rs:490-492).

- The eight refusal causes, each named, in their fixed order; the fifteen session errors; four exit statuses; seven
  argument kinds with bounds (refusal.rs:35; error.rs:80; schema.rs:506; security-plan §Input Validation).

- Stable element ids: four tiers, computed on demand, persistent across a re-render, a remount and a fresh process,
  carried as AccessKit `author_id`, with no `NodeId` crossing. The actionable-key check runs in process only, with no
  wire form (arch §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge).

- The snapshot: id · role · name · state · bounds, thirteen node keys; its text form under the 10,000-byte budget; its
  parts (`snapshot --part`, 1 to 1,000); its diff by stable id, with `differs` naming the readings that moved (arch
  §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge).

- Acting and settling: each acting verb is one settled step returning the diff; the refusal order `stale` /
  `not-found`, then `disabled` · `off-screen` · `covered`; `type` replaces what a control holds, and on a select it
  chooses by label prefix; `scroll` goes through every scrolling box and answers `in_view`; the load wait is `LOAD_WAIT`,
  5 s of wall time, on the five acting verbs, moving no time (arch §Standard Contracts → Driver session).

- One virtual clock: `advance` moves the session's clock by exactly `ms`; two `click`s on one point with no `advance` of
  500 ms between them read as a double click — (sampler) a11y-plan/keyboard-navigation#2.4.

- The headless screenshot: a PNG equal to the harness raster, the whole screen or one element's visible part,
  `fonts-unavailable` when no `sans-serif` family resolves (design-system §Typography).

- The visual lint: six defects with ids, closed words and numbers only, changing nothing (arch §Standard Contracts →
  Driver session).

- Session recording and replay: `--record <dir>`, owner-only, a masked `type` kept as the stand-in, a shot without
  pixels, replay through `Session::run` that stops at the first difference; the two committed Counter checks are the
  one public exception (security-plan §Data Protection).

- Engine behaviours every document gets: the range input model, keyboard activation by Enter and Space, a button's and
  a select's click focus, the single-choice select model, `inert` and `disabled` read by presence on a form control
  (arch §Established Decisions → Scrolling and input · DOM semantics).

- Snapshot, text, parts, diff and the actionable-key check stand behind the default `accessibility` feature, which
  escher-driver names unconditionally — (sampler) architecture/cross-cutting-patterns#1.1.

- The stand everything is proven on: four lean tasks booted headless, offline, at a pinned 800 × 600 Light viewport
  with one bundled DejaVu Sans; author ids on all seven tasks (layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native).

- The toolchain and pins a consumer builds against: edition 2024, rust-version 1.91.0 — (sampler)
  architecture/stack-and-technologies#1.1. Escher's version (0.2.0) is kept apart from the crates' shared workspace
  version 0.3.0-beta.4 — (sampler) architecture/stack-and-technologies#1.2. The stack: Stylo 0.22.0, Taffy 0.15,
  Dioxus 0.7.3, with the waiting upgrades named as next-version work — (sampler) architecture/project-intent#1.0. The
  escher crates set `publish = false`, so they are reached from the repository — (sampler)
  architecture/inherited-defaults#1.1.
**Stated limits** (grouped: measured-off readings · pinned by a check · asserted by no check · unmeasured · not built)

- The three measured-off readings, in the tool's own words (refusal.rs:20-29): `covered` on a box clipped on one axis,
  `covered` on a box with no width or height, and `off-screen` inside a transformed scrolling box.
- The boolean model's two limits, pinned at unit and engine level only.

- CARRY 2: an acting verb's diff and a lint's findings are not paged; they are held only by the 1,048,576-byte answer
  bound, while `snapshot` alone reads a screen in parts (large-screen-in-parts report, «The stated limit»).

- The socket host, client and recording are unix only (`Unsupported` elsewhere); a session held in process and the
  MCP stdio role run elsewhere too (arch §Standard Contracts → Driver session; test-plan §2).
- A shot's PNG bytes repeat on one host and differ across OSes (CI#39225375577).
- The bounded record of ids (4096) — past it a once-read id reads `not-found`.
- Not built: a settle verb or busy-source reply.

- The select: `multiple` and `optgroup` options not modelled, no popup, an option not clicked (refused `covered`),
  asserted by no check; a controlled app must write `selected` back or a choice reverts. A single-choice select shows
  its chosen option's label alone — (sampler) design-system/surface#1.2. Its contrast pair is unmeasured — (sampler)
  a11y-plan/visual-design-verification#1.6. A `multiple` select still maps to `ListBox` — (sampler)
  a11y-plan/aria-patterns-roles#2.5.

- `text_extent`: RTL and vertical text are read as LTR lines and a transformed box at its client rect, pinned by
  `text_extent`. Vertical writing modes are in no default feature set — (sampler)
  architecture/established-decisions#5.1.

- HTML's focus fixup is not built (pinned by `inert_subtree`); `:focus-visible` · `:valid` · `:invalid` · `:required` ·
  `:target` always read false — (sampler) a11y-plan/keyboard-navigation#1.9.

- The Dioxus bridge: focus and blur events are not queued — (sampler) a11y-plan/keyboard-navigation#4.6; IME events are
  not handled — (sampler) a11y-plan/keyboard-navigation#4.8; animation and transition event data, and twelve
  event-data conversions in all, are `unimplemented!()` — (sampler) design-system/motion#4.3, (sampler)
  security-plan/error-handling#2.1.

- No verb takes a URL; `file:` URLs are read with no path restriction; no request timeout, the load wait bounding the
  driver; no same-origin or CORS check — (sampler) security-plan/input-validation#1.35; security-plan §API Security.
  A document handed no providers runs on the no-op defaults — (sampler) architecture/design-philosophy#2.1.

- The telemetry sink's reach: stderr only, records outside the two prefix sets dropped at every level, the rest
  scrubbed — (sampler) architecture/cross-cutting-patterns#2.1 (×2). Its holes: the raw panic message, and `log.file`
  on a bridged `js_console` record. The upstream apps' `fmt::init()` and the WPT runner are unscrubbed. Both binaries
  log `service.name=seven_guis`. There is no OTel export or trace propagation, and no log schema or log file. Engine
  tracing is behind each crate's feature, while escher's spans are ungated — (sampler)
  architecture/inherited-defaults#3.1. A paged `part` read through the host's sink is unmeasured.

- The session state directory is caller-named, owner-only, holds the socket alone and is removed at `stop` or idle
  expiry — (sampler) architecture/occupied-resources#3.1, (sampler) obs-plan/ci-integration#1.6.

- The wasm builds of the examples are browser-target builds via Trunk, not a target the driver runs on — (sampler)
  architecture/stack-and-technologies#1.15.

- Unmeasured: windowed end-to-end runs; typed text on the windowed binary's log; reduced-motion handling (observed
  absent); the engine's WPT conformance, one report-only reading at 966 → 967 of 2292 in `css/cssom-view` — (sampler)
  test-plan/test-strategy#6.1.
**Accessibility reach**

- Tier 0: SC 2.1.1 · 1.4.3 · 2.4.3, proven headless on the stand by `stand_keyboard`, `stand_contrast` and
  `stand_accessibility_ids`.

- The `a11y` leg's fourteen files at 14 · 84 · 0 · 0 (CI#40134371519), with no required status check; eight of them
  also run three rounds in `stand-repeat` — (sampler) test-plan/ci-integration#5.1.

- Contrast: white on `#3a5ce5` at 5.47, hover 6.83, active 8.27, on the stand's accent controls; the lint's `contrast`
  defect uses the same reader and exempt rule.

- Unmeasured: what an assistive technology reads. No stand binary builds a platform adapter (probe 0 at
  2026-10-24-a11y-re-read); the residuals line is `re-carried:0.2.0` and this version does not reach it. The platform
  adapters' own gaps (Android `set_focus` and `set_window_bounds` empty, Windows `set_focus` and macOS
  `set_window_bounds` no-ops) — (sampler) a11y-plan/a11y-strategy#3.3. The native checked state is absent from the
  tree. `aria-activedescendant` is unread (SC 4.1.2, outside tier 0). No snapshot field says an element reacts to a
  click. Descriptions reach the adapter only. A `role` attribute reaches the tree through the engine's one role-name
  mapping — (sampler) a11y-plan/aria-patterns-roles#2.1.

**What an MCP client carries onward** — the boundary is the spawning client holding stdio, with no authentication. The
carried set is listed as in the security Acceptance criterion. The client's onward use is the client's. The measured
instance is the 2026-10-15 cold-agent live run: the stand's screen reached the model provider through the operator's
own login. It was one run, eleven tools, 43 calls, 0 wrong, no `screenshot`, not re-fired since `lint`. Its verdict
holds counts, booleans and closed words only — (sampler) obs-plan/log-coverage#2.1.

**Where each claim is proven** — the witnesses by file name and the CI legs. The stand checks run three rounds under
the zero-failure budget in `stand-repeat`: 48 `stand_*` files, ten named targets and eight seven_guis process checks,
CI 198 · 837 · 0 · 21 — (sampler) architecture/stack-and-technologies#1.23, (sampler)
test-plan/quality-gates-coverage-targets#3.1, (sampler) test-plan/ci-integration#5.1. The 0.2.0 record is
`WITNESSES_020`: nine rows, 46 witnesses.

- **Marker:** 2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar · **Version:** escher-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-25T14:11:33Z

0.2.0 ends with one cold-agent run over its new capabilities, judged by the founder's bar (intent §7, v020-11). The
founder chose the stand as the ground and asked that it cover all the checks (inputs#I1). At P4 he confirmed four
things (inputs#I3). F1, «Да, весь стенд (Рекомендую)»: extend the whole stand. F2, «Страница загрузки рядом
(Рекомендую)»: a load page beside the 7GUIs tasks, its request answered in process. F3, «Один запуск, до $3
(Рекомендую)»: one live run, up to $3. F4, «Не больше 5% (Рекомендую)»: at most 5 % of calls wrong.

So the chunk builds three things. First, the stand grows until the driver serves a case for every 0.2.0 check: Cells
(a screen in parts), the flight booker's one-way / return choice as a real `select`, and a load page whose click meets
a load in flight. Second, the cold-agent pipe gets goals that make a fresh agent exercise recording, lint, `advance`,
the load wait, the select and the read in parts, with the founder's bar as a verdict reason. Third, it fires the one
live run on the operator's word.

The engine and the driver do not move (scope Boundaries). The select model, the load wait and the paged snapshot
already stand (arch §Established Decisions → select model; §Standard Contracts → Driver session). The stand is example
code and stays offline: the load page's request is answered by an in-process stand-in through the `NetProvider` seam,
as the fixtures already do (arch §Design Philosophy; test-plan §8).

1. **The flight booker's choice as a controlled `select`** (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/flight_booker.rs`:66-81).
   - **The control:** the two `type-btn` buttons `flight-one-way` and `flight-return` give way to one single-choice
     `select` with id `flight-type`, named by `aria-label` "Flight type".
   - **Its options:** two, each with an author id. `flight-type-one-way` has value `one-way` and text "one-way flight".
     `flight-type-return` has value `return` and text "return flight". An option with no author key reads in
     `unkeyed_actionable` (test-plan §1, the select's limits).
   - **Its state:** each option's `selected:` reads the existing `flight_type` signal. An `oninput` handler writes the
     signal through a closed match: the value `return` becomes `"return"`, and every other value becomes `"one-way"`.
     The match never trusts `NativeFormData::valid`, which always reads true (security-plan §Input Validation, Forms).
     This is the controlled-select pattern of `select_interaction.rs`:34-46. A controlled app that writes no `selected`
     sees its choice revert (arch §Established Decisions → DOM semantics).
   - **Its look:** the declared look of the card's date inputs — 15px, `#1a1a1a` on `#ffffff`, `1px solid #c0c0c0`, the
     file's input radius and padding. Its focus cue is the `#3a5ce5` border the date inputs use, since the outline is
     removed ((sampler) visual-design-verification#3.4).
   - **CSS:** the `.flight-type-row` and `.type-btn*` rules go with the buttons, and no CSS selects by an id
     (layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens).
   - **Unchanged:** the dates, the Book button, the invalid and success colours, `aria-invalid`, the booking text and
     the card's shadow and radius (design-system §Color Palette → Semantic Colors; a11y-plan §8).

2. **Cells and the load page served by the stand** (`examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs`).
   - **Cells:** `boot_cells(HarnessOptions)` mounts `Task::Cells` in `TaskShell` through the same root and options as
     `boot`. Cells joins beside `LeanTask`, never as a fifth variant: 22 `stand_*` files iterate `LeanTask::ALL`
     against four-task tables (research.md §Graph impact).
   - **The load page's markup:** `boot_load(HarnessOptions)` mounts a small page in `TaskShell` titled "Load". Its
     `load-fetch` button "Load" adds a `link rel="stylesheet"` to `http://stand.test/load.css`, as `stand_load_wait`'s
     fixture does (stand_load_wait.rs:35-46). The page also holds a `load-done` paragraph "Loaded", hidden by a class
     the page's own style sets to `display: none`, which the loaded sheet shows. No CSS selects by id.
   - **The stand-in:** the page's boot alone carries one in-process `NetProvider`. It answers each request with that
     sheet's bytes from a thread of its own after 200 ms, as `LateNet` does (stand_load_wait.rs:48-60). It has no
     `is_noop` override, so the harness counts its load (test-plan §8 Network). It holds no `blitz_net`, print, env read,
     socket or listener (arch §Standard Contracts → Headless stand; obs-plan §3).
   - **Every other boot stays offline:** the provider rides only `boot_load`'s options, through `..options(true)`
     (stand_load_wait.rs:66-70). `options` keeps `net_provider: None` for every other caller (27 file names reference it,
     research.md §Graph impact).
   - **Docs:** the module's `//!` doc names the lean four, Cells and the load page.

3. **`start` serves six tasks** (`examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs`:13-43).
   - **The slugs:** `counter` · `flight-booker` · `timer` · `crud` · `cells` · `load`, each mapped to its boot. The
     Timer's boot still carries `stand::timer_step` through `Session::with_time`.
   - **What it moves:** the binary's usage line and the MCP `start` tool's `enum`, both built from the slugs. That is the
     program's own fixed text, not a widening (cli.rs:343-365; mcp/listing.rs:63-72; security-plan §Input Validation).
   - **The binary's `//!`** states the six.

4. **The shared stand tables re-pinned** (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`:25-26, :55-56, :79-80, :151-152).
   - The flight booker's rows in `controls`, `rendered`, `tab_order` and `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER` hold `flight-type` and its
     two options in place of the two buttons, each measured on the changed task, never assumed.
   - The enabled state is reached by keyboard alone: Tab to `flight-type`, then ArrowDown chooses return
     (a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation).
   - `session_common`'s `change` moves the flight booker's mode by `type` on `flight-type`.

5. **The stand checks that pin the old buttons re-pinned:** 13 files hold
   `git grep -P 'flight-(one-way|return)(?!-date)'` hits (research.md §Sweeps), and `stand_diff` and `stand_snapshot`
   read the flight booker's layout. Every reading is re-measured in both layout modes and recorded. In detail:
   - **`stand_keyboard`:** the two mode buttons' Enter and Space rows leave, a select being no activation target, and
     the row count is restated. The select's arrows moving the choice are asserted.
   - **`stand_contrast`:** the accent row `flight-one-way` gives way to the `flight-type` row, its pair measured
     through the shared reader. The three `return-chosen` state rows are re-measured. Every non-exempt row meets 4.5,
     and the exempt class stays exactly `enabled == Some(false)` (a11y-plan §6).
   - **`stand_act_states` and `stand_snapshot_state`:** "exactly the active flight mode reads pressed" becomes the
     select's `value` and its options' `selected`, each equal to its accessibility node (a11y-plan §7).
   - **`stand_act_disabled`:** the return date is enabled by `type flight-type return`.
   - **`stand_act_ids`:** the 77 / 70 / 7 click census is re-measured, an unchosen option refused `covered`.
   - **`stand_act_diff` and `stand_diff`:** the choice step and Book's moved nodes are re-read.
   - **`stand_element_ids`, `stand_id_persistence` and `stand_snapshot`:** the select's and the options' ids are pinned.
   - **`stand_session_recording`:** its flight booker call becomes a `type`.
   - **`stand_requirement_sweep`:** its flight call `click flight-return` becomes `type flight-type return`.

6. **`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_cells_served.rs` (new).** Cells booted through `stand::boot_cells`, held by
   `Session::start` and driven through `Session::run` alone, in both layout modes:
   - The screen reads in parts: `parts` ≥ 2, each part within `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET`, the parts concatenating to the
     whole text, which P3 measured at 47,949 bytes in 5 parts — record what the run measures.
   - `unkeyed_actionable` reads empty.
   - `5` committed into `cell-A0` and `=A0*2` into `cell-B1` read `"5"` and `"10"`.
   - `scroll cell-Z25` brings it into view. A formula committed there reads in the last part.
   - Lint at boot is recorded as measured: P3 read 490 findings in both modes. The check pins the reading it makes.
   - Failure messages hold the mode and a row index only.

7. **`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_load_page.rs` (new).** The load page booted through `stand::boot_load`, held, in
   both layout modes:
   - Before the click: `load-done` does not read on the screen.
   - The click: `click load-fetch` returns `settled` with no `busy`, and its diff adds `load-done` with name "Loaded".
   - The clock: `harness().time()` is the same before and after.
   - No wall-clock read and no sleep in the check: the stand-in's delay is the stand's, not the check's
     (test-plan §5 Wall time). Then `type`-free `snapshot` reads the message.

8. **`WITNESSES_020` gains the stand witnesses** (`stand_requirement_sweep.rs`): `stand_load_page` on v020-07,
   `stand_act_states` (the flight booker's select) on v020-08 and `stand_cells_served` on v020-09. Each is found by its
   `stand_` prefix inside `stand-repeat` (test-plan §1).

9. **seven_guis' process checks.**
   - **`cli_commands`:** its `TASKS` table holds the six, each started, answered and stopped. The usage line names
     `cells` and `load`.
   - **`host_log` (the residual):** a test drives `start cells`, then `snapshot --part 2` and `stop` at
     `RUST_LOG=trace` through the host's own sink. It reads 0 id and 0 name needles, the needles taken from the
     in-process Cells screen's part 2, under both builds. This measures the read `.andromeda/residuals.md:38` owns.
   - **`common/mod.rs`:** states the Cells needles once beside `stand_needles`.

10. **The cold-agent pipe's goals and verdict** (`scripts/cold-agent.sh`).
    - **`STAND_PROMPT`:** names the six apps by name — counter, flight booker, timer, CRUD, cells and the load page —
      and their goals:
      - Counter: the display reads 3.
      - Flight booker: a return flight 24.12.2026 → 31.12.2026, chosen on its type control.
      - Timer: duration 10 s, elapsed 10.0s.
      - CRUD: as today.
      - Cells: `A0` 5, `B1` `=A0*2` reading 10, and `Z25` `=B1+1` reading 11.
      - Load page: its resource loaded and its message shown.
      - A screenshot of the flight booker's final screen, and one visual lint of the Cells screen.
      - The check as the last fenced json block.
    - **The prompt's limits:** it still names no element id, and `test_the_prompt_names_no_stand_id` moves with its
      goal list (security-plan §Input Validation, CLI arguments).
    - **`DONE`:** six apps, the load page met by `'Paragraph "Loaded" id="load-done"'` and Cells by `cell-B1` reading
      `"10"` and `cell-Z25` reading `"11"`.
    - **`tasks_met` and paged answers:** `tasks_met` decodes a paged answer's JSON line `{"text","part","parts"}`
      before matching (its quotes are escaped — research.md, scope). A paged app is met from the latest answer of each
      part read while it is the started app.
    - **New verdict fields, counts and bools only:**
      - `lint_calls`, `screenshot_calls`, `advance_calls`: accepted `tool_call` lines per `tool`.
      - `part_reads`: accepted `snapshot` uses whose arguments hold `part`, read from the transcript as a count.
      - `recorded_sessions` and `recording_kept`: each accepted `start` left one kept check that parses as a JSON array
        opening with its app's `start` record.
      - `wrong_call_bar_pct`: 5.
    - **New reasons:** `capability-unused` (any of the four counts 0), `recording-not-kept` and
      `wrong-calls-over-bar` (wrong_calls × 100 > 5 × tool_calls). `wrong_calls` now decides.
    - **Recording:** the live server child runs `mcp --record target/cold-agent/record`, the directory made `0700` by
      the pipe. The kept checks are never printed, copied or committed, and `cleanup` removes them with the state.
    - **Bounds and replay unchanged:** `valid_step`, `MAX_CHECK_*`, `REPLY_BOUND` and the two replay children; the
      replays run without `--record`. `scripts/cold-agent.ps1` delegates and does not change.

12. **The one live run, on the operator's word only** (the gate entry `cargo build --locked -p seven_guis --bin
    escher-session && bash scripts/cold-agent.sh run stand`). The founder's F3 is one run up to $3 (inputs#I3).
    `/implement` stops at that entry and asks the operator. On the word it fires exactly once, never re-fired
    whatever it reads. Then `evidence/` takes:
    - `live-verdict.json` and `live-events.jsonl` as written;
    - `live-check.json`, the agent's check;
    - `live-transcript.jsonl`, with the session dir and home prefix masked;
    - `live-run.md`: the counts — tool calls by verb, `wrong_calls` with its parts, `spacer_calls`, the five new
      fields, cost, duration and the `claude` version.

    No kept check from `target/cold-agent/record/` is committed (security-plan §Data Protection). Each committed line
    holds no host temp path, even as prose (the handoff's deferred learning).
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_cells_served.rs` — Cells served and walked in parts (step 6)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_load_page.rs` — the load page's load waited out (step 7)
- `escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar/evidence/` — the live run's record (step 12) and the gates' readings
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/flight_booker.rs` — the controlled select (step 1)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs` — `boot_cells`, `boot_load`, the load page and its stand-in (step 2)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs` — six served tasks (step 3)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs` — the tables (step 4)

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/{stand_keyboard,stand_contrast,stand_act_states,stand_snapshot_state,stand_act_disabled,stand_act_ids,stand_act_diff,stand_diff,stand_element_ids,stand_id_persistence,stand_snapshot,stand_session_recording,stand_requirement_sweep}.rs` — re-pinned (steps 5, 8)
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/{cli_commands,host_log}.rs`, `examples/seven_guis/tests/common/mod.rs` — step 9
- `scripts/cold-agent.sh` — step 10
- `.github/scripts/test_cold_agent.py` — step 11

Impact: `LeanTask` has 466 reference sites in 49 files, `stand::options` 27 referencing file names (research.md §Graph
impact, `tree-query-2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar.json`). Neither signature changes: the new boots are added beside them.

- **The live leg:** one entry starts a model session, the operator entry of step 12, reserved for the operator's word.
  `claude --version` before it is its non-priming probe, `operator` like it, since the run is the founder's one.

- **What the live leg reads:** it produces `target/cold-agent/verdict.json` (its `artifact`). Step 12 copies that to
  `evidence/live-verdict.json`, and the reader of the copy carries no `artifact`.

- **No other model session:** the pipe's behaviour is pinned under the shim, and no other entry runs
  `cold-agent.sh run`.

- **No boot smoke and no self-verify:** the stand is headless, so `/implement` P3 boots nothing windowed and the
  project has no headful self-verify.
- **Long entries:** `stand-repeat`, `coverage` and the workspace `fast` run in the background, their logs read whole.

- **The operator pass:** the chunk adds `cfg(unix)` test items (step 9) and its acceptance needs CI, so the plan
  carries the hygiene, push and CI read.

   - `over 15: 85`.

   included.

   and their logs are read whole. Record the counts in `evidence/counts.md` against the baselines and predictions
   named in each entry's `note`.

  code)

No live leg runs this chunk and no external process is driven. Every check boots in process or spawns its own
binary. The chunk changes no UI and the stand stays headless, so there is no `self-verify` entry. `/implement` P3's
boot smoke is the agent-run boot/run pair below.
Two entries are long and run in the background, their logs read whole:

- `stand-repeat`: three rounds over 50 `stand_*` files, the ten named blitz-tests targets and the eight seven_guis
  checks.
- `coverage`: an instrumented workspace run.

The complexity reading is the one new instrument. It is rust-code-analysis 0.0.25, the audit's tool, installed on the
dev host at `~/.cargo/bin`. The entry runs it over the audit's committed file list into a `mktemp` directory, so it
leaves no residue. No CI leg runs it: it is a dev-host reading, as the audit is.

Step 4's row-guard controls mutate source and revert, so they are no entry. They are a one-shot run at implement,
with both readings of each in `evidence/row-controls.md`. The listed suites guard the same rows on every re-run:
`cargo test -p escher-driver --locked` and the `stand_lint` / `stand_requirement_sweep` entries. The complexity
instrument and the inline guards ran their must-pass and must-fail controls at P5, before first graded use
(`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-26T23-36-49-phase/p5-controls.md`).

The chunk adds no OS-conditional site. Its acceptance reads "every check green", which a CI run witnesses, so the plan
carries the operator pass's hygiene, push and CI read.

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-10-27-upstream-sync-engine-debts · **Version:** escher-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-10-27T09:35Z

- **Base:** `de85792f5e9dcb895d75bb65a3b91e79a4ea24c2` (build/escher-0.3.0 HEAD at P4) · **Upstream read:** `ebacd68bd35552e42ed546faa7fa53dfccc109af` (upstream/main, 17 commits past the last sync's reading `f9cbb2756`, 27 of 40 past the merge base `23b9b26a9` not yet in)

- **Take shape:** the founder's own word on the P4 fork, by dialog from his phone, relayed verbatim by the overseer: «Одиннадцать коммитов (Рекомендую)» (2026-10-27, inputs#I4; the operator's dialog answer and note, inputs#I3) — the builder's option «Cherry-pick the eleven (Recommended)». It ratifies the take, so nothing in it is PROVISIONAL, and the playbook pattern «An engine behaviour change for every document» is ratified by him for this take.
- **Run mode:** the operator's directive (inputs#I1): one Workflow per P2 batch, every transcript and the run dir kept, forks to the operator by dialog.

Bring escher's engine up to upstream's current `main` as far as the registry pins allow — the founder's last shape (inputs#I2), repeated on his own word (inputs#I4). The take is eleven of upstream's seventeen new commits by no-commit cherry-pick in upstream order: `d63ed2c8c` (#1268, browser tab lenses), `6587e7e79` (#1269, shell redraw requests through the event loop), `e6f4615ec` (#1270, blitz-vibey-script's runtime and element bindings split into modules), `a7ea9631b` · `b5b163450` (#1274, #1275, `publish-browser.yml`), `7fc9ee3af` (IME enabled when a focused text input's editor is constructed), `2963b65a2` (#1280, `::before`/`::after` pseudos vote in flow classification, with its new test), `cee6b8731` (#1283, only a `file:` document may load a `file:` URL), `53e9d81c6` (#1007, `<details>`/`<dialog>` `:open`), `6fee0db25` (#1295, the WPT pin) and `efdc5472a` (#1297, CSS properties as `CSSStyleDeclaration` accessors). Every pin stays: Stylo 0.22.0, taffy 0.15 from the registry, Dioxus 0.7.3, winit `=0.31.0-beta.3`, no git dependency; `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `deny.toml` stay byte-identical (architecture §Established Decisions → [Dependency pinning]; security-plan §Dependency Security, Pinning).

The take was measured whole at P3 in a throwaway worktree (research.md §The trial takes). Eight commits pick clean in upstream order. Three conflict in one hunk each, and each is resolved to upstream's text plus escher's addition. On the result, check, fmt, clippy, the audit (`advisories ok, licenses ok`) and the workspace tests read green at 209 result lines · 1125 passed · 0 failed · 12 ignored — the base plus exactly upstream's new target and eight new tests. Sixteen commits stay out for Epoch 3's sync: residual line 35's ten (git Taffy, git Stylo 0.23-pre, Dioxus 0.8.0-alpha.3), plus winit beta.4 (`a09f46792`, `527394724`), git Taffy's `d3ed4e2c7` · `ccfe15332`, the reversed scroll origins `0980cce5f` (git Taffy, authored on Stylo 0.23, colliding with escher's scrolled-box bounds and hit) and its panic fix `ebacd68bd`.

Beside the take, the chunk re-reads residual line 36's merge surfaces per row and sends nothing upstream. It re-reads the sink allowlist against the take's added lines and the per-OS tallies on the take's green CI run (scope.md §Folded freight; per obs-plan §8, test-plan §9).

1. **Before readings** (`evidence/before.md`): the base sha above. CI#40466575975 on it reads green, 17/17. Record P5's baseline readings of this plan's entries as they stand on the base. These are the workspace tally 208 · 1117 · 0 · 12 (test-plan-detail/ci-integration.md:43, CI#40434241601), `run stand`'s and `run all`'s run.end, the a11y leg's 14 · 85, the 147 `.rs` files and 50 `stand_*` files under `tests/blitz-tests/tests/`, blitz-vibey-script `tests/dom.rs` 27 and dioxus-native-dom's lib 81.

   - `cee6b8731` and `efdc5472a` edit the `runtime/` modules `e6f4615ec` creates, so they pick clean only after it, as this order has them.
   Record each resolution as a non-additive edit, with the hunk before and after. A further gate-driven edit is named and minimal there too, never a loosened assertion.

A moved number (a bound, a byte size, a contrast ratio, a kept Counter answer, a lint figure) is re-measured and recorded with the commit that moved it, never loosened. None is forecast to move: P3's run of the whole workspace on the take read every stand check, `stand_replay` and seven_guis `recording` green (research.md §The trial takes).

5. **Readings** (`evidence/readings.md`): residual line 36's merge surfaces, per row, against the take (scope.md §Folded freight):

   `evidence/sink.md` holds the fixed-sha census of the take's added lines and the silence census of `pseudo_element_flow_classification`. `evidence/counts.md` holds every moved count by name.

6. **Operator pass** (the last four entries): hygiene, the pre-CI commit, the push, the CI read, and the per-OS tallies re-read into `evidence/ci.md` against CI#40434241601.
   - The pre-CI commit's subject is exactly `chore(2026-10-27-upstream-sync-engine-debts): operator pre-CI commit, for the run this chunk's verdict reads`.
