title: The trial takes (worktree `target/tmp/trial-wt`, target dir `target/tmp/trial-target`, base HEAD `de85792f5`, upstream `ebacd68bd`)

data.head: ## The trial takes (worktree `target/tmp/trial-wt`, target dir `target/tmp/trial-target`, base HEAD `de85792f5`, upstream `ebacd68bd`)

body: Each commit cherry-picked with `-x` and `-c rerere.enabled=false` (this host has `rerere.enabled true`; nothing was recorded in `.git/rr-cache` this time), then `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked`. The gates are scratch script `gates.sh`: check · `cargo fmt --all --check` · `cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings` · `cargo deny --locked --workspace --all-features check advisories licenses` · `cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast`, result lines summed from `^test result:`.

- **Already in, 13 of the 40:** a per-commit read of `23b9b26a9..upstream/main` against `(cherry picked from commit {sha})` trailers on our branch — `fb8d6c15e`, `38ca4e777`, `17de049b1` and the Epoch 5 ten (`git cherry` marks all 40 `+`, since a conflict-resolved pick changes its patch id). 27 remain.

- **Shape A — the cherry-pick take, pins unchanged: eleven commits.** In upstream order: `d63ed2c8c` · `6587e7e79` · `e6f4615ec` · `a7ea9631b` · `b5b163450` · `7fc9ee3af` · `2963b65a2` · `cee6b8731` · `53e9d81c6` · `6fee0db25` · `efdc5472a`. Eight pick clean (`cee6b8731` and `efdc5472a` only on top of `e6f4615ec`, whose new `runtime/` modules they edit); three conflict in one hunk each:
  - `e6f4615ec` (`runtime.rs` split into `runtime/` and `dom/element/` modules) — our side of `runtime.rs` since `23b9b26a9` is one two-line comment (select-by-id, `14818317c`: "Blitz generates a `change` event for a `select` alone …"). Resolution: upstream's `runtime.rs`, the comment carried to its new home `runtime/events.rs:171-173`. Against `e6f4615ec` itself the take's tree differs only by our three earlier rustdoc link fixes in `document.rs`.
  - `7fc9ee3af` (IME enabled when a focused text input's editor is created) — its engine hunk (`construct.rs` `create_text_editor`, 7 lines) picks clean; the conflict is `dioxus_document.rs`'s test module, where upstream's context holds `task_polled_during_render_can_access_document` from `286874cc1` (not taken). Resolution: ours, plus upstream's new test `input_focused_on_mount_enables_ime` alone; it passes (`cargo test -p dioxus-native-dom --lib input_focused_on_mount_enables_ime`: 1 passed).
  - `53e9d81c6` (`<details>`/`<dialog>` `:open`) — `mutator.rs` `set_attribute`: our range re-sanitize arm (`min`/`max`/`step` → `resanitize_range_input`) and upstream's `open` arm (`flush_open_state`) at one spot. Resolution: both, ours first, each an independent `if`; `remove_attribute`'s `open` arm picks clean.
  No manifest, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` line moves (`git diff --stat HEAD 02b24fccf -- Cargo.toml Cargo.lock deny.toml '*/Cargo.toml'`: empty). Gates on the take (`02b24fccf`): check 0 · fmt 0 · clippy 0 · audit 0, `advisories ok, licenses ok` · tests 0, **209 result lines · 1125 passed · 0 failed · 12 ignored**, 0 `Running tests/all.rs` lines, 169 s. Against the recorded 208 · 1117 · 0 · 12 (test-plan, 2026-10-26-codebase-health, CI#40434241601 linux): +1 line, upstream's new target `pseudo_element_flow_classification`, and +8 passed, exactly the take's added `#[test]`s by `git diff HEAD 02b24fccf` — 3 in `pseudo_element_flow_classification.rs`, 3 in blitz-vibey-script `tests/dom.rs` (`cee6b8731` 2, `efdc5472a` 1), 1 in `dioxus_document.rs` (the IME test), 1 in `apps/browser/src/tab.rs`. The audit keeps its two standing warnings (`license-not-encountered`, `yanked` clipboard-win 5.4.1).

- **Shape B — A plus winit beta.4: thirteen commits.** `a09f46792` (winit `=0.31.0-beta.3` → `=0.31.0-beta.4`) picks clean with its own lock hunk and checks green under `--locked`; `527394724` (winit's clipboard API in place of `arboard`) conflicts in `Cargo.lock` alone (escher's own `escher-*` entries beside upstream's removals), resolved as ours and re-pruned by `cargo metadata`. The lock against shape A: `arboard` 3.6.1, `clipboard-win` 5.4.1 and `error-code` 3.4.0 leave; eleven winit-family entries move beta.3 → beta.4; `x11rb` 0.14.0 and `x11rb-protocol` 0.14.0 enter (`MIT OR Apache-2.0`, psychon/x11rb, `build = false`, no proc-macro; direct dependent `winit-x11` 0.31.0-beta.4, beside the standing `x11rb` 0.13.2 of softbuffer). Gates on the take (`fb1f87191`): check 0 · fmt 0 · clippy 0 · audit 0, `advisories ok, licenses ok`, the `yanked` clipboard-win warning gone, RUSTSEC-2026-0192 still encountered (ttf-parser 0.25.1 · owned_ttf_parser · ab_glyph 0.2.32 · sctk-adwaita 0.12.0 all in the beta.4 lock) · tests 0, **210 · 1128 · 0 · 12**, 0 `Running tests/all.rs`, 186 s — +1 line, upstream's `clipboard` target (1 test), and +3 passed, that one and `node/text.rs`'s two new IME tests · CI scripts `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts`: 108 tests OK · rustdoc `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked`: exit 0. (The doc and CI-scripts legs were read on shape B, a superset of A's files.)

- **The git-Taffy probe** (on shape B): upstream's `taffy` line (git `c2560562…`) and `cargo update -p taffy` alone fail `cargo check` with 10 errors in blitz-dom — `ScrollableOverflow` replaced `scrollable_overflow_rect`'s Rect fields (`node/node.rs:1487`, `:1489`, `:1985`, `:1992`, `debug.rs:97-100`), `place_floated_box` takes a sixth argument (`layout/inline/layout.rs:752`), a Rect mismatch (`layout/inline/layout.rs:1144`): the Taffy pin and `0980cce5f` are one unit. `0980cce5f` on top conflicts in four hunks — `document.rs` (its context is `06ecec886`'s Stylo-0.23 pref names: the commit was authored on git Stylo), `layout/writing_mode.rs:554` (upstream subtracts the node's own scroll offset and passes `is_scroll_container` where escher's scrolled-box bounds fix excludes the own offset — 2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit) and `node/node.rs` ×2 (an import, and `matches_self` — upstream's scroll-offset test against escher's `own_x`/`own_y` hit at a scrolled box). `ebacd68bd` conflicts in `node/node.rs` alone because it edits the line `0980cce5f` introduces (`layout_style()` direction in `hit_inner`); its own message says it fixes a panic "Since #1294". Unmeasured past the conflicts: resolving them is design work on two of escher's engine changes.

- **Shape C — the whole merge of `ebacd68bd`**, not re-built at P3: the in-memory `git merge-tree` exits 1 with nine files conflicted (scope.md). Its blockers measured at the last sync still stand at HEAD — our `contain: paint` stop's `style.get_box().clone_contain()` (`node/node.rs:1544`), absent under Stylo 0.23 (escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-24-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship/research.md §The trial takes, shape C); Dioxus `0.8.0-alpha.3` against escher's `element_id.rs`, still on 0.7's vdom (`node_id_mapping` / `dynamic_nodes` / `mounted_root`: 2 hits; 10 + 15 errors then, shape B there); upstream's manifest names git Stylo `d6502e00…`, git Taffy `c2560562…`, Dioxus `0.8.0-alpha.3` and winit `=0.31.0-beta.4`.
- **Shape D — take nothing**, the 27 carried to Epoch 3's «Upstream sync ahead of the UI graph».

- **Left standing:** the worktree `target/tmp/trial-wt` stays registered (`git worktree list`), detached at shape B `fb1f87191`; its trial commits are detached objects (shape A `02b24fccf`, shape B `fb1f87191`, the Taffy probe `f79c01fa0`). The operator removes it; nothing was written to `.git/rr-cache`.

- `packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime.rs` at HEAD (1100-1110, 1669-1676) and `runtime/events.rs` at `e6f4615ec` (15-26, 171-174) — `report_js_error`'s `#[cfg(feature = "tracing")] tracing::error!("Uncaught JS error in {what}: {error}")` moves whole; our one comment lands at `events.rs:171-173`.

- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs` (423-480, 722-760) — the test module's helpers `rerender` (470) and `poll_until_idle` (475) that upstream's IME test calls exist on our side; the bridge's `accessibility_tree` override and `#[path]` children untouched by the take.

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs` (`create_text_editor`, 860-885 at `7fc9ee3af`; the flow-classification vote at `2963b65a2`) — the IME enable reads `is_focussed()` before the editor's creation and calls `shell_provider.set_ime_enabled(true)`; `RangeInputData`'s seeding untouched.

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` (358-372, 513-524 on the take) — the `open` arm sits after the range arm in `set_attribute` and after the link flush in `remove_attribute`; the changed-set inserts, the range re-seed on `value` and the select arms untouched.

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/element.rs` (485-550 on the take) — `flush_open_state` sets `ElementState::OPEN` on a `details` or `dialog` carrying `open`, called from `ElementData::new`; `is_disabled` and `flush_is_focussable` untouched.
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo.rs` (507-512) — `NonTSPseudoClass::Open` now reads `ElementState::OPEN`; the `:focus-within` matching (`38ca4e777`) untouched.

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/driver.rs` (224-300 on shape B) — `UiEvent::Paste(text)` targets the focused node and is applied as an IME `Commit` through `ime::handle_ime_event`, then the queue is processed.

- `packages/blitz-traits/src/events.rs` (71-75) and `shell.rs` (25-33) on shape B — `UiEvent::Paste(String)`; `ShellProvider::get_clipboard_text` becomes `request_clipboard_text() -> Result<(), ClipboardError>`, its text delivered later as a `UiEvent`. No escher crate implements or calls either (`git grep` outside blitz-shell, blitz-traits and blitz-dom: 0 source hits).

- `packages/blitz-shell/src/application.rs` at `upstream/main` (55-62) — `event_loop.set_clipboard(data)`'s error logged by `#[cfg(feature = "tracing")] tracing::error!("Failed to set clipboard: {_error}")`, target `blitz_shell::application`.

- `packages/blitz-shell/src/convert_events.rs` and `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/text.rs` at `a09f46792` — the `_ =>` arm logging "unsupported Ime variant" leaves (winit beta.4's `Ime` is matched exhaustively), and an IME `Commit` now calls `driver.clear_compose()` before inserting.

- `packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/fetch.rs` and `document.rs` at `cee6b8731` — `FetchError::Forbidden(Url)` and `document_may_load(base_url, url)`; `ScriptDocument` refuses a disallowed `<script src>` with a recorded error and omits it from the prefetch list; upstream's message: "Remote pages could read any local file via fetch('file:///...'), import 'file:///...' or <script src="file:///...">".

- `deny.toml` (19-25) — RUSTSEC-2026-0192's reason names winit 0.31.0-beta.3 explicitly ("it reaches the graph only through winit 0.31.0-beta.3 -> winit-wayland -> sctk-adwaita -> ab_glyph -> owned_ttf_parser"); under shape B the chain stands at beta.4, so the ID stays and its reason's version text moves.

- `packages/blitz-shell/Cargo.toml` (14, 20), `packages/dioxus-native/Cargo.toml` (13, 30), `apps/browser/Cargo.toml` (51) at HEAD — the `clipboard` feature and `dep:arboard`, which `527394724` removes; seven_guis and the escher crates name neither (`git grep`).

body: - (matrix) `verification-matrix.json#v030-04` — each debt the intent names reaches the founder as a fork and ends as his word says, by the table below, each witness named (per `scope.md` §The founder's word; inputs#I8, inputs#I9).

- (F1, arch, design) In both layout modes, a target in a transformed world's inner scrolling box reads its centre inside `visible_region` and is hit, at translate and at `translate + scale(2)`; a driver `click` on it is accepted and lands, a lint reads no `off-screen` or `truncated` there; a plain page reads as today; a target panned out reads outside and is not hit (`visible_region_transformed`, `stand_act_transformed`, `transformed_client_rect`) (per arch §Standard Contracts → Scrolling, selection, tree).
- (F1, security) A `visible_region` over `scale(0)` and a non-invertible matrix on a scrolling box reads no panic and `None`, in both layout modes (per security-plan §Input Validation, Paint values).
- (F2) A box under a non-invertible transform takes no hit at (300, 200) and (590, 390) in a 600 × 400 clip, and an invertible twin is hit, in both layout modes (`hit_non_invertible_transform`).

- (F3, a11y) Once a focused node or its ancestor becomes inert, the engine's focus, the snapshot's `focused` node and the tree's focus agree on none, Enter clicks nothing, a typed character lands nowhere, `has_changes` reads true after a drain, the next Tab lands on the first stop, and Tab, the hit and the tree keep skipping it, in both layout modes (`inert_subtree`) (per a11y-plan §5 Focus order per layout).

- (F4, a11y) The tree's focus is the window when the focused node was not built, for `inert`, `display: none` and `hidden`, read through `&dyn Document` (`inert_subtree`); what an assistive technology reads stays unmeasured (per a11y-plan §1).

- (F5, a11y) A stated table of native checkbox and radio rows reads `toggled` true or false through `&dyn Document`, its count asserted, a `role="button"` row none, the snapshot's `checked` and `pressed` unmoved, in both layout modes (`accessibility_states`) (per a11y-plan §2 Role derivation).

- (F6, a11y) A `multiple` select lays out its rows with boxes of their own, reads `ListBox`, takes its keys, Shift, Ctrl and Space, and its clicks by the pointer, one `input` then one `change` per change and none for no change, `evt.values()` reading the set; its form entries are the chosen rows that are not disabled (`select_interaction`, `form.rs`'s tests) (per a11y-plan §5 Keyboard handling; arch §Established Decisions → the select model).

- (F6, the click, driver) A driver `click` on a `multiple` select's row is accepted and chooses it; `type` chooses its match alone with no stray click; an option of a closed single select stays refused `covered`, under a group too (`stand_act_select`) (his «Только строки multiple (Рекомендую)»).

- (F7) An `optgroup`'s options are listed in tree order, chosen by a single select's keys and shown alone, a disabled group's rows skipped and left out of the form's entries (`select_interaction`, `form.rs`'s tests).

- (F8) Enter and Space open nothing on a single select, and no popup is built: `git diff` adds no paint module and `packages/blitz-paint/` shows no diff (`select_interaction`, the plan's touchpoints).

- (F9) `stand_lint` reads `[0, 0, 0, 0]` on the lean tasks at boot, a closed select's options read no overlap, under a group too, a `multiple` select's planted row reads its one finding, CRUD's clipped row still reads, in both layout modes; each finding holds `id`, `defect`, `bounds` and its reason's keys alone (`stand_lint`) (per security-plan §Input Validation, Driver command schema row).

- (F10) A click and a Space on a checkbox each fire one `input` then one `change`; a radio's second click fires `input` alone; script hears one `change`, in both layout modes (`checkable_change_event`, blitz-vibey-script `dom`).
- (F11) A text input and a range fire `input` and no `change`, asserted (`text_range_no_change_event`).

- (F12, a11y) The load page holds a Tab-order row, Enter and Space activation rows through harness and driver, and contrast rows at their `required_ratio`, in both layout modes; the OPEN gap closes; the `a11y` leg stays fourteen files (`stand_keyboard`, `stand_contrast`, `stand_load_page`) (per a11y-plan §5 Test harness pattern).

- (F13, a11y) By keyboard alone on Cells: Tab reaches `cells-grid`, arrows move the current cell and bring it into view, Enter opens its editor focused, a typed value and Enter commit it, focus returns to the grid; a pointer-opened editor reads as it did; a filled cell, the headers and the editor meet their ratios, in both layout modes (`stand_keyboard`, `stand_contrast`, `stand_cells_served`).

- (CARRY 2) `:open` reads right on a `details` and a `dialog` through construction, write and removal and a `summary`'s click and Enter (`open_state`); the redraw route's first hop reads a request through the proxy to its receiver and one wake-up, the check stating what it cannot read (`blitz-shell`'s unit test); `pseudo_element_flow_classification`'s three tests hold in both layout modes.

- (closed sets, arch, obs) No verb, `NODE_FIELDS` key, cause, `Defect` or session error is added: `describe`'s count row reads `[12, 13, 12, 3, 8, 4, 15]`; escher-driver holds 2 `info_span!` sites and 0 events; the added-lines census reads 0; `host_log` and `mcp_log` read 0 needles under both builds (per arch §Standard Contracts → Driver session; obs-plan §4; obs-plan §8).

data.head: ## Graph impact (from the code-graph query; trace `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-31T03-24-40-phase/tree-query-2026-10-31-engine-debts.json`)

body: - **`visible_region`** — 3 production callers: `in_view` @ `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:454`, `crop` @ `execute.rs:465`, `clip_region` @ `packages/escher-driver/src/lint.rs:394`; 4 test callers. A fix moves the act gate's `off-screen`, the shot's crop and the lint's clip together.

- **`build_accessibility_tree`** — `accessibility_tree` @ `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:197`, `handle_blitz_shell_event` @ `packages/blitz-shell/src/application.rs:82`, `accessibility_tree` @ `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:298`.

- **`set_focus_to`** — production callers include `flush` @ `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:1040`, the only focus move in the mutator; **`clear_focus`** — `handle_click` @ `events/pointer.rs:971`, script's `blur`, Dioxus `set_focus`, and no site in the mutator.
- **`is_select_option` · `options`** — read at `accessibility.rs:157,173,260`, `document.rs:739`, `keyboard.rs:176,280`, `form.rs:277`, `mutator.rs:1252`: the reach of an `optgroup` model.
- **`is_native_checkable`** — one caller, `build_accessibility_node` @ `accessibility.rs:190`.

Measured by a throwaway target, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/zz_p3_probe.rs`, run on the tree at `2109f1c2e`, stand options, both layout modes, every row reading alike in both, then removed; `git status --short -- tests packages examples` printed nothing afterwards.

- **Plain pan/zoom already reads right.** A `transform` on a world box holding absolutely positioned nodes, under an untransformed `overflow:hidden` viewport: translate, `translate + scale(2)` and `scale(0.5)` each read the target's centre inside its region and the hit on the target; a target panned out reads outside and is not hit; a driver `click` on `translate + scale(2)` is accepted. On that fixture the lint reads one finding, the zoomed world box `clipped` by the viewport, a true reading.

- **The limit fires where a box that clips lies under the transform.** An inner `overflow:auto` node body under a translated or a `scale(2)` world reads region (50, 30, 80, 40) with the target at (150, 80) or (100, 60): centre outside, hit on the target. Through the driver at `translate + scale(2)`: `click` refused `off-screen`, lint `off-screen` and `truncated` on the target. A clipping box whose own shown place happens to cover the target reads right by coincidence (`vp-transformed-*`, `world-clips-*`).

- **The fix's equality.** For a clipping box's padding box P and the mapping `transformed_bounds` already computes, region = viewport ∩ AABB(map(P)): exact under translate and scale, an over-reading under rotation (the AABB holds corners the rotated clip does not). `transformed_bounds` returns `None` with no transform on the chain, so a page with none reads as today. Not yet run: this equality is the plan's to prove.

- **A non-invertible transform swallows hits.** `scale(0)` and `matrix(0,0,0,0,0,0)` with no clip of their own: a hit at (300, 200) and (590, 390) answers the target inside, nothing painted there; with `overflow:hidden` on the same box, no hit. `t.inverse()` at `node.rs:1472` leaves NaN coordinates, and `matches_self`'s `!(x < 0 || …)` reads true on NaN. No panic. Client rect reads 0 × 0.

- **`inert` with focus held.** After `inert` lands on a focused button's box: engine focus still on it, snapshot `focused` count 0, the tree's `focus` id absent from its nodes, no `blur`; Enter still clicks it (count 1 → 2); a focused text input takes a typed character. Tab leaves, and the tree's focus is whole again. AccessKit's consumer panics when focus is not in the node list (`inputs#I6`, `src/tree.rs:89-94`); read from source, and no stand binary builds an adapter.

- **`:open` reads right on every path.** At boot, on `open`'s write, on its removal, on a `summary` click and on `summary` Enter, for `details` and `dialog` as each applies, both modes. `toggle_details_open` goes through the mutator.

The stand holds no checkbox or radio (`git grep` over `examples/seven_guis`), so no committed Counter check moves. **Working entry (verbatim, title and scope hint; `escher-0.3.0/working-route.md:18`):** Engine debts — transformed scrolling box, `inert` focus fixup, native checkedness, select limits, select-option overlap, served pages' keyboard and contrast rows; each the founder's fork (v030-04)

**Intent anchor:** `escher-0.3.0/intent.md` Findings §4 «The engine's recorded debts»: "EXPECT: each debt is taken to the founder as a fork, then fixed, pinned as a stated limit, or kept as a residual by his word. Every fix is proven on the stand or a fixture." Principles, «One engine-debts entry»: the founder, 2026-10-26, «Один пункт «долги движка» (Рекомендую)» — "each engine change comes to him as its own fork (the playbook's engine-change rule)." The requirement `v030-04` (`escher-0.3.0/requirements.md:15`) names residual lines 31, 32, 33, 34, 39 and 40.

**Run mode:** the operator's word at invocation (inputs#I1): the sampler is forced for this phase (`detail.py sample --side phase --force`); the 0.4.0 inputs are snapped; the founder is asleep, so the operator is AWAY on the operator's own word and every fork takes the away form — ALL forks, with their dependences, in one file in the run dir, handed to the operator at P4, with **no provisional answer**. The take-up therefore stops at P4 until the founder's word comes back; no plan reaches a P5 card on an unanswered fork.

Six recorded debts, each ending as the founder's word says — fixed and proven on the stand or a fixture, pinned as a stated limit, or kept as a residual. The forks are P4's; what follows is each debt as recorded, its options P3's to measure.

1. **The transformed scrolling box** (`.andromeda/residuals.md:31`). `visible_region` reads a scrolling box under a transform where it stands untransformed, so a target inside a translated scrolling box reads outside its visible region and a driver call on it can be refused `off-screen` though it shows. Pinned by `transformed_client_rect::a_target_inside_a_translated_scrolling_box_reads_outside_its_visible_region` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/transformed_client_rect.rs:186`, present); stated in `off-screen`'s meaning. A fix is an engine change for every document.
   - **The founder's adaptation (inputs#I2, inputs#I3 item 7, inputs#I4):** if the fix is taken, it is proven on a pan/zoom container like the node graph's — a CSS `transform` on a container holding absolutely positioned nodes, not only on the existing translated fixture. The relay: "Each is a direction for the phase, not a decision. Where an adaptation changes a contract or widens a boundary, the phase brings it to the founder as a fork. None of them adds a 0.4.0 capability to 0.3.0." A scale is in the fix's reach: measured, an inner scroller under `scale(2)` reads the limit as a translate does. [premise-corrected: the overseer's "pan and zoom hit exactly this case" (inputs#I4) holds only where a box that clips lies under the transform; a plain pan/zoom world under an untransformed clipping viewport already reads right, in both layout modes, by harness and driver — research.md §Patterns detected]

2. **`inert` focus fixup** (`.andromeda/residuals.md:32`). HTML's focus fixup is not built: a node that holds focus when it or an ancestor becomes inert keeps focus until focus moves. Pinned by `inert_subtree::removing_inert_restores_focus_hit_and_tree` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/inert_subtree.rs:145`, present). A fix is an engine change for every document, and focus is a11y surface (SC 2.4.3).

3. **Native checkedness** (`.andromeda/residuals.md:33`). An `<input type="checkbox">` or `type="radio"` writes no `toggled` from its own checked state, so the tree the shell hands the adapter never states it checked (HTML-AAM), while the snapshot's `checked` reads the element and is right. The founder's «Исправить позже (Рекомендую)» (2026-10-18) left it for "a later chunk or the nearest accessibility work". A fix is an engine change for every document. It crosses to the platform adapter as a closed value, a state already ratified on that crossing (`.claude/rules/security.md`). `Reading`'s `pressed` is written from the same node property but filtered off the five checkable roles (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs:178-181`), and `checked` reads the element first (`:169`), so no snapshot reading moves on a native control's own role; only a native control whose `role` attribute names a non-checkable role would begin to read `pressed`, which the fork states.

4. **The select model's stated limits** (`.andromeda/residuals.md:34`). A `multiple` select and an `optgroup`'s options are not modelled (a `multiple` select lays out as an empty bordered box and takes no key), no popup is painted and an option is not clicked (a driver `click` on one is refused `covered`), and a checkbox, radio or text input fires no engine `change`. Stated in the masters. These are several debts under one residual line: P4 splits them into one fork each where their cost differs, since a painted popup and a `change` event on a checkbox are not one decision (the costs measured in research.md).

5. **The select-option overlap** (`.andromeda/residuals.md:39`). The snapshot gives each `ListBoxOption` its select's client rect, so `lint` reports an `overlap` between a select's two options in every document; on the stand the flight booker at boot reads one (`flight-type-one-way` × `flight-type-return`), `stand_lint` pinned `[0, 1, 0, 0]` as measured. Its recorded fix is a driver change for every document in `lint.rs`'s `overlaps`. Note the dependence: a painted popup (item 4) would change what an option's bounds should read, so this fork is asked with that one.

6. **The served pages' rows** (`.andromeda/residuals.md:40`). Cells and the load page hold no Tab-order, keyboard-activation or contrast row, so SC 2.1.1 and 1.4.3 are unasserted on the load page's `load-fetch` Button, a stand control; stated as an OPEN gap in a11y-plan §5. On the load page this adds checks and changes no engine: every row read green when measured. [premise-corrected: Cells reads red on SC 2.1.1 already — Tab reaches `back-btn` alone and 0 of its 676 cells are focusable, measured in both layout modes — so the further fork the scope foresaw exists now, and it moves the stand's markup, not its colour or the engine's keys.] The route's «A11y re-read» (Epoch 6) re-asserts SC 2.1.1 · 2.4.3 · 1.4.3 on "stand and served pages after engine debts", so these rows are its ground.
`route.py pins` lists three `CARRY:` blocks on this entry (475, 504 and 444 chars), each folded whole, each read from the entry's own line; no `BLOCKED-ON`, `PREREQ`, `CONTEXT` or `WATCH`.

The reading is `evidence/readings.md` §The transformed scrolling box of that chunk: `scrolling.rs` and `layout/writing_mode.rs` untouched by the take.

- **No live leg:** no external process is driven.
- **No cold-agent run:** its live run is the operator's, and `v030-15`'s. The new `covered` clause and the list can move `wrong_calls`, stated here; no entry reads it.

- **The windowed smoke** needs `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`. Unset, it reads `not run`, and the windowed build stays proven by its `build` entry and CI. It proves the boot alone: the windowed list is read and not run, a stated limit, since no test launches a window (test-plan `e2e-test-strategy.md:25`).
- **MSRV, coverage and the stand repeat** are CI's jobs, read by the CI entry.
- **The CI read** spans two runs by construction, so the operator's commit and push precede it.
- **Git reads** of what this chunk changed name the base `3af5a9bcf078b70ea37b97f516fcaf444a3da0f0`.
- **OS-sensitive cases:** none is added. No `cfg(unix)`, `cfg(windows)` or `cfg!(…)` site lands, and the `feature = "scrollbars"` gate is no OS. The CI entry's `note` says so.

body: - (`verification-matrix.json#v030-17`) A closed select opens a painted list of its options; a person or an agent chooses one by pointer and by key and the select then reads that choice; an option of the opened list can be acted on through the driver; the list closes without a choice. Concretely, in both layout modes through the real dispatch: `select_popup` opens by click, Enter and Space, chooses by click, Enter, Space and Tab, one `input` then one `change` per change, and closes by Escape, a second click and a click outside with no event; `select_popup_painted` reads the rows on frames; `stand_act_popup` accepts `click flight-type`, then `click flight-type-return`, the next snapshot reading value `return`, and closes by `press escape` with the value unchanged.
- (arch) Every choice from the list passes through `apply_select_choice`, a choice of the chosen option firing nothing (per architecture §Established Decisions → Scrolling and input).

- (arch) The driver's verb list stays twelve and its causes eight, with `covered` restated once in the schema's source and the count row `[12, 13, 12, 3, 8, 4, 15]` unmoved (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session).

- (arch) The list shows through `paint_scene` alone, with no shell or renderer code moved: the preservation guard reads `packages/blitz-shell`, `packages/dioxus-native`, manifests and the lock unchanged (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Paint and shell). The windowed list is read and not run, a stated limit; the windowed smoke proves the boot.

- (arch) `stand_act_popup` reads two `click`s on one point with no `advance` as open then close, each still focusing (per architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session, `standard-contracts.md:175`).

- (security) With the select disabled or inert, an option disabled, or a select under a non-invertible transform, pointer, key and driver open nothing or change no choice and fire no `input` or `change`; a select removed, disabled, hidden or made inert with its list open closes with no panic, in both layout modes (per security-plan §Input Validation, Markup attributes).

- (security) A page with a non-numeric, a `0` and an oversized `size`, 2,000 options and a 5,500-character label opens or refuses the list with finite geometry and no panic, in both layout modes (per security-plan §Input Validation, Markup numeric attributes).

- (security) `host_log` and `mcp_log` read 0 option id, name and value needles at `trace` under the per-package build and, through `ci-leg.sh fast`, the workspace build, and `stand_act_spans` holds its eight fields (per security-plan §Logging & Monitoring).

- (design) With a select inside `overflow: hidden` and `contain: paint` boxes and under an `opacity` ancestor, each row paints whole and is hit where it paints, and a point the list does not cover answers what paint shows (per design-system §Depth Strategy → Engine depth behavior).

- (design) The list holds no motion, and a step that opens or closes it reads the new state in its next `snapshot` with no `advance`, the `VirtualClock` unmoved (per design-system §Motion → Animation runtime).

- (design) `screenshot` of an open list shows its rows in the form-control family with non-zero boxes, and an app with no `sans-serif` family stays refused `fonts-unavailable` (per design-system §Typography → Loading).

- (layouts) After open and close with no choice the snapshot reads the same `ComboBox` value and the same two `ListBoxOption`s at the select's client rect as at boot, at 800 × 600, in both layout modes, and the Tab walk `back-btn` → `flight-type` → `flight-start` → `flight-book` holds (per layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → Primary screens).
- (layouts) A pointer at the centre of an open row lands on that option unscrolled and with the viewport scrolled before opening (per layout-templates §Surface: desktop-native → IA notes).

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run stand` and `run all` exit 0 with outcome `passed`; `ci-leg.sh fast`, `doc`, `audit` and `a11y` pass; CI reads `verdict: green`, the stand repeat over seventeen named targets, the coverage floors 3 of 3 (per test-plan §3 Agent-run contract; §10).

now shows an agent what is drawn: a snapshot, stable ids, refusal causes, a visual lint and replayable checks. It does
not show what the UI knows beyond what it draws. An agent cannot see which component rendered a node, which handlers
it carries, which state those handlers write, or which nodes read that state. It learns that an action is refused
only by trying it. It explores by hand, starting from boot every time. It sees an error only through the log sink,
detached from the action that caused it. Layout, randomness and fonts still depend on the host. Beside that gap, the
code that grew 0.2.0 needs care again: functions over the complexity ceiling went 84 → 87 → 88. The README still
describes 0.2.0 as planned, upstream has moved, and the engine's recorded debts are still open.

The user is still an agent with no display, and Viola's UI is still the first real consumer: escher leads Viola. The
founder, 2026-10-20: «Глубокий агентский слой». The priority goes to what no alternative has. Escher should know the
UI's structure, its handlers and its state, so an agent can ask what it may do, explore on its own, and tie an error
to its cause.

- **The codebase, the README and upstream first.** The first three entries are, in order, the improvement on the
  Epoch 5 audit, the README, and the upstream sync (the founder, 2026-10-26).

- **D2 first, then its consumers.** The UI graph is built before B3, E3, E2 and D1 read it. Its first step is a probe
  of how much the Dioxus runtime exposes without a fork-level change, and what the probe shows reaches the founder
  before the graph is built (the founder, 2026-10-26; his standing rule «infrastructure ahead of the queue»).
- **One engine-debts entry**, after the first three. Each engine change comes to the founder as its own fork.

- **Kept from 0.2.0.** escher leads Viola. The stand is the proof, with a minimal fixture beside it where the tasks
  lack a case. Upstream is merged at each epoch boundary while our changes stay mostly additive. The API explains
  itself. In prose the name is «Escher»; crate, binary and path names stay lowercase.

Opt-in OTel export, MCP revision `2026-07-28`, the platform accessibility adapter and its windowed AT witness, Cells'
selected-cell state, and the dependency advisories with their drop conditions all stay residuals. Upstream pull
requests to DioxusLabs/blitz wait on #1083's reaction.
- The audit's three escher-written functions over the ceiling are back under it, and every check is green.

- The GitHub page shows 0.2.0 done and verified and 0.3.0 planned, and the capabilities statement describes the
  2026-10-25 run.
- Upstream's new work is taken in by the founder's chosen take, and every engine debt is dispositioned by his word.

- One read gives, for the current screen, node → component → handlers → the state they write → the nodes that read
  it.

- An agent can ask what it may do on the screen and why. It can see which handlers no check reached, start in a given
  state, explore breadth-first into replayable checks, and receive the errors its action caused.

- An agent can ask why an element sits where it does, render one component alone, and get the same state on two hosts
  from a seed and bundled fonts.
- A cold-agent run over the new capabilities passes the bar the founder sets from 0.2.0's baseline.

# As-built baseline — escher-0.1.0

The adopted workspace, untouched (HEAD `eaca28ba`), measured on this host on 2026-10-05. Summaries and exit statuses

the gate trail is `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-05T19-48-32-implement/`.

## Host

Re-measured at implement time (2026-10-05T19:48Z); every fact equals the P3 reading (research.md §Host facts measured)
except `target/`, noted last.

| fact | reading |
|---|---|
| OS | Omarchy 4.0.4 (Arch-based; `/etc/os-release` NAME `Omarchy`, BUILD_ID `4.0.4`) |

| cargo | `cargo 1.99.0 (5f94df478 2026-08-27)` |
| active toolchain | `stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (default)`; no `rust-toolchain*` file in the repo |
| cargo config | no `.cargo/config*` in the repo or the user's home |
| system packages | `fontconfig 2:2.18.3-2` · `openssl 3.6.4-1` · `pkgconf 3.0.7-1` · `python 3.14.7-1` (`pkg-config --modversion fontconfig openssl` → 2.18.3 / 3.6.4) |
| fonts (`fc-match`) | sans-serif → Liberation Sans · serif → Liberation Serif · monospace → JetBrainsMono Nerd Font; `fc-list` → 798 faces |
| env handles | `PAINT_TREE_BENCH_HTML` unset · `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` unset · `RUSTFLAGS` unset (set/unset only) |
| graphical session | `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and `DISPLAY` set — not decisive: `blitz-test-harness` carries no `winit`/`wgpu` dependency |

- **Toolchain against the pins.** Host stable 1.99.0 is above the workspace MSRV `rust-version = "1.91.0"`, edition
  2024 (Cargo.toml:39-40, :242/:246). The flake's `pkgs.rust-bin.stable."1.90.0"` pin (flake.nix:31) is not used on
  this host and sits below the MSRV it would build against.
- **Arch stand-ins for CI's apt packages.** CI installs `libfontconfig1-dev` (ci.yml) and relies on the runner's
  build-time python3; here `fontconfig` (headers + `.pc` file in the one Arch package), `pkgconf`, `openssl` and
  `python` play those roles. Nothing was installed for this run.
- **`target/` state.** P3 read 1.4G of setup-time build-script outputs; by take-up it held 85G (P5's baseline runs).
  `cargo clean` at 2026-10-05T19:48:49Z removed 32 888 files, 104.0 GiB, in 1m 43s — `target/` absent before entry 1.

## Commands

Fired through the gate tool (`gate v1.10`, shell `/usr/bin/bash -c`, bound GNU `timeout`), in this order, from the
project root:

1. `cargo build --workspace --locked`
2. `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked`
3. `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test text_selection_anonymous_block -- --nocapture`
4. `cargo test --workspace --locked`
5. `cargo fmt --all --check`
6. `cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings`
7. `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked --keep-going`
8. `git status --porcelain -- packages tests examples apps wpt Cargo.toml Cargo.lock`
9. `grep -cE '^## (Host|Commands|Wall-clock|Tests|A11y-bearing files|Wider gates)$' escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-05-as-built-baseline/evidence/baseline.md`
10. the credential probe — `cat …/evidence/*.md | grep -ciE '{pattern}'`, verbatim at `plan.md` §Test Commands
    (gate 10). Its pattern is not copied here: a verbatim copy in this file is itself a hit (measured: the warm run
    read `1`, the hit being this line).

- **Profile:** dev (`dev` / `test` profiles, unoptimized + debuginfo). No `--release`, no `production` / `p2` profile.
- **Features:** workspace defaults — no `--no-default-features`, no `--features`. `blitz-tests` forces `blitz-dom`
  `accessibility` · `floats` · `system-fonts` and `blitz-paint` `scrollbars` · `svg` through its dev-dependencies.
  `log-times` / `log-frame-times` / `log-phase-times` are off (not default, not requested).
- **CI's `perl -pi.bak -e 's/opt-level = 2/opt-level = 0/g' Cargo.toml` rewrite was NOT applied:** its one target line
  is `[profile.p2]`'s `opt-level = 2` (Cargo.toml:210, the sole hit), so a dev-profile build compiles identically
  without it, and `Cargo.toml` stays untouched (entry 8).
- **`--locked`** is added to every cargo build/test/lint form (CI passes none); the committed `Cargo.lock` resolved
  without change.
- Entry 7 is the workspace form, not CI's docs job (`cargo doc`, bare): the root manifest is the lib-less package
  `blitz-examples` (Cargo.toml:238-239), so a bare `cargo doc` documents no library crate (§Wider gates).

## Wall-clock

Seconds are the gate tool's per-entry wall-clock (process start → exit, GNU `timeout` wrapper included), entries run
strictly in sequence in one `target/` directory.

| # | entry | cold (s) | warm (s) | cargo's own `Finished` line (cold) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `cargo build --workspace` | 120.26 | 5.54 | `dev` profile in 2m 00s (warm: 5.48s) |
| 2 | `cargo test -p blitz-tests` | 486.45 | 7.41 | `test` profile in 8m 00s (warm: 0.21s) |

| 8–10 | tree guard · evidence probe · credential probe | 0.01 · 0.01 · 0.00 | 0.01 · 0.00 · 0.00 | — |

- **Cold basis:** the first block run after `cargo clean` (gate run 2026-10-05T19:50Z). Entry 1 is a from-empty
  compile of the whole workspace and its dependencies; each later entry is cold for what it alone compiles (the `test`
  profile, clippy's check metadata, rustdoc) and reuses what the entries before it left in `target/` — so entry 2's
  figure is "after a workspace dev build", not "from empty".
- **Warm basis:** the immediately following re-run of the whole block over the same `target/`, no source change.
  Warm run 2026-10-05T20:29Z: entries 1-9 as on the cold run (entry 9 now green, reading `6`); same tallies
  (blitz-tests 61 lines, 255 · 0 · 3; workspace 108 lines, 407 · 0 · 3), same rustdoc errors. Warm seconds are
  test execution plus cargo's freshness check; entry 1's cargo `Finished` line read 5.48s (not near-zero) — cause not measured.
  Entry 10 read red once on the warm run on a self-match (§Commands, item 10) and green on its re-run after the fix.
- The test-profile compile dominates: entries 2 + 4 are 2119.33 s of the cold run's 2278.96 s total, against a 120 s
  dev build. P5's reading (`cargo test -p blitz-tests` 744.88 s, `cargo test --workspace` 1724.48 s, dev build 182.3 s)
  ran over a different `target/` state; the two are not one basis.

## Tests

`cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked` (entry 2), exit 0, log lacks `test result: FAILED`:

# Dependency audit — the firing set under the committed `deny.toml` (plan step 5)

Tool: cargo-deny 0.20.2 (dev host), advisory database `https://github.com/RustSec/advisory-db` fetched
at the run (2026-10-05T22:53Z). Command: `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh audit` →
`cargo deny --locked check advisories`, config `deny.toml` (`[graph]`: the six ci.yml platforms,
`all-features = true`).

## Firing set with `ignore = []` (rustls already at 0.23.45)

`advisories FAILED`, exit 1 — ONE finding:

- `error[unmaintained]` **RUSTSEC-2026-0192** `ttf-parser 0.25.1` — `Solution: No safe upgrade is available!`
  Chain: ttf-parser ← owned_ttf_parser 0.25.1 ← ab_glyph 0.2.32 ← sctk-adwaita 0.12.0 ← winit-wayland
  0.31.0-beta.3 ← winit 0.31.0-beta.3 ← blitz-shell / dioxus-native. winit is an exact coupled pin
  (CLAUDE.md "winit exact beta"), so no fix is reachable inside the pins → per-ID ignore with its reason
  in `deny.toml`.

With that one ignore: `advisories ok`, exit 0.

## The other three lockfile advisories

| advisory | crate | how it leaves the audit |
|---|---|---|
| RUSTSEC-2026-0285 (vulnerability) | rustls 0.23.43 | FIXED: `cargo update -p rustls@0.23.43 --precise 0.23.45` (plan step 1); the lockfile delta is the rustls version line alone. cargo-deny also logs `filtered rustls 0.23.45` — no build graph reaches it |
| RUSTSEC-2024-0436 (unmaintained) | paste 1.0.15 | not fired: cargo-deny logs `filtered paste 1.0.15` (and `filtered rav1e 0.8.1`, `filtered ravif 0.13.0`) |
| RUSTSEC-2026-0186 (unsound) | memmap2 0.5.10 | not fired: cargo-deny logs `filtered memmap2 0.5.10` (and `filtered cacache 13.1.0`, `filtered http-cache 1.0.0-alpha.6`) |

**Observed reach gap (for the wrap's security-plan amendment, not fixed here).** paste and memmap2 ARE
in cargo's own graph for a target the config lists:
`cargo tree --workspace --all-features --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -e normal,build -i memmap2@0.5.10`
→ memmap2 ← cacache 13.1.0 ← http-cache 1.0.0-alpha.6 ← blitz-net (its optional `cache` feature,
`packages/blitz-net/Cargo.toml:17`); `-i paste@1.0.15` → paste ← rav1e 0.8.1 ← ravif 0.13.0 ← image
0.25.10. cargo-deny 0.20.2's graph prunes `http-cache` and `ravif` even with `all-features = true`
(`-L debug`: `filtered http-cache 1.0.0-alpha.6`, `filtered ravif 0.13.0`), and passing `--all-features`
on the command line reads the same single finding. So the audit leg's reach is cargo-deny's feature
resolution, which is narrower than `cargo tree`'s on these two optional chains; a lockfile-wide scanner
(cargo-audit 0.22.2, research.md §Measurements) still reports paste and memmap2 as warnings. Neither is
ignored in `deny.toml` — an ignore for an advisory that does not fire would be dead config.

# P3 smoke: the windowed stand with accessibility on

- **When:** 2026-10-06T12:39Z, at /implement P3, by hand (not a plan entry).
- **Why this form:** the plan names `just seven_guis` as the windowed boot. seven_guis enables no `accessibility` feature, though (the workspace pins dioxus-native with `default-features = false`). So that recipe never compiles the shell's AccessKit path. The smoke built the same binary with the feature forced: `cargo build -p seven_guis --bin seven_guis_native --features dioxus-native/accessibility`, exit 0. `cargo tree` with the same flag shows `dioxus-native-dom feature "accessibility"` on, through the dioxus-native companion edge.
- **Boot:** `timeout -s TERM -k 5 15 ./target/debug/seven_guis_native` exited 124 (it stayed up for the whole bound). Its stderr is one line, a winit Wayland `WARN` that `xdg_toplevel_icon_manager_v1` is not supported. It has 0 `panic` / `already borrowed` / `BorrowMutError` lines. Afterwards the process list had no `seven_guis_native`.
- **What it does not prove:** the host's AT-SPI bus read `org.a11y.Status IsEnabled = false` (`busctl --user get-property`, read-only). So the AccessKit adapter was inactive, and `update_if_active` never ran `Document::accessibility_tree` in the window. The smoke proves the windowed boot with the re-threaded `update_tree` callers compiled in. It does not prove a platform tree build. That output is proved headlessly by `stand_accessibility_ids` through the same trait method. The bus flag was left untouched, because it is the operator's desktop state.

# Entry 3 (presentation-unchanged) — surfaced at implement, 2026-10-06T10:15Z

## Why the entry reads red
Person keys only give a keyed list once the filter moves out of the `for` body and into its iterator. In the old
form each `for` item was an unkeyed `if` wrapper around the keyed row `div`. Dioxus therefore diffed the items by
position, and when an inner key changed it replaced every shifted row. Measured: with `key: "{person.id}"` inside the

With the filtered iterator it reads green, because Delete drops only Hans's row node.

Removing the `if` level un-nests the row `div` by one level. Entry 3's `diff` compares the grepped lines with their
whitespace. Its only difference is 4 leading spaces on the row's `class:` line, and the class expression is
byte-identical:

title: I1-relay-1.md.txt
body:
Question put to the founder at this phase's P1 (the route entry leaves it to promotion):

"The route entry leaves this to be settled at promotion: which edits to an app's code must leave an in-place element's id unchanged? (Today an element with an HTML `id` reads that id; every other element reads a positional path like `TaskShell/Crud/div:0/div:1/div:0/div[7]`, and its children inherit that path even under a keyed parent.)"

Options offered:
1. "Anchor at keyed ancestors (Recommended)" — Keyed elements survive any edit that leaves them in place. Unkeyed elements survive any edit outside their nearest keyed ancestor's subtree, plus edits inside it that don't touch their own relative path. Needs a rule change: an unkeyed element's path starts at its nearest keyed ancestor instead of the component root. Path ids under keyed ancestors change once, now, before the diff and driver depend on them; the id tests for v010-01/02 are re-pinned and the architecture contract is amended at wrap (a change to a locked contract, so it is yours to ratify).
2. "Today's rule, proven" — No rule change; prove and document which edits keep an id.
3. "Every actionable element keyed" — a stand rule plus a check: every focusable or role-bearing stand element must carry an author key, and the check fails on one that reads a positional path. Can be combined with the first option.

The founder's answer, verbatim:

Selected: "Anchor at keyed ancestors (Recommended)"

Notes: "Combine it with the third option: both rules in this chunk. (1) An unkeyed element path starts at its nearest keyed ancestor. (2) Every element an agent can act on (focusable or role-bearing) must carry an author key, and a check fails on one that reads a positional path, naming the element and the remedy. Also: v010-16 observed_gap in the matrix is still v010-01 text ("no semantic id exists") and is stale; correct it through matrix.py refine or a dated note before the claim."

title: I2-relay-2.md.txt
body:
Three plan forks put to the founder at this phase's P4, after research, with the founder's answers verbatim.

1. Question: "Research found that every lean task's root sits directly under keyed containers that belong to the shell, not to the task (`main` > `task-shell` > `task-body` > the task component). Should a keyed ancestor outside an element's own component anchor its path?"
   Options offered: "Inside one component (Recommended)" — a component's root keeps starting at its component names, as today; the anchor applies only to unkeyed elements under a keyed element of the same component. · "Across components" — every unkeyed path starts at the nearest keyed DOM ancestor, whatever component owns it.
   Answer: "Inside one component (Recommended)"

2. Question: "The ruling defines an element an agent can act on as "focusable or role-bearing". CRUD's person row is a `div` with a click handler: it is not focusable and reads a generic role, so those two readers miss it, yet the stand's own CRUD check clicks it. Should carrying an event listener also count?"
   Options offered: "Add listener-bearing (Recommended)" — actionable = focusable, or an interactive role, or carries an event listener; each row gains an author key built from the person's model id; no focusability or tabindex change is made to the row. · "Focusable or role only" — the ruling as worded; no stand element gains a key.
   Answer: "Add listener-bearing (Recommended)"

3. Question: "How should an anchored path be spelled? It must never equal an author key, a component path or a document path. A bare `key/segment` can: a key spelled like a component name would read that component's path."
   Options offered: "#key/segment (Recommended)" · "key/segment, bare"
   Answer (the founder's own text): "Neither as written: spell an anchored path key//segment (a double slash after the anchor key, no leading sigil). A leading # starts a comment in bash and zsh, so an unquoted id would silently cut the command line, and intent finding 7 wants stand flows scriptable in shell alone. key//segment is collision-free by construction too: an author key holds no slash, a component path never has an empty segment, a document path starts with a slash. If research finds a case where // is not collision-free, tell me before planning around it."

row.path: message: the founder, 2026-10-06, answering this phase P4 fork round in session
row.why: answered at the P4 fork round, closing research three open questions: the anchor acts inside one component only; a listener-bearing element is actionable; an anchored path is spelled key//segment

title: evidence/controls.md
body:
# Controls — four mutations of the executor, each shown red and reverted

Step 12's record, made by hand on the dev host (Linux) on 2026-10-07. Each mutation was applied
alone to `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs`, the six driver-action checks were run, and the
file was restored before the next one.

- Command, the same for every mutation:
  `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --no-fail-fast --test stand_act_ids --test stand_act_diff --test stand_act_timer --test stand_act_refused --test stand_act_keys --test stand_act_range`
- Before the first mutation the same six files read 16 passed, 0 failed (6 · 2 · 2 · 1 · 2 · 3
  in the order diff, ids, keys, range, refused, timer).
- The pristine file's sha256 is `0216a8b1ced17c75c754aa27283183b179b15a4337da81f4bf41e238285ab897`
  before the first mutation and after the last revert.
- Every failure below is the first one a test met, in the `incremental=false` pass, which runs
  first; no test reached its `incremental=true` pass once it had failed. A message is quoted as
  the check printed it: a layout mode, a task and an index, no id and nothing a screen reads.

## 1 — the settle removed from a settled step

`settled_step`: `let busy = harness.settle().err().map(|not_settled| not_settled.busy);` replaced
by `let busy: Option<Busy> = None;` — the snapshot after the step is taken with no pass in between.

Named check: `stand_act_timer`. **Red** — cargo exit 101, 3 of 16 tests failed:

| file | test | first failure |
|---|---|---|
| `stand_act_timer` | `a_reset_then_an_advance_returns_settled_with_the_delayed_update_present` | `incremental=false: Timer: step 0: the elapsed time is in the returned diff as it reads after the advance` |
| `stand_act_diff` | `an_advance_on_the_timer_returns_the_elapsed_time` | `incremental=false: Timer: step 0 names exactly the nodes stated for it` |
| `stand_act_ids` | `an_id_addressed_click_has_the_effect_of_a_selector_click_on_a_twin` | `incremental=false: Timer: the driver's diff for Reset is the selector click's` |

The other 13 stayed green. What that shows: without the settle only `advance` reads wrong — its
ticks are delivered and no pass applies them before the second snapshot. `click`, `type` and
`press` stay green because each harness input helper makes one pass of its own, and no stand step
driven here needs a second. The settle's second-pass case (a write made while an element mounts)
is `stand_settle`'s, not a driver check's.

## 2 — the diff replaced by an empty one

`settled_step`: `(busy, before.diff(&after))` replaced by `(busy, before.diff(&before))`.

Named check: `stand_act_diff`. **Red** — cargo exit 101, 12 of 16 tests failed, in all six files:

| file | failed / tests | first failure of its first test |
|---|---|---|
| `stand_act_diff` | 5 / 6 | `incremental=false: Counter: step 0 returns the diff of the snapshots before and after it` |
| `stand_act_ids` | 1 / 2 | `incremental=false: Counter: control 1: the driver's diff is the selector click's` |
| `stand_act_keys` | 2 / 2 | `incremental=false: step 0 names exactly the controls stated for it` |
| `stand_act_range` | 1 / 1 | `incremental=false: sequence B: step 0 names exactly the controls stated for it` |
| `stand_act_refused` | 1 / 2 | `incremental=false: row 3: the steps before the call ran` |
| `stand_act_timer` | 2 / 3 | `incremental=false: Timer: step 0: the elapsed time is in the returned diff as it reads after the advance` |

The four that stayed green assert nothing a non-empty diff carries: the empty-diff check on a
click that changes nothing, the id acceptance check, the bound check on an id's length and the
refused `advance`. In `stand_act_diff` the password check went red on its positive control —
`incremental=false: fixture: what the call returned, written out whole, holds the mask` — which
is what keeps its "holds none of the typed text" assertion from passing on an empty result.

## 3 — an unresolved id answered with the first element

`centre_of`: the lookup `.find(|(_, listed)| listed == id).ok_or(not_found)?` given a fallback to
the first pair `element_ids()` lists, so an id that names nothing clicks the `html` element.

Named check: `stand_act_refused`. **Red** — cargo exit 101, 3 of 16 tests failed:

| file | test | first failure |
|---|---|---|
| `stand_act_refused` | `a_refused_call_names_its_cause_and_leaves_the_instance_unchanged` | `incremental=false: row 2: the call is refused` |
| `stand_act_refused` | `the_longest_admitted_id_is_looked_up_and_one_byte_more_is_malformed` | `incremental=false: an id of the longest admitted length reaches the lookup` |
| `stand_act_ids` | `the_snapshot_the_accessibility_tree_and_the_driver_read_one_id` | `incremental=false: Counter: an id no element carries is refused not-found` |

Rows 0 and 1 of the refused table (an unknown verb, a missing argument) passed before row 2
failed: they are refused by `validate`, which the mutation does not touch.

## 4 — `advanced_ms` returned as the milliseconds asked

`Session::run`, the `advance` arm: `advanced_ms = step(harness, ms).min(ms);` replaced by
`step(harness, ms); advanced_ms = ms;`.

Named check: `stand_act_timer`. **Red** — cargo exit 101, 1 of 16 tests failed:

| file | test | first failure |
|---|---|---|
| `stand_act_timer` | `a_reset_then_an_advance_returns_settled_with_the_delayed_update_present` | `incremental=false: Timer: step 2: the advance reports the whole ticks it moved` |

Step 2 is the advance of 50 ms, which moves no whole tick; steps 0 and 1 ask for whole ticks
(1000 and 300) and pass under the mutation, as they must.

## 5 — the clamp removed (a fifth control, beside the plan's four)

Mutation 4 removes the clamp together with the step's own report, so it does not isolate the
clamp, and the stand's step never claims more than it was asked. A seventeenth test was therefore
added after mutations 1 to 4 were run — `stand_act_timer`'s
`an_advance_reports_no_more_than_it_was_asked`, on a fixture session whose time step claims a
fixed amount — and the six files read 17 passed, 0 failed (6 · 2 · 2 · 1 · 2 · 4) on the pristine
file. Then:

`Session::run`, the `advance` arm: `advanced_ms = step(harness, ms).min(ms);` replaced by
`advanced_ms = step(harness, ms);`.

**Red** — cargo exit 101, 1 of 17 tests failed:

| file | test | first failure |
|---|---|---|
| `stand_act_timer` | `an_advance_reports_no_more_than_it_was_asked` | `incremental=false: fixture: row 3: the advance reports the lesser of what was asked and what the step claims` |

Row 3 asks for 100 ms of a step that claims 600; rows 0 to 2 claim no more than was asked and
pass under the mutation. The file's sha256 after the revert is the pristine one above.

## Not controlled

- The macOS arm of `press` (`deleteBackward:` dispatched after a `backspace`) is compiled out
  on the dev host; no mutation of it was run.

## A reading beside the controls — the delete binding on the dev host

Not a mutation. Read once through a temporary probe, deleted afterwards, in both layout modes:
on a held CRUD session with `crud-name` reading `Ad`, `Harness::apple_keybinding("deleteBackward:")`
left it reading `A`. So the binding the macOS arm dispatches deletes one character backward on
Linux, where the engine compiles the same handler. Whether a macOS build then deletes exactly one
character per `press backspace` — the key arm compiled out there, the binding alone acting — is
not measurable on this host; its one witness is the fork's macOS CI leg running `stand_act_keys`.

`3c58ce5c` and once after the one-line manifest edit
(`packages/escher-driver/Cargo.toml`: `dioxus-native-dom = { workspace = true, features = ["accessibility"] }`).

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `cargo tree -p escher-driver -e features --locked -i dioxus-native-dom` | exit 0 · no feature line for `dioxus-native-dom` | exit 0 · `dioxus-native-dom feature "accessibility"` ← `escher-driver` |

| 4 | `cargo tree -p seven_guis -e features --locked -i dioxus-native-dom` | exit 0 · no feature line for `dioxus-native-dom` | exit 0 · `dioxus-native-dom feature "accessibility"` ← `escher-driver` |
| 5 | `cargo tree -p seven_guis -e normal --locked -i accesskit_winit` | exit 101 · `did not match any packages` | exit 101 · `did not match any packages` |

Reads 1 and 2 are the two `cargo tree` entries of the plan's `## Test Commands`; read 3 is the
third reading step 1 names; reads 4 and 5 are the same question asked of the stand's feature graph
and of the winit adapter.

## Read 1 after the edit, whole

```text
dioxus-native-dom v0.7.0 (packages/dioxus-native-dom)
└── blitz-test-harness v0.3.0-beta.2 (packages/blitz-test-harness)
    └── blitz-test-harness feature "default"

```

The stand's own features on `dioxus-native` are unchanged: `prelude`, `system-fonts`,

## Read 3 after the edit, the edge the edit adds

├── blitz-dom v0.3.0-beta.2 (packages/blitz-dom)
│   └── … (the 16 lines read before the edit, unchanged)

## What the readings measure

- No platform adapter is in the stand's graph: `accesskit_xplat` and `accesskit_winit` each read

- `Cargo.lock` is byte-identical: sha256 `1e9a4587f631860f9af77e588d1abb4360b0a8d565b745888724dabdf1508ec2`

The plan's three `leg = 'operator'` entries (20, 21, 22 of `## Test Commands`) and the pre-CI
commit between the first two, each driven once by hand, in plan order, on the dev host (Linux).

**Who drove it:** the implementing agent, in the operator's stead and on the operator's word —

verdict reads", the fast leg with the clean-tree guard and the push, then ci.py conclusion --sha

prints it. Every exit was read from the bare command, never through a pipe.

title: evidence/range-input.md
body:
# Range input — the Timer's `timer-duration` slider driven through the driver

Step 11's measurement, taken by hand on the dev host (Linux) on 2026-10-07 and pinned by
`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_range.rs`. Every action below is a `Session::run` call; nothing
reaches the held harness by selector, coordinate or direct dispatch. Readings are the snapshot's
(`DioxusDocument::snapshot`), taken after each call returned.

## Fixture

- The stand's Timer task, booted through `seven_guis::stand::boot_timer(stand::options(incremental))`
  and held in a `Session` carrying the stand's time step (`session_common::hold(LeanTask::Timer, …)`).
- Both layout modes: `incremental = false` and `incremental = true`. Every reading below is the
  same in both.
- The control: id `timer-duration` · role `Slider` · name `Duration:` · enabled · value `15` at
  boot (the `value` attribute the app writes from its 15 s duration) · not focused at boot.
- The display beside it: id `timer-duration-value`, name `15.0s` at boot.
- The markup: `input type="range" min="0" max="30" step="0.5"` with an `oninput` handler that
  sets the duration (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs`).

## Sequence A — the plan's: a click on the id, then four keys

| # | call | settled | diff | `timer-duration` value | focused | `timer-duration-value` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | (boot) | — | — | `15` | no | `15.0s` |
| 1 | `click` id=`timer-duration` | yes | empty | `15` | no | `15.0s` |
| 2 | `press` key=`arrow-right` | yes | empty | `15` | no | `15.0s` |
| 3 | `press` key=`arrow-left` | yes | empty | `15` | no | `15.0s` |
| 4 | `press` key=`home` | yes | empty | `15` | no | `15.0s` |
| 5 | `press` key=`end` | yes | empty | `15` | no | `15.0s` |

The click is accepted (the id resolves; no refusal) and changes nothing: it does not move the
value and it does not focus the slider, so the four presses that follow land on no focused control.

## Sequence B — focus reached by the keyboard, then the same four keys

Added to the plan's sequence because sequence A's click left the slider unfocused: an agent's
other way to reach it is Tab. On a fresh instance:

| # | call | settled | diff (`changed`) | `timer-duration` value | focused | `timer-duration-value` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | (boot) | — | — | `15` | no | `15.0s` |
| 1 | `press` key=`tab` | yes | `back-btn` | `15` | no | `15.0s` |
| 2 | `press` key=`tab` | yes | `back-btn`, `timer-duration` | `15` | yes | `15.0s` |
| 3 | `press` key=`arrow-right` | yes | empty | `15` | yes | `15.0s` |
| 4 | `press` key=`arrow-left` | yes | empty | `15` | yes | `15.0s` |
| 5 | `press` key=`home` | yes | empty | `15` | yes | `15.0s` |
| 6 | `press` key=`end` | yes | empty | `15` | yes | `15.0s` |

With the slider holding focus the four keys still change nothing.

## What the run measures

- Predicted from the code read (research.md §Patterns detected, "No range interaction model"):
  the value reads the same after every call. **Measured: it does** — `15` and `15.0s` after each
  of the eleven calls above, in both layout modes.
- Not predicted, measured: a pointer click on the slider does not focus it; Tab does.
- So through the driver's five verbs the Timer's duration cannot be changed: neither a click nor
  an arrow, Home or End key moves a range input, focused or not.

## Not measured

- A pointer drag along the slider's track: the verb table has no drag, so an agent cannot make one.
- `arrow-up` and `arrow-down` are in the key list and were read once, after sequence A (the
  slider unfocused), with the same result — value `15`, empty diff. They were not read with the
  slider focused, are outside the plan's four keys and are not pinned.
- Any platform other than the dev host's.

No engine code was written for a range input, and no owner is named here: the owner is decided at
the wrap (the operator, 2026-10-07, at the P4 forks).

title: evidence/timer-host-boot.md
body:
# Timer host boot — the one branch `session_host.rs` gained, booted for real

A hand-driven smoke at implement P3, on the dev host (Linux), 2026-10-07T14:00Z. It has no listed
producer: the plan's two smoke entries boot the `counter` host (`host_binary`) and the windowed
stand, and `host_log` boots `crud`, so no listed entry starts `escher-session` on the `timer`
task — the only task whose session is handed a time step (step 8).

## What was run

- The binary the gate run built: `target/debug/escher-session`, built after the last source edit.
- `target/debug/escher-session timer target/tmp/p3-timer`, `RUST_LOG=info`, stdin closed, stdout
  and stderr piped, under an outer bound of 60 s; the socket was awaited for at most 30 s and the
  exit for at most 10 s, with SIGTERM then SIGKILL held in reserve (neither was needed).
- Two lines sent over `session.sock`, each on its own connection, as the wire states them:
  `hello v1` twice, then `stop v1`.

## What it read

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| state directory mode while serving | `0700` |
| first `hello` reply | `ok v1 pid=<the spawned pid> label=timer served=0` |
| second `hello` reply | differs from the first (its count) |
| `stop` reply | `ok v1 stopping` |
| host exit code | `0` |
| host stdout | 0 bytes |

test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 7 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 57 filtered out; finished in 0.04s

first diagnostic of each (file:line as the control tree had them, then the assertion's message):
- changed_set_fresh_document_reads_no_change @ packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:3360:9 — a fresh document's changed set is empty
- changed_set_drained_id_of_a_dropped_node_reads_none @ packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:3530:9 — the drained set holds the dropped node's id
- changed_set_attribute_write_marks_its_node_until_drained @ packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:3377:9 — a tracked write reads as a change
- changed_set_idle_resolve_marks_nothing_in_either_layout_mode @ packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:3511:13 — incremental=false: a resolve with nothing written marks no node
- changed_set_focus_move_marks_both_nodes_and_hover_marks_nothing @ packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:3434:9 — assertion `left == right` failed: the node that lost focus and the node that gained it
- changed_set_write_outside_the_document_marks_nothing @ packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:3417:9 — assertion failed: doc.take_changed_nodes().is_empty()
- changed_set_checked_change_marks_its_node @ packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:3485:9 — assertion `left == right` failed

what it measures:
- attribute write: on a document nothing has drained, `has_changes()` answers false after an in-document attribute write — research's by-code-read claim that the flag is constant, now read from a run.
- fresh document: the set is non-empty at construction (the root node, through `create_node`).
- idle resolve, incremental=false: a second `resolve` with nothing written puts nodes into the drained set — layout re-creates the anonymous block through `create_node` (research had this as not measured).
- focus, checked, dropped node: no write site marks them; outside-the-document: `create_node` marks a detached node.

an earlier run of the same control (same exit, 0 passed; 7 failed) had the idle-resolve test fail on its own fixture assertion: elements built with `qual_name!("div")` are in no namespace, the default stylesheet's type selectors match only the HTML namespace, so `body` and `div` laid out inline and no anonymous block was built. The fixture now creates its elements with `qual_name!(.., html)`; the lines above are the run after that fix.

# The answers to the two P4 forks — 2026-10-07-driver-command-spans

Given through the session's question dialog at phase P4, 2026-10-07. The questions and option labels are this phase's wording; the answers and the note are verbatim.

## Fork 1

**Question:** How should a driver command's span reach the log through the scrub layer? As built, escher's sink prints events only: a span writes no line, and a span's fields never pass the scrub.

**Options offered:**
- Sink prints closed spans (Recommended) — The span carries the readings as its own fields, and escher-telemetry learns to print one line per closed span of an admitted target, each span field judged by the scrub, with the sink's own timing. The driver reads no clock, and every later escher span (CLI, MCP) prints with no extra call site. Cost: edits escher-telemetry, moves 'one line per printed event' in the masters, and admits a new record class to the sink — the playbook's Boundary widening pattern, ratified only by the operator's own word.
- One event inside the span — The driver opens a span with no fields and states the readings on one event inside it; the sink is untouched and the diff is smallest. The span itself stays invisible on stderr, no duration is available without a clock read in the driver (three recorded clauses forbid one), every later span needs its own event, and a span field added later would sit outside the scrub.

**Answer:** Sink prints closed spans (Recommended)

**Note given with the answer (verbatim):** Record the widening as PROVISIONAL: this answer is not the founder own word for a new record class in the sink. List it for his batch at the Epoch 4 boundary and name it in the handoff.

## Fork 2

**Question:** Should the driver's tracing call site sit behind a cargo feature?

**Options offered:**
- Ungated (Recommended) — tracing becomes an ordinary dependency of escher-driver, as it is of escher-telemetry; no [features] table. With no subscriber installed a span costs nothing and writes nothing. Only the recorded 'no tracing dependency' clause moves, and no check can have the span silently compiled out.
- Behind a `tracing` feature — Matches the engine crates' rule (call sites under cfg with a no-op fallback). It gives escher-driver its first [features] table and a second cfg gate in the executor — three recorded clauses change — and seven_guis and blitz-tests must each name the feature, or the span is compiled out while the workspace build still shows it.

**Answer:** Ungated (Recommended)

row.why: fork 1: the sink prints closed spans, the widening recorded PROVISIONAL (not the founder own word), listed for his batch at the Epoch 4 boundary and named in the handoff; fork 2: the driver call site is ungated

Read at this chunk's wrap, 2026-10-07T22:50Z, on the dev host, from cargo's resolved feature graph

| invocation | `blitz-dom feature "tracing"` in the graph |

| `cargo tree --workspace --locked -e features -i blitz-dom` | present — 1 node, reached from `blitz-html feature "tracing"`, `blitz-shell feature "tracing"` and the example crate `wgpu_texture` |
| `cargo tree -p blitz-tests --locked -e features -i blitz-dom` | absent — 0 lines |
| `cargo tree -p seven_guis --locked -e features -i blitz-dom` | absent — 0 lines |

- `packages/blitz/Cargo.toml:14` — `default = ["net", "accessibility", "tracing"]`
- `packages/blitz/Cargo.toml:17` — `tracing = ["dep:tracing", "blitz-shell/tracing", "blitz-html/tracing", "blitz-net/tracing"]`

# Relay 1 — the P4 fork on what `attach` crosses, and the answer

Asked by /andromeda-phase P4 on 2026-10-07, chunk 2026-10-07-driver-session, as one question round (two questions).

## Question 1 (verbatim)
What should `attach` cross in this chunk? (Playbook pattern "Boundary widening", verdict: escalate — the project has no listener, socket or pipe today, so this is your word, not my lean.)

Options as written:
1. **Unix socket now (Recommended)** — A std-only Unix-domain socket in an owner-only session state directory; only lifecycle messages cross (hello, stop) — no ids, names or values. Why: v010-12 needs separate CLI invocations to reach one held instance, so a local endpoint is unavoidable; building it here keeps infrastructure ahead of the CLI and adds no dependency. Cost: arch's "listeners: none" becomes one local socket, Windows gets a typed "unsupported" in 0.1.0, and it is a boundary widening to ratify.
2. **Stdio child only** — The session host is a child of whoever starts it, driven over its stdin/stdout pipes — the one crossing shape already ratified (the cold-agent stub). `attach` is an in-process handle to that child. Trade-off: no listener and it works on Windows, but separate CLI invocations cannot share a session, so the Driver CLI entry reopens this question and may rework the lifecycle.
3. **Library only** — An in-process `Session` type that holds the instance; no process and no crossing in this chunk. Trade-off: zero boundary change and the smallest chunk, but the entry's "one process" and `attach` are not built — a later entry (Driver CLI) carries the process, the endpoint and this same question.

## Question 2 (verbatim)
Whose word is this answer, for the record? A boundary widening is ratified only by the founder's own word; a delegate's answer is recorded PROVISIONAL until the epoch boundary.

Options as written:
1. **Founder's own word** — You are the founder answering here; the answer is recorded as ratified (founder, 2026-10-07).
2. **Delegate (provisional)** — You are answering in the founder's stead; the work proceeds on it and it is recorded PROVISIONAL, superseded by the founder's word at the Epoch 4 boundary.

## The answer (verbatim, as returned to the session)
- Question 1: "Unix socket now (Recommended)"
- Question 2: "Founder's own word"

title: evidence/host-stderr-by-level.md
body:
# What the `escher-session` binary writes to stderr, by `RUST_LOG` level

Hand probe by /andromeda-implement, 2026-10-07T05:46Z (the last run's output file, read from its mtime), on the working tree of this chunk (base `7d9f351d`).
Not a gate of the plan: it was run because the quiet check's child installs no log sink, so `RUST_LOG=trace`
is inert there and says nothing about a host that does install one.

**Form.** `target/debug/escher-session crud {state-dir}` started with `RUST_LOG={level}`, stdout and stderr to
files; one `hello v1`, then `stop v1` over the socket; the host exited 0 and the state directory was gone at
every level. Nothing was typed into the instance (no command can type yet), so the typed-text case is not
measured here. Occurrences are plain substring counts over the whole of stderr.

| level | stderr lines | stdout bytes | `crud-surname` | `crud-name` | `back-btn` | `task-title` | `Emil` | `Mustermann` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `warn` (the default) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `info` | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `debug` | 1165 | 0 | 12 | 49 | 33 | 26 | 0 | 0 |
| `trace` | 1501 | 0 | 20 | 60 | 42 | 34 | 3 | 3 |

**Where the ids and names come from at `trace`** (the first probe run, 1501 lines: DEBUG 1164 · TRACE 336 ·
INFO 1; 1,104,899 bytes):

| needle | level | target | lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| `crud-surname` | DEBUG | `style::traversal` | 6 |
| `crud-surname` | DEBUG | `style::sharing` | 2 |
| `crud-surname` | TRACE | `style::traversal` | 4 |
| `crud-surname` | TRACE | `dioxus_core::diff::node` | 1 |
| `Emil` | TRACE | `dioxus_core::diff::node` | 3 |

The emitting targets are third-party crates — Stylo's `style::*` and `selectors::matching` through the `log`
bridge, and `dioxus_core::diff::node` — none of which is in the sink's `ENGINE_TARGET_PREFIXES`
(`packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs`), so their `message` and fields print as written. The windowed
`seven_guis_native` binary installs the same sink and boots the same components.

**Reading.** At the default level and at `info` the host's stderr holds no id and no name. At `debug` it holds
stable ids; at `trace` it also holds accessible names (a fixture row's text). stdout is empty at every level.
