# Merge record — 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship

Read 2026-10-13 by /andromeda-implement. The merge is staged, not committed: the operator's pre-CI commit records it with both parents.

## The pin
- Chunk start (HEAD): `a703136878e47c0cf583448bbac02f06f8365be5`.
- `git rev-parse upstream/main` read `434e06615d5f47a3df92c0f94e916df088fdcf4d`, which equals the pin, so upstream had not moved. Its subject is "Clip object-fit/object-position overflow of images to the content box (#1195)".
- The merge base is `7832c177ff272128154bac58afe56c2b9164b417`, the base the last sync merged. Upstream is 16 commits past it, with 45 files changed (+2147 −208).
- `git merge --no-ff --no-commit 434e06615d5f47a3df92c0f94e916df088fdcf4d` exited 1 on conflicts and left `MERGE_HEAD` = `434e06615d5f47a3df92c0f94e916df088fdcf4d`. The two resolved files were then staged with `git add`, and nothing was committed.

## The two conflicts
`git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` listed exactly the two paths the P3 trial merge predicted (tree `2481e052`), one region each:

1. `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs` — the `pub use events::{…}` line. **Both sides kept.** The line reads `pub use events::{NodeHandle, synthetic_click_event, synthetic_form_event};`, followed unchanged by our three `#[cfg(feature = "accessibility")]` re-exports (`snapshot`, `snapshot_diff`, `snapshot_text`).
2. `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/mutation_writer.rs` — the falsy-attribute line in `set_attribute_inner`. **Upstream's side taken:** `if is_falsy && is_bool_attr(local_name) {`.
   - Our `BOOLEAN_ATTRIBUTES` constant (27 names, from Dioxus 0.7.10's `isBoolAttr`) and its doc comment are deleted. The conflicted line was its one reference.
   - Upstream's `is_bool_attr` names 28 attributes: all 27 of ours plus `inert`, which is the one name it adds (`comm` of the two sorted lists: none of ours missing, `"inert"` added). A falsy `inert` is now cleared too.
   - The resolved file is byte-identical to upstream's at the pin (sha256 `e40d0a1e…` on both). Our only change to this file since `7832c177` was the constant and that line, so the file is fully de-forked.
   - `set_attribute_inner` is still the one site both attribute paths reach (the dynamic `set_attribute` arms and the static template path), so the clear covers both.

## Additivity — our edits beyond a conflict
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs` (step 6, +2 −11), the test `a_removed_element_reads_no_id`. Its premise changed with the merged engine (#1185 drops a Dioxus-removed node at removal).
  - Removed: the detached-parent assertion and the hand call to `remove_node_if_unparented`, which would now be handed a dropped id.
  - Now asserts that, after the re-render, the removed `p` no longer resolves (`get_node(removed)` is `None`), its `element_id` is `None`, and `element_ids()` lists no pair with it.
  - The test name and its first assertions stand.
- `Cargo.lock` (step 7): the `version` lines of `escher-driver` and `escher-telemetry`, `0.3.0-beta.2` → `0.3.0-beta.3`, by `cargo update --workspace` (see `lock.md`).
- `README.md` (step 8, our own front page, +1 −1 on line 48): eleven driver verbs, and the built screenshot.
- No other file of ours or upstream's was edited by hand. No gate went red, so step 10 made no fix.

## The standing difference in `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml`
`git diff 434e06615 -- tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml` after the merge shows that the difference is kept:
- Upstream's `autotests = false` stays absent.
- `[[test]] all` keeps `test = false` under its comment.
- Our dev-dependencies stand: `escher-telemetry`, `escher-driver`, `seven_guis`, `png`, `tracing`, `tracing-log`, and `dioxus-native-dom` with `accessibility`.
- Upstream's `cursor-icon` is merged beside them.
- `BlitzTestsTargetsTest` reads ok (gate entry 23).

# The bounded dpkg repair — CARRY 5, the operator's fork 4

## The change

`.github/scripts/apt-install.sh` gains `repair`, beside `bounded`: `sudo timeout --kill-after="$GRACE" "$BOUND"
dpkg --configure -a`, the same privilege, bound and kill grace as each `apt-get` call. `attempt_once` takes the
attempt's number and, on every attempt after the first, runs the repair first in phase `repair`; a failed
repair fails that attempt, and the existing diagnostic names it — `apt-install: attempt {n} of {N} failed in
repair (exit {status})`. The first attempt runs no repair, so a healthy install calls no `dpkg`. The usage
gate is unchanged and still exits 2 before `sudo`, `timeout`, `apt-get` or `dpkg` runs. The header comment
states the repair and why: a bound firing inside an install can leave dpkg interrupted.

## Its checks (`InstallScriptTest`, the `ci-scripts` leg)

title: evidence/stderr-by-level.py
body:
"""What escher's binaries write to stderr, by RUST_LOG level and by build. Counts only; report-only.

Run from the repository root:

    python3 escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-14-quality-gates/evidence/stderr-by-level.py

It builds twice, in turn, and measures each build before the next overwrites target/debug:

`alone`     — `cargo build -p seven_guis --locked`: the stand's own feature set, the engine's
              tracing call sites compiled out.
`workspace` — `cargo build --workspace --locked`: the binaries as the workspace builds them, the
              engine's tracing call sites compiled in.

Per build and per level (unset, info, debug, trace):

(a) `client` — the `escher-session` client's own stderr, each command run with RUST_LOG at the
    level, over one flow on CRUD: start · snapshot · click · type (a sentinel) · screenshot · stop.
    The host `start` spawns writes to /dev/null, so this is the client's alone.
(b) `host-counter`, `host-flight` — the host in its foreground role (`serve`), RUST_LOG at the level,
    stderr to a file, driven by the client (RUST_LOG unset) through the commands of
    examples/seven_guis/tests/flows/{counter,flight}.sh, then stopped.
(c) `windowed` — workspace build only: `timeout 10 target/debug/seven_guis_native`, on Home for 10 s,
    stderr to a file. The `timeout` this script starts ends it; no process is signalled by name.

For each run: stderr bytes and lines, lines by level and target, command-span lines, and the needle
counts — ids (every id holding a `-` that a snapshot answer of the run's task read), names (the
screen's texts of four characters or more), the typed sentinels, and the first 64 base64 characters
of the shot's PNG. State directories are relative, target/tmp/qg-*; every stream goes to
target/tmp/qg-streams/ and is removed. Nothing a binary wrote is printed.
"""
import collections
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time

BINARY = "target/debug/escher-session"
WINDOWED = "target/debug/seven_guis_native"
SCRATCH = "target/tmp/qg-streams"
LEVELS = ["(unset)", "info", "debug", "trace"]
BUILDS = [
    ("alone", ["cargo", "build", "-p", "seven_guis", "--locked"]),
    ("workspace", ["cargo", "build", "--workspace", "--locked"]),
]
LINE = re.compile(r"^\S+ (TRACE|DEBUG|INFO|WARN|ERROR) (\S+) ")
SENTINEL = "Typed-Sentinel-qg7Rm2"
ID = re.compile(r'id="([^"]+)"')
NAME = re.compile(r'^\s*\S+ "([^"]+)"', re.M)
HOME_NAMES = ["Temp Converter", "Flight Booker", "Circle Drawer", "Constraints", "Concurrency",
              "Reactivity", "List Ops", "Data Flow"]

CLIENT_FLOW = [
    ["start", "crud"],
    ["snapshot"],
    ["click", "--id", "crud-create"],
    ["type", "--id", "crud-name", "--text", SENTINEL],
    ["screenshot"],
    ["stop"],
]
FLOWS = {
    "counter": [
        ["snapshot"],
        ["click", "--id", "counter-increment"],
        ["snapshot"],
        ["click", "--id", "flow-names-no-element"],
        ["snapshot"],
    ],
    "flight-booker": [
        ["snapshot"],
        ["type", "--id", "flight-start", "--text", "next week"],
        ["click", "--id", "flight-book"],
        ["type", "--id", "flight-start", "--text", "24.12.2026"],
        ["click", "--id", "flight-book"],
    ],
}
TYPED = {"crud": [SENTINEL], "counter": [], "flight-booker": ["next week", "24.12.2026"]}


def env_at(level):
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.pop("RUST_LOG", None)
    if level != "(unset)":
        env["RUST_LOG"] = level
    return env


def client(args, state, level="(unset)", err=subprocess.DEVNULL):
    done = subprocess.run([BINARY, *args, "--session", state], env=env_at(level), timeout=90,
                          stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=err)
    return done.returncode, done.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")


def needles_of(answers):
    """Ids and names a snapshot answer read, and the shot's first 64 base64 characters."""
    ids, names, shot = set(), set(), None
    for answer in answers:
        try:
            value = json.loads(answer)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if isinstance(value.get("text"), str):
            ids.update(i for i in ID.findall(value["text"]) if "-" in i)
            names.update(n for n in NAME.findall(value["text"])
                         if len(n) >= 4 and any(c.isalpha() for c in n))
        if isinstance(value.get("png"), str):
            shot = value["png"][:64]
    return ids, names, shot


def count(path, ids, names, typed, shot):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        text = f.read()
    lines = text.splitlines()
    targets = collections.Counter()
    spans = 0
    for line in lines:
        m = LINE.match(line)
        targets[f"{m.group(1)} {m.group(2)}" if m else "(not the sink's line shape)"] += 1
        if m and m.group(2) == "escher_driver" and ' span="command"' in line:
            spans += 1
    return {
        "bytes": os.path.getsize(path),
        "lines": len(lines),
        "targets": " · ".join(f"{t} ×{n}" for t, n in sorted(targets.items())) or "none",
        "spans": spans,
        "ids": sum(1 for n in ids if n in text),
        "names": sum(1 for n in names if n in text),
        "typed": sum(text.count(t) for t in typed),
        "shot": text.count(shot) if shot else None,
    }


def report(build, level, run, detail, c, ids, names, typed, shot):
    shot_word = "no shot" if shot is None else f"{c['shot']}"
    print(f"| {build} | {run} | {level} | {c['bytes']} B · {c['lines']} | {c['targets']} | "
          f"{c['spans']} | {c['ids']} of {len(ids)} | {c['names']} of {len(names)} | "
          f"{c['typed']} of {len(typed)} sentinels | {shot_word} | {detail} |")
    sys.stdout.flush()


def run_client(build, level, tag):
    state = f"target/tmp/qg-c-{tag}"
    err_path = os.path.join(SCRATCH, f"client-{tag}.err")
    statuses, answers = [], []
    with open(err_path, "wb") as err:
        for command in CLIENT_FLOW:
            status, answer = client(command, state, level, err)
            statuses.append(status)
            answers.append(answer)
    if os.path.exists(state):
        client(["stop"], state)
    ids, names, shot = needles_of(answers)
    c = count(err_path, ids, names, TYPED["crud"], shot)
    detail = f"statuses {statuses} · state dir left {os.path.exists(state)}"
    report(build, level, "(a) client · crud", detail, c, ids, names, TYPED["crud"], shot)


def run_host(build, level, tag, task):
    state = f"target/tmp/qg-h-{tag}-{task[:6]}"
    err_path = os.path.join(SCRATCH, f"host-{tag}-{task}.err")
    out_path = os.path.join(SCRATCH, f"host-{tag}-{task}.out")
    with open(err_path, "wb") as err, open(out_path, "wb") as out:
        host = subprocess.Popen([BINARY, "serve", task, "--session", state], env=env_at(level),
                                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=out, stderr=err)
        deadline = time.time() + 60
        ready = False
        while time.time() < deadline and host.poll() is None:
            if os.path.exists(os.path.join(state, "session.sock")):
                ready = client(["status"], state)[0] == 0
                if ready:
                    break
            time.sleep(0.01)
        statuses, answers = [], []
        if ready:
            for command in FLOWS[task]:
                status, answer = client(command, state)
                statuses.append(status)
                answers.append(answer)
            client(["stop"], state)
        try:
            code = host.wait(timeout=15)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            host.kill()
            code = host.wait()
    ids, names, shot = needles_of(answers)
    c = count(err_path, ids, names, TYPED[task], shot)
    detail = (f"host exit {code} · statuses {statuses} · stdout {os.path.getsize(out_path)} B · "
              f"state dir left {os.path.exists(state)}")
    report(build, level, f"(b) host · {task}", detail, c, ids, names, TYPED[task], shot)
    return ids, names


def run_windowed(build, level, tag, ids, names):
    err_path = os.path.join(SCRATCH, f"windowed-{tag}.err")
    with open(err_path, "wb") as err:
        app = subprocess.Popen(["timeout", "10", WINDOWED], env=env_at(level),
                               stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=err)
        try:
            code = app.wait(timeout=40)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            app.kill()
            code = app.wait()
    all_names = names | set(HOME_NAMES)
    c = count(err_path, ids, all_names, [], None)
    report(build, level, "(c) windowed · home", f"exit {code} (124: ended by its timeout)", c,
           ids, all_names, [], None)


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 1:
        sys.exit("usage: stderr-by-level.py")
    print("| build | run | RUST_LOG | stderr | lines by level and target | command spans | ids | "
          "names | typed | shot base64 | run |")
    print("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for build, command in BUILDS:
        built = subprocess.run(command, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                               stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        print(f"| {build} | build | `{' '.join(command)}` exit {built.returncode} | | | | | | | | |")
        sys.stdout.flush()
        if built.returncode != 0:
            sys.exit(1)
        os.makedirs(SCRATCH, exist_ok=True)
        for level in LEVELS:
            tag = f"{build[0]}{level.strip('()')[0]}"
            run_client(build, level, tag)
            all_ids, all_names = set(), set()
            for task in FLOWS:
                ids, names = run_host(build, level, tag, task)
                all_ids |= ids
                all_names |= names
            if build == "workspace":
                run_windowed(build, level, tag, all_ids, all_names)
        shutil.rmtree(SCRATCH)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

title: evidence/log-counts.py
body:
"""What the `escher-session` host and its `mcp` role write to stderr while they run one CRUD flow,
at RUST_LOG `info` and `trace`, under both builds. Counts only. Report-only: it grades nothing.

Run from the repository root:

    python3 escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep/evidence/log-counts.py

It builds the binary twice, in turn, and measures each build before the next overwrites it (both
write target/debug/escher-session):

`alone`     — `cargo build -p seven_guis --bin escher-session --locked`: the stand's own feature
              set, the engine's tracing call sites compiled out.
`workspace` — `cargo build --workspace --locked`: the engine's tracing call sites compiled in.

The host flow is 2026-10-10-driver-cli's by-level procedure: the host in its foreground role on
CRUD, three commands through the binary as a client with RUST_LOG unset — a `snapshot`, a `click`
on Create and a `type` of a sentinel into the name field — then `stop`. The `mcp` flow is
2026-10-10-mcp-surface's: `initialize`, then tool calls `start crud`, `snapshot`, `type` into
`crud-name`, `click crud-create`, `stop`, fed on the role's stdin, its stdout drained on a thread.

Each run's streams go to files under target/tmp/log-counts/, are counted, and are removed. Nothing
a binary wrote is printed: per run, the stderr's lines and bytes, its lines per level and target,
the `command` and `tool_call` span lines, the id and name needles found, and the sentinel's
occurrences.
"""
import collections
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time

BINARY = "target/debug/escher-session"
SCRATCH = "target/tmp/log-counts"
LEVELS = ["info", "trace"]
BUILDS = [
    ("alone", ["cargo", "build", "-p", "seven_guis", "--bin", "escher-session", "--locked"]),
    ("workspace", ["cargo", "build", "--workspace", "--locked"]),
]
LINE = re.compile(r"^\S+ (TRACE|DEBUG|INFO|WARN|ERROR) (\S+) service\.name=")
SENTINEL = "Typed-Sentinel-40pXgd"

IDS = ["task-shell", "task-header", "back-btn", "task-title", "task-body", "crud-filter",
       "crud-list", "crud-name", "crud-surname", "crud-create", "crud-update", "crud-delete",
       "crud-person-0", "crud-person-1", "crud-person-2"]
NAMES = ["Emil, Hans", "Mustermann, Max", "Tisch, Roman", "Filter prefix:", "Name:", "Surname:",
         "People"]
COMMANDS = [
    ["snapshot"],
    ["click", "--id", "crud-create"],
    ["type", "--id", "crud-name", "--text", SENTINEL],
]
TOOL_CALLS = [
    ("start", {"app": "crud"}),
    ("snapshot", {}),
    ("type", {"id": "crud-name", "text": SENTINEL}),
    ("click", {"id": "crud-create"}),
    ("stop", {}),
]


def env_at(level):
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env["RUST_LOG"] = level
    return env


def client(args, state):
    """One command through the binary as a client, RUST_LOG unset: its status."""
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.pop("RUST_LOG", None)
    done = subprocess.run([BINARY, *args, "--session", state], env=env, timeout=60,
                          stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True)
    return done.returncode


def host_flow(level, err, out, tag):
    state = f"target/tmp/lc-{tag}"
    host = subprocess.Popen([BINARY, "serve", "crud", "--session", state], env=env_at(level),
                            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=out, stderr=err)
    deadline = time.time() + 60
    answered = False
    while time.time() < deadline and host.poll() is None:
        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(state, "session.sock")):
            answered = client(["status"], state) == 0
            if answered:
                break
        time.sleep(0.01)
    statuses = []
    if answered:
        statuses = [client(command, state) for command in COMMANDS]
        client(["stop"], state)
    try:
        code = host.wait(timeout=10)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        host.kill()
        code = host.wait()
    return code, f"client statuses {statuses} · state dir left {os.path.exists(state)}"


def mcp_flow(level, err, out, tag):
    role = subprocess.Popen([BINARY, "mcp"], env=env_at(level), stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
                            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=err)
    answers = []

    def drain():
        for line in role.stdout:
            out.write(line)
            answers.append(line)

    reader = threading.Thread(target=drain)
    reader.start()
    requests = [{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "initialize",
                 "params": {"protocolVersion": "2025-11-25", "capabilities": {},
                            "clientInfo": {"name": "log-counts", "version": "0"}}},
                {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"}]
    for n, (tool, arguments) in enumerate(TOOL_CALLS, start=2):
        requests.append({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": n, "method": "tools/call",
                         "params": {"name": tool, "arguments": arguments}})
    expected = 1 + len(TOOL_CALLS)
    for request in requests:
        role.stdin.write((json.dumps(request) + "\n").encode())
        role.stdin.flush()
        if "id" in request:
            deadline = time.time() + 30
            while len(answers) < request["id"] and time.time() < deadline:
                time.sleep(0.01)
    role.stdin.close()
    try:
        code = role.wait(timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        role.kill()
        code = role.wait()
    reader.join(timeout=5)
    errors = sum(1 for line in answers if b'"isError":true' in line)
    return code, f"stdout lines {len(answers)} of {expected} · isError {errors}"


def count(build, flow, level, run):
    tag = f"{build}-{flow}-{level}"
    err_path = os.path.join(SCRATCH, f"{tag}.err")
    out_path = os.path.join(SCRATCH, f"{tag}.out")
    with open(err_path, "wb") as err, open(out_path, "wb") as out:
        code, detail = run(level, err, out, tag)
    with open(err_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        text = f.read()
    lines = text.splitlines()
    targets = collections.Counter()
    spans = collections.Counter()
    ids = set()
    names = set()
    for line in lines:
        m = LINE.match(line)
        targets[f"{m.group(1)} {m.group(2)}" if m else "(not the sink's line shape)"] += 1
        for span in ("command", "tool_call"):
            if m and m.group(2) == "escher_driver" and f' span="{span}"' in line:
                spans[span] += 1
        ids.update(needle for needle in IDS if needle in line)
        names.update(needle for needle in NAMES if needle in line)
    print(f"## {build} · {flow} · RUST_LOG {level} · exit {code} · {detail}")
    print(f"   stderr {os.path.getsize(err_path)} B · {len(lines)} lines · command {spans['command']}"
          f" · tool_call {spans['tool_call']} · id needles {len(ids)} of {len(IDS)} · name "
          f"needles {len(names)} of {len(NAMES)} · sentinel {text.count(SENTINEL)}")
    print("   targets: " + (" · ".join(f"{t} ×{n}" for t, n in sorted(targets.items())) or "none"))
    sys.stdout.flush()


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 1:
        sys.exit("usage: log-counts.py")
    for build, command in BUILDS:
        built = subprocess.run(command, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                               stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        print(f"# build {build}: {' '.join(command)} · exit {built.returncode}")
        sys.stdout.flush()
        if built.returncode != 0:
            sys.exit(1)
        os.makedirs(SCRATCH, exist_ok=True)
        for level in LEVELS:
            count(build, "host", level, host_flow)
            count(build, "mcp", level, mcp_flow)
        shutil.rmtree(SCRATCH)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

title: evidence/complexity.py
body:
"""Reads `rust-code-analysis-cli -m -O json` output the way the version-end audit did.

Every space of kind `function` (closures included) is measured by `metrics.cognitive.sum`
(`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-15T10-44-59-code-audit/record.json`, `commands.complexity`). One line
is printed per function at or over 16, `{file}:{start_line} {name} {cognitive}`, then
`over-ceiling: {names}` in ascending byte order. Exit 1 when a parent handler reads its HEAD
figure or more (`handle_click` 74, `handle_pointerdown` 40, `handle_key_or_input_event` 56),
2 on a usage error, else 0.
"""

import json
import os
import sys

CEILING = 15
HEAD_FIGURES = {
    "handle_click": 74,
    "handle_pointerdown": 40,
    "handle_key_or_input_event": 56,
}


def functions(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        root = json.load(f)
    stack = [root]
    while stack:
        space = stack.pop()
        stack.extend(space.get("spaces", []))
        if space["kind"] == "function":
            yield (root["name"], space["start_line"], space.get("name"),
                   space["metrics"]["cognitive"]["sum"])


def main(argv):
    if len(argv) != 2 or not os.path.isdir(argv[1]):
        print("usage: complexity.py <rust-code-analysis-cli json directory>")
        return 2
    found = []
    for dirpath, _, filenames in os.walk(argv[1]):
        for filename in filenames:
            if filename.endswith(".json"):
                found.extend(functions(os.path.join(dirpath, filename)))
    found.sort(key=lambda fn: (fn[0], fn[1]))

    over = [fn for fn in found if fn[3] > CEILING]
    for file, line, name, cognitive in over:
        print(f"{file}:{line} {name} {cognitive:g}")
    names = sorted((fn[2] for fn in over), key=lambda name: name.encode("utf-8"))
    print("over-ceiling: " + " ".join(names))

    at_head = [fn for fn in found if fn[2] in HEAD_FIGURES and fn[3] >= HEAD_FIGURES[fn[2]]]
    return 1 if at_head else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

title: I5-fork-ownership-founder-vs-operator.md.txt

---
name: fork-ownership-founder-vs-operator
description: "In escher, which planning forks go to the founder and which are the operator's — a P4 fork changing engine behaviour for every document is the founder's (playbook :64); how far a ruled fix reaches, and consequences of his answers, are the operator's"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 6d3afa93-e4d4-4bd9-9918-a724b944116a
  modified: 2026-10-13T20:20:33.155Z
---

In escher's /andromeda-phase, a fork that only decides **how far a fix the founder has already ruled reaches**, inside a principle he already set, is a **technical fork — the operator's**, asked in the dialog. It does not go into the founder's forks file.

What happened (2026-10-10, chunk `2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit`): I put two forks into `p4-founder-forks.md` — which boxes stop a hit at their edge, and whether a second engine reader with the same defect is left, measured or fixed — reasoning that each was "a behaviour change for every document". The operator answered both himself at the P5 review and said the placement was wrong: neither widens a boundary nor changes what the project is for.

**Why:** the founder has a standing delegation of technical decisions to the operator. His own word is needed for a boundary widening (something new crossing a hardened boundary), for what an agent meets changing beyond what was ruled, and for what the project is for — not for the reach of an engine fix he already ruled, even when that fix changes behaviour for every document.

**Correction (2026-10-13, chunk `2026-10-13-range-input-interaction`):** I put three P4 forks that shape an engine
change for every document (where a range value lives, which keys step it, whether a click focuses) to the operator as
"technical forks within the founder's ruling". The overseer routed all three to the founder instead, citing the
playbook rule "An engine behaviour change for every document" (`.andromeda/playbook.md:64`): it is routine only "on
the founder's own word at that chunk's P4 fork". The founder answered, one answer against my recommendation. So a P4
fork whose options each change engine behaviour for every document is the founder's, asked as a dialog the overseer
relays. The operator then confirmed my leans that followed from his answers (form submission, re-seed on attribute
write, pointer-down vs click) "as consequences of the founder's own answers, not new forks" — those stay the operator's.

**How to apply:** before writing a fork for the founder, ask whether he has already ruled the change itself and set its principle. If yes, and no boundary widens, put the fork to the operator in the dialog with a marked recommendation. When unsure, ask the operator whose it is rather than routing it to the founder and planning on the narrowest option — that cost a full extra review round here. My interpretation: the playbook's "behaviour change for every document" clause is about a change with no ruling behind it, not about the extent of a ruled one.

When a chunk leaves an edited code path with no check, the route owner for that owed check is the earliest markerless entry that plausibly takes it — not the catch-all "Quality gates" entry near the route's end.

**What happened (2026-10-10, the wrap of 2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit):** I proposed "Quality gates" for two unchecked paths (a box both transformed and scrolled; a scrolled box under a vertical writing mode). **Why:** a check owed on code that already shipped should be written as soon as an entry can take it; an entry late in the route leaves the path unchecked for longer.

**How to apply:** when proposing owners at a wrap's P5, order the candidate entries by position and lean to the first one whose scope fits, saying why. My interpretation, not the operator's words: this is about owed checks on shipped code, not about every open finding — a decision question ("does the fork gate on licences") can still belong on the entry that decides that class. # Lock — `Cargo.lock` resolved at the pin

## The conflict
One region, in the `blitz-tests` package's dependency list: ours listed `escher-driver`, `escher-telemetry` and
`keyboard-types 0.7.0`; upstream `keyboard-types 0.8.3`. Resolved to `escher-driver`, `escher-telemetry`,
`keyboard-types 0.8.3` — our two workspace dependents kept, upstream's keyboard-types taken (the workspace moves to
"0.8" with the merged `Cargo.toml`). Every other lock hunk auto-merged.

## The refresh (plan step 4)
- `cargo metadata --locked` on the resolved lock: exit 101 (`cannot update the lock file … because --locked was
  passed`) — the two `escher-*` entries still read `0.3.0-beta.3` beside a `0.3.0-beta.4` workspace.
- `cargo update -p escher-driver -p escher-telemetry`: exit 0, `Locking 2 packages`, `escher-driver v0.3.0-beta.3 …
  -> v0.3.0-beta.4`, `escher-telemetry v0.3.0-beta.3 … -> v0.3.0-beta.4`. `diff` of the lock before and after this
  call: the two `version` lines alone (lock lines 3094 and 3105).
- `cargo metadata --locked` after it: exit 0. It downloaded `test-that` 0.6.0 and `test-that-macro` 0.6.0.

## The set against the pin
The name@version set of the lock, `escher-*` entries set aside, against `git show 23b9b26a9:Cargo.lock`: `diff`
exit 0, no output — no third-party package enters, leaves or moves beyond upstream's set.

Against HEAD `143b6013`'s lock (whole set): the eleven in-repo packages and our two `escher-*` go 0.3.0-beta.3 →
0.3.0-beta.4; `bump` 0.0.0, `toml_datetime` 0.6.11, `toml_edit` 0.22.27 and `toml_write` 0.1.2 leave; `test-that` and
`test-that-macro` go 0.5.2 → 0.6.0. Nothing else moves (`syn` 3.0.6, the macro's dependency, was in the lock at HEAD).

## `test-that` / `test-that-macro` 0.6.0, reviewed by hand
Read from the registry sources cargo unpacked (`~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/test-that{,-macro}-0.6.0/Cargo.toml`):

| Crate | Licence | Repository | Build script | proc-macro | Dependencies (lock) | Direct dependent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `test-that` 0.6.0 | Apache-2.0 (0.5.2: the same) | https://github.com/hovinen/test-that (the same) | none — `build = false`, no `build.rs` | no | `num-traits`, `regex`, `test-that-macro` | `blitz-tests` (dev-dependency, `tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml:39`, workspace `test-that = "0.6.0"` at `Cargo.toml:198`) |
| `test-that-macro` 0.6.0 | Apache-2.0 (the same) | the same | none — `build = false`, no `build.rs` | yes (as 0.5.2) | `quote`, `syn` 3.0.6 | `test-that` |

licence is in `deny.toml`'s allow list as before (the audit entry reads `licenses ok`).

and `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs` (both-sides files), the rest upstream's alone. git printed `Recorded
preimage` for both conflicts (the host has `rerere` on); no recorded resolution was replayed.

Staged by the merge: `Cargo.toml` · `justfile` · `apps/bump/{Cargo.toml,src/main.rs}` (deleted) ·
`packages/blitz-dom/src/{events/keyboard.rs,layout/inline.rs,node/text.rs,util.rs}` ·
`packages/blitz-shell/src/convert_events.rs` · `packages/blitz-vibey-script/{src/dom/element.rs,src/runtime.rs,tests/preact.rs}` ·
`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/{events.rs,keyboard_compat.rs (new),lib.rs}` ·
`tests/blitz-tests/tests/{accessibility_description.rs (new),accessibility_label.rs (new),all.rs}`.

## `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs` — the five regions (cited by symbol; the trial's line numbers move)

| Region | Ours (HEAD) | Upstream (`23b9b26a9`) | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — the `use` lines | `crate::{BaseDocument, ElementData, Node as BlitzDomNode, local_name}`; `accesskit::{Invalid, …, Toggled, …}` | `crate::{…, NodeData, NodeId as BlitzDomNodeId, local_name}`; `accesskit::{…}` without `Invalid`/`Toggled` | union: upstream's `crate` line, our `accesskit` line |
| 2 — `build_accessibility_tree`'s collections | `let mut labels` | `let mut labelled_by_nodes`, `let mut described_by_nodes` | all three, ours first |
| 3 — the visit | `label` element → `labels.push` | `aria-labelledby` holder → `labelled_by_nodes.push`; `aria-describedby` holder → `described_by_nodes.push` | all three `if`s, ours first |
| 4 — after the visit | the label → input `push_labelled_by` loop | the `aria-labelledby` loop (`clear_labelled_by`, push targets, `write_text_alternative`, computed `set_label`); the `aria-describedby` loop (`push_described_by`) | ours, then upstream's two loops as written — so `aria-labelledby` (accname 2B) outranks a native `<label>` (2D) |
| 5 — `build_accessibility_node` | the closed-set trimmed `aria-selected` · `aria-pressed` · `aria-invalid` reads | `aria-expanded` · `aria-disabled` · `aria-selected` (`parse::<bool>`) · `aria-label` (unfiltered) · `aria-description` · `aria-level` with tag/role defaults · `set_html_tag` | ours kept; upstream's `aria-expanded`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-description`, `aria-level` (+ defaults) and `set_html_tag` (last) kept as written; **dropped:** upstream's `aria-selected` read (`if let Some(aria_selected) … parse() … set_selected`) and its `aria-label` read (`if let Some(aria_label) … set_label(aria_label)`) |

Outside the regions, and unchanged: our trimmed non-empty `aria-label` read (accname 2C) in `build_accessibility_node`;
upstream's helpers `referenced_dom_ids_to_node_ids`, `BlitzDomNode::write_text_alternative`,
`BlitzDomNode::write_flat_text_content`, `FlatText`, `default_level_for_tag`, `default_level_for_role`, as upstream
wrote them. `label_bound_input_element` is still called from the builder's label loop.

The two drops change no outcome (research.md §Patterns detected): upstream's strict `parse::<bool>` decides a subset
of ours with the same value, and its unfiltered `aria-label` differs from ours only on a blank label, which our
ratified contract names nothing (a11y-plan §7) and no upstream test asserts.

Result: 0 conflict markers (`command grep -n -E '^(<<<<<<<|=======|>>>>>>>)'`: no hit), `rustfmt --edition 2024
--check` exit 0.

title: I2-founder-forks.md.txt
body:
# Founder forks — 2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock («One virtual clock», v020-06)

The founder is away. The operator answers these in his stead (inputs#I1), and each answer is recorded as a delegate's, PROVISIONAL, for the founder's epoch-boundary batch (`.andromeda/playbook.md`, «Provisional discharge»). Each fork below is his because it changes what the engine does for every document, or what an agent meets. None of the options widens a boundary: no new carrier, verb, argument, field, log field or exit. The evidence for each claim is in `escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock/research.md` and `scope.md`.

Answer with one letter per fork (e.g. `F1 B · F2 A · F2b A · F3 A`). A free-text answer is fine too.

---

## F1 — Where a document's time comes from

**The fork.** The engine reads the wall clock directly in five places: the overlay scrollbar fade (`packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:1870,1879,1887`, `resolve.rs:71`), double-click detection (`events/pointer.rs:394-407`), the smooth-scroll start and frame (`scrolling.rs:515,896`), the fling frame (`scrolling.rs:871`) and pan timing (`pointer.rs:267,717`). The requirement is that in a headless run all of them read one clock that only the driver moves. CSS animations and transitions already read the time `resolve(time)` is handed (`stylo.rs:135`); the harness hands its own `time`, and the windowed shell hands wall seconds (`blitz-shell/src/window.rs:280-302`).

- **A — One document clock for every document: `resolve`'s time.** The document keeps the time its last `resolve` was handed, and every read above takes it. Activity is stamped at the next `resolve`, so the fade starts from the next frame rather than the event's instant. Windowed documents change too: the fade measures from frame times, and double-click compares the frame times of two clicks. An idle window that has not resolved between two clicks can read them as nearer together than they were.
  - *Engine change for every document:* yes, windowed included.
  - *Merge surface:* `document.rs`, `resolve.rs`, `events/pointer.rs`, `scrolling.rs`. A CARRY on «Upstream sync ahead of visual lint and real-app readiness».
  - *Risk:* windowed double-click and fade timing move off the event instant. That needs a windowed check this chunk does not have (the stand's windowed binary is measured only for the log needles).
- **B — A clock the embedder supplies, the wall clock by default (Recommended).** `DocumentConfig` gains one optional clock provider, on the same `Option<Arc<dyn …>>` shape as its net, navigation and shell providers (`config.rs:31-60`). With none supplied it reads `web_time::Instant`, exactly what every read does today. Every read above goes through it. The harness supplies a virtual clock whose time is the harness's own `time`, so `resolve(time)` and the engine's reads are one clock, moved by `tick` and the driver's `advance`.
  - *Engine change for every document:* an API addition. With no clock supplied, behaviour is unchanged: the same reads, now taken through the default.
  - *Merge surface:* as A, plus `config.rs` and a new `clock.rs`. A CARRY on the same upstream-sync entry.
  - *Why recommended:* it meets the requirement headlessly, which is the requirement's scope ("in a headless run"). It leaves the windowed engine as it is, and it follows the embedder-services pattern the architecture records ("Embedder services are injected, with no-op defaults").
- **C — The fade alone, through a harness override.** The harness pins the fade's clock, and every other read stays on the wall clock.
  - *Engine change for every document:* none beyond a test hook.
  - *What it fails:* "every time the engine reads". Double-click stays on the wall clock, and that does move driver readings (F3), so v020-06 could not be claimed whole.

**Dependences:** F3's options read "the one clock" as F1 defines it. Under F1 C, F3 can only be C. Under B, which technical reads move with the fade (all five, or the fade and double-click) is a technical fork for the operator. Under A, every moved read is a windowed change and so the founder's.

---

## F2 — What `advance` moves

**The fork.** Today `advance --ms N` hands N to the session's time step alone — only the Timer's session gets one. It reports `advanced_ms` as the time delivered to the app (`execute.rs:175-187`; whole 100 ms Timer ticks with the remainder dropped, so 250 reads 200 and 99 reads 0). The harness's clock stays where it was (`stand.rs:90-93`), and any other session refuses `advance` as `time-unavailable`. With nothing moving the instance's clock, a scrollbar thumb shown by a driver `scroll` would never fade, which fails v020-06's second clause ("the fade moves only when the driver advances time").

- **A — `advance` moves the held instance's one clock on every session (Recommended).** The clock moves by exactly N. The app's time step, where the session's caller handed one, then receives N. `advanced_ms` reads the clock's move, always N.
  - The stand's Timer step carries the sub-tick remainder, so the Timer reads the one clock: 250 then 250 shows 0.5 s, where today it shows 0.4 s. That is a stand change: `timer_step`, with its unit-test rows moving.
  - `advance` then answers on counter, flight booker and CRUD too, and `time-unavailable` is never returned (F2b).
  - *What an agent meets:* `advance` works on every task, and `advanced_ms` always equals the milliseconds asked.
  - *Checks that move:* `host_timer` (250 → `advanced_ms` 250), `cli_commands`, `stand_act_timer` (its "the animation clock is where it was" assertions become "the clock moved by N"), `stand_act_spans` and `stand_mcp_tools` (a refused `advance` becomes accepted, its `tool_call` `ending` `accepted`).
- **B — `advance` moves the clock only on a session handed a time step.** The stand host and the checks' `hold` hand every lean task a step (a clock-only step for the three that have no app time). A library session given none still refuses `time-unavailable`, so "all nine causes are returned by code" stays true. `advanced_ms` keeps its meaning, the time delivered to the app: the Timer keeps whole ticks with the remainder dropped, and the other tasks read N.
  - *What an agent meets:* the same `advance` on every stand task, the Timer's readings unchanged.
  - *Cost:* the Timer's app time and the engine's clock drift apart by the dropped remainder (250 moves the clock 250 and the Timer 200). The app's time is then not strictly the one clock.
- **C — Leave `advance` as it is.** In a driver session nothing moves the instance's clock: a thumb shown by a scroll stays at full opacity until the session ends. The repeat-shot half of v020-06 holds, but "the fade moves only when the driver advances time" cannot, so the cap could not be claimed whole.

**Dependences:** F2b exists only under A. Under B or C, `time-unavailable` stays as it is.

### F2b — What becomes of `time-unavailable` (under F2 A)
- **A — Retire it (Recommended).** The refusal set closes at eight causes. `help`, the self-description and the MCP listing stop naming it, and "every cause is returned by code" stays true at eight.
  - *What an agent meets:* one fewer refusal, and every one it reads in `help` can actually occur.
  - *Ripple (code):* `refusal.rs`, `execute.rs`, the schema's cause table and its pins, `stand_act_spans` (its `cause="time-unavailable"` line), `stand_act_timer`, `stand_mcp_tools`, `cli_commands`.
  - *Ripple (docs, at the wrap):* the count "nine" in CLAUDE.md, the architecture, the security, obs and test plans, and the leaves.
- **B — Keep it in the table, never returned.** The cause set stays nine, and the recorded fact becomes "eight of nine returned by code". An agent reading `help` meets a cause it can never be given, against the tool's rule that it states its own limits truly (2026-10-10-driver-cli).

---

## F3 — Two driver clicks on one point, on the one clock

**The fork.** The engine counts a second mousedown within 500 ms and 2 px as click 2 (`pointer.rs:394-407`). Click 2 selects the word in a text field (`pointer.rs:548-556`), selects all in a password field (`pointer.rs:647-651`) and sends the app a `DoubleClick` (`pointer.rs:968-974`); the stand's Circle Drawer opens its dialog on one (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/circle_drawer.rs:72`). Today wall time decides, so two driver `click`s on a text field read differently by how fast the agent sends them. On a clock only the driver moves, two clicks with no `advance` between them are 0 ms apart.

- **A — The double-click window reads the one clock (Recommended).** A second `click` on the same point within 500 ms of the session's time is a double click, whatever wall time passes. Two single clicks need an `advance` of at least 500 ms between them. `click`'s help says so, in the program's own fixed text inside the ratified carrier.
  - *What an agent meets:* deterministic clicks. Clicking a button twice still runs its click handler twice (the counter increments twice), now plus a `DoubleClick` the app may ignore. A second click on a text field selects the word, and Circle Drawer's dialog opens by two clicks as it does by hand today.
  - *Checks:* `stand_non_lean_tasks.rs:82` and `password_caret_click.rs:107` become deterministic rather than wall-window-dependent; their comments are restated.
- **B — Every driver `click` lands as a first click.** The session resets the count before each click. Deterministic, but a double click is unreachable through the driver: Circle Drawer's dialog cannot be opened by an agent, and a second click on a text field never selects a word.
- **C — Leave the double-click window on the wall clock.** Two driver clicks still read by how fast they arrive. This fails "every time the engine reads", so v020-06's requirement is met for the fade alone. The limit is stated in `click`'s help.

**Dependences:** under F1 B, the window reads the document's clock: virtual in a harness, the wall clock in a window, so windowed double-click is unchanged. Under F1 A, it reads frame times in every document. Under F1 C, only C is open.

---

**Recommendation in one line:** `F1 B · F2 A · F2b A · F3 A`. The headless engine reads one clock, the driver's `advance` moves it on every task, the refusal set stays truthful at eight, and two clicks are a double click by the session's time. Windowed behaviour is untouched.

---

## Answer (the operator, as the founder's delegate — PROVISIONAL, 2026-10-18T07:36Z)

Verbatim:

> Founder forks, answered in his stead (delegate operator, PROVISIONAL): F1 B · F2 A · F2b A · F3 A, each the recommended option for the reason the file argues (B keeps the windowed engine unchanged; the refusal set stays truthful at eight; two clicks read by the session time). Record them in founder-forks.md and go on with P4 and P5.

| Fork | Answer | Authority | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 — where a document's time comes from | B — a clock the embedder supplies through `DocumentConfig`, wall by default; the harness supplies a virtual clock | delegate operator | PROVISIONAL, for the founder's epoch batch |
| F2 — what `advance` moves | A — the held instance's one clock on every session, by exactly the milliseconds asked; `advanced_ms` reads that move; the Timer's step carries its remainder | delegate operator | PROVISIONAL |
| F2b — `time-unavailable` | A — retired; the refusal set closes at eight causes | delegate operator | PROVISIONAL |
| F3 — two driver clicks on one point | A — the double-click window reads the one clock | delegate operator | PROVISIONAL |

The technical forks, answered by the operator in the P4 dialog (2026-10-18): one 800 ms sleep between the two shots, the no-sleep rule's single recorded exception; the proof on the stand's CRUD list, in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_virtual_clock.rs`; all five engine reads (fade, double click, smooth-scroll start and frame, fling frame, pan times) through the document's clock.

body:
# Founder forks — 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay («Recorded-check replay», v020-04)

Phase P4 of `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-19T07-10-33-phase/`. On the operator's directive (inputs#I1, `relay-1.md`),
every fork that is the founder's is written here: its options whole, its dependences, a marked recommendation, and
the option that widens least named as such. There is one.

**What is already his and settled.** The founder widened F3 to B on 2026-10-19
(`escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-19-session-recording/inputs/I4-relay-1.md.txt`). A kept check now keeps each answer
whole, as the driver wrote it, under an `answer` key after `digest`. It is masked as on every carrier, and a shot keeps
its size but never its pixels. That widening is at rest in the owner-only file of F1 A: `check-{n}.json`, `0600`, in
a `0700` directory the launcher names. This chunk carries it out, and it goes on this chunk's wrap card as ratified.
It is not asked again here.

**Why the fork below is his.** v020-04's acceptance asks for recorded checks to run «as ordinary tests in CI»,
passing on the unchanged app and failing when its behaviour changes, «with no hand edit of the recording». The
natural form is a kept check committed to the repository as test input. But a committed file is not owner-only. It
sits in git as an ordinary file, and it is pushed to `Turbolet85/escher`, which is a **public** repository
(`gh repo view`: `"visibility":"PUBLIC"`). The security plan today keeps every kept check owner-only (§Data
Protection, «Files (kept checks)»). A kept check's content on a medium never ratified is what the playbook's
«Boundary widening» pattern names (verdict `escalate`). So whether a kept check may live in the repository is his
call, not the operator's.

**What research measured** (`escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay/research.md`):
- A replay target named `stand_*` in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/` is picked up, with no script change, by
  `agent-run.sh run stand` (`scripts/agent-run.sh:181-185`), by the `stand-repeat` leg's glob
  (`.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh:50-52`), and by the CI `test` leg on linux, windows and macos.
- The binary's command line and its `mcp` role already keep byte-identical checks of one script
  (`examples/seven_guis/tests/recording.rs:143-144`). A committed check can therefore be re-recorded by the binary and
  compared byte for byte. That comparison is the proof of «no hand edit».
- The stand's screen readings are already in the public repository as committed evidence: the cold-agent pipe's
  `escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-15-cold-agent-test/evidence/live-check.json` and two host-path-masked transcripts. They
  hold stand ids, names and values. A stand task's ids, names and fixed text are in its own source.

---

## F1 — Where the checks that CI replays come from: committed to the repository, or recorded inside each test run

Either way, these things are the same:
- The `answer` key (F3 B) lands in the owner-only recorder.
- Replay runs every kept call through `Session::run`, which validates first.
- A test-only variant of a stand task proves that a replay reads red when behaviour changes, naming the step and the
  answer keys that differ. A red names only a step index and closed schema words, never what a screen reads.

**A. Two checks committed to the repository, written by the binary and never edited. (Recommended)**
- **What is committed.** One check recorded through the command line (`escher-session start <task> --record`) and one
  through the `mcp` role (`escher-session mcp --record`). Each is a short scripted session on a lean stand task.
  Both are committed byte for byte as the binary wrote them, under `tests/blitz-tests/checks/`.
  - **What they hold:** the calls (ids, keys, `advance` ms, and only the script's own synthetic typed text) and each
    answer whole (ids, names, values, snapshot text and diffs of the stand's own screens). A shot keeps no pixels.
  - **What they never hold:** a password's text, a user's session, or a host path. The scripts type into no masked
    control, and any masked `type` keeps the fixed stand-in.
- **What runs.**
  - A `stand_replay` target replays both checks on freshly booted stand sessions in both layout modes. It reads green
    while the stand holds.
  - The target reads red, at the step that changed, against the variant.
  - A seven_guis process check records the same two scripts through the binary again and compares the bytes with the
    committed files. That proves they are current and unedited.
- **What it buys.** These are real regression checks, matching the entry's «failing when the UI's behaviour changes».
  A later chunk that changes a lean task's behaviour turns them red until someone deliberately re-records them, and
  the red says which step changed and which keys differ.
- **What widens.** A kept check's content gets a new at-rest medium: a world-readable file in a public git
  repository, not `0600` in `0700`. The content is the stand's own fixed screens plus a test script's synthetic text,
  the same class already committed as cold-agent evidence. The rule «every kept check is owner-only» then gains a
  stated exception: a check the repository itself records of its own stand, as test input. A check a launcher
  records of any other session stays owner-only and is never committed.
- **Why it is recommended.** It is the only option where a replay can turn red because the code changed between two
  commits, which is v020-04's purpose. What it puts at rest is already public: the stand's source and its committed
  evidence. No user content can reach it, because the committed files are only ever the two scripted stand sessions,
  and a byte-equality check refuses any other content.
- **Dependences.**
  - Arch §Occupied Resources gains the `tests/blitz-tests/checks/` registration.
  - The security plan's §Data Protection «Files (kept checks)» and obs-plan §9's «Recording directory» row gain the
    committed-check exception.
  - Cross-OS determinism is unmeasured. The CI run on windows and macos is its first reading. If a reading such as a
    sub-pixel bound differs by OS, the committed scripts keep to steps that hold everywhere, and the limit is recorded.

**B. No committed check: each test records its session at run time, then replays it.**
- Each replay test drives a scripted session with recording on, into an owner-only directory under `target/tmp/`
  (`0700` / `0600`, as today). The CLI case runs through the binary (seven_guis). The MCP case runs through the `mcp`
  role or `serve_mcp` in process. The test then reads the check back, replays it on a fresh session (green) and on
  the variant (red).
- **What widens:** nothing. Every kept check stays owner-only and local, as the founder's F1 A set it. Nothing new
  rests in the repository.
- **What it costs.**
  - The recording and its replay always run on the same code, so a real behaviour change between commits re-records
    itself and stays green. Only the in-test variant ever reads red.
  - v020-04 is then met in form (recorded and replayed in CI, red on a changed app) but not in its use (a check that
    catches a regression across commits). The CLI half can run under agent-run only if it is recorded in process,
    since blitz-tests cannot run the binary.

**Widens least:** **B**. Nothing new is at rest anywhere.
- **A** adds one bounded exception: the repository's own two scripted stand checks, committed and public.
- **A** is the least-widening option that still makes a replay red on a real change between commits.

---

## Dependences on the technical forks that follow (the operator's, asked in the dialog once F1 is answered)
- **T1, the replay runner.** A public `escher-driver` API, or a test-only helper. Under A or B alike.
- **T2, the variant's mount.** `TaskShell` made `pub` in seven_guis (a visibility change, no markup), or the shell's
  markup replicated in the test. Under A or B alike.
- **Where the committed checks live** (`tests/blitz-tests/checks/`) and the freshness check apply under A only.

## Answer
_Appended here verbatim when it arrives; then this file is snapped (`--message-file`, `--kind relay`) and cited
`inputs#I{n}` where the answer stands._

The operator's message, 2026-10-19, verbatim:

> The founder answered F1 by dialog in the overseer session (2026-10-19 08:04Z), relayed by the overseer:
> «Коммитить две проверки (Рекомендую)», that is option A. Record it as his own word (not PROVISIONAL), append it to
> founder-forks.md, snapshot it, and go on to T1 and T2 in your dialog.

- F1 → **A** — the founder's own word, «Коммитить две проверки (Рекомендую)» (the founder, 2026-10-19 08:04Z, by
  question dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the overseer). Ratified by the founder (2026-10-19); not
  PROVISIONAL.

title: I2-founder-forks.md.txt
body:
# Founder forks — 2026-10-19-session-recording («Session recording», v020-04)

Phase P4 of `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-19T02-56-17-phase/`. The founder is away. On the operator's directive
(inputs#I1, `relay-1.md`) every fork that is his is written here: its options whole, its dependences, a marked
recommendation, and the option that widens least named as such. The operator answers in his stead. Each answer is
recorded as a delegate's answer (`delegate the operator`), PROVISIONAL. Each fork's option ships what the playbook's
«Boundary widening» pattern names (verdict `escalate`), so whatever is answered here, the wrap still escalates it in
full. The founder's own word at the next epoch boundary discharges the PROVISIONAL marks (the playbook's «Provisional
discharge» rule).

**Why these three are his.** Today the security plan says «no log, event or file carries an id, a name, a value, the
snapshot's text or a diff's content» (security-plan §Input Validation, the 2026-10-10-driver-cli row). §Data
Protection lists no file the driver writes. A typed password crosses in and nowhere else: every screen reading of it is
the mask `MASKED_VALUE`, and its text «reaches no log, event or file». A kept check is a new carrier and a new exit
(CLAUDE.md Critical Warnings; the founder's rule of 2026-10-10: «a new carrier or a new exit still is» a widening).
- F1 decides where that carrier lives and how a recording is asked for.
- F2 decides what it holds of a password.
- F3 decides what it holds of the screen.

**What research measured** (`escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-19-session-recording/research.md`):
- The host's teardown removes the socket, then the state directory with a non-recursive remove whose failure is ignored
  (`packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:80-81`). `stand_session_quiet` pins the directory's listing to `session.sock`
  alone (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_session_quiet.rs:70-80`). `stand_session_lifecycle` pins the directory gone
  after `stop` and the expiry.
- The `mcp` role takes no argument at all: `mcp --session d` is usage (`packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs:456-458`).
  `serve_mcp` takes no location (`packages/escher-driver/src/mcp.rs:82`).
- Whether a control is masked (an `input` of type `password` or `file`) is decided inside dioxus-native-dom's private
  snapshot reader (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs:231-243`).

---

## F1 — Where a kept check lives, and how a recording is asked for

Two things are decided together:
- the carrier (a file escher writes, or an answer the caller keeps);
- who names its place: whoever launches the driver, or the agent inside a call.

The verb table, `help` and `tools/list` change only under option D.

**A. A recording directory named by whoever launches the driver — opt-in, never named by a call. (Recommended)**
- **Off by default.** Nothing is recorded unless the launcher names a directory:
  - `escher-session start <task> --session <dir> --record <dir>` on the command line. `start` passes it to the host
    role it spawns: `serve <task> --session <dir> --record <dir>`.
  - `escher-session mcp --record <dir>` for the MCP role. The launcher is whoever writes the MCP client's server
    config: the operator, never the model.
- **What is written.** One check per session, from `start` to `stop` or the idle expiry, as one file in that directory.
  - The directory is created `0700`, or refused when it is open to its group or others. The state directory follows
    the same rule.
  - The file is created new and `0600`. It never replaces an existing file, and its name is a fixed pattern holding
    no id, label or text.
- **What stays unchanged.**
  - The state directory and its teardown: `session.sock` alone, removed at `stop`, so `stand_session_quiet` and
    `stand_session_lifecycle` read as today.
  - No tool argument, verb or result field is added, so the eleven verbs, `help`'s line and `tools/list` stay
    byte-identical. Only the closed argv reader gains the one option, on `start`, `serve` and `mcp`, and so does the
    usage line built from it.
- **What widens.** A new at-rest carrier: an owner-only file holding call content (F2) and screen readings (F3). It
  needs a new §Occupied Resources entry (arch) and a §Data Protection medium (security).
- **Why it is recommended.** It is the only option that keeps escher itself owner-only at rest, as the entry asks. No
  agent inside a call can choose where escher writes. Typed text never re-crosses the stdout or MCP stdio, and the
  session contract is untouched.
- **Dependences.** F2 and F3 decide its content. Under A the MCP role gains its first argument, an amendment to the
  ratified `mcp` crossing's grammar (layout-templates §Surface: cli; security-plan §Input Validation, the CLI
  arguments row).

**B. Inside the session's own state directory, `{session}/` — hosted sessions only.**
- The host writes the check beside `session.sock` and leaves it at `stop`. The state directory then outlives the
  session (its non-recursive remove fails on the file), and the session contract changes:
  - the `session-state` label, «`session.sock` alone, absent after `stop`»;
  - the obs-plan §9 state-directory row;
  - `stand_session_quiet`'s listing and `stand_session_lifecycle`'s absence pins.
- The MCP role has no state directory. MCP recording would still need A's `mcp --record <dir>`, or would not exist,
  which breaks the entry's «via CLI or MCP».
- **What widens:** the same new carrier as A, plus a change to the ratified session-state contract.
- **Dependence:** with no MCP half, B meets the entry only together with A for the MCP role.

**C. No file from escher: the check leaves in an answer and the caller keeps it.**
- The recording is held in memory and returned whole. The return is either `stop`'s answer or a new `record`-style
  answer, on the command line's stdout and as an MCP result.
- Escher writes no file, adds no §Occupied Resources entry and needs no new argument if the hand-back is `stop`'s.
- **What widens.** A new exit for typed text, which today crosses in only. The command line's rule «no ending writes
  back anything the caller typed» breaks. Every typed text, a password's included unless F2 masks it, rides stdout and
  the MCP stdio to the client, and from there into whatever the client keeps (a model's transcript included).
  «Owner-only at rest» becomes the caller's concern, not escher's.
- **Dependence:** F2 then decides what of a password crosses that exit. A new verb, if chosen for the hand-back, also
  widens the verb table: the founder's call (arch §Standard Contracts, Driver session).

**D. A file at a path a tool call names (an argument of `start`, on the command line and as an MCP tool argument).**
- The agent chooses where escher writes, per session.
- **What widens.**
  - A write-anywhere primitive given to the MCP client (the model): any new file path the user can create.
  - A new argument kind (a path) in the verb table, `help` and `tools/list`.
  - A new carrier, as in A.
- This is the widest option.

**Widens least:** **A.** It is the narrowest option that meets the entry's «owner-only» and «via CLI or MCP».
- B adds a state-contract change on top of A's carrier.
- C sends typed text out over two ratified carriers and into the client's own records, where escher's owner-only rule
  cannot follow it.
- D adds a write-anywhere argument.

---

## F2 — What a kept check holds of text typed into a masked control (a password or file input)

Typed text into every other control is kept verbatim. It is the text the screen already reads back as that control's
`value` (a textarea and a text input are unmasked by design: a11y history, 2026-10-09-audit-corrections-agent-surfaces).
Only a `type` whose target is masked is at stake.

**A. Kept verbatim, at rest in the owner-only file.**
- A replay types exactly what was typed, so the replay is exact.
- **What widens.** A typed secret at rest for the first time. The security plan's «reaches no log, event or file»
  is broken for the password's own text: amended, not kept.

**B. Replaced by a fixed stand-in; the step marked masked. (Recommended)**
- The kept step holds a fixed placeholder text (one fixed string, the same for every password, never the typed
  text's length) and a closed flag saying the target was a masked control.
- A replay types the placeholder.
- Every kept screen reading of that control is already `MASKED_VALUE` (F3), so the control's own reading replays the
  same.
- **Stated limit.** A behaviour that depends on the secret's content (a "too short" message, a login that accepts only
  the real password) can replay differently. The masked flag lets the next entry («Recorded-check replay») name such
  a step instead of reporting an unexplained change.
- **What widens.** Nothing of the secret: not its text, its length or a digest. The file holds only the fact that a
  masked control was typed into.
- **Why it is recommended.** It keeps the security plan's password rule whole while every session stays recordable,
  and its one limit is named in the check itself.
- **Dependences.**
  - The driver needs to know a `type` target is masked. That is a public reader in dioxus-native-dom beside the
    private one (`snapshot.rs:231-243`): a technical change inside escher's own crate, no boundary.
  - Under F1 C the placeholder, not the secret, is what crosses the new exit.

**C. Refused: a session that types into a masked control keeps no check.**
- The `type` still runs and answers as today. The recording is dropped, and the session's check is never written. Its
  ending says so in a fixed word (F1 decides where that word is read).
- No false red can come from a stand-in, but no session with a login in it can be recorded.
- **What widens.** Nothing of a masked control reaches the file: not even the fact that one was typed into.

**Widens least:** **C.** Nothing of a masked control is kept at all. B keeps one closed flag and a fixed placeholder,
no byte of the secret. A keeps the secret.

---

## F3 — What a kept check holds of the screen each step answered

For the next entry's replay to be «red on behaviour change, green otherwise», a step needs something to compare.
Every reading already holds a password and a file input as `MASKED_VALUE`, and a shot paints a password as bullets.

**A. Each step's answer whole, as the driver wrote it — a shot's PNG included.**
- The snapshot text, the `to_json` line with its diff, `in_view` and `advanced_ms`, and a shot's base64 PNG: screen
  pixels at rest.
- A replay can say exactly what changed and compare pixels.
- **What widens.** Ids, names, values, snapshot text, diffs and pixels in a file for the first time. That breaks the
  kept «no … file carries …» sentence and puts an in-band image on an at-rest carrier. Size grows by up to about 1 MiB
  per shot.

**B. Each step's answer whole except a shot's pixels: a shot step keeps its width and height. (Recommended)**
- As A, but a `screenshot` step keeps whether it was accepted and its dimensions, never its PNG.
- A replay can name what changed for every verb but `screenshot`. A shot is checked as having run at the same size;
  pixel comparison stays out of this version.
- **What widens.** Ids, names, values (masked as on every carrier), snapshot text and diffs in the owner-only file.
  This is the same content the ratified socket and stdio already carry, now at rest. Pixels never are.
- **Why it is recommended.** A replay that turns red has to say what changed, or an agent cannot act on it. The
  content is what the same owner's session already shows them, and pixels — the largest content, and the one a
  masked password is painted in — stay out of the file.

**C. Each step's answer as a digest only (a fixed 64-bit hash, hand-written: no new dependency).**
- No screen content at rest. A replay detects any change of an answer but cannot say what changed: to see it, an agent
  re-runs the session live.
- **What widens.** No id, name, value or pixel reaches the file. The hash of each answer does, a closed fixed-width
  word.

**D. No answer kept: the calls and whether each was accepted, nothing else.**
- A replay is red only when a step is refused where it was accepted, or the reverse. A changed value, name or
  screen goes unnoticed, so v020-04's «failing when the UI's behaviour changes» is met only for refusals.
- **What widens:** nothing of the screen.

**Widens least:** **D**, at the cost of a replay that misses every change but a refusal. **C** is the least-widening
option that still detects every changed answer.

---

## Dependences across the three
- F1 C turns F2 and F3 from «what is at rest» into «what crosses a new exit to the client». The same option letters
  then apply to that exit.
- F2 B relies on F3 keeping the masked control's own readings as `MASKED_VALUE`, which every F3 option does, since
  the readings come from the snapshot.
- F3 C or D leaves the next entry's replay with less to report. Its red stays a red, but without «what changed».
- The technical forks that follow these answers — the file's form, where the recorder sits, whether the in-process
  round trip is this chunk's — are the operator's, asked in the dialog once these three are answered.

## Answers (the operator, in the founder's stead — a delegate's answers, PROVISIONAL)
_Appended here verbatim when they arrive; then this file is snapped (`--message-file`, `--kind relay`) and cited
`inputs#I{n}` where each answer stands._

> 0600 in 0700). F2 B (a fixed stand-in plus the masked flag: no byte, length or digest of the secret). F3 C (each
> answer as the fixed 64-bit digest only: no id, name, value or pixel at rest; a red still turns red). His word may
> widen F3 to B later, and the plan should say so. Record them and go on to the technical forks.

- F1 → **A** — delegate the operator, PROVISIONAL.
- F2 → **B** — delegate the operator, PROVISIONAL.
- F3 → **C** — delegate the operator, PROVISIONAL; the founder's own word may widen it to **B** later.

# Operator pass — 2026-10-19-session-recording

Fired by hand in plan order on the operator's direction (2026-10-19): «Run the operator pass … each entry by hand in
plan order … Stop and tell me if any entry is red; start no wrap.»

**Verdict: RED at entry 17.** CI#39199277925 failed `Test (windows)`. The pass stopped there and no wrap was started.

## Entry 15 — hygiene (fired as written, before the pre-CI commit)
```

hygiene: clean — read 113 (runs 108 · evidence 0 · inputs 5) · trails 14 not read · copies 3 not read by P1 — 0 host paths kept · binary 0 not read by P1

## The pre-CI commit

parent is `93336e886`. The tree was clean after the commit (`git status --short` read 0 rows).

## Entry 16 — `gate.py run --plan … --operator 16` (backgrounded)
```

```
green. The history move is the intended push of `9da7b75d` to `origin/build/escher-0.2.0`.

## Entry 17 — `ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1800` (fired as written, backgrounded)
```
ci v1.3 · 2b582a9b
repo Turbolet85/escher (the push remote `origin`) · polled 31× over 929 s
9da7b75dd4ec verdict: red · checks 17/17 · first-fail +916 s Test (windows) · wall 916 s · runs CI#39199277925 complete…
runs: CI#39199277925 push completed/failure
failed 1: Test (windows) (failure)
log: gh api --allow-escape-sequences repos/Turbolet85/escher/actions/jobs/117889991186/logs
run failed: CI#39199277925 failure
```
**red** — `contains verdict: green` fails.

### The failing test, read from the job log (job 117889991186)
```
test a_recording_mcp_role_logs_nothing_of_its_checks_at_trace ... FAILED
thread 'a_recording_mcp_role_logs_nothing_of_its_checks_at_trace' (2524) panicked at examples\seven_guis\tests\mcp_log.rs:145:36:
test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 1.33s
```
- **Cause, as read:** recording is unix-only by this chunk's design. `Session::recording_into` and
  `recording::prepare_dir` return `SessionError::Unsupported` off unix, so `escher-session mcp --record <dir>` ends
  with exit 3 before it answers.
- The new `mcp_log` test `a_recording_mcp_role_logs_nothing_of_its_checks_at_trace` is not `cfg(unix)`-gated. The
  file is gated only `not(target_arch = "wasm32")`.
- So on the Windows runner the test waits for a reply that never comes. It panics at `mcp_log.rs:145`, which is the
  snapshot reply's `string_at(...).expect`.
- This chunk's red, introduced by step 13's new test. The host's Linux gates cannot reproduce it, because there the
  recording works.
- **Not fixed: the operator's direction was to stop.** A fix would gate the recorded `mcp_log` test and its
  `recorded_needles` helper `cfg(unix)`, as `host_log` and `recording.rs` already are. It would land as a
  `fix(2026-10-19-session-recording): operator fix after CI run 39199277925, …` commit, re-pushed through entry 16 and
  re-read through entry 17.
- Cargo stops at the first failing target on that runner, so any seven_guis target after `mcp_log` went unrun on
  Windows in this run.

## Fix round 1 — on the operator's direction (2026-10-19)
The direction: «Gate that test and its helper with #[cfg(unix)]. Before committing, sweep every test this chunk added
or changed … for a recording path not gated to unix, and gate any you find the same way. Add a test that off unix
--record refuses with Unsupported … Commit it as the fix commit you named, then re-fire entries 16 and 17.»

- **Sweep:** one gap, `mcp_log`'s recorded test and its `recorded_needles` helper. Both were gated `#[cfg(unix)]`, along
  with the recorded-needle read inside `mcp_flow`. Every other recording path was already gated:
  - whole-file gates: `stand_session_recording.rs`, the seven_guis `recording.rs`, `cli_commands.rs`
  - per-item gates: the `host_log` recorded flow and its helper, the `mcp_tests` recording units, the `session` units,
    and the `recording` units (`cfg(all(test, unix))`)
  - the `cli`, `wire`, `describe`, `json` and `error` units touch no recording path.
- **Off-unix refusal pinned:**
  - `recording.rs` (`off_unix_tests`): `prepare_dir` and `Recording::create` return `Unsupported`.
  - `session.rs`: `recording_into` returns `Unsupported` and creates nothing.
  - `mcp_tests.rs`: a recording boot's `start` is answered `failed(Unsupported)`.
  - `examples/seven_guis/tests/recording.rs`, moved from a file-wide `cfg(unix)` to per-item gates:
    `mcp --record` ends with exit 3 and the fixed message on stderr, `start … --record` answers kind `unsupported`,
    and no directory is created.
- Linux before the commit: `cargo test -p escher-driver` 87 passed; `host_log` 2, `mcp_log` 2 and `recording` 3 passed;
  `ci-leg.sh clippy` exit 0; `cargo fmt --check` exit 0.
- **The `cfg(not(unix))` code could not be compiled on this host.** Only `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` is installed.
- Commit: `00a6c26bf fix(2026-10-19-session-recording): operator fix after CI run 39199277925, gate the recorded mcp_log check to unix and pin the off-unix refusal`.

**The failure, read from the job log (job 117895198720):** a compile error on Windows, from the fix itself.
```
error[E0425]: cannot find function `mode` in this scope
  --> examples\seven_guis\tests\recording.rs:67:13

  --> examples\seven_guis\tests\recording.rs:40:4

  --> examples\seven_guis\tests\recording.rs:69:13

  is configured out.

## Fix round 2 — on the operator's direction (2026-10-19)
The direction: «Gate the_check with #[cfg(unix)] as the fix commit you named. Do NOT add the Windows target: no host
toolchain change while the founder is away. Instead, before committing, read recording.rs and every file this chunk
touched for an item gated to unix that an ungated item calls or names, and list each pair you checked in
operator-pass.md.»

- `the_check` (`examples/seven_guis/tests/recording.rs`) is gated `#[cfg(unix)]`.

### The audit
- **Basis.**
  - The 26 `.rs` files `git diff --name-only 93336e886 HEAD` names, read for every `cfg(unix)`, `cfg(not(unix))`,
    `cfg(all(test, unix))`, `cfg(all(test, not(unix)))` and `cfg_attr(not(unix), …)`.
  - 14 of the 26 carry a gate.
  - Each gated item's callers were found with `command grep -n` over its file. `mode(` and the `session_common`
    readers were searched over `tests/blitz-tests/tests/`.
- **The rule.** An item configured out off unix may be named only by an item that is itself configured out off
  unix, or by a twin defined under `cfg(not(unix))`.
- **Each pair below** reads: gated item → the item that names it → that naming item's own gate → verdict.

**`examples/seven_guis/tests/recording.rs`.** It carries `#![cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` and
`#![cfg_attr(not(unix), allow(dead_code, unused_imports))]`.

**`examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs`.** It carries `#![cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`.

- off unix, `mcp_flow`'s `record` is still read at L140 (`--record`), and `found` and `lines` are still read by the

**`packages/escher-driver/src/recording.rs`.**
- `mod imp` [unix] and `mod imp` [not unix] each define `prepare_dir` (L198 · L271), `create_check` (L224 · L275),

    L172 `remove`) and `prepare_dir` (L182) — ok

  `SessionError` — ok

**`packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs`.**

  `a_recording_that_ends_reads_failed_once` [unix] (L313) — ok

  `a_call_that_ends_the_recording_is_answered_as_its_session_error` [unix] (L661) — ok

**`packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs`.**

  `host::imp` and matched in the ungated `client::read_answer`. It is dead off unix and allowed — ok

The plan forecast that "the floor reading does not move", and research said "moved lines stay counted" (because

uncovered. The two dioxus-native-dom and blitz-test-harness readings are identical. This belongs to the wrap: the
test-plan coverage text and research's premise.
