title: I2-founder-forks.md.txt
body:
# Founder forks — 2026-10-20-select-by-id (phase P4)

Chunk: Select by id (v020-08) — escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-20-select-by-id/scope.md. Gathered per the operator's
directive (inputs#I1): every fork that widens a boundary (a new driver command, verb, argument, exit or log field, an
engine behaviour change for every document) or turns the project's direction, each with its options in order, the
recommendation marked and the most conservative option marked. Playbook patterns each touches: «Boundary widening»
(verdict: escalate) for a new verb or argument; «An engine behaviour change for every document» (routine only on the
founder's own word at this fork; a delegate's answer leaves it PROVISIONAL, «Provisional discharge»).

What the measurement found (research.md §Measured, evidence/select-probe-readings.txt — both layout modes alike): a
`select` today lays out as nothing. It computes `display: inline` with every `option` `display: none`, reads no client
rect, and so is left out of the snapshot; `click`, `type` and `screenshot` on its id are refused `not-found`. The tree
holds it as an empty `ComboBox` (no options, no value); a `<label>` names nothing but an `input`, while `aria-label`
names it. It takes its Tab stop in document order and takes no key. So v020-08 needs four things the engine lacks: a
box, a chosen option it holds, a value the snapshot reads, and a way for an agent to choose.

Decided without a fork (leans an artifact settles, stated here so the whole picture is on one page):
- The chosen option is held by the engine apart from the markup, seeded from the `selected` attribute (else the first
  option that is not disabled), re-seeded when the app writes an option's `selected` or adds or removes options — the
  range model's shape (2026-10-13-range-input-interaction), cited to the WHATWG `select` element.
- The snapshot's `value` for a select is HTML's `select.value` — the chosen option's `value` attribute, else its text —
  in the existing `value` key, inside the control-value crossing the founder ratified on 2026-10-10 (a text input's
  author-written `value` attribute already crosses there). No new key.
- Single-choice selects only; a `multiple` select and `optgroup` stay a stated limit (scope §Boundaries). A disabled
  option is never chosen by a key. A disabled select takes no key and no click (`ElementData::is_disabled`).

## F1 — How an agent chooses an option

The engine has no select keys today. Every option below makes a click on a select focus it, as a click on a button does
(today a click on any other element clears focus), in every document.

1. **Keys and typeahead, through the verbs there are — (Recommended)**
   On a focused select, in every document: ArrowDown / ArrowUp choose the next / previous option that is not disabled,
   Home / End the first / last; a typed character chooses the first option whose label starts with the text typed so
   far (case-insensitive, as browsers do; the typed text starts afresh at a click on the select and after 1 s of the
   document's clock). An agent chooses with `type --id <select> --text <label>` in one call — `type` already clicks its
   target and then types — or with `click --id` then `press arrow-down`. Each change fires the app's events (F4). No new
   verb, argument, key name or exit; `type`'s help gains one fixed sentence for a select.
   Why: one call by the select's own id, the way an agent already sets a text field; keyboard users get the browser's
   keys (SC 2.1.1); nothing new crosses the driver's surface.
2. **Keys only, through `press` — (Most conservative)**
   As 1 without typeahead: an agent focuses the select by `click --id` and steps with `press arrow-down` / `arrow-up` /
   `home` / `end`, one option per call, reading the value back each time. No change to `type`.
   Trade-off: choosing the fifth option takes five calls, and `type` on a select types nothing useful.
3. **A new instance verb `choose --id <select> --option <label>`**
   The twelfth verb, on every carrier (socket, command line, MCP, `help`), recorded in a kept check; it chooses the
   option by its label directly, and is refused `not-found` (an existing cause) when no option has that label. The
   engine still gains the held choice; keys are left out unless also chosen.
   Trade-off: a new verb and a new argument kind widen the validated surface (as `scroll` and `screenshot` did) and
   move every count site of the verb table.

## F2 — The select's box

1. **The engine lays a select out as an inline block showing its chosen option's label — (Recommended)**
   The user-agent stylesheet gives `select` `display: inline-block` with a border and padding like `input`'s, and
   layout gives it the chosen option's label as its content, so every select on every page — remote ones included —
   takes a size, reads in the snapshot and paints its value (no arrow glyph, no popup).
   Why: a real app's unstyled select becomes visible to the agent and on screen, as in a browser.
2. **The engine gives a select a box but paints no label**
   `display: inline-block` and a minimum size in the stylesheet only; the select is clickable and read in the snapshot,
   but its value shows nowhere on screen.
3. **No engine layout change: the fixture sizes its select in its own CSS — (Most conservative)**
   The fixture page sets the select's display, width and height; an unstyled select on a real page still has no box and
   stays out of the snapshot — a stated limit until a later chunk.

## F3 — The options in the tree and the snapshot

1. **Each option read as the select's child, named by its label, the chosen one `selected` — (Recommended)**
   The accessibility builder keeps a select's options (today dropped as `display: none`) as `ListBoxOption` children,
   in every document; the snapshot lists them under the select by their own stable ids, each named by its label, the
   chosen one `selected`, its bounds the select's box. An option's label crosses as a name, inside the ratified name
   crossing; `selected` is the existing closed reading. An option is not a Tab stop and is not clicked (a click on one
   is refused as any element under another).
   Why: an agent sees the choices it can make before it makes one.
2. **The select's value alone — no option read — (Most conservative)**
   The snapshot reads the select and its chosen value; the other options are not read, so an agent learns them only by
   stepping through with keys.

## F4 — What else a real app reads from a select (choose any)

1. **A `change` event after `input` — (Recommended)**
   Each change fires `input` then `change`, as HTML does: blitz-traits gains a `Change` event kind and the Dioxus bridge
   hands it to `onchange`, in every document. Without it an app's `onchange` on a select never runs (today only
   `oninput` can be reached, as the range model's change is).
2. **A `<label>` names a select (HTML's labelable elements) — (Recommended)**
   `label_bound_input_element` binds a `<label>` to every labelable element HTML names (`button`, `input` not hidden,
   `meter`, `output`, `progress`, `select`, `textarea`), in every document; the label then names it in the tree, and a
   click on the label focuses it (the same function serves `handle_click`).
3. **Neither — `input` alone, and a select named by `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` — (Most conservative)**

## Answers (the operator, by question dialog, read 2026-10-20T04:00Z — delegate operator, PROVISIONAL)

- F1: «Keys + typeahead (Recommended)»
- F2: «Engine shows its label (Recommended)»
- F3: «Options as children (Recommended)»
- F4: «`change` event (Recommended)», «`<label>` names it (Recommended)»
- The operator's note, verbatim: «Delegate answers while the founder is away, PROVISIONAL until his word in
  founder-forks.md (an engine behaviour change for every document, as the :focus-within take): no new verb, argument or
  carrier — option labels inside the ratified name crossing.»
- Authority: delegate operator (the founder away). Every answer is an engine behaviour change for every document,
  PROVISIONAL until the founder's own word on this file, discharged in the Epoch 4 boundary batch («Provisional
  discharge»); built now, not gated — as the carried `:focus-within` take was.

row.why: F1 keys+typeahead, F2 engine shows label, F3 options as children, F4 change event and label names it; delegate, PROVISIONAL until the founder word, built now not gated

# Step 3 — the `:checked` mechanism, measured before steps 4-16

Run 2026-10-20 by /andromeda-implement (run dir `.andromeda/runs/2026-10-20T04-14-31-implement/`), after steps 2 and
3 only (`option` seeds `CHECKED` from `selected` at creation; `select { display: inline-block }` with `input`'s
border, padding and background; `select:not([multiple]) > option:checked { display: inline }`), before any other
step. A throwaway blitz-tests target `zz_checked_probe.rs`, removed after the run, booted an `HtmlDocument` through
`Harness::from_html_with` holding the step-16 fixture's selects (`fx-pick` Apple / Banana `selected` / Cherry,
`fx-named` Red / Green `selected`, `fx-off` `disabled` X `selected`), read each select's and option's computed
display and `get_client_bounding_rect`, then moved `CHECKED` from `fx-banana` to `fx-cherry` through
`BaseDocument::snapshot_node_and` (each option's element state swapped, `mark_ancestors_dirty`, as `toggle_radio`
writes it), pumped and read again. `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test zz_checked_probe -- --nocapture`:
exit 0, `1 passed; 0 failed`.

Readings, identical in both layout modes (`incremental` false and true):

| reading | at boot | after `CHECKED` moved to `fx-cherry` |
|---|---|---|
| `fx-pick` display · rect | `Display(259)` (inline-block) · 109.125, 8, **62 × 24** | `Display(259)` · 109.125, 8, **55 × 24** |
| `fx-apple` | `Display(0)` (none) · 0 × 0 | `Display(0)` · 0 × 0 |
| `fx-banana` | `Display(258)` (inline) · 112.125, 11, **55.171875 × 18** | `Display(0)` · 0 × 0 |
| `fx-cherry` | `Display(0)` · 0 × 0 | `Display(258)` · 112.125, 11, **48.015625 × 18** |
| `fx-named` | `Display(259)` · 175.125, 8, 51 × 24 | `Display(259)` · 168.125, 8, 51 × 24 |
| `fx-off` | `Display(259)` · 230.125, 8, 17 × 24 | `Display(259)` · 223.125, 8, 17 × 24 |

- A select reads a client rect at least as wide as its chosen label: 62 ≥ 55.17 (Banana), then 55 ≥ 48.02 (Cherry);
  its chosen option lies inside it, inset by border 1 + padding 2 (x 112.125 = 109.125 + 3, y 11 = 8 + 3).
- Moving `CHECKED` restyles: the old option goes back to `display: none`, the new one lays out, the select shrinks to
  the new label and the selects after it move left by the 7 px difference — in both modes.

The restyle follows the state, so the plan's premise holds and steps 4-16 build on it. Research's reading of the
untouched tree (`fx-pick` `Display(258)`, 0×0, rect `None`) is the before.

title: I1-README.md.txt
body:
# viola 0.2.0 — Incubator

**Status:** PRE-route material for **v0.2.0**, gathered while v0.1.0 is in flight. Later it is assembled into
`intent.md`.

> ⚠️ **This is NOT a version folder.** The `-incubator` suffix keeps it out of Andromeda's version cursor. New-session
> and phase read only the highest *strict* `viola-X.Y.Z/` dir, and `0.2.0-incubator` is not `X.Y.Z`, so the cursor
> stays at `viola-0.1.0`. The real `viola-0.2.0/` is created later by `/andromeda-route --version 0.2.0`, from
> the `intent.md` assembled here. Do not treat this folder as the active version. It is gitignored
> (`.gitignore`, as Pulse's `andromeda-pulse-0.4.0-incubator/` is) and stays local and untracked until it is
> promoted.

## Purpose
The pattern is **intent-driven**: one `intent.md` → `/andromeda-route` derives the vision, requirements, working
route and verification matrix → the loop builds and gates each cap. This folder is where the *material* for 0.2.0's
intent accumulates (research, rulings, sharp questions), so the intent is assembled from a measured base when 0.1.0
ships, not invented cold.

## The 0.2.0 direction (the frame)

> **Reframe pending (founder direction 2026-10-04):** the frame below was written for a Windows host. The founder
> wants the next versions rethought for a tiling host (Omarchy/Hyprland). See `open-questions.md` Q9 before reading
> Q1/Q2 as settled.

**0.2.0 makes the session hierarchy visible and reachable.**

- **One node graph per project:** `overseer1` → the project overseers → their builders and workers. It is drawn
  with React Flow on the React + TypeScript web front that 0.1.0 lands (the Lit → React switch is a 0.1.0 item,
  founder-ruled 2026-10-01, entering the route at the Epoch 2b corrective wrap).
- **The founder's pain behind it:** with ~10 overseers running at once, the problem is *finding the right terminal
  to type into*. A graph that only shows the sessions does not solve that. **RAISE is therefore the core of 0.2.0,
  not a nicety:** picking a node must bring that session's terminal to the foreground.
- **The hard fact under the frame:** on the founder's host the foreground-lock timeout is infinite
  (`SPI_GETFOREGROUNDLOCKTIMEOUT` = 2147483647 ms, *measured* 2026-09-30). A click in the graph reaches the
  background `viola ui` server, which therefore **cannot** raise a window by itself. So 0.2.0's real decision is
  the raise *trigger*, and every candidate trigger touches the security plan. The forks are in `open-questions.md`.
- **0.2.0 is also where sessions are CREATED, not only seen and reached** (the founder's direction,
  2026-10-01).
  - Every session runs under viola, the overseers included, and one registry holds every session id and every
    edge.
  - The parent is declared at launch; observed `link`s are drawn on top, styled apart.
  - The founder clicks an overseer's node, presses "add worker", and viola launches the session and records the
    edge at once, replacing today's hand-run `.ps1` launcher.
  - That makes the spawn button the GUI's first write route (code-bearing, so it needs full write auth), and it
    makes viola-opened named terminal windows (R3) central rather than opt-in. See `open-questions.md` Q5/Q6 and
    the re-weighed `raise-and-focus.md`.

**Already decided for 0.1.0, so not in 0.2.0's scope:** revive (`viola revive <name>`, the study's V2: resume in
place, no launch replay, with P4/P5/P6/P7/P12 as its measurement step) and the React + TypeScript toolchain chunk
at Epoch 8's head (frontend sources in the code-graph ts plane). Founder ruling, 2026-10-01.

## Contents
- **`open-questions.md`** — the forks the 0.2.0 intent must resolve: the raise trigger, the window identity model,
  the gating probes (P1/P2/P3/P9 + P13–P15), the security-plan entries, the graph registry (Q5, direction
  founder-ruled), spawn from the UI (Q6, direction founder-ruled), and the Unix legs. **Read this first.**
- **`raise-and-focus.md`** — the 0.2.0 half of the session-memory study, re-weighed 2026-10-01: R3 + R5 + V4 are
  core, R1 + R2 become a deferrable hand-started leg, R4 is not planned, with the comparison and size tables.
- **`deferred-from-0.1.0.md`** — the items deliberately kept out of 0.1.0: launch-spec replay, V3, V4, V5b, and
  V5a (rejected), each with its reason and its status after spawn (`launch.json`, V4 and V5b move to 0.2.0's
  core; V3 for spawned sessions only).
- **`research/`** — findings from probes and delegated research. Drop results here as they come.
- **The source study:** `refs/session-memory-options.md` (tracked, commit `4a3062d`) holds the full reasoning,
  the measured facts F1–F8 / M1–M9 and the probe list P1–P12. The notes here point into it rather than copying it.

## How this becomes the intent
When v0.1.0 ships and the material is rich enough: assemble `intent.md` from this folder (the frame plus the
resolved open questions, in OBSERVED → EXPECT shape), then `/andromeda-route --version 0.2.0` derives the version.

**Cap numbering:** 0.1.0 used `v1-01..v1-53` (*measured*: `viola-0.1.0/requirements.md` and
`verification-matrix.json`, 53 ids). 0.2.0's id scheme is the route's to pick: either `v1-54+` continuing the
series, or a new `v2-01` prefix. Settle it before the intent cites any cap id.

# The founder's word on «Cold-agent bar» (2026-10-25), given ahead of its phase

The founder raised the question himself in the escher overseer session on 2026-10-25, while chunk 4's wrap was
running: «нам же надо проверить весь функционал колд агентом, но на чем его проверять?». The phase is not promoted
yet. The entry is `escher-0.2.0/working-route.md:55` (v020-11). This relay goes into that phase's `inputs/`.

**What the overseer measured and put to him:**
- The cold-agent pipe has one task set, `stand` (`scripts/cold-agent.sh`, `TASKS=(stand)`).
- The driver's `start` boots four lean tasks: `counter`, `flight-booker`, `timer`, `crud` (`examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:14-17`).
- On those four, an agent can reach lint, `advance`, the screenshot, and recording and replay.
- It cannot reach the `select` (v020-08), the load wait (v020-07) or the screen read in parts (v020-09). Each of those is proven only on an in-file test fixture (`stand_act_select`, `stand_load_wait`, `stand_snapshot_parts`), and `start` does not boot those fixtures.
- `cells` is the stand's one screen over the 10,000-byte budget, and the driver does not serve it.
- Flight booker's one-way and return choice is two buttons, not a `select`.

**The three options:**
1. Extend the stand inside the chunk. Serve `cells` to the driver, make flight booker's choice a real `select` as the 7GUIs spec's combobox, and give the agent goals for lint, `advance`, the screenshot and recording. The load wait does not fall naturally on the stand.
2. A dedicated fixture app holding a select, a load and a large screen.
3. Keep the four tasks and add goals for lint, `advance`, the screenshot and recording only.

**His word, verbatim:** «поскольку живого проекта на котором можно потестить нет то думаю надо расширять стенд, чтоб он покрывал все проверки, так что первый вариант наверно»

How to read it:
- He chose option 1: extend the stand.
- His reason is that no live project exists to test on.
- His scope is wider than option 1 as offered. He wants the stand to cover ALL the checks, «чтоб он покрывал все проверки». The load wait is included in that, although option 1 had left it to its fixture test. The phase settles how the stand carries a load in flight.
- «наверно» is his hedge. It is still the direction he chose, not a delegate's answer, so it is not marked PROVISIONAL. The phase confirms it at P4, together with the wrong-call bar.

**Still open, for that phase's P4:** the wrong-call bar itself, set from 0.1.0's baseline of 0 wrong in 43 calls.

# The founder's word on the four P4 forks of 2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar

Asked by question dialog at P4 (2026-10-25, the session's clock read 2026-10-25T14:04:58Z right after). The founder
answered in the escher overseer session, and the operator relayed his answers verbatim with the note: «The founder's
own word on all four forks, by dialog in the escher overseer session, relayed verbatim.» Each question, its options in
order (the recommendation marked «(Рекомендую)», first), then his chosen label verbatim.

## F1 — Стенд
Question: «Cold-agent bar»: подтверждаете расширение стенда как в варианте 1, но на ВСЕ проверки? Это значит: Cells
отдаётся драйверу (`start cells`, экран 47 949 байт, 5 частей — измерено), выбор «туда / туда-обратно» во Flight
Booker становится настоящим `select`, на стенде появляется загрузка, а холодный агент получает цели на все шесть
возможностей 0.2.0 (запись, lint, `advance`, ожидание загрузки, `select`, чтение по частям). Ваше «наверно» фаза
подтверждает здесь.
Options: «Да, весь стенд (Рекомендую)» · «Без загрузки» · «Только цели на 4 задачах»
Answer: «Да, весь стенд (Рекомендую)»

## F2 — Загрузка
Question: Как стенд несёт загрузку «в полёте» (её ждёт драйвер до 5 с)? Ни один вариант не открывает сеть: запрос
отвечает подставной провайдер внутри процесса (как `LateNet` в тесте `stand_load_wait`), без порта, без `blitz_net`.
Options: «Страница загрузки рядом (Рекомендую)» — `start load` отдаёт маленькую страницу рядом с задачами 7GUIs,
кнопка подгружает ресурс, провайдер отвечает через 200 мс · «Бронь грузит посадочный» · «Оставить на фикстуре»
Answer: «Страница загрузки рядом (Рекомендую)»

## F3 — Прогон
Question: Второй живой прогон. Ратификация 2026-10-15 «Один запуск, до $3» покрыла ОДИН прогон (43 вызова, без
скриншотов). Новый прогон понесёт поставщику модели через ваш логин новые экраны: содержимое Cells, опции и значение
select, находки lint и, возможно, скриншоты — те же классы, что уже ратифицированы на носителе, но новая перевозка.
Это расширение границы (паттерн playbook «Boundary widening»), поэтому вопрос ваш.
Options: «Один запуск, до $3 (Рекомендую)» · «Один запуск, до $5» · «Пока не запускать»
Answer: «Один запуск, до $3 (Рекомендую)»

## F4 — Порог
Question: Порог ошибочных вызовов для 0.2.0. База 0.1.0: 0 ошибочных из 43. Ошибочный = отказ драйвера + ошибка +
чужой инструмент + отказ в разрешении (как считает труба сейчас; сейчас счёт ничего не решает, порог сделает его
условием прохождения).
Options: «Не больше 5% (Рекомендую)» — например, ≤5 из 100 вызовов · «Ноль ошибочных» · «Не больше 3 вызовов»
Answer: «Не больше 5% (Рекомендую)»

# Row-guard controls — 2026-10-26-codebase-health (plan step 4)

Taken on the refactored tree after the gate block read green (implement run
`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-27T01-14-55-implement/`, 2026-10-27). One control at a time, by a scratchpad script

mutation, asserting it found its site. It runs the named test alone with `cargo test … -- --exact {test}` (stderr
merged into stdout), then writes the saved bytes back and compares sha256 before the next control. A control reads
red when the run exits 101, prints `FAILED` at the test line and has zero `error[` / `could not compile` lines.

title: I3-adapt-0.3.0-for-canvas.md.txt
body:
# Adapting 0.3.0's planned work to the 0.4.0 canvas plans (the escher overseer's reconnaissance, 2026-10-29)

**Why.** The founder, 2026-10-29: «давай теперь сделай разведку чтоб понять возможно то что мы планируем делать сейчас
стоит адаптировать с учетом планов, чтоб не получилось что мы что то строим а в итоге прийдется полностью переделывать
изза новых требований». The 0.4.0 plans are in `canvas-and-node-graph.md`: virtual nodes inside a canvas, the canvas
observed as data, a `drag` verb, and pan and zoom through a transform.

**Read at `a6c6a37c7`**: `escher-0.3.0/requirements.md`, `working-route.md`,
`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs`, `snapshot.rs`, and `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs`,
`command.rs`, `wire.rs`. These are the overseer's reading of the code, not measurements.

## What already fits (no rework expected)
- **The snapshot is built from the accesskit tree** (`snapshot.rs:98`: «its id and role from that tree»). That tree
  carries non-DOM nodes natively, so a canvas's virtual nodes can enter it without a new carrier.
- **An action lands on a point.** `click` and `type` press the centre of the target's bounds
  (`execute.rs:360`, `:427-439`). A virtual node with bounds can be clicked the same way, as long as the canvas app
  hit-tests its own pointer events.
- **The wire is versioned** (`wire.rs:37`, `v3`), so a new verb is an additive, versioned change.

## Where 0.3.0 could build something 0.4.0 would have to redo
1. **The stable-id grammar** (`element_id.rs`). Today an id is an author key, an anchored path (`//`), a component path,
   or a document path (`/…`), all derived from DOM and vdom elements. A virtual node has no DOM element. If D2, B3,
   E2's recorded checks and replay store ids in this grammar, 0.4.0 needs a form for `{canvas element}` + `{virtual
   key}` that collides with none of the four. **Adapt in «The UI graph» (v030-05): reserve that form now (a separator no
   current id can hold), even if nothing produces it yet.**
2. **The node model of the UI graph and of «What can I do here»** (v030-05, v030-06). If the graph and the actionable
   list are keyed on a DOM element (`Target.node: NodeId`, `execute.rs:354`), a virtual node does not fit. **Adapt: key
   them on the agent-visible node (the accesskit node with its bounds), with an optional owner element, and let a
   handler sit on an owner element and serve sub-targets.** A canvas typically has one listener that dispatches inside.
3. **Verbs as a closed list in B3 and E2** (v030-06, v030-09). If «What can I do here» and auto-exploration hard-code
   `click`/`type`/`press`/`scroll`, adding `drag` (two points or a node plus a destination) means reshaping both.
   **Adapt: read the per-node verbs from the schema's verb table, and let the recorded-check step format carry verbs
   with more than one target, versioned.**
4. **Handler coverage** (v030-07) counts DOM listeners. A canvas's internal handlers are invisible to it. **Adapt:
   state that limit in its acceptance, so 0.4.0 extends it rather than redefines it.**
5. **Layout explained** (v030-11) reads Taffy and Stylo. A virtual node's place is the app's own. **Adapt: let its
   answer name the "placed by the app inside canvas X" case, so the field set is not closed.**
6. **Bundled fonts** (v030-14). Canvas text (`GlyphRun`) must draw from the same bundled fonts, or a canvas reads
   differently across hosts. **Adapt: in its acceptance, name canvas text as a reader of the bundled set.**
7. **Engine debts** (v030-04). The transform `visible_region` fix should be proven on a pan/zoom container like the
   node graph's (`canvas-and-node-graph.md`).

## What 0.3.0 should not take on
The canvas renderer itself, the CPU renderer's custom-paint gap, `drag`, and virtual-node production all stay in 0.4.0.
The adaptations above keep 0.3.0's shapes open; they add no 0.4.0 capability.

## His words
- On the limit: «Просто мое имхо такое что без этой части фреймворк получается сильно ограничен в возможностях, жесткие
  рамки веб лайк онли для десктопа это такое себе». He asked «А если добавить к нам в работу хедлесс канвас работу это в
  принципе реализуемо? Просто на будущее когда добавим все уже запланированное».
- On Viola: «один экран основной где видно все виола проекты со статистикой сколько там работают сколько оверсиров
  работников и все такое … html css, но вот вторая часть где разворачиваешь отдельный проект думал сделать в стиле
  нодового графа аля гудини».
- **The scope: «Ну я думаю для начала можно взять 1 3 это уже сильно расширит возможности, а 3д оставить на потом».**

## The three layers the overseer put to him
1. **TAKEN. A 2D canvas through anyrender, headless.** The app's Rust code paints paths and shapes into a `<canvas>`
   through the anyrender `PaintScene` API (`examples/custom_widget.rs`, the `custom-widget` feature). These are ordinary
   scene commands, so the CPU screenshot renderer most likely draws them already. That is **unmeasured**. Measure it on
   the stand first.
2. **LATER («3д оставить на потом»). A wgpu canvas, headless.** The app's own wgpu render into a texture
   (`examples/wgpu_texture`, WGSL). It needs a headless GPU device: a software adapter in CI (lavapipe or llvmpipe,
   WARP). It also needs the CPU renderer's custom-paint gap closed (see below), or screenshots taken by a GPU renderer.
   Pixels differ across hardware. escher already never compares shots byte for byte.
3. **TAKEN. The agent sees inside the canvas.** The app declares virtual nodes inside a canvas: an id, a role, a name
   and a region. The driver treats them as elements: they appear in the snapshot, they take `click` and `drag`, and
   they reach the UI graph and "what can I do here". A likely carrier is the accessibility tree escher already builds
   (accesskit). This is design work, probably an epoch. Nothing else has it.

## Observing the canvas as data, not pixels (the founder, 2026-10-29)
**His words:** «Просто по идее если это параметрический 2д то мы можем обсервить это не только скриншотами».

The code already has the base for it:
- anyrender records a scene as structured commands. `anyrender-0.14.0/src/recording.rs` defines
  `RenderCommand`: `Fill`, `Stroke`, `GlyphRun`, `PushLayer`, `PushClipLayer` and `PopLayer`, each carrying its shape,
  transform and brush. They are `serde`-serializable.
- `anyrender_serialize` 0.8.0 is in the workspace (`Cargo.toml:122`) and used by `apps/browser`'s `capture` feature. It
  writes a recorded scene as `draw_commands.json` with its resources.

So layer 1 can carry an observation verb that reads a canvas's recorded commands as data. It is deterministic,
independent of hardware and diffable between two states. Lint-like checks can run inside a canvas, for example a label
overflowing its node or a wire's ends. With layer 3's virtual nodes, the commands inside a node's region bind to its
id, so «node X is drawn here, with these shapes and this text». Screenshots stay for people and for visual questions;
they stop being the primary observation. **This is the overseer's reading of the code. Nothing here is measured
through the driver yet.**

## Code facts measured on 2026-10-29 (at `a6c6a37c7`, build/escher-0.3.0)
- Headless screenshots render on the CPU: `VelloCpuImageRenderer` (`packages/blitz-test-harness/src/screenshot.rs:83`).
- **That renderer draws custom paint transparent:** `anyrender_vello_cpu-0.18.0/src/scene.rs:42-44`
  (`// TODO: custom paint`, `Paint::Custom(_) => … TRANSPARENT`). A wgpu-texture canvas reads empty in a headless shot
  today. This blocks layer 2, not layer 1.
- A `<canvas>` is `SpecialElementData::Canvas(CanvasData { custom_paint_source_id })`
  (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/element.rs:997`), set from its `src` in `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:1416`.
- The driver's twelve verbs hold no `drag` (`docs/capabilities.md`, the schema).

## What Viola's node-graph screen asks of escher (the overseer's reading)
These are not his words. They are the overseer's read of what his Houdini-style graph needs:
- **A hybrid build:** each node is an HTML element, so the agent sees and acts on it. Wires go in an SVG or canvas
  layer. Pan and zoom are a CSS `transform` on the container.
- **A `drag` verb** to move nodes and pull wires. The driver has none.
- **`visible_region` under a transform:** the engine debt that can refuse a target inside a transformed box as
  `off-screen`. It is in 0.3.0's «Engine debts» entry, and pan and zoom hit exactly that case. When that chunk runs,
  prove the fix on a transformed container like the graph's.
- **Unmeasured:** speed with hundreds of absolutely positioned nodes, and zoom by wheel (`scroll` scrolls, it does not
  zoom).
- The main screen (projects with their stats) is plain HTML/CSS and needs nothing new.

title: I5-external-specs-p3.md.txt
body:
# External specification text read at P3 (2026-10-31), as a fetch agent quoted it

Verbatim quotes, link markup and backticks removed by the agent. Pages read: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html and https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html (HTML Living Standard, "Last Updated 30 October 2026"), https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/ (W3C Working Draft, 26 October 2026). The synchronous-fixup target `infrastructure.html#node-remove-focus-fixup` was not fetched.

## Focus fixup — https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#event-loop-processing-model, the "update the rendering" steps, step 17

"For each doc of docs, if the focused area of doc is not a focusable area, then run the focusing steps for doc's viewport, and set doc's relevant global object's navigation API's focus changed during ongoing navigation to false."

Its note:

"For example, this might happen because an element has the hidden attribute added, causing it to stop being rendered. It might also happen to an input element when the element gets disabled."

"This will usually fire blur events, and possibly change events."

"In addition to this asynchronous fixup, if the focused area of the document is removed, there is a synchronous fixup. That one will not fire blur or change events."

## Inert — https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html

#inert-subtrees: "Inert nodes generally cannot be focused, and user agents do not expose the inert nodes to accessibility APIs or assistive technologies."

#the-inert-attribute: "The inert attribute is a boolean attribute that indicates, by its presence, that the element and all its flat tree descendants which don't otherwise escape inertness (such as modal dialogs) are to be made inert by the user agent."

#data-model, under "Elements that meet all the following criteria:": "the element is not inert;"

#focus-processing-model, key event routing: "If target node is not inert:"

No sentence the agent read states in words what happens to focus when a focused element becomes inert; the mechanism is step 17 above with the "not inert" criterion.

## Native checkedness — https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/

#el-input-checkbox: "checkbox role, with the aria-checked state set to "mixed" if the element's indeterminate IDL attribute is true, or "true" if the element's checkedness is true, or "false" otherwise"

#el-input-radio: "radio role, with the aria-checked state set to "true" if the element's checkedness is true, or "false" otherwise."

title: I8-founder-forks.md.txt
body:
# Engine debts — the founder's forks

Chunk `2026-10-31-engine-debts`, entry «Engine debts» (`v030-04`). Written at P4 in the away form on the operator's word (inputs#I1): every fork, with its dependences, in one file, **no provisional answer given**. The plan is not written and nothing is built until his word returns.

Each fork below changes behaviour for every document unless it says otherwise. By the playbook's engine-change rule his own answer is the ratification, recorded with his word as he gives it. A delegate's answer would stand PROVISIONAL. Every reading below was measured at `2109f1c2e` in both layout modes unless it says "read from source".

**To answer:** one line per fork, its number and the option's letter, e.g. `F1 A`, or his own words. `F6 A` and `all recommended` are both fine.

## All thirteen at a glance

| # | The question | Recommended | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | `visible_region` under a transform | A — fix it | small |
| F2 | A `scale(0)` box answers hits where nothing shows *(found at P3)* | A — fix it | small |
| F3 | `inert` focus fixup | A — clear focus at the mutator's flush | small |
| F4 | The tree names a focus it does not hold *(found at P3)* | A — fall back to the window | very small |
| F5 | Native checkedness in the tree | A — write it on checkable roles | very small |
| F6 | `multiple` select | A — pin as a stated limit | pin small · build large |
| F7 | `optgroup` | A — pin as a stated limit | pin small · build medium |
| F8 | Popup and clicking an option | A — no popup, option stays refused, pin | pin small · popup large |
| F9 | Lint's option overlap | A — exempt a select's options in `overlaps` | small |
| F10 | `change` on checkbox and radio | A — the engine fires it, script's copy removed | small |
| F11 | `change` on text input and range | A — pin as a stated limit | pin small · build medium |
| F12 | Load page's keyboard and contrast rows | A — add them | small |
| F13 | Cells has no keyboard path | A — the grid becomes one Tab stop with keys | medium, stand only |

## What depends on what

- **F9 depends on F8.** F9 A's exemption assumes options have no box of their own. Under F8 C (a painted popup) it must read "closed" only, and F9 is restated with the popup's work. F9 B is incompatible with F8 A and B unless he accepts every closed option reading `zero-size` or `off-screen`.
- **F8 B moves what F9 A leaves.** A driver click on an option changes `covered`'s stated limit and `stand_act_ids`' table; it does not change option bounds, so F9 A still holds.
- **F6 B pulls in F8.** A modelled `multiple` select shows rows, and its rows must take clicks; it needs F8's option click for that select at least. Its options also read real boxes, so F9 A's exemption would not cover them.
- **F7 B touches F9.** The exemption must also read an option under an `optgroup`.
- **F3 and F4 are separate on purpose.** F3 stops an inert node keeping focus. F4 stops the tree naming a focus it does not hold, for every cause, `display: none` and `hidden` included. F3 A alone leaves those; F4 A alone leaves the inert node taking keys. Choosing F3 C makes F4 the only guard.
- **F3 and F11.** Under F3 A the fixup fires no DOM event, so under F11 B or C a dirty text input made inert would lose its `change`.
- **F10 and the script runtime.** The script runtime already synthesises `change` on a checkbox or radio; an engine `change` without its removal fires twice.
- **F1 and F2.** Independent, but F1 A reads a degenerate clip as nothing visible, while F2 is what stops that box taking hits. Taking only F1 leaves a `scale(0)` box with no clip of its own swallowing clicks.
- **F12 and F13 are the ground of Epoch 6's «A11y re-read».** It re-asserts SC 2.1.1 · 2.4.3 · 1.4.3 on the served pages. Under F13 B or C it inherits a red row on Cells.
- **Upstream.** F2's lines sit beside `0980cce5f`'s `hit_inner` hunk, a textual conflict for Epoch 3's sync. Nothing here pre-empts that commit's meaning.

---

## Group 1 — Transforms

### F1 — `visible_region` under a transform

A scrolling box under a transform is read where it stands untransformed, so a driver call on a target that shows can be refused `off-screen`.

**Measured, and it narrows the debt.** The reconnaissance expected pan/zoom to hit this. A plain pan/zoom world (a `transform` on a box of absolutely positioned nodes, under an untransformed `overflow:hidden` viewport) **already reads right** at translate, `translate + scale(2)` and `scale(0.5)`, by harness and by driver `click`. The limit fires only where a box that clips lies under the transform: a node with its own `overflow:auto` body inside a panned or zoomed world. There, `click` is refused `off-screen` and lint reads `off-screen` and `truncated`, while the hit lands on the target. A scale is in reach, as his adaptation asked.

His adaptation's proof, the pan/zoom fixture, is written under every option. It adds no capability.

- **A — Fix it (Recommended).** `visible_region` maps each clipping box's padding box through the transforms, using the mapping the client rect already has. Exact under translate and scale. Under rotation it over-reads, since the region is the bounding box of the rotated clip. A page with no transform reads as today. It moves the act gate, the shot's crop and the lint together, drops `off-screen`'s limit sentence (and `docs/capabilities.md`'s, by hand), and renames the limit's pin. A node graph with scrolling node bodies then works through the driver. Cost: one method, one visibility.
- **B — Pin it as a stated limit.** No engine change. Plain pan/zoom is proven and the inner-scroller reading pinned; the text stays. A scrolling node body stays refused until someone fixes this.
- **C — Keep it as a residual.** No fix and no new proof beyond the fixture.

### F2 — A `scale(0)` box answers hits where nothing shows *(found at P3, not a recorded debt)*

A box under a non-invertible transform (`scale(0)`, `matrix(0,0,0,0,0,0)`) with no clip of its own takes a hit at points far from it: measured at (300, 200) and (590, 390) inside a 600 × 400 clip, though nothing is painted there. The inverse leaves NaN coordinates, and the hit's bounds test reads true on NaN. No panic. Any remote page can do this, and a click at such a point would land on the control that does not show.

- **A — Fix it (Recommended).** A non-invertible transform takes no hit for its subtree, as paint shows nothing there. A few lines in `hit_inner`, with a check of its own. It sits next to `0980cce5f`'s hunk: a textual conflict for Epoch 3.
- **B — Keep it as a residual.** A new `.andromeda/residuals.md` line owns it; no check. The behaviour stands.

---

## Group 2 — Focus

### F3 — `inert` focus fixup

Today, when `inert` lands on a focused node's box: the engine still says it is focused, the snapshot reads nothing focused, and no `blur` runs. **It still takes keys**: Enter clicked the inert button (count 1 → 2) and a focused inert text input took a typed character. Tab leaves it normally.

HTML (inputs#I5) runs the fixup in "update the rendering", and its note says that "will usually fire blur events, and possibly change events"; only the fixup on removal fires none.

- **A — Clear focus at the mutator's flush, for `inert` alone (Recommended).** Focus goes to the viewport through `clear_focus` (focus states, `FOCUS_WITHIN` chain, IME off, redraw, changed set), exactly what removing a focused node does today. **No DOM `blur` or `focusout` fires**, which departs from HTML's note: the mutator holds no route to dispatch events. Consequences: the next Tab starts from the document's first stop, not after the box; `inert_subtree`'s pin is restated; `disabled` and `hidden` are left as they read.
- **B — HTML's fixup at resolve, with `blur`.** Read `is_focussable` in the rendering step and fire `blur`. Closest to HTML, and it also covers a control disabled after taking focus, which **moves a pinned reading** (`a_button_disabled_after_it_took_focus_takes_no_key` says it keeps focus). It needs a new route from resolve to event dispatch, and page script then sees a new event trigger. `hidden` and `display: none` still need `is_focussable` to read them. Larger, and more for Epoch 3's merge.
- **C — Keep the limit.** Pin and text stand; an inert node keeps taking keys until focus moves.

### F4 — The tree names a focus it does not hold *(found at P3, not a recorded debt)*

`build_accessibility_tree` writes `focus` from the focused node with no check that the node was built. So an inert focused node, measured, leaves `focus` naming an absent id; `display: none` and `hidden` go through the same lines. AccessKit's consumer **panics** on that: `"Focused ID {:?} is not in the node list"` (inputs#I6, `src/tree.rs:89-94`). **Read from source, not run:** it needs a platform adapter and an active assistive technology. No stand binary builds an adapter. `rdme` and any embedder on the `blitz` crate's default features do (`blitz-shell`'s default `accessibility`), and the browser does with its optional `accessibility` feature; there, a page's own markup could trigger it.

- **A — Fall back to the window (Recommended).** The builder writes the window's id when the focused node was not built. About one line; a check through `&dyn Document`. No snapshot reading moves. The engine's focus is untouched; F3 deals with that.
- **B — Keep it as a residual.** A new line owns it, its proof waiting on the adapter witness that this version does not reach.

---

## Group 3 — Native checkedness

### F5 — A native checkbox or radio states its checked state in the tree

HTML-AAM (inputs#I5) maps checkedness to `aria-checked`. Today nothing is written. His «Исправить позже (Рекомендую)» (2026-10-18) left it for "a later chunk or the nearest accessibility work". The value is closed, on a crossing already ratified, so this is no widening (the playbook's field-inside-a-ratified-carrier rule).

**Measured from the code:** the snapshot's `checked` reads the element first and `pressed` is filtered off the five checkable roles, so **no snapshot, text or diff reading moves on a native control's own role**. The stand holds no checkbox or radio, so no committed check moves. Only `accessibility_states`' fourth test is restated. Clicks already mark the changed set. Proof stops at the tree handed to the adapter; what an assistive technology reads stays unmeasured. There is no `indeterminate` model, so `mixed` has no source.

- **A — Write it where the role is checkable (Recommended).** `toggled` true or false from the element's state when its role is one of the five. A native control whose `role` attribute names something else stays silent, so `pressed` never begins to read on it. About three lines.
- **B — Write it on every native checkbox and radio.** Closest to HTML-AAM's letter. `<input type=checkbox role=button>` would begin to read `pressed`, a reading that moves; it would be stated, not hidden.
- **C — Keep it as a residual.**

---

## Group 4 — The select model

### F6 — `multiple` select

It lays out as an empty bordered box and takes no key.

- **A — Pin it as a stated limit, with a check of its own (Recommended).** The stand holds none and the 0.4.0 inputs ask for none. The limit stays in the masters and is asserted by a check, not only stated.
- **B — Build it now.** A chosen set, list layout, rows, ctrl and shift selection, form entries, a select value beyond one, `type`'s meaning restated, and a default-sheet change for every document. Its own chunk in all but name, and it needs F8's option click.
- **C — Keep it as a residual, unpinned.**

### F7 — `optgroup`

Options inside an `optgroup` are not listed, so such a select holds no choice and shows nothing. Real pages use this.

- **A — Pin it as a stated limit, with a check of its own (Recommended).** The stand and the 0.4.0 inputs need none. The cost of leaving it is on remote pages only.
- **B — Build it now.** Walk one level in the option list, across `is_select_option`, the builder, `form.rs`, the mutator's selectedness, the snapshot's option parent and the default sheet's child combinator, with a disabled group's rule. About seven files; every document. No new key or verb.
- **C — Keep it as a residual, unpinned.**

### F8 — A painted popup, and clicking an option

No popup is painted; a driver `click` on an option is refused `covered`. Today an agent chooses through `type` or the arrows.

- **A — No popup; the option stays refused; pin it (Recommended).** `covered`'s reading, and Enter and Space opening nothing, get a check of their own. Nothing moves.
- **B — No popup; a driver `click` on an option chooses it.** Through `apply_select_choice`, keeping one write path. Convenient for agents, but a click then does something no pointer can, and `covered`'s text and `stand_act_ids`' table (68 accepted · 9 refused) move. Driver only; no engine change.
- **C — Paint a popup.** A new overlay in paint, hit and keys; a focus and key contract he would state; reduced-motion handling; colours as a new engine default, since the engine holds no tokens; `default.css` for every document. Option bounds then read real boxes when open, restating F9. Needs a route entry of its own: too large for this chunk. *Playbook: Boundary widening* — a validated surface would admit new input and pixels, so the wrap would still halt on it once, as his answer card.

### F9 — Lint reads a select's options as overlapping *(asked with F8)*

Every option is given its select's rect, so `lint` reports an `overlap` in every document; the flight booker reads one at boot.

- **A — Exempt a select's options in `overlaps` (Recommended).** A driver change only. Bounds stay; `stand_lint` becomes `[0, 0, 0, 0]`. It tells real select options from CRUD's `role="option"` rows by the element, not the role. No new field; a finding's form is unchanged.
- **B — Move the option bounds.** The snapshot gives each option a box of its own. It moves every reader: closed options would read `zero-size` or `off-screen`, the shot's crop and the refusal change, and the owner moves from the driver to the snapshot.
- **C — Keep it, pinned as measured.**

### F10 — `change` on checkbox and radio

The engine fires `input` alone, so a Dioxus app's `onchange` never runs. The script runtime already synthesises its own `change`.

- **A — The engine fires it; the script runtime's synthesis is removed (Recommended).** One event for both kinds of app: `change` after `input`, per HTML. Dioxus handlers gain a trigger they do not have today. A radio's `change` fires only on an actual change, which also narrows what script sees today (its synthesis fires on every `input`); a radio's unconditional `input` stays as it reads.
- **B — Pin it as a stated limit.** Dioxus `onchange` stays silent on these; script keeps its own.

### F11 — `change` on text input and range

HTML fires it on commit, not per keystroke, which needs per-input "value at focus" state and a route through blur.

- **A — Pin it as a stated limit, with a check of its own (Recommended).** The stand uses `oninput` throughout (`git grep` over `examples/seven_guis/src`), so nothing waits on it.
- **B — Build it for text input only.** A password's or file input's value must stay masked on every carrier, proven by a typed-sentinel check at `RUST_LOG=trace`. A file input's value holds a host path. Range stays `input` alone, stated.
- **C — Build it for text input and range.** As B, and range's founder-ratified rule of one `input` per change, with no `change`, is restated.

*Playbook, for B and C: Boundary widening* — the security plan calls a further exit for a control's value a boundary question, so the wrap would still halt on it once, as his answer card.

---

## Group 5 — The served pages' rows

### F12 — The load page's rows

**All read green when measured, so no colour or engine move is in play.** Tab `back-btn` → `load-fetch`, wrapping. Enter and Space each start the load. Contrast: `load-fetch` 5.47 · hover 6.83 · active 8.27, `back-btn` 11.09, `task-title` 18.88, `load-done` 15.96, each against 4.5.

- **A — Add the rows (Recommended).** In `stand_keyboard` and `stand_contrast`, beside the tables keyed by `LeanTask`, not inside them. Those two files already run in both legs, so **the `a11y` leg's fourteen-file list, which is his word, does not move**. Closes the OPEN gap in a11y-plan §5 and the load page's half of residual line 40.
- **B — Leave the gap open.** It stays with its residual line for «A11y re-read».

### F13 — Cells has no keyboard path

**Red on SC 2.1.1, measured, and it is the further fork the scope foresaw.** Tab stays on `back-btn`; **0 of 676 cells are focusable**; a cell opens only by pointer, and its editor then holds no focus. Contrast read so far is green: `back-btn` 11.09, `task-title` 18.88, `cell-input` 15.19; an empty cell holds no text; **a filled cell is not yet measured**, and any option below measures it.

- **A — The grid becomes one Tab stop with keys (Recommended).** The shape `crud-list` already has on the stand: one stop, arrows move the current cell, Enter opens the editor focused, Enter commits. A stand change, no engine change. It adds a stand element or attribute and new key handling, so the Tab table, the measured 5 parts and the lint's 490 may move and are re-measured. The current cell stays unstated to assistive technology, as `crud-list`'s row does; residual line 24 stays out.
- **B — Every cell a Tab stop.** 676 stops. Meets the letter of 2.1.1 and is poor to use; moves the screen most.
- **C — Pin the measured reading.** A row asserts Tab reaching `back-btn` alone; the gap stays owned, and «A11y re-read» inherits a red.

---

## Not asked — decided from the record, for his information

- **CARRY 2's three checks are written regardless.** `:open` read right on every path (boot, write, removal, `summary` click and Enter; `details` and `dialog`), so its check is new and moves nothing. A wrong reading would have come here as a fork.
- **The redraw route's check reaches its first hop only.** With a stand-in for winit's proxy provider, `send_event` is read through to its receiver and one wake-up, with no window. `BlitzShellProvider` and `application.rs` need a real window and stay with the windowed boot smoke; the check says so. It lives in blitz-shell's unit tests, so blitz-tests gains no dependency.
- **`pseudo_element_flow_classification` runs in both layout modes.** An edit to an upstream test; its first test, sampled, read alike in both. The additivity note records it, and the both-modes exception's text moves at wrap.
- **CARRY 3's stale `remove_attribute` is a wrap amendment**, never a phase edit.
- **No option above adds a verb, node key, cause, listener, env var or dependency.** A fix's merge surface goes to Epoch 3's «Upstream sync ahead of the UI graph». Nothing is sent upstream.

---

## His answers (2026-10-31, by dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the operator)

## The first firing, on `42eed99a6`: the entries, as they printed

```

failed 1: Stand checks repeated (failure)
running 5: oldest Test (windows) 182 s

**Entry 37** was not fired on this run.

## The job states at the stop

| Job | State |
|---|---|
| Rustfmt · Clippy · Test [default features] · Test CI scripts · Build counter example · Dependency audit · Build [default features] · MSRV Build [Rust 1.91] · Documentation · Accessibility (a11y) tests · Test (ios) | success |

## The failure

Read from the job's log (job 124508189681).

- **No test ran.** The log reaches `stand-repeat: round 1 of 3`, and the build fails in that round.
- **The linker died**, on three test binaries: `text_range_no_change_event`, `visible_region_transformed` and
  `stand_act_states`. Each reads `linking with cc failed`, `collect2: fatal error: ld terminated with signal 7 [Bus
  error], core dumped`.
- **The runner's disk was full:** `You are running out of disk space … Free space left: 5 MB`. That line stands after the
  failure, in the job's upload step.

`ld`'s bus error on a full disk is the expected form of this failure, and the warning names the disk. That is the direct
cause as read. The log holds no `df` reading from before the link.

## What is and is not known about why

| Reading | Value |
|---|---|
| The same job on the last green run, CI#40507800481 at `a6c6a37c7` | success, 3 rounds |
| Its restored cache, that run and this one | 957 MB in each |
| Targets this chunk added to this job (step 18) | 5 |
| One such test binary on the dev host, in debug | about 200 MB (`visible_region_transformed` 194 MB, `stand_act_states` 222 MB) |
| A free-disk step in this job | none. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:386` has one, on the `matrix_test` job alone |

**Inferred, not measured:** this chunk's five targets, near 1 GB by the dev host's figure, took a job already near its
limit over it. Three things stand against reading that as proven: the runner's own figures were not read, the two runs'
free space before the link is unknown, and `Test [default features]` built these targets among more and passed, with no
free-disk step either. Runner variance is not ruled out.

The operator, in session, 2026-10-31: "Operator's word: the free-disk step. The other 16 jobs read green. Give stand-repeat
ci.yml:386's action at its pinned sha, before rust-cache, with android: true, large-packages: false, swap-storage: false.
Entry 1 loses .github/workflows on this word: record that in the plan and evidence/ci.md, and scope records ci.yml."

The first report said the same action "already runs on the `matrix_test` job at `ci.yml:386`". **That was wrong.** The step

workflow held no measured run of the action before this fix, and the new run is its first witness here.

body:
# Select popup: the founder's forks

Chunk `2026-10-31-select-popup`, `v030-17`, last of Epoch 2. Answers are his to give, by dialog, relayed verbatim (inputs#I1). Each option's first line is its label. **Every fork here changes what the engine does for every document, remote pages included.** His own answer ratifies it; a delegate's would stand provisional. All together they are a *Boundary widening* (a validated surface admits new input and new pixels: an option's label and a group's label, painted, in every shot), so this chunk's wrap halts once as his answer card, as the route entry already says.

**What is common to every option below.** The list is drawn by the engine, inside the window, on top of the page and past any box that would clip it. Its rows are the select's own `option` elements, so each keeps its stable id open and closed. No new verb, cause, key name, carrier, port or crate is needed by any recommended answer.

**How far the browser comparisons go.** What Chromium, macOS and native menus do is from memory, not measured in this run. The code's behaviour is read from the tree (research.md).

---

## Group 1: focus and keys

### F1: What opens the list, and what a closed select's keys do

Today Enter and Space open nothing. The arrows, Home, End and typing change the choice directly, with no list. A click only focuses.

- **A: Click, Enter, Space open; the rest stays (Recommended).** A click on the select opens it and a second click closes it. Enter and Space open it (a Space while typed text still stands joins the text, as now). The arrows, Home, End and typing keep choosing with the list closed. This is how Chromium behaves on Windows and Linux. The stand's keyboard route to the return flight stays as it reads, so its Tab tables hold.
- **B: The arrows open too.** The arrows, Home and End open the list and no longer change a closed select's choice. This is the W3C pattern and macOS. It ends a ratified reading and moves `stand_keyboard`'s route and `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER`'s way in.
- **C: Only a click opens.** Enter and Space stay as they are. A keyboard user keeps choosing through the arrows and never sees the list, so the acceptance's "chosen by key" holds only for a closed select.

A disabled or inert select opens nothing under any option.

### F2: Keys while the list is open

- **A: Highlight, then confirm (Recommended).** The arrows, Home, End and typing move a highlighted row, skipping disabled ones; nothing is chosen yet. Enter or Space chooses it and closes. Escape closes with no choice. Tab chooses the highlighted row, closes and moves on, as Chromium and the W3C pattern do, and as Cells' open editor already does. One `input` then one `change` on a real change, none otherwise. Cost: the highlight is not in the snapshot, so an agent pressing keys sees it only in a screenshot. An agent can `click` a row by id instead, and the tool's help says so.
- **B: The same, but Tab closes with no choice.** Tab loses nothing typed by accident, but a keyboard user who tabs away discards the highlighted row.
- **C: The arrows choose at once.** Each step fires `input` and `change` with the list still open; Escape restores the value at opening, firing them again. Nothing is hidden from an agent. Apps hear every row passed over, a flight booker recalculating at each step.

### F3: Where focus is while the list is open

- **A: Stays on the select (Recommended).** Rows never take focus, so the Tab order does not change. The accessibility tree gains a native "expanded" on the select, the shape of F5 in Engine debts. The tree's focus stays on the select and `aria-activedescendant` stays unread by his «Оставить записанным (Рекомендую)» (2026-10-14), so an assistive technology hears that the list is open but not which row is highlighted. That is a stated limit. The list closes whenever the select stops holding focus, by any route, including `inert` (which fires no `blur`), `disabled`, `hidden` and removal.
- **B: Focus moves onto the rows.** Assistive technology can follow the row. Options become focusable, which moves every stated Tab table's meaning and the actionable-key check, and it reopens his word on `aria-activedescendant` for the same purpose by another road. Large.

### F4: A click outside the open list

- **A: Closes, and the click goes on (Recommended).** The list closes with no choice and the click acts on whatever it landed on, in one step. A driver's accepted `click` always lands, so its promise holds.
- **B: Closes, and the click is swallowed.** The target gets nothing, as some native menus behave. A driver's `click` on a visible button would be accepted and do nothing, which an agent cannot tell from a dead button.

---

## Group 2: the look

### F5: Reduced motion

The engine has no reduced-motion handling (measured absent).

- **A: No motion (Recommended).** The list appears and goes in one frame, so there is nothing to reduce and no OS setting to read. A long list's scrollbar fades as every scrollbar does today.
- **B: A short fade, with reduced-motion handling.** Needs a new read of the OS setting, registered as a new crossing, and a driver step that returns before the fade has run until an `advance`.

### F6: The engine's colours for the list

The engine holds no tokens, so these are new hardcoded defaults, as the `multiple` row's pair was.

- **A: Follow the select, one fixed highlight (Recommended).** The list takes the select's own text and background colours and its `1px solid #999` border (black on white by default; the stand's `#1a1a1a` on `#ffffff` carries over). The highlighted row is `#000000` on `#c8c8c8`, 12.56:1, the pair `multiple` rows already use. A disabled row is `#6d6d6d` on white, 5.17:1 by my arithmetic, to be measured. No shadow, no radius, no separate mark for the chosen row: the highlight starts on it, as in Chromium. Every pair is measured by a test.
- **B: A stronger highlight.** White on `#3a5ce5`, 5.47:1. More visible, but it makes the stand's accent an engine default, against the rule that stand values and engine defaults are kept apart.
- **C: Dark and Light palettes, chosen by the scheme, as scrollbars are.** More pairs to measure, and it mismatches the select itself, which stays white under Dark because the default sheet is Light-only.

---

## Group 3: the two limits the route gave this chunk

### F7: A group's label

Named in the tree and unpainted today. Its name there rests on an operator lean, not on his F7 of Engine debts, so this answer settles both.

- **A: Painted as a header row (Recommended).** In the list's colours, bold, unselectable, its options under it. A click on it does nothing and leaves the list open. It is page text in pixels and stays inside the ratified name crossing.
- **B: Left unpainted.** The rows run flat with no headers, and the limit stays stated.

### F8: `size`

Sent here by his «В чанк с попапом (Рекомендую)».

- **A: Read on a `multiple` select when written (Recommended).** A valid `size` makes it that many rows tall and the rest scroll. With no `size` it stays all rows, as built, so no existing page moves. A single select's `size` stays unread, a stated limit: it is always a closed box and a list.
- **B: HTML's whole rule.** A `multiple` select defaults to 4 rows, and a single select with `size` above 1 becomes an open list box. Correct, but it moves every `multiple` page and adds a second way a single select reads.
- **C: Left unread.** Pinned as a stated limit, with its owner a residual line. Cheapest.

---

## Group 4: what the driver reads

### F9: A driver `click` on an option of a *closed* select

The route says `covered`'s closed-option reading ends here. An option of the *open* list is accepted under every option; this asks about the closed one.

- **A: Still refused `covered`, its meaning restated (Recommended).** The fixed text gains that such an option lies under its select: click the select first. An agent reaches it in two calls, each something a pointer can do. Eight causes kept.
- **B: The click opens and chooses in one call.** Convenient, but a driver click then does what no pointer can, the objection in the text of his F8 B.

### F10: The lint on an open list (his F9, restated)

A list sits over the page by design. The rows have real boxes while open.

- **A: Rows read no `overlap`, the rest as usual (Recommended).** `overlaps` skips an open list's rows on either side, and they keep `clipped`, `off-screen` and `contrast`. A closed select reads exactly as today, and `stand_lint` stays `[0, 0, 0, 0]`.
- **B: Rows read `overlap`.** One finding per page element under the list, on every page with a list open: true and of no use.

---

## What he is not being asked

These are my leans, so a reader can object. Each stands unless he or the operator says otherwise.

- **Placement.** Below the select, or above where there is more room; at least the select's width; at most 20 rows, scrolling within. The list ignores a transform on the select's ancestors beyond starting at its on-screen box. It stays inside its own document, so inside an iframe it stays in the iframe.
- **Driver.** `click` on a select opens it. `type` on a select stays what it is today, choosing by its text with no list left open, and focuses with no click. `scroll` on a row scrolls the list. A click on a disabled row is accepted, changes nothing and leaves the list open, as a `multiple` select's row does.
- **A label's click** focuses the select and opens nothing, as browsers do.
- **The page scrolling** closes the list with no choice.
- **Windowed.** The same list reaches the window through the one paint path. No test launches a window, so it is read, not run; the existing boot smoke is all that runs it.
- **Reading whether it is open.** No new node key: an open list's rows read bounds of their own, a closed one's read the select's, and `differs` names them. By the closed-field rule (2026-10-10) this is not his to rule, and the operator is asked it separately.

---

## His answers (2026-10-31, by dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim)

# CI — 2026-10-31-select-popup

Two CI reads. The first, on the pre-CI commit, stopped the operator pass red on `Test (macos)`, a defect of this chunk's. The
operator's word took the fix and the second read: "your fix, a header heavier than a row on every build, the test as written;
a run with no synthesized bold paints as before."

## The first pass, in plan order

| Entry | What ran | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| 28 | `gate.py hygiene` | `hygiene: clean — read 708 (runs 697 · evidence 2 · inputs 9) · trails 14 not read · copies 7 not read by P1 — 0 host paths kept · binary 0 not read by P1` |

| 30 | `ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1800` (the operator's bound; the plan writes 2400) | **red**, below |
| 31 | the per-OS tally | not run, the pass having stopped |

Entry 30, verbatim:

```

runs: CI#41233234207 push in_progress/-
failed 1: Test (macos) (failure)
running 3: oldest Test (windows) 385 s
run open: CI#41233234207 in_progress
```

### CI#41233234207, read to its end

`completed · failure`, 17 jobs. **Failure, one:** Test (macos). **Success, sixteen:** Test [default features] · Rustfmt · Clippy
· Test CI scripts · Build counter example · Build wasm examples · Documentation · Dependency audit · MSRV Build [Rust 1.91] ·
Coverage report · Stand checks repeated · Test (ios) · Test (windows) · Test (android) · Accessibility (a11y) tests · Build
[default features].

The failure, from job 124633136964's log:

```
test a_groups_header_is_darker_than_a_row_by_weight ... FAILED
thread 'a_groups_header_is_darker_than_a_row_by_weight' panicked at tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_popup_painted.rs:292:9:
incremental false: the header reads 70972, the row 70972
test result: FAILED. 5 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

`cargo` stops at the first failing target by default, so that job's later targets were not read on this run.

## The cause, reproduced on this host

`packages/blitz-paint/src/text.rs` emboldened a run when `FONT_EMBOLDEN_ENABLED || (paint.synthesize_bold &&
synthesis.embolden())`, one vector for both arms. So on a build with the flag on, every run took one embolden and a header
read no heavier than a row. `FONT_EMBOLDEN_ENABLED` is true on macOS under `apple-font-embolden`, which `apps/browser`'s
default features name, and on any platform under `font-embolden`.

`cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --no-fail-fast --features blitz-paint/font-embolden --test select_popup_painted`, before the
fix, on this linux host:

```
test a_groups_header_is_darker_than_a_row_by_weight ... FAILED
incremental false: the header reads 70972, the row 70972
test result: FAILED. 5 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

The same two numbers macOS read. The same target with no feature read `6 passed; 0 failed`. No local gate builds that feature,
so the full block's green did not witness this, and the plan's "no OS-sensitive case" did not hold for it.

## The fix, read both ways

A synthesized bold now adds to the build's embolden, in place of standing beside it. The test is as written:
`git diff 8cd9c1286 -- tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_popup_painted.rs` prints nothing.

`--test select_popup --test select_popup_painted --test stand_act_popup`, after the fix:

| Build | `select_popup` | `select_popup_painted` | `stand_act_popup` |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain | 25 · 0 | 6 · 0 | 12 · 0 |
| `blitz-paint/font-embolden` | 25 · 0 | 6 · 0 | 12 · 0 |

### A run with no synthesized bold paints as before

A hash of the whole frame on each build, before and after the fix, from a throwaway test target removed before the commit.
The authored-bold paragraph goes through the ordinary path, which asks for no synthesized bold.

| Frame | Plain, before | Plain, after | Emboldening, before | Emboldening, after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| closed stand | `0d0c736a9a887c2d` | same | `2d2d15cbd4c193db` | same |
| open list, no header | `c523c16ac28cb124` | same | `543ea04ccbe22e96` | same |
| authored bold, closed | `8e827d95625ef994` | same | `ecee47a20afb4abd` | same |
| authored bold, open list | `d5bdbc31be8a2285` | same | `e981874a7ac52497` | same |
| open list with a header | `5f679e03df361e51` | same | `84b3332ff404b632` | **`f8295ffd12736ac5`** |

Only the frame holding a synthesized header moved, and only on the build that had the defect.

## The second pass, on the fix

| Entry | What ran | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| the commit | `fix(2026-10-31-select-popup): a group header heavier than a row on an emboldening build` | `715798ce2e5c7bb378b6474c6d2e2fe5b35fcc00`, above the pre-CI commit · 4 files · tree clean after |

| 30 | `ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 2400` | **green**, below |

Entry 30, verbatim:

```
715798ce2e5c verdict: green · checks 17/17 · wall 1381 s · runs CI#41235503227 completed/success

checks: Accessibility (a11y) tests · Build [default features] · Build counter example · Build wasm examples · Clippy

### The per-OS tally, against CI#41192433140

Result lines · passed · failed · ignored.

| Test [default features] | 214 · 1181 · 0 · 12 | 217 · 1236 · 0 · 12 | +3 · +55 |

Every moved count, by name:

- **+55 passed:** `select_popup` 25, `select_popup_painted` 6, `stand_act_popup` 12, blitz-dom's `node::select_list` tables 6,
  `stand_keyboard` 2, `stand_lint` 1, `cli_commands` 1, `host_log` 1, `mcp_log` 1.
